Validation: `dataObject` must name a data object of the project whose `membershipSettings.hasMembership` is true with `membershipObjectName`, `membershipObjectIdProperty` and `membershipUserIdProperty` set (an owner field alone is the user level, not this one); `managers` and `users` must be roles the membership role field can carry (the `rolePermissions` roles, the role property's enum options, or the built-in `member` of a roleless membership), compared case-insensitively; with `managers` empty the object needs an owner field (`sessionSettings.isOwnerField`), because only the creator could ever set a key; `idFrom` is required unless `mode` is `off` and must be a property path of `params` or `session`; one data object name may be resource-scoped in one service only, because a key's owner is `<object>:<row id>`; `budget.dailyCostCeilingUsd` must be a positive number; the brand must support scoped keys (google, azure-openai, bedrock, ollama and mock cannot take this level; fal and custom warn that saved keys are stored unverified); and an AgentHarness with `modelSettings.auth: userSubscription` may not use an entry whose resource mode is not `off`.

AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__mode.doc: `off` (default), `optional` or `required`. `optional`: a member's call uses the row's key when the row has one, and falls through to the tenant and saas levels otherwise. `required`: a call that names a row must use that row's key; with no key, or when the caller is not a member of the row, it fails with HTTP 428 `AI_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` naming the resource, and the saas key is never used. A `required` resource level makes the saas key in `configuration` optional, as a required tenant or user level does. Runs with no verified human actor (cron, a system session) skip the level, even when it is `required`.
AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__dataObject.doc: The data object whose rows own the keys, e.g. `workspace`. It must carry a complete membership configuration (`objectSettings.membershipSettings`). The service that declares the object owns the level: it runs the membership check and serves the key management of its rows. Use `serviceName:objectName` when the bare name is not unique in the project, to pick the service; every entry that names the object must then pick the same service, since a key's owner is `<object>:<row id>`.
AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__idFrom.doc: A property path of `params` or `session` that yields the row id (a string), e.g. `{ "js": "params.workspaceId" }`, `session.workspaceId` or `params['workspace-id']`. `params` is the call's parameters (a business API's resolved parameters, an agent's run input, a harness session's start body, the chat body's `context`), and `session` the verified caller session (attributes only). It is a path, not an expression: dot steps and quoted-string brackets only, no call, operator, function, template literal, computed key or optional chain, and no step through `constructor`, `__proto__` or `prototype`; anything else is a validation error. The path is language-neutral: a source for another language, when given, must be the same path or another path of `params` or `session`. `this` and `request` are not available, because the same path serves every caller. A value that is not a string reads as "no row named": the level is then skipped (`optional`) or refused (`required`).
AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__managers.doc: Member roles that may set, replace and delete the row's key, e.g. `["admin"]`. The row's creator (its `isOwnerField` property) always may. Each name must be a role of the data object's membership configuration. Empty: only the creator manages the key, which needs an owner field on the object.
AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__users.doc: Member roles whose calls may use the row's key, e.g. `["member", "admin"]`. The creator and the managers always may. Each name must be a role of the data object's membership configuration. Empty: every member whose membership row passes the configured status check.
AiProviderResourceCredentialScope.__budget.doc: Optional spend limit for calls made on a row's key. Under `costPolicy: ownerPays` the cost governors (agents, agentHub and AgentHarness sessions, the MCP-BFF chat) compare it with that row's own daily spend before every call; past it the call is refused `429 AGENT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` with `bucket: resource` and the row id. Other rows, and the application owner's budgets, are never read or charged. Absent = no ceiling for the row (the per-user daily token budget still applies).

__AiProviderResourceCredentialBudget.doc: The per-row spend limit of the resource level. Usage on a row's key is charged to the caller and to the row's own budget, never to the application owner's budgets.

AiProviderResourceCredentialBudget.__dailyCostCeilingUsd.doc: Maximum estimated spend in USD per row per UTC day on that row's key, priced from the same model price table as the agent cost ceilings; a positive number. Enforced per service replica, like every agent cost ceiling, before each call (see `budget`). Null = no ceiling.

__AmqpProvidersSettings.doc: Container for external AMQP broker configurations. Each entry is a named broker the project mirrors Kafka topics with — the mcpbff KafkaAMQPMirror discovers the entries from the blueprint and runs the bridging; regular services stay pure Kafka and never open AMQP connections. The deployed mcpbff gets AMQP_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider: HOST, PORT, VHOST and USE_TLS as committed env lines on every slot, USERNAME, PASSWORD and CONNECTION_STRING as CI/CD variables of the mcpbff repo; no business service carries any. Mirrors the bucketProvidersSettings / notificationProvidersSettings shape — a named array; multiple entries can share the same provider brand (e.g. two RabbitMQ clusters, or one RabbitMQ + one Azure Service Bus).

AmqpProvidersSettings.__amqpProviders.doc: List of configured external AMQP brokers. Add one entry per broker you want mirrored with the project's Kafka bus. Multiple entries can share the same provider brand (e.g. two RabbitMQ vhosts on different clusters).

__AmqpProvider.doc: A named external AMQP broker configuration. The `name` is the lookup key and the env-var prefix (e.g. `ordersBroker` → `AMQP_ORDERSBROKER_*`). The `provider` enum is the broker BRAND, and each brand declares which AMQP protocol the mcpbff mirror speaks to it: `rabbitmq` and `cloudamqp` speak AMQP 0-9-1; `artemis` and `azureServiceBus` speak AMQP 1.0. The `configuration` holds the connection credentials plus the explicit `mirroredTopics` mapping list (no wildcards — every mirrored address/topic pair is declared).

AmqpProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key by the mcpbff KafkaAMQPMirror and as the env-var prefix (AMQP_<NAME>_*). Must be a valid codeName.
AmqpProvider.name: String
AmqpProvider.__provider.doc: The broker brand. Each brand declares the AMQP protocol the mirror speaks: 'rabbitmq' = RabbitMQ (AMQP 0-9-1); 'cloudamqp' = CloudAMQP hosted RabbitMQ (AMQP 0-9-1); 'artemis' = Apache ActiveMQ Artemis (AMQP 1.0); 'azureServiceBus' = Azure Service Bus (AMQP 1.0).
AmqpProvider.__configuration.doc: Connection details + the mirroredTopics mapping list. The required keys depend on the brand — rabbitmq/cloudamqp: host, port (5672 default plain / 5671 TLS), vhost, username, password; artemis: host, port, username, password; azureServiceBus: connectionString. `username`, `password` and `connectionString` are delivered to the deployed mcpbff as CI/CD variables (AMQP_<NAME>_USERNAME / _PASSWORD / _CONNECTION_STRING), never as committed env lines; `password` and `connectionString` are masked in API responses.

__AmqpProviderConfig.doc: External AMQP broker connection credentials and the mirrored-topics mapping. Connection fields are a flat superset across both protocol families — only those relevant to the selected brand are read at runtime. `password` and `connectionString` are secret (masked in API responses). `mirroredTopics` is the EXPLICIT list of address/topic mappings the mcpbff KafkaAMQPMirror bridges — no wildcards.

AmqpProviderConfig.__host.doc: [rabbitmq|cloudamqp|artemis] The broker host, e.g. `rabbit.example.com`. Not used when `connectionString` is set (azureServiceBus).
AmqpProviderConfig.__port.doc: [rabbitmq|cloudamqp|artemis] The broker port. AMQP 0-9-1 default: 5672 (5671 with TLS); AMQP 1.0 (artemis) default: 5672.
AmqpProviderConfig.__vhost.doc: [rabbitmq|cloudamqp] The AMQP 0-9-1 virtual host, e.g. `/`. Ignored by AMQP 1.0 brands.
AmqpProviderConfig.__password.doc: [rabbitmq|cloudamqp|artemis] The broker password. Secret — masked in API responses; delivered to the deployed mcpbff as the CI/CD variable AMQP_<NAME>_PASSWORD (never a committed env line).
AmqpProviderConfig.__connectionString.doc: [azureServiceBus] The full Service Bus connection string (Endpoint=sb://…;SharedAccessKeyName=…;SharedAccessKey=…). Secret — masked in API responses; delivered to the deployed mcpbff as the CI/CD variable AMQP_<NAME>_CONNECTION_STRING (never a committed env line). When set, the host/port/username/password fields are not used.
AmqpProviderConfig.__useTls.doc: [rabbitmq|cloudamqp|artemis] Set true to connect over TLS (amqps). azureServiceBus is always TLS via its connection string.
AmqpProviderConfig.__mirroredTopics.doc: EXPLICIT list of mirrored address/topic mappings the mcpbff KafkaAMQPMirror bridges for this broker. Each entry declares a direction (`amqpToKafka` or `kafkaToAmqp`), the AMQP address (queue/exchange/topic on the broker), and optionally the Kafka topic (defaults to the amqpAddress when omitted). No wildcards — every mapping is declared. Duplicate mappings (same direction + amqpAddress + effective kafkaTopic) are rejected.

__AmqpMirroredTopic.doc: One explicit mirrored mapping between an AMQP address and a Kafka topic. `direction` decides the flow: `amqpToKafka` consumes the AMQP address and produces to the Kafka topic; `kafkaToAmqp` consumes the Kafka topic and publishes to the AMQP address. `kafkaTopic` defaults to `amqpAddress` when omitted. No wildcards — one entry per mirrored pair.

AmqpMirroredTopic.__direction.doc: The mirroring direction. 'amqpToKafka' = consume messages from the AMQP address and produce them to the Kafka topic; 'kafkaToAmqp' = consume the Kafka topic and publish to the AMQP address. Required.
AmqpMirroredTopic.__amqpAddress.doc: The address on the AMQP broker — a queue / exchange (0-9-1) or an AMQP 1.0 address (Artemis address, Service Bus queue/topic). Required, non-empty. No wildcards.
AmqpMirroredTopic.__kafkaTopic.doc: The Kafka topic on the project bus this mapping mirrors with. Optional — defaults to `amqpAddress` when omitted.

__AmqpProviderType.doc.#: The external AMQP broker brand for an AmqpProvider. Each brand declares which AMQP protocol the mcpbff KafkaAMQPMirror speaks to it — additional brands are additive behind the same enum.

__AmqpMirrorDirection.doc.#: The flow direction of one mirrored AMQP/Kafka mapping.
__AmqpMirrorDirection.doc.amqpToKafka: Consume from the AMQP address, produce to the Kafka topic.
__AmqpMirrorDirection.doc.kafkaToAmqp: Consume from the Kafka topic, publish to the AMQP address.

__VideoProvidersSettings.doc: Container for video-conference / live-broadcast provider configurations (docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §3). Each entry is a named media backend that a service `videoRooms[]` VideoRoom references by `roomBasics.providerName`. The generated service is the CONTROL PLANE only — it mints join tokens, drives the provider's room API, and receives webhooks; audio/video/RTMP/HLS media flows directly between clients and the provider's SFU/CDN, never through the service. The generator emits VIDEO_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct the provider client at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the bucketProvidersSettings / aiProvidersSettings shape — a named array; multiple entries can share the same provider brand (e.g. one LiveKit cluster for meetings and one AWS IVS account for broadcasts).

VideoProvidersSettings.__videoProviders.doc: List of configured video providers. Add one entry per media backend you want available. The `native` brand needs no credentials — the hosting platform provisions and manages the media server (locally the FARM LiveKit, in deploy a per-project instance).

__VideoProvider.doc:
A named video-conference / live-broadcast provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by `VideoRoom.roomBasics.providerName` and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainVideo` → `VIDEO_MAINVIDEO_*`). The `provider` enum selects the backend adapter; the `configuration` is a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the chosen `provider` (the aiProvidersSettings idiom). The brands cover the four adoption levels of docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §3a — embedded video API (MVP), CPaaS (growing SaaS), self-hosted (enterprise), and platform-provisioned native — so a project can start on a managed brand and migrate to self-hosted/native WITHOUT touching its VideoRoom business design (only the provider entry changes).

Capabilities per brand — interactive (SFU rooms: oneToOne/groupMeeting/webinar) vs broadcast (HLS out / RTMP in, the `broadcast` room kind):
- native: interactive + broadcast (platform-provisioned LiveKit incl. egress/ingress)
- livekit: interactive + broadcast (egress/ingress)
- jitsi: interactive (broadcast partial, via jibri)
- daily: interactive + broadcast
- whereby: interactive ONLY (Embedded join-URL model — the token route returns a room URL, not an SFU token; no server-side egress pipeline)
- zoom: interactive (Zoom Video SDK, NOT Zoom Meetings; broadcast partial via RTMP livestream)
- twilio: interactive ONLY (Twilio Video — carries platform risk: EOL announced 2023 then walked back; prefer other brands for new projects)
- vonage: interactive + broadcast (Vonage Video API, ex-TokBox/OpenTok; HLS/RTMP broadcast supported)
- agora: interactive + broadcast
- hundredMs: interactive + broadcast (100ms; HLS live streaming)
- awsIvs: broadcast ONLY
- mux: broadcast ONLY
- cloudflareStream: broadcast ONLY

Expected configuration keys per provider:
- native: NO keys — the hosting platform provisions the server (NativeBucket precedent); resolved at runtime from VIDEO_<NAME>_URL / VIDEO_<NAME>_API_KEY / VIDEO_<NAME>_API_SECRET (locally the FARM LiveKit ws://localhost:17880, devkey/secret)
- livekit: url (ws(s):// server url), apiKey, apiSecret (secret)
- jitsi: domain (e.g. meet.example.com), appId, appSecret (secret — JWT auth for self-hosted/JaaS)
- daily: domain (e.g. yourteam.daily.co), apiKey (secret)
- whereby: apiKey (secret — Whereby Embedded API key)
- zoom: sdkKey, sdkSecret (secret — Zoom Video SDK credentials)
- twilio: accountSid, apiKeySid, apiKeySecret (secret)
- vonage: applicationId, privateKey (secret — Vonage application private key)
- agora: appId, appCertificate (secret)
- hundredMs: accessKey, secret (secret — 100ms management credentials), templateId (optional default room template)
- awsIvs: awsAccessKeyId (secret), awsSecretAccessKey (secret), awsRegion
- mux: tokenId, tokenSecret (secret)
- cloudflareStream: accountId, apiToken (secret)

Secret keys (apiSecret, appSecret, apiKey, sdkSecret, apiKeySecret, privateKey, appCertificate, secret, awsAccessKeyId, awsSecretAccessKey, tokenSecret, apiToken) are masked in API responses and emitted to VIDEO_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

VideoProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from VideoRoom.roomBasics.providerName and as the env-var prefix (VIDEO_<NAME>_*). Must be a valid codeName.
VideoProvider.name: String
VideoProvider.__provider.doc: The backend provider brand. Decides which keys are expected in `configuration`, which adapter the codegen wires up, and which room kinds the provider can host (interactive SFU kinds vs the broadcast kind — see the VideoProvider doc string capability list).
VideoProvider.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of provider-specific credentials and settings. The required keys depend on `provider` — see the VideoProvider doc string for the per-provider key list. Empty/absent for the `native` brand (the hosting platform provisions the server). Sensitive keys are masked in API responses and emitted to environment variables at codegen time.

__VideoProviderType.doc.#: The media backend brand for a VideoProvider. Interactive brands host SFU rooms (oneToOne/groupMeeting/webinar); broadcast-capable brands host the broadcast room kind (HLS/CDN delivery, optional RTMP ingest). Additional brands are additive behind the same enum.
__VideoProviderType.doc.native: Platform-provisioned LiveKit — interactive + broadcast, NO designer credentials (the NativeBucket precedent). Locally backed by the FARM LiveKit (:17880); in deploy the deployer stands up a per-project server.
__VideoProviderType.doc.livekit: LiveKit (self-hosted or LiveKit Cloud) — interactive + broadcast via egress/ingress. url + apiKey/apiSecret.
__VideoProviderType.doc.jitsi: Jitsi Meet (self-hosted or JaaS) — interactive; broadcast only partial (jibri).
__VideoProviderType.doc.daily: Daily — SaaS, interactive + broadcast. The most startup-friendly embedded video API.
__VideoProviderType.doc.whereby: Whereby Embedded — SaaS, interactive ONLY via the join-URL model (rooms are created through the API and joined by URL/iframe; no SFU token, no server-side egress). The fastest MVP path.
__VideoProviderType.doc.zoom: Zoom Video SDK (NOT Zoom Meetings) — SaaS, interactive; broadcast partial via RTMP livestream. Build-your-own-UI SDK; common in healthcare.
__VideoProviderType.doc.twilio: Twilio Video — SaaS, interactive ONLY. CAVEAT: platform risk — Twilio announced Programmable Video EOL in 2023 and later walked it back; prefer other brands for new projects.
__VideoProviderType.doc.vonage: Vonage Video API (ex-TokBox/OpenTok) — SaaS, interactive + broadcast (HLS/RTMP). Long healthcare history.
__VideoProviderType.doc.agora: Agora — SaaS, interactive + broadcast. Excellent mobile performance, strong in Asia.
__VideoProviderType.doc.hundredMs: 100ms — SaaS, interactive + broadcast (HLS live streaming). Developer-first, template-driven rooms.
__VideoProviderType.doc.awsIvs: Amazon IVS — broadcast ONLY (YouTube-Live-style channels, RTMP ingest → HLS).
__VideoProviderType.doc.mux: Mux Live — broadcast ONLY (RTMP ingest → HLS).
__VideoProviderType.doc.cloudflareStream: Cloudflare Stream Live — broadcast ONLY (RTMP/SRT ingest → HLS).

__MailAccountsSettings.doc: Container for project-level mail-account configurations (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md). An entry is a mailbox the project owns or, with ownerScope tenant / user, a mailbox template that tenants or users connect their own mailboxes to. A MailAccount is a REAL MAILBOX the project owns — unlike a NotificationProvider (a fire-and-forget outbound channel), a mail account is bidirectional: it can be listened to (autoListen → normalized inbound-mail envelopes on Kafka), checked and read on demand, and used to send or reply on behalf of the account. The mcpbff bridge host owns ALL mailbox connectivity — regular services never open an IMAP/API connection; they consume the Kafka envelope topic and reach the mailbox through mail actions (the amqpProvidersSettings / enterpriseIntegrationsSettings precedent). The generator emits MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_* environment variables per account so the bridge can construct the mailbox client at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the notificationProvidersSettings shape — a named array; multiple entries can share the same platform (e.g. two IMAP hosts, or one Gmail plus one Microsoft 365 account).

MailAccountsSettings.__mailAccounts.doc: List of configured mail accounts. Add one entry per mailbox you want available. Multiple entries can share the same platform (e.g. two IMAP/SMTP accounts on different hosts, or one Gmail and one Microsoft 365 account — distinct names).

__MailAccount.doc:
A named mail account — a real mailbox the project can listen to, check, read, and send from (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md). The `name` is the lookup key used by mail actions (check / read / send-on-behalf reference an account by name) and the env-var prefix (e.g. `support` → `MAIL_ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_*`). The `platform` enum selects the connector: `imapSmtp` speaks RFC-standard IMAP (listen/read) + SMTP (send) and works against any standards-compliant host — including Gmail and Microsoft 365 when paired with authKind=xoauth2; `gmail` selects the native Gmail API connector (users.messages/history, users.watch push); `microsoftGraph` selects the native Microsoft Graph connector (/me or /users/{address} messages, change-notification subscriptions with delta-query polling fallback). The `authKind` selects the credential model: `password` is basic auth and is valid ONLY for imapSmtp (Google and Microsoft retired basic auth on their mailboxes); `xoauth2` is the OAuth2 bearer model (SASL XOAUTH2 on IMAP/SMTP, native OAuth on the API connectors). The `configuration` is a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the (platform, authKind) pair; blueprint validation rejects incomplete combos.

Expected configuration keys per (platform, authKind):
- imapSmtp + password: imapHost, smtpHost, username, password (secret). Optional: imapPort (default 993), smtpPort (default 587), imapSecure (default true), smtpSecure (default false = STARTTLS on 587).
- imapSmtp + xoauth2: imapHost, smtpHost, username, clientId, clientSecret (secret), refreshToken (secret), tokenUrl (the OAuth2 token endpoint, e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token). Optional: imapPort, smtpPort, imapSecure, smtpSecure, scope.
- gmail + xoauth2: clientId, clientSecret (secret), refreshToken (secret). The account `address` doubles as the API principal. Optional: tokenUrl (default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token), scope, pubsubTopic (full Pub/Sub topic name for users.watch push wake-ups — operator setup in the ADR).
- microsoftGraph + xoauth2: tenantId, clientId, clientSecret (secret) — app-only client-credentials against Microsoft Graph (the dynamics365 enterprise-integration precedent). Optional: tokenUrl (default the tenant-scoped Azure AD v2.0 endpoint https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenantId>/oauth2/v2.0/token), scope (default https://graph.microsoft.com/.default), refreshToken (secret — opt into the delegated flow, addressing /me instead of /users/<address>), notificationUrl (a public HTTPS callback for a Graph change-notification subscription — operator setup in the ADR).
- gmail + password / microsoftGraph + password: INVALID — both platforms retired basic auth; validation rejects the combo (MAIL_ACCOUNT_INVALID_AUTH_KIND).

Secret keys (password, clientSecret, refreshToken) are masked in API responses and emitted to MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

Owner scope: `ownerScope` absent or `project` is everything above. `tenant` / `user` make the entry a MAILBOX TEMPLATE (see the ownerScope field): no `address`, no username / refreshToken / password in `configuration` (the owner's connection supplies the IMAP login and the credential), and `maxMailboxesPerOwner` (unset = 5, bounds 1 to 20) and `inlineBody` (unset = false, metadata-only events) apply. Required template keys per (platform, authKind): imapSmtp + password: none (imapHost / smtpHost optional: set, they fix the server; unset, the owner names a server at connect time, validated to public DNS on fixed ports); imapSmtp + xoauth2: imapHost, smtpHost, clientId, clientSecret (secret), tokenUrl; gmail + xoauth2: clientId, clientSecret (secret); microsoftGraph + xoauth2: tenantId, clientId, clientSecret (secret); the token endpoint is built from tenantId: a directory id admits that directory's mailboxes only, `organizations` (or `common`) admits any work or school directory of a multi-tenant app. The OAuth app keys stay project secrets on the MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_* env path.

MailAccount.__name.doc: Unique account identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from mail actions and as the env-var prefix (MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_*). Must be a valid codeName.
MailAccount.name: String
MailAccount.__ownerScope.doc: Who owns the mailbox behind this entry. `project` (the default; an absent ownerScope is project) is the single mailbox the project itself owns: its address and every credential are on this entry, secrets delivered as MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_* deploy env. `tenant` and `user` turn the entry into a MAILBOX TEMPLATE: it fixes the platform, the authKind, the OAuth app (clientId, clientSecret, tokenUrl, tenantId: project secrets on the same MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_* env path), the listen settings and the send / reply flags, and each owner connects their own mailboxes to it, at most `maxMailboxesPerOwner` each. With `tenant` the owner is a tenant and a tenant admin connects the mailbox (a shared info@ inbox); `tenant` needs a multi-tenant project (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TENANT_SCOPE_SINGLE_TENANT). With `user` every user connects their own company mailbox; `user` needs the auth service, i.e. a configured authentication module (MAIL_ACCOUNT_USER_SCOPE_NO_AUTH). The owner's credential (refreshToken for xoauth2, password for password auth), the IMAP login and the mailbox address come from the owner's connection, never from the blueprint: a template leaves `address` empty (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_ADDRESS) and refuses username / refreshToken / password in `configuration` (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_OWNER_CREDENTIAL). Template mailboxes are run by the mcpbff, the mail runtime: its manifest lists a template as a dynamic account with no env lookup for owner credentials. A mail action in a nodejs service names a template together with a runtime `mailbox` reference (the mailbox of the triggering event, or the session owner's own mailbox; the codename alone is MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_STATIC_REFERENCE); in a service whose language has no template support a template is refused (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED); project accounts work in every language as before. The mcpbff listens to every connected mailbox of a template with autoListen and publishes each message as an owner-stamped event (tenantId, ownerUserId or the owner tenant, the mailbox, the message id and its metadata) on the project-scoped wire name of the template's listenTopic, `<projectCodename>-<listenTopic>`, keyed by mailbox; a listening template may not share a listenTopic with a listening project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_TOPIC_SHARED).
MailAccount.__address.doc: The mailbox email address this account represents (e.g. support@acme.com). Used as the From/Sender identity for on-behalf sends and as the API principal for the native connectors. Required on a project account; left empty on a template (ownerScope tenant or user), where every connected mailbox brings its own address (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_ADDRESS).
MailAccount.__platform.doc: The mailbox platform connector. `imapSmtp` is the standards-based connector (any IMAP/SMTP host, including Gmail and Microsoft 365 via xoauth2); `gmail` selects the native Gmail API connector; `microsoftGraph` selects the native Microsoft Graph connector. Decides which keys are expected in `configuration`.
MailAccount.__authKind.doc: The credential model. `password` = basic username/password auth, valid only for platform=imapSmtp (Google/Microsoft retired basic auth). `xoauth2` = OAuth2 bearer credentials (SASL XOAUTH2 for imapSmtp, native OAuth for gmail/microsoftGraph).
MailAccount.__autoListen.doc: When true, the mcpbff bridge host watches this mailbox (IMAP IDLE / API subscription) and publishes every new message as a normalized envelope to the Kafka topic in `listenTopic`. When false, the mailbox is only reachable on demand through mail actions.
MailAccount.__listenTopic.doc: Kafka topic the listener publishes normalized inbound-mail envelopes to. Defaults to the project-wide `new-email-arrived`; override per account to route a mailbox to its own topic (e.g. a dedicated topic for invoices@). A project account publishes its bare envelope on exactly this name; a mailbox template (ownerScope tenant or user) publishes its owner-stamped events on the project-scoped wire name `<projectCodename>-<listenTopic>` (a Kafka controller naming the bare topic is scoped onto it), so a listening template and a listening project account may not share one listenTopic (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_TOPIC_SHARED).
MailAccount.__markAsSeen.doc: When true (default), the listener flags a message as seen on the mailbox only AFTER its envelope is successfully published to Kafka — an unseen message always means an undelivered envelope, and a crash between fetch and publish redelivers rather than drops. Set false to leave the mailbox untouched (e.g. when humans share the inbox).
MailAccount.__sendEnabled.doc: When true, send actions may originate new mail on behalf of this account. Disable for listen-only mailboxes (e.g. an intake address that must never send).
MailAccount.__replyEnabled.doc: When true, send actions may reply within an existing thread on behalf of this account (threading via inReplyTo/references headers). Disable to allow only fresh outbound mail — or combine with sendEnabled=false for a fully read-only account.
MailAccount.__maxMailboxesPerOwner.doc: Template only (ownerScope tenant or user): the most mailboxes ONE owner (one tenant, or one user) may connect to this template. Unset reads 5. Bounds: 1 to 20 inclusive (MAIL_ACCOUNT_MAX_MAILBOXES_OUT_OF_RANGE); the scoped-credential store that holds the connected mailboxes applies the same default and ceiling. Refused when set on a project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_KEY_ON_PROJECT), which is exactly one mailbox; unset is accepted there.
MailAccount.__inlineBody.doc: Template only (ownerScope tenant or user): when true, the inbound-mail event of a connected mailbox also carries the message body (text and html). Unset or false (the default) publishes metadata only: from, to, subject, date, attachment metadata, message id, tenantId, ownerUserId and mailbox; a consumer reads the body on demand through ReadMail. Refused when true on a project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_KEY_ON_PROJECT), whose event shape is unchanged; unset or false is accepted there. The body on the bus is the one exception to metadata-only: set it only when every consumer of the template's topic may read the owners' mail.
MailAccount.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of connection settings and credentials. The required keys depend on the (platform, authKind) pair — see the MailAccount doc string for the per-combo key list. Sensitive keys (password, clientSecret, refreshToken) are masked in API responses and emitted to MAIL_ACCOUNT_<NAME>_* environment variables at codegen time.

__MailAccountOwnerScope.doc.#: Who owns the mailbox of a MailAccount. `project` is a mailbox the project owns (one entry, one mailbox); `tenant` and `user` make the entry a template that owners connect their own mailboxes to.
__MailAccountOwnerScope.doc.project: The project owns the mailbox: address and credentials are on the entry (the default; absent means project).
__MailAccountOwnerScope.doc.tenant: Template: each tenant connects its own mailboxes (by a tenant admin, e.g. a shared info@ inbox). Needs a multi-tenant project.
__MailAccountOwnerScope.doc.user: Template: each user connects their own mailboxes. Needs the auth service.

__MailAccountPlatform.doc.#: The mailbox platform connector for a MailAccount. All three have shipped runtimes: `imapSmtp` (v1), `gmail` (native Gmail API), `microsoftGraph` (native Microsoft Graph). Additional platforms are additive behind the same enum.
__MailAccountPlatform.doc.imapSmtp: RFC-standard IMAP (listen/read) + SMTP (send). Works against any standards-compliant host — including Gmail and Microsoft 365 when paired with authKind=xoauth2 (both retired basic auth).
__MailAccountPlatform.doc.gmail: Gmail API native connector (users.messages / users.watch push notifications). OAuth2 client credentials + refresh token; the account address is the API principal. Also reachable via imapSmtp+xoauth2 against imap.gmail.com.
__MailAccountPlatform.doc.microsoftGraph: Microsoft Graph native connector (/me or /users/{address} messages, change-notification subscriptions with delta-query polling fallback). App-only client-credentials (tenantId/clientId/clientSecret) by default, or a delegated refresh token; the account address is the API principal. Also reachable via imapSmtp+xoauth2 against outlook.office365.com where protocol access is enabled.

__MailAccountAuthKind.doc.#: The credential model for a MailAccount.
__MailAccountAuthKind.doc.password: Basic username/password (or app-password) auth. Valid ONLY for platform=imapSmtp — Google and Microsoft retired basic auth on their mailboxes.
__MailAccountAuthKind.doc.xoauth2: OAuth2 bearer credentials — SASL XOAUTH2 on IMAP/SMTP, native OAuth on the gmail/microsoftGraph connectors. Required for Microsoft 365 and Gmail mailboxes.

__EnterpriseIntegrationsSettings.doc: Container for enterprise-platform integrations. Each entry is a named integration bound to one platform (Salesforce, SAP S/4HANA + ECC, Dynamics 365, HubSpot). The mcpbff service discovers the entries from the blueprint and owns ALL connectivity to the platform — regular services never open a connection; they run business logic around the enterprise object and reach the platform through the mcpbff bridge over signed M2M. The generator emits ENTERPRISE_<NAME>_* environment variables per integration so the mcpbff bridge can construct the platform client at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the amqpProvidersSettings shape — a named array; the connectors are TypeScript-only (mcpbff), never ported to the 6 non-Node targets.

EnterpriseIntegrationsSettings.__enterpriseIntegrations.doc: List of configured enterprise-platform integrations. Add one entry per platform instance you want the project's mcpbff to connect to. Multiple entries can target the same platform (e.g. a Salesforce sandbox and a Salesforce production org — distinct names).

__EnterpriseIntegration.doc:
A named enterprise-platform integration. The `name` is the lookup key used by the mcpbff bridge and the env-var prefix (e.g. `salesProd` → `ENTERPRISE_SALESPROD_*`). The `platform` enum selects the connector implementation shipped under `_in/mcpbff/_template/src/enterprise/connectors/` — connectors are TypeScript-only and run exclusively in mcpbff. The `configuration` is a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the chosen `platform`; the UI and the agent ontology doc enforce the per-platform shape.

Expected configuration keys per platform:
- salesforce: loginUrl (required, My-Domain login URL e.g. https://acme.my.salesforce.com), clientId (required, Connected App consumer key), clientSecret (required, secret), apiVersion (optional, defaults to v60.0)
- sapS4Hana / sapEcc: baseUrl (required, Gateway/OData base URL), sapClient (optional, SAP client number), username (communication/service user — the normal on-prem option), password (secret), apiKey (secret — alternative auth for API-hub-style hosts; used when username/password absent), services (optional, array of OData service descriptors [{name,path}]). At least one complete auth family (username+password OR apiKey) must be present.
- dynamics365: tenantId (required, Azure AD/Entra tenant id), clientId (required, app registration client id), clientSecret (required, secret), environmentUrl (required, Dataverse environment URL)
- hubspot: accessToken (required, secret, private-app pat-… token), baseUrl (optional, defaults to https://api.hubapi.com)
- netsuite (anticipated — no connector yet, mcpbff answers 501): accountId (required, account/realm id), consumerKey, consumerSecret (secret), tokenId (secret), tokenSecret (secret) — token-based auth quartet
- servicenow (anticipated — no connector yet, mcpbff answers 501): instanceUrl (required), username + password (secret) OR clientId + clientSecret (secret)
- workday (anticipated — no connector yet, mcpbff answers 501): baseUrl (required), tenant (required), clientId + clientSecret (secret) + refreshToken (secret) OR username + password (secret, ISU)
- zoho (anticipated — no connector yet, mcpbff answers 501): clientId (required), clientSecret (required, secret), refreshToken (required, secret), accountsUrl (optional, defaults to https://accounts.zoho.com), apiDomain (optional, defaults to https://www.zohoapis.com)

Secret keys (clientSecret, password, apiKey, accessToken, consumerSecret, tokenId, tokenSecret, refreshToken) are masked in API responses and emitted to ENTERPRISE_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time. sapEcc shares the exact SAP Gateway OData contract + connector as sapS4Hana — a distinct brand only so the integration records which ERP it really is.

EnterpriseIntegration.__name.doc: Unique integration identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key by the mcpbff bridge and as the env-var prefix (ENTERPRISE_<NAME>_*). Must be a valid codeName.
EnterpriseIntegration.name: String
EnterpriseIntegration.__platform.doc: The enterprise platform this integration connects to. Selects which connector the mcpbff bridge instantiates and which keys are expected in `configuration`.
EnterpriseIntegration.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of platform-specific credentials and connection settings. The required keys depend on `platform` — see the EnterpriseIntegration doc string for the per-platform key list. Sensitive keys (clientSecret, password, apiKey, accessToken, consumerSecret, tokenId, tokenSecret, refreshToken) are masked in API responses and emitted to ENTERPRISE_<NAME>_* environment variables at codegen time.

__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.#: Identifies the enterprise platform backend for an EnterpriseIntegration. Connector-backed values map to a TypeScript connector under `_in/mcpbff/_template/src/enterprise/connectors/` that the mcpbff bridge instantiates — these are NOT ported to the 6 non-Node codegen targets. Anticipated values (netsuite, servicenow, workday, zoho) are accepted and validated against the provider-config catalog, but the mcpbff bridge answers 501 until their connector ships. Additional platforms are additive behind the same enum.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.salesforce: Salesforce — CRM. OAuth client-credentials (Connected App); sObject describe metadata.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.sapS4Hana: SAP S/4HANA — ERP via SAP Gateway OData. $metadata (EDMX) ingestion with communication-user (basic) auth, or APIKey for API-hub hosts.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.sapEcc: SAP ECC via SAP Gateway — same OData catalog + $metadata surface and connector as sapS4Hana; a distinct brand so the integration records the real ERP. Gateway-less ECC (RFC/BAPI/IDoc) is NOT covered.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.dynamics365: Microsoft Dynamics 365 — Dataverse via Azure AD (Entra) client-credentials; $metadata schema.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.hubspot: HubSpot — CRM. Private-app token; CRM object schemas.
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.netsuite: Oracle NetSuite — ERP. Anticipated: token-based auth (accountId + consumer/token pairs); no mcpbff connector yet (501 at runtime).
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.servicenow: ServiceNow — ITSM. Anticipated: instanceUrl + basic or OAuth auth; no mcpbff connector yet (501 at runtime).
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.workday: Workday — HCM/Financials. Anticipated: tenant + REST OAuth or ISU basic auth; no mcpbff connector yet (501 at runtime).
__EnterprisePlatformType.doc.zoho: Zoho — CRM. Anticipated: OAuth refresh-token trio (clientId/clientSecret/refreshToken) + data-center hosts; no mcpbff connector yet (501 at runtime).

__EnterpriseHubConfig.doc: The project-level enterprise-integration asset hub (module). Holds one EnterpriseModel per connected enterprise platform. An EnterpriseModel catalogs the external assets a designer works with — business objects, business events, and business actions — authored against the platform's design-time metadata. These assets are then consumed by services: DataObject projection, BusinessApi Kafka triggers, and ExternalBusinessAction. The connection credentials themselves live in projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings; this module is the design-time catalog, not the connection config. Mirrors the AgentHubConfig module shape.

EnterpriseHubConfig.__enterpriseModels.doc: One EnterpriseModel per connected enterprise platform. Each model binds to a single integration (by integrationName) and catalogs its objects, events, and actions. Add a model per platform you integrate with (e.g. an SAP model and a Salesforce model).

__EnterpriseModel.doc: A model of one connected enterprise platform's assets (chapter). Bound to a single integration via modelBasics.integrationName (must match a projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings.enterpriseIntegrations[].name). Catalogs the external assets authored against that platform's metadata: enterpriseObjects (referenceable business objects), enterpriseEvents (business events mapped to Kafka), enterpriseActions (invokable business functions). Mirrors the AIAgent chapter shape (a named chapter in a module-level array).

EnterpriseModel.__enterpriseObjects.doc: External business objects this model exposes — each references an object in the platform's metadata (e.g. SAP A_BusinessPartner, Salesforce Account). Services can project a DataObject onto one via objectSettings, or read/search it through the mcpbff bridge.
EnterpriseModel.__enterpriseEvents.doc: Business events this model subscribes to — each maps a platform event source to a Kafka topic (via the AMQP→Kafka mirror for AMQP-native platforms like SAP Event Mesh). A BusinessApi can then be triggered by the mapped Kafka event.
EnterpriseModel.__enterpriseActions.doc: Invokable business functions this model exposes — each references a platform-side function (SAP BAPI / OData function import, Salesforce Apex/invocable action, …). A BusinessApi ExternalBusinessAction invokes one through the mcpbff bridge.
EnterpriseModel.__modelBasics.doc: Core settings of the model (section): names the model and binds it to a configured integration via `integrationName` — shared by every asset in the model.

__EnterpriseModelBasics.doc: Core settings for an EnterpriseModel (section). Names the model and binds it to a configured integration; the integrationName is shared by every asset in the model.

EnterpriseModelBasics.__name.doc: Unique model identifier within the project's enterpriseHub. Names this model (e.g. 'sapErp', 'salesforceCrm'). Must be a valid codeName.
EnterpriseModelBasics.name: String
EnterpriseModelBasics.__integrationName.doc: The connected integration this model binds to. Must match a projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings.enterpriseIntegrations[].name — that entry supplies the platform + credentials the mcpbff bridge uses at runtime. Every asset in this model targets that integration's platform.
EnterpriseModelBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this enterprise model covers.

__EnterpriseObject.doc: A reference to a business object in the platform's metadata (section) — e.g. SAP A_BusinessPartner, Salesforce Account, HubSpot contacts. It can be read/searched through the mcpbff bridge, used as an action's param/result shape, or projected onto a DataObject (objectSettings.enterpriseProjection, later slice) with a field map. Defining an EnterpriseObject does NOT require a DataObject — projection is a separate, optional step.

EnterpriseObject.__name.doc: Unique object identifier within this model. The name services reference. Must be a valid codeName.
EnterpriseObject.name: String
EnterpriseObject.__platformObject.doc: The object's identifier in the platform's metadata — the entity set / sObject / object type name (e.g. 'A_BusinessPartner', 'Account', 'contacts'). The authoring agent picks this from the design-time metadata snapshot.
EnterpriseObject.__externalIdField.doc: The platform field that is the object's primary key / stable identity (e.g. 'BusinessPartner', 'Id'). Used to dedupe on read and to key upserts when the object is projected/synced.
EnterpriseObject.__selectedFields.doc: The subset of the platform object's fields this model works with (metadata field names). Empty/null means all fields. Drives which columns are read and which are offered when mapping to a DataObject.

__EnterpriseEvent.doc: A business event the model subscribes to (section), mapped to a Kafka topic so the rest of the OpenAPPL application can consume it. For AMQP-native platforms (SAP Event Mesh, Azure Service Bus) the mapping rides the existing AMQP→Kafka mirror; other platforms get a per-platform listener adapter in the mcpbff bridge (later slice). Once on Kafka, any BusinessApi can be triggered by it via its kafka controller.

EnterpriseEvent.__name.doc: Unique event identifier within this model. Must be a valid codeName.
EnterpriseEvent.name: String
EnterpriseEvent.__amqpProviderName.doc: For AMQP-native event transports (SAP Event Mesh = AMQP 1.0; Microsoft Dynamics via Azure Service Bus = AMQP 1.0), the broker this event streams from — must match a projectSettings.amqpProvidersSettings.amqpProviders[].name. The existing KafkaAMQPMirror bridges the platform address to `kafkaTopic`; no new runtime. Leave null for non-AMQP platforms (Salesforce Pub/Sub, HubSpot webhooks) — their source bindings + mcpbff listener adapters land in a later slice, publishing to the same `kafkaTopic`.
EnterpriseEvent.__platformEventSource.doc: The platform-side event source address. For AMQP-native transports this is the AMQP address (queue / topic / exchange) on `amqpProviderName` the mirror consumes; for Salesforce it is the Pub/Sub topic / CDC channel, for HubSpot the webhook subscription (both wired in later slices).
EnterpriseEvent.__kafkaTopic.doc: The Kafka topic the platform event is mirrored onto — the uniform output contract regardless of source transport. A BusinessApi consumes this via its kafkaSettings controller. Defaults to the event name when omitted.

__EnterpriseAction.doc: An invokable platform-side business function (section) — a SAP BAPI / OData function import / action, a Salesforce Apex REST or invocable action, a Dataverse bound/unbound action, etc. A BusinessApi's ExternalBusinessAction (later slice) invokes it through the mcpbff bridge, mapping request params in and the platform result out.

EnterpriseAction.__name.doc: Unique action identifier within this model. The name a BusinessApi's ExternalBusinessAction references. Must be a valid codeName.
EnterpriseAction.name: String
EnterpriseAction.__functionName.doc: The platform-side function identifier — the BAPI / OData function-import / bound-action / Apex-method name to invoke (e.g. 'BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2', 'A_SalesOrder/com.sap.gateway...'). The authoring agent picks this from the design-time metadata.

__EnterpriseProjection.doc: Projects a DataObject onto an EnterpriseObject (section, under objectSettings). Binds this local object to an external business object on an enterprise platform: `enterpriseModelName` + `enterpriseObjectName` name the asset in enterpriseHub, `fieldMap` maps local properties to platform fields, and `syncMode` picks the data-flow direction. The mcpbff bridge performs the platform I/O; slice 3.1 covers read/search (readThrough / pullMirror), write modes land later.

EnterpriseProjection.__enterpriseModelName.doc: The EnterpriseModel this projection targets — must match an enterpriseHub.enterpriseModels[].modelBasics.name. Identifies which integration/platform the object lives on.
EnterpriseProjection.__enterpriseObjectName.doc: The EnterpriseObject within the model — must match one of that model's enterpriseObjects[].name. Its `platformObject` is the actual entity read/written on the platform.
EnterpriseProjection.__syncMode.doc: The READ / STORAGE strategy for this projection. `readThrough`: reads proxy to the platform live, nothing is stored locally. `pullMirror`: the platform is the source of truth, records are pulled into this object and persisted (read + event upsert). This axis is INDEPENDENT of write-back — whether fields are pushed to the platform is governed per-field by `fieldMap[].direction` (`out`/`both`), not by syncMode. A projection can pull most fields (`in`) and push a few (`out`) under either syncMode (e.g. mirror SAP invoices, write `paymentDueDate` back).
EnterpriseProjection.__fieldMap.doc: Maps this DataObject's properties to the external object's fields. Each entry binds one local property to one platform field with a direction. Properties not mapped are local-only; platform fields not mapped are ignored.

__EnterpriseFieldMapItem.doc: One property↔field binding in an EnterpriseProjection.fieldMap (subsection). Maps a local DataObject property to a field on the external platform object, with a flow direction.

EnterpriseFieldMapItem.__property.doc: The local DataObject property name this entry binds. Must be a real property of the owning DataObject.
EnterpriseFieldMapItem.__externalField.doc: The platform field name this property maps to (a field of the EnterpriseObject's platformObject, e.g. 'BusinessPartnerName'). When the EnterpriseObject declares selectedFields, this must be one of them.
EnterpriseFieldMapItem.__direction.doc: Flow direction for this field, INDEPENDENT of syncMode: `in` (platform → local, read/pull), `out` (local → platform, write-back), `both`. Defaults to `in`. A projection may mix directions per field — e.g. pull invoice fields (`in`) and push `paymentDueDate` back (`out`) under the same pullMirror projection. The read side (`in`/`both`) is wired in slice 3.2; the write-back side (`out`/`both`) in slice 3.3.

__EnterpriseSyncMode.doc.#: The READ / STORAGE strategy for a projection. Independent of write-back, which is governed per-field by fieldMap[].direction.
__EnterpriseSyncMode.doc.readThrough: Reads proxy to the platform live; nothing is stored locally. Good for on-demand lookups.
__EnterpriseSyncMode.doc.pullMirror: The platform is the source of truth; records are pulled into the local DataObject (initial read + event-driven upsert). Local reads hit the mirror.

__EnterpriseFieldDirection.doc.#: Per-field flow direction within an EnterpriseProjection.fieldMap.

__ClamAvSettings.doc: Settings for the ClamAV scanner that checks files uploaded through DbBucket / NativeBucket / RemoteBucket when bucket.virusScan is true. When useClamAv is false (default) the runtime scanner uses the platform ClamAV REST service (POST `/api/v1/scan` on the default ClamAV host `clamav.mindbricks.com`, one file per request in the multipart field FILES, at most 100 MB per file). Use this block when you run your own ClamAV (a REST endpoint with the same contract, or a clamd daemon spoken to with INSTREAM), want to override the timeout, or want a default scan mode for buckets that don't set virusScanMode. The platform endpoint is plain HTTP as published: file bytes travel in clear text to that host.

ClamAvSettings.__useClamAv.doc: When true, the generator writes this connection into the env files of every service with a virus-scanning bucket. It emits CLAMAV_PROTOCOL, then CLAMAV_BASE_URL (rest) or CLAMAV_HOST and CLAMAV_PORT (clamd), and CLAMAV_TIMEOUT_MS, on all four slots. A key already set is never overwritten, and a blueprint custom variable or per-env overlay row for CLAMAV_PROTOCOL, CLAMAV_HOST or CLAMAV_BASE_URL owns the transport in that slot: no protocol, url, host or port line is added beside it (a custom CLAMAV_HOST alone means clamd on that host). defaultMode is not emitted as an env var; it is resolved per bucket at design time. When false, nothing is emitted and the scanner uses REST against the platform ClamAV host. This flag does NOT enable scanning on buckets - each bucket must opt in via bucketBasics.virusScan.
ClamAvSettings.__configuration.doc: Connection details for the ClamAV scanner (REST endpoint or clamd daemon). Leave null when useClamAv is false.

__ClamAvSettingsConfig.doc: ClamAV connection configuration: protocol picks REST (url) or clamd INSTREAM (host:port), and scanTimeoutMs bounds every scan. With protocol null, a host other than the default ClamAV host (the field's default value) selects clamd, so a blueprint written for a self-hosted clamd keeps it; anything else selects REST against url (default: the platform ClamAV host). A scan that cannot run (unreachable, timeout, non-2xx, success=false, unparsable answer, a file over the REST service's 100 MB limit) is reported as a scan error, never as a detection, and CLAMAV_ON_ERROR decides whether it blocks.

ClamAvSettingsConfig.__protocol.doc: How the scanner talks to ClamAV: 'rest' (POST <url>/api/v1/scan, multipart field FILES, one file per request) or 'clamd' (INSTREAM over TCP to host:port). Null (default) means: clamd when host names a server other than the default ClamAV host (the field's default value), otherwise rest. The platform ClamAV host serves REST only, so clamd needs your own daemon in host.
ClamAvSettingsConfig.__url.doc: (rest) Base URL of the ClamAV REST service; the scanner posts to <url>/api/v1/scan. Default: `clamav.mindbricks.com`, the platform ClamAV host. That endpoint is plain HTTP, so file bytes travel in clear text to it; use an https URL where your scanner offers one. Ignored when protocol resolves to clamd.
ClamAvSettingsConfig.__host.doc: (clamd) Hostname of a self-hosted ClamAV daemon spoken to with INSTREAM. Default: `clamav.mindbricks.com`, which serves REST only. With protocol null, a host other than that one selects clamd; ignored when protocol is rest.
ClamAvSettingsConfig.__port.doc: (clamd) TCP port of the self-hosted ClamAV daemon (INSTREAM). Default: 3310. Ignored when protocol resolves to rest.
ClamAvSettingsConfig.__scanTimeoutMs.doc: Maximum time in milliseconds a scan may take (the whole HTTP call for rest, the socket session for clamd) before it is aborted. Default: 30000 (30s). A timed-out scan is a scan that could not run, not a detection: CLAMAV_ON_ERROR decides whether the upload is refused with 503 VIRUS_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE or accepted unscanned.
ClamAvSettingsConfig.__defaultMode.doc: Default scan mode applied to buckets whose virusScan=true but didn't specify a virusScanMode. 'block' rejects infected uploads with 422; 'quarantine' persists them with scanStatus='infected' and refuses downloads. This is a FALLBACK, not an override: a bucket that sets its own virusScanMode keeps it. The winner is resolved per bucket at design time and baked into the generated service, so changing this value only affects buckets that left virusScanMode null. It is NOT the same knob as the CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE env var, which overrides the resolved value at runtime for every bucket in the process; do not wire a deployment to emit CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE from this field, because that would make the project default beat the per-bucket value and invert the documented precedence. Lane status: this design-time resolution is honoured in nodejs, dotnet, python, php and golang (golang bakes the resolved per-bucket literal into the bucket router and lets CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE override it in both directions), and rust honours it but cannot be overridden back down to 'block'.

__BucketProvidersSettings.doc: Container for cloud-storage bucket provider configurations. Each entry is a named provider (e.g. 'mainStorage', 'videoArchive') that can be referenced by RemoteBucket assets via `providerName`. The generator emits BUCKET_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct an SDK client at runtime without revisiting the project config.

BucketProvidersSettings.__bucketProviders.doc: List of configured bucket providers. Add an entry per cloud-storage account you want available to remote buckets. Multiple entries can share a provider type (e.g. two S3 accounts).

__BucketProvider.doc: A named cloud-storage bucket provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by RemoteBuckets and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainStorage` → `BUCKET_MAINSTORAGE_*`). The `provider` enum decides which credentials in `configuration` are read.

BucketProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from RemoteBucket.providerName and the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
BucketProvider.name: String
BucketProvider.__provider.doc: The storage backend type. 's3' = AWS S3; 'r2' = Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible); 's3Compatible' = any other S3-compatible object store reached via a custom endpoint (e.g. MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, company-owned storage); 'gcs' = Google Cloud Storage; 'azure' = Azure Blob Storage. Providers configure EXTERNAL storage only — for platform-provisioned self-hosted storage define `nativeBuckets` (no provider entry needed).
BucketProvider.__configuration.doc: Provider credentials and defaults. Fields are flat across all provider types — only those relevant to the selected `provider` are read at runtime and emitted to env; sensitive fields are marked secret and masked in API responses.

__GraphProvidersSettings.doc: Container for graph-database provider configurations (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §1). Each entry is a named graph connection (e.g. 'mainGraph') that can be referenced by DataObject `objectSettings.graphProjection.provider`, property `graphEdge`, `service.graphLayer` (edges/queries/resources), `GraphQueryAction.provider`, and `ComputeJob.graphIO.provider`. The generator emits GRAPH_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct a Bolt driver pool at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the bucketProvidersSettings shape — a named array.

GraphProvidersSettings.__graphProviders.doc: List of configured graph-database providers. Add one entry per graph connection you want available project-wide. Multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two Neo4j instances).

__GraphProvider.doc: A named graph-database provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used everywhere a graph provider is referenced (objectSettings.graphProjection.provider, property graphEdge, service.graphLayer (edges/queries/resources), GraphQueryAction.provider, ComputeJob.graphIO.provider) and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainGraph` → `GRAPH_MAINGRAPH_*`). The `provider` enum selects the backend driver (only `neo4j` ships first; the surface is provider-agnostic so a later Memgraph/Neptune/ArangoDB adapter is additive). The `configuration` is a flat superset whose relevant keys depend on `provider` — the same modeling BucketProviderConfig uses. Secret keys (password) are masked in API responses and emitted to GRAPH_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

GraphProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from graphProjection/graphEdge/graphLayer.queries/GraphQueryAction/graphIO and as the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
GraphProvider.name: String
GraphProvider.__provider.doc: The graph-database backend type. Only `neo4j` ships first; the data-plane runtime branches on this so additional providers (Memgraph, Neptune, ArangoDB) are additive behind the same enum.
GraphProvider.__configuration.doc: Connection details for the graph database. The required keys depend on `provider` — for neo4j: uri (bolt://… or neo4j+s:// for Aura), username, password (secret), database (optional), maxPoolSize (optional).

__GraphProviderConfig.doc: Graph-database connection credentials and defaults. Fields are a flat superset across all provider types — only those relevant to the selected `provider` are read at runtime and emitted to env. `password` is secret (masked in API responses, emitted to GRAPH_<NAME>_PASSWORD).

GraphProviderConfig.__uri.doc: The Bolt connection URI, e.g. `bolt://localhost:7687`, or `neo4j+s://<id>.databases.neo4j.io` for Neo4j Aura.
GraphProviderConfig.__password.doc: The graph-database password. Secret — masked in API responses and emitted to the GRAPH_<NAME>_PASSWORD env var at codegen time.
GraphProviderConfig.__database.doc: Optional named database within the instance (Neo4j 4+ multi-database). Defaults to the server default (`neo4j`) when absent.
GraphProviderConfig.__maxPoolSize.doc: Optional maximum size of the Bolt connection pool. Defaults to the driver default when absent.

__GraphDatabaseType.doc.#: The graph-database backend type for a GraphProvider. Only `neo4j` ships first; the enum is the extension point for additional providers.
__GraphDatabaseType.doc.neo4j: Neo4j (Bolt protocol + Cypher). The first and, for the initial milestones, only shipped provider.

__BigLoadProvidersSettings.doc: Container for big-load datastore provider configurations. Each entry is a named hot/cold/analytics store referenced by an `EventStream`'s hotStore / coldSink / analytics bindings. The generator emits BIGLOAD_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code resolves the store client at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the bucketProvidersSettings shape — a named array. No separate big-load system service (consistent with the buckets/graph have-no-service precedent).

BigLoadProvidersSettings.__bigLoadStores.doc: List of configured big-load datastore providers. Add one entry per store you want available project-wide. Multiple entries can share the same engine (e.g. two ClickHouse clusters).

__BigLoadStoreProvider.doc: A named big-load datastore provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by `EventStream` hotStore / coldSink / analytics bindings and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainHot` → `BIGLOAD_MAINHOT_*`). The `engine` enum selects the backend driver and decides which credentials in `configuration` are read.

BigLoadStoreProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from EventStream hotStore / coldSink / analytics bindings and the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
BigLoadStoreProvider.name: String
BigLoadStoreProvider.__engine.doc: The big-load datastore backend type. `cassandra` = write-optimized hot/time-series store (current-state + last-N + TTL); `clickhouse` = columnar OLAP analytics store (rollups/aggregations/KPI); `s3Parquet` = cold columnar archive / data lake (full append-only history as Parquet objects, reuses the RemoteBucket S3 credential shape).
BigLoadStoreProvider.__configuration.doc: Connection details for the store. The required keys depend on `engine` (flat superset, same modeling BucketProviderConfig/GraphProviderConfig use). Secret keys (password, secretAccessKey) are masked in API responses and emitted to BIGLOAD_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

__BigLoadStoreConfig.doc: Big-load datastore connection credentials and defaults. Fields are a flat superset across all engine types — only those relevant to the selected `engine` are read at runtime and emitted to env. `password` and `secretAccessKey` are secret (masked in API responses).

BigLoadStoreConfig.__contactPoints.doc: [cassandra] Comma-separated host:port contact points. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` are local-development-only endpoints (for example, FARM `localhost:19042`); leave this blank to use the managed endpoint, or provide a reachable remote endpoint for deployed services.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__localDataCenter.doc: [cassandra] The local data-center name the driver pins to, e.g. `datacenter1`.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__keyspace.doc: [cassandra] The keyspace the big-load tables live in, baked into generated stream descriptors. Auto-created on boot when absent. No BIGLOAD_*_KEYSPACE runtime override is emitted.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__url.doc: [clickhouse] The HTTP endpoint. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` are local-development-only endpoints (for example, FARM `http://localhost:18123`); leave this blank to use the managed endpoint, or provide a reachable remote endpoint for deployed services.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__database.doc: [clickhouse] The database the analytics tables live in. Defaults to the server default when absent.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__password.doc: [cassandra|clickhouse] The store password. Secret — masked in API responses and emitted to BIGLOAD_<NAME>_PASSWORD at codegen time.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__bucket.doc: [s3Parquet] The S3 bucket name for the cold Parquet archive.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__prefix.doc: [s3Parquet] Optional key prefix under which Parquet objects are written.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__endpoint.doc: [s3Parquet] Optional S3-compatible endpoint (Cloudflare R2 / SeaweedFS / MinIO). Omit for AWS S3.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__secretAccessKey.doc: [s3Parquet] The S3 secret access key. Secret — masked in API responses and emitted to BIGLOAD_<NAME>_SECRETACCESSKEY at codegen time.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__host.doc: Reserved legacy field; the redis big-load engine is retired and has no runtime.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__port.doc: Reserved legacy field; the redis big-load engine is retired and has no runtime.
BigLoadStoreConfig.__livyUrl.doc: [spark] The Apache Livy REST endpoint the cleaningPipeline orchestration client submits/polls batches against, e.g. `http://localhost:18998`. FARM default = http://localhost:18998. (A Spark-Connect gRPC endpoint would also live here if that transport is selected.)

__BigLoadEngine.doc.#: The big-load datastore backend type for a BigLoadStoreProvider. The data-plane runtime branches on this so additional engines are additive behind the same enum.
__BigLoadEngine.doc.cassandra: Cassandra (CQL) — write-optimized hot/time-series store (current-state + last-N + TTL).
__BigLoadEngine.doc.clickhouse: ClickHouse — columnar OLAP analytics store (rollups/aggregations/KPI queries).
__BigLoadEngine.doc.s3Parquet: S3 + Parquet — cold columnar archive / data lake (full append-only history). Reuses the RemoteBucket S3 credential/SDK path.
__BigLoadEngine.doc.spark: Apache Spark — an external batch/stream ETL compute provider (NOT a store), used by the EventStream `cleaningPipeline` to run the data-cleaning transform off the ingest path (§4.1). Connection config points at the cluster's Livy REST / Spark-Connect endpoint; the generated service only submits/monitors the job.

__EventStream.doc: Declares a high-throughput event pipeline with ingestion, storage and read surfaces. The headline asset of the big-load pattern family — a chapter on `services.eventStreams[]` declaring one high-throughput ingest→hot/cold/analytics pipeline over a logical event topic, with its read surfaces. Folds the cross-cutting big-load concerns (ingestion write contract / partitioning + back-pressure / hot store / cold sink / analytics / retention / cleaning) into SECTIONS rather than a flat bag of peers — exactly the way `ComputeJob` folds spec/input/result/resourceProfile/retryPolicy. Composes the existing kafka/compute/realtime layers (ingestion publishes to a Kafka topic; dispatch reuses ComputeJob; fan-out reuses realtimeHubs); it adds only the missing hot/cold/analytics store BINDINGS, the ingestion/retention DECLARATIONS, and the read SURFACES. In Phase 3 the nodejs big-load-layer wires `streamBasics` + `ingestion` + `hotStore` (Cassandra) + `readSurfaces`; `coldSink` / `analytics` / `retention` / `cleaningPipeline` are defined-but-deferred to P4+ (the schema holds them).

EventStream.__streamBasics.doc: The stream's scalar identity + axes (EventStreamBasics): name/codeName, the Kafka topic, the event/telemetry schema (the field shape the ingest API accepts), the partition key, delivery semantics, and the back-pressure / load-shedding knobs. Grouped into a section because a chapter is a container of sections, not loose scalar columns (the ComputeJob.jobBasics idiom).
EventStream.__ingestion.doc: The write path (IngestionSettings): batch size + flush interval for the async batched insert, optional idempotency/dedup key, optional ingest rate limit, and the load-shedding priority. The generated ingestion handler does auth → schema-validate → (dedup) → enqueue/batch → fast return; it MUST NOT run heavy per-row work (the big-load discipline). Null = sensible defaults.
EventStream.__hotStore.doc: Binds the hot store (HotStoreBinding): the bigLoadProvidersSettings provider name (engine cassandra), the table/keyspace, the partition + clustering columns, and the row TTL. The generated hot consumer/writer upserts current-state + last-N into this store. REQUIRED for a Phase-3 stream (it is the round-trip target).
EventStream.__coldSink.doc: [P4 DONE; s3Parquet=P5] Binds the durable/archival sink for the full append-only history (ColdSinkBinding): a bigLoadProvidersSettings provider name (cassandra append in P4 / s3Parquet in P5). The cold consumer appends every record off the same batched flush that feeds the hot store (no extra request-time work).
EventStream.__analytics.doc: [P4 DONE] Binds the analytics store + declares rollups/windowed aggregations (AnalyticsBinding): a bigLoadProvidersSettings clickhouse provider name + the rollup definitions. Codegen emits a raw MergeTree landing table + one materialized-view→AggregatingMergeTree per rollup, fed off the batched flush (the request path never aggregates).
EventStream.__retention.doc: [P4 DONE] Hot TTL / cold retention / rollup cadence / archival trigger (RetentionPolicy), driving a generated retention cron that prunes cold rows older than coldRetentionDays (the hot tier ages via its TTL).
EventStream.__readSurfaces.doc: The generated read APIs over the stores (EventStreamReadSurface[]). Each surface is a query archetype — latestN (last-N pings for a partition from the hot store), currentState, historySince, analyticsRollup, replaySince — exposed as an api-layer route. Phase 3 wires the hot-store surfaces (latestN / currentState).
EventStream.__cleaningPipeline.doc: [P5b, defined-but-deferred] The Spark-offloaded ETL cleaning stage (EtlPipelineBinding, §4.1) — the transform runs on an EXTERNAL Spark cluster, NEVER in the generated service (running heavy ETL on the ingest path would break the big-load strategy). Declares the spark provider name, source/sink tiers, the declarative cleanup rules (or a custom script), and the schedule. The schema holds it now; the thin Spark orchestration client lands in Phase 5b.

__EventStreamBasics.doc: The scalar identity + axes of an EventStream (the chapter's first section). Holds the name/codeName, the Kafka topic the ingest path publishes to, the event/telemetry SCHEMA (the field shape the ingest API validates + the hot row columns), the partition key, the delivery semantics, and the global back-pressure / load-shedding knobs. Grouped into a section because a chapter contains sections, not loose scalar columns.

EventStreamBasics.__name.doc: Unique stream identifier within the service. Drives the generated ingest route base (`/ingest/<name>`), the hot table default name, the read-surface route base, and the asset-name-path. Must be a valid codeName.
EventStreamBasics.name: String
EventStreamBasics.__codeName.doc: Optional machine code name override. Defaults to `name` when absent.
EventStreamBasics.__description.doc: Optional human-readable description of what telemetry this stream carries.
EventStreamBasics.__topic.doc: The Kafka topic the ingestion path publishes to (and the hot/cold/analytics consumers read). When absent, codegen derives `<projectCodename>-<service>-<name>` (the standard event-topic shape). Phase 3 may write the hot store directly from the ingest handler for the live round-trip; the topic remains the seam for the decoupled consumers (P4).
EventStreamBasics.__eventSchema.doc: The telemetry/event field shape the ingest API accepts and the hot row stores (EventStreamEventField[]). Each field is a typed column; the ingestion handler validates the body against these and the hot writer maps them onto the table. Keep this lean (the big-load discipline) — large blobs belong in a bucket, referenced by key.
EventStreamBasics.__partitionKey.doc: Name of the eventSchema field used as the storage partition key (e.g. `vehicleId`). The hot store partitions by this so all rows for one entity colocate; reads target one partition. REQUIRED — the big-load family is partition-first.
EventStreamBasics.__clusteringKey.doc: Name of the eventSchema field rows are clustered/ordered by within a partition (typically the timestamp, e.g. `ts`). Drives the hot-store clustering column + the latest-N ordering. Defaults to the first Date-typed field when absent.
EventStreamBasics.__deliverySemantics.doc: Delivery guarantee for the ingest→store path: `atMostOnce` (fastest, may drop under shed), `atLeastOnce` (default, may duplicate — dedup via ingestion.idempotencyKey), `exactlyOnce` (strongest, highest cost). Kept as String in v1.
EventStreamBasics.__maxInFlight.doc: Back-pressure knob: the maximum number of un-flushed records the ingest handler buffers before it applies back-pressure. Admission past the bound is rejected with HTTP 429 — the buffer never grows past maxInFlight. Guards the thin write path from unbounded memory growth under a burst. Defaults to 10000 when absent.
EventStreamBasics.__loadSheddingPriority.doc: Drop order under aggregate pressure (low | normal | high | critical, default normal): as the service's aggregate in-flight total (the sum of every stream's un-flushed buffer) fills the aggregate capacity (the sum of every stream's maxInFlight), lower priorities start rejecting (HTTP 429) earlier — `low` sheds at >=50% aggregate fill, `normal` at >=75%, `high` at >=90%; `critical` is never shed by aggregate pressure and is bounded only by its own maxInFlight. Kept as String in v1.

__EventStreamEventField.doc: One field of an EventStream's telemetry schema — a typed column the ingest API validates and the hot store persists. The partitionKey / clusteringKey reference these by name.

EventStreamEventField.__name.doc: The field name as it appears in the ingest body and the hot store column.
EventStreamEventField.name: String
EventStreamEventField.__type.doc: The field DataType. Maps to a CQL column type in the Cassandra hot store (String/Text→text, Integer/Short→int, Double/Float→double, Boolean→boolean, Date→timestamp, ID→uuid, Object/Any→text JSON, GeoPoint→text). Defaults to String.
EventStreamEventField.__required.doc: When true, the ingestion handler rejects a body missing this field (400). The partition key is always implicitly required.

__IngestionSettings.doc: The write-path tuning for an EventStream (see the family's design record, §5). Governs the thin, fast, async batched insert the generated ingest handler performs — batching cadence, dedup, rate limit, shedding. The handler does auth → schema-validate → (dedup) → enqueue/batch → fast return; NO heavy per-row work runs here (that belongs in the compute layer or the Spark cleaning stage).

IngestionSettings.__batchSize.doc: Number of records the ingest handler accumulates before flushing one batched insert to the hot store. Larger = fewer round-trips / higher throughput; smaller = lower latency. Defaults to a balanced value.
IngestionSettings.__flushIntervalMs.doc: Maximum milliseconds a partial batch waits before it is flushed regardless of batchSize (so low-rate streams still land promptly). Defaults to a small value.
IngestionSettings.__idempotencyKey.doc: Optional name of an eventSchema field used as the dedup/idempotency key. When set, the handler drops a record whose key was already seen in the dedup window (atLeastOnce → effectively once). Null = no dedup.
IngestionSettings.__rateLimitPerSecond.doc: Optional per-client ingest rate cap (records/sec), enforced as a fixed per-second window in-memory per instance. The client key is the authenticated session user id when present, else the remote IP. Over the cap the handler rejects with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header (seconds). Null = no ingest-side rate limit.
IngestionSettings.__loginRequired.doc: When true, `POST /ingest/<stream>` requires a valid login token and answers an anonymous caller 401 LOGIN_REQUIRED. Defaults to false, which keeps the ingest open (unauthenticated device telemetry); in a multi-tenant project an open ingest raises a design-time warning (EVENTSTREAM_INGEST_OPEN_MULTI_TENANT).
IngestionSettings.__actorField.doc: Optional name of an eventSchema field the ingest handler stamps with the caller's session `userId`. The value the client sent in that field is always discarded; an anonymous caller leaves it empty. Null = no actor stamping.
IngestionSettings.__sessionField.doc: Optional name of an eventSchema field the ingest handler stamps with the caller's session `sessionId`. The value the client sent in that field is always discarded; an anonymous caller leaves it empty. Null = no session stamping.
IngestionSettings.__tenantField.doc: [multi-tenant] Optional name of an eventSchema field that carries the tenant. The ingest handler stamps it with the caller's session tenant (`<tenantName>Id`) and discards the client value, and every read surface of the stream is tenant-scoped: when it is the partition key, a caller reads only the partition named by its own tenant; otherwise only the rows whose tenant equals its own. A caller with no session tenant is refused (403 TENANT_SCOPE_REQUIRED). Null = the stream is not tenant-scoped (warned in a multi-tenant project: EVENTSTREAM_NOT_TENANT_SCOPED).

__HotStoreBinding.doc: Binds an EventStream's hot store. References a `projectSettings.bigLoadProvidersSettings` store BY NAME (engine cassandra) and declares the table/keyspace, the partition + clustering columns, and the row TTL. The generated hot writer creates the keyspace/table on boot (partition by partitionColumn, cluster by clusteringColumn DESC, TTL) and upserts current-state + last-N rows.

HotStoreBinding.__provider.doc: Name of the bigLoadProvidersSettings store this hot store binds to (must match a projectSettings.bigLoadProvidersSettings.bigLoadStores[].name whose engine is cassandra). The big-load-layer resolves its client from BIGLOAD_<NAME>_* env at runtime.
HotStoreBinding.__keyspace.doc: [cassandra] The keyspace the hot table lives in. Defaults to the provider's configured keyspace, else the service codename. Auto-created on boot when absent.
HotStoreBinding.__table.doc: The hot table name. Defaults to the stream name snake_cased + `_hot` (e.g. `vehiclePing` → `vehicle_pings`). Auto-created on boot.
HotStoreBinding.__partitionColumn.doc: The CQL partition column. Defaults to streamBasics.partitionKey. All rows for one entity colocate under this partition.
HotStoreBinding.__clusteringColumn.doc: The CQL clustering column (rows ordered within a partition). Defaults to streamBasics.clusteringKey (the timestamp). Read surfaces order/limit by this.
HotStoreBinding.__ttlSeconds.doc: Row TTL in seconds — Cassandra ages hot rows out automatically so the hot store stays small/fast (the full history lives in the cold sink, P4). 0 or absent = no TTL.

__ColdSinkBinding.doc: [P4 DONE; s3Parquet=P5] Binds an EventStream's durable/archival sink for the full append-only history. References a `bigLoadProvidersSettings` store BY NAME (engine cassandra or s3Parquet). The cold writer appends every record off the batched flush into a NO-TTL Cassandra table (P4); for s3Parquet it batches rows into Parquet objects via the bucket adapter (Phase 5).

ColdSinkBinding.__provider.doc: Name of the bigLoadProvidersSettings store the cold history is written to (engine cassandra or s3Parquet).
ColdSinkBinding.__table.doc: [cassandra] The append table name. [s3Parquet] ignored (objects keyed under the provider prefix).
