__GraphQuery.doc: A declarative graph-traversal query archetype on a service (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). Follows the ComputeJob idiom exactly: `type` (GraphQueryType) selects the archetype, and a single `spec` wrapper (GraphQuerySpec) holds every typed sub-spec as nullable sub-objects — the one matching `type` is read by codegen and compiled to a parameterized Cypher template. Referenced by name from GraphQueryAction.query and ComputeJob.graphIO.reads.query. `permissionExplain` is the differentiator — it returns the matched PATH (which group/folder/grant), not just a boolean.

GraphQuery.__name.doc: The query name. Unique within the service; used as the lookup key from GraphQueryAction.query (`named:<name>`) and ComputeJob.graphIO.reads.query, and to name the generated query runner. Must be a valid codeName.
GraphQuery.__provider.doc: Name of the graphProvider to run against (must match a projectSettings.graphProvidersSettings.graphProviders[].name).
GraphQuery.__type.doc: Selects the curated traversal archetype (GraphQueryType) — which sub-spec under `spec` is active and which Cypher template is compiled.
GraphQuery.__spec.doc: The type-specific payload, keyed by `type`. Because the pattern system has no native discriminated-union type, `spec` is a single GraphQuerySpec wrapper holding all typed sub-specs as nullable sub-objects; the active one matches `type`. Codegen reads only the spec keyed by `type` (mirrors ComputeJobSpec).
GraphQuery.name: String

__GraphQueryType.doc.#: The curated graph-traversal archetype a GraphQuery compiles to (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). Each value selects the matching sub-spec under GraphQuerySpec and a parameterized Cypher template.
__GraphQueryType.doc.reachableNodes: Variable-length MATCH from a source over given edge types with WHERE on filterable props — 'all documents user X can read where category=finance'.
__GraphQueryType.doc.effectivePermission: Path-existence subject → resource over permission/membership/containment edges — 'can user X CAN_READ resource Y?' (boolean).
__GraphQueryType.doc.permissionExplain: Returns the matched path(s) subject → resource — 'WHY can X access Y, via which group/folder/grant?'. The enterprise differentiator.
__GraphQueryType.doc.ancestors: Upward traversal of a hierarchy edge — 'all managers above this person'.
__GraphQueryType.doc.descendants: Downward traversal of a hierarchy edge — 'headcount under this department'.
__GraphQueryType.doc.shortestPath: shortestPath((a)-[*]-(b)) — 'degrees of separation', 'is account A linked to flagged account B?'.
__GraphQueryType.doc.neighborhood: N-hop expansion around a node — 'everything within 2 hops' (fraud, knowledge graph).
__GraphQueryType.doc.recommendation: Collaborative-filtering traversal (peers sharing edges → their other targets) — 'users like me also viewed…'.
__GraphQueryType.doc.custom: Author-supplied Cypher template + named params — the bring-your-own escape hatch.
__GraphQueryType.doc.scopedRolePermission: RBAC over ReBAC — reads the subject's role from a membership edge at the most specific scope reachable from the resource and turns it into allow/deny — 'may user X deploy in project P, given a Viewer role on P and an Admin role on its workspace?'. Always exactly one row: `allowed`, `role`, `scope`, `scopeId`, `denied` (ScopedRolePermissionSpec).
__GraphQueryType.doc.scopedRoleExplain: The candidate list behind `scopedRolePermission` — one row per membership or deny candidate (`kind`, `scope`, `scopeId`, `hops`, `role`, `granted`, `selected`), at most 25 — 'which scopes gave X a role on P, and which one decided?' (ScopedRolePermissionSpec).

__GraphQuerySpec.doc: The discriminated type-specific payload of a GraphQuery, keyed by `GraphQuery.type` (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). The pattern system has no native one-of type, so this wrapper holds every sub-spec as a nullable sub-object; exactly the one matching the query's `type` is populated and read by codegen. `ancestors` and `descendants` share HierarchyTraversalSpec; `scopedRolePermission` and `scopedRoleExplain` share ScopedRolePermissionSpec. Mirrors ComputeJobSpec exactly.

GraphQuerySpec.__custom.doc: Active when `type` is `custom` — the bring-your-own-Cypher escape hatch (CustomGraphQuerySpec).
GraphQuerySpec.__scopedRolePermission.doc: Active when `type` is `scopedRolePermission` (ScopedRolePermissionSpec). Required for that type: a missing spec is SCOPED_ROLE_SPEC_MISSING.
GraphQuerySpec.__scopedRoleExplain.doc: Active when `type` is `scopedRoleExplain` (ScopedRolePermissionSpec, the same spec shape as `scopedRolePermission`). Required for that type: a missing spec is SCOPED_ROLE_SPEC_MISSING.

__ReachableNodesSpec.doc: Spec for `reachableNodes` — variable-length traversal from a source node over given edge types, filtered on the target's projected properties (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b / Cypher map).

ReachableNodesSpec.__sourceLabel.doc: The label of the source node the traversal starts from (e.g. `User`).
ReachableNodesSpec.__targetLabel.doc: The label of the reachable target nodes returned (e.g. `Document`).
ReachableNodesSpec.__edgeTypes.doc: The relationship types traversed, in path order (e.g. ['MEMBER_OF','CAN_READ','CONTAINS']).
ReachableNodesSpec.__maxDepth.doc: The maximum variable-length depth of the hierarchy/containment portion of the traversal (the `*0..N` bound).
ReachableNodesSpec.__filterProperties.doc: Names of the target's filterable properties allowed in the WHERE clause (e.g. ['category','status']).

__EffectivePermissionSpec.doc: Spec for `effectivePermission` — boolean path-existence from a subject to a resource over membership + grant + containment edges (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b / Cypher map). Returns whether the subject effectively holds the access.

EffectivePermissionSpec.__subjectLabel.doc: The label of the subject node (e.g. `User`).
EffectivePermissionSpec.__resourceLabels.doc: Candidate labels of the resource node (e.g. ['Folder','Document']).
EffectivePermissionSpec.__pathEdges.doc: The relationship types forming the access path, in order (e.g. ['MEMBER_OF','CAN_READ','CONTAINS']).
EffectivePermissionSpec.__maxDepth.doc: The maximum variable-length depth of the containment/membership portion (the `*0..N` bound).

__PermissionExplainSpec.doc: Spec for `permissionExplain` — returns the matched PATH(S) from subject to resource, not just a boolean (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b / Cypher map). The enterprise-grade 'why can they access this — which group/role/folder/grant granted it?' query that pure CRUD cannot offer.

PermissionExplainSpec.__subjectLabel.doc: The label of the subject node whose access is being explained (e.g. `User`).
PermissionExplainSpec.__resourceLabels.doc: Candidate labels of the resource node (e.g. ['Folder','Document']).
PermissionExplainSpec.__pathEdges.doc: The relationship types forming the access path, in order (e.g. ['MEMBER_OF','CAN_READ','CONTAINS']).
PermissionExplainSpec.__maxDepth.doc: The maximum variable-length depth of the containment/membership portion (the `*0..N` bound).

__HierarchyTraversalSpec.doc: Spec shared by `ancestors` and `descendants` — upward or downward traversal of a single hierarchy edge (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). `ancestors` walks the edge toward the root ('all managers above'); `descendants` walks toward the leaves ('headcount under').

HierarchyTraversalSpec.__nodeLabel.doc: The label of the nodes in the hierarchy (e.g. `Employee` or `Folder`).
HierarchyTraversalSpec.__edgeType.doc: The hierarchy relationship type traversed (e.g. `REPORTS_TO` or `CONTAINS`).
HierarchyTraversalSpec.__maxDepth.doc: The maximum number of hops to traverse (the `*1..N` bound). Unset = unbounded.

__ShortestPathSpec.doc: Spec for `shortestPath` — `shortestPath((a)-[*]-(b))` between two nodes (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). 'Degrees of separation', 'is account A linked to flagged account B?'.

ShortestPathSpec.__fromLabel.doc: The label of the start node `a`.
ShortestPathSpec.__toLabel.doc: The label of the end node `b`.
ShortestPathSpec.__edgeTypes.doc: Optional restriction of the relationship types the path may traverse (empty = any).
ShortestPathSpec.__maxDepth.doc: Optional maximum path length (the `*..N` bound). Unset = unbounded.

__NeighborhoodSpec.doc: Spec for `neighborhood` — N-hop expansion around a node (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). 'Everything within 2 hops' (fraud, knowledge graph).

NeighborhoodSpec.__centerLabel.doc: The label of the center node the neighborhood expands around.
NeighborhoodSpec.__edgeTypes.doc: Optional restriction of the relationship types expanded over (empty = any).
NeighborhoodSpec.__hops.doc: The number of hops to expand (the `*1..N` bound).

__RecommendationSpec.doc: Spec for `recommendation` — a collaborative-filtering traversal: peers who share an edge with the subject, then THEIR other targets (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b / §12). 'Users like me also viewed…'. For learned/scored recommendation use a ComputeJob with graphIO instead.

RecommendationSpec.__subjectLabel.doc: The label of the subject the recommendation is for (e.g. `User`).
RecommendationSpec.__viaEdge.doc: The relationship type shared between the subject and its peers (e.g. `VIEWED`).
RecommendationSpec.__targetLabel.doc: The label of the recommended target nodes (e.g. `Document`).
RecommendationSpec.__limit.doc: Maximum number of recommended targets to return.

__CustomGraphQuerySpec.doc: Spec for `custom` — the bring-your-own-Cypher escape hatch (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8b). The author supplies a parameterized Cypher template and declares its named parameters; codegen wires it like any other query.

CustomGraphQuerySpec.__cypher.doc: The parameterized Cypher template, using `$param` placeholders for its named parameters.
CustomGraphQuerySpec.__params.doc: The names of the parameters the Cypher template expects (bound from the GraphQueryAction.params object at call time). Must match the Cypher's `$name` tokens exactly (case-sensitive): a `$token` no entry declares is a CUSTOM_QUERY_PARAM_MISMATCH error and fails codegen, and a declared name the Cypher never references is a CUSTOM_QUERY_PARAM_UNUSED warning. A `$` inside a string literal, a backtick-quoted name or a comment is not a token.

__ScopedRolePermissionSpec.doc: Spec shared by `scopedRolePermission` and `scopedRoleExplain` — RBAC over ReBAC. The subject's role is read from a property of a membership edge (`(User)-[:MEMBER_OF {role}]->(Project)`) at each declared scope reachable from the resource; ONE role is picked (by default the most specific scope wins, so a project `Viewer` is NOT rescued by a workspace `Admin`) and `grant` turns it into a decision, while an explicit `deny` always wins. Answer contract: `scopedRolePermission` returns exactly ONE row, also for an unknown subject or resource — `allowed` (boolean), `role` (the picked role; null = not a member at any scope), `scope` (the scope `name` it came from), `scopeId` (that scope node's id), `denied` (an explicit deny was hit) and one `<name>Id` column per `returnId` scope. `role` null is not_a_member; `role` set with `allowed` and `denied` false is a plain permission_denied. `scopedRoleExplain` returns one row per candidate (`kind` membership/deny, `scope`, `scopeId`, `hops`, `role`, `granted`, `selected`), at most 25; zero rows = no membership and no deny anywhere. Params: `subjectId`, `resourceId`, `tenantId`, plus `permission` in `graph` grant mode; the resource, scope, role and permission nodes are tenant-filtered like every other graph query. Use it instead of `effectivePermission` when the decision depends on a role stored on the membership, on which scope that role came from, or on a role -> permission join (`effectivePermission` only answers whether an edge path exists, and a stronger role further out would wrongly win). Use it instead of a hand-written `custom` query for this shape: it is validated at design time and emits the tested Cypher.

ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__subjectLabel.doc: Label of the subject node matched by `$subjectId` (e.g. `User`). Null matches the id on any label. The subject node is not tenant-filtered: users cross tenants and the membership decides.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__subjectPathEdges.doc: Optional group hop before the membership edge: edge types walked OUTBOUND from the subject (e.g. ['IN_TEAM']), so a membership held by a team the subject belongs to counts too. Empty (default) = only the subject's own memberships.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__subjectPathMaxDepth.doc: Maximum hops of the `subjectPathEdges` walk (default 0 = direct membership only; at most 50).
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__resourceLabels.doc: Candidate labels of the node matched by `$resourceId` (e.g. ['Project','Workspace']). Several are allowed; empty = any label.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__scopes.doc: The scope levels a role can be held at, ORDERED MOST SPECIFIC FIRST (e.g. `project`, then `workspace`). At least one. With `precedence: nearestScope` the first scope that has a membership decides.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__membershipEdge.doc: Relationship type from the subject to a scope node that carries the role (e.g. `MEMBER_OF`). Its projection must write `roleProperty` (and every condition property and `activeProperty`) as edgeProperties, otherwise every check answers `role: null`.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__roleProperty.doc: The membership edge property holding the role value (default `role`).
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__membershipConditions.doc: Extra equality filters on the membership edge; all must hold (e.g. `[{ "property": "status", "equals": "active" }]`).
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__activeProperty.doc: Soft-delete flag checked as `coalesce(x.<property>, true)` on the membership edge, the role node, the grant edge and the permission node (e.g. `isActive`): a record whose flag is false no longer grants. Null (default) = no soft-delete filter.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__precedence.doc: How one role is picked from the candidates: `nearestScope` (default: the earliest declared scope with a membership wins, then the fewest hops) or `highestRank` (the strongest role by `roleRanking`, at any scope).
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__roleRanking.doc: `highestRank` only: role values, strongest first (e.g. ['owner','admin','member']). A role not in the list ranks below every listed one. Required with `highestRank`, ignored (with a warning) with `nearestScope`.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__roleMatch.doc: How a role value is compared with the role node key, `roleRanking` and `allowedRoles`: `exact` (default) or `caseInsensitive` (e.g. an edge carrying `Admin` against a role node keyed `admin`).
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__grant.doc: How the picked role becomes allow/deny (ScopedRoleGrant): `graph` joins the role to a permission node, `roleList` checks a fixed list, `membership` allows any member.
ScopedRolePermissionSpec.__deny.doc: Optional explicit denies (ScopedRoleDeny). A deny always wins over a grant.

__ScopedRoleScope.doc: One scope level of a ScopedRolePermissionSpec — where a role can be held (e.g. the project itself, or the workspace the project belongs to). The scope node is reached by walking `pathEdges` from the resource in `direction` (OUTBOUND by default, INBOUND for a parent -> child containment edge), and the subject's membership edge into that node supplies a candidate role. Inside one scope the nearest node wins (fewest hops).

ScopedRoleScope.__name.doc: Scope name returned in the answer's `scope` column (e.g. `project`, `workspace`). A bare identifier, unique within `scopes`.
ScopedRoleScope.__pathEdges.doc: Edge types walked from the resource to reach the scope node, in `direction` (e.g. ['BELONGS_TO']). Empty with `maxDepth: 0` = the resource itself is the scope node.
ScopedRoleScope.__minDepth.doc: Minimum hops of that walk (default 0). With 0 the resource itself also matches when it carries `label`, so one query answers both for a project and for a workspace passed directly as `$resourceId`.
ScopedRoleScope.__maxDepth.doc: Maximum hops of that walk (default 0 = the resource itself; at most 50).
ScopedRoleScope.__direction.doc: Which way the `pathEdges` walk goes (ScopedRoleScopeDirection): `outbound` (default) follows the edges from the resource, `(r)-[:E*]->(scope)`, for containment written child -> parent (e.g. `BELONGS_TO`, `CONTAINED_IN`); `inbound` walks against them, `(r)<-[:E*]-(scope)`, for containment written parent -> child (the FK `CONTAINS` convention: a `folder.parentId` / `doc.folderId` graphEdge with direction inbound points parent -> child, so a folder scope walks CONTAINS with direction inbound). The validator warns (SCOPED_ROLE_SCOPE_DIRECTION_UNREACHABLE) when no projected writer of the path edges can be walked this way from the resource labels to the scope label.
ScopedRoleScope.__tenantRoot.doc: Multi-tenant projects: this scope's nodes ARE the tenants (e.g. the workspace of a workspace-per-tenant model). The node must then be `$tenantId` itself instead of carrying the tenant property, so a role there resolves only inside the caller's own tenant and a caller that binds no tenant resolves nothing. Default false.
ScopedRoleScope.__returnId.doc: Also return a `<name>Id` column (e.g. `workspaceId`): the id of the nearest node of this scope reachable from the resource, member or not. Default false.
ScopedRoleScope.name: String
ScopedRoleScope.label: String

__ScopedRoleScopeDirection.doc.#: Which way a ScopedRoleScope walks its `pathEdges` from the resource to the scope node.
__ScopedRoleScopeDirection.doc.outbound: Follow the edges from the resource, `(r)-[:E*]->(scope)`: containment written child -> parent (e.g. `BELONGS_TO`, `CONTAINED_IN`).
__ScopedRoleScopeDirection.doc.inbound: Walk against the edges, `(r)<-[:E*]-(scope)`: containment written parent -> child (e.g. the FK `CONTAINS` convention).

__ScopedRoleCondition.doc: An equality filter on the membership edge of a ScopedRolePermissionSpec (e.g. `status` equals `active`).

ScopedRoleCondition.__property.doc: The membership edge property compared (e.g. `status`). The membership edge projection must write it as an edge property.
ScopedRoleCondition.__equals.doc: The literal the property must equal (e.g. `active`, `true`, `1`): a boolean, a number, or a string of letters, digits, spaces and `_ . : @ -`. It is written into the query text, so any other character is refused.

__ScopedRoleGrant.doc: How the role picked by a ScopedRolePermissionSpec becomes a decision. `graph` allows when the role node (`roleLabel`, keyed by `roleKeyProperty` = the role value) has a `grantEdge` to the permission node (`permissionLabel`, keyed by `permissionKeyProperty` = `$permission`), e.g. `(Role {key})-[:CAN]->(Action {key: $permission})`; `roleList` allows when the role is in `allowedRoles` (no `$permission` param); `membership` allows whenever a role was picked.

ScopedRoleGrant.__roleLabel.doc: `graph` mode (required there): label of the role node (e.g. `Role`).
ScopedRoleGrant.__roleKeyProperty.doc: `graph` mode: the role node property matched against the picked role value (default `key`).
ScopedRoleGrant.__grantEdge.doc: `graph` mode (required there): relationship type from the role node to the permission node (e.g. `CAN`).
ScopedRoleGrant.__permissionLabel.doc: `graph` mode (required there): label of the permission node (e.g. `Action`).
ScopedRoleGrant.__permissionKeyProperty.doc: `graph` mode: the permission node property matched against `$permission` (default `key`).
ScopedRoleGrant.__allowedRoles.doc: `roleList` mode (required and non-empty there): the role values that allow (e.g. ['admin','owner']).

__ScopedRoleDeny.doc: Explicit denies of a ScopedRolePermissionSpec. A hit answers `allowed: false, denied: true`, whatever role was picked (deny overrides allow).

ScopedRoleDeny.__scopeEdge.doc: Relationship type from the subject to ANY declared scope node reachable from the resource that denies (e.g. `BLOCKED_FROM`), whatever the precedence picked.
ScopedRoleDeny.__grantEdge.doc: `graph` grant mode only: relationship type from the picked role node to the permission node that denies even when the role also has the grant edge (e.g. `CANNOT`).

__ScopedRolePrecedence.doc.#: How a ScopedRolePermissionSpec picks one role from the candidate memberships.
__ScopedRolePrecedence.doc.nearestScope: The earliest declared scope that has a membership decides, then the fewest hops; a weaker role there is not rescued by a stronger role further out.
__ScopedRolePrecedence.doc.highestRank: The strongest role by `roleRanking` wins at any scope; ties go to the earlier scope, then the fewest hops. An unranked role sorts last.

__ScopedRoleMatch.doc.#: How a ScopedRolePermissionSpec compares a role value with the role node key, `roleRanking` and `allowedRoles`.
__ScopedRoleMatch.doc.caseInsensitive: Both sides lower-cased before comparing (a legacy TitleCase `Admin` on the edge matches a role node keyed `admin`).

__ScopedRoleGrantMode.doc.#: How the role picked by a ScopedRolePermissionSpec becomes a decision (ScopedRoleGrant.mode).
__ScopedRoleGrantMode.doc.graph: The picked role's node has the grant edge to the permission node keyed `$permission` (a role -> permission join in the graph).
__ScopedRoleGrantMode.doc.roleList: The picked role is one of `allowedRoles` (no `$permission` param).
__ScopedRoleGrantMode.doc.membership: Any picked role allows: a membership check that still reports the role and scope.

__HierarchicalResourceGraph.doc: The flagship composite graph pattern (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §9). A single high-level declaration expands into node projections on the underlying DataObjects, the hierarchy/permission edges (CONTAINS / MEMBER_OF / CAN_*), a PermissionInheritancePolicy that shapes the generated Cypher, and a ready set of graphQueries (effectivePermission / permissionExplain / reachableNodes). One declaration yields the whole document-management authorization use case — folder hierarchy, inherited permissions, group access, document-level overrides, and explainable access checks.

HierarchicalResourceGraph.__name.doc: The composite's name. Unique within the service; used to name the expanded queries and assets. Must be a valid codeName.
HierarchicalResourceGraph.__provider.doc: Name of the graphProvider the composite projects into (must match a projectSettings.graphProvidersSettings.graphProviders[].name).
HierarchicalResourceGraph.__nodes.doc: The DataObjects projected as node labels (DataObjectName[]), e.g. ['user','group','folder','document'].
HierarchicalResourceGraph.__edges.doc: The hierarchy/permission edges between the node labels (HierarchicalEdge[]) — CONTAINS / MEMBER_OF / CAN_READ / CAN_EDIT etc.
HierarchicalResourceGraph.__inheritance.doc: The PermissionInheritancePolicy that shapes the generated Cypher (flow-down via *0..N, deny-override via negative-path filters, document-level overrides).
HierarchicalResourceGraph.name: String

__HierarchicalEdge.doc: One edge of a HierarchicalResourceGraph (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §9). `from` / `to` may each be a single node label or a list of candidate labels (e.g. a CAN_READ edge from ['user','group'] to ['folder','document']).

HierarchicalEdge.__from.doc: Source node label(s) of the edge — a single label or candidate labels (e.g. `folder`, or ['user','group']).
HierarchicalEdge.__to.doc: Target node label(s) of the edge — a single label or candidate labels (e.g. `document`, or ['folder','document']).

__PermissionInheritancePolicy.doc: The inheritance semantics that shape a HierarchicalResourceGraph's generated Cypher (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §9). Controls flow-down (a grant on a folder reaches its subtree via *0..N), deny-override (an explicit deny beats an inherited allow via negative-path filters), and document-level overrides.

PermissionInheritancePolicy.__permissionsFlowDown.doc: When true, a permission granted on a folder grants its entire subtree (flow-down via variable-length CONTAINS).
PermissionInheritancePolicy.__denyOverridesAllow.doc: When true, an explicit deny beats an inherited allow (negative-path filter in the generated Cypher).
PermissionInheritancePolicy.__documentOverrideAllowed.doc: When true, a document-level grant overrides the inherited folder-level permission.

__BucketProviderConfig.doc:
Provider credentials and defaults. Fields are flat across all provider types — only those relevant to the selected `provider` are read at runtime and emitted to env. Sensitive fields are marked secret and masked in API responses.

Azure auth modes (exactly one must be configured when provider='azure'):
- `connectionString` — full Azure Blob connection string (includes account name + key + endpoint).
- `useManagedIdentity=true` — authenticate via `DefaultAzureCredential` (managed identity / workload identity); no secret in config.
- `accountName` + `accountKey` — shared-key pair, supplied separately.

BucketProviderConfig.__defaultBucketName.doc: Default physical bucket name at the provider. Used by any RemoteBucket that doesn't override `remoteBucketName`. The bucket must already exist — it is not auto-created. Names are checked against the bound provider: s3 uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, begins and ends alphanumeric, rejects adjacent dots, IP-shaped names and reserved prefixes/suffixes (including xn-- and -s3alias); r2 uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with alphanumeric ends; gcs allows lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, alphanumeric ends, 3-63 characters without dots or up to 222 with 1-63-character components, and rejects IP-shaped and Google-reserved names; azure uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with alphanumeric ends and no consecutive hyphens (the reserved containers $root, $web and $logs are allowed). Violations are BUCKET_NAME_INVALID errors, except s3Compatible receives warnings. The exact REPLACE_ME placeholder is a BUCKET_NAME_PLACEHOLDER warning. A RemoteBucket with no effective override or provider default is a REMOTE_BUCKET_NAME_EMPTY error. See the bucket-providers integration guide for details.
BucketProviderConfig.__accessKeyId.doc: (s3/r2/s3Compatible) Access Key ID for the storage account.
BucketProviderConfig.__secretAccessKey.doc: (s3/r2/s3Compatible) Secret Access Key for the storage account.
BucketProviderConfig.__region.doc: (s3/r2/s3Compatible) AWS region, e.g. 'us-east-1'. For R2 use 'auto'; for s3Compatible stores use any region string the endpoint accepts (often 'us-east-1').
BucketProviderConfig.__endpoint.doc: (r2/s3Compatible, optional for s3) Custom endpoint URL. Required for R2 (https://<accountId>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com) and for s3Compatible stores (the store's S3 API URL); leave empty for AWS S3.
BucketProviderConfig.__forcePathStyle.doc: (r2/s3Compatible) Set true to force path-style URLs. Usually true for s3Compatible stores (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, ...); usually false for AWS and R2.
BucketProviderConfig.__publicPresignBase.doc: (s3/r2/s3Compatible) PUBLIC base URL (scheme + host[:port]) that presigned upload/download URLs are signed against, for stores whose `endpoint` is a private/in-cluster address behind an ingress or reverse proxy. Presigned URLs are SIGNED against this base (SigV4 binds the Host header, so a post-hoc host rewrite would fail signature validation); server-side operations keep dialing `endpoint`. Leave empty when the endpoint is already reachable by clients (AWS S3, R2, a public MinIO).
BucketProviderConfig.__apiEndpoint.doc: (gcs, optional) Absolute HTTP(S) API endpoint URL. Leave empty for Google Cloud Storage. HTTP endpoints use emulator credentials without Google authentication; HTTPS custom endpoints retain service-account authentication (env: BUCKET_<NAME>_GCS_API_ENDPOINT).
BucketProviderConfig.__projectId.doc: (gcs) Google Cloud project ID that owns the bucket.
BucketProviderConfig.__clientEmail.doc: (gcs) Service-account email used to sign API requests.
BucketProviderConfig.__privateKey.doc: (gcs) Service-account private key (PEM). Multi-line value — paste the full BEGIN/END block as a single string.
BucketProviderConfig.__connectionString.doc: (azure) Full Azure Blob connection string (DefaultEndpointsProtocol=...;AccountName=...;AccountKey=...). One of `connectionString`, `useManagedIdentity=true`, or `accountName`+`accountKey` is required for the azure provider.
BucketProviderConfig.__useManagedIdentity.doc: (azure) When true, the adapter authenticates using `DefaultAzureCredential` (managed identity / workload identity / az login chain) instead of a shared key. The hosting environment must supply the credential — no secret is needed in the config. Mutually exclusive with `connectionString` and `accountName`+`accountKey`.
BucketProviderConfig.__accountName.doc: (azure) Storage account name. Paired with `accountKey` to build a `StorageSharedKeyCredential`. Use this when you have the account name + key separately rather than a connection string. Both `accountName` and `accountKey` must be set together.
BucketProviderConfig.__accountKey.doc: (azure) Storage account shared key. Paired with `accountName`. Sensitive value — masked in API responses and emitted to env at codegen time.

__ComputeSettings.doc: Project-level compute-layer configuration (docs/ADR-calculation-layer.md §10). Sizes the single bounded compute pool and queue that the compute-worker controller uses to drain submitted ComputeJobs on any rust/python host service. These are global guard-rails: the framework never spawns unbounded threads/processes, so `maxConcurrentJobs` and `queueDepth` bound inter-job concurrency and backpressure, while `defaultResourceProfile` supplies the per-job ComputeResourceProfile for jobs that don't declare their own. `pythonFreeThreaded` opts a Python host into the free-threaded 3.13+/3.14 interpreter (off by default; §8). `gpuEnabled` is a project-wide flag that allows jobs with `resourceProfile.gpuRequired` to be scheduled.

ComputeSettings.__maxConcurrentJobs.doc: Upper bound on the number of ComputeJobs a host service runs concurrently across its worker pool. Bounds inter-job concurrency (§8); the framework never exceeds it.
ComputeSettings.__queueDepth.doc: Maximum number of submitted-but-not-yet-running jobs the ComputeQueue holds before applying backpressure (rejecting new submits). Sizes the DB-polled / Kafka-backed queue depth (§2, §10).
ComputeSettings.__defaultResourceProfile.doc: The default ComputeResourceProfile applied to a ComputeJob that does not declare its own `resourceProfile`. Drives the worker pool sizing and the deploy manifest's resource requests (§9).
ComputeSettings.__pythonFreeThreaded.doc: When true, Python compute hosts are generated against the free-threaded (no-GIL) 3.13+/3.14 interpreter as an opt-in (§8). Off by default — the GIL trade-off is documented in generated code regardless.
ComputeSettings.__gpuEnabled.doc: Project-wide switch that permits scheduling of ComputeJobs whose `resourceProfile.gpuRequired` is true. In v1 this is a scheduling flag only (GPU pooling/lifecycle is deferred).

__CorsSettings.doc: Defines CORS settings for service accesses. When enabled Cross Origins will be accepted according to the settings.

CorsSettings.__useCorsControl.doc: Specifies whether CORS control is enabled. Leave false if you allow service accesses from any domain.
CorsSettings.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for the CORS settings. Leave it null if useCorsControl is false.

__CorsSettingsConfig.doc: Defines the configuration for CORS settings. This object is used when useCorsControl is set to true. Note that if your service is in a different subdomain, the generated service automatically uses wildcard url control and allows other subdomains in the same main domain. Localhost Vite ports are also allowed automatically.

CorsSettingsConfig.__allowedOrigins.doc: A list of full url addresses that are allowed as cross origin.(with https or http)
CorsSettingsConfig.__allowAllSubdomains.doc: When set to true, the services will accept all cross origins that have different subdomain but same domain. It is not recommended if your services share a domain with foreign subdomains.

__PipelineTemplate.doc: The asset to store a template for generating custom pipeline files. Used in project level and applied to all microservices.

PipelineTemplate.__filename.doc: The name of the pipeline file that will be generated like .gitlab-ci.yml
PipelineTemplate.__template.doc: The ejs source code of the template that renders the pipeline file.

__ServicePlanEntry.doc: One service the project INTENDS to create, as named by the microservice-definition plan. An entry is a statement of intent, never evidence of existence: nothing in the framework may resolve, load, join to or emit against it, and codegen never reads it. Its only effect is on DESIGN-TIME validation — a cross-service reference whose target is named here is reported as a WARNING (planned, not created yet) instead of an ERROR, which is what makes a forward reference distinguishable from a typo. A reference to a service the plan does NOT name stays a hard error.

ServicePlanEntry.__serviceName.doc: Name of the planned service, exactly as it will be created. Matched case-insensitively against the project's real services[] entries; once that service exists the entry is inert.
ServicePlanEntry.__dataObjects.doc: Data objects the plan expects this service to hold. DOCUMENTATION ONLY — nothing validates, resolves or tiers on this list, so it may go stale without consequence. It exists so a human (and the diagram legend) can read what the planned service is for; keeping it in step with the real blueprint is explicitly NOT required.

__NotificationService.doc: Defines the global notification configuration for the project. Includes provider defaults (under NotificationServiceSettings.serviceOptions) and event-driven notification behaviors. Geofences are NOT declared here — they are runtime data managed via the GeoFence DataObject emitted by the notification factory; EventNotifications match fences at runtime via fenceTags / fenceFilter (see GeofenceTrigger).

NotificationService.__serviceSettings.doc: NotificationServiceSettings defines the basic notification configuration for the project — module-level UX prompt + default-provider-name selection.
NotificationService.__eventNotifications.doc: An array of event-based notification definitions. These are triggered either by a Kafka topic (triggerSource='kafka', default) or by a geofence crossing (triggerSource='geofence'). Each entry defines how and where a notification should be delivered.
NotificationService.__whatsappIngress.doc: OPTIONAL — extra listeners on the WhatsApp (Meta Cloud) inbound dispatcher. The dispatcher itself needs no configuration: every WhatsApp notification provider (`kind: whatsapp`, `provider: whatsapp`) gets ONE door `/v1/whatsapp-webhooks/meta/<providerName>` on the notification service, verified with that provider's `whatsappAppSecret`, and its events are routed per provider — inbound messages to the agents and mcpbff exposures whose chat surface names the provider (`chatSurfaces[].provider`), delivery statuses to the notification delivery log, other field changes to `<codename>-whatsapp-inbound-other`, and events nothing is bound to to `<codename>-whatsapp-inbound-unrouted`. Declare a route here only for an EXTRA listener that needs its own topic or exclusivity; a plain extra consumer subscribes to `<codename>-whatsapp-inbound-message` with an AgentKafkaController or a kafka-controller BusinessApi and filters on `data.providerName`.

__WhatsAppIngressSettings.doc: Explicit routes of the WhatsApp inbound dispatcher (`notificationService.whatsappIngress`). Each route publishes the matching events of ONE WhatsApp provider's door to its own topic `<codename>-whatsapp-route-<name>`, in addition to (or, with `exclusive: true`, instead of) the implicit routing to the bound agents / bots and the notification delivery log.

WhatsAppIngressSettings.__routes.doc: The explicit routes. Optional; the implicit per-provider routing covers the common case.

__WhatsAppIngressRoute.doc: One explicit listener on a WhatsApp provider's door. The matching events are published to `<codename>-whatsapp-route-<name>` (one envelope per message / status / other change, the same event shape as the implicit topics). `exclusive: true` takes the matching events AWAY from the implicit consumers — for example a human-desk number whose messages must never reach the agent.

WhatsAppIngressRoute.__name.doc: Unique route name; the topic is `<codename>-whatsapp-route-<name>`. Must be a valid codeName.
WhatsAppIngressRoute.name: String
WhatsAppIngressRoute.__provider.doc: The WhatsApp notification provider (`kind: whatsapp`, `provider: whatsapp`) whose door this route listens on. Must name an existing provider (WHATSAPP_ROUTE_UNKNOWN_PROVIDER otherwise).
WhatsAppIngressRoute.__events.doc: Which events of the provider the route takes: `messages`, `statuses`, `other`, or `all`. Absent or empty = all.
WhatsAppIngressRoute.__messageTypes.doc: For `messages`: only these Meta message types (`text`, `interactive`, `image`, `audio`, `document`, `location`, `reaction`, ...). Absent = every type.
WhatsAppIngressRoute.__exclusive.doc: When true, the events this route matches are published ONLY to the route topic and no longer reach the implicit consumers (the bound agents / bots for messages, the notification delivery log for statuses). Default false: the route is an additional copy.

__WhatsAppIngressEventKind.doc.#: An event family of a WhatsApp provider's door, as an explicit route selects it.
__WhatsAppIngressEventKind.doc.messages: Inbound customer messages (`value.messages[]`), one event per message.
__WhatsAppIngressEventKind.doc.statuses: Delivery statuses of the platform's own sends (`value.statuses[]`), one event per status.
__WhatsAppIngressEventKind.doc.other: Every other webhook field change (template status, phone number quality, account updates, ...).

__NotificationServiceSettings.doc: Defines the basic notification configuration for the project. Provider credentials live under projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[]; this chapter only holds module-level UX prompt and default-provider-name selection.

NotificationServiceSettings.__documentation.doc: Module-level UX prompt for MindUI's in-app notification UI generation (notification center, bell icon, toast layer, realtime delivery, read/unread states, categorisation, email template style).
NotificationServiceSettings.__serviceOptions.doc: Defines the default notification provider per channel and storage policy. References entries in projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[] by name.

__NotificationServiceOptions.doc: Default notification provider per channel plus storage policy. Provider names must resolve to entries in projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[] of compatible `kind`. Each EventNotification may override the default via its own providerName.

NotificationServiceOptions.__storedNotice.doc: Determines whether notifications will be persisted and listed within the app. If true, notifications are stored in the database and can be retrieved later. If false, they are sent transiently and not stored. Disabling storage can improve performance in simple use cases where tracking historical notifications is unnecessary.
NotificationServiceOptions.__defaultEmailProviderName.doc: Codename of the default email-channel provider for this project. Must match a notificationProviders[] entry with kind='email' (or kind='multi').
NotificationServiceOptions.__defaultSmsProviderName.doc: Codename of the default SMS-channel provider. Must match a notificationProviders[] entry with kind='sms' (or kind='multi').
NotificationServiceOptions.__defaultPushProviderName.doc: Codename of the default push-channel provider. Must match a notificationProviders[] entry with kind='push' (or kind='multi').
NotificationServiceOptions.__defaultTelegramProviderName.doc: Codename of the default Telegram-channel provider. Must match a notificationProviders[] entry with kind='telegram'.
NotificationServiceOptions.__defaultWhatsappProviderName.doc: Codename of the default WhatsApp-channel provider. Must match a notificationProviders[] entry with kind='whatsapp'.
NotificationServiceOptions.__notificationLogRetentionDays.doc: Retention window in days for the ES-backed notificationLog index (slice 9.5). Every send attempt across every channel is logged here for the admin audit view; older rows are deleted by an ILM policy / daily cleanup job. Default 7. Set to 0 to disable retention enforcement (logs live forever — only safe with external ES housekeeping).
NotificationServiceOptions.__logRetentionDays.doc: Database retention window in days for notificationLog delivery-attempt rows. A positive integer enables an hourly, single-replica sweep that hard-deletes older log rows in bounded batches. Unset or null keeps database logs indefinitely and emits no sweep. New projects start with 90 days; loading an existing project never opts it in. Rendered subject and body are not truncated, and in-app notification rows are never deleted by this setting. The separate notificationLogRetentionDays setting still controls Elasticsearch retention.

__NotificationProviderKind.doc.#: The notification channel a NotificationProvider entry serves.
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.email: Email channel — smtp / sendgrid / resend / amazonses / mailgun / postmark. Email over AWS is amazonses (Amazon SES); amazonsns is NOT an email brand (its SNS email adapter was removed).
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.sms: SMS channel — twilio / vonage / netgsm / amazonsns. 'amazonsns' here uses SNS direct PhoneNumber publish (not topic).
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.push: Mobile push channel — firebase / onesignal / amazonsns. firebase and onesignal consume the raw FCM/APNs tokens of the device-token pipeline directly; amazonsns registers a raw token against its platformApplicationArn (CreatePlatformEndpoint) or publishes straight to an SNS platform-endpoint ARN.
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.telegram: Telegram chat channel via Telegram Bot API.
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.whatsapp: WhatsApp Business channel — whatsapp (Meta Cloud API direct) or twilio (Twilio WhatsApp channel).
__NotificationProviderKind.doc.multi: Provider spans multiple channels (e.g. Twilio used for SMS + WhatsApp). Only a brand whose _types lists two or more channels may be declared kind='multi'.

__NotificationProviderType.doc.#: Backend provider implementations supported by OpenAPPL. Each is a native integration with framework-owned SDK glue. The (kind, provider) pair selects the codegen branch.
__NotificationProviderType.doc.resend: Resend transactional email HTTPS API (resend.com). kind=email. Uses the `resend` npm package.
__NotificationProviderType.doc.amazonsns: Amazon Simple Notification Service. kind=sms or kind=push (one entry per channel; kind=multi is refused). The 'sms' kind publishes direct to a PhoneNumber (payload.to). The 'push' kind publishes SNS mobile push to a platform-endpoint ARN; a raw FCM/APNs device token is registered first against the entry's platformApplicationArn (CreatePlatformEndpoint). NOT email: the SNS email adapter was removed; use amazonses for email over AWS.
__NotificationProviderType.doc.amazonses: Amazon SES v2 API — person-addressable transactional email, and the only AWS email brand. kind=email.
__NotificationProviderType.doc.twilio: Twilio. kind=sms (plain SMS) or kind=whatsapp (Twilio WhatsApp channel).

__AiProviderType.doc.#: Backend AI provider implementations supported by OpenAPPL. Each is a native integration with framework-owned adapter code shipped under `_common/nodejs/src/common/ai-providers/`. Deliberately not the same path as `IntegrationAction` integrations — AI providers are first-class infrastructure, not designer-defined HTTP endpoints.
__AiProviderType.doc.openai: OpenAI — chat (GPT-4 / 4o / etc.), image (DALL·E), audio (Whisper STT, TTS). Uses the openai npm package.
__AiProviderType.doc.anthropic: Anthropic Claude — chat with tool use. Uses the @anthropic-ai/sdk package.
__AiProviderType.doc.xai: xAI Grok — chat. Uses OpenAI-compatible REST.
__AiProviderType.doc.deepseek: DeepSeek — chat + code models. Uses OpenAI-compatible REST.
__AiProviderType.doc.moonshot: Moonshot (Kimi) — long-context chat. Uses OpenAI-compatible REST.
__AiProviderType.doc.google: Google Vertex AI / Gemini — chat + multimodal.
__AiProviderType.doc.azure-openai: Azure OpenAI Service — same models as openai, deployment-name routing.
__AiProviderType.doc.bedrock: AWS Bedrock — multi-vendor model gateway. Uses @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime.
__AiProviderType.doc.ollama: Self-hosted Ollama — local LLMs. No API key; baseUrl-driven.
__AiProviderType.doc.custom: Catch-all — designer supplies baseUrl + apiFormat ('openai' / 'anthropic' / 'raw'). For private / on-prem / OpenAI-compatible inference servers without a dedicated adapter.
__AiProviderType.doc.mock: Explicit keyless offline text completions, deterministic from seed and messages. Node.js and Rust; never a credential fallback.

__ProviderCredentialScopeMode.doc.#: How one credential level (tenant, resource or user) takes part in supplying a provider entry's key.
__ProviderCredentialScopeMode.doc.off: The level is not used. The default, which keeps the entry exactly as it was.
__ProviderCredentialScopeMode.doc.optional: The level may save a key. It is used when present; otherwise the next level up supplies the key.
__ProviderCredentialScopeMode.doc.required: The level must save a key. A call without one fails with HTTP 428 AI_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED and the application owner's key is never used.

__ProviderCredentialCostPolicy.doc.#: Who pays for provider calls made on a tenant or user key.
__ProviderCredentialCostPolicy.doc.ownerPays: The key owner pays. Usage on a user key counts toward that user, usage on a tenant key toward that tenant, and neither counts toward the project ceilings. The default.
__ProviderCredentialCostPolicy.doc.saasPays: The application owner's accounting applies to every call, as without scoped keys.

__DecisionProvidersSettings.doc: Container for calibrated decision provider configurations — System One models that answer typed questions about a piece of state with a calibrated probability (docs/ADR-decision-layer-system-one.md). Each entry is a named provider that decision-consuming patterns reference by name. The generator emits DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct the adapter at runtime without revisiting the project config. Mirrors the bucketProvidersSettings shape — a named array; multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. one typesafe entry pinned to jev-1.13.0 in production use + a second entry pinned to a newer version under evaluation).

DecisionProvidersSettings.__decisionProviders.doc: List of configured decision providers. Add one entry per decision backend you want available. Multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two typesafe entries pinned to different model versions).

__DecisionProvider.doc: A named calibrated decision provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by decision-consuming patterns (DecisionAction.providerName and its siblings) and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainJev` → `DECISION_PROVIDER_MAINJEV_*`). The `provider` enum selects the adapter shipped under `_common/nodejs/src/common/decision-providers/`. The `capabilities` block advertises what the adapter behind this entry supports (question types, choice-option ceiling, context ceilings); its defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time, so a decision surface that needs more than the entry advertises fails validation at design time instead of surprising at runtime. The `configuration` is a typed flat config — only the fields relevant to the selected `provider` are read (see DecisionProviderConfig). The model version MUST be pinned (e.g. `jev-1.13.0`): a floating tag like `jev-latest` is refused with validation ERROR DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED, because an unpinned model means the same blueprint answers differently on two consecutive days, reddening tests with no attributable cause and poisoning every cache whose key includes the model version. A decision provider answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities; it NEVER makes authorization decisions (DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE). Native nodejs and java adapters implement this provider contract. Java supports the qualified DecisionAction, agent gate, property source, fuzzy query, enumerable classify and data-object/hub/notification and staged ContentModel editorial moderation surfaces. Other unported languages retain their refusal gates.

DecisionProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from decision-consuming patterns and as the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
DecisionProvider.name: String
DecisionProvider.__provider.doc: The backend provider implementation. Selects which DecisionProviderConfig fields are read, which capabilities the entry defaults to, and which adapter the codegen wires up. `mock` is a REAL transport — it answers deterministically with no key and never reaches the network.
DecisionProvider.__capabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags. Defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time so designers don't fill them; advanced users can narrow them per-entry (e.g. disable score questions on an entry meant only for yes/no gating). Designers should leave this null unless intentionally restricting what the provider would otherwise support.
DecisionProvider.__configuration.doc: Provider credentials and settings. Fields are flat across all provider types — only those relevant to the selected `provider` are read at runtime and emitted to env; sensitive fields are marked secret and masked in API responses.

__DecisionProviderConfig.doc: Provider credentials and settings for a DecisionProvider entry. Fields are flat across all provider types — only those relevant to the selected `provider` are read at runtime and emitted to DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* env vars. Per provider: typesafe reads apiKey (secret, required), model (required, PINNED — e.g. 'jev-1.13.0'), baseUrl (optional override of https://api.typesafe.ai for proxies and test harnesses); custom reads baseUrl (required), apiFormat, apiKey (secret, optional), model (optional), extraHeaders; mock is keyless and optionally reads seed. `apiKey` is masked in API responses and delivered via $SECRET_ env at deploy time — it never reaches a log line or an error body.

DecisionProviderConfig.__apiKey.doc: (typesafe/custom) API key. Secret — masked in API responses and emitted to DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_API_KEY at codegen time. Required for typesafe; optional for custom (a private emulation endpoint may be keyless). The key never reaches a log line or an error body.
DecisionProviderConfig.__model.doc: (typesafe/custom) The PINNED model version the adapter sends on every request, e.g. 'jev-1.13.0'. Floating tags ('jev-latest', 'latest', a bare family name with no version) are refused at validation with ERROR DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED: an unpinned model makes the same blueprint answer differently on two consecutive days, which reddens tests with no attributable cause and breaks decision caches whose key includes the model version.
DecisionProviderConfig.__baseUrl.doc: (custom: required; typesafe: optional) Endpoint base URL. For typesafe it overrides https://api.typesafe.ai (test harnesses, mock integrator servers and proxies — leave empty in production). For custom it is the designer-supplied endpoint the apiFormat is spoken against.
DecisionProviderConfig.__apiFormat.doc: (custom) The wire protocol spoken against baseUrl. 'systemone' (default) = the TypeSafe /v1/systemone request/response contract, verbatim; 'openai' / 'anthropic' = the decision interface emulated over that vendor's structured-output call (the adapter builds the JSON-schema envelope and parses the typed answer back).
DecisionProviderConfig.__extraHeaders.doc: (custom) Additional HTTP headers sent on every request to baseUrl (e.g. an internal gateway routing header). Values are NOT masked — put real secrets in apiKey, never here.
DecisionProviderConfig.__seed.doc: (mock) Deterministic seed mixed into the mock's answer derivation. The mock answers all three question types deterministically from (seed, state, question), so a generated test can assert on a decision without a key; change the seed to shift the whole answer surface at once. Optional — defaults to a fixed seed so two builds agree.

__DecisionCapabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags for a DecisionProvider — which question types the adapter behind this entry supports and the ceilings it enforces (mirrors PaymentCapabilities). Defaults are derived from the `provider` enum value when this block is omitted. A decision surface that asks a question type the entry doesn't advertise, or a choice question wider than maxChoiceOptions, is refused at design time with a validation ERROR; nothing throws at codegen. Set a flag to false to intentionally narrow an entry (e.g. disable score questions on an entry meant only for yes/no gating).

DecisionCapabilities.__supportsNoul.doc: Adapter supports `noul` questions — the probability 0..1 that a statement holds about the state. All shipped brands support this by default.
DecisionCapabilities.__supportsChoice.doc: Adapter supports `choice` questions — one key out of a criteria map, answered with the full probability distribution over the options.
DecisionCapabilities.__supportsScore.doc: Adapter supports `score` questions — a (possibly fractional) position on 2..10 ordered levels.
DecisionCapabilities.__maxChoiceOptions.doc: Upper bound on the criteria map size of a single choice question (Jev: 255). A choice question with more options than this bound is a design-time validation error, not a runtime surprise.
DecisionCapabilities.__contextTokenCeiling.doc: Upper bound on state + ALL questions of one request, in tokens (Jev: 65536).
DecisionCapabilities.__singleQuestionTokenCeiling.doc: Upper bound on state + the single longest question of one request, in tokens (Jev: 32768).
DecisionCapabilities.__probabilityDriftBand.doc: Half-width of the band within which this provider's PROBABILITY is not reproducible across identical requests. Measured for jev-1.13.0 (one noul, 0.03 spread) and per question type: six noul, six choice and six score questions, 12 identical requests each, held every discrete answer and drifted at worst 0.07 (noul probability), 0.10 (choice confidence) and 0.07 (score confidence). The types do not differ materially, so the band is one number per brand: 0.2 for typesafe, twice the worst spread of any type. A DecisionAction whose confidenceThreshold sits within this band of a decision boundary can flip between two runs of the SAME request, which is DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED's failure arriving through the threshold instead of the model version - hence DECISION_THRESHOLD_IN_DRIFT_BAND. Defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time; a designer should leave this null. Set it only from a measurement of the brand behind this entry.

__DecisionProviderType.doc.#: Identifies the decision provider backend. Each value maps to a native adapter under `_common/nodejs/src/common/decision-providers/<name>.ts` implementing the canonical `DecisionProvider` interface. This is deliberately NOT an AiProviderType brand: a System One model has no prompt, a typed answer instead of a response format, and free output tokens, so the AI family's ontology and price table would state false things about it — see docs/ADR-decision-layer-system-one.md Decision 1.
__DecisionProviderType.doc.typesafe: TypeSafe AI — Jev, the first System One model. POST /v1/systemone with a state and a map of typed questions; every question in one request is evaluated in parallel against the same state, and answers arrive with calibrated probabilities. Reference implementation.
__DecisionProviderType.doc.custom: Escape hatch — designer supplies baseUrl (+ apiFormat): either a TypeSafe-wire-compatible endpoint, or the same decision interface emulated over an OpenAI/Anthropic structured-output call. Capability overrides via the capabilities block.
__DecisionProviderType.doc.mock: Keyless deterministic mock — a REAL transport (the payment MOCK_TRANSPORT_BRANDS precedent): answers all three question types deterministically from a seed, never reaches the network, so CI and generated tests never depend on the vendor being up, reachable, or in business. Off production only, the answer can be STEERED: a `[[mock-decision <question>=<value>@<confidence>]]` directive written into any text field of the decided state (`*` as the question name addresses every question; `@<confidence>` is optional and a low one drives the escalation branch) replaces the hashed answer for that question, so a test can reach accept, reject and low-confidence escalation on purpose. The value must be legal for the question (a choice option key, a score level, or 0..1 / yes / no for noul) or the call is refused with `MOCK_DECISION_DIRECTIVE_INVALID`, never silently hashed. The reserved value `undecided` (any question type, no `@`) answers that question UNDECIDED instead: value null, `undecided: true`, reason `mockDirective` - the answer a provider with missing credentials gives to every question, so each pattern's undecided path can be tested without a key. On production, and on every real provider, directives are inert.

__DecisionApiFormat.doc.#: Wire protocol a `custom` decision provider speaks against its baseUrl.
__DecisionApiFormat.doc.systemone: The TypeSafe /v1/systemone request/response contract, verbatim — for self-hosted or proxied System One-compatible endpoints.
__DecisionApiFormat.doc.openai: Decision interface emulated over an OpenAI-style structured-output chat completion at baseUrl.
__DecisionApiFormat.doc.anthropic: Decision interface emulated over an Anthropic-style structured-output message call at baseUrl.

__DecisionQuestionType.doc: The three question shapes a System One provider answers. `noul` returns the probability 0..1 that a statement holds (no separate confidence field). `choice` returns one key out of the criteria map plus the distribution and a confidence. `score` returns a fractional position across 2-10 ordered criteria levels plus a confidence.
__DecisionLowConfidenceAction.doc: What a DecisionAction does when an answer's confidence falls below `confidenceThreshold`. `escalate` runs the aiCallAction/agentCallAction named by `escalateTo` - the seam that makes this a decision LAYER rather than a cheap classifier, and the posture every published adopter converged on. `reject` fails the action. `passThrough` keeps the low-confidence answer and records that it was below threshold. `defaultAnswer` substitutes the question's own defaultAnswer.
__DecisionErrorAction.doc: What a DecisionAction does when the provider itself fails (timeout, 5xx, 529). `failClosed` is the default and the only safe choice for a decision that NARROWS a result set or gates an operation: a narrowing filter that fails open returns the unfiltered set, which is a data leak wearing the costume of a degraded-mode fallback. `failOpen` is legitimate only where the worst case is a badly ordered page. `defaultAnswer` substitutes each question's defaultAnswer.
__DecisionQuestion.doc: One typed question inside a DecisionAction's bundle. Every question in a request is judged in parallel against the same state, so adding a question is nearly free - ask for everything the workflow needs about this state in one action rather than splitting it.

DecisionQuestion.__name.doc: Question identifier within the action, and the key the answer is written under in the context: `this.decisions.<actionName>.<name>`. Must be a valid codeName.
DecisionQuestion.__type.doc: The question shape (DecisionQuestionType). The provider entry's `capabilities` must advertise support for it, or the build fails with DECISION_QUESTION_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED rather than surprising at runtime.
DecisionQuestion.__instructions.doc: The statement or instruction the provider judges, in plain language. For `noul` it is a statement that is either true or false of the state ('the customer is asking for a refund'), NOT a question. There is no prompt and no system message: a System One model takes the state and the instruction and answers typed, so prompt-engineering idioms (role play, few-shot examples, output-format demands) belong nowhere in this field.
DecisionQuestion.__criteria.doc: [choice] The option map: each entry's `name` is the key the answer returns and its `value` is the description the provider judges against. [score] The ordered levels, lowest first - entry ORDER is the scale. Ignored for `noul`. A `choice` MUST include an escape option ('other', 'none of these') or validation fails with DECISION_CHOICE_NO_ESCAPE_OPTION: measured, a forced choice none of whose options fit produced a wrong pick at confidence 0.51, so the only signal of the mismatch is a confidence somebody has to remember to check. Forcing the escape option is cheaper. The entry count must stay within the provider's advertised maxChoiceOptions (DECISION_CHOICE_OVER_CEILING); 121 options measured correct at full confidence, so the ceiling is the brand's, not a framework guess.
DecisionQuestion.__defaultAnswer.doc: The answer substituted when `onLowConfidence` or `onProviderError` is `defaultAnswer`. For `noul` a 'true'/'false' string, for `choice` one of the criteria keys, for `score` a level. Required when either option selects defaultAnswer (DECISION_DEFAULT_ANSWER_MISSING).
DecisionQuestion.name: String

__DecisionCacheSettings.doc: Caching for a DecisionAction or a FuzzyDomainFilter - both use the ONE decision cache of the decision layer, stored in the service's Redis. Here caching is not only an optimisation: the provider's probability is not reproducible across identical requests, so a stored decision is what keeps a boundary case from moving between runs.

DecisionCacheSettings.__enabled.doc: When true, an identical (provider, pinned model, instructions, criteria, state) tuple reuses a stored DECISION instead of re-asking. Caching is what makes the query-time form (A) affordable and it is also a CORRECTNESS mechanism here: the probability drifts across identical requests, so re-deriving a boundary case answers differently on different days. Default false.
DecisionCacheSettings.__ttlSeconds.doc: Lifetime of a cached decision in seconds. Null = no expiry (invalidate by key change only).
DecisionCacheSettings.__keyExtra.doc: Optional MScript appended to the cache key for a dimension the framework cannot see (tenant, locale, a policy version). The key ALWAYS includes the pinned model version, the instructions text and the criteria: omit any of those and a designer corrects a criterion, re-runs, sees the old answer and concludes the criterion did not matter (DECISION_CACHE_KEY_INCOMPLETE guards the framework-built half).

__DecisionAction.doc: Asks a calibrated decision provider typed questions about a piece of state and writes the typed answers into the workflow context. They land under `this.decisions.<actionName>.<questionName>` as { value, confidence, probabilities, model }. Sits between ValidationAction (an MScript boolean) and AiCallAction (a full LLM call): it answers the judgements MScript cannot express without paying for text generation, at ~250-400 ms and free output tokens. It NEVER makes an authorization decision - a calibrated probability has no rationale and cannot be audited or explained, so DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE refuses a decision standing in for permissionCheck, membershipCheck, objectPermissionCheck or an absoluteRoles bypass. See docs/ADR-decision-layer-system-one.md.

DecisionAction.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry this action asks. Credentials are read from DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* at runtime. A dangling name fails validation.
DecisionAction.__model.doc: The PINNED provider model version for this action, overriding the provider entry's own. A floating tag (`jev-latest`, a bare family name) is refused with DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED: an unpinned model answers differently on two consecutive days, reddens tests with no attributable cause, and poisons every cache whose key includes the version. Leave null to inherit the provider entry's pin. Nodejs forwards this model on cached and uncached provider requests. Cache identity includes the selected model. The deterministic mock retains its own model identity.
DecisionAction.__state.doc: ONE MScript expression producing the state the questions are asked about - an object, an array, or text. An ARRAY carries several independent subjects in one request: measured, per-item accuracy held at 1.00 from 1 to 256 subjects with explicit item ids, at ~54 tokens and ~1.9 ms per subject. Address array members by an explicit `id` field named in each question's instructions; ordinal phrasing ('the first item') does not scale.
DecisionAction.__questions.doc: The question bundle asked about this one state. EVERY question in a request is evaluated in PARALLEL against the same state, so a dozen questions cost barely more than one - which is why the unit of this pattern is a state plus a bundle and not a single question. Modelling one action per decision, the way AiCallAction is modelled, would send the same subject once per question and throw away the cheapest property of the model.
DecisionAction.__checkType.doc: How a failing decision is handled, in ValidationAction's vocabulary. `liveCheck` throws immediately; `storedCheck` writes the answers to the context and continues, for deferred or compound logic. Default storedCheck: a decision is usually an input to later logic, not a gate.
DecisionAction.__confidenceThreshold.doc: Confidence at or above which an answer is acted on directly; below it `onLowConfidence` decides. Must sit outside the provider's `capabilities.probabilityDriftBand` of a decision boundary (DECISION_THRESHOLD_IN_DRIFT_BAND): the probability is not reproducible across identical requests, so a threshold inside the band makes the same request answer differently on different days. Null = act on every answer regardless of confidence.
DecisionAction.__onLowConfidence.doc: What happens below `confidenceThreshold`. Default escalate when `escalateTo` is set, else passThrough. An undecided answer always takes this policy; a low-confidence answer takes it only when confidenceThreshold is set.
DecisionAction.__escalateTo.doc: Name of an `aiCallActions[]` or `agentCallActions[]` entry of the same Business API that answers the cases this action was not confident about. This field is what makes the pattern a decision LAYER: the cheap calibrated model takes the confident majority and an LLM takes the ambiguous minority, with the run recording which path answered. A dangling name, or one that lives in another API of the service, fails validation: the escalation calls this API's own action method.
DecisionAction.__onProviderError.doc: What happens when the provider fails rather than answers. Default failClosed. See DecisionErrorAction - a narrowing filter that fails open is a data leak, not a fallback.
DecisionAction.__timeoutMs.doc: Positive per-request deadline in milliseconds for the decision adapter, including retries and response-body reads. The adapter aborts HTTP on timeout and routes DecisionTransportError through onProviderError. Null means no adapter deadline. This does not bound state MScript evaluation or Redis access.
DecisionAction.__cache.doc: Decision caching (DecisionCacheSettings): one cache entry per QUESTION, keyed on (provider, pinned model version, question type, instructions, criteria, state, keyExtra); a fully cached bundle makes no provider request and a partly cached one asks only the missing questions, still in one request. The entry stores the DECISION and is the authority: a concurrent first answer wins and is served until the key changes or the TTL runs out. Null or enabled=false = no caching, every execution asks the provider.

__FuzzyDomainFilter.doc: Narrows a list API by a judgement no column holds, by classifying the DISTINCT VALUES of one column with a decision provider, never the rows (ADR binding point A). Example: 'people whose profession requires a university education'. Each distinct value is decided ONCE as a noul against `criterion` and cached; the values whose probability reaches `confidenceThreshold` are merged into the where clause as `targetProperty IN (...)`. The cost is independent of the row count: a cold cache asks at most one decision per distinct value (batched, id-addressed, several hundred per request), a warm cache asks none. The cache is the AUTHORITY (no TTL by default): the provider's probability drifts across identical requests while its decision holds, so a value decided once stays decided until the criterion, the model or the provider changes. A value whose probability lands within the brand's dead band of the threshold (half of `probabilityDriftBand` each side: 0.1 for typesafe, 0 for mock) is EXCLUDED and logged as FuzzyDomainNearThreshold rather than silently classified either way. The filter fails CLOSED: a provider outage is an error (or the empty set under `matchNothing`), never the unfiltered set. Responses it narrowed carry `fuzzyDomainFilters` attribution (filter, property, provider, model, criterionHash, threshold). Never an authorization surface (DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE). List APIs only, implemented for nodejs and java.

FuzzyDomainFilter.__name.doc: A code-safe name for the filter, unique within the Business API. It names the filter in the response attribution and in logs.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__condition.doc: Optional MScript gating whether the filter applies to this request (like ExtendedClause.condition). Null = always applied. A condition that reads the caller's roles, permissions or memberships turns the classifier into a visibility gate and is refused (DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE).
FuzzyDomainFilter.__targetProperty.doc: The property whose distinct values are classified: a scalar property of the API's data object (in `whereClause.fuzzyDomainFilters`) or of the joined data object (in `ListJointFilter.fuzzyDomainFilters`). An Enum property's domain is its declared options and is checked against `maxDomainSize` at design time; any other property's domain is read from the store at request time and checked there. Never an authorization-bearing column (id, the tenant column, a session-bound or owner column): DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__criterion.doc: The statement judged about ONE value, as a noul: the probability it holds of that value. Write it about the item, e.g. 'names a profession that normally requires a completed university degree to practise'. It is part of the cache key, so editing it re-classifies the whole domain on the next request - which is the point: a corrected criterion must change the answer.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry that classifies the values. A dangling name fails validation (DECISION_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND).
FuzzyDomainFilter.__model.doc: The PINNED model version, overriding the provider entry's own; a floating tag is refused (DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED). Null = inherit the provider entry's pin, which must then exist. The version is part of the cache key, so a model upgrade re-classifies the domain. The override reaches ordinary and joint filters; model changes classify into separate cache keys.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__confidenceThreshold.doc: Probability at or above which a value qualifies. Default 0.8. Must sit outside the provider's `probabilityDriftBand` of 0.5 (DECISION_THRESHOLD_IN_DRIFT_BAND): for typesafe a threshold in (0.3, 0.7) is refused. Values within half the band of the threshold are excluded as near-threshold rather than flipped in and out.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__maxDomainSize.doc: Ceiling on the distinct values this filter classifies. Default 1000, framework ceiling 5000 - set by what a designer can review and re-derive when the criterion changes, and by cost; NOT by request rate (the vendor's published request-rate limit was measured unenforced and is not a budget). Checked at design time for an Enum property (FUZZY_DOMAIN_CARDINALITY_EXCEEDED, naming the property and its cardinality) and at request time for any other, where an over-ceiling domain fails CLOSED with the same code.
FuzzyDomainFilter.__onProviderError.doc: What happens when the provider cannot answer. `failClosed` (default): the request fails with FUZZY_DOMAIN_PROVIDER_FAILED. `matchNothing`: the filter resolves to the empty set and its attribution is marked degraded. There is no fail-open: this filter narrows, and an outage that returned the unfiltered set would be a data leak (ADR rule 4).
FuzzyDomainFilter.__cache.doc: The decision cache settings (DecisionCacheSettings). The cache is ALWAYS on for a fuzzy filter - it is what keeps the IN set from moving between requests - so `enabled: false` is refused (FUZZY_DOMAIN_CACHE_REQUIRED). `ttlSeconds` defaults to no expiry; a TTL makes every value re-derive at expiry and is warned about (FUZZY_DOMAIN_CACHE_TTL_REDERIVES). `keyExtra` adds a key dimension the framework cannot see.
FuzzyDomainFilter.name: String

__FuzzyDomainFailureMode.doc: What a FuzzyDomainFilter does when its provider cannot answer. Both options keep the filter NARROWING - there is deliberately no fail-open (ADR rule 4). `failClosed` fails the request with FUZZY_DOMAIN_PROVIDER_FAILED; `matchNothing` answers an empty result and marks the response attribution degraded.
__PaymentProvidersSettings.doc: Container for payment provider configurations — PSPs and merchant-of-record providers. Each entry is a named provider that can be referenced by DataObject `checkout` / `subscription` / `marketplace` opt-ins and by payment-related business-API actions. The generator emits PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct an SDK client at runtime without revisiting the project config. Replaces the legacy `stripeSettings` (single managed Stripe key pair) with the same shape used by aiProvidersSettings / bucketProvidersSettings / notificationProvidersSettings — multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. one Stripe account for one-time charges + a second Stripe Connect account for marketplace payouts; or one Paddle store for subscriptions + one Stripe for one-time donations).

PaymentProvidersSettings.__paymentProviders.doc: List of configured payment providers. Add one entry per payment account / backend you want available. Multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two Stripe accounts for test and live, or a primary Stripe + a marketplace-only Stripe Connect).

__PaymentProvider.doc:
A named payment provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by `DataObject.checkout.providerName`, `DataObject.subscription.providerName`, `DataObject.marketplace.providerName`, `PaymentAction.providerName`, `RefundAction.providerName`, `SubscriptionAction.providerName`, `PayoutAction.providerName`, and the env-var prefix (e.g. `defaultStripe` → `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_DEFAULTSTRIPE_*`). The `provider` enum selects the backend SDK / adapter shipped under `_common/nodejs/src/common/payment-providers/`. The `capabilities` block reflects what the underlying provider can do — its defaults are derived from `provider`, advanced users can narrow them per-entry (e.g. disable subscriptions on a Stripe entry used only for one-time donations). The `configuration` is a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the chosen `provider`; the UI and the agent ontology doc enforce the per-provider shape.

Expected configuration keys per provider:
- stripe: secretKey, publishableKey, connectClientId (optional, marketplace), apiVersion (optional), kycReturnUrl (required for createKycSession — landing URL Stripe sends the merchant to after onboarding completes; can also be supplied per-call), kycRefreshUrl (optional, falls back to kycReturnUrl — URL Stripe sends the merchant to when the onboarding link expires), honourRadarReview (optional boolean, default true: a payment Stripe Radar places in review is held started / FRAUD_REVIEW until the review closes; approved settles it success, refunded_as_fraud or refunded settles it failed; only false turns it off), newCardThreeDSThreshold / savedCardThreeDSMode ('threshold' or 'verifyOnce': a stored card forced until a live read proves an authenticated 3-D Secure on it, then not forced; Stripe may still challenge) / savedCardThreeDSThreshold / threeDSRequestLevel ('any'|'challenge', default 'any') / threeDSThresholdCurrency (optional, server configuration only: at or above a threshold the PaymentIntent carries payment_method_options.card.request_three_d_secure, forcing 3-D Secure; below it Stripe and the issuer decide, the service cannot skip a challenge; unset = never forced; an unreadable value forces), savedCardOffSession (optional, 'never' default | 'verified', server configuration only: beside savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce', a charge from a PaymentAction declared buyerAbsent on a proven, verified stored card is a merchant-initiated off_session charge with no 3-D Secure liability shift; for buyer-absent charges under a stored-credential agreement only). NOTE: `webhookSecret` is deliberately NOT a stripe configuration key — the webhook endpoint and its signing secret are PROVISIONING STATE: the framework registers the endpoint and captures the secret itself (POST /v1/payments/admin/webhooks/provision), storing it under PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
- paypal: clientId, clientSecret, webhookId, environment ('sandbox'|'live'), partnerAttributionId (optional, marketplace)
- iyzico: apiKey, secretKey, baseUrl (e.g. 'https://sandbox-api.iyzipay.com' or 'https://api.iyzipay.com'), subMerchantPrefix (optional, marketplace), savedCardThreeDSMode (optional, 'verifyOnce'|'threshold', server configuration only: verifyOnce skips 3-D Secure on a card once a 3-D Secure charge on it settled success, threshold skips it below savedCardThreeDSThreshold; unset = always 3-D Secure), savedCardThreeDSThreshold (optional, threshold mode), newCardThreeDSThreshold (optional, forces 3-D Secure on the hosted Checkout Form at or above it), directCardEntry (optional boolean, nodejs: the project's own frontend takes a new card and the service sends it to iyzico instead of the hosted Checkout Form; widens the merchant's PCI scope), marketplaceActive (optional boolean, nodejs: the merchant account is marketplace-activated; every basket is routed: a seller's split, or the platform's own sale by ownSaleStrategy; paymentGroup becomes framework-owned; a subscription in the default hosted mode may not bind such an entry), ownSaleStrategy (optional, 'listing'|'ownSubMerchant', default 'listing': how own sales are sent), ownSubMerchantKey (the operator's own sub-merchant key, required by 'ownSubMerchant'), subscriptionMode (optional, 'hosted'|'tokenized', default 'hosted', nodejs: 'tokenized' makes the framework recharge the buyer's stored card every period; the mode a marketplace-active entry uses for subscriptions).
