The slice-1 keys threeDSMode / nonThreeDSMaxAmount are retired: ignored at runtime (always 3-D Secure unless savedCardThreeDSMode says otherwise) and a validator warning (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_KEYS_RETIRED)
- adyen: apiKey, merchantAccount, hmacKey, clientKey, environment ('test'|'live'), liveEndpointUrlPrefix (required when environment='live')
- paddle: vendorId, apiKey, webhookSecretKey (the notification destination secret key; verifies the Paddle-Signature h1 HMAC, required for webhooks only), environment ('sandbox'|'live'), priceMode (optional, 'auto'|'explicit'). `webhookPublicKey` is retired (Paddle Classic): it is ignored and draws a warning.
- lemonsqueezy: apiKey, storeId, signingSecret, webhookSecret (optional — the webhook-subscription secret; signingSecret is what verifies inbound webhooks)
- mangopay: clientId, apiKey, baseUrl (its host decides sandbox vs production, and the live-key guard reads it), environment ('sandbox'|'production'), payInDefaultReturnUrl. Mangopay hooks are unsigned GETs to the same webhook URL; the receiver re-fetches the resource with clientId + apiKey.
- custom: baseUrl, apiKey (optional), webhookSecret (optional), capabilitiesOverride (explicit JSON — escape hatch)

Secret keys (secretKey, clientSecret, apiKey, signingSecret, etc.) are masked in API responses and emitted to PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

PaymentProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from DataObject checkout/subscription/marketplace opt-ins and from payment-related business-API actions, and as the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
PaymentProvider.name: String
PaymentProvider.__provider.doc: The backend provider implementation. Selects which keys are expected in `configuration`, which capabilities the entry defaults to, and which adapter the codegen wires up.
PaymentProvider.__capabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags. Defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time so designers don't fill them; advanced users can narrow them per-entry (e.g. disable subscriptions on a Stripe entry used only for one-time donations). Designers should leave this null unless intentionally restricting features the provider would otherwise support.
PaymentProvider.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of provider-specific credentials and settings. The required keys depend on `provider` — see the PaymentProvider doc string for the per-provider key list. The UI enforces the right form fields per provider; agents emit only keys that match. Sensitive keys (secretKey, clientSecret, apiKey, signingSecret, etc.) are masked in API responses and emitted to environment variables at codegen time.
PaymentProvider.__kycOnboarding.doc: Marketplace KYC onboarding configuration. Only meaningful when capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true and capabilities.supportsConnectedKYC=true. The kycMode discriminator drives codegen branching (ConnectedAccountManager.startOnboarding) and panel UI affordance shape. Leave null to use the per-provider default; set explicitly to override the default mode or to wire a returnUrlTemplate / steps[] / documentTypes[] customized to the project's flow.
PaymentProvider.__payoutCadence.doc: Payout scheduling + reserve configuration. Only meaningful when capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true. The mode discriminator drives codegen branching (PayoutManager.createPayout) and panel UI affordance (create button enabled/disabled/cadence label). Leave null to use the per-provider default.
PaymentProvider.__webhookOwnerService.doc: The service that receives this entry's provider webhooks when the payment patterns of MORE THAN ONE service bind the entry (a commerce service selling tickets and a plans service selling subscriptions on the same PSP account). A PSP account registers one webhook URL, so one service owns it: the owner verifies the vendor signature once, resolves whether the event's ticket is its own, and relays the verified, normalized event to the other services that carry the entry over the inter-service M2M channel; a relay is accepted only from the declared owner's verified machine identity. Name a service whose data objects carry a checkout, subscription or marketplace opt-in bound to this entry. Leave null when one service carries the entry; with several carriers and no owner the FIRST carrier in project order owns the URL and validation warns (PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_OWNER_UNDECLARED). The devops guide lists one webhook URL per entry and names the owner.

__PaymentCapabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags for a PaymentProvider. Each flag advertises what the underlying provider can do behind this named entry; the framework gates calls accordingly (e.g. a SubscriptionAction bound to a provider with supportsSubscriptions=false is refused at design time with validation ERROR INCOMPATIBLE_PAYMENT_PROVIDER_CAPABILITY, and the runtime adapter throws CapabilityLimitedError on any call that slips through; nothing throws at codegen). Defaults are derived from the `provider` enum value when this block is omitted. Set a flag to false to intentionally narrow capabilities — e.g. disable subscriptions on a Stripe entry used only for one-time donations, or disable marketplace on a Stripe account that is not a Connect account.

PaymentCapabilities.__supportsOneTime.doc: Provider can charge a single payment (createPaymentIntent + capture). All providers in the enum support this by default.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsRefundsFull.doc: Provider supports full refunds of a captured payment.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsRefundsPartial.doc: Provider supports partial refunds. When false but supportsRefundsFull=true, refund requests must omit `amount` (full-only).
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsSubscriptions.doc: Provider supports recurring subscriptions (plans, renewals, cancellations). Set false on a provider that natively supports subscriptions if this entry is intentionally one-time-only.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsProration.doc: Provider supports proration on plan changes (upgrade / downgrade mid-period). Only meaningful when supportsSubscriptions=true.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsMarketplace.doc: Provider supports marketplace flows (connected accounts, transfers, payouts to sub-merchants).
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsConnectedKYC.doc: Provider exposes a hosted KYC flow for connected accounts. Only meaningful when supportsMarketplace=true.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsDisputes.doc: Provider emits dispute / chargeback events on its webhook and accepts evidence submissions.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsSavedCards.doc: Provider supports tokenized payment methods that can be saved on a customer and re-used.
PaymentCapabilities.__supportsApplePayGooglePay.doc: Provider's hosted fields / SDK support Apple Pay and Google Pay wallets.
PaymentCapabilities.__supports3DSecure.doc: Provider supports 3-D Secure / SCA-compliant authentication for card payments.
PaymentCapabilities.__isMerchantOfRecord.doc: Provider acts as merchant of record (handles tax collection, remittance, and compliance — e.g. Paddle, Lemon Squeezy). Affects how the framework wires tax-related hooks: when true, the framework does NOT emit tax-handling lifecycle hooks because the provider takes care of it.
PaymentCapabilities.__webhookStyle.doc: Signature verification style used by this provider's webhooks. The adapter uses this hint at verification time. Values: 'hmac' (HMAC-SHA256 with a shared secret, e.g. Stripe, Adyen, Paddle), 'rsa-pub' (RSA public-key signature; no shipped adapter uses it), 'cert' (X.509 certificate, e.g. PayPal), 'signature' (custom signature scheme, e.g. Lemon Squeezy), 'refetch' (unsigned GET notification, the adapter re-fetches the resource, e.g. Mangopay). Defaults per `provider` enum value.

__PaymentProviderType.doc.#: Identifies the payment provider backend. Each value maps to a native adapter under `_common/nodejs/src/common/payment-providers/<name>.ts` that implements the canonical `PaymentProvider` interface — these are first-class natives, NOT routed through the legacy `businessapi/integrations/` mechanism.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.stripe: Stripe — PSP. Full feature set (one-time, refunds, subscriptions, marketplace via Connect, disputes). Reference implementation; the other adapters target capability parity where the underlying provider allows. 3-D Secure is finished in the browser by Stripe.js (`handleNextAction` / `confirmPayment` / `confirmCardPayment`) and recorded by the generated webhook route `/v1/payments/webhook/<provider>`: no complete stage and no return route are involved. A subscription whose first payment needs the buyer answers `past_due` with `nextAction` (`allow_incomplete`). Off-session (merchant-initiated) charging is not supported.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.paypal: PayPal — PSP. Order / Capture model. Marketplace via Hyperwallet or partner accounts. The buyer approves on PayPal's page and returns to the start's `return_url`; no generated route captures an approved order, so the capture is a PaymentAction `complete` stage in a session api the return page calls with the payment id, never a webhook api.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.iyzico: iyzico — PSP. Turkish market focus; mandatory 3DS flow shapes the intent state path. Marketplace via sub-merchant model. Both card shapes are completed by generated service routes, never by an authored complete stage: the hosted Checkout Form (no saved card) through `/v1/payments/checkout-return/<provider>`, a saved card's 3-D Secure through `/v1/payments/threeds-return/<provider>`, which calls 3dsecure/auth. A saved card's paymentMethodId is `<cardUserKey>:<cardToken>`; a buyer has ONE cardUserKey, minted by iyzico on the buyer's first save and stored by the framework on the buyer's payment-customer mapping. A hosted-form buyer who never returns is settled from iyzico's `CHECKOUT_FORM_AUTH` webhook. Either `storePaymentMethod` switch (CheckoutConfig or SubscriptionConfig) lets the buyer save the card on the hosted form. Subscriptions start on iyzico's hosted subscription Checkout Form: the subscribe answers `pending_provider` plus `checkoutForm`, and `/v1/payments/subscription-checkout-return/<provider>` confirms it.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.adyen: Adyen — enterprise PSP. Wide alternative-payment-method coverage (iDEAL, Klarna, etc.). Marketplace via MarketPay. A redirect or 3-D Secure action is completed through the generated `PATCH /v1/complete<object>payment/:orderId` route with the `details` Adyen Web returns, never by an authored complete stage.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.paddle: Paddle — merchant of record. Handles tax / compliance. Subscriptions are first-class; no marketplace.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.lemonsqueezy: Lemon Squeezy — merchant of record. Simpler API than Paddle; store-scoped. No marketplace.
__PaymentProviderType.doc.mangopay: Mangopay — wallet / e-money based. Marketplace-native (its strength); subscriptions are NOT native (supportsSubscriptions defaults to false).
__PaymentProviderType.doc.custom: Escape hatch — designer supplies `baseUrl` + capability overrides. For provider-agnostic webhook ingestion or for adapters that don't have a dedicated native implementation yet.

__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.#: Signature verification style used by a payment provider's inbound webhooks. The adapter uses this hint at verification time to pick the right signing primitive.
__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.hmac: HMAC-SHA256 with a shared secret in the configuration. Default for Stripe, iyzico, Adyen, Paddle (Paddle Billing h1 over '<ts>:<raw body>').
__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.rsa-pub: RSA public-key signature. No shipped adapter uses it (it was Paddle Classic's scheme; Paddle Billing signs with HMAC); kept so an existing capabilities override still parses.
__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.cert: X.509 certificate-based verification. Default for PayPal.
__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.signature: Custom signature scheme — adapter-specific. Default for Lemon Squeezy.
__PaymentWebhookStyle.doc.refetch: Unsigned notification: the provider calls a GET with query parameters and the adapter re-fetches the named resource from the provider API, trusting only that answer. Default for Mangopay (hooks carry EventType, RessourceId, Date).

__KycMode.doc.#: Discriminator for how a PaymentProvider drives marketplace KYC onboarding. Each mode requires a different per-provider configuration shape — see KycOnboardingConfig — and a different panel-side UI affordance: hosted modes link out to a provider URL; the document-api mode lists the missing document types; partner-referrals mints a fresh Partner Referrals URL per call. The 'none' value is reserved for providers without marketplace support (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy); the KycOnboardingConfig pattern does NOT attach to such providers in practice.
__KycMode.doc.hosted-url: Provider exposes a single hosted onboarding URL (Stripe Connect Express / Standard). The framework mints the URL on demand and the operator is responsible for opening it.
__KycMode.doc.hosted-stepwise: Provider exposes a stepwise hosted dashboard (iyzico sub-merchant: basic → IBAN → identity → contract; Adyen AfP: KYC tier × document × country matrix). Each step has its own affordance; the panel surfaces a pending-steps badge.
__KycMode.doc.document-api: Provider has NO hosted shopper-facing URL — KYC is an API-driven document upload flow (Mangopay). The merchant-side dashboard deep-link is exposed for operators; designers list the required document types up front.
__KycMode.doc.partner-referrals: Provider uses a referral-based onboarding (PayPal Partner Referrals). Each call mints a fresh URL with the configured return target; no resume endpoint exists.
__KycMode.doc.none: Provider does not support marketplace KYC. Reserved value — KycOnboardingConfig should not be attached to such providers.

__PayoutCadenceMode.doc.#: How payouts to connected accounts are scheduled. 'on_demand' = framework calls provider.createPayout synchronously. 'scheduled' = framework writes a sys_<X>Payout row with status='scheduled' + a next-fire timestamp; a project-level payout-scheduler cron picks it up. 'provider_driven' = the provider runs its own settlement cadence (iyzico daily/weekly settlements, Adyen-side payout schedule, Stripe Connect automatic payouts); createPayout from the framework throws PaymentGateError(409) and the panel UI greys out the 'Create payout' button.
__PayoutCadenceMode.doc.on_demand: Framework drives the payout synchronously — provider.createPayout is called at request time.
__PayoutCadenceMode.doc.scheduled: Framework owns the schedule — sys_<X>Payout rows carry status='scheduled' + scheduledFor; a cron worker fires the provider call when due.
__PayoutCadenceMode.doc.provider_driven: Provider runs its own settlement cadence — programmatic createPayout from the framework is not supported and throws PaymentGateError(409).

__PayoutSchedule.doc.#: Cadence for framework-driven scheduled payouts. Only meaningful when PayoutCadenceConfig.mode='scheduled'.
__PayoutSchedule.doc.daily: Fire the queued payout the next calendar day.
__PayoutSchedule.doc.weekly: Fire the queued payout the next calendar week (same weekday it was scheduled).
__PayoutSchedule.doc.monthly: Fire the queued payout the next calendar month (same day-of-month, clamped to month length).

__KycOnboardingConfig.doc:
Per-provider marketplace KYC onboarding configuration. Attached to a PaymentProvider when the provider supports marketplace + connected KYC. The `kycMode` discriminator drives both codegen (ConnectedAccountManager branches on it) and the panel UI affordance: hosted-url → 'Open onboarding' button; hosted-stepwise → 'Open dashboard' + pending-steps badge; document-api → 'Upload documents' + missing-types list; partner-referrals → 'Start referral' that mints a fresh URL.

Per-mode required fields:
- hosted-url: returnUrlTemplate
- hosted-stepwise: steps[] + dashboardDeepLinkTemplate
- document-api: documentTypes[] + merchantDashboardUrl
- partner-referrals: returnUrlTemplate (partnerAttributionId optional)
- none: no fields required (and the pattern should not be attached)

The per-provider tier/document/country matrix (Adyen AfP, Stripe Connect Express tiers, etc.) is intentionally NOT modeled here — that logic lives in each adapter's `createConnectedAccount` / `createKycSession` / `uploadKycDocument` implementation. This config only carries the discriminator + the configuration the codegen + panel need to branch on.

KycOnboardingConfig.__kycMode.doc: Discriminator for the onboarding flow shape. Leave null to take the PER-PROVIDER default (stripe → hosted-url, paypal → partner-referrals, iyzico/adyen → hosted-stepwise, mangopay → document-api, paddle/lemonsqueezy → none); set it to override that default. There is deliberately NO schema-level default here: a single global one would be wrong for every provider but stripe, and the mode a provider cannot serve (iyzico has no hosted onboarding URL) must never be the mode the platform picks for it.
KycOnboardingConfig.__returnUrlTemplate.doc: (hosted-url / partner-referrals) URL template the provider redirects to after onboarding completes (a page of YOUR app). Tokens: `{accountId}` = the local connected-account row id (what the /v1/payments/connected-accounts/:accountId routes take), `{providerAccountId}` = the provider-side account id. Required for hosted-url and partner-referrals modes.
KycOnboardingConfig.__steps.doc: (hosted-stepwise) Ordered list of onboarding steps the provider walks an operator through (e.g. ['basic','iban','identity','contract'] for iyzico sub-merchant; ['tier1','tier2','documents','bank'] for Adyen AfP). The panel renders a per-step pending badge against this list. Required for hosted-stepwise mode.
KycOnboardingConfig.__dashboardDeepLinkTemplate.doc: (hosted-stepwise) URL template the panel deep-links operators to - a PROVIDER dashboard, so `{accountId}` and `{providerAccountId}` both resolve to the provider-side account id at runtime (a row with no providerAccountId is refused 409 CONNECTED_ACCOUNT_NOT_PROVISIONED). Required for hosted-stepwise mode.
KycOnboardingConfig.__documentTypes.doc: (document-api) Ordered list of KYC document types the provider needs (e.g. ['IDENTITY_PROOF','ADDRESS_PROOF','ARTICLES_OF_ASSOCIATION'] for Mangopay LegalUser). The panel renders a per-type missing-badge and the ConnectedAccountManager.uploadKycDocument call gates against this set. Required for document-api mode.
KycOnboardingConfig.__merchantDashboardUrl.doc: (document-api) Merchant-side dashboard URL the panel deep-links operators to. For Mangopay this is the hub URL (https://hub.mangopay.com/users/{providerAccountId}/kyc); the provider exposes no hosted shopper-facing UI. `{accountId}` and `{providerAccountId}` both resolve to the provider-side account id here. Required for document-api mode.
KycOnboardingConfig.__partnerAttributionId.doc: (partner-referrals) Optional partner attribution id forwarded on the Partner Referrals create call. Only meaningful for PayPal-style flows.

__PayoutCadenceConfig.doc:
Per-provider payout scheduling + reserve configuration. Attached to a PaymentProvider when the provider supports marketplace. The codegen-emitted PayoutManager branches on `mode`: on_demand → synchronous provider call; scheduled → row inserted into sys_<X>Payout with status='scheduled' for the payout-scheduler cron to pick up; provider_driven → throws PaymentGateError(409) and the panel UI greys out the create button.

`reserveDays` is a hold on each payout: when the PayoutManager books a sys_<X>Payout row it stamps availableForPayoutAt = max(scheduledFor, createdAt + reserveDays), and the payout-scheduler never sends the row before that time. With reserveDays > 0 an on_demand create is booked for the scheduler instead of paid synchronously. The window runs from the payout's creation; it is not yet tied to the capture of the specific payments the payout pays out.

Per-provider defaults. These are the EFFECTIVE defaults, not documentation: leave `mode` null and this table decides — the validator, the pattern instance and every PayoutManager template all read it, so the generated code runs the cadence the provider actually does. An authored `mode` overrides it.
- stripe: mode='provider_driven' (Stripe Connect controls), reserveDays=0
- paypal: mode='on_demand', reserveDays=0
- iyzico: mode='provider_driven' (daily/weekly settlement), reserveDays=0
- adyen: mode='provider_driven' (Adyen surfaces reserve in webhook), reserveDays=varies
- paddle: mode='on_demand', reserveDays=0
- lemonsqueezy: mode='on_demand', reserveDays=0
- mangopay: mode='on_demand', reserveDays=0
- custom: mode='on_demand', reserveDays=0

An entry with no `provider` is read as stripe (the same default `indexPaymentProviders` and the templates apply); a provider type with no row here falls back to the `custom` row.

PayoutCadenceConfig.__mode.doc: How payouts are scheduled. on_demand = framework-driven synchronous call; scheduled = framework-driven cron; provider_driven = provider owns the cadence. Leave null to take the PER-PROVIDER default (stripe/iyzico/adyen → provider_driven, paypal/paddle/lemonsqueezy/mangopay/custom → on_demand); set it to override that default. There is deliberately NO schema-level default here: a single global one would be wrong for the three providers that run their own settlement, and because a schema default is WRITTEN into the blueprint at validation time it would silently make the per-provider table dead for exactly those providers.
PayoutCadenceConfig.__schedule.doc: (mode='scheduled' only) Cadence — daily / weekly / monthly. Required when mode='scheduled'; ignored otherwise.
PayoutCadenceConfig.__reserveDays.doc: Number of days a payout is held before it may be sent. 0 = no hold. Each booked sys_<X>Payout row is stamped availableForPayoutAt = max(scheduledFor, createdAt + reserveDays) and the payout-scheduler does not send it earlier; with reserveDays > 0 an on_demand create is booked for the scheduler rather than paid synchronously. The window counts from the payout's creation, not from the capture of the funds it pays out. A provider_driven cadence (the stripe / iyzico / adyen default when mode is not set) books no payout, so nothing applies the reserve there: a PayoutAction on a marketplace owner bound to such a provider with reserveDays > 0 is a validation ERROR (PAYOUT_ACTION_PROVIDER_DRIVEN_RESERVE_OR_GATE) - set mode to scheduled (or on_demand) or keep reserveDays at 0.

__InvoiceProvidersSettings.doc: Container for invoice provider configurations — the backends that issue, number, finalize and collect legal/commercial invoices for the project's invoicing-enabled data objects. Each entry is a named provider that can be referenced by DataObject `invoicing` opt-ins (`invoicing.configuration.providerName`) and, in later slices, by invoice-related business-API actions. Invoicing is a SEPARATE axis from payment: a PaymentProvider moves money, an InvoiceProvider produces the billing document — one object can bind checkout to Stripe payments and invoicing to a local ERP at the same time. The generator emits INVOICE_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* environment variables per NATIVE provider so service code can construct an adapter at runtime; BRIDGE brands (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger) carry no credentials of their own — they name an `enterpriseIntegrationsSettings` entry via `integrationName` and reach the platform through the mcpbff bridge. Mirrors the paymentProvidersSettings / aiProvidersSettings shape — a named array; multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two Parasut companies, or one internal series for drafts + one stripe for customer-facing invoices).

InvoiceProvidersSettings.__invoiceProviders.doc: List of configured invoice providers. Add one entry per invoicing backend / account you want available. Multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two logoIsbasi firms, or an internal series next to a stripe account). The built-in `internal` brand needs no credentials — declare it when you want a named internal series, or simply leave a data object's `providerName` null to bind the framework-native invoicing implicitly.

__InvoiceProvider.doc:
A named invoice provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by `DataObject.invoicing.configuration.providerName` and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainParasut` → `INVOICE_PROVIDER_MAINPARASUT_*`). The `provider` enum selects the backend adapter; brands split into two families:

- NATIVE brands (internal, stripe, logoIsbasi, mikro, parasut, custom) own their credentials here, in `configuration` — a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the chosen `provider` (the UI and the agent ontology doc enforce the per-provider shape). `integrationName` MUST stay null for them.
- BRIDGE brands (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger) carry NO configuration keys of their own: they REQUIRE `integrationName` to name a `projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings.enterpriseIntegrations[]` entry, whose platform credentials the mcpbff bridge already holds. Declaring credentials twice is exactly the drift the split exists to prevent.

Expected configuration keys per NATIVE provider:
- internal: (none — the framework issues, numbers and stores invoices itself)
- stripe: secretKey, webhookSecret
- logoIsbasi: clientId, clientSecret, firmId
- mikro: baseUrl, apiKey, companyCode (optional)
- parasut: clientId, clientSecret, companyId, username (optional), password (optional)
- custom: baseUrl, apiKey (optional)

The `capabilities` block reflects what the underlying provider can do — its defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time, advanced users can narrow them per-entry. Secret keys (secretKey, clientSecret, apiKey, password, webhookSecret) are masked in API responses and emitted to INVOICE_PROVIDER_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

BRAND -> PLATFORM PAIRING (bridge brands only). A bridge brand drives ONE enterprise platform family, and the validator enforces the pairing after it resolves `integrationName`: naming an integration that exists is not enough, the resolved entry's `platform` must be one the brand can drive.
- sap: sapS4Hana or sapEcc (one invoice brand over both SAP Gateway platforms - the named integration decides which)
- dynamics365: dynamics365
- netsuite: netsuite
- logoTiger: NO platform yet - EnterprisePlatformType carries no Logo value, so no integrationName can ever satisfy this brand and declaring it is a typed error (INVOICE_PROVIDER_PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE)
A mismatch is INVOICE_PROVIDER_PLATFORM_MISMATCH and names the allowed platforms. The pairing table is machine-readable, not prose: it is the `platforms` field of each brand's row in the provider config catalog's `__brandStatus` block.

SHIPPED STATE (honest). Only `internal` (Faz 1b) and `stripe` (Faz 2) have adapters today. `logoIsbasi`, `mikro` and `parasut` are Faz 3.5; all four bridge brands are Faz 4+ and additionally wait on the EnterpriseBridge semantic layer. Those brands are DECLARABLE - the blueprint accepts them and their credential keys are catalogued - but binding a data object to one is a typed 501 at runtime naming the phase. `custom` is the bring-your-own escape hatch: the project registers its own adapter, so the framework ships none on purpose. A settings UI must read the per-brand `status` field from GET {apiBase}/patterns/provider-config-catalog (family=invoiceProvider, `brandStatus`) rather than hardcoding this roster, and mark the roadmap brands instead of offering a form that cannot be completed.

InvoiceProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from DataObject `invoicing` opt-ins and as the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
InvoiceProvider.name: String
InvoiceProvider.__provider.doc: The backend provider implementation. Selects which keys are expected in `configuration` (native brands), or that the entry is a BRIDGE onto an enterprise integration (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger — these require `integrationName` and take no configuration keys). Defaults to `internal`, the framework-native invoicing that needs no credentials at all. A bridge brand also pins WHICH enterprise platform the named integration may run on (sap accepts sapS4Hana or sapEcc; dynamics365 and netsuite pair one-to-one; logoTiger has no platform yet and cannot be completed at all). Brands differ in shipped state: internal and stripe have adapters today, every other brand except the bring-your-own `custom` is declarable-but-unshipped and answers a typed 501 when bound - read the `brandStatus` block of the provider config catalog for the machine-readable state.
InvoiceProvider.__integrationName.doc: BRIDGE brands only (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger): the name of the `projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings.enterpriseIntegrations[]` entry whose platform this provider issues invoices on. The mcpbff bridge owns the connectivity and the credentials — this entry adds none of its own. MUST be null for native brands (internal, stripe, logoIsbasi, mikro, parasut, custom), whose credentials live in `configuration` here.
InvoiceProvider.__capabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags. Defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time so designers don't fill them; advanced users can narrow them per-entry (e.g. disable collection on a stripe entry used only for record-keeping invoices). Designers should leave this null unless intentionally restricting features the provider would otherwise support.
InvoiceProvider.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of provider-specific credentials and settings — NATIVE brands only. The required keys depend on `provider` — see the InvoiceProvider doc string for the per-provider key list. The UI enforces the right form fields per provider; agents emit only keys that match. Bridge brands (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger) take no keys here — their credentials live on the named enterprise integration. Sensitive keys (secretKey, clientSecret, apiKey, password, webhookSecret) are masked in API responses and emitted to environment variables at codegen time.

__InvoiceCapabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags for an InvoiceProvider. Each flag advertises what the underlying provider can do behind this named entry; the framework gates design-time bindings accordingly and the runtime adapter refuses calls outside the advertised set. Defaults are derived from the `provider` enum value when this block is omitted. Set a flag to false to intentionally narrow capabilities — e.g. disable collection on an entry whose invoices are settled outside the platform.

InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsFinalization.doc: Provider distinguishes DRAFT from FINALIZED invoices — a finalized invoice is immutable and legally numbered. Providers without it treat every issued invoice as final immediately.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsCollection.doc: Provider can collect payment for the invoice itself (send-and-collect or charge-automatically flows). When false, the invoice is a document only and money moves through a PaymentProvider or outside the platform.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsCreditNotes.doc: Provider can issue credit notes / corrective invoices against a finalized invoice.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsPartialPayments.doc: Provider tracks partial payments against an invoice balance rather than a single paid/unpaid flag.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsCustomerBalance.doc: Provider keeps a per-customer running balance (credits, overpayments) that invoices can draw on.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsVoid.doc: Provider can VOID a finalized invoice (a legal cancellation that keeps the number). When false, correction happens through credit notes or deletion of drafts only.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsPdfRendering.doc: Provider renders a PDF document for the invoice that the framework can fetch and store/serve.
InvoiceCapabilities.__supportsNumbering.doc: Provider owns the legal invoice-number sequence. When false, the framework's own numbering (`invoicing.configuration.numbering`) is authoritative and the number is pushed to the provider.
InvoiceCapabilities.__webhookStyle.doc: Signature verification style used by this provider's inbound webhooks, when it has any. Values: 'hmac' (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, shared secret — stripe), 'signature' (custom signature scheme), 'none' (no webhook surface — state advances by polling or synchronous responses; internal, the Turkish ERP adapters and all bridge brands). Defaults per `provider` enum value.

__InvoiceProviderType.doc.#: Identifies the invoice provider backend. NATIVE brands (internal, stripe, logoIsbasi, mikro, parasut, custom) map to framework-owned adapters and carry their credentials in the entry's `configuration`; BRIDGE brands (sap, dynamics365, netsuite, logoTiger) issue invoices on an enterprise platform through the mcpbff bridge — they carry NO credentials here and instead REQUIRE `integrationName` to point at a `projectSettings.enterpriseIntegrationsSettings` entry.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.internal: Built-in invoicing — the framework issues, numbers, finalizes and stores invoices itself, with PDF rendering through the pdf template family. No credentials; the default, and the implicit binding when a data object's `invoicing.configuration.providerName` is null.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.stripe: Stripe Invoicing — draft/finalize/send/void through the Stripe invoice API, collection via the linked Stripe account, state advanced by webhooks.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.sap: SAP billing (S/4HANA / ECC) — BRIDGE brand: invoices are created on the SAP platform named by `integrationName`; the mcpbff bridge owns connectivity and credentials.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.dynamics365: Microsoft Dynamics 365 invoices — BRIDGE brand via `integrationName`; the mcpbff bridge owns connectivity and credentials.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.netsuite: Oracle NetSuite invoicing — BRIDGE brand via `integrationName` (anticipated connector — accepted at design time, the bridge answers 501 until it ships).
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.logoTiger: Logo Tiger ERP (on-prem) — BRIDGE brand via `integrationName`; reached through the enterprise integration's connectivity, never directly from services.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.logoIsbasi: Logo Isbasi (cloud) — native REST adapter; e-invoice / e-archive issuance for the Turkish market. Credentials: clientId, clientSecret, firmId.
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.mikro: Mikro Yazilim — native REST adapter for Mikro's cloud API. Credentials: baseUrl, apiKey (+ optional companyCode).
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.parasut: Parasut — native REST adapter; Turkish SMB invoicing (e-invoice / e-archive through Parasut's own operator). Credentials: clientId, clientSecret, companyId (+ optional username/password for the password grant).
__InvoiceProviderType.doc.custom: Escape hatch — designer supplies `baseUrl` (+ optional apiKey) and capability overrides. For in-house invoicing services or adapters that don't have a dedicated native implementation yet.

__InvoiceWebhookStyle.doc.#: Signature verification style used by an invoice provider's inbound webhooks. The adapter uses this hint at verification time to pick the right signing primitive — or to know there is no webhook surface at all.
__InvoiceWebhookStyle.doc.hmac: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body, shared secret in the configuration. Default for stripe.
__InvoiceWebhookStyle.doc.none: No webhook surface — invoice state advances by polling or synchronous API responses. Default for internal, the Turkish ERP adapters (logoIsbasi, mikro, parasut), custom, and every bridge brand.

__FiscalProvidersSettings.doc: Container for fiscal provider configurations - the integrators that submit documents into a government's fiscal infrastructure (e-invoice, e-archive, real-time reporting). They serve the project's fiscalization-enabled data objects: each entry is a named provider that can be referenced by DataObject `fiscalization` opt-ins (`fiscalization.configuration.fiscalProviderName`). Fiscalization is a SEPARATE axis from both payment and invoicing: a PaymentProvider moves money, an InvoiceProvider produces the commercial billing document, and a FiscalProvider is the regulatory transport - one object can bind checkout to Stripe, invoicing to a local ERP and fiscalization to a Turkish special integrator at the same time. There is NO internal brand: fiscalization always goes through an integrator or the credential-free `mock` adapter, and a null `fiscalProviderName` binds implicitly ONLY when exactly one entry is declared. Every brand is NATIVE - fiscal integrators are SaaS APIs, so there is no bridge family and no `integrationName` on an entry - and the generator emits FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* environment variables per provider so service code can construct an adapter at runtime. Mirrors the invoiceProvidersSettings shape - a named array; multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two Foriba accounts for two seller companies).

FiscalProvidersSettings.__fiscalProviders.doc: List of configured fiscal providers. Add one entry per fiscalization backend / account the project can submit documents through. Multiple entries can share the same provider type (e.g. two Foriba accounts for two seller companies). Unlike invoice providers there is NO built-in internal brand: fiscalization always talks to a government fiscal infrastructure through an integrator (or the mock adapter in non-production environments), so a data object's `fiscalProviderName` binds implicitly only when exactly one entry is declared.

__FiscalProvider.doc:
A named fiscal provider configuration. The `name` is the lookup key used by `DataObject.fiscalization.configuration.fiscalProviderName` and the env-var prefix (e.g. `mainForiba` → `FISCAL_PROVIDER_MAINFORIBA_*`). The `provider` enum selects the backend adapter (v1 is Turkey-first: elogo, foriba, nilvera, izibiz and uyumsoft all ship adapters; plus mock and custom); `network` names the government fiscal infrastructure the adapter talks to and is informational plus validation input — the Turkish integrators serve GIB. Credentials live in `configuration`, a free-form key/value list whose required keys depend on the chosen `provider` (the UI and the agent ontology doc enforce the per-provider shape). Secret keys are masked in API responses and emitted to FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_<KEY> env vars at codegen time.

Expected configuration keys per provider:
- elogo: username, password, environment (optional, test or production), baseUrl (optional override)
- foriba: clientId, clientSecret (the Sovos Indirect Tax API OAuth2 app pair - Foriba is Sovos Turkey), environment (optional, test or production), baseUrl (optional override)
- nilvera: apiKey, environment (optional), baseUrl (optional override)
- izibiz: username, password, senderAlias (optional), environment (optional, test or production), baseUrl (optional override)
- uyumsoft: username, password, senderAlias (optional), environment (optional, test or production), baseUrl (optional override)
- mock: (none — accepts everything, records submissions, for development and test projects)
- custom: baseUrl, apiKey (optional)

EVERY brand also accepts the project's own SELLER IDENTITY, all optional and all NON-SECRET: sellerTaxId (Turkey: VKN), sellerName (unvan), sellerAddress (adres), sellerDistrict (ilçe) and sellerCity (il), emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SELLER_TAX_ID / _SELLER_NAME / _SELLER_ADDRESS / _SELLER_DISTRICT / _SELLER_CITY. sellerDistrict and sellerCity matter more than they look: UBL-TR makes cbc:CitySubdivisionName and cbc:CityName MANDATORY PostalAddress members (Uyumsoft's schema validation refused the first live document without them); when unset the document builder falls back to a documented generic default ('Merkez' + the country context) so the XML stays schema-valid, but production documents should carry the real values. The seller identity is one fact per project, it must equal the authenticated integrator account's own identity, and it varies per environment - a sandbox account's tax id is not the production one - so it lives with the credentials that select the account rather than on every fiscalized DataObject, the way a sender identity lives on a mail account. A tax id is PUBLIC information: these keys are catalogued secret:false and are never masked in API responses. A DataObject's fiscalization.configuration.sellerParty still overrides them for the genuine per-row seller case.

EVERY brand also accepts the wire-serial and zero-VAT keys, all NON-SECRET: serialPrefix (REQUIRED for e-Arsiv routes - 3 uppercase letters; the fiscal layer allocates the GIB cbc:ID serial prefix+year+9-digit sequence from it at prepare time and refuses a TR_EARSIV submission with a typed 400 naming the key when it is absent or invalid, before any vendor call), eInvoiceSerialPrefix (REQUIRED for e-Fatura routes - GIB keeps e-Fatura and e-Arsiv on SEPARATE series, so TR_EFATURA documents draw from this second prefix and its own counter; it must differ from serialPrefix, refused at design time with FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED and at submission with a typed 400; a resubmit whose scheme changed takes a fresh serial from the new scheme's series), serialSequenceStart / eInvoiceSerialSequenceStart (optional - the FLOOR of each series' 9-digit sequence for an account whose prefix already issued numbers elsewhere: every allocation takes max(lastNumber, start - 1) + 1, a whole number 1..999999999, refused with a typed 400 naming the key otherwise), serialSequenceStartYear / eInvoiceSerialSequenceStartYear (optional - the 4-digit year each floor belongs to: set, the floor applies only to that year's serials and every other year starts at 1; unset, the floor re-applies every January, which validation WARNS about), serialAssignment (optional - who numbers the documents: "platform", the default, allocates the serial from the counters above; "vendor" lets the integrator number each document at submission, uyumsoft only (mock simulates it), a design-time ERROR on any other brand: cbc:ID then carries only the series prefix (empty = the account's default series), no counter is kept, the floors are ignored, and the number the integrator answers becomes the document's documentSerial; never mix the two in one series, and define the prefix at the integrator first), plus vatExemptionReasonCode / vatExemptionReason (the TaxExemptionReason pair GIB requires on zero-amount 0015 KDV buckets; the builder defaults to 350 with the official GIB text of the code when unset; a line's own code from InvoiceLineRelation.vatExemptionCodeProperty wins). Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SERIAL_PREFIX / _SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START / _SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START_YEAR / _E_INVOICE_SERIAL_PREFIX / _E_INVOICE_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START / _E_INVOICE_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START_YEAR / _SERIAL_ASSIGNMENT / _VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON_CODE / _VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON.

The `capabilities` block reflects what the underlying provider and network can do — its defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time, advanced users can narrow them per-entry. A serialPrefix belongs to exactly ONE service: the counter behind it lives in the emitting service's own database, so two services sharing an entry (and therefore a prefix) silently keep two counters for one vendor-side series. Validation refuses that shape (FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED). The exception is an entry with serialAssignment "vendor" (uyumsoft, mock): the integrator numbers its documents and the platform keeps no counter, so several services may bind it (a serialAssignment left blank for deploy time is judged as platform numbering). A per-environment `_envValueOverlay` row on serialAssignment whose value is anything other than "vendor" cancels that exemption, so the shared entry is refused again with FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED. At runtime the build records the entries bound by several services, and FiscalizationManager answers a typed 400 (FISCAL_SHARED_ENTRY_PLATFORM_NUMBERING_REFUSED) for platform numbering on such an entry, before any serial is allocated. Otherwise declare one entry per fiscalizing service - same brand, same credentials, its own serialPrefix and eInvoiceSerialPrefix, each series registered with the integrator first. Two entries that share ANY prefix (either key against either key) on one account are one series and are refused the same way, unless BOTH entries are vendor-numbered (a vendor-numbered entry and a platform-numbered entry on one series stay refused).

FiscalProvider.__name.doc: Unique provider identifier within the project. Used as the lookup key from DataObject `fiscalization` opt-ins and as the env-var prefix. Must be a valid codeName.
FiscalProvider.name: String
FiscalProvider.__provider.doc: The backend provider implementation. Selects which keys are expected in `configuration` and which adapter the runtime constructs. v1 is Turkey-first: `elogo`, `foriba`, `nilvera`, `izibiz` and `uyumsoft` are GIB-facing integrators with shipped adapters; `mock` is the credential-free development adapter; `custom` is the escape hatch for an in-house fiscal gateway.
FiscalProvider.__network.doc: The government fiscal infrastructure this entry submits into (informational plus validation input — the adapter, not the blueprint, owns the wire protocol). The Turkish integrators (elogo, foriba, nilvera, izibiz, uyumsoft) serve GIB; a mismatched pairing is reported as a warning. Leave null for mock and custom entries, or when the adapter's own default applies.
FiscalProvider.__capabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags. Defaults are derived from `provider` at codegen time so designers don't fill them; advanced users can narrow them per-entry (e.g. disable cancellation on an entry used only for archival reporting). Designers should leave this null unless intentionally restricting features the provider would otherwise support.
FiscalProvider.__configuration.doc: Free-form key/value list of provider-specific credentials and settings. The required keys depend on `provider` — see the FiscalProvider doc string for the per-provider key list. The UI enforces the right form fields per provider; agents emit only keys that match. Sensitive keys (password, apiKey) are masked in API responses and emitted to environment variables at codegen time. The catalogued sellerTaxId / sellerName / sellerAddress / sellerDistrict / sellerCity keys carry the project's OWN seller identity for the documents this account issues; they are deliberately NOT secret - a tax id is public information, and masking it would only make it unreadable in the panel. The keys serialPrefix (GIB wire-serial prefix, required for TR routes) and vatExemptionReasonCode / vatExemptionReason (the zero-VAT TaxExemptionReason pair, defaulting to 350 with the official GIB text 'Diğerleri') are likewise catalogued non-secret on every brand.

__FiscalCapabilities.doc: Per-entry capability flags for a FiscalProvider. Each flag advertises what the provider and its network can do behind this named entry; the framework gates design-time bindings accordingly and the runtime adapter refuses calls outside the advertised set. Defaults are derived from the `provider` enum value when this block is omitted. The three MODE flags (clearance / exchange / reporting) are independent on purpose — one entry can serve several regimes, and the jurisdiction policy routes each document to a mode per its own rules (Turkey is itself hybrid: the same integrator entry produces an EXCHANGE route for registered e-invoice buyers and a REPORTING route for everyone else).

FiscalCapabilities.__supportsClearance.doc: The authority approves the document BEFORE it is valid (clearance regimes: DIAN, NF-e). The pipeline must wait for approval before treating the document as issued.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsExchange.doc: The document travels to the recipient THROUGH the network (exchange regimes: Turkish e-invoice, SdI, KSeF). Delivery is part of the fiscal flow, not a separate email.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsReporting.doc: Document data is reported TO the authority after issuance (reporting regimes: Turkish e-archive, NAV). The document itself reaches the buyer outside the network.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsValidation.doc: Provider can pre-validate a document against the network's schema and business rules before submission.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsSigning.doc: Provider applies the legally required signature or seal itself. When false, the framework must deliver a signed document — v1 relies on providers that sign (integrators do), and direct-to-authority signing with a local HSM is out of scope.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsCancellation.doc: Provider can cancel an accepted document through the network's cancellation or objection flow.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsCreditNote.doc: Provider can submit credit notes / corrective documents referencing an accepted document.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsStatusQuery.doc: Provider can be POLLED for document status. In the GIB world polling is the norm and webhooks the exception — the fiscal status cron drives the FSM for entries with this flag.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsInboundDocuments.doc: Provider can fetch documents ADDRESSED TO the seller (incoming invoices). Opt-in, default false. Node.js uyumsoft implements it (inbox polling of decided documents); the other brands and the java / dotnet uyumsoft adapters answer inbound polling as unsupported.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsArchiving.doc: Provider offers legally compliant long-term archiving of submitted documents.
FiscalCapabilities.__supportsBuyerLookup.doc: Provider can answer whether a tax id belongs to a registered network user (Turkey: is the buyer an e-invoice taxpayer?). The heart of Turkish routing — without it the policy falls back to reporting-mode for every buyer.
FiscalCapabilities.__webhookStyle.doc: Signature verification style used by this provider's inbound webhooks, when it has any. Values: 'hmac' (HMAC over the raw body, shared secret), 'signature' (custom signature scheme), 'none' (no webhook surface — state advances by polling; the norm for GIB integrators). Defaults per `provider` enum value.

__FiscalProviderType.doc.#: Identifies the fiscal provider backend. v1 is Turkey-first: nearly all Turkish e-invoicing goes through OZEL ENTEGRATOR (special integrator) APIs rather than direct GIB portals, so the roster is the common integrator set plus the credential-free mock and the custom escape hatch. Every brand is NATIVE — fiscal integrators are SaaS APIs, so there is no bridge family and no integrationName on this entry. All five integrator brands ship adapters (Faz 3d: elogo, foriba, nilvera in wave 1; izibiz, uyumsoft in wave 2). Additional brands (efinans, edm) follow on demand: a brand added to the enum before its adapter ships is DECLARABLE - the blueprint accepts it, binding a data object to it is a typed runtime error, and its credential keys are re-verified against the integrator's current API documentation when the adapter lands.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.elogo: eLogo — Logo Yazilim's GIB-facing integrator for Turkish e-invoice and e-archive. Completes the Logo story across the two families: logoTiger/logoIsbasi are INVOICE providers (the commercial system of record), elogo is the FISCAL transport of the same company. The adapter speaks the vendor's real SOAP surface (PostBoxService.svc, session in the body). Credentials: username, password. Wave-1 adapter, reworked to the real vendor surface.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.foriba: Foriba (Sovos Turkey) - GIB-facing integrator for Turkish e-invoice and e-archive. The adapter speaks the modern Sovos Indirect Tax API (REST, OAuth2 client_credentials; Foriba has been Sovos since 2019). Credentials: clientId, clientSecret. Wave-1 adapter, reworked to the real vendor surface.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.nilvera: Nilvera — GIB-facing integrator with a modern REST API for Turkish e-invoice and e-archive. Credentials: apiKey. Wave-1 adapter ships.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.izibiz: IZIBIZ — GIB-facing integrator for Turkish e-invoice and e-archive. Credentials: username, password (+ optional senderAlias). Wave-2 adapter ships.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.uyumsoft: Uyumsoft — GIB-facing integrator for Turkish e-invoice and e-archive. Credentials: username, password (+ optional senderAlias). Wave-2 adapter ships.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.mock: Mock adapter — no credentials, records submissions and answers status queries deterministically. For development, test projects and CI. Its outcome is selected by the entry's `configuration.behavior`, or per document by `metadata.__mockFiscalScenario`: `accept` (the default - every document is accepted), `reject`, `pending` (resolved later by the status poll), `fail` (the FIRST submit the service process serves fails with a provider error and every later one is accepted, so a `failed` document is reachable and its resubmit has a success branch; a restart re-arms it) and `failAlways`. A `failed` fiscal document is reachable no other way.
__FiscalProviderType.doc.custom: Escape hatch — designer supplies `baseUrl` (+ optional apiKey) and capability overrides. For in-house fiscal gateways or integrators without a dedicated native implementation yet.

__FiscalNetworkType.doc.#: The government fiscal infrastructure a FiscalProvider entry submits into. Informational plus validation input: the adapter owns the wire protocol, the jurisdiction policy owns the routing rules, and this value lets design-time validation catch a provider paired with a network it does not serve.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.GIB: Turkey — the GIB revenue administration: e-invoice (exchange) and e-archive (reporting).
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.SDI: Italy — Sistema di Interscambio: FatturaPA exchange.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.KSEF: Poland — Krajowy System e-Faktur: structured invoice exchange.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.ZATCA: Saudi Arabia — FATOORA platform: clearance and reporting by document type.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.DIAN: Colombia — DIAN: pre-clearance of electronic invoices.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.IRP: India — Invoice Registration Portal: IRN clearance.
__FiscalNetworkType.doc.NAV: Hungary — the NAV online invoice system: real-time invoice data reporting.

__FiscalWebhookStyle.doc.#: Signature verification style used by a fiscal provider's inbound webhooks. The adapter uses this hint at verification time to pick the right signing primitive — or to know there is no webhook surface at all.
__FiscalWebhookStyle.doc.hmac: HMAC over the raw request body, shared secret in the configuration.
__FiscalWebhookStyle.doc.none: No webhook surface — document state advances by polling (the fiscal status cron) or synchronous API responses. The norm for GIB integrators, and the default for mock and custom.

__EventNotification.doc: Defines a single event-triggered notification within the project. The trigger is either a Kafka topic (triggerSource='kafka', the default — eventDataSettings.channel names the topic) or a geofence crossing (triggerSource='geofence' — geofenceTrigger names the fences + action). Delivered as email, SMS, push, telegram, whatsapp, or in-app message depending on jobType. Both MScript condition slots, the event-level eventDataSettings.condition and each NotificationTarget.condition, evaluate against the SAME null-normalized receiver: `this.payload`, `this.dataSource`, `this.old`, `this.actor` and `this.metadata` each read as an empty object when the event does not carry them, and a chain rooted at one of those five is null-safe at every link past the root, so a missing-data read evaluates as `undefined` at ANY DEPTH instead of throwing. That can change whether the notification fires, so see eventDataSettings.condition before relying on it. A chain rooted at a declared member is null-safe at EVERY link past the root, so `this.dataSource.owner.tier` on an event with no `owner` folds to `undefined` and answers false - a silent skip, with nothing recorded. On the nodejs listener only a chain rooted OUTSIDE those five members (`this.target.isPublic`, `this.data.owner.id`) still throws, and only that case is recorded as a failed delivery. Which reads fail rather than fold is a per-listener property and not portable: see the LANGUAGE NOTE on eventDataSettings.condition before relying on the failure row.

EventNotification.__eventNotificationBasics.doc: Basic properties of the event notification, including its name, description, storage behavior, and job type.
EventNotification.__eventDataSettings.doc: Settings for how the notification extracts and processes data from the incoming event. For triggerSource='kafka' the channel field names the topic. For triggerSource='geofence' the channel is auto-derived by the factory and the data source is the synthetic crossing payload.
EventNotification.__geofenceTrigger.doc: Required when triggerSource='geofence'. Names the fences + action that drive this notification.
EventNotification.__targets.doc: A list of NotificationTarget objects that define how to extract recipients from the rendered data. Each target specifies a path in the notification data where userId/email/phone/handle can be found.
EventNotification.__template.doc: The notification template used to render the notification content. Template variables are the notification metadata keys at TOP LEVEL — the triggering event record's fields addressed directly (`<%= followerFullname %>`, never `<%= data.followerFullname %>`; the bare `data` root exists only in the condition MScript slots, not in templates). See NotificationTemplate for the full scope.
EventNotification.__contentModeration.doc: Decision-moderated outbound content for this notification: objectModeration applied to the RENDERED subject and body. When `enabled`, each distinct rendered content of an event is judged ONCE by a calibrated decision provider before any recipient receives it, on every channel (email, sms, push, inApp, telegram, whatsapp). An `accept` is sent unchanged, a `review` is HELD (nothing sent, nothing stored) in the framework-generated `sys_NotificationModerationReview` object until a reviewer accepts it, and a `reject` is never sent. Optional - omit (or null) when unused.

__EventTriggerSource.doc.#: What kind of event triggers an EventNotification.
__EventTriggerSource.doc.kafka: Real Kafka topic — eventDataSettings.channel names it. Default.
__EventTriggerSource.doc.geofence: Synthetic Kafka topic produced by the notification service when a user device crosses a fence. geofenceTrigger names the fence(s) + action.

__GeofenceTrigger.doc:
Geofence trigger spec — applied to EventNotifications with triggerSource='geofence'. Fences are runtime DATA (managed via the GeoFence DataObject the notification factory emits), not design-time assets, so this block declares a RULE that matches fences at crossing time rather than specific fence names.

Matching pipeline at runtime: per crossing event {action, fence, userId, ...}, the notification handler subscribes by `action` (one Kafka topic per action: enter/exit/dwell), then filters by `fenceTags` (any-of match against the fence record's tags array, when set), then evaluates the optional `fenceFilter` MScript against the fence record, then evaluates the optional `condition` MScript against the full event payload. All filters default to 'match' when null.

GeofenceTrigger.__action.doc: Which crossing kind triggers this notification: enter | exit | dwell. 'dwell' fires after the device has been continuously inside the fence for at least the fence record's dwellSeconds.
GeofenceTrigger.__fenceTags.doc: Optional tag any-of filter. When set, the notification only fires for fences whose `tags` array shares at least one entry with this list. Use for the common case 'notify on entry to a parking-category fence'. Null/empty = match every fence.
GeofenceTrigger.__fenceFilter.doc: Optional MScript filter evaluated against the fence record at crossing time. Available scope: `fence` (the matched GeoFence row), `crossing` ({ userId, deviceId, lat, lng, occurredAt }). Use when fenceTags isn't expressive enough — e.g. `{ "js": "fence.metadata.priority > 5" }`. Null = match.
GeofenceTrigger.__condition.doc: Optional MScript condition evaluated against the full event payload (event + fence + crossing). Mirrors eventDataSettings.condition semantics. Null = match.

__GeofenceTriggerAction.doc.#: What kind of geofence crossing triggers the notification.
__GeofenceTriggerAction.doc.enter: Fires when the device moves from outside the fence to inside.
__GeofenceTriggerAction.doc.exit: Fires when the device moves from inside the fence to outside.
__GeofenceTriggerAction.doc.dwell: Fires after the device has been continuously inside the fence for at least fence.dwellSeconds. Skipped when the fence has no dwellSeconds.

__EventNotificationBasics.doc: Defines the basic properties of an event notification, including its name, description, storage behavior, and job type. This section is used to configure how the notification behaves and what type of message it sends.

EventNotificationBasics.__name.doc: The unique, human-readable name of the event notification. Use one-word camelCase names such as userCreated or orderShipped. For services resolved to Java, authored Kafka listener names and group IDs are limited to 249 Unicode code points; longer values are refused at design time before Spring listener startup. This Java-specific bound does not refuse other service languages or unresolved contexts.
EventNotificationBasics.__description.doc: A brief explanation of the event notification's purpose and scope.
EventNotificationBasics.__isStored.doc: Determines whether the notification should be stored in the database for future reference. If true, notifications are saved and can be listed in the frontend. If false, they are only sent during the request lifecycle and are not retained.
EventNotificationBasics.__jobType.doc: The type of notification to send: email, sms, push, telegram, whatsapp, or inApp. A whatsapp notification sends free-form text unless its template declares `whatsappTemplate` (see NotificationTemplate.whatsappTemplate): free-form WhatsApp is delivered only inside the 24-hour customer-service window, so a business-initiated whatsapp notification (order, shipment, refund, OTP) needs an approved template. An email, sms, push, telegram or whatsapp notification in a project that declares no provider of that channel still builds: it sends to the channel's built-in sink on every deployment, and project validation warns once per channel (MAIL_ / SMS_ / PUSH_ / TELEGRAM_ / WHATSAPP_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK).
EventNotificationBasics.__actionDeepLink.doc: An MScript expression that generates a deep link for client-side actions. The frontend can use this to navigate or perform custom logic when the user interacts with the notification. Leave null for no integration case.
EventNotificationBasics.__actionText.doc: An MScript expression defining the display text for the action deep link in the frontend interface. Leave null for no integration case.
EventNotificationBasics.__fromUser.doc: An MScript expression identifying the sender of the notification (e.g., for inApp messages or email 'from' fields).
EventNotificationBasics.__dedupKey.doc: An optional MScript expression that names WHAT this notification is about, for the delivery dedup gate of the Node.js notification listener. Before every delivery (a provider send, or the stored in-app row) the listener claims the identity (notification name, channel, recipient, dedup key) in Redis with SET NX and a TTL; a second claim of the same identity inside the window is logged and skipped, so a redelivered event does not send twice. Leave it null to use the event envelope id, which stops exactly the redelivery of one event. Set it to deduplicate across events, e.g. `data.orderId + ':shipped'` sends the shipped notice once per order and recipient even when two events announce it. It is evaluated once per event, after the DataView read and includeData, with the same `this` and `data` as the condition; a null, empty or throwing value falls back to the envelope id. A constant value would suppress every later event for the same recipient for the whole window. The window is the NOTIFICATION_DEDUP_TTL_SECONDS env var of the notification service (default 86400 = 24 h, 0 turns the gate off). When Redis is unavailable the gate fails open: it delivers and logs a warning. A failed send gives its claim back. Other service languages do not apply it yet (NOTIF_DEDUP_KEY_NOT_EMITTED).
EventNotificationBasics.name: String
EventNotificationBasics.__triggerSource.doc: What triggers this notification. 'kafka' (default) — a real Kafka topic named in eventDataSettings.channel (typically a DB-event topic from another service). 'geofence' — a user device entering/exiting/dwelling inside one of the named fences in geofenceTrigger.fenceNames. The factory auto-derives eventDataSettings.channel for geofence events; designers do not set it.
EventNotificationBasics.__providerName.doc: Optional override of the default notification provider for this event. When set, must match an entry in projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name with kind compatible with eventNotificationBasics.jobType. When null, the matching default*ProviderName from NotificationServiceOptions is used.

__EventDataSettings.doc: Defines how the event notification extracts and processes data from incoming Kafka messages. This includes the data source, paths to relevant information, and any additional data to include in the notification.

EventDataSettings.__channel.doc: The Kafka topic name that will trigger this notification. The notification manager listens on this channel.
EventDataSettings.__condition.doc: An optional MScript condition to determine whether the notification should be triggered, based on the incoming Kafka message payload. To access data from both data source and the received Kafka event, use `this.dataSource`. The receiver carries exactly five members, `this.payload`, `this.dataSource`, `this.old`, `this.actor` and `this.metadata`, and it is NULL-NORMALIZED before the expression runs: a member the event does not carry is substituted with an empty object. A chain ROOTED at one of those five is additionally made null-safe at every link past the root (a read of `this.dataSource.owner.tier` on an event with no `owner` yields `undefined` instead of failing; the nodejs listener implements this by splicing optional-chaining into the compiled expression, other listeners by their own null-safe accessor), so a read through absent data reads `undefined` at ANY DEPTH and the expression is EVALUATED on that instead of throwing. Nothing is recorded when that happens: the condition simply answers, and a false answer skips the notification silently, with no NotificationDeliveryLog and no NotificationLog row. Evaluating instead of throwing can flip the answer EITHER WAY, so re-read any event-level condition that reads through `this.dataSource` on an event with no `dataViewName`: `this.dataSource.tier === 'gold'` and `this.dataSource.owner.tier === 'gold'` both fold to false and skip the notification, while a negated or absence-testing condition (`!this.dataSource.blocked`, `!this.dataSource.owner.tier`, `this.dataSource.tier === undefined`) evaluates TRUE and the notification FIRES, where the earlier throw used to suppress it. On the NODEJS listener, only a chain rooted OUTSIDE those five members still throws (`this.target.isPublic`, `this.data.x`). The two BARE bindings (no leading `this.`) differ in this EVENT-LEVEL slot: a bare `target` identifier is not bound at all here — the event-level condition is evaluated BEFORE any target is resolved, so there is no `target` binding here at all, and target-dependent logic belongs in the per-target `condition` slot instead; a bare `data` IS bound here, to `this.dataSource ?? this.payload` (the script root, the same one `includeData` values read). Only the rooted-chain throw case is recorded as a failed NotificationDeliveryLog + NotificationLog row naming the event. LANGUAGE NOTE: the throw-versus-fold boundary is a per-listener property, not a portable guarantee. The null-safe fold landed in the nodejs tree only. The dotnet, rust and golang listeners resolve member reads through a null-safe accessor REGARDLESS of the chain root, so they fold an out-of-contract read to false with no throw and no failed row; dotnet does print a ONE-SHOT runtime warning naming the undeclared member, which is the only trace the skip leaves there, and rust and golang leave none. The python listener is NOT in that group: it applies the same root-keyed boundary as nodejs, so an out-of-contract read RAISES and takes the durable failed-row path. The java listener does not reach a runtime at all - it lowers `this.<member>` to a literal field read against a condition context that declares a fixed set, so an out-of-contract member is a missing symbol and the generated service does not compile. Do not rely on the durable failure row as a portable suppression backstop: write the condition so that its TRUE branch is the one you want on every target language. Three authoring shapes keep throwing as well, because `?.` cannot legally be spliced into them, namely a chain inside a `new` callee or a tagged-template tag, a chain re-entered through parentheses (`(this.dataSource.a).b.c`), and a chain continued past a call (`this.payload.fn().x.y`). CAUTION: the fold keys on the chain ROOT, so a MISSPELLED member deeper in a declared chain (`this.dataSource.ownr.tier`) is indistinguishable from absent data. It reads `undefined`, the condition answers false, and the notification is never sent, with no runtime row and no design-time warning, because the receiver-unknown check (NOTIF_TARGET_CONDITION_RECEIVER_UNKNOWN) inspects chain ROOTS only. That check runs on BOTH condition slots - this one and the per-target one - at the ERROR tier, with the same code and the same reported shape, so a root outside the five members is refused here at design time and never reaches a runtime. A misspelled member DEEPER in a declared chain is a different case and is still not caught, because the root is legitimate. Measured before that tier was raised: the corpus carried 109 event-level condition slots, 54 of them live, and every one of the 54 roots at a declared member, so the refusal rejects nothing that exists. Where an out-of-contract root did already ship, the dotnet listener's one-shot runtime warning is what names it. Spell deep chains against the DataView's own shape.
EventDataSettings.__dataViewName.doc: The name of the data view to use when the data source is 'dataView'.
EventDataSettings.__dataViewIdPathInPayload.doc: The dot-path of the id used to fetch the data view document, resolved against the event RECORD (the unified event envelope's `data` — the same root targetPathInData reads), never against the envelope itself. Defaults to 'id', the record's own id.
EventDataSettings.__includeData.doc: An optional list of key-value mappings to merge additional values into the notification metadata: each entry writes `metadata[name] = value`, where `value` is an MScript evaluated per event against the same receiver as `condition` (`this.payload` is the event record, `this.dataSource` the fetched DataView document when `dataViewName` is set, plus `this.old`, `this.actor`, `this.metadata`; the bare root `data` is `this.dataSource ?? this.payload`). The metadata is the stored Notification row's `metadata` column and the template render scope; the NotificationLog row keeps the entry's value bounded (strings cut at 256 characters, objects reduced to a marker) next to references to the source event, and the NotificationDeliveryLog row carries no metadata, so an entry named `targetType` is read by the template as `<%= targetType %>`. ORDER: the entries are applied AFTER the DataView merge (so a value may read `this.dataSource.<field>`) and BEFORE the `actionDeepLink` / `actionText` slots. An entry whose value evaluates to `null` or `undefined` (or whose script throws; the throw is logged once) removes the key, including any value inherited from the event record. Non-null falsy values (`0`, the empty string and `false`) are preserved. RESERVED NAMES: `_old`, `_actor`, `actionDeepLink`, `actionText` and `dataSource` are framework-managed metadata keys and are rejected at validation (NOTIF_INCLUDE_DATA_RESERVED_KEY). LANGUAGE NOTE: all six active target languages - nodejs, python, rust, golang, java and dotnet - emit these entries through their notification listeners.

__NotificationTemplate.doc: Defines a notification template used to render the content of event notifications. Templates are written in EJS. **Variable scope**: the template's variables are the notification metadata keys at TOP LEVEL — the triggering event RECORD's own fields (the unified envelope's `data`, the very same root `targetPathInData` reads), spread directly into the render scope. Write `<%= followerFullname %>`, NEVER `<%= data.followerFullname %>`: there is no `data` wrapper in templates — the bare `data` root exists only in the condition MScript slots — so a `data.` read throws a ReferenceError at render time, the render degrades to an empty string, and a notification whose subject and body are both empty because of a render error is recorded as a FAILED delivery instead of being sent. Besides the record's fields the scope carries `_old` (the envelope's previous-row image on update/delete db events, else null), `_actor` (the envelope actor, else null), `actionDeepLink`/`actionText` (the evaluated MScript values; each key is absent when its script fails), and — only when `eventDataSettings.dataViewName` is set — `dataSource`, the whole fetched DataView document as ONE nested object (`<%= dataSource.someJoinedField %>`; the record's fields stay at top level beside it). **Required locals**: every free root identifier of the compiled template body is REQUIRED unless the template proves it tolerates absence, either by mentioning it once as a `typeof` operand or by reading it only through the always-bound `locals` object. At render time a required local the bound context does not carry REFUSES the delivery and NAMES it (`renderErrorCode: 'NOTIF_TEMPLATE_MISSING_LOCAL'`, `missingLocals: [...]`), including when only the other slot rendered fine: nothing is sent and nothing is stored. A key bound to null counts as PRESENT, so `_old` never triggers this. At design time the same parse warns `NOTIF_TEMPLATE_ROOT_NOT_IN_CONTEXT` when a required root is neither a framework binding, nor a flat field of the producing event's record, nor a declared `includeData` key. A property the declared DataView projects is NOT a top-level local: the view document is bound only under `dataSource`, so a field the record does not carry is read as `<%= dataSource.<field> %>`, and the warning names that read.

NotificationTemplate.__parser.doc: The template rendering engine. Currently, only 'ejs' is supported.
NotificationTemplate.__name.doc: The unique name of the notification template. This is used to reference the template in event notifications.
NotificationTemplate.__description.doc: A brief description of the template's purpose and usage.
NotificationTemplate.__subjectTemplate.doc: The EJS template text used to generate the notification subject line. Variables are the notification metadata keys at TOP LEVEL — the triggering event record's fields, addressed directly: `<%= followerFullname %>`, never `<%= data.followerFullname %>` (there is no `data` wrapper in templates; an undefined root identifier fails the whole render, and an error-empty render is recorded as a FAILED delivery, nothing is sent). Also available: `_old`, `_actor`, `actionDeepLink`, `actionText`, and `dataSource` (the DataView document) when eventDataSettings.dataViewName is set. Every bare root read here is a REQUIRED local: if the bound context does not carry it the delivery is refused and the local is named, even when the body rendered fine. Guard a genuinely optional local with `typeof someLocal !== 'undefined'`.
NotificationTemplate.__bodyTemplate.doc:
The EJS template text used to generate the notification body content. Variables are the notification metadata keys at TOP LEVEL — the triggering event record's fields, addressed directly: `

<%= followerFullname %> followed you.

`, never `<%= data.followerFullname %>` (there is no `data` wrapper in templates; an undefined root identifier fails the whole render, and an error-empty render is recorded as a FAILED delivery, nothing is sent). Also available: `_old`, `_actor`, `actionDeepLink`, `actionText`, and `dataSource` (the DataView document) when eventDataSettings.dataViewName is set. Every bare root read here is a REQUIRED local: if the bound context does not carry it the delivery is refused and the local is named, even when the subject rendered fine. Guard a genuinely optional local with `typeof someLocal !== 'undefined'`.
NotificationTemplate.__variants.doc: Per-language versions of THIS template. Each variant names a `language` and carries its own `subjectTemplate` / `bodyTemplate`; `subjectTemplate` / `bodyTemplate` on the template itself stay as the MANDATORY whole-template fallback used for every recipient whose language matches no variant. The framework renders each declared variant AT MOST ONCE per event (never once per recipient) and then maps each recipient to a variant by the user's language, so an email carries ONE language instead of both stacked. The recipient's language is read from the auth user record with the fallback chain `preferredLanguage`, `language`, `locale`, `lang` - none of those is a standard auth field, so declare the one you use in `authentication.userProperties[]`. Matching is case-insensitive and falls back from a regional tag to its base (`tr-TR` matches a `tr` variant). Leave empty for a single-language template. The `data-lang` span + regex picker convention is the interim workaround this supersedes.
NotificationTemplate.__whatsappTemplate.doc: The WhatsApp TEMPLATE this notification sends on a jobType='whatsapp' event, instead of the rendered subject/body text. WhatsApp delivers free-form text only inside the 24-hour customer-service window (the 24 hours after the recipient last wrote to you); outside it Meta refuses the message (error 131047) and Twilio refuses it (error 63016) AFTER the API has accepted the request, so a business-initiated notification - order, shipment, refund, OTP - sent as text is recorded as delivered and never arrives. When this block is set the provider sends the approved template: Meta Cloud API sends `{ type: 'template', template: { name, language: { code }, components } }`, Twilio sends `{ contentSid, contentVariables }` with no body. The subject/body templates are still rendered (they are what the notification log and a stored Notification row show) but are not what the recipient receives. A recipient whose language selects a variant that declares its own whatsappTemplate gets that one; every other recipient gets this one, with the language defaulting to the selected variant's language. Ignored on every other jobType (design-time warning WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_IGNORED). A whatsapp notification with no whatsappTemplate here raises the design-time warning WHATSAPP_FREEFORM_OUTSIDE_WINDOW.
NotificationTemplate.__renderPerRecipient.doc: Opt in to rendering this template INSIDE the recipient fan-out, once per recipient, with a `recipient` object (`{ userId, handle, language, channel }`) in template scope.
