The default (false) renders once per event, or once per declared `variants` entry, which is what almost every template wants: language is already handled by `variants`, and a hundred-recipient reminder event pays one render instead of a hundred. Turn this on ONLY for genuine per-recipient personalization (`<%= recipient.userId %>`-keyed content); the template author knowingly pays the N-render cost. `variants` still apply: each recipient renders the variant their language selects.
NotificationTemplate.name: String

NotificationTemplateVariant.__language.doc: The language this variant is written in, as a BCP-47-ish tag: `en`, `tr`, `de`, or a regional tag such as `pt-BR`. Compared case-insensitively against the recipient's language, and a recipient tag falls back to its base subtag (`tr-TR` selects a `tr` variant). Must be unique across the template's variants.
NotificationTemplateVariant.__subjectTemplate.doc: This language's subject line. Same render scope and the same REQUIRED-local rules as the template's own `subjectTemplate`: metadata keys at TOP LEVEL, plus `_old`, `_actor`, `actionDeepLink`, `actionText`, `dataSource`, and `recipient` when `renderPerRecipient` is on. Leave empty only if this language deliberately has no subject - it does NOT fall back to the template's subject, because variant selection is WHOLE-TEMPLATE (a recipient gets this variant's two slots or the fallback's two slots, never one of each).
NotificationTemplateVariant.__bodyTemplate.doc: This language's body. Same render scope and the same REQUIRED-local rules as the template's own `bodyTemplate`. Leave empty only if this language deliberately has no body - it does NOT fall back to the template's body, because variant selection is WHOLE-TEMPLATE.
NotificationTemplateVariant.__whatsappTemplate.doc: This language's WhatsApp template (same shape as NotificationTemplate.whatsappTemplate). Used for recipients whose language selects this variant; its `language` defaults to this variant's `language` (a `-` becomes `_`, so `pt-BR` is sent as `pt_BR`). When a variant declares none, its recipients get the template's own whatsappTemplate with this variant's language as the default code - the usual Meta shape, where ONE template name is approved in several languages. Declare one here when this language uses a different template name or a different Twilio Content SID.

__NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.doc: An approved WhatsApp template for a jobType='whatsapp' EventNotification: the Meta template name or the Twilio Content SID, its language, and the parameter scripts. Business-initiated WhatsApp messages must be template messages: free-form text is delivered only inside the 24-hour customer-service window. `components` and `contentVariables` are MScripts evaluated ONCE per event, against the same receiver as eventDataSettings.includeData (`this.payload` the event record, `this.dataSource` the DataView document when dataViewName is set, `this.old`, `this.actor`, `this.metadata` - the finished notification metadata, includeData entries included - and the bare root `data` = `this.dataSource ?? this.payload`). A script that throws, or that returns a value of the wrong shape, fails the delivery visibly (failed NotificationDeliveryLog + NotificationLog rows naming the slot); nothing is sent as free-form text in its place. Only the slot the provider reads is used: Meta reads name / language / components, Twilio reads name / contentVariables. LANGUAGE NOTE: implemented by the nodejs and dotnet notification listeners and providers; the other language targets still send free-form text.

NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__name.doc: The template to send. For a Meta WhatsApp Cloud API provider (provider='whatsapp') this is the APPROVED template name as registered in WhatsApp Manager: lower-case letters, digits and underscores only (`^[a-z0-9_]+$`, e.g. `order_shipped`). For a Twilio provider (provider='twilio') it is the Content SID of the approved content template: `HX` followed by 32 lower-case hex digits (`^HX[0-9a-f]{32}$`). Case-sensitive and never rewritten (it is NOT a codeName). The format is checked at design time against the event's resolved provider (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME_INVALID, ERROR).
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__language.doc: The Meta template language code, exactly as the template is approved: `en`, `en_US`, `tr`, `pt_BR`. Optional. When empty it defaults to the language of the variant the recipient selected (with `-` turned into `_`), and to `en` for a recipient served by the template's own block with no variant. Twilio ignores it: a Content SID already names one language.
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__components.doc: Meta only. An MScript returning the template's `components` array, e.g. `[{ type: 'body', parameters: [{ type: 'text', text: this.payload.orderNumber }] }]`. The positional shorthand is accepted too: an array of plain values (`[this.payload.customerName, this.payload.orderNumber]`) is sent as the BODY text parameters {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in order. Leave empty for a template without parameters. Evaluated once per event (see NotificationWhatsAppTemplate for the scope).
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__contentVariables.doc: Twilio only. An MScript returning the Content API variables object, e.g. `{ '1': this.payload.customerName, '2': this.payload.orderNumber }`; an array is numbered from 1. Sent as `contentVariables: JSON.stringify(value)`. Twilio fills a missing variable from the content template's SAMPLE value, so declare every variable the template uses. Evaluated once per event (see NotificationWhatsAppTemplate for the scope).
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__category.doc: The Meta template category the template is submitted under: `utility` (a transactional update the recipient expects, e.g. an order confirmation), `marketing` (promotions, offers, re-engagement) or `authentication` (one-time passwords). Meta may re-categorise a template on review. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself. Set it together with `body` (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_DOC_INCOMPLETE warns when one is set without the other).
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__body.doc: The Meta-approved BODY text of the template, with positional variables `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, ... numbered from 1 without gaps, e.g. `Your order {{1}} has shipped; it arrives on {{2}}.` The positional `components` shorthand fills them in order. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself. Validation (warnings): the placeholders must be numbered 1..N without gaps (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_PLACEHOLDERS_GAP), `samples` must carry one value per placeholder (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_SAMPLES_MISMATCH), and a positional-shorthand `components` array must carry N values (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_PARAMETER_COUNT_MISMATCH).
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__header.doc: Optional TEXT header of the template, exactly as approved. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself.
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__footer.doc: Optional footer text of the template, exactly as approved. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself.
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__buttons.doc: Optional buttons of the template, in the approved order: quick replies, a URL or a phone number. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself.
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.__samples.doc: One sample value per body placeholder, in `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, ... order (Meta requires a sample for every variable when the template is submitted), e.g. `["B261009-3LHPJQ", "530,00 TL"]`. Not a credential: printed verbatim in the DevOps guide. DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this field documents the template for its submission to Meta and is printed in the project's DevOps guide; it is NOT sent at runtime, because Meta renders the approved text itself.
NotificationWhatsAppTemplate.name: String

__WhatsAppTemplateButton.doc: One button of an approved WhatsApp template (Meta). DOCUMENTATION ONLY: printed in the project's DevOps guide for the template's submission to Meta; never sent at runtime.

WhatsAppTemplateButton.__type.doc: The button type: `quick_reply` (a reply button carrying `text`), `url` (opens `url`) or `phone_number` (calls `phoneNumber`).
WhatsAppTemplateButton.__text.doc: The button label, exactly as approved.
WhatsAppTemplateButton.__url.doc: `url` buttons only: the target URL as approved (a dynamic URL may end in `{{1}}`).
WhatsAppTemplateButton.__phoneNumber.doc: `phone_number` buttons only: the number to call, in international format (e.g. `+905551112233`).

__WhatsAppTemplateCategory.doc.utility: A transactional update the recipient expects (order, shipment, account notices).

__WhatsAppTemplateButtonType.doc.#: The type of a WhatsApp template button.
__WhatsAppTemplateButtonType.doc.quick_reply: A reply button; the tap is delivered back as an inbound message.

__NotificationTarget.doc: Defines a recipient or list of recipients for an event notification. Targets are derived from the notification data and can be conditional. By default `targetKind: 'userId'` resolves to an authenticated user and the system looks up the user's email/phone/devices via auth-service. Set `targetKind` to one of `email` / `phoneNumber` / `whatsappPhone` / `telegramHandle` / `deviceToken` when the resolved value at `targetPathInData` is already the direct contact handle — typically when notifying non-users (leads, opted-in subscribers, etc.) whose contact details live in the application database, not the auth user table. The AUDIENCE kinds `role` / `userGroup` address a set of users instead of a payload-sourced value: `targetValue` names a declared role value or user group, the notification service asks the auth service (M2M) for the matching users at delivery time, and each resolved user then follows the normal `userId` delivery path (dedup across targets included).

NotificationTarget.__targetName.doc: A unique, human-readable name for the target. Use camelCase (e.g., 'customer', 'internalApprovers'). A blank value (empty or whitespace-only) is the UNSET state: the notification layer trims before reading it, so a name of `' '` behaves exactly like no name at all rather than as a genuinely-set target name. The same blank-is-unset rule applies to `targetPathInData`, `targetValue`, `targetUserIdInArrayTargetItem` and `targetItemNameInArray`. Normalizing the name never affects the target itself: its `condition` gate is bound to the target by POSITION, not by name, so a blank-named (or duplicate-named) target still evaluates its OWN condition and is still skipped when that condition is false.
NotificationTarget.__targetKind.doc: What kind of recipient this target declares. Default 'userId' — the value at `targetPathInData` is an application user id and email/phone/devices are looked up via auth-service. The direct-handle kinds skip the user lookup and treat the resolved value as the contact handle. The audience kinds 'role' / 'userGroup' ignore `targetPathInData` entirely: `targetValue` names a declared role value or user group name, and the delivery-time fan-out resolves it to user ids via the auth service (M2M). Must be compatible with the parent EventNotification's `jobType`: jobType 'email' accepts userId|email; 'sms' accepts userId|phoneNumber; 'push' accepts userId|deviceToken; 'telegram' accepts userId|telegramHandle; 'whatsapp' accepts userId|whatsappPhone; 'role' and 'userGroup' resolve to user ids and are accepted by every jobType (like userId).
NotificationTarget.__targetPathInData.doc: The path to the contact handle(s) inside the notification's data. **The root is the event RECORD, not the wire envelope**: the generated listener unwraps the unified event envelope — `record = event.data` — before reading this path, so NEVER prefix it with `data.`. A `data.` prefix reads through a second, non-existent envelope, resolves to `undefined`, and the notification silently targets nobody. What the record holds depends on the producer: for a topic published by a `PublishEventAction` it is the authored message object (address its keys directly), for a db-event topic it is the row, for an API-event topic it is the API's result record. This is the opposite binding from an AIAgent `kafkaController.dataMapping`, which is handed the RAW wire message and therefore does read `message.data.<key>`. When the notification declares `eventDataSettings.dataViewName`, the root is the fetched DataView document instead. In the shared vocabulary this surface is read scope 'record', the same scope as a BusinessApi Kafka controller's `requestParameters[].dataPath` and as an AIAgent `kafkaController` with NO `dataMapping`; only an AIAgent `kafkaController` that DOES declare a `dataMapping` is read scope 'envelope'. See the Kafka-topics reference page for the full wire-vs-reader table, or ask the `getKafkaEventPayloadStructure` tool, whose every answer returns it as `consumerBindings`. When `targetKind: 'userId'`, the value is a user id (single or array). Otherwise the value is the direct contact handle (email address / E.164 phone / @telegramHandle / device token). For nested objects use `prop1.prop2.prop3` notation. Required for every payload-sourced kind; leave it null for the audience kinds `role`/`userGroup`, which take their audience from `targetValue` instead and ignore this path. VALUE SHAPES the resolver accepts, at every read site (the scalar value, an array item that is its own value, a per-item path inside an object item, and the direct-handle mapper): a non-empty STRING is taken as-is, and a WHOLE NUMBER within +/-2^53 is stringified, so a numeric primary key resolves. Booleans, objects, arrays, NaN/Infinity and non-integers are REJECTED and the target resolves nobody. An id BEYOND 2^53 is rejected too, and must be published as a STRING: JSON parsing rounds such a number before any handler sees it, so the digits that arrive are not the digits that were sent. On a rejection the target contributes no recipient and the notification is recorded as a delivery FAILURE; the offending shape is named in the service LOG line, not in the stored row. Point this path at the scalar id or handle field, never at the object that contains it. PORTING STATUS: only the nodejs listener implements this contract today. Six of the eight service trees have a notification target resolver at all; rust and mcpbff have no notification layer. The java, python, golang and php listeners are string-only, so a numeric id resolves nobody there and the target fails visibly, exactly as an unresolvable path does. The dotnet listener is NOT a second implementation of this contract, and it is the one tree where a numeric id is actively unsafe rather than merely unsupported: its handler unwraps the whole wire payload through the shared JS-shaped request-bag unwrap before any target is read, and that unwrap boxes EVERY JSON number as a double on purpose, so the listener never sees the raw token. A whole number within 2^53 does resolve there, matching nodejs. An id BEYOND 2^53 has already been rounded by that unwrap, and dotnet then ACCEPTS the rounded value instead of rejecting it, so the notification is delivered to a NEIGHBOURING id (a real, different user in a sequential-integer schema) rather than recorded as a failure. A non-integer is accepted there too, and rendered under the process culture. Publish ids as STRINGS: that is the only shape all six listeners agree on.
NotificationTarget.__isArray.doc: Indicates whether the target path contains a list of contact handles. If true, the notification will be sent to each entry in the array.
NotificationTarget.__targetItemNameInArray.doc: If the target is an array, the path to the ARRAY CONTAINER - the array itself - inside the notification data. Despite the name this is NOT a per-item property name: declaring it makes targetPathInData the path read INSIDE each item, so targetItemNameInArray: 'members' with targetPathInData: 'memberUserId' reads members[].memberUserId. Leave it empty when targetPathInData already points at the array; the items are then the user ids / contact handles themselves, unless targetUserIdInArrayTargetItem names the id property inside each item.
NotificationTarget.__targetUserIdInArrayTargetItem.doc: When `targetKind: 'userId'` and `isArray: true`, this is the property name inside each item that holds the user id. Ignored when targetKind is not 'userId'.
NotificationTarget.__condition.doc: An MScript expression evaluated ONCE PER TARGET, never per array item. For isArray targets, target is the whole array; use itemCondition to filter individual recipients. It determines whether the notification should be sent to this target, based on the target data. Access the target data using `target` (without `this`) and data source using `this.dataSource`. The `this` receiver is the same five null-normalized members the event-level eventDataSettings.condition gets, with the same null-safe-to-any-depth fold for chains rooted at one of them, so read that slot's description before relying on a missing-data read: the fold makes the condition ANSWER FALSE and skip this target silently, it does not record a delivery failure. Reading a member the receiver does not have is a misdeclaration, and design-time validation REFUSES it: NOTIF_TARGET_CONDITION_RECEIVER_UNKNOWN is an ERROR on this slot, not a warning, so a condition rooted at anything outside the five members does not build. The tier was raised on a measured census over every committed blueprint - 187 targets, 174 per-target condition slots, and zero rooted outside the five members - and it exists because what the read DOES at runtime is not portable and cannot be made portable without forking the shared MScript accessor per language. What every listener agrees on is only that the target is NEVER SENT while the read stands; HOW that happens is a property of the listener. A plain comparison against such a member (`this.target`, `this.data`) reads `undefined` and folds to false, so the target is skipped silently. A deeper read through one (`this.target.isPublic`, `this.data.owner.id`) fails condition evaluation on the nodejs and python listeners, which record a failed per-target delivery; on java the same read does not COMPILE at all, because `this.<member>` lowers to a field the listener's condition context does not declare; and on the null-safe listeners (dotnet, rust, golang) it folds to false and the target is skipped instead, and dotnet additionally logs a one-shot runtime warning naming the member so the skip leaves a trace to find, while rust and golang leave none. The same read through a DECLARED member (`this.dataSource.owner.tier`) is null-safe at every link past the root and simply answers false. The event-level eventDataSettings.condition slot carries the identical rule - same receiver, same code, same ERROR tier - so neither slot accepts a root the other refuses. See the LANGUAGE NOTE on eventDataSettings.condition: which reads fail rather than fold is a per-listener property, not a portable guarantee.
NotificationTarget.__targetValue.doc: The STATIC audience name for the audience target kinds — ignored (and normally null) for every other kind. For `targetKind: 'role'` this is a declared role VALUE (the literal a session carries in `roleId`): a built-in system role — superAdmin/admin/user in single-tenant projects, superAdmin/saasAdmin/tenantOwner/tenantAdmin/tenantUser/saasUser in multi-tenant projects — or the `value` of a custom RoleItem declared under accessControl.roleSettings. For `targetKind: 'userGroup'` this is a user group's `groupName` (groups are runtime data of the auth service's userGroup object; the name is resolved at delivery time, so `userGroupsActive` must be enabled). Validators reject an unknown role value at design time; an unknown group name surfaces at delivery time as a failed delivery record, never a silent drop.
NotificationTarget.__scope.doc: Tenant scope of an audience (`role`/`userGroup`) target in a MULTI-TENANT project — ignored elsewhere. Default 'tenant': the fan-out resolves users within the EVENT's tenant (tenant id taken from the event envelope's actor, falling back to the record's tenant id field); when no tenant id is resolvable at delivery time the target FAILS VISIBLY (error log + failed delivery record) rather than silently notifying across tenants. Set 'global' to deliberately fan out across all tenants (e.g. a saasAdmin broadcast).
NotificationTarget.__itemCondition.doc: Optional per-item MScript filter for an isArray target on nodejs. The existing condition runs ONCE PER TARGET with target bound to the whole array; use itemCondition to skip individual recipients. In itemCondition, bare target is the current item, data is the DataView-first event record, and this carries payload, dataSource, old, actor and metadata. A targetItemNameInArray container path with a valid, non-conflicting JavaScript identifier root also binds the current item (reserved roots such as data, target and runMScript keep their existing meanings; use bare target for those paths): for members use members.active; for group.members use group.members.active. The container path keeps its existing meaning for recipient resolution. Example: targetItemNameInArray: 'members', targetPathInData: 'userId', itemCondition: { js: 'members.active && target.userId !== this.actor.userId' }. False skips that item; an evaluation error warns and skips only that item, continuing its siblings. Filtering every item is an intentional empty audience, not a delivery failure. Other language listeners require the corresponding port before using this slot.

__NotificationTargetKind.doc.#: What kind of contact handle a NotificationTarget resolves to. Drives both the listener-handler emission branch and the target-vs-jobType compatibility check.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.userId: An application user id. The runtime resolves it to email/phone/devices via auth-service identity lookup. Universally compatible with every jobType.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.email: A bare email address. Compatible with jobType='email' only.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.phoneNumber: A bare phone number in E.164 format. Compatible with jobType='sms' only (WhatsApp targets use `whatsappPhone` even though both are phone numbers — opt-in rules differ).
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.whatsappPhone: A WhatsApp-opted-in phone number in E.164. Compatible with jobType='whatsapp' only.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.telegramHandle: A Telegram handle (e.g. '@alice' or numeric chat id). Compatible with jobType='telegram' only.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.deviceToken: A push notification device token (FCM/APNs/OneSignal id). Compatible with jobType='push' only.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.role: An AUDIENCE kind: `targetValue` names a declared role value (built-in system role or custom RoleItem value) and the delivery-time fan-out asks the auth service (M2M listUsersByRole) for every user holding that role — tenant-scoped by default in multi-tenant projects (see NotificationTarget.scope). Each resolved user follows the userId delivery path, so this kind is compatible with every jobType. Empty resolution or an unreachable auth service is recorded as a FAILED delivery, never silently dropped.
__NotificationTargetKind.doc.userGroup: An AUDIENCE kind: `targetValue` names a user group (`groupName` of the auth service's userGroup object, which must be enabled via userGroupsActive) and the delivery-time fan-out asks the auth service (M2M listUsersByUserGroup) for the group's members. Each resolved user follows the userId delivery path, so this kind is compatible with every jobType. Empty resolution, an unknown group name, or an unreachable auth service is recorded as a FAILED delivery, never silently dropped.

__NotificationTargetScope.doc.#: Tenant scope of an audience (role/userGroup) NotificationTarget in a multi-tenant project. Ignored in single-tenant projects and for non-audience target kinds.
__NotificationTargetScope.doc.tenant: Default. Resolve the audience within the EVENT's tenant — the tenant id comes from the event envelope's actor, falling back to the record's tenant id field. No resolvable tenant id at delivery time is a visible FAILURE (error log + failed delivery record), not a cross-tenant fan-out.
__NotificationTargetScope.doc.global: Deliberately resolve the audience across ALL tenants (e.g. a saasAdmin broadcast).

__NotificationJobTypes.doc.#: Specifies the medium through which the notification will be sent.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.email: Send the notification as an email using the configured email provider.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.sms: Send the notification as an SMS using the configured SMS provider.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.push: Send the notification as a push message using the configured push provider.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.telegram: Send the notification as a Telegram message using the configured telegram provider.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.whatsapp: Send the notification as a WhatsApp Business message using the configured whatsapp provider.
__NotificationJobTypes.doc.inApp: Create an in-app notification stored in the system. It will be listed in the default InAppNotification object with auto-generated routes.

__ProjectAuthentication.doc: Defines the authentication and authorization configuration for the entire project. This module serves as the foundation for user identity, login behavior, access control, and verification flows. All services in the project, especially user services, rely on these centralized settings.

ProjectAuthentication.__authenticationEssentials.doc: Basic authentication settings for the project. Defines the core authentication method (e.g., email/password, token-based) and global authentication behaviors.
ProjectAuthentication.__loginDefinition.doc: Specifies how users, user groups, and tenants are defined in the project's data model. These definitions allow the generated service to dynamically extract identity and authorization data from project-specific data objects.
ProjectAuthentication.__verificationServices.doc: Defines optional verification flows such as password reset, email confirmation, mobile verification, and 2FA. An OpenAPPL compiler automatically generates the required backend logic for these features under the user service.
ProjectAuthentication.__accessControl.doc: Specifies permission-based access control settings. These govern what users or roles can access, based on project-wide authorization rules.
ProjectAuthentication.__socialLogins.doc: Configuration for allowing users to sign in or register using external identity providers. Supported providers include Google, Apple, Facebook, Microsoft, LinkedIn, GitHub, and GitLab.
ProjectAuthentication.__sessionGeoSensitivity.doc: Location-sensitivity rules for sessions. The generated service resolves the client's geo-location (country/region/city) from the internal geoip-service at login and stamps it onto the session and userSession record. When active, you can require a step-up (email/SMS verification) or force re-login when a login arrives from a location the user has not used before, and/or invalidate a live session when its request location drifts. Leave inactive to keep location enrichment without enforcement.
ProjectAuthentication.__foreignPermissionProvider.doc: Optional delegation of per-BusinessApi authorization to a FOREIGN permission server (a centralized policy engine), declared once here and generated into EVERY service. When set, any BusinessApi that opts in via `basics.authOptions.foreignPermissionCheck` sends a request (shaped from the api's MScript params + the caller's session bindings) to this server over gRPC or REST and is denied (403 by default) when the server's response trips `denyWhen`. The provider is a project constant (one server, one transport); the per-api QUESTION is independent of the data pattern. Leave null to keep the generated service's built-in authorization only.
ProjectAuthentication.__profileSettings.doc: Declares whether OTHER people may read a user's profile, and which of the user's own custom properties they see. The auth service generates `GET /userprofiles/:userId` by default: it serves the display identity (the user object's own name shape — `fullname`, or `name` + `surname` — plus `avatar`) and every property listed in `publicFields`, so an app can always render WHO a record belongs to. Switch it off with `hasPublicProfile: false` for projects where users must stay invisible to each other; then no profile route is generated at all and `GET /users/:userId` remains owner/admin-only, which is the auth service's confidentiality posture for the full user record. The AUDIENCE is an independent decision: `loginRequired` (default true) shares the profile with logged-in users only; `loginRequired: false` is the deliberate widening to anonymous callers. For a richer profile (cover images, social links, follower counts) model a separate profile DataObject in a business service, linked by `userId`; this block stays the identity surface.
ProjectAuthentication.__userProperties.doc: Defines additional properties to include in the user data object. These are added to the default fields [ email, password, fullname, name, surname, mobile, emailVerified, mobileVerified, roleId] and shape the structure of the User model in the generated user service. Note: Standard fields (`id`, `isActive`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) are automatically created. Every one of those thirteen names is RESERVED: a declaration here colliding with one is REFUSED at design time (`AUTH_USER_PROPERTY_NAME_RESERVED`), and so is a name declared twice in this list. Both comparisons IGNORE CASE - `Email` is the built-in `email`, and `displayName` beside `displayname` is one property declared twice - because a differently-cased spelling is not a different column: the DB index name is the column name snake_cased and LOWER-cased, so two such properties would emit one index name and only the first index would ever be created. For the same reason two names that merely PROJECT onto one index name (`ownerId` and `owner_id`) are refused too (`AUTH_USER_PROPERTY_INDEX_NAME_COLLISION`).
ProjectAuthentication.__tenantProperties.doc: Defines additional properties to include in the tenant data object, alongside the built-ins the auth service always emits: `name`, `codename` (unique, server-minted from the name), `fullname`, `avatar` and `ownerId`. Every one of those five names is RESERVED, and so are the standard fields `id`, `isActive`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, which are created automatically: a declaration here colliding with any of the nine is REFUSED at design time (`AUTH_TENANT_PROPERTY_NAME_RESERVED`) - declare a differently-named property instead. The comparison IGNORES CASE, and so does the duplicate check within this list: `Name` is the built-in `name`, and `displayName` beside `displayname` is one property declared twice. A differently-cased spelling is not a different column - the DB index name is the column name snake_cased and LOWER-cased, so two such properties would emit one index name and only the first index would ever be created. For the same reason two names that merely PROJECT onto one index name (`ownerId` and `owner_id`) are refused too (`AUTH_TENANT_PROPERTY_INDEX_NAME_COLLISION`). So this list does not redeclare the tenant `name`. To make the tenant name unique, set `uniqueTenantName: true` on the tenant configuration, which stamps `indexSettings.unique` on the built-in `name` for you; for a tenant identity that is a PAIR of columns, declare the pair in `compositeIndexSettings`.
ProjectAuthentication.__businessLogic.doc: Custom Business APIs to be included in the generated auth service. These APIs follow the same patterns as regular service Business APIs—supporting REST, WebSocket, Kafka, and cron triggers with full workflow capabilities. Standard auth API names (login, register, verify, resetPassword, etc.) are reserved and cannot be overridden. Use this to extend the auth service with project-specific operations on User, Tenant, or other auth-related data objects. Role writes: roles are not badges, so an api or crud action here that writes the auth user's `roleId` is refused (AUTH_USER_ROLE_WRITE_UNGUARDED, non-bypassable) - use updateUserRole / createUser, and model an earned label as a badge data object. The one exception is a real role change after an operation, run by a service: a create / update api on `user` declaring `authOptions.requiredCallerKind: "machineWithoutUserIdentity"` (with M2MAllowed true and loginRequired left on) that writes `roleId` in its own dataClauseItems. The generated api then refuses a caller whose session carries a user identity (400 M2M_CALLER_WITHOUT_USER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED) and stores only a declared role, in its canonical spelling: never an administrator role (superAdmin, saasAdmin, admin, tenantOwner, tenantAdmin: 400 ADMINISTRATOR_ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE), never a SaaS-level role (saasAdmin, saasUser - a machine caller is no SaaS operator: 400 SAAS_ROLE_GRANT_FORBIDDEN), never an empty role list when users have multiple roles (400 ROLE_LIST_EMPTY); an undeclared role: 400 ROLE_NOT_DEFINED. Both role refusals are case- and separator-insensitive. A crud action or bulk create onto `user` is never that door.
ProjectAuthentication.__dataObjects.doc: Custom DataObject definitions to host IN the generated auth service (the process that owns the givenPermission table). This lets a project attach project-specific CRUD objects—e.g. a permissionCheck-guarded object—to the auth service so the native-permission resolver can decide over real givenPermission rows. Objects whose name collides with a system auth object (user/userGroup/givenPermission/...) are skipped.

__ProfileSettings.doc: The project's declaration of a readable user profile — the sanctioned way to show WHO a record belongs to. Two independent axes: `hasPublicProfile` (is there a profile route at all — default TRUE, so an app can always render a display identity) and `loginRequired` (who may call it — default true, logged-in callers only). While `hasPublicProfile` is on, the auth service generates `GET /userprofiles/:userId`, which serves the user object's own display identity (`fullname`, or the `name` + `surname` pair when the project splits the name, plus `avatar`) and every property named in `publicFields`, projected AT THE QUERY so no other column is ever read. The response rides the standard envelope with `_type: "user"` (the discriminator is always the data object's name); it is a PROJECTION of the user record — only the served columns are present, never the full row. There is deliberately no public LIST of profiles: a list makes the user set enumerable, so a profile is only ever readable by id.

ProfileSettings.__hasPublicProfile.doc: Master switch for the generated profile route. TRUE by default: an app that shows an author name beside a post, an avatar in a member list, or an assignee on a task needs this surface, and a project that silently lacked it could not render a user's identity at all. Set it false for projects where users must stay invisible to each other — then NO route is generated and nothing about a user is readable by anyone but that user and admins (`GET /users/:userId` is owner/admin-only by design). Leaving it on does not by itself expose anything to the anonymous internet — see `loginRequired`.
ProfileSettings.__loginRequired.doc: The AUDIENCE of the generated profile route. True (the default) shares the profile with the LIMITED public — any logged-in user of the project — which is the right choice when identities are shown inside the app to signed-in people. False is the deliberate widening to the WIDER public: anonymous callers with no session; set it when the project genuinely serves public-facing pages (blog authors, marketplace sellers, a public directory). Widening the audience never changes WHICH columns are served — that is `publicFields` alone. Anonymous-by-default was considered and declined: it would make a project's entire user base — names and avatars — enumerable by iterating userIds without a session, which is personal data under KVKK/GDPR, so the widening stays an explicit act by the designer.
ProfileSettings.__publicFields.doc: Extra properties of the user object to serve on the profile, on top of the always-included display identity (the user object's own name shape — `fullname`, or `name` + `surname` — and `avatar`). Entries MUST name CUSTOM user properties declared in `authentication.userProperties` (e.g. `bio`, `title`, `websiteUrl`); naming a property that does not exist is a design-time error. Confidential system columns are refused outright — email, mobile, password-derived columns, verification/2FA flags, role and tenant columns, and session/login bookkeeping can never be listed here, whatever the project declares. Leave empty to serve the display identity only.
ProfileSettings.__publicFields.doc_array: A custom user property (from `authentication.userProperties`) to include in the public profile.

__ForeignPermissionProvider.doc: Project-wide foreign permission server configuration (one foreign server, one transport). Codegen generates ONE permission client per service from this block — a gRPC stub (proto emitted from `protoSource`, called via grpcUnaryCall) or a REST caller (fetch) — shared by every api that opts in via `authOptions.foreignPermissionCheck`. `endpoint` / `headers` / `tls.caCert` `$ENV:` refs resolve at runtime.

ForeignPermissionProvider.__tls.doc: [grpc only] Optional transport security. When omitted or `mode: 'insecure'` (the dev default) the channel uses insecure credentials. `mode: 'ssl'` uses TLS; `caCert` (literal PEM or `$ENV:VAR`) overrides the system trust roots when the server presents a private/self-signed certificate.
ForeignPermissionProvider.__headers.doc: [rest only] STATIC auth headers sent on every call to the permission server (e.g. an API key the server requires). Each value may be a literal or a `$ENV:VAR` reference resolved at runtime.
ForeignPermissionProvider.__sessionBindings.doc: Session field → request param bindings, applied to BOTH transports. For each entry the gate pulls `this.session.<from>` (the access token is also reachable via `this.request.headers.authorization` / `this.session.accessToken`) into the merged request under `<as>`. Bindings + the per-api `foreignPermissionCheck.params` together form the request body/message.
ForeignPermissionProvider.__providerBasics.doc: Transport and decision policy of the foreign permission server: the grpc/rest transport selector, the endpoint, the proto/method binding (grpc) or path/method (rest), and the deny/message/status/failOpen/cache rules.

__ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.doc: Transport and decision policy of the foreign permission server (one server, one transport). Carries the grpc/rest selector, the endpoint, the transport-specific binding (proto package/service/method for grpc; restMethod/restPath/requestIn for rest), and the deny/message/status/failOpen/cache rules classified over the server's response.

ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__type.doc: Transport for the permission server: `grpc` (call a foreign gRPC `service.method` via the shipped grpcUnaryCall machinery, proto emitted from `protoSource`) or `rest` (HTTP `fetch` to `endpoint + restPath`). REQUIRED.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__endpoint.doc: The permission server address. For gRPC: a `host:port` (e.g. `permissions.internal:50051`). For REST: a base URL (e.g. `https://perm.internal`). Either a literal or a `$ENV:VAR` reference (e.g. `$ENV:PERMISSION_SERVER_URL`) resolved at runtime. Prefer `$ENV:` so the endpoint isn't baked into the generated code. REQUIRED.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__protoSource.doc: [grpc only] The FOREIGN permission server's `.proto` contract, supplied INLINE as proto text. Codegen writes it verbatim and loads it through proto-loader. The proto MUST declare the `package` and `service` named below, and the `method` must be one of that service's rpc methods. A request can use explicit proto fields matching the params/sessionBindings keys, or `google.protobuf.Struct` for a fully-dynamic map.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__package.doc: [grpc only] The proto `package` name to load from `protoSource` (e.g. `permission`). Must match the `package` declared in the proto.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__service.doc: [grpc only] The proto `service` name to load from `protoSource` (e.g. `Permission`). Must match a `service` declared in the proto.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__method.doc: [grpc only] The rpc method name to invoke on `service` (e.g. `Check`). Must be declared in the proto. Unary only.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__restMethod.doc: [rest only] HTTP method used to call the permission server (`POST` default or `GET`).
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__restPath.doc: [rest only] The path appended to `endpoint` for the permission check (e.g. `/check`). REQUIRED for rest.
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__requestIn.doc: [rest only] Where the merged request (params + sessionBindings) is placed on the HTTP call: `body` (JSON body, default — for POST) or `query` (query string — for GET).
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__denyWhen.doc: MScript RULE evaluated with `result` bound to the RAW server response (any shape — boolean / int / string / complex object); TRUE ⇒ DENY. E.g. `!result.allowed` | `result !== 'GRANTED'` | `result.code != 0`. When omitted the default rule is `result === false || result?.allowed === false`. (Interpreted in Phase 2.)
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__messageFrom.doc: Optional MScript over `result` → the user-facing deny message (e.g. `result.message || result.errorCode`). The per-api `denyMessage` takes precedence when both are set. (Interpreted in Phase 2.)
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__statusFrom.doc: Optional MScript over `result` → the HTTP status to raise on deny (e.g. `result.status` to honor 401 invalid-token / 403 denied / 400 / 500). Defaults to 403 when omitted. (Interpreted in Phase 2.)
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__failOpen.doc: Transport error / server down policy: `false` (default, fail-CLOSED → deny/403) vs `true` (fail-OPEN → allow). Default fail-closed for safety. A REST answer with a non-2xx HTTP status is a failed check too, whatever its body says, unless the body is an explicit deny (`denyWhen` true), which denies with its own status and message: a 500 `{ error }` or a 404 problem document is never an allow. Both transports are bounded at 10000 ms (the REST fetch through an abort signal, the grpc call through its deadline); a call that outlives it is a transport error. A failed check is never cached. (Interpreted in Phase 2.)
ForeignPermissionProviderBasics.__cacheTtlSeconds.doc: Optional Redis result cache for the permission DECISION (the latency follow-on the ADR flags). When > 0, the gate caches the classified allow/deny outcome (message + detail + status) keyed by a stable hash of the SUBJECT + the QUESTION — `sha256(<projectCodename>:foreignperm:<session.userId ?? 'guest'>:<hash of the compiled params>)`, NOT the volatile bearer token — and checks it BEFORE calling the server, so the same user asking the same permission in the same scope reuses the cached decision across requests/sessions for this many seconds. On a miss it calls the server, classifies, then stores the outcome with this TTL (BOTH allow and deny are cached). Redis errors are fail-soft (fall through to a live call). `0` (default) or absent = NO cache: behavior is byte-identical to the always-call gate.

__ForeignPermissionSessionBinding.doc: One session-field → request-PLACEMENT binding. The gate pulls `this.session.<from>` (the caller's application JWT is reachable as `accessToken`) and PLACES it on the permission request per `in`: into the bearer token, a request header, the JSON body, or a query param — under key `<as>` (ignored for `bearer`, which is always `Authorization: Bearer <value>`).

ForeignPermissionSessionBinding.__in.doc: WHERE the resolved value is PLACED on the permission request: `bearer` (sent as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` — REST header / gRPC `metadata.authorization`; `as` IGNORED), `header` (a REST request header / gRPC metadata entry named `<as>`), `body` (a JSON body field / gRPC proto message field `<as>` — DEFAULT, alongside the per-api params) or `query` (a REST query-string param `<as>`; IGNORED for grpc). Existing `{from,as}` configs default to `body`, unchanged.
ForeignPermissionSessionBinding.__as.doc: The header-name / body-key / query-key the value is placed under (e.g. `userToken` for a server that wants the JWT in a `userToken` body field, or `perm-user-id` for a header). IGNORED when `in` is `bearer` (the value is always `Authorization: Bearer <value>`).

__AuthBasics.doc: Defines the fundamental authentication configuration for the project. These settings determine the authentication method(s) used across all services, including token-based or API key authentication.

AuthBasics.__documentation.doc: Module-level UX prompt + freeform description of the auth service. Read by MindUI for login / register / verification / password-reset page generation.
AuthBasics.__JWTAuthentication.doc: Configuration for JWT-based authentication, where the project issues and verifies its own JSON Web Tokens. This is the recommended authentication method in OpenAPPL for secure, scalable identity management.
AuthBasics.__ssoAuthentication.doc: Retained Single Sign-On (SSO) configuration. SSO authentication is not available yet: useSSOForAuthentication=true is refused with SSO_NOT_SUPPORTED. No SSO login flow, environment variables or deploy secrets are generated.
AuthBasics.__remoteServiceAuthentication.doc: Disabled slot, not available: authentication cannot be delegated to an external user service. A blueprint that sets remoteServiceAuthentication under authenticationEssentials is refused with UNKNOWN_PROPERTY.
AuthBasics.__remoteSessionSettings.doc: Disabled slot, not available: session information cannot be read from a remote user service. A blueprint that sets remoteSessionSettings under authenticationEssentials is refused with UNKNOWN_PROPERTY.
AuthBasics.__apiKeyAuthentication.doc: Enables API key-based authentication for accessing the project's services. This method can be used either as the primary authentication mechanism or as a secondary option alongside others.
AuthBasics.__refreshTokenSettings.doc: Opt-in refresh-token support. When enabled, every login ALSO returns a long-lived `refreshToken` the client stores locally and later presents to `/relogin` to obtain a fresh access token after the access token expires. When disabled, no refresh token is issued and an expired access token means the user logs in again. NOTE: the `/relogin` route exists in BOTH modes — with the feature off it still accepts a currently-valid (but about-to-expire) access token and returns a fresh one, so a client can always extend its session before expiry.
AuthBasics.__httpSettings.doc: Defines the HTTP configuration of the auth service. Primarily includes the port on which the auth service will accept HTTP requests.
AuthBasics.__cookieSettings.doc: Use these settings to arrange the allowed domains of your application's session cookie. A generated service always sets its session cookie httpOnly with SameSite lax (SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, emitted as lax), and Secure on an HTTPS request or when COOKIE_SECURE is true (stage, prod and test); these settings change neither. The cookie domain is set from the login request host when that host is in the allowed list; with allowedDomains set, a login on any other host gets no session cookie.

__RefreshTokenSettings.doc: Configures opt-in refresh tokens for the auth service. A refresh token is an opaque random string whose SHA-256 hash is stored server-side (never the token itself), so it is revocable — logout can genuinely kill it, which a stateless refresh JWT cannot. Each refresh token is single-use: presenting it at `/relogin` mints a successor and retires the presented one, so a retired token showing up again is evidence of theft and revokes the whole token family issued from that login.

RefreshTokenSettings.__useRefreshToken.doc: Enable refresh tokens. When true, every login response carries a `refreshToken` alongside the access token (the password login, a social login through `/auth/social-login-result` and the register auto-login), and `/relogin` accepts either credential. When false (default) no refresh token is issued and `/relogin` accepts only a still-valid access token.
RefreshTokenSettings.__refreshTokenTTLDays.doc: How many days a refresh token stays valid, counted from the moment it is issued. It should comfortably outlive the access token — that is the point of the mechanism. Default 30.
RefreshTokenSettings.__rotationGraceSeconds.doc: Seconds a just-retired refresh token is still accepted after rotation. This exists for one specific failure: if the `/relogin` response is lost in flight (dropped connection, app killed mid-request) the server has already rotated but the client never received the successor, so an honest retry presents a retired token and would otherwise be treated as theft and log the user out. The window makes that retry succeed while keeping the replay window small. Default 60. Overridable at runtime with REFRESH_TOKEN_GRACE_SECONDS.

__ModuleDocumentation.doc: Holds the module-level frontendDocument UX prompt. Reused across auth / bff / notification modules for consistency. MindUI reads frontendDocument to generate page UX; the section exists so module-level primitives stay in proper sections rather than at module/chapter root.

ModuleDocumentation.__frontendDocument.doc: Module-level UX prompt for MindUI. Describes intended page placement, navigation patterns, empty/error states, and any role-specific landing rules. Empty = MindUI works from technical schema alone.

__AuthHttpSettings.doc: Defines the HTTP configuration of the auth service. Primarily includes the port on which the auth service will accept HTTP requests.

AuthHttpSettings.__httpPort.doc: The port number that the auth service will use to listen for HTTP traffic. Recommended to use ports in the 3000-3099 range for consistency across microservices.
AuthHttpSettings.__routerSuffix.doc: Use this in your custom deployment if you have any suffix in your auth service url to be removed before evaluated in express router. AI Agents should keep this null.

__JWTAuth.doc: Defines the configuration for JWT-based authentication, where the project issues and verifies its own JSON Web Tokens. This is the recommended authentication method in OpenAPPL due to its stateless nature and scalability.

JWTAuth.__useJWTForAuthentication.doc: Indicates whether JWT authentication is enabled for the project.
JWTAuth.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for JWT authentication. Leave it null if useJWTForAuthentication is false.

__JWTAuthConfig.doc: Defines the configuration details for JWT-based authentication. This object is used when useJWTForAuthentication is set to true. It includes token and key refresh periods.

JWTAuthConfig.__tokenPeriodInDays.doc: Specifies the lifespan of each JWT token, in days. After this period, the token will expire and require reauthentication.
JWTAuthConfig.__sessionCookieMaxAgeDays.doc: How long the browser session COOKIE is allowed to live, in days. Leave it unset and the cookie follows tokenPeriodInDays, which is what you want unless you have a reason to diverge. Set it to let the cookie expire sooner than the token: the token and its server-side session stay valid for tokenPeriodInDays, the browser simply stops sending the cookie earlier. The generated service emits this as the SESSION_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS environment variable in MILLISECONDS (days multiplied by 86400000), and the runtime hands the browser the SMALLER of that ceiling and the token's own expiry, so a value LARGER than tokenPeriodInDays extends nothing. Must be a positive number of days when set.

__SSOAuth.doc: Retained Single Sign-On (SSO) configuration schema. SSO authentication is not available yet: useSSOForAuthentication=true is refused with SSO_NOT_SUPPORTED, even with complete identity provider settings. No SSO login flow, environment variables or deploy secrets are generated.

SSOAuth.__useSSOForAuthentication.doc: Keep false. Setting true is refused at design time with SSO_NOT_SUPPORTED because SSO authentication is not available yet.
SSOAuth.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for the SSO provider. Leave it null if useSSOForAuthentication is false.

__SSOAuthConfig.doc: Retained external identity provider settings for the unavailable SSO feature. Configuring these fields does not enable SSO; useSSOForAuthentication=true is refused with SSO_NOT_SUPPORTED. No profile mapping or account linking flow is generated.

SSOAuthConfig.__ssoName.doc: A human-readable name to identify this SSO provider in your project (e.g., 'corporateSSO' or 'okta').
SSOAuthConfig.__tokenPeriodInMinutes.doc: Retained token period setting in minutes. Existing token period resolution is unchanged; this value does not enable an SSO login flow.
SSOAuthConfig.__ssoServerSettings.doc: Configuration of the SSO provider's endpoints and client credentials. Includes authorization, token, user profile, and logout URLs as well as client ID and secret.
SSOAuthConfig.__ssoUserIdPropertyInProfile.doc: The field in the SSO profile payload that will be used as the unique SSO user ID in the generated application. Common defaults are 'sub' or 'id'.
SSOAuthConfig.__emailPropertyInProfile.doc: The field in the SSO profile payload to use as the user's email address. Used for identifying or creating the user record.
SSOAuthConfig.__userNamePropertyInProfile.doc: The field in the SSO profile payload to use as the user's display name. Used when creating a new user on first login.

__SSOServerSettings.doc: Retained endpoint and credential settings for the unavailable SSO feature. These settings do not generate an OAuth2/OIDC flow, environment variables or deploy secrets. Enabling SSO is refused with SSO_NOT_SUPPORTED.

SSOServerSettings.__tokenHost.doc: The base URL of the SSO provider (e.g., https://auth.example.com). This value is used as the root for building all other endpoint paths.
SSOServerSettings.__authPath.doc: The relative path to initiate user authorization on the SSO provider (e.g., /oauth2/authorize).
SSOServerSettings.__tokenPath.doc: The relative path to request access tokens from the SSO provider (e.g., /oauth2/token).
SSOServerSettings.__userInfoPath.doc: The relative path to fetch the authenticated user's profile information (e.g., /userinfo).
SSOServerSettings.__logoutPath.doc: The relative path to perform logout on the SSO provider (e.g., /logout).
SSOServerSettings.__redirectUrl.doc: The full callback URL of the client application to which the SSO provider will redirect after login. This URL must match the one registered with the SSO provider.
SSOServerSettings.__clientId.doc: The client identifier issued to your application by the SSO provider. This ID is used to identify your app during the authentication flow.
SSOServerSettings.__clientSecret.doc: The secret associated with the client ID, used to authenticate your application with the SSO provider when exchanging tokens.

__RemoteServiceAuthentication.doc: Not available: AuthBasics carries this type only as a disabled slot, so no blueprint can enable it and nothing is generated from it. It describes delegating authentication to an external user service outside of the generated system, where the generated service would validate tokens and retrieve sessions via remote APIs.

RemoteServiceAuthentication.__isRemoteServiceAuthenticationActive.do: Indicates whether remote user service authentication is enabled for the project.
RemoteServiceAuthentication.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for remote service authentication. Leave it null if isRemoteServiceAuthenticationActive is false.

__RemoteServiceAuthenticationConfig.doc: Not available: reachable only through the disabled RemoteServiceAuthentication slot of AuthBasics, so nothing is generated from it. Configuration details for remote service authentication, including remote request and session handling.

RemoteServiceAuthenticationConfig.__remoteServiceRequest.doc: Specifies the HTTPRequest used to authenticate the user via a remote user service. This request should validate a token and return session details.
RemoteServiceAuthenticationConfig.__sessionIdPathInToken.doc: The path to the session ID within the decoded authentication token. This value is used to locate the user's session.
RemoteServiceAuthenticationConfig.__sessionReadLocation.doc: Defines where the session data should be fetched from after extracting the session ID. Options include session store, token itself, or remote service.

__CookieSettings.doc: Arranges the allow-list for the session cookie. The cookie itself is always httpOnly; Secure and SameSite come from the runtime env (COOKIE_SECURE, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE). This section decides two things: which hosts may receive the cookie at all, and what its Domain attribute is.

CookieSettings.__allowedDomains.doc: The hosts allowed to receive the session cookie, each given either as a base domain (xapp.com - the cookie is then shared across all of its subdomains, which is what enables SSO between app. and api. hosts) or as a specific host (web.xapp.com). Emitted as the COOKIE_DOMAINS environment variable into the stage/prod/test slots only, so local development is never gated. Leave it empty to keep the permissive default; once it is set, a login served on a host outside the list receives NO session cookie and the refusal is logged. List the API hosts that actually serve the login response, not only the frontend origins.

__SessionReadLocation.doc.#: An enum type that specifies where to retrieve session data after extracting the session ID from a decoded token. Used RemoteService authentication flows.
__SessionReadLocation.doc.readFromSessionStore: The session data is read from the local session store of the project.
__SessionReadLocation.doc.tokenIsSession: The session data is embedded directly in the token itself; no additional fetch is required.
__SessionReadLocation.doc.readFromRemoteService: The session data is retrieved from an external service using RemoteSession settings.

__RequestLocations.doc.#: An enum type to refer to a specific section of an HTTP request where data (e.g., tokens or parameters) can be located.
__RequestLocations.doc.bearer: Use when the data is sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. No name is required for this mode.
__RequestLocations.doc.cookie: Use when the data is sent in cookies. The name refers to the cookie's key.
__RequestLocations.doc.header: Use when the data is sent in a custom HTTP header. The name is the header's name.
__RequestLocations.doc.query: Use when the data is sent as a query parameter. The name is the name of the query parameter.
__RequestLocations.doc.body: Use when the data is sent in the body of the request. The name refers to a property in the request body.
__RequestLocations.doc.urlpath: Use when the data is part of the dynamic URL path (e.g., /users/:id). The name is the parameter name.
__RequestLocations.doc.session: Use when the data is extracted from the server-side session object.
__RequestLocations.doc.request: Use when the data exists directly on the root of the request object.

__RemoteSession.doc: Not available: AuthBasics carries this type only as a disabled slot, so no blueprint can enable it and nothing is generated from it. It describes retrieving session data from an external session service with an HTTP request to a remote endpoint, for session management handled outside of the generated application.

RemoteSession.__useRemoteSession.doc: Indicates whether remote session retrieval is enabled. If true, session data will be fetched from an external service using the settings defined in 'configuration'.
RemoteSession.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for remote session retrieval. Leave it null if useRemoteSession is false.

__RemoteSessionConfig.doc: Not available: reachable only through the disabled RemoteSession slot of AuthBasics, so nothing is generated from it. Configuration details for remote session retrieval, including session path, ID extraction, caching, and the HTTP request to the remote service.

RemoteSessionConfig.__sessionPath.doc: The path to the session object within the HTTP response body. If undefined, the entire response body is assumed to be the session object.
RemoteSessionConfig.__sessionIdPath.doc: The path to the session ID within the session object. This is used to extract a unique session identifier.
RemoteSessionConfig.__writeInStore.doc: Determines whether the retrieved session should be cached locally. If true, the issuer's answer is stored locally for a short revalidation window (5 minutes, HexaAuth.REMOTE_SESSION_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) and then fetched again; a cached copy that predates its owner's session-invalidation epoch (a log-out-everywhere, a deleted or blocked user) is dropped on the next request.
RemoteSessionConfig.__sessionRequest.doc: Defines the HTTP request used to retrieve the session from the remote service. This includes method, URL, headers, and any required parameters.

__HTTPRequest.doc: Defines a reusable HTTP request configuration to interact with a remote service and retrieve a JSON response. This object is used across the platform for scenarios such as remote authentication, remote data access, and integration with external APIs (CRUD operations, searches, etc.).

HTTPRequest.__httpRequestUrl.doc: The full URL of the remote service endpoint, as a static literal: it is not MScript and is never evaluated. On an ApiCallAction, `{name}` placeholders in its PATH are filled from the action's `httpRequestPath` entries; every other user of HTTPRequest sends the URL verbatim.
HTTPRequest.__httpRequestMethod.doc: The HTTP method to use when making the request. Supported methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
HTTPRequest.__tokenLocation.doc: The section of the request where the authentication token should be placed (e.g., header, cookie). Defaults to 'bearer'. An ApiCallAction sends its `tokenValue` only to `bearer` (the default when unset), `header`, `cookie` or `query`; any other location (the inbound members `body`, `urlpath`, `session`, `request`, or a value outside the enum), or `header` / `cookie` / `query` with no `tokenName`, is a design-time error (API_CALL_TOKEN_LOCATION_UNSUPPORTED / API_CALL_TOKEN_NAME_MISSING) and the generated call refuses to run instead of sending the request without its credential.
HTTPRequest.__tokenName.doc: The name or key under which the token will be sent in the specified location.
HTTPRequest.__tokenValue.doc: The token value to be sent, if static. This field is optional and typically used for hardcoded tokens or fallback defaults.
HTTPRequest.__httpRequestParameters.doc: The parameters to send with the request, including body, query string, headers, and cookies.
HTTPRequest.__cacheResponse.doc: Indicates whether the response of this request should be cached for reuse. Useful for minimizing repeated remote calls.

__HTTPRequestParameters.doc: Defines the parameters to be sent with an HTTP request. This includes data sent in the request body, query string, headers, or cookies. All item names here are WIRE names: they are sent verbatim on the request (never camelCase-normalized).

HTTPRequestParameters.__httpRequestBody.doc: Key-value pairs to include in the body of the request. Keys are emitted verbatim as JSON body keys (e.g. `customer_id` stays `customer_id`).
HTTPRequestParameters.__httpRequestQuery.doc: Key-value pairs to include as query string parameters. Names are emitted verbatim (URL-encoded) into the query string (e.g. `filter[status]`).
HTTPRequestParameters.__httpRequestHeaders.doc: Custom headers to include in the request. Header names are wire tokens sent verbatim (e.g. `x-api-key` stays `x-api-key`, NOT camelCased).
HTTPRequestParameters.__httpRequestCookies.doc: Cookies to be attached to the request. Cookie names are wire tokens sent verbatim in the Cookie header.

__DataMapItem.doc: Represents a single key-value pair used in most context. The value can be defined dynamically using an MScript.

DataMapItem.__name.doc: The key name for the data item (e.g., a header name or parameter name).
DataMapItem.__value.doc: The value of the data item, defined using MScript to allow dynamic expressions or literals.
DataMapItem.name: String

__WireTokenMapItem.doc: A key-value pair whose name is a WIRE-PROTOCOL token (HTTP header or cookie name). The name is preserved VERBATIM — never renamed or camelCase-normalized (never-silently-rename policy) — and must match the RFC 7230 token charset. The value is defined using an MScript.

WireTokenMapItem.__name.doc: The wire token name (HTTP header or cookie name), sent verbatim on the request. Must be an RFC 7230 token: letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~ (e.g. `x-api-key`, `X-Request-Id`). Invalid characters are a validation error — the name is never auto-renamed.
WireTokenMapItem.__value.doc: The value of the data item, defined using MScript to allow dynamic expressions or literals.
WireTokenMapItem.name: String

__WireKeyMapItem.doc: A key-value pair whose name is a WIRE key (URL query parameter name or JSON body key). The name is preserved VERBATIM — never renamed or camelCase-normalized (never-silently-rename policy) — and must be printable ASCII without spaces. The value is defined using an MScript.

WireKeyMapItem.__name.doc: The wire key name (query parameter name or JSON body key), sent verbatim on the request (query names URL-encoded, body keys JSON-escaped). Printable ASCII without spaces or control characters (e.g. `customer_id`, `filter[status]`, `@id`). Invalid characters are a validation error — the name is never auto-renamed.
WireKeyMapItem.__value.doc: The value of the data item, defined using MScript to allow dynamic expressions or literals.
WireKeyMapItem.name: String

__providerConfigCatalog.doc.#: Machine-readable per-provider configuration key catalog. Single source of truth for the free-form configuration[] (DataMapSimpleItem) fields on the provider families below. Each family maps a provider brand to its expected configuration keys, each with a value type, a secret flag (masked in API responses + delivered via $SECRET_ env at deploy time), a required flag, and a doc line. Drives provider-aware frontend forms, structured agent schema, required-key + unknown-key validation, and secret classification. NOT a pattern class — the __ prefix keeps it out of pattern/enum discovery and the orphan checker. Per-family __envPrefix + __envKeyStyle describe how a key name becomes an environment variable (upperSnake: camelCase->UPPER_SNAKE; verbatim: kept as-is). mapsTo names a runtime alias the adapter reads under a different key (e.g. defaultModel->model). group tags an either/or set (at least one full group must be present). Keys marked required are validated as present; unknown keys (not listed for the selected brand) are rejected as typos. The bucketProvider family documents the FIXED-SHAPE BucketProviderConfig object (not a DataMapSimpleItem[] list): its keys are pattern-class fields, presence/auth-mode validation stays with the BucketProvider pattern validator, and env names that carry a brand infix (GCS_/AZURE_) are spelled out in the key docs. Every family also carries a `__credentials` slot. Its fields, for a settings UI and an agent: `overlayFamily` is the env-values / organization registry family name (null: no overlay); `credentialSets` says whether the Sandbox (test + stage rows) and Live (prod rows) sets apply; `credentialModes` lists the values of the reserved `credentialMode` key (`auto` = no row; `mock` only where `mockCredentialMode` is `allowed`, never for the prod slot); `mockBrand` names a blueprint brand that is itself a test double (a different thing from the credential mode); `liveDetection` says how the build tells that a base value reads live (`keyMode`, `environmentField`, `none`); `credentialScopes` lists the levels that can supply the credential (`saas` = the application owner's deploy secret; `tenant` / `resource` / `user` = the scoped-credential store), opted into through `scopeField`. Modes and slot-suffixed secrets are honoured by nodejs services only; a project with a service of another language gets the WARNING `PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MODE_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED`. Pinned to the code constants by src/patterns/__tests__/provider-config-catalog-credentials-8754.test.ts. The organization families with no entry here (graph, bigLoad, chat, amqp) have no catalogued keys and refuse the credential mode `mock`.

__credentials.note: The sets carry the SECRET keys only: a non-secret AI key is baked into the manifest. The `mock` BRAND is a keyless offline adapter a designer picks in the blueprint (provider `mock`, nodejs only, never a credential fallback); it is NOT the credential mode `mock`, which this family refuses (`PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MODE_MOCK_UNSUPPORTED`). Tenant, resource and user keys need `credentialScopes` on the entry and a brand in `scopedBrands`. A `subscriptionToken` credential (AgentHarness `modelSettings.auth: userSubscription`) is tenant or user only: the saas level is refused (`AGENT_HARNESS_SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE_OFF`).

__familyKeys.#: Family-wide keys: catalogued for EVERY aiProvider brand, custom included, matched case-insensitively. The secret classifier reads this table after the brand's own row and before the keyword backstop. The numeric tuning keys are non-secret, so a name that trips the backstop (maxTokens, tokenLimit: the 'token' keyword) keeps its typed value in the generated manifest instead of moving to a string env var. serviceAccountJson is credential material under any brand and any casing, and its name trips no backstop keyword, so it is listed as a secret here.

maxTokens.doc: Default cap on generated tokens per call (number). Read by every adapter as maxTokens. The AgentHarness runner's model gateway also clamps a translated call's max_tokens to it (then to maxOutputTokens, then maxCompletionTokens, the first one set).

maxOutputTokens.doc: Output-token cap under the name some provider APIs use (number). The bundled adapters read maxTokens; this row keeps a value authored under this name typed and non-secret.

maxCompletionTokens.doc: Output-token cap under the OpenAI reasoning-model name (number). The bundled adapters read maxTokens; this row keeps a value authored under this name typed and non-secret.

tokenLimit.doc: Overall token cap (number). Not read by the bundled adapters; this row keeps a value authored under this name typed and non-secret.

contextWindowTokens.doc: Override of the model's context window in tokens, used for compaction (number).

temperature.doc: Default sampling temperature (number). Read by the bundled adapters as temperature.

topP.doc: Nucleus-sampling probability mass (number). Not read by the bundled adapters; catalogued so the value stays typed.

serviceAccountJson.doc: Service-account JSON (credential material) under any brand and any casing: always a deploy secret, never compiled into the service. The google brand row documents its use.

topK.doc: Top-k sampling cutoff (number). Not read by the bundled adapters; catalogued so the value stays typed.

baseUrl.doc: API root of a proxy or gateway that serves the Anthropic Messages API, e.g. https://gateway.example.com. The adapter posts to <baseUrl>/v1/messages (a baseUrl that already ends in /v1 gets /messages only). Unset means https://api.anthropic.com.

apiKey.doc: NOT SUPPORTED - the Vertex adapter never reads an apiKey, and validation refuses it with AI_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG. Vertex authenticates with projectId + location, plus serviceAccountJson for an inline service account or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS on the deployment for Application Default Credentials; for the key-only Gemini Developer API use provider="custom" against a Gemini-compatible baseUrl. This key is listed ONLY so that an already-authored blueprint value stays classified as a secret - masking and deploy-secret relocation read this table, and dropping the entry would turn a real credential into an unrecognised key carried in clear.

serviceAccountJson.doc: Vertex service-account JSON (inline). Omit it to authenticate with Application Default Credentials - the deployer sets GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS instead.

baseUrl.doc: Azure OpenAI endpoint URL.

awsAccessKeyId.doc: AWS access key id. Credential material: delivered as a deploy secret, never compiled into the service.

baseUrl.doc: Ollama server URL, e.g. http://localhost:11434.

Target base URL. With apiFormat openai it is the API root the /chat/completions path is appended to (usually ending in /v1); with apiFormat anthropic the adapter posts to <baseUrl>/v1/messages (a baseUrl that already ends in /v1 gets /messages only).

extraHeaders.doc: Extra request headers as a JSON string.

seed.doc: Optional deterministic mock AI seed, defaults to `mindbricks`. Mixed with messages to derive offline text/JSON replies; no key or network.

awsAccessKeyId.doc: AWS access key id. Credential material: delivered as a deploy secret, never compiled into the service.

__credentials.note: Mock runs the sinks (email, SMS, WhatsApp, Telegram, push); the SMS and channel sinks keep their slot rule and never run in production.

rejectUnauthorized.doc: Verify the server TLS certificate. Defaults to true; set false only for a mock/self-signed endpoint (the built-in mail-sink).

awsAccessKeyId.doc: AWS access key id. Credential material: delivered as a deploy secret, never compiled into the service.

platformApplicationArn.doc: Push channel only: the SNS platform application (FCM or APNs) the project's device tokens belong to, e.g. arn:aws:sns:eu-central-1:111111111111:app/GCM/myApp. A raw device token is registered against it with CreatePlatformEndpoint before the publish; without it a push can only address an SNS platform-endpoint ARN.

awsAccessKeyId.doc: AWS access key id. Credential material: delivered as a deploy secret, never compiled into the service.

awsRegion.doc: AWS region of the SES identity (e.g. eu-central-1).

emailFrom.doc: Verified SES From address (or an address on a verified domain).

mailgunBaseUrl.doc: API base URL; set https://api.eu.mailgun.net for EU-hosted domains.

postmarkMessageStream.doc: Message stream id; defaults to the transactional 'outbound' stream.

whatsappFrom.doc: WhatsApp sender (whatsapp:+... ) for the whatsapp channel.

netgsmSender.doc: Sender header (msgheader) approved on the Netgsm account. Required: Netgsm refuses a send whose header is not defined on the account (result code 40).

telegramBotToken.doc: Telegram bot token. Also the outbound credential of every aiAgent chat surface or mcpbff exposure bound to this provider (chat bots are retired).

telegramWebhookSecret.doc: The secret token Telegram presents (X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token, the setWebhook secret_token) on the webhook of the aiAgent surface or mcpbff exposure bound to this provider; without it that webhook refuses every update (fails closed). Not needed for outbound-only use.

whatsappAccessToken.doc: WhatsApp Cloud API access token. Also the outbound credential of the aiAgent chat surface or mcpbff exposure bound to this provider (chat bots are retired).

whatsappApiVersion.doc: Graph API version the sends and the chat replies post through (default v20.0).

whatsappAppSecret.doc: Meta app secret. Verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 of every webhook Meta posts to this provider's ONE inbound door on the notification service (POST /v1/whatsapp-webhooks/meta/<name>: inbound customer messages for the agents and bots bound to this provider, delivery statuses for the delivery log, other field changes); without it the door refuses everything (503). The only place the secret lives: an aiAgent surface or mcpbff exposure names this provider and carries no secret of its own.

whatsappVerifyToken.doc: The verify token you enter when subscribing this provider's inbound door (GET /v1/whatsapp-webhooks/meta/<name>, hub.verify_token handshake) in the Meta app dashboard; without it the subscription is refused.

__credentials.note: `liveDetection: keyMode` reads each brand's `__keyMode` row; the build finding `liveCredentials` (action `moveProviderCredentialsToLive`) fires only for a value that reads live, so a brand whose row says `detection: none` is never flagged. Tenant and user payment credentials are not built (ADR-scoped-provider-credentials D6.2).

__planIdOrigin.#: Per-brand ORIGIN of `sys_<X>SubscriptionPlan.providerPlanId`. This is the fact that decides whether a PRE-SEEDED providerPlanId is legitimate for a brand at all. `provider-generated` = the provider mints the reference and the adapter READS IT BACK from the create response, so any value a designer seeds by hand is wrong by construction and can only be obtained by calling createPlan (POST /v1/payments/admin/plans/provision). `caller-chosen` = the adapter derives the reference from values the caller already owns, so a seeded value is legitimate and the provisioning sweep stores the same string. Measured from each adapter's own createPlanImpl in _common/nodejs/src/common/payment-providers/. `adoption` = the brand's VENDOR-SIDE idempotency story when the local providerPlanId is null but a vendor object may already exist: `list-and-adopt` = the adapter implements listPlans and the sweep adopts an identity-matched existing object instead of minting a duplicate; `create-only` = no listPlans, a cleared providerPlanId re-mints at the vendor and the orphan is cleaned in the vendor's panel.

stripe.note: createPlanImpl creates a Product then a recurring Price and returns `price.id`. Stripe mints the id.
stripe.adoptionNote: listPlans walks GET /v1/prices (recurring, active, product expanded); the product metadata carries the identity stamp - and the `code` key createPlanImpl has always stamped, which is what matches pre-stamp objects.

paypal.note: createPlanImpl creates a catalog Product then POST /v1/billing/plans and returns the plan `id` PayPal assigned.
paypal.adoptionNote: No listPlans implemented; GET /v1/billing/plans exists but the adapter does not walk it yet, so a cleared providerPlanId re-mints and the orphan is cleaned in the PayPal panel.

iyzico.note: createPlanImpl creates the product then the pricing plan and reads `pricingPlanReferenceCode` BACK from iyzico; the create call sends no reference of its own. createSubscriptionImpl then sends that value as `pricingPlanReferenceCode`, so a seeded plan code can never match. This is the brand the pre-seeded providerPlanId problem was found on.
iyzico.adoptionNote: No listPlans implemented and the pricing-plan objects carry no caller metadata to stamp, so an orphaned plan is recognised by name in the iyzico panel only.
