adyen.note: Adyen has no plan object at all; createPlanImpl echoes `input.code` and the synthetic subscription id is `shopperReference:planCode`. Seeding the plan code is correct for this brand.
adyen.adoptionNote: Nothing to adopt: there IS no vendor-side plan object, so a re-run mints nothing and duplicates are impossible for this brand by construction.

paddle.note: createPlanImpl creates a Product then a Price and returns `price.id`. It falls back to the plan code only when Paddle returned no id, which is an error path rather than a contract.
paddle.adoptionNote: No listPlans implemented; Paddle products carry custom_data the stamp could live in, which makes this brand the first list-and-adopt follow-up.

lemonsqueezy.shape: variant id, else the plan code
lemonsqueezy.note: Variants are dashboard-managed; createPlanImpl returns `metadata.variantId` when the designer supplied one and otherwise echoes `input.code`. Seeding the variant id is the intended path.
lemonsqueezy.adoptionNote: Variants are dashboard-managed and createPlanImpl mints no vendor object, so there is nothing for a sweep to duplicate or adopt.

mangopay.note: No createPlanImpl - the adapter inherits the base, which throws CapabilityLimitedError. There is no provider-side plan object to reference.

custom.note: Bring-your-own adapter: the project registers it, so the framework cannot state the origin. Whatever the registered createPlan returns is what the provisioning sweep stores. If it implements listPlans, the sweep list-and-adopts through it.

__webhookProvisioning.#: Per-brand WEBHOOK PROVISIONING origin - can a program register this brand's webhook endpoint and receive its signing material back, or must a human do it in the vendor's panel? `api-returns-secret` = the create call answers with the signing secret, so the framework can reach verified-webhook state with no human touching a dashboard (POST /v1/payments/admin/webhooks/provision). `api-no-secret` = an endpoint can be created over the API but no signing secret comes back, because the brand verifies with something else. `panel-only` = the endpoint is registered in the vendor's panel. `shipped` says whether THIS framework implements the capture yet, which is a different fact from whether the vendor offers it. Measured from each adapter's own verifyWebhook and its endpoint-creation calls in _common/nodejs/src/common/payment-providers/.

stripe.note: POST /v1/webhook_endpoints returns the signing secret (whsec_*) ONLY in the creation response - never readable again, only rotatable. createWebhookEndpoint captures it there; rotation is create-then-delete, because a secret only ever comes out of a creation. Because the sweep captures it, `webhookSecret` is PROVISIONING STATE, not an authored configuration key: this brand catalogues no such key (removed in the webhook-provisioning catalog alignment), and the captured value lives under PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

adyen.note: Adyen's Management API creates a standard webhook and generates its HMAC key, so this brand CAN self-provision - but the adapter implements no creation call, so the sweep reports it unsupported. It is the only other brand that can be live-but-unverifiable (requiredFor webhook + webhookVerificationUnavailable), which makes it the first follow-up.

paypal.note: POST /v1/notifications/webhooks creates the webhook and returns its id, but PayPal issues NO signing secret at all: verifyWebhookAsync posts the event back to /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature with that id. Provisioning would capture an id, not a secret - a different shape from the stripe path.

paddle.note: The adapter verifies the Paddle-Signature h1 HMAC with the notification destination's secret key. Paddle's notification-settings API creates a destination and returns that key as endpoint_secret_key, so this brand CAN self-provision - but the adapter implements no creation call, so the sweep reports it unsupported and the key is set by hand (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY).

lemonsqueezy.note: The author CHOOSES the signing secret when creating the webhook in the Lemon Squeezy dashboard, and the adapter requires it to construct - so there is no secret for a create call to hand back and no live-but-unverifiable state to fix.

iyzico.note: iyzico webhook verification uses the configured API secretKey; there is no separate signing key to capture. Verification accepts only V3 signatures and requires the privately configured merchantId for subscription notifications, refusing them when it is absent. The merchantId is never taken from the webhook body. The webhook URL is registered in the merchant panel.

mangopay.note: Mangopay hooks are unsigned GET requests (EventType, RessourceId, Date) and no signing secret exists. The receiver re-fetches the named resource with the adapter's own clientId + apiKey and trusts only that answer, so there is nothing to capture. Hooks are registered per EventType in the Mangopay dashboard or with POST /hooks; the adapter implements no creation call.

__keyMode.#: Per-brand LIVE/TEST credential-mode detectability - can the framework tell, from the entry's own resolved configuration, whether this credential moves REAL money? `key-prefix` = the mode is encoded in the credential string itself (stripe sk_test_/sk_live_); `keyPrefixes` maps each detectable config key to its live/test prefix classes, and ONLY those catalogued prefix strings may ever be echoed into a log or an error - never any further part of the key. `base-url` = the mode is encoded in the endpoint host (`urlKey` names the config key; `sandboxMarkers` are matched case-insensitively BEFORE `liveMarkers`, because iyzico's sandbox host contains its live host as a substring; a base-url row that also names `environmentKey`/`liveValues`/`testValues` falls back to that environment field when the URL matches no marker). `environment-field` = an explicit environment enum config key decides (`environmentKey`/`liveValues`/`testValues`; `environmentDefault` is the value the adapter factory falls back to when the key is unset, so detection answers what the adapter will actually do). `none` = nothing detectable; the mode reports `unknown`. This fact feeds the live-key runtime guard: a detected `live` mode refuses to construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment unless the entry sets `allowLiveInPreview`, and /v1/payments/mock-status reports the mode per provider. Detection rules are mirrored (and parity-tested) in _common/nodejs/src/common/payment-providers/key-mode.ts, which ships inside generated services where this catalog does not exist.

stripe.note: Stripe encodes the mode in every key: sk_/pk_ test vs live, plus rk_ restricted keys. The factory reads secretKey and publishableKey from env only (legacyStripe reads the flat STRIPE_* spellings), so detection reads the same sources. Any live prefix wins over a test prefix - a mixed pair is a misconfiguration and the live half is the dangerous one.

paypal.note: PayPal client id/secret carry no mode marker; the adapter picks api-m.paypal.com vs api-m.sandbox.paypal.com from the `environment` config key, defaulting to sandbox (createPayPalFromManifest).

iyzico.note: iyzico keys carry no mode marker; the sandbox and live accounts differ only by host (sandbox-api.iyzipay.com vs api.iyzipay.com). Sandbox markers are checked first - the sandbox host CONTAINS the live host as a substring. An empty or unrecognized baseUrl reports unknown.

adyen.note: Adyen's `environment` enum is test/live and the factory defaults it to test (the direction that cannot move real money). The adapter accepts the two values case-insensitively and refuses any other, so a value this table reads as unknown never reaches the live hosts.

paddle.note: Paddle's `environment` enum is sandbox/live and the factory defaults it to sandbox; the API key itself carries no mode marker the framework can rely on.

lemonsqueezy.note: The API key is a JWT with no mode marker, and test mode is a per-store dashboard toggle invisible to the credential - nothing in the entry's configuration encodes the mode.

mangopay.note: Every Mangopay API URL is built from baseUrl, so a recognised host decides: api.mangopay.com (and its api-mtls. twin) is live, api.sandbox.mangopay.com is test, whatever `environment` says (a production baseUrl next to the default environment=sandbox used to pass the guard). An empty or unrecognised baseUrl (a proxy) falls back to the `environment` key: production is live, sandbox is test, unset is unknown (no default).

custom.note: Bring-your-own gateway: the project registers the adapter, so the framework cannot read a mode off an arbitrary credential shape.

kycReturnUrl.doc: Return URL after Connect onboarding completes.

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. Without it, a live-mode credential refuses to construct outside prod (typed PaymentGateError). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_ALLOW_LIVE_IN_PREVIEW or an inline configuration value.

kycRefreshUrl.doc: Refresh URL when the onboarding link expires (falls back to kycReturnUrl).

honourRadarReview.doc: Honour Stripe Radar reviews (default true, also when unset). Stripe captures automatically, so a payment Radar places in review is already succeeded; with this on, every PaymentIntent read expands its charge and review, and a payment under review is held: its ticket stays started with paymentStatus FRAUD_REVIEW, no afterPaymentCaptured, invoice or settlement accrual runs, and a new start of the order answers 409 until the review closes. A review closed approved settles the payment success once; closed refunded_as_fraud or refunded settles it failed (FRAUD_REJECTED, afterPaymentFailed) and the refund Stripe makes runs no refund lifecycle. A payment_intent.succeeded webhook is confirmed by a live read before it settles anything, review.opened and review.closed are mapped and provisioned, and the provider review sweeper is the backstop for a lost review.closed. Only the text or boolean false turns it off (the behaviour from before the review was modelled); any other value is read as true. nodejs services only for now. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_HONOUR_RADAR_REVIEW or an inline configuration value.

newCardThreeDSThreshold.doc: New cards (the Payment Element, where the browser confirms the PaymentIntent, and a fresh browser token pm_ the server confirms): at or above this amount (major units of the charge currency, e.g. 500 for 500.00) the PaymentIntent is created with payment_method_options.card.request_three_d_secure (threeDSRequestLevel, default any), which FORCES 3-D Secure; set at create, it persists to the browser's confirm. Inclusive: a charge equal to the threshold is forced. Below it nothing is written and Stripe and the card issuer decide (Stripe's automatic rule, SCA exemptions included): the service cannot skip a challenge Stripe or the issuer asks for. Unset: never forced (the request is exactly as before). 0 forces every new-card charge. A value that is not 0 or a positive number is read as 0 (always forced, fail closed) and draws PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID. Server configuration only: a caller's providerOptions.payment_method_options.card.request_three_d_secure stays refused (400). nodejs services only for now. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_NEW_CARD_THREE_DSTHRESHOLD (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_NEW_CARD_THREE_DS_THRESHOLD) or an inline configuration value.

savedCardThreeDSMode.doc: Saved-card 3-D Secure model on Stripe, server configuration only. 'threshold': a charge on a stored card (a pm_ attached to the charge's customer) at or above savedCardThreeDSThreshold is forced through 3-D Secure (request_three_d_secure, threeDSRequestLevel); below it Stripe and the issuer decide. 'verifyOnce': a stored card is forced through 3-D Secure (request_three_d_secure, threeDSRequestLevel) on every charge until a charge on it is AUTHENTICATED; the stored payment method is then marked threeDSVerified (with threeDSVerifiedAt, machine-written on the auth service through setPaymentMethodThreeDSVerifiedForMachine, never by a request body, an attach or a webhook payload) and its later charges are not forced: Stripe and the issuer still decide, so Stripe may still challenge, and a charge completed without 3-D Secure carries no liability shift. The mark is written after the payment settles, by the stored report that claims its capture lifecycle (webhook, refresh, sweeper or the start), only when a live PaymentIntent read (expand latest_charge) shows latest_charge.payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure.result exactly 'authenticated' on the stored method the start recorded (attempt_acknowledged, exempted, failed or none never mark). Only the generated start route and a PaymentAction start or simple, which prove the caller owns the stored method, relax a verified card; the thin startPayment / processSimplePayment shims and a PaymentAction naming a Stripe entry on an order bound to another brand always force. A card added again (POST /v1/payment-methods/add) loses the mark. savedCardThreeDSThreshold is ignored under it (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID); newCardThreeDSThreshold still governs new cards. Needs the auth service: without it no card is marked and every stored-card charge stays forced. Unset with savedCardThreeDSThreshold set: threshold mode. Unset with no threshold: never forced. An unknown value is read as threshold 0 (always forced, fail closed), never as verifyOnce. Stripe can only force 3-D Secure, never skip it, so no value charges a card without the challenge Stripe or the issuer asks for. When the two thresholds give different answers for a charge naming a pm_, the adapter reads the method from Stripe to tell a stored card from a fresh token; a method of another customer, or a failed read, is forced. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DSMODE (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DS_MODE).

savedCardThreeDSThreshold.doc: The amount (major units of the charge currency) from which a saved-card charge is forced through 3-D Secure on Stripe; inclusive. Below it nothing is written and Stripe and the issuer decide. 0 forces every saved-card charge. Missing under savedCardThreeDSMode 'threshold', negative or not a number: read as 0 (always forced, fail closed), with PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID. Ignored under savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce' (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DSTHRESHOLD (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DS_THRESHOLD).

threeDSRequestLevel.doc: The request_three_d_secure value a forced Stripe charge carries: 'any' (default; 3-D Secure runs, a frictionless authentication is allowed) or 'challenge' (Stripe asks the issuer for a challenge). Used only when a threshold forces the charge. Any other value is read as 'any' (the charge is still forced) and draws PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_THREE_DSREQUEST_LEVEL (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_THREE_DS_REQUEST_LEVEL).

threeDSThresholdCurrency.doc: Optional ISO 4217 currency of the Stripe 3-D Secure thresholds (e.g. EUR). When set, a charge in any other currency is forced through 3-D Secure whenever a threshold applies to it, because the threshold amount means nothing in another currency. Unset: the thresholds are read in the charge currency. A value that is not a three-letter code matches no currency, so it forces every charge under a configured threshold (fail closed, PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_CONFIG_INVALID). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_THREE_DSTHRESHOLD_CURRENCY (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_THREE_DS_THRESHOLD_CURRENCY).

savedCardOffSession.doc: Off-session (merchant-initiated) charging of a verified stored card on Stripe, server configuration only. 'never' (default, also when unset): no charge is ever sent with off_session. 'verified': a PaymentAction start or simple on a checkout order object (the ticketed seam, which proves the caller owns the stored method and charges under the order's start-claim idempotency key) that the design declares buyer-absent (PaymentAction.buyerAbsent: true), on a stored pm_ whose proven stored-method row is threeDSVerified, is created with off_session: true and confirm: true, a merchant-initiated transaction (MIT) with no buyer step. A PaymentAction that does not declare buyerAbsent (the default, every buyer-present checkout) is never off-session on this entry, whatever the request carries. It takes effect only beside savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce' (the only mode that marks a card verified) and is never applied on the generated REST start route, the thin startPayment / processSimplePayment shims, an unverified card, a fresh token, a card typed on the page or a charge forced through 3-D Secure; a caller's providerOptions.off_session or setup_future_usage stays refused (400). LIABILITY: an MIT carries no 3-D Secure liability shift, so a fraud chargeback on it is the merchant's; card-network rules allow it only for a charge made while the buyer is absent, under a stored-credential agreement the buyer accepted when the card was saved, never for a buyer-present one-click. When the issuer still asks for authentication Stripe declines with 402 authentication_required: the start releases the order's claim and answers the typed refusal (PAYMENT_DECLINED, providerErrorCode authentication_required), and the buyer pays on-session. Each off-session charge logs one info line (StripeOffSessionCharge, no card data). 'verified' draws the validator warning PAYMENT_PROVIDER_OFF_SESSION_ENABLED (the liability text), and PAYMENT_PROVIDER_OFF_SESSION_NO_BUYER_ABSENT_ACTION when no PaymentAction bound to the entry declares buyerAbsent (the key then does nothing); any other value is read as 'never' (fail closed) and draws PAYMENT_PROVIDER_OFF_SESSION_CONFIG_INVALID, as does 'verified' without verifyOnce. nodejs services only for now. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_OFF_SESSION or an inline configuration value.

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. Without it, a live-mode credential refuses to construct outside prod (typed PaymentGateError). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_ALLOW_LIVE_IN_PREVIEW or an inline configuration value.

merchantId.doc: Private merchant id required to verify subscription V3 webhooks. Configure the merchant's own id privately; it is never read from the webhook payload. Missing merchantId refuses subscription webhook verification with a configuration error. Direct and hosted-payment-page webhooks need no merchantId, and its absence does not prevent provider construction.

baseUrl.doc: iyzico base URL (sandbox or live).

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. Without it, a live-mode credential refuses to construct outside prod (typed PaymentGateError). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_ALLOW_LIVE_IN_PREVIEW or an inline configuration value.

subMerchantPrefix.doc: Optional, marketplace only. Our own namespace for iyzico sub-merchant external ids, not an iyzico field (iyzico has no prefix concept): the adapter sends subMerchantExternalId = <subMerchantPrefix><connected account id>, so several marketplaces or environments can share one iyzico merchant account without their sellers' ids colliding. Empty by default (the id is used unprefixed). Changing it later does not migrate existing sub-merchants: they keep the external id and subMerchantKey stored at creation, and a re-provisioned seller is looked up under the new prefixed id.

savedCardThreeDSMode.doc: Saved-card 3-D Secure model, server configuration only (the client can never choose it). 'verifyOnce': the FIRST charge on a saved card goes through 3-D Secure (POST /payment/3dsecure/initialize); when it settles success at the 3-D Secure return the stored payment method is marked threeDSVerified (with threeDSVerifiedAt, readable on the payment-method record, machine-written only), and later charges on that card skip 3-D Secure (POST /payment/auth) with NO amount limit. The mark is reset when the card is added again. 'threshold': a saved-card charge below savedCardThreeDSThreshold skips 3-D Secure, one at or above it goes through 3-D Secure; threshold 0 is always 3-D Secure. Unset: every saved card goes through 3-D Secure. The retired slice-1 keys threeDSMode / nonThreeDSMaxAmount are not read (a validator WARNING, PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_KEYS_RETIRED, names this key and savedCardThreeDSThreshold instead). Set a non-3DS model only when iyzico has confirmed that your merchant account allows non-3DS charges: without the challenge the issuer's fraud liability shift is lost on those charges (card-not-present fraud chargebacks fall on the merchant), and any caller that may start a payment on a saved card charges it without the cardholder confirming. Only starts that prove the caller owns the saved card skip 3-D Secure. An unknown value is read as threshold 0. nodejs services only for now; other backend languages keep 3-D Secure. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DSMODE (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DS_MODE). A validator WARNING (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_THREE_DS_DISABLED) marks verifyOnce and a threshold above 0.

savedCardThreeDSThreshold.doc: With savedCardThreeDSMode 'threshold' only: the charge amount (major units of the charge currency, e.g. 500 for 500.00 TRY) from which a saved-card charge goes through 3-D Secure; a charge below it skips 3-D Secure (POST /payment/auth). 0 means always 3-D Secure. Missing, negative or not a number: read as 0 (fail closed). Ignored under 'verifyOnce'. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DSTHRESHOLD (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SAVED_CARD_THREE_DS_THRESHOLD).

newCardThreeDSThreshold.doc: New cards (the hosted Checkout Form, every iyzico charge without a saved card): at or above this amount (major units of the charge currency) the form is opened with iyzico's forceThreeDS: 1, so the buyer goes through 3-D Secure. Below it nothing is sent and the form follows the merchant account's own 3-D Secure setting: the framework cannot turn 3-D Secure OFF for a new card, because the card is typed on iyzico's page and never reaches this service (PCI). Unset: never forced (the form's own setting, as before). A value that is not 0 or a positive number is read as 0 (always forced, fail closed). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_NEW_CARD_THREE_DSTHRESHOLD (or PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_NEW_CARD_THREE_DS_THRESHOLD). A new card typed on the project's own frontend (directCardEntry) applies the same threshold, fail closed: at or above it, or with no threshold set, the payment goes through 3-D Secure (POST /payment/3dsecure/initialize); only below a set threshold is it charged without (POST /payment/auth).

directCardEntry.doc: Lets the project's OWN frontend take a new card and the service send it to iyzico, instead of iyzico's hosted Checkout Form. Default false (the hosted form). When true, the start route (PATCH /v1/start<object>payment/:orderId, body paymentUserParams.cardInfo = { cardHolderName, cardNumber, expireMonth, expireYear, cvc } plus an optional saveCard: true) and a PaymentAction start (cardInfo / saveCard request parameters) charge the card: validated server-side first (shape, Luhn, expiry not past, a 3- or 4-digit cvc; a typed 400 that never echoes a value), then POST /payment/3dsecure/initialize at or above newCardThreeDSThreshold (or with no threshold: fail closed; the answer is the saved-card 3-D Secure step, nextAction.raw.threeDSHtmlContent, completed by the service's own 3-D Secure return route) or POST /payment/auth below it (success at once, or a typed 422 with iyzico's code). saveCard: true registers the card under the buyer's own card storage key and files it in the buyer's wallet once the payment settles success; a refused payment saves nothing. A start carrying cardInfo on an entry without this key is refused 400 PAYMENT_DIRECT_CARD_NOT_ENABLED before iyzico is called. PCI: the card then passes through your frontend and this service (never stored, logged or echoed by it), which moves the merchant from the hosted-form scope to the scope of a merchant that handles card data in transit (PCI DSS SAQ D for the service, the frontend in scope too); turn it on only when that is accepted. nodejs services only. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_DIRECT_CARD_ENTRY.

marketplaceActive.doc: The iyzico merchant account is MARKETPLACE-activated (sub-merchants enabled). iyzico then requires a subMerchantKey and subMerchantPrice on every PRODUCT basket item (an unkeyed item is refused with errorCode 5077) on every payment endpoint: the Checkout Form initialize, POST /payment/3dsecure/initialize and POST /payment/auth (a new card typed on the project's own frontend, a saved card and the merchant-initiated recharge alike). With this key true the framework routes every basket: a start whose order row resolves a seller (the marketplace seller binding) is split to that seller (paymentGroup PRODUCT, the seller's key on every item); a start with no seller is the platform's OWN sale and follows ownSaleStrategy. paymentGroup is then framework-owned: a caller's providerOptions.paymentGroup is accepted and overwritten. After capture the framework reads the payment's item transactions and approves the own-sale items (POST /payment/iyzipos/item/approve) only when iyzico reports them as awaiting approval (a LISTING item never does: it settles as transactionStatus 2); an own sale books no seller payout and no seller earnings. A subscription object (iyzico hosted subscriptions) may not bind a marketplace-active entry: iyzico cannot activate subscriptions and sub-merchants on one account, so use a separate iyzico entry for hosted subscriptions (a validator ERROR, PAYMENT_PROVIDER_MARKETPLACE_SUBSCRIPTION_INTERLOCK), or set subscriptionMode 'tokenized', where the framework drives the cycle and every recharge is an own sale. Default false: every request is built exactly as on a plain account. nodejs services only. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_MARKETPLACE_ACTIVE.

ownSaleStrategy.doc: With marketplaceActive true only: how the platform's OWN sales (a start whose order row names no seller) are sent to the marketplace account. 'listing' (the default when unset): paymentGroup LISTING with no subMerchantKey on any item (iyzico refuses a key on a LISTING payment); verified on the iyzico sandbox (a marketplace account, non-3DS POST /payment/auth): the payment succeeds and its item settles to the merchant as transactionStatus 2 (subMerchantKey null, no sub-merchant payout), with no approval step. 'ownSubMerchant': the operator's own iyzico sub-merchant (ownSubMerchantKey, onboarded once for the platform's own legal entity) on every item, subMerchantPrice = the item price, paymentGroup PRODUCT. An unknown value refuses every own sale before the vendor call (400 IYZICO_OWN_SALE_NOT_CONFIGURED). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_OWN_SALE_STRATEGY.

ownSubMerchantKey.doc: With ownSaleStrategy 'ownSubMerchant' only: the subMerchantKey iyzico answered when the operator's own sub-merchant was created (POST /onboarding/submerchant for the platform's own legal entity). Stamped on every own-sale basket item; those items are approved after capture and are never paid out as seller earnings. Missing under 'ownSubMerchant': own sales are refused before the vendor call (400 IYZICO_OWN_SALE_NOT_CONFIGURED), and a validator ERROR (PAYMENT_PROVIDER_OWN_SUB_MERCHANT_KEY_MISSING) is raised when a checkout object without a seller binding uses the entry. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_OWN_SUB_MERCHANT_KEY.

subscriptionMode.doc: Who drives the subscription cycle of this iyzico entry, server configuration only. 'hosted' (the default, also for an absent or unknown value): iyzico's v2 subscription module (plans are provisioned at iyzico, the buyer opens the subscription on iyzico's hosted subscription Checkout Form, renewals arrive as webhooks). 'tokenized': the framework drives the cycle, as for adyen. Plans stay in the local catalog (plans/provision stamps providerPlanId = the plan code, no iyzico call); the subscribe route (POST /v1/subscribe<object>/:orderId) opens the subscription locally on the buyer's stored card, which the opening customer-initiated payment saved (storePaymentMethod on the hosted Checkout Form, or a directCardEntry start with saveCard: true; a subscribe whose buyer has no stored iyzico card is refused 409 SUBSCRIPTION_STORED_CARD_REQUIRED); and every period the recharge scheduler charges that card merchant-initiated with POST /payment/auth, never 3-D Secure: there is no buyer to pass a challenge. Set savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce' (the card is then charged without 3-D Secure once its first 3-D Secure charge settled) or 'threshold', and only when iyzico has confirmed that the merchant account allows non-3DS charges. The card's verified mark is read once, when the buyer subscribes, and kept on the subscription row: the buyer subscribes after the opening payment settled through the service's 3-D Secure return; a subscription opened before that fails every recharge, and the recovery is a new subscription. A recharge that would need 3-D Secure (an unverified card, a threshold the amount reaches, no savedCardThreeDSMode) is settled failed with failureReason RECHARGE_REQUIRES_3DS_VERIFIED_CARD, and a refused one with iyzico's error code; both take a dunning step (maxDunningAttempts, then dunningExhaustedState), neither is left started. On an entry with marketplaceActive the recharge is the platform's own sale (marketplaceRouting own). This is the mode a marketplace-activated iyzico account must use: the hosted v2 subscription module has no sub-merchant support and is refused there (a design-time error). nodejs services only. Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SUBSCRIPTION_MODE.

hmacKey.doc: Adyen webhook HMAC key. Required to VERIFY inbound notifications, not to construct the adapter — without it the adapter is live for payments and only webhook verification refuses.

environment.doc: Adyen environment: 'test' calls the *-test.adyen.com hosts, 'live' the live hosts (with liveEndpointUrlPrefix). Case and surrounding space are forgiven; any other value is refused when the adapter is constructed. Unset means test.

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. Without it, a live-mode credential refuses to construct outside prod (typed PaymentGateError). Resolved from PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_ALLOW_LIVE_IN_PREVIEW or an inline configuration value.

liveEndpointUrlPrefix.doc: Live endpoint URL prefix (required when environment=live).

webhookSecretKey.doc: Paddle Billing notification destination secret key (pdl_ntfset_...), from Paddle > Developer tools > Notifications > (destination) > Secret key. verifyWebhook checks the Paddle-Signature header (ts=<unix>;h1=<hex>): HMAC-SHA256 over '<ts>:<raw body>' keyed with this value, any h1 matching, ts within 5 seconds. Required to VERIFY inbound webhooks, not to construct the adapter: without it the adapter is live for payments and the webhook route answers SIGNATURE_UNVERIFIABLE naming PAYMENT_PROVIDER_<NAME>_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY. Replaces the retired webhookPublicKey (Paddle Classic's RSA public key, which Paddle Billing never signs with); a blueprint that still carries webhookPublicKey gets a warning, and the key is ignored.

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. webhookSecret.doc: OPTIONAL. The secret used when REGISTERING a webhook subscription with Lemon Squeezy — not a verification key. It was formerly catalogued required + requiredFor:'webhook', which forced every integrator to provision a secret no code path consumes and named the wrong field as the verifier.

allowLiveInPreview.doc: Operator escape hatch for the live-key guard: set to true to let a detected LIVE-mode credential construct the real adapter on a non-prod deployment. signingSecret.doc: THE webhook verification key: verifyWebhook computes HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, signingSecret) and constant-time-compares it to the X-Signature header. Also required to CONSTRUCT — the adapter throws PaymentGateError without it — so an inbound webhook can never arrive at a lemonsqueezy adapter that is unable to verify it. That is why lemonsqueezy has no requiredFor:'webhook' key and no webhookVerificationUnavailable().

username.doc: eLogo API account username. Treated as a secret: paired with the password it is a full credential set.

sellerTaxId.doc: The PROJECT's own seller tax identifier (Turkey: VKN) for the documents this integrator account issues - the platform's legal identity, never a fact about an invoiced row. sellerAddress.doc: The PROJECT's own registered address (Turkey: adres) for the documents this integrator account issues. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SELLER_ADDRESS. Not a secret. Overridden by a DataObject sellerParty address binding when one is present.

sellerDistrict.doc: The PROJECT's own registered district (Turkey: ilçe) for the documents this integrator account issues - UBL-TR makes cbc:CitySubdivisionName a MANDATORY PostalAddress member (Uyumsoft's schema validation refused a document without it), so the builder falls back to a documented generic default ('Merkez') when this is unset. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SELLER_DISTRICT. Not a secret. Set the real ilçe for production documents.

sellerCity.doc: The PROJECT's own registered city/province (Turkey: il) for the documents this integrator account issues - UBL-TR makes cbc:CityName a MANDATORY PostalAddress member, so the builder falls back to the party's country context when this is unset. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SELLER_CITY. Not a secret. Set the real il for production documents.

serialPrefix.doc: The 3-uppercase-letter GIB document serial prefix of the e-Arsiv series. TR fiscal documents must carry cbc:ID as a GIB DOCUMENT SERIAL - prefix + 4-digit issue year + 9-digit zero-padded sequence (e.g. ABC2026000000001) - allocated by the fiscal layer at prepare time from the sys_fiscalSerialSequence counter (one counter per prefix) and REUSED on resubmit; the app-side invoice number is correlation data (an AdditionalDocumentReference), never the wire id. GIB keeps e-Fatura and e-Arsiv on SEPARATE series: TR_EARSIV documents draw from serialPrefix, TR_EFATURA documents from eInvoiceSerialPrefix, and the two must differ. REQUIRED for e-Arsiv routes: a TR_EARSIV submission without a valid serialPrefix is refused with a typed 400 naming this key BEFORE any vendor call. Validated [A-Z]{3}. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SERIAL_PREFIX. Not a secret.

serialSequenceStart.doc: The FLOOR of the GIB wire-serial sequence: the first 9-digit sequence number this service may issue under serialPrefix, for an integrator account whose prefix already issued numbers outside this service's own sys_fiscalSerialSequence counter (a migrated account, or a service moved onto a new provider entry). Honoured on every allocation as next = max(lastNumber, serialSequenceStart - 1) + 1, so a fresh counter starts AT this number and a counter already past it just continues; it never lowers a counter and never changes a document that already carries its serial (the burn-and-advance resubmit is unchanged). A whole number from 1 to 999999999; any other value is refused at submission with a typed 400 naming this key, before any vendor call. Optional - unset means the series starts at 1. It does NOT make two services on one provider entry safe (that shape stays the FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED design-time error). Scope it to one year with serialSequenceStartYear: the floor exists because that year's numbers were already issued outside the counter, so with the year set it applies ONLY to that year's serials and every other year starts at 1; without the year it applies every year, so a new year's series starts at the floor again (a design-time WARNING says so). Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START. Not a secret.

serialSequenceStartYear.doc: The 4-digit YEAR the serialSequenceStart floor belongs to. A floor exists because that year's serials were already issued outside this service's counter (a migrated account); with the year set, the floor applies ONLY to allocations whose serial year (the Turkey-local issue year, the year inside the serial) equals it, and every other year's series starts at 1. Unset, the floor applies every year, so each January the new year's series starts at the floor again. Anything but a 4-digit year is refused at submission with a typed 400 naming this key, before any vendor call. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START_YEAR. Not a secret.

eInvoiceSerialPrefix.doc: The 3-uppercase-letter GIB document serial prefix of the e-Fatura series. GIB keeps e-Fatura and e-Arsiv on SEPARATE series, each consecutive on its own, so a TR_EFATURA document (a buyer registered on the e-Fatura network) draws its cbc:ID serial - prefix + 4-digit issue year + 9-digit zero-padded sequence - from this prefix and its own sys_fiscalSerialSequence counter, while TR_EARSIV keeps serialPrefix. Register the series with the integrator first (the account must know a series before a document may carry it). Must differ from serialPrefix: an equal value is refused at design time (FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED) and at submission (typed 400). REQUIRED for e-Fatura routes: a TR_EFATURA submission without a valid eInvoiceSerialPrefix is refused with a typed 400 naming this key BEFORE any vendor call. A resubmit of the same scheme reuses the document's serial; a resubmit whose scheme changed (e-Arsiv refused, then e-Fatura) takes a fresh serial from the new scheme's series. Validated [A-Z]{3}. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_E_INVOICE_SERIAL_PREFIX. Not a secret.

eInvoiceSerialSequenceStart.doc: The FLOOR of the e-Fatura series (eInvoiceSerialPrefix): the first 9-digit sequence number this service may issue under eInvoiceSerialPrefix, with the same contract as serialSequenceStart - next = max(lastNumber, eInvoiceSerialSequenceStart - 1) + 1, a whole number from 1 to 999999999, refused at submission with a typed 400 naming this key otherwise. Optional - unset means the e-Fatura series starts at 1. Scope it to one year with eInvoiceSerialSequenceStartYear (the same rule as serialSequenceStartYear, independently of it). Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_E_INVOICE_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START. Not a secret.

eInvoiceSerialSequenceStartYear.doc: The 4-digit YEAR the eInvoiceSerialSequenceStart floor belongs to - the same rule as serialSequenceStartYear, for the e-Fatura series and independent of it. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_E_INVOICE_SERIAL_SEQUENCE_START_YEAR. Not a secret.

serialAssignment.doc: Who numbers this entry's fiscal documents. "platform" (the default; unset means the same): the fiscal layer allocates the GIB serial (cbc:ID) from its own sys_fiscalSerialSequence counter, with serialPrefix / eInvoiceSerialPrefix and the serialSequenceStart floors. "vendor": the INTEGRATOR numbers each document when it accepts the submission - supported by uyumsoft only (and simulated by mock); any other brand is a design-time ERROR (FISCAL_SERIAL_ASSIGNMENT_UNSUPPORTED) and a typed 400 at submission. In vendor mode the platform keeps no counter for the entry: cbc:ID carries only the series prefix (eInvoiceSerialPrefix for e-Fatura, serialPrefix for e-Arsiv; empty when unset, which numbers from the integrator account's default series), the ETTN (cbc:UUID) and LocalDocumentId are still the platform's and stay the same across re-sends, and the number the integrator answers is written to the fiscal document's documentSerial (null until it is known; recovered from the outbox when the answer was lost). A synchronous refusal consumes no number, so the series stays gapless except for a document the integrator numbered and GIB later refused. The serialSequenceStart floors do not apply (WARNING FISCAL_SERIAL_ASSIGNMENT_VENDOR_IGNORES_FLOOR when set). Operational rules: never mix explicit (platform) and vendor numbering in one series - the integrator's counter does not skip explicitly issued numbers and the series then refuses every document (FISCAL_VENDOR_SERIAL_CONFLICT); a series moved from platform numbering needs its counter at the integrator set past the highest issued number first (or a fresh prefix); a prefix must be defined for the account in the integrator's portal first (Uyumsoft: Ayarlar > Fatura Seri Tanimlari) - an undefined prefix is not refused, the integrator silently numbers from the default series (logged as FISCAL_VENDOR_SERIAL_PREFIX_MISMATCH). Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_SERIAL_ASSIGNMENT. Not a secret.

vatExemptionReasonCode.doc: GIB KDV exemption reason CODE for zero-amount VAT buckets: the schematron requires cbc:TaxExemptionReasonCode + cbc:TaxExemptionReason on every 0015 KDV bucket whose tax amount is 0, at the line-level and document-level TaxTotals alike. Optional - when unset the document builder applies the documented generic default 350 (the KDV exemption list's generic bucket, 'Diğerleri'). This is the PROVIDER-WIDE fallback: a line's own code (InvoiceLineRelation.vatExemptionCodeProperty) wins for that line. Set the real exemption code when the project's zero VAT has a specific legal basis; an exemption code (2xx/3xx, 350 included) makes the document ISTISNA, while 351 (a 0% line that is NOT exempt) keeps SATIS. A value that is not a 3-digit GIB code is a design-time WARNING. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON_CODE. Not a secret.

vatExemptionReason.doc: GIB KDV exemption reason TEXT paired with vatExemptionReasonCode, stamped on the same zero-amount 0015 buckets. Optional - when unset the document builder writes the official GIB text of the resolved code (350: 'Diğerleri'); must be non-empty on the wire (the schematron refuses a blank reason). It pairs ONLY with this entry's own vatExemptionReasonCode: a line or invoice that names its own code gets that code's official text. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON. Not a secret.

A value that is not a 3-digit GIB code is a design-time WARNING. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON_CODE. Not a secret.

vatExemptionReason.doc: GIB KDV exemption reason TEXT paired with vatExemptionReasonCode, stamped on the same zero-amount 0015 buckets. Optional - when unset the document builder writes the official GIB text of the resolved code (350: 'Diğerleri'); must be non-empty on the wire (the schematron refuses a blank reason). It pairs ONLY with this entry's own vatExemptionReasonCode: a line or invoice that names its own code gets that code's official text. Emitted as FISCAL_PROVIDER_<NAME>_VAT_EXEMPTION_REASON. Not a secret.

decisionProvider.__note: Calibrated decision layer (System One models; Jev-first — docs/ADR-decision-layer-system-one.md). Its own family, never a brand under aiProvider: a System One model has no prompt, a typed answer instead of a response format, and free output tokens, so the AI family's price table would misprice a call by ~70x and fire cost ceilings on the cheapest thing in the project. The mock brand is a REAL transport (the payment MOCK_TRANSPORT_BRANDS precedent), so a build never blocks on a missing credential and CI never reaches the network.

apiKey.doc: TypeSafe AI API key (Bearer). Emitted as DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_API_KEY, masked in API responses; never reaches a log line or an error body.

model.doc: PINNED Jev model version sent on every request, e.g. 'jev-1.13.0'. A floating tag ('jev-latest', 'latest', a bare family name) is refused at validation with DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED: an unpinned model answers differently on two consecutive days and breaks every cache whose key includes the model version.

baseUrl.doc: Override for the default https://api.typesafe.ai base URL — test harnesses, mock integrator servers and proxies. Leave empty in production.
Custom decision endpoint base URL — either a TypeSafe-wire-compatible endpoint or the vendor endpoint an emulation apiFormat is spoken against.

apiKey.doc: Optional API key for the custom endpoint (a private emulation endpoint may be keyless). Masked in API responses; never reaches a log line or an error body.

apiFormat.doc: Wire protocol spoken against baseUrl: 'systemone' = the TypeSafe /v1/systemone contract verbatim; 'openai' / 'anthropic' = the decision interface emulated over that vendor's structured-output call.

model.doc: Pinned model version forwarded to the endpoint (systemone) or the underlying LLM model id (openai/anthropic emulation). The DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED rule applies when set.

extraHeaders.doc: Additional HTTP headers sent on every request, as a JSON object (e.g. an internal gateway routing header). NOT masked — real secrets go in apiKey, never here.

seed.doc: Deterministic seed mixed into the mock's answer derivation — the mock answers all three question types (noul/choice/score) deterministically from (seed, state, question), so a generated test can assert on a decision without a key. Optional; defaults to a fixed seed so two builds agree.

__credentials.note: `ownerScope: project` (the default) is the saas level: the mailbox and its credentials are on the entry. `tenant` and `user` turn the entry into a template whose mailboxes the owners connect themselves (the scoped-credential store, family `mail`, at most `maxMailboxesPerOwner` per owner).
Not an organization or overlay family: no sets, no credential mode. The credentials live once on the entry and every bridge brand that names it reads them.

SAP OData base URL.
HubSpot API base URL override.

instanceUrl.doc: ServiceNow instance URL, e.g. https://acme.service-now.com. No connector ships yet.

region.doc: AWS region the bucket ACTUALLY lives in, e.g. us-east-2. The default is a starting value, not a guess to leave alone: real AWS S3 answers 301 PermanentRedirect to a request signed for the wrong region, and on a PRESIGNED url that failure lands in the end user's browser at upload time - past every build, validation and health check. A pilot lost every upload path in its product to a us-east-1 signature against a us-east-2 bucket, which is why validation warns (BUCKET_PROVIDER_AWS_REGION_UNCONFIRMED) when this brand has no endpoint and the region is unset or still the default. S3-COMPATIBLE stores (s3Compatible, r2) ignore the region entirely and are never warned about.

endpoint.doc: Custom endpoint URL; leave empty for AWS S3.

publicPresignBase.doc: Public base URL presigned URLs are signed against when the endpoint is not client-reachable; leave empty for AWS S3.
