__DataMapSimpleItem.doc: Represents a single key-value pair used in most context. The value is constant.

DataMapSimpleItem.__name.doc: The key name for the data item (e.g., a header name or parameter name).
DataMapSimpleItem.__value.doc: The value of the data item, should be deifned as string even it is a number.
DataMapSimpleItem.__secret.doc: Classifies this entry's value as a deploy secret. A secret is masked in the committed env files (a blank $SECRET_ placeholder) and delivered as a CI/CD variable at deploy time. Leave it unset unless you mean to override the default. On a provider configuration entry, true forces a secret, and false or unset lets the provider catalog and the keyword classifier decide: a key named like a credential stays a secret, the flag cannot publish it. On a customVariables entry (project or service), unset means a name with a secret-shaped segment (TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, APIKEY, PASSWORD, PASSWD, PASS, PASSPHRASE, PRIVATE, CREDENTIAL, or a plural of one, split on _ - . and camelCase) is a secret and any other name is plain; true forces a secret; an explicit false keeps the value plain in every committed env file and, for a secret-shaped name, raises the validation warning CUSTOM_VARIABLE_SECRET_SHAPED_PLAIN.
DataMapSimpleItem.name: String

__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.#: An enum representing the HTTP method to use in a request.
__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.GET: Retrieve data from the remote service.
__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.POST: Submit new data to the remote service.
__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.PUT: Replace existing data in the remote service.
__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.PATCH: Partially update existing data in the remote service.
__HTTPRequestMethods.doc.DELETE: Remove data from the remote service.

__APIKeyAuth.doc: Enables API key authentication for the project. When enabled, an OpenAPPL compiler generates an apiKey data object, management APIs (create, list, delete), and validation endpoints. Secret API keys use the sk_mbx_ prefix and allow tokenless, session-based authentication — ideal for server-to-server integrations, AI agents, CI/CD pipelines, and MCP connections. Public API keys are defined in the configuration schema for future support but are not yet implemented.

APIKeyAuth.__useAPIKeyForAuthentication.doc: Enable or disable API key authentication for this project. When true, the auth service will include the apiKey data object and key management APIs.
APIKeyAuth.__configuration.doc: Configuration for API key behavior, required when useAPIKeyForAuthentication is true (a null configuration is refused with REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING). An empty object keeps the defaults: secret-only keys sent in the Bearer header. Set its fields to customize key types, locations, or names.

__APIKeyAuthConfig.doc: Fine-tune API key authentication behavior. Controls which key types are generated, where keys are located in requests, and the custom header, query parameter, cookie or body field name. With its fields left unset (an empty object), the generated service defaults to secret-only keys in the Authorization Bearer header with the sk_mbx_ prefix — no additional configuration needed for standard usage. Note: public API key fields (publicApiKeyLocation, publicApiKeyName) are reserved for future support and have no effect currently.

APIKeyAuthConfig.__apiKeyType.doc: The type of API keys to generate. 'secret' (default) creates sk_mbx_-prefixed keys that authenticate on behalf of a user and create server-side sessions. 'public' and 'both' options are reserved for future support — only 'secret' is currently implemented.
APIKeyAuthConfig.__secretApiKeyLocation.doc: Where secret API keys are read from in HTTP requests. Defaults to 'bearer' (Authorization: Bearer sk_mbx_...). When set to 'header', 'query', 'cookie' or 'body', the secretApiKeyName field names the header, query parameter, cookie or request-body field. The other location values ('urlpath', 'session', 'request') are not supported: no key is read from them.
APIKeyAuthConfig.__publicApiKeyLocation.doc: Reserved for future support. Where public API keys will be sent in HTTP requests. Defaults to 'query'. Has no effect until public API key support is implemented.
APIKeyAuthConfig.__secretApiKeyName.doc: Custom header, query parameter, cookie or request-body field name for secret API keys. Required when secretApiKeyLocation is not 'bearer': without it no key is read. When location is 'bearer', the sk_mbx_ prefix is used for automatic detection and this field is ignored.
APIKeyAuthConfig.__publicApiKeyName.doc: Reserved for future support. Custom header or query parameter name for public API keys. Has no effect until public API key support is implemented.

__APIKeyType.doc.#: Specifies the type of API key to use. This can be either 'secret', 'public', or 'both'. If not set, the default is 'secret'. If you need to use both secret and public keys, you can set this to 'both'.
__APIKeyType.doc.secret: Secret API key is used in trusted parties to access on behalf of the user to the sensitive data.
__APIKeyType.doc.public: Public API key is used to identify the client's public access key. Use public keys if you need to identify the client when you need to identify the client when from a frontend based access to non-sensitive data.
__APIKeyType.doc.both: Both secret and public API keys are used. This is useful if you need to use both secret and public keys for the same client.

__LoginDefinition.doc: Defines the core login architecture of the project, including the user and tenant structures that underpin authentication and access. These settings enable an OpenAPPL compiler to generate a built-in 'auth' service tailored to your data model, supporting user registration, login, permissions, and optional multi-tenant behavior.

LoginDefinition.__userSettings.doc: Defines how the built-in user object is configured and authenticated within the project. While the user data model is fully managed by the compiler, this setting allows you to control aspects such as super admin credentials, registration behavior, user group support, and whether mobile-based features are enabled. These settings shape how authentication flows and access are handled at the user level.
LoginDefinition.__tenantSettings.doc: Configuration for multi-tenant applications, including tenant object definitions and their relationship to users and user groups. When enabled, this isolates resources by tenant and supports tenant-scoped access control. Omit this section for single-tenant projects.

__LoginDefUserSettings.doc: Defines how users are stored, managed, and authenticated within the project. This includes super admin credentials, login identifiers, optional mobile and email verification settings, public registration policies, and whether user groups are active. This structure governs the behavior and structure of the user service's primary data model.

LoginDefUserSettings.__superAdminIdentifier.doc: The login identifier of the super admin user. This user has full permissions across the project and is not tenant-scoped. DEFAULTS TO THE PROJECT OWNER'S OWN IDENTITY: project creation stamps the creating user's email (or mobile, on a mobile-primary project) here, so the bootstrap account is addressable at an inbox a real person owns. Do NOT replace it with a cosmetic invention like 'superadmin@<project>.com' — a made-up address receives no password-reset mail and may collide with a real user of the project. When primaryLoginIdentifier is 'email' or 'emailOrMobile' this must be an email address; when 'mobile', a number in E.164 format (e.g. +905551234567). Changing this value only affects a project whose database does not yet hold the super-admin row: once seeded, the identifier is owned by the target database and is changed from the preview/deployer DB admin panels instead.
LoginDefUserSettings.__superAdminPassword.doc: The bootstrap password of the super admin user, seeded into the project database in EVERY environment (dev, preview, stage, prod) so a freshly deployed project always has a working administrator. Project creation mints a random per-project value; leave it as generated rather than authoring a memorable literal. It is deliberately readable in the blueprint — it is the only credential that exists before anyone has logged in, so the owner reads it back to perform the first login and the preview panel/frontends prefill it. What protects stage and production is scope, not secrecy: a session authenticated with the unrotated seed password receives 403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED on every route except the password-rotation surface, so it can be used to take ownership of the account and nothing else. Once the super-admin row exists in the target database this value no longer affects it — rotate through the application's own password flow.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userNameType.doc: Specifies whether the user's name will be stored as a single 'fullname' or as separate 'name' and 'surname' fields.
LoginDefUserSettings.__superAdminData.doc: Preset values for the super admin user. Required only for custom properties beyond the standard fields (email, name, password, etc.).
LoginDefUserSettings.__primaryLoginIdentifier.doc: Specifies which field is used as the primary login identifier. When set to 'mobile', users register and log in with a phone number instead of email. When set to 'emailOrMobile', both are supported. Defaults to 'email' for backward compatibility.
LoginDefUserSettings.__secondaryIdentifierPresence.doc: Controls whether the non-primary identifier field (mobile when email is primary, email when mobile is primary) is stored in the user data model. When set to 'none', the field is omitted entirely. When 'optional', the field exists but is not required. When 'required', the field must be provided during registration. Ignored when primaryLoginIdentifier is 'emailOrMobile' (both fields always exist).
LoginDefUserSettings.__dualIdentifierRegistration.doc: Only applies when primaryLoginIdentifier is 'emailOrMobile'. Controls whether users must provide both email and mobile during registration, or just one of them. When 'atLeastOne', users can register with either identifier. When 'both', users must provide both.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userGroupsActive.doc: Indicates whether user group functionality is enabled. When active, a 'userGroup' data object is added to the user service with fixed fields (id, name, description), optionally scoped by tenant.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userRegisterIsPublic.doc: Determines if users can self-register. If false, only administrators can create users.
LoginDefUserSettings.__registrationExcludedUserProperties.doc: Custom user properties (declared in `authentication.userProperties`) that the PUBLIC registration door must not accept. Every custom user property is otherwise added to `register`, `registerUser`, `register<Tenant>Owner` and `register<Tenant>User` as an optional body parameter AND as a write target, so an internal column — a moderation flag (`isBanned`), a lifecycle stamp (`bannedAt`), a credit balance — can be set by the caller who is signing themselves up. Listing the property here removes it from those four apis' requestParameters and dataClauseItems entirely; the column keeps its `basicSettings.defaultValue` at registration. The property stays fully writable on the ADMIN doors — `createUser`, `create<Tenant>OwnerOnSaas`, `create<Tenant>UserOnSaas` — and on any role-gated api the project declares for it, so this is a narrowing of the public surface only, never of the data model. Entries MUST name custom user properties: the built-in identity and system columns (email, password, the name shape, roleId, the verification flags) are governed by their own settings and naming one here is a design-time error. Leave empty (the default) to keep every custom property on the register surface.
A custom user property (from `authentication.userProperties`) to keep off the public register apis.
LoginDefUserSettings.__emailVerificationRequiredForLogin.doc: Indicates whether users must verify their email address before they can log in. Related verification flows must be enabled in VerificationServices. Every login door honours it: the password login and the social login (OAuth callback) both refuse an unverified user with 403 errMsg_EmailNotVerified, and a social registration whose provider email is not verified (see the provider's emailVerification setting) creates an unverified account that verifies through the normal email verification flow before it can log in. Default true, applied wherever the flag is read (the design tool, the generated password login, the social login and the registration auto-login), so a blueprint that omits the key requires a verified email; set false explicitly to turn it off. An omitted key without an enabled verificationServices.emailVerification flow is warned about (VERIFICATION_FLOW_MISMATCH_BY_DEFAULT). A registration issues no session (no auto-login, emailVerificationNeeded: true) under exactly the condition the login refuses: the requirement on a project whose users have an email, required or optional. Only a user who HAS an email is gated: with an optional email the check is `user.email == null || user.emailVerified === true` (a user registered without an email logs in; one with an unverified email is refused), with a required email it is `user.emailVerified === true`. An optional email sent empty (`''`) is stored as null, so that user has no email. Unlike email2FARequiredForLogin, this requirement is allowed on an optional email. relogin (refresh token or live session) re-reads the user row and applies the same check with the same 403, so an old refresh token cannot mint a session for a user whose email is no longer verified.
LoginDefUserSettings.__mobileVerificationRequiredForLogin.doc: Indicates whether users must verify their mobile number before logging in. This applies only when the mobile field is present in the user data model (i.e. secondaryIdentifierPresence is not 'none' when email is primary, or always when mobile is primary or emailOrMobile). The password login and the social login (OAuth callback) both refuse an unverified mobile with 403 errMsg_MobileNotVerified. Default false, applied wherever the flag is read, so a blueprint that omits the key does not require a verified mobile. A registration issues no session (no auto-login, mobileVerificationNeeded: true) under exactly the condition the login refuses: the requirement on a project whose users have a mobile. Only a user who HAS a mobile is gated: with an optional mobile the check is `user.mobile == null || user.mobileVerified === true`, with a required mobile it is `user.mobileVerified === true`. An optional mobile sent empty (`''`) is stored as null, so that user has no mobile. Unlike mobile2FARequiredForLogin, this requirement is allowed on an optional mobile. relogin (refresh token or live session) re-reads the user row and applies the same check with the same 403.
LoginDefUserSettings.__email2FARequiredForLogin.doc: Indicates whether two-factor authentication via email is required during login. Related verification flows must be enabled in VerificationServices. Default false, applied wherever the flag is read (an omitted key never arms the login second factor). The password login, relogin and the social login stamp sessionNeedsEmail2FA from one decision. It needs a REQUIRED email: true together with an optional (or absent) email, judged by primaryLoginIdentifier / secondaryIdentifierPresence / dualIdentifierRegistration, is a design-time error (LOGIN_2FA_ON_OPTIONAL_IDENTITY); make the email required or set this flag to false.
LoginDefUserSettings.__mobile2FARequiredForLogin.doc: Indicates whether two-factor authentication via mobile is required during login. This applies only when the mobile field is present in the user data model. Default false, applied wherever the flag is read (an omitted key never arms the login second factor). The password login, relogin and the social login stamp sessionNeedsMobile2FA from one decision. It needs a REQUIRED mobile: true together with an optional mobile, judged by primaryLoginIdentifier / secondaryIdentifierPresence / dualIdentifierRegistration, is a design-time error (LOGIN_2FA_ON_OPTIONAL_IDENTITY); make the mobile required or set this flag to false.
LoginDefUserSettings.__announceLoginEvent.doc: Whether a successful login publishes the `<codename>-auth-service-user-logged-in` Kafka event carrying the freshly minted session. Defaults to true, which is the historical behavior — leave it on whenever anything in the project (an event notification, a subscription, a hub event, an agent controller, a kafka-triggered business api or edge controller) consumes the login event, or whenever an external system is wired to the topic. Set it to false on a project that has no login-event consumer: the publish is then omitted from the generated login api entirely, which drops one Kafka round-trip from the login hot path and clears the TOPIC_NO_CONSUMER advisory validateProject otherwise raises for a topic nobody listens to. Turning it off does NOT affect the userSession row, the session cache, or the login response — only the event fan-out.
LoginDefUserSettings.__allowUserLevel2FA.doc: Opt-in per-user login second factor. Default false: the login second factor is project-global only (email2FARequiredForLogin / mobile2FARequiredForLogin). When true, the auth user object gains framework-owned enrolment flags, one per 2FA channel whose verification flow is active: `email2FAEnabled` (when verificationServices.email2Factor is active) and `mobile2FAEnabled` (when verificationServices.mobile2Factor is active and the user object has a mobile). Both default false. The password login, relogin (refresh token alone) and the social login stamp sessionNeedsEmail2FA for a user whose `email2FAEnabled` is true, and sessionNeedsMobile2FA for a user whose `mobile2FAEnabled` and `mobileVerified` are both true, IN ADDITION to the global flags: a global flag still challenges every user, enrolled or not. The 2FA-pending session completes through the same email/mobile 2FA start and complete routes and is gated by the same checkValidLogin second-factor gate. The flags are not writable through register, updateUser or updateProfile. The session owner changes them only through the enrolment routes `POST /api/auth/verify/email-2factor-enrolment/start|complete` and `POST /api/auth/verify/mobile-2factor-enrolment/start|complete`: start takes `enable` (true to enrol, false to disenrol) and sends a code to that channel, complete takes the `secretCode` and writes the flag, the enrolment code is valid for at most 10 minutes and five attempts, counted atomically, so turning a factor on or off needs a completed challenge of that channel; a session that still owes its login second factor is refused, so a pending session cannot disenrol itself. An administrator resets them through `PATCH /user2faenrolment/:userId` (the updateUserVerification gate). `/currentuser` returns both flags; they carry no secret. A true value with neither 2FA verification flow active is warned about (USER_LEVEL_2FA_WITHOUT_FLOW): no enrolment flag is emitted and no user can enrol. Implemented by the nodejs, java, dotnet and rust auth services: a build whose auth service is generated in another language refuses the flag (USER_LEVEL_2FA_LANGUAGE), because that login would not enforce the enrolled factor; where the language is known only advisorily it is warned as USER_LEVEL_2FA_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userGroupsInTenantLevel.doc: If true, user groups are defined per tenant; otherwise, they are defined globally across the SaaS. Applies only when user groups are enabled.
LoginDefUserSettings.__loginBlockedProperty.doc: Names ONE custom user property (declared in `authentication.userProperties`) whose value decides whether the account may log in at all — the moderation / account-status gate. Leave it null (the default) and login is refused only for the framework's own reasons (soft-deleted row, unverified email, unverified mobile). Set it to a property such as `accountStatus` and list the refusing values in `loginBlockedValues`: every session-minting path (login, relogin, api-key exchange, trusted proxy login, auto-login after register) then refuses the account while the property holds one of those values, and lets it in again the moment the value leaves the set. This is deliberately NOT a soft delete: the row keeps `isActive: true`, so a suspended user still appears in admin and user-directory reads and can be un-suspended by writing the property back. The property must exist on the user object — naming one that is not declared in `authentication.userProperties` is a design-time error, since the gate would otherwise read `undefined` forever and silently never fire. Only custom properties are accepted: the built-in verification/soft-delete columns already have their own switches (`emailVerificationRequiredForLogin`, `mobileVerificationRequiredForLogin`, `isActive`).
LoginDefUserSettings.__loginBlockedValues.doc: The values of `loginBlockedProperty` that REFUSE a login. Each is matched against the value the user row carries, so `['suspended','banned']` on an Enum property blocks exactly those two states and lets `active` (or any other value, including null) through. Required when `loginBlockedProperty` is set — a named property with no blocked values is a gate that can never fire — and meaningless without it. Model the gate so the permitted state is the DEFAULT value of the property: a user created before the gate existed, or created by a path that does not set the property, must be able to log in.
LoginDefUserSettings.__loginBlockedValues.doc_array: A value of the blocked property that refuses login (e.g. `suspended`).
LoginDefUserSettings.__loginBlockedErrorCode.doc: The error code / message the refusal carries, so a frontend can tell a moderation block apart from a refused credential (401 `errMsg_InvalidCredentials`) or an unverified email (403 `errMsg_EmailNotVerified`). Defaults to `errMsg_AccountBlocked`. Applies only when `loginBlockedProperty` is set.
LoginDefUserSettings.__loginBlockedStatus.doc: The HTTP status the refusal returns. Defaults to `403` — the caller is authenticated (the password matched) but the account is not permitted to hold a session. Any ErrorStatus value is accepted; `429` suits a TEMPORARY lockout that clears with time (callers retry a 429, errorCode TOO_MANY_REQUESTS), never a permanent block. Applies only when `loginBlockedProperty` is set.
LoginDefUserSettings.__archivedIdentifierReuse.doc: When the login identifier (email / mobile) of an ARCHIVED user account may register a new account. `afterDays` (the default) keeps the identifier reserved for `archivedIdentifierHoldDays` days after the archive: inside that window `register`, `registerUser` and `createUser` (and the social registration that runs through `register`) refuse it with 400 `YourProfileIsArchivedAskAnAdminToRestore` (`ThisProfileIsArchivedAskAnAdminToRestore` on the admin `createUser`); after it, the registration creates a NEW account with a new id and the archived one stays archived. `never` keeps the identifier reserved for as long as the archived account exists, so it can only come back through the admin `restoreUser` api (`PATCH /users/:userId/restore`). An archived row whose archive time is not recorded is never matched by the `afterDays` window.
LoginDefUserSettings.__archivedIdentifierHoldDays.doc: How many days an archived account's login identifier stays reserved when `archivedIdentifierReuse` is `afterDays`. A positive integer, default 30 (the historical fixed window). Ignored with `never`.
LoginDefUserSettings.__selfArchive.doc: The built-in self-delete door `archiveProfile` (`DELETE /archiveprofile/:userId`, an owner archiving their own account). `enabled` (the default, the historical behaviour): every signed-in user may archive their own account; the generated output is unchanged. `adminOnly`: the route stays, but only the admin roles of the user-management gate (`deleteUser`'s: superAdmin / admin, or superAdmin / tenantAdmin on a multi-tenant project) may call it, still on their OWN account; any other caller is refused 403. `disabled`: the auth service does not emit `archiveProfile` at all (no route, so 404; no MCP tool, no SDK / panel / doc mention), and the name is free for a custom auth api. Use `disabled` (or `adminOnly`) when the project owns its account-deletion flow, for example a custom `deleteMyAccount` api that checks cross-service blockers (unpaid earnings, pending refunds) before it archives: with the built-in door left on, a direct caller skips those checks. Admins keep archiving any account through `deleteUser` in every mode.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userGroupAutoAvatarScript.doc: An MScript expression that generates a default avatar for the user group. This is used when no avatar is provided in the request.
LoginDefUserSettings.__userAutoAvatarScript.doc: An MScript expression that generates a default avatar for the user. This is used when no avatar is provided in the request.

__UserNameType.doc.#: Specifies how user names are represented in the data model.
__UserNameType.doc.asFullname: Stores the user's name in a single 'fullname' field.
__UserNameType.doc.asNamePair: Stores the user's name in separate 'name' and 'surname' fields.

__PrimaryLoginIdentifier.doc.#: Specifies which field is used as the primary login identifier for user accounts.
__PrimaryLoginIdentifier.doc.email: Email is the primary login identifier. Users must register and log in with an email address. This is the default behavior.
__PrimaryLoginIdentifier.doc.mobile: Mobile number is the primary login identifier. Users register and log in with a phone number (WhatsApp-style). Email becomes optional.
__PrimaryLoginIdentifier.doc.emailOrMobile: Both email and mobile are supported as login identifiers. Users can register and log in with either an email address or a mobile number.

__SecondaryIdentifierPresence.doc.#: Controls the presence and requirement level of the non-primary identifier field in the user data model.
__SecondaryIdentifierPresence.doc.none: The secondary identifier field is not stored in the user data model at all. When email is primary, mobile is omitted. When mobile is primary, email is omitted.
__SecondaryIdentifierPresence.doc.optional: The secondary identifier field exists in the user data model but is not required during registration. Users may optionally provide it.
__SecondaryIdentifierPresence.doc.required: The secondary identifier field exists in the user data model and must be provided during registration.

__DualIdentifierRegistration.doc.#: Controls registration behavior when primaryLoginIdentifier is 'emailOrMobile'. Ignored for other primaryLoginIdentifier values.
__DualIdentifierRegistration.doc.atLeastOne: Users must provide at least one identifier (email or mobile) during registration. They can log in with whichever they provided.
__DualIdentifierRegistration.doc.both: Users must provide both email and mobile during registration. Both fields are required and both can be used for login.

__ArchivedIdentifierReuse.doc.#: When the login identifier of an archived user account may register a new account (LoginDefUserSettings.archivedIdentifierReuse).
__ArchivedIdentifierReuse.doc.afterDays: The identifier stays reserved for archivedIdentifierHoldDays days after the archive; after that a registration creates a new account with a new id.
__ArchivedIdentifierReuse.doc.never: The identifier stays reserved for as long as the archived account exists; only the admin restoreUser api brings it back.

__SelfArchiveMode.doc.#: Who may call the built-in archiveProfile self-delete route (LoginDefUserSettings.selfArchive).
__SelfArchiveMode.doc.enabled: Every signed-in user archives their own account (the default, the historical behaviour).
__SelfArchiveMode.doc.adminOnly: The route stays, gated to the admin roles of the user-management gate; an admin archives only their own account through it, every other caller gets 403.
__SelfArchiveMode.doc.disabled: The built-in archiveProfile route is not emitted (404); the project provides its own account-deletion flow, and the name is free for a custom auth api.

__LoginDefTenantSettings.doc: Specifies how tenant-based access control is structured for multi-tenant projects. This includes the tenant object name, registration permissions, and tenant separation logic. When enabled, this enforces strict data and user isolation by tenant.

LoginDefTenantSettings.__useMultiTenantFeature.doc: Enable this if the project requires multi-tenant architecture. If false, the project will be treated as single-tenant and no tenant-based separation is applied. Generated code carries only the tenancy form this setting selects (for example the OAuth login router's tenant-scoped lookup), decided at code generation rather than checked per request, so changing it takes effect on the next build. The string "true" is read as true by every design-time check and by the build alike, so validateService, the build gate and validateProject agree on which objects carry the tenant column.
LoginDefTenantSettings.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for tenant settings. Leave it null if useMultiTenantFeature is false.

__LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.doc: Configuration details for tenant-based access control, including tenant registration, naming, and avatar script.

LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__tenantRegisterIsPublic.doc: If true, any user can create a tenant. If false, only SaaS admins can register tenants. When a user creates a tenant, they are automatically assigned as the tenant owner.
LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__tenantName.doc: Defines the name of the tenant object in the system (e.g., 'client', 'organization', 'workspace'). This name will be used to generate code, database models, and field references. It must start with a lowercase letter: the tenant foreign-key column every tenant-scoped object carries is synthesized as the lower-first name plus 'Id', so an upper-first value is normalized to camelCase automatically. REQUIRED whenever `useMultiTenantFeature` is on: a value that is absent, blank, whitespace-only or not a string is REFUSED at design time (`AUTH_TENANT_NAME_REQUIRED`), because a multi-tenant project with no name for its tenant model emits a tenant id column on the auth user that nothing seeds or stamps and no tenant column at all on your own objects. Turn `useMultiTenantFeature` off for a single-tenant project instead; there `tenantName` is ignored and may stay null. The tenant codename HEADER rule is a separate contract and is unchanged by that refusal, because it also serves single-tenant and not-yet-validated projects. A blank or whitespace-only value is treated as absent and the default name 'tenant' is used; surrounding whitespace is trimmed (a padded '  store  ' is 'store'), so the tenant codename header the services read is always `mbx-<tenantName>-codename` built from the trimmed name (or the `tenantNameHeaderName` override).
LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__tenantNameHeaderName.doc: Optional HTTP header name used to carry the tenant codename. A nonblank value overrides the default `mbx-<tenantName>-codename` header; blank or omitted values use that default.
LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__tenantAutoAvatarScript.doc: An MScript expression that generates a default avatar for the tenant. This is used when no avatar is provided in the request.
LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__uniqueTenantName.doc: If true, two active tenants may not share the same `name`, and the owner-provisioning APIs refuse a replay instead of minting a second tenant. Default FALSE, because one person legitimately owning several tenants (and two unrelated tenants both called 'Acme') is a valid product shape and must keep working. Turn it on when the tenant name is a real identity in your product. It marks the tenant's `name` property unique, which emits a single unique database index on that column (partial on `isActive`, so a soft-deleted tenant releases its name), so the refusal is a constraint the database enforces and not a read-then-write probe two concurrent registrations can both pass; the loser gets a 409. The rule compares names EXACTLY: 'Acme', 'acme' and 'Acme Ltd' are three different tenant names to it, and so are two names differing only in interior whitespace. Note that `codename` being unique is NOT this rule: the codename is server-minted with a counter suffix ('acme' then 'acme1'), so it can never collide and therefore never refuses anything. If you also declare a `compositeIndexSettings` entry covering `name`, that composite wins and this knob ships nothing (the project validator warns).
LoginDefTenantSettingsConfig.__compositeIndexSettings.doc: Composite indexes for the tenant object, for a tenant identity that is a PAIR of columns rather than a single name (e.g. `name` + a declared region property). Each entry is the same { indexName, indexFields, onDuplicate } shape a DataObject's compositeIndexSettings takes, and `indexFields` may name a built-in tenant column (`name`, `codename`, `fullname`, `avatar`, `ownerId`), one of your own `tenantProperties`, or a framework column every object carries (`id`, `isActive`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `_archivedAt`). A name that is none of those is REFUSED at design time, the same way a DataObject composite index refuses a column its object does not declare. MULTI-COLUMN ONLY: a composite index is named after its fields, so a single-field entry collides with the plain index that column already has and the unique constraint is never created in the database - the project validator warns about it. Express single-column uniqueness through that tenant property's `indexSettings.unique`, or through `uniqueTenantName` for the tenant name.

__VerificationServices.doc:
Defines user-related verification features such as password resets and two-factor authentication (2FA). An OpenAPPL compiler generates backend support code for these features automatically, based on this configuration, as part of the user service module.

WHERE THE CODE GOES, PER DEPLOYMENT SLOT. Preview and a local dev stack answer start/complete WITH the secret code, so a flow completes without a mailbox or handset. Stage and production NEVER put the code in the answer. On every slot the code is also sent: through the configured mail/SMS provider when its credentials are set; otherwise mail goes to the built-in mail sink (every slot) and SMS goes to the built-in SMS sink on dev, preview and stage, which stores each SMS in the mail sink as a mail to sms-<digits>@sms-sink.invalid. Production has no SMS sink for a DECLARED sms provider without credentials: the send fails there. A project that declares NO sms provider sends every SMS to the SMS sink on every slot, production included - the mail sink's rule for a project without a mail provider - so its mobile flows are built, no VERIFICATION_FLOW_MISSING_PROVIDER is reported, and validation warns once with SMS_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK (non-blocking) until a real sms provider is declared. On the local FARM both sinks are read in the Mailpit inbox (http://localhost:18025); where a stage deployment's sink inbox is read is not documented yet. A project that declares NO email provider sends its email flows to the mail sink on every slot, production included, and validation warns once with MAIL_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK (non-blocking) until a real email provider is declared.

NO APPROVE FLOW. There is no approve-by-email / approve-by-mobile verification flow and no block for one: the standalone action-approve flows (a start / complete pair keyed by a caller-chosen action id) are retired, and a blueprint carrying `completeActionApproveByEmail` / `completeActionApproveByMobile` is refused UNKNOWN_PROPERTY. A critical operation asks for a step-up approval where it runs: `authOptions.requireApproval` on the Business API (ApiApprovalRequirement), a fixed pipeline milestone after the authorization checks and before the first write, bound to the call's input.

VerificationServices.__verificationSettings.doc: General options for all verifications. Its only field, verificationMode, is RETIRED: whether a verification answer carries the code is decided by the deployment slot, not by the blueprint.
VerificationServices.__passwordResetByEmail.doc: Configures email-based password reset functionality. Includes template, expiration, and verification strategy (link or code).
VerificationServices.__passwordResetByMobile.doc: Configures SMS-based password reset functionality. Requires active mobile field in user schema.
VerificationServices.__email2Factor.doc: Enables and configures two-factor authentication via email. Typically used during login or sensitive actions.
VerificationServices.__mobile2Factor.doc: Enables and configures two-factor authentication via SMS. Requires mobile phone to be active in user schema.
VerificationServices.__emailVerification.doc: Configures email verification flow, including delivery method (link or code), expiration, and resend timing.
VerificationServices.__mobileVerification.doc: Configures mobile verification flow via SMS, with support for link-based or code-based confirmation. The SMS goes through the project's declared sms provider; on dev, preview and stage a provider whose credentials are not set sends to the built-in SMS sink instead, while production fails the send. With no sms provider declared the SMS goes to the SMS sink on every deployment (see VerificationServices).

__VerificationSettings.doc: General options for all verifications. Its only field, verificationMode, is RETIRED and has no effect: the deployment slot decides whether a verification answer carries the code.
__PasswordResetByEmail.doc: Configuration for enabling password reset via email. Defines whether the feature is active, how long the reset token remains valid, and how frequently a user can request resending the verification message.
__PasswordResetByMobile.doc: Configuration for enabling password reset via mobile. Specifies token expiration time, resend intervals, and verification type (link or code).
__Email2Factor.doc: Configuration for email-based two-factor authentication. Activates the feature and defines verification expiration and resend rules.
__Mobile2Factor.doc: Configuration for mobile-based two-factor authentication. Allows setup of token validity duration, resend rate, and type of verification mechanism.
__EmailVerification.doc: Defines the settings for verifying a user's email address. Includes token expiration duration, resend interval, and whether verification is handled via link or code.
__MobileVerification.doc: Defines the settings for verifying a user's mobile number. Includes resend interval, expiration period, and verification method (link or code).

VerificationSettings.__verificationMode.doc: RETIRED - leave it at the default or remove it; the value has no effect. The deployment slot alone decides whether the verification start/complete answers carry the secret code (and the userId): the preview deployment and a local dev stack always answer with them, so flows can be completed without a mailbox; stage and production never do, whatever this field says, and the code reaches the user only through the configured mail/SMS provider (or a sink: mail with no complete mail provider goes to the deployment's mail sink, on dev, preview and stage an SMS whose sms provider has no credentials set goes to the SMS sink, which stores it in the mail sink as a mail to sms-<digits>@sms-sink.invalid, and a project with no sms provider sends every SMS there on every deployment). It used to let stage follow the blueprint; a stage deployment is a real, reachable environment with real users, so that no longer depends on one blueprint value. A blueprint carrying the field still validates; a value other than the default draws the VERIFICATION_MODE_INERT warning.

__VerificationMode.doc.#: RETIRED: the value of verificationMode has no effect; the deployment slot decides (preview and dev: test mode, stage and production: live mode).
__VerificationMode.doc.testMode: The default. Inert: the preview and dev slots always answer with the secret code, stage and production never do.
__VerificationMode.doc.liveMode: Inert (VERIFICATION_MODE_INERT): stage and production are always live, whatever this says; preview and dev are always test mode.

PasswordResetByEmail.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for password reset by email. Leave it null if passwordResetByEmailIsActive is false.

__VerificationConfig.doc: Defines the configuration for verification flows, including password resets and two-factor authentication. This object is used when the respective feature is active.

VerificationConfig.__resendTimeWindow.doc: Interval in seconds before the user can request another verification message.
VerificationConfig.__expireTimeWindow.doc: Duration in seconds after which the verification link/code expires.
VerificationConfig.__verificationType.doc: Specifies whether verification is triggered by clicking a link or entering a code.
VerificationConfig.__verificationTemplate.doc: An ejs template source to render the message that will be sent to the user for the verification process. The template will be rendered with the verification data that includes the user object. The framework sends it through the notification service for every active flow. (There is no approve-by-email / approve-by-mobile flow: the standalone action-approve flows are retired. A Business API asks for a step-up approval through authOptions.requireApproval, whose message is the framework's approval text and has no template field.) Body and subject share frontendURL from FRONTEND_URL (empty when unset), user, secretCode and expireTime.
VerificationConfig.__subjectTemplate.doc: Optional EJS subject for all six verification, password-reset and 2FA flows. Absent or blank retains the existing English subject. Uses the same locals as verificationTemplate: user, expireTime, secretCode and frontendURL (the notification service FRONTEND_URL, empty when unset). Subjects are retained in notificationLog; never include secretCode. A reference produces VERIFICATION_SUBJECT_SECRET_CODE warning.

__VerificationType.doc.#: Defines the method used for user verification flows such as password reset, two-factor authentication, or account confirmation. This enum helps determine whether the user interacts with a clickable link or a manually entered code.
__VerificationType.doc.byLink: Sends a clickable verification link via email or SMS. The user verifies by clicking the link.
__VerificationType.doc.byCode: Sends a numerical or alphanumerical code. The user verifies by entering the code into the application interface.

__SessionGeoSensitivity.doc: Activates location-based session sensitivity. When active, the generated service compares each login's resolved location against the user's login history and enforces the configured action, and/or re-checks a live session's location on each request.

SessionGeoSensitivity.__locationSensitivityIsActive.doc: Enables or disables location-sensitivity enforcement. Geo enrichment of sessions happens regardless; this flag gates only the enforcement rules.
SessionGeoSensitivity.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for the location-sensitivity rules. Leave it null if locationSensitivityIsActive is false.

__SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.doc: Defines how a location change is detected and what happens when it occurs.

SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.__enforcementMode.doc: When the rule is applied: 'loginTime' (resolve + compare once per login), 'perRequest' (re-check the live session's location on each authenticated request) or 'both'.
SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.__trackBy.doc: The granularity of a 'location change': by 'country', 'region' (state/province, within a country), 'city', or 'ip' (the raw client IP — the runtime's ipChange sensitivity; strictest and noisiest, and the only one that needs no geoip lookup).
SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.__onLocationChange.doc: Login-time action when a login arrives from a new location: 'stepUpEmail' / 'stepUpMobile' (require a verification challenge before the session is issued), 'forceRelogin' (reject + terminate the user's other sessions) or 'notify' (issue the session and publish a new-location alert event).
SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.__onSessionDrift.doc: Per-request action when a live session's request location drifts from where it was issued: 'invalidateSession' (drop the session, force a fresh login) or 'notify' (allow, publish an alert event).
SessionGeoSensitivityConfig.__graceWindowMinutes.doc: Grace period in minutes after a session is issued during which location changes are ignored (mobile networks can hop between cities/regions). 0 disables the grace window.

__GeoEnforcementMode.doc.#: When a session geo-sensitivity rule is applied.
__GeoEnforcementMode.doc.loginTime: Resolve and compare the location once per login.
__GeoEnforcementMode.doc.perRequest: Re-check the live session's location on each authenticated request.
__GeoEnforcementMode.doc.both: Apply the rule both at login time and on every authenticated request.

__GeoTrackBy.doc.#: The granularity at which a 'location change' is detected for session geo-sensitivity.
__GeoTrackBy.doc.region: A change of region (state/province, within a country).
__GeoTrackBy.doc.ip: A change of the raw client IP address. The strictest and noisiest setting — a mobile network re-IPs a user constantly, so expect frequent step-ups. It is the only granularity that needs no geoip lookup, so it keeps enforcing even when the geoip service is unreachable.

__GeoLoginAction.doc.#: Login-time action when a login arrives from a new location.
__GeoLoginAction.doc.stepUpEmail: Require an email verification challenge before the session is issued.
__GeoLoginAction.doc.stepUpMobile: Require a mobile (SMS) verification challenge before the session is issued.
__GeoLoginAction.doc.forceRelogin: Reject the login and terminate the user's other sessions.
__GeoLoginAction.doc.notify: Issue the session and publish a new-location alert event.

__GeoDriftAction.doc.#: Per-request action when a live session's request location drifts from where it was issued.
__GeoDriftAction.doc.invalidateSession: Drop the session and force a fresh login.
__GeoDriftAction.doc.notify: Allow the request and publish an alert event.

__AccessControl.doc: Configuration chapter for defining the access control architecture of the project. OpenAPPL supports multiple authorization models including role-based, user-based, object-based, and attribute-based access controls. This section enables a unified, flexible, and scalable permission system that ensures resources and operations are securely accessed based on defined authorization rules across services.

AccessControl.__roleSettings.doc: Settings for Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), which defines how roles are assigned to users and how roles are mapped to permissions. This is the most common access control strategy in projects. Roles are authorization, not badges: a label a user earns is a badge, an ordinary data object with its own apis (a userBadge pattern is planned). A user's role is written only by the built-in doors (updateUserRole, the admin createUser, create<Tenant>UserOnSaas), which accept a declared role below the caller's own, or by a machine-to-machine-only auth api (requiredCallerKind machineWithoutUserIdentity), which may store a declared role that is neither an administrator nor a SaaS-level (saasAdmin, saasUser) role. A multi-tenant project has no admin and no user role: its end users are tenantUser and saasUser.
AccessControl.__permissionBasics.doc: Defines the core permission vocabulary of the project, including permission groups and named permissions. These are referenced in access control logic across services.
AccessControl.__permissionTypes.doc: Specifies which permission application methods are active in the project. OpenAPPL supports role-based, user-based, user-group-based, object-based (OBAC), and attribute-based (ABAC) authorization models. Multiple types can be active concurrently.
AccessControl.__objectBasedSettings.doc: Settings related to Object-Based Access Control (OBAC). In this model, access is determined based on the user's relation to a specific object instance, such as ownership.
AccessControl.__attributeBasedSettings.doc: Settings for Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). In this model, access decisions are based on dynamic rules involving user, object, or contextual attributes.

__PermissionBasics.doc: Defines the foundational permission model of the project. This section enables Permission-Based Access Control (PBAC) by allowing the architect to organize granular permissions into named groups. These permission groups act as the reference set for roles, users, and object-level rules throughout the project.

PermissionBasics.__pbacIsActive.doc: A boolean flag indicating whether Permission-Based Access Control (PBAC) is active for this project. If enabled, the generated service will enforce permission checks according to the defined permission model.
PermissionBasics.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for permission basics. Leave it null if pbacIsActive is false.

__PermissionBasicsConfig.doc: Configuration details for permission basics, including permission groups.

PermissionBasicsConfig.__permissionGroups.doc: An array of PermissionGroup objects that define the named permissions of the project grouped under logical categories. These groups help structure and reuse permission definitions across services.

__PermissionGroup.doc: Defines a group of permissions under a shared namespace. Each permission group has a unique groupName and a list of permissions that are referenced across the project using either 'groupName.permission' or standalone permission identifiers. These groups simplify permission management in large-scale projects.

PermissionGroup.__groupName.doc: The unique identifier of the permission group. It is used as a namespace in the format groupName.permission when referencing permissions in roles or other rules.
PermissionGroup.__permissions.doc: A list of permission names (strings) defined under this group. These should be unique across the project to ensure consistent access rules.

__RBACSettings.doc: Configuration for Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) within the project. When enabled, RBAC allows permissions to be assigned to named roles, which are then associated with users. This setup supports both single-role and multi-role configurations, along with custom logical roles defined by dynamic lookup conditions.

RBACSettings.__rbacIsActive.doc: A boolean value to enable or disable role-based access control (RBAC) in the project. When enabled, access decisions can be made based on user roles.
RBACSettings.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for RBAC settings. Leave it null if rbacIsActive is false.

__RBACSettingsConfig.doc: Configuration details for RBAC, including roles, role ID data type, custom role lookups, and multi-role support.

RBACSettingsConfig.__roleItems.doc: Defines the list of roles available in the project. Each role is represented as a RoleItem object with a name and a value. These roles will be used to assign permissions and will appear in session data during authentication. The system roles always exist, even when RBAC is not active: superAdmin, admin and user in a single-tenant project; superAdmin, saasAdmin, tenantOwner, tenantAdmin, tenantUser and saasUser in a multi-tenant one. Every role item here is an additional role beside them and must not repeat one (RBAC_ROLE_NAME_RESERVED). A multi-tenant project has no role named admin and none named user: its end users are tenantUser (a tenant member, the default role of a new user) and saasUser (a platform-level user), so a role item named or valued admin or user is refused there, every role-write door refuses them (400 ROLE_NOT_DEFINED) and a session-role list naming them is refused (MULTI_TENANT_ADMIN_ROLE_REFERENCE / MULTI_TENANT_USER_ROLE_REFERENCE). Roles are not badges: a label a user earns (premium, gold, verified seller) is a badge - an ordinary data object with its own apis (a userBadge pattern is planned) - not a role item.
RBACSettingsConfig.__customRoleLookups.doc: An optional mapping of custom logical roles and their evaluation logic. Each entry maps a role name to an MScript condition that determines whether the role is assigned to a user dynamically.
RBACSettingsConfig.__usersHaveMultipleRoles.doc: Indicates whether users can have multiple roles. If true, the `roleId` in the session and user model will be treated as an array of role values. Every door that writes a role list (updateUserRole, the admin createUser, create<Tenant>UserOnSaas and the machine-to-machine role-write door) refuses an empty list with 400 ROLE_LIST_EMPTY: it would strip every role the user holds.
RBACSettingsConfig.__rolePermissions.doc: Optional SEED of default role-to-permission grants (ADR-native-permission-system §9.1). Each entry binds a declared role (by its RoleItem name) to a list of declared permissions (PermissionGroup permission names). At project boot these are upserted into the `givenPermission` store as L4 global-role grant rows (`{ roleId: <role value>, permissionName, canDo: true }`), so a session carrying that role is granted those permissions by default. These are SEED defaults only — an admin can edit the live bindings at runtime via the PBAC management API.

__RolePermission.doc: A single SEED role-to-permission binding (ADR-native-permission-system §9.1). Binds a role (referenced by its RoleItem `name`) to a list of permission names (declared under a PermissionGroup). Seeded at boot as L4 global-role grant rows in the `givenPermission` store.

RolePermission.__role.doc: The role this binding grants permissions to. Must match the `name` of a declared RoleItem (or a built-in system role). The seed resolves this to the role's session value (the `roleId` a session carries).
RolePermission.__permissions.doc: The list of permission names granted to the role. Each must resolve to a permission declared under a PermissionGroup.

__RoleItem.doc: Represents a role definition in the RBAC system. Each role includes a `name` for display and a `value` used in session data and permission checks.

RoleItem.__name.doc: The display name of the role (e.g., 'grpAdmin', 'editor'). This name will be used for reference in the code and documentation purposes. Please ensure that it is one word with no special characters. For multiple words use camleCase. It must not repeat a system role; in a multi-tenant project the names (and values) admin and user are reserved too (use tenantUser for an ordinary tenant member).
RoleItem.__value.doc: The internal value of the role, which will be stored in the `roleId` field of the user or session data. This value is used during authorization checks and should be a string. Make it same as the name to prevent confusion unless you have a reason. When you use a role reference in any authorization configuration, write donw this value not the name.
RoleItem.name: String

__PermissionTypes.doc: Defines the active permission mechanisms in the project. OpenAPPL supports multiple types of permission strategies including role-based (RBAC), user-specific overrides, user group-level permissions, object-level (OBAC), and tenant-specific rules. This configuration determines which of these models are enabled for the access control logic.

PermissionTypes.__roleBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: Enables Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for the project. When active, permissions can be assigned to roles, and users inherit access through their roles.
PermissionTypes.__userBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: Enables user-specific permission overrides. When active, admins can assign custom permissions directly to individual users regardless of their roles or groups.
PermissionTypes.__userGroupBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: Enables permission control via user groups. When active, permissions can be assigned to defined user groups and inherited by all members.
PermissionTypes.__objectBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: Enables Object-Based Access Control (OBAC). When active, permission rules can be defined per individual data object (e.g., per record) and evaluated dynamically based on the object's relation to the user.
PermissionTypes.__tenantBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: Activates tenant-specific permission logic. In multi-tenant projects, this allows SaaS administrators to define custom permission profiles per tenant, enabling isolated authorization policies.

__OBACPermission.doc: Configuration for Object-Based Access Control (OBAC), which restricts access to specific data objects based on object ownership or association. If your system requires permissions that vary per object instance (e.g., 'only the creator can edit this record'), OBAC should be enabled and the relevant data objects listed.

OBACPermission.__objectBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: A boolean value that enables object-level permission checks. When true, permissions can be enforced per record based on ownership or related fields.
OBACPermission.__dataObjects.doc: An array of data object names to which object-level permissions will apply. These are the models for which individual access control should be enforced.

__AbacPermission.doc: Configuration for Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), allowing fine-grained permission control using attribute-level rules on data objects. ABAC evaluates access by applying custom filter conditions to each object. When a rule matches, the user session may be granted specific permissions or even dynamic roles for that object. These rules can supplement or override standard RBAC or OBAC logic.

AbacPermission.__attributeBasedPermissionsIsActive.doc: A boolean value that enables attribute-level access control. When true, data access will be filtered according to ABAC rules defined in `abacDefinitions`.
AbacPermission.__abacDefinitions.doc: An object array to define ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) rules. Each rule applies a conditional filter to determine which records a user can access, and grants either dynamic permissions or a role for matching records.

__ABACDefinititon.doc: Defines a single ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) rule for a given data object. Each rule applies a conditional filter to determine which records a user can access, and grants either dynamic permissions or a role for matching records.

ABACDefinititon.__dataObject.doc: The name of the data object to which this ABAC rule applies.
ABACDefinititon.__whereClause.doc: A BOOLEAN MScript expression over the ABAC decision context — `subject` (the session user), `object` (the candidate record) and `env` — that decides whether this rule grants its permissions for a record, e.g. `{ "js": "object.ownerId === subject.userId" }`. This is NOT a `$`-operator MQuery filter object and never raw driver/ORM code: it is a predicate. For the LIST direction the build-time classifier (abac-classify) translates the predicate into an MQuery list filter when it fits the bounded translatable grammar (`subject.<field>` / `object.<field>` comparisons joined by &&/||); anything richer stays CHECK-ONLY — evaluated per record after fetch, excluded from list filtering with a build warning.
ABACDefinititon.__name.doc: The unique identifier for this ABAC rule. It is used in the backend logic, database, and UI for reference.
ABACDefinititon.__permissions.doc: A list of permission strings that will be granted when the ABAC rule matches a record. These permissions are context-specific and take precedence over less-specific permission types (such as role-based permissions).
ABACDefinititon.name: String

__SocialLoginSettings.doc: Configuration for enabling social login support within the project. This object defines integration settings for third-party authentication providers, such as Google, Apple, Facebook, Microsoft, LinkedIn, GitHub, and GitLab, allowing users to sign in or register using their existing accounts. Each provider must be configured with its credentials and registration behavior. Each provider also carries emailVerification, which decides when its email counts as verified; only a verified email lets a social sign-in reach an existing account with that email.

SocialLoginSettings.__google.doc: Settings for enabling Google OAuth login and optional user registration. Defined as a GoogleLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__apple.doc: Settings for enabling Apple OAuth login and optional user registration. Defined as an AppleLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__facebook.doc: Settings for enabling Facebook OAuth login and optional user registration. This also covers Instagram accounts since Meta uses a unified login system. Defined as a FacebookLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__microsoft.doc: Settings for enabling Microsoft Azure AD / Microsoft Entra ID login and optional user registration. Supports personal Microsoft accounts, work/school (Azure AD) accounts, or both. Defined as a MicrosoftLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__linkedin.doc: Settings for enabling LinkedIn OAuth login and optional user registration. Defined as a LinkedinLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__gitlab.doc: Settings for enabling GitLab OAuth login and optional user registration. Defined as a GitlabLoginSetting object.
SocialLoginSettings.__github.doc: Settings for enabling GitHub OAuth login and optional user registration. Defined as a GithubLoginSetting object.

__SocialLoginProvidersSettings.doc: Container for social login provider entries, one per brand (google, apple, facebook, microsoft, linkedin, github, gitlab). Each entry carries the brand, its OAuth client credentials and its emailVerification decision; the auth service generates the OAuth start and callback routes of every listed brand. Mirrors the other provider families (a named array under projectSettings, org-shelf shareable, per-environment values addressed by family socialLogin and the entry name), with one difference: a brand may appear at most once (validation ERROR SOCIAL_LOGIN_PROVIDER_DUPLICATE_BRAND), because the runtime reads every brand from fixed env variable names.

SocialLoginProvidersSettings.__socialLoginProviders.doc: List of social login providers, one entry per brand. An entry in the list is active: there is no enable flag, remove the entry to turn the brand off. A second entry of the same brand is a validation ERROR; different clients per environment come from the environment values of the entry, not from a second entry.

__SocialLoginProvider.doc: One social login provider: the brand, its OAuth client credentials and when the email it returns counts as verified. The `provider` brand fixes the OAuth endpoints and the env variable names the auth service reads (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID ...), so a brand appears at most once in the list. The `name` addresses the entry in the org shelf, in its per-environment values and in the encrypted secret store; the legacy `authentication.socialLogins` normalization and the moveSocialLoginsToProviders tool name an entry after its brand. Missing credentials are not a validation error: the login route answers a typed 503 at runtime and the production credential report names the missing variables. `mock` is not a credential mode of this family: there is no runtime mock OAuth.

SocialLoginProvider.__name.doc: Unique entry name within the project (a codeName), conventionally the brand itself (`google`). It addresses the entry in the org shelf, its per-environment values (family socialLogin) and its relocated secrets; the env variable names do not depend on it.
SocialLoginProvider.name: String
SocialLoginProvider.__provider.doc: The social login brand. One entry per brand: a second entry of the same brand is validation ERROR SOCIAL_LOGIN_PROVIDER_DUPLICATE_BRAND. The brand selects the OAuth endpoints, the configuration fields that are read and the env variable names.
SocialLoginProvider.__configuration.doc: OAuth client credentials (SocialLoginProviderConfig); only the fields of the selected brand are read. Missing values never fail validation, the build or the boot: the login route of the brand answers a typed 503 errMsg_OAuthProviderNotConfigured_<brand> until they are set.
SocialLoginProvider.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this provider counts the returned email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the provider's own verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The decision marks a new account's email verified and is what lets a sign-in reach an EXISTING account with the same email: an email this setting does not count as verified creates an unverified account (which verifies through the normal email verification flow) and never signs in to an existing account by email; that sign-in is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified and the user signs in with the existing method instead. A provider account linked to a user in the auth userSocialAccount object (written at the social registration and at a verified-email sign-in) is matched first and reaches that user whatever this setting decides. 'trusted' is only for a deployment locked to one directory you control (for Microsoft: configuration.tenant set to your own directory ID); see the SocialEmailVerification value docs for the warning.

__SocialLoginProviderConfig.doc: OAuth client credentials of a SocialLoginProvider entry. Fields are flat across brands and only the ones of the selected `provider` are read: google, facebook, linkedin, github and gitlab read clientId and clientSecret; microsoft also reads tenant; apple reads clientId (the Services ID), teamId, keyId and privateKey (the .p8 key contents) instead of a clientSecret. clientSecret and privateKey are secrets: masked in API responses, written as blank placeholders into the committed env files and delivered as CI/CD variables to the service that hosts the OAuth routes only.

SocialLoginProviderConfig.__clientId.doc: (all brands) OAuth client id: the Google client ID, the Facebook App ID, the Microsoft Application (client) ID, the LinkedIn / GitHub / GitLab client ID, or the Apple Services ID (not the App ID). Emitted as <BRAND>_CLIENT_ID (FACEBOOK_APP_ID for facebook).
SocialLoginProviderConfig.__clientSecret.doc: (every brand except apple) OAuth client secret. Secret: emitted as <BRAND>_CLIENT_SECRET (FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET for facebook) through the secret store and CI/CD, never committed.
SocialLoginProviderConfig.__tenant.doc: (microsoft) Which Microsoft accounts may sign in: 'common' (default, personal and work/school), 'organizations' (work/school only), 'consumers' (personal only), or your own directory (tenant) ID for a single-tenant app. Emitted as MICROSOFT_TENANT.
SocialLoginProviderConfig.__teamId.doc: (apple) Your Apple Developer Team ID, a 10-character string. Emitted as APPLE_TEAM_ID.
SocialLoginProviderConfig.__keyId.doc: (apple) The Key ID of the Sign In with Apple private key. Emitted as APPLE_KEY_ID.
SocialLoginProviderConfig.__privateKey.doc: (apple) The contents of the Sign In with Apple .p8 key, which signs the short-lived ES256 client secret. Secret: emitted as APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY through the secret store and CI/CD (use \n for newlines in an env value).

__SocialLoginProviderType.doc.#: The social login brand of a SocialLoginProvider entry. Each value is one OAuth provider of the auth service runtime; there is no custom brand and no mock brand.
__SocialLoginProviderType.doc.apple: Sign In with Apple (clientId = Services ID, teamId, keyId, privateKey; the client secret is an ES256 JWT signed at runtime).
__SocialLoginProviderType.doc.facebook: Facebook Login, which also covers Instagram accounts (clientId = App ID, clientSecret = App Secret).
__SocialLoginProviderType.doc.microsoft: Microsoft identity platform / Entra ID (clientId + clientSecret, tenant selects the accepted accounts).
__SocialLoginProviderType.doc.github: GitHub OAuth App (clientId + clientSecret). A GitHub OAuth App takes ONE callback URL.

__SocialEmailVerification.doc.#: How a social login decides that the email a provider returns is verified (the emailVerification setting of each social login provider).
__SocialEmailVerification.doc.providerSignal: Default. Verified only when the provider's own verification signal says so: Google, Apple and LinkedIn email_verified, GitHub the primary AND verified address, GitLab confirmed_at, Microsoft the ID token xms_edov claim for the same address, Facebook never.
__SocialEmailVerification.doc.requireVerification: Never count this provider's email as verified. A new account is created unverified and verifies through the normal email verification flow; a sign-in with this provider never reaches an existing account by its email, only through the provider account link (the account it registered, or linked earlier by a verified-email sign-in).
__SocialEmailVerification.doc.trusted: Always count this provider's email as verified. WARNING: use it only for a deployment locked to ONE directory you control, for Microsoft a configuration.tenant that is your own directory ID. A provider app that accepts accounts from any directory (Microsoft tenant common, organizations or consumers) returns addresses the provider has not verified, so 'trusted' must not be used there; design time warns on that combination (SOCIAL_LOGIN_TRUSTED_EMAIL_OPEN_DIRECTORY).

__FrontendUrl.doc: Per-environment base URLs for the frontend application. Sets the FRONTEND_URL environment variable used at runtime for social login callback redirects (defaults to FRONTEND_URL + /auth/callback), email notification links, and other frontend-facing URLs. If not set, defaults are derived from the project codename: dev=http://localhost:5173, test=`https://{codename}.<test-domain>`, stage=`https://{codename}-stage.<app-domain>`, prod=`https://{codename}.<app-domain>`, where the domains are set by the hosting platform.

FrontendUrl.__dev.doc: Frontend base URL for local development environment. Default: http://localhost:5173
FrontendUrl.__test.doc: Frontend base URL for the test/preview environment. Default: `https://{projectCodename}.<test-domain>`, where the domain is set by the hosting platform
FrontendUrl.__stage.doc: Frontend base URL for the staging environment. Default: `https://{projectCodename}-stage.<app-domain>`, where the domain is set by the hosting platform
FrontendUrl.__prod.doc: Frontend base URL for the production environment. Default: `https://{projectCodename}.<app-domain>`, where the domain is set by the hosting platform
FrontendUrl.__test.label: Preview
FrontendUrl.__dev.label: Local
FrontendUrl.__stage.label: Staging
FrontendUrl.__prod.label: Production

__GoogleLoginSetting.doc: Configuration for Google OAuth login. This section defines whether Google login is enabled, the client ID and secret, and whether users can register using their Google accounts.

GoogleLoginSetting.__useGoogleLogin.doc: A boolean value to enable or disable Google OAuth login. When true, users can sign in using their Google accounts.
GoogleLoginSetting.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for Google OAuth login. Leave it null if useGoogleLogin is false.
GoogleLoginSetting.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this provider counts the returned email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the provider's own verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The decision marks a new account's email verified and is what lets a sign-in reach an EXISTING account with the same email: an email this setting does not count as verified creates an unverified account (which verifies through the normal email verification flow) and never signs in to an existing account by email; that sign-in is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified and the user signs in with the existing method instead. A provider account linked to a user in the auth userSocialAccount object (written at the social registration and at a verified-email sign-in) is matched first and reaches that user whatever this setting decides. 'trusted' is only for a deployment locked to one directory you control (for Microsoft: configuration.tenant set to your own directory ID); see the SocialEmailVerification value docs for the warning.

__GoogleLoginConfig.doc: Configuration details for Google OAuth login, including client ID and secret. This object is used when Google login is enabled. Registration is always allowed via social login.

GoogleLoginConfig.__clientId.doc: The Google OAuth client ID. This should match the identifier registered in your Google Developer Console.
GoogleLoginConfig.__clientSecret.doc: The Google OAuth client secret. This is a confidential key issued by Google, stored securely in the platform secret store.

__AppleLoginSetting.doc: Configuration for Apple Sign In with Apple. This section defines whether Apple login is enabled and its configuration. Apple OAuth requires a Service ID, Team ID, Key ID, and a private key (.p8 file contents) — all obtained from the Apple Developer portal.

AppleLoginSetting.__useAppleLogin.doc: A boolean value to enable or disable Apple OAuth login. When true, users can sign in using their Apple accounts.
AppleLoginSetting.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for Apple OAuth login. Leave it null if useAppleLogin is false.
AppleLoginSetting.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this provider counts the returned email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the provider's own verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The decision marks a new account's email verified and is what lets a sign-in reach an EXISTING account with the same email: an email this setting does not count as verified creates an unverified account (which verifies through the normal email verification flow) and never signs in to an existing account by email; that sign-in is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified and the user signs in with the existing method instead. A provider account linked to a user in the auth userSocialAccount object (written at the social registration and at a verified-email sign-in) is matched first and reaches that user whatever this setting decides. 'trusted' is only for a deployment locked to one directory you control (for Microsoft: configuration.tenant set to your own directory ID); see the SocialEmailVerification value docs for the warning.

__AppleLoginConfig.doc: Configuration details for Apple Sign In. Apple uses a JWT-based client secret generated from a private key, unlike other providers that use a static client secret. Registration is always allowed via social login.

AppleLoginConfig.__clientId.doc: The Apple Service ID (not the App ID). This is the identifier you create under 'Services IDs' in the Apple Developer portal (e.g., com.yourapp.web.signin).
AppleLoginConfig.__teamId.doc: Your Apple Developer Team ID. A 10-character alphanumeric string found in your Apple Developer account membership details.
AppleLoginConfig.__keyId.doc: The Key ID of the Sign In with Apple private key. Found in the Apple Developer portal under 'Keys' after creating a Sign In with Apple key.
AppleLoginConfig.__privateKey.doc: The contents of the .p8 private key file downloaded from Apple. This key is used to generate a JWT client secret for token exchange. Store securely — use \n for newlines in environment variables.

__GitlabLoginSetting.doc: Configuration for GitLab OAuth login. This section defines whether GitLab login is enabled, the client ID and secret, and whether users can register using their GitLab accounts.

GitlabLoginSetting.__useGitlabLogin.doc: A boolean value to enable or disable GitLab OAuth login. When true, users can sign in using their GitLab accounts.
GitlabLoginSetting.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for GitLab OAuth login. Leave it null if useGitlabLogin is false.
GitlabLoginSetting.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this provider counts the returned email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the provider's own verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The decision marks a new account's email verified and is what lets a sign-in reach an EXISTING account with the same email: an email this setting does not count as verified creates an unverified account (which verifies through the normal email verification flow) and never signs in to an existing account by email; that sign-in is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified and the user signs in with the existing method instead. A provider account linked to a user in the auth userSocialAccount object (written at the social registration and at a verified-email sign-in) is matched first and reaches that user whatever this setting decides. 'trusted' is only for a deployment locked to one directory you control (for Microsoft: configuration.tenant set to your own directory ID); see the SocialEmailVerification value docs for the warning.

__GitlabLoginConfig.doc: Configuration details for GitLab OAuth login, including client ID and secret. This object is used when GitLab login is enabled. Registration is always allowed via social login.

GitlabLoginConfig.__clientId.doc: The GitLab OAuth client ID. This should match the identifier registered in your GitLab application settings.
GitlabLoginConfig.__clientSecret.doc: The GitLab OAuth client secret. This is a confidential key issued by GitLab, stored securely in the platform secret store.

__GithubLoginSetting.doc: Configuration for GitHub OAuth login. This section defines whether GitHub login is enabled, the client ID and secret, and whether users can register using their GitHub accounts.

GithubLoginSetting.__useGithubLogin.doc: A boolean value to enable or disable GitHub OAuth login. When true, users can sign in using their GitHub accounts.
GithubLoginSetting.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for GitHub OAuth login. Leave it null if useGithubLogin is false.
GithubLoginSetting.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this provider counts the returned email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the provider's own verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The decision marks a new account's email verified and is what lets a sign-in reach an EXISTING account with the same email: an email this setting does not count as verified creates an unverified account (which verifies through the normal email verification flow) and never signs in to an existing account by email; that sign-in is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified and the user signs in with the existing method instead. __GithubLoginConfig.doc: Configuration details for GitHub OAuth login, including client ID and secret. This object is used when GitHub login is enabled. Registration is always allowed via social login.

GithubLoginConfig.__clientId.doc: The GitHub OAuth client ID. This should match the identifier registered in your GitHub application settings.
GithubLoginConfig.__clientSecret.doc: The GitHub OAuth client secret. This is a confidential key issued by GitHub, stored securely in the platform secret store.

__FacebookLoginSetting.doc: Configuration for Facebook OAuth login. This section defines whether Facebook login is enabled, the App ID and App Secret, and whether users can register using their Facebook accounts. This also covers Instagram accounts since Meta uses a unified login system (Facebook Login).
