INLINE (`inline: true`, the default): the object already belongs to a user (an address, a saved card, a user's membership row); the user's default is the `isDefault` flag on the object's own row, at most one per `scopeField` value - the owner field unless the block names another property, and per tenant on a tenant-level object - enforced by a partial unique index. The first row created in a scope becomes its default; deleting the default row (hard or soft delete) makes the most recently created remaining row of that scope the default, and no remaining row means no default. RELATED (`inline: false`): the object is global (a shipping company); `isDefault` marks the ONE system default (per tenant on a tenant-level object), the first row created becomes it and deleting it promotes the newest remaining row; each user may override it through the generated table `sys_UserDefaultFor<Object>` (`userId`, `default<Object>Id`, the tenant column on a tenant-level object, unique per user), and deleting an object removes the override rows that point at it so those users fall back to the system default. Four apis are injected per object, with fixed names: set<Object>AsDefault(id) - inline: makes the row the default of its own scope, behind the object's normal ownership check; related: sets the system default, platform operator only. getDefault<Object>() - inline: the session user's default or null; related: the system default or null. set<Object>AsDefaultForUser(id, userId?) - the same for another user's scope (inline) or the user's own override row (related); `userId` absent means the session user, and naming another user is operator-only. getDefault<Object>ForUser(userId?) - that user's default; in related mode the user's override, else the system default, and the answer says which in `defaultSource` (user | system). A set is atomic: unsetting the previous default and setting the new one happen in one transaction, and the changed rows go out on the normal update events. `isDefault` is not writable through the object's generic create / update apis - a request parameter or dataClauseItems entry naming it is refused at design time (DEFAULT_CHOICE_MANAGED_COLUMN_WRITTEN) - so the one-default invariant cannot be broken by a designer write. Validation: an inline object with no `scopeField` and no owner field is refused (DEFAULT_CHOICE_SCOPE_MISSING); an unknown `scopeField` is refused (DEFAULT_CHOICE_SCOPE_FIELD_NOT_FOUND); an authored property named `isDefault` that is not a Boolean is refused (DEFAULT_CHOICE_COLUMN_CONFLICT) and a Boolean one is warned about (DEFAULT_CHOICE_COLUMN_MANAGED - the pattern manages it); related mode on an object that declares an owner field is warned about (DEFAULT_CHOICE_RELATED_WITH_OWNER - did you mean inline?). Refused on framework `sys_` objects and auth-service objects (DEFAULT_CHOICE_ON_SYSTEM_OBJECT). The guide is the docs-site page [Default choice](../mastering/default-choice.md).

DefaultChoice.__isActive.doc: Turns the default-row feature on for this object. False (the default) leaves the block inert: no column, no index, no override table, no injected api, and the object is generated exactly as without the block. The other fields are only checked while this is true.
DefaultChoice.__inline.doc: `true` (the default): the object belongs to a user and the default is a flag on the object's own rows, one per `scopeField` value. `false`: the object is global; `isDefault` marks the one system default and each user may override it through the generated `sys_UserDefaultFor<Object>` table. Choose `false` only for an object that has no owner field (DEFAULT_CHOICE_RELATED_WITH_OWNER warns otherwise).
DefaultChoice.__scopeField.doc: Inline mode only. The property that groups rows into scopes, one default per value: the user field of a relation object (e.g. `userId` on a membership row), or any other declared property. Defaults to the object's owner field (`sessionSettings.isOwnerField`); when the object has no owner field it is required (DEFAULT_CHOICE_SCOPE_MISSING). Must be a declared property of this object (DEFAULT_CHOICE_SCOPE_FIELD_NOT_FOUND). Ignored in related mode.

__ObjectGeoSettings.doc: Design-time settings for the /geo REST surface a data object's geo-typed properties generate. The geo routes return full rows unless `selectProperties` narrows them, so an object whose moderation/publication state gates its BusinessApi reads needs the same discipline on the map surface: the access gate comes from `objectSettings.authorization.dataObjectAccess` (non-accessPublic ⇒ session required; accessPrivate additionally owner-scopes when the object has an owner field), and `visibilityFilter` narrows what any caller can see. TENANT ISOLATION IS NOT YOURS TO AUTHOR HERE: on a multi-tenant project the /geo quartet of an object declared `objectDataIsInTenantLevel: true` is pinned by the framework to the caller's own tenant, taken from the verified session and from nowhere else, and such an object therefore REQUIRES a session whatever `dataObjectAccess` says - an accessPublic tenant-level object is no longer anonymously readable on this surface, and a session that carries no tenant is answered 401 TENANT_REQUIRED rather than served. Previously no geo route carried a tenant term at all and a tenant-level object's map queries returned every tenant's rows.

ObjectGeoSettings.__visibilityFilter.doc: A STATIC where object merged into the query of every geo route of this object (all four ops, on relational/PostGIS and MongoDB storage alike). Keys are first-level property names of the owning data object; values are scalar literals (string, number, boolean, or null) a row must equal to be visible through the geo surface. Typical use: { "moderationStatus": "approved", "isPublished": true } so unmoderated or unpublished rows never leak through map queries. Non-scalar values are rejected at design time because array/object operands do not mean the same thing on both storage engines. Do NOT try to spell tenant isolation in here: a static literal would pin every geo query to one hard-coded tenant id, the framework already applies the tenant term itself, and it is merged AFTER this filter so a key that names the tenant column cannot override the session value. DECLARE IT WHENEVER THE OBJECT HAS A PUBLICATION GATE: with no filter here, the only narrowing left is the anonymous backstop, which recognises exactly three column shapes - `withdrawn` (Boolean), `isPublished` (Boolean) and `moderationStatus` (Enum carrying "approved") - and narrows a SESSION-LESS caller only. A `verificationStatus` column, a `moderationStatus` typed String rather than Enum, or an Enum whose publishable value is spelled anything else reads exactly like the covered shapes and narrows NOTHING, so unapproved rows stay plotted on the map while the object's list/get apis hide them. Validation reports that shape as GEO_PUBLIC_SURFACE_UNFILTERED (warning).
ObjectGeoSettings.__selectProperties.doc: The columns the geo routes of this object answer with: a list of first-level property names of the owning data object. Leave it unset (or empty) to answer full rows, the default. When set, the projection is applied AT THE QUERY on every geo route (`attributes` on relational/PostGIS storage, a projection on MongoDB), so a column left out never leaves the database. Always kept, whether listed or not: `id`, the geo field the route queries, and every column the route's own filters compare (the visibilityFilter keys, the owner and tenant pins, the moderation and publication gates, `isActive` on a soft-delete object); the computed `distance_m` of the proximity routes stays too. Use it on a PUBLIC geo-indexed object (dataObjectAccess accessPublic) so internal columns such as review notes are not served to anonymous map callers. A name that is not a property of the object is a design-time error (PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND).

__ObjectModerationMode.doc.#: Where a moderated write lands while it waits for a verdict. Both modes keep the sys_<X>ModerationReview queue - the decision record, the analysis, the reviewer queue and the accepted-snapshot audit live there in either mode; the modes differ only in where the write lands.
__ObjectModerationMode.doc.staged: The write is held as a snapshot on the review row and the real object is created or updated only when it is accepted. A pending insert has no real row; a pending update leaves the real row byte-identical, still serving the previously approved state. The real object never carries a moderation status, because it never holds unapproved data.
__ObjectModerationMode.doc.onPlace: The write lands on the real row immediately and a framework-injected, read-only `moderationStatus` column carries the verdict; the generated read paths the framework controls hide a non-accepted row from non-privileged callers (the author still sees their own unapproved rows), and an update touching `moderatedProperties` is decided again in the same request: unless the new verdict is accept, the row leaves public view until a reviewer accepts it. For objects whose children need the parent's real id during a multi-step flow (an event and its ticket types), which `staged` cannot give.

__ObjectModerationUserMessageMode.doc.#: What the AUTHOR of a rejected or held submission is told. The reviewer-only `analysis` is never shown to the author in either mode.
__ObjectModerationUserMessageMode.doc.llm: The author sees the `userMessage` the `escalateTo` agent produced, falling back to `genericMessage` when the agent returned none. Requires `wantReason`.

__ObjectModerationProviderErrorPolicy.do.#: What happens when the decision provider fails instead of answering (a 529, a 429 with its retries exhausted, a timeout). A failure never publishes the write, in either policy.
__ObjectModerationProviderErrorPolicy.do.failToReview: The submission is held for a human: the review row goes to `review` and names the transport failure. The default.
__ObjectModerationProviderErrorPolicy.do.failToReject: The submission is rejected outright and the review row names the transport failure.

__ObjectModeration.doc: Decision-moderated writes on a data object. When `enabled`, the create and update Business APIs of this object ask the decision provider named by `providerName` ONE framework-owned `choice` question, `verdict`, over { accept, reject, review }, with `policy` as its instructions and the written values (restricted to `moderatedProperties`) as its state. `review` is the escape option - a human should decide - and it is always offered, because a forced choice with no way out answers wrong with high confidence; a verdict whose confidence is below `confidenceThreshold` is routed to `review` too. The decision is synchronous, inside the request: an isolated provider call measured 250-400 ms. On `accept` the write continues in the same request with every hook, event and response of a direct write. In `staged` mode a `reject` or `review` answers 202 with { moderation: { id, status, message } } and NOTHING is written to the object; in `onPlace` mode the write lands whatever the verdict and the answer carries `moderation` beside the record. Over gRPC the response message of a moderated create / update declares the same outcome as a `moderation` field (tag 1000): a hold answers OK with only that field set and the `x-moderation-status` / `x-moderation-id` metadata. Every submission is a row of the framework-generated `sys_<X>ModerationReview` object, which STORES the decision (value, confidence, probabilities, pinned model, decidedBy: provider | mock | human); it is never re-derived later, because the decision is reproducible across identical requests and the probability is not. One submission is pending per target row: a newer update supersedes the older one visibly, it is not deleted. `reviewerRoles` accept or reject held rows through injected Business APIs, never their own; an accept replays the author's original write through the api's own path, so its events and post-write workflow fire as on a direct write. WHO IS MODERATED: every caller except trusted system transports (cron, internal calls) and `exemptRoles`. This is CONTENT moderation, not authorization - `absoluteRoles` do NOT bypass it, and the verdict never feeds a permission check. An update that touches none of the `moderatedProperties` writes straight through, so a counter bumped by a sale never queues. Refused on auth-service objects and framework `sys_` objects. Both modes, the onPlace read gate and what it does not cover, the reviewer apis, the review row and every validation code are in the docs-site guide [Object content moderation](../mastering/object-moderation.md). Data-object moderation is implemented for nodejs and java. ContentModel staged editorial moderation has a separate qualified nodejs/java support gate; onPlace remains refused.

ObjectModeration.__enabled.doc: Turns moderation on for this object. False (the default) leaves the block inert: no review object, no injected api, no interception, and the object is generated exactly as without the block. The other fields are only checked while this is true.
ObjectModeration.__mode.doc: Where a moderated write lands while it waits (ObjectModerationMode). `staged` (the default) holds it on the review row until accept, so the real object never shows unapproved data. `onPlace` writes the real row at once behind a framework-managed `moderationStatus` visibility gate, for parents whose children need the real row id mid-flow.
ObjectModeration.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry that judges this object's writes. Its credentials come from DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* at runtime. Required when enabled; a name that matches no entry fails validation (OBJECT_MODERATION_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND).
ObjectModeration.__model.doc: Optional PINNED model version for this object's decisions, overriding the provider entry's configured model. A floating tag (`jev-latest`, a bare family name) is refused with DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED: an unpinned model can answer the same submission differently on two days, and the review row records the model a decision came from. Leave null to use the entry's model.
ObjectModeration.__policy.doc: The moderation guideline in plain language - the instructions of the `verdict` question, judged against the submitted values. Write the rule, not a prompt: there is no system message and no few-shot slot (e.g. "Listings must describe a real item for sale; no contact details, no offensive language, no prohibited goods."). Required when enabled (OBJECT_MODERATION_POLICY_MISSING).
ObjectModeration.__confidenceThreshold.doc: Confidence at or above which an `accept` or `reject` verdict is acted on directly; below it the submission goes to `review` for a human. Must lie in (0, 1] (OBJECT_MODERATION_THRESHOLD_RANGE). Default 0.8.
ObjectModeration.__moderatedProperties.doc: The properties whose values are judged, and whose change triggers moderation. Only these fields make up the decision state, and an update that touches none of them writes straight through - so a system- or action-driven field (a `soldCount` incremented by a sale) never sends approved content back to the queue. Null or empty = every user-writable property of the object. Each entry must be a property of this object (OBJECT_MODERATION_PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND).
ObjectModeration.__exemptRoles.doc: Roles whose writes bypass moderation and land directly. Default [] (nobody is exempt). Moderation is content policy, not authorization, so `absoluteRoles` are NOT implicitly exempt: list a role here to exempt it. Each entry must be a declared role (OBJECT_MODERATION_UNKNOWN_ROLE).
ObjectModeration.__reviewerRoles.doc: Roles that see the review queue and accept or reject held submissions. Null or empty = the platform operator (admin and superAdmin; saasAdmin and superAdmin in a multi-tenant project). A reviewer can never decide a submission they authored (MODERATION_SELF_DECISION, 403). Each entry must be a declared role (OBJECT_MODERATION_UNKNOWN_ROLE).
ObjectModeration.__wantReason.doc: When true, a `reject` or `review` verdict is escalated to the `escalateTo` agent for a written analysis, after the response and bounded in time. The analysis is stored on the review row and is visible to reviewer roles only. Requires `escalateTo` (OBJECT_MODERATION_REASON_WITHOUT_ESCALATION).
ObjectModeration.__escalateTo.doc: Name of the AI agent that writes the reason for a `reject` or `review` verdict: an entry of this service's `aiAgents[]` or an agent the agent hub serves. It receives { snapshot, verdict, policy } and returns either the analysis text or { analysis, userMessage }. Required when `wantReason` is true; a name that resolves to no agent fails validation (OBJECT_MODERATION_ESCALATION_TARGET_NOT_FOUND).
ObjectModeration.__userMessageMode.doc: What the author of a held or rejected submission is told (ObjectModerationUserMessageMode): `generic` (the default) shows `genericMessage`; `llm` shows the agent's `userMessage`, and requires `wantReason` (OBJECT_MODERATION_LLM_MESSAGE_WITHOUT_REASON).
ObjectModeration.__genericMessage.doc: The message the author sees for a held or rejected submission when no agent-written message applies.
ObjectModeration.__onProviderError.doc: What happens when the decision provider fails instead of answering (ObjectModerationProviderErrorPolicy): `failToReview` (the default) holds the submission for a human, `failToReject` rejects it. Either way the review row names the transport failure, and a failure never publishes the write.
ObjectModeration.__timeoutMs.doc: Timeout of one provider decision in milliseconds, enforced by the framework (the provider adapters carry none); a timeout is a transport failure and follows `onProviderError`. An isolated call measured 250-400 ms, so a value under ~1000 cuts healthy calls. Default 5000.

__ContentModeration.doc: Decision moderation of content that is not a DataObject write: objectModeration applied to RealtimeHub messages and outbound notification content. It is the SAME mechanism as ObjectModeration, not a second one: ONE framework-owned `choice` question, `verdict`, over { accept, reject, review } with `policy` as its instructions, the same `confidenceThreshold` (below it a verdict goes to review), the same `onProviderError` posture, the same two-tier reasons (`wantReason` + `escalateTo`) and the same review row shape (`sys_<X>ModerationReview`, decided through the same injected reviewer Business APIs). What differs is the surface: a held message or notification is not written anywhere until a reviewer accepts it, and the accept DELIVERS it (the room receives the message, the recipients the notification). A ContentModel uses its own `contentModeration` block, an ObjectModeration the framework applies to the content objects it synthesizes. Hub and notification moderation is implemented for nodejs and java; other unported languages retain OBJECT_MODERATION_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED.

ContentModeration.__enabled.doc: Turns moderation on for this surface. False (the default) leaves the block inert: no review object, no injected api, no interception, and the hub or notification is generated exactly as without the block. The other fields are only checked while this is true.
ContentModeration.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry that judges this surface's content. Its credentials come from DECISION_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* at runtime. Required when enabled (OBJECT_MODERATION_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND, the objectModeration code).
ContentModeration.__model.doc: Optional PINNED model version for this surface's decisions, overriding the provider entry's configured model. A floating tag is refused with DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED. Leave null to use the entry's model.
ContentModeration.__policy.doc: The moderation guideline in plain language - the instructions of the `verdict` question, judged against the content (a hub message's type and content; a notification's rendered subject and body). Required when enabled (OBJECT_MODERATION_POLICY_MISSING).
ContentModeration.__confidenceThreshold.doc: Confidence at or above which an `accept` or `reject` verdict is acted on directly; below it the content goes to `review` for a human. Must lie in (0, 1] (OBJECT_MODERATION_THRESHOLD_RANGE). Default 0.8, applied when omitted.
ContentModeration.__messageTypes.doc: RealtimeHub only: the message types that are judged. Null or empty = every message type of the hub that no HubLogic handler processes. Each entry must be a message type of the hub (CONTENT_MODERATION_MESSAGE_TYPE_NOT_FOUND), and a type a HubLogic handler processes is refused (CONTENT_MODERATION_HANDLED_MESSAGE_TYPE). Ignored with a warning on a notification.
ContentModeration.__exemptRoles.doc: RealtimeHub only: roles whose messages bypass moderation and are delivered directly. Default [] (nobody is exempt). Each entry must be a declared role (OBJECT_MODERATION_UNKNOWN_ROLE). A notification has no sender session, so the list is ignored there with a warning.
ContentModeration.__reviewerRoles.doc: Roles that see the review queue and accept or reject held content. Null or empty = the platform operator (admin). A reviewer can never decide a hub message they sent (MODERATION_SELF_DECISION, 403). Each entry must be a declared role (OBJECT_MODERATION_UNKNOWN_ROLE).
ContentModeration.__wantReason.doc: When true, a `reject` or `review` verdict is escalated to the `escalateTo` agent for a written analysis, after the sender is answered and bounded in time; stored on the review row for reviewers only. Requires `escalateTo` (OBJECT_MODERATION_REASON_WITHOUT_ESCALATION).
ContentModeration.__escalateTo.doc: Name of the AI agent that writes the reason for a `reject` or `review` verdict: an AI agent of the service or one the agent hub serves (OBJECT_MODERATION_ESCALATION_TARGET_NOT_FOUND). It receives { snapshot, verdict, policy }.
ContentModeration.__userMessageMode.doc: What the sender of a held or rejected hub message is told (ObjectModerationUserMessageMode): `generic` (the default) shows `genericMessage`; `llm` shows the agent's `userMessage` on the review row and requires `wantReason` (OBJECT_MODERATION_LLM_MESSAGE_WITHOUT_REASON).
ContentModeration.__genericMessage.doc: The message the sender of a held or rejected hub message sees when no agent-written message applies.
ContentModeration.__onProviderError.doc: What happens when the decision provider fails instead of answering (ObjectModerationProviderErrorPolicy): `failToReview` (the default) holds the content for a human, `failToReject` rejects it. Either way the content is never delivered on a failure and the review row names it.
ContentModeration.__timeoutMs.doc: Timeout of one provider decision in milliseconds, enforced by the framework; a timeout is a transport failure and follows `onProviderError`. An isolated call measured 250-400 ms, and on a hub that time is added to every moderated message. Default 5000.

__GraphProjection.doc: Projects a DataObject into a graph database (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §3/§4b/§5). Node-shaped (set `labels` + `projectedProperties`) OR edge-shaped (set `projectsAsEdge`), never both. Node mode: on every write of the row, `projectToGraph` does an idempotent `MERGE (n:Label {identity}) SET n += $props` over the `projectedProperties` subset; `filterableProperties` (a subset) drive Neo4j indexes so traversals can filter in-graph. Edge mode: the object's rows are relationships (a join/grant table) — see GraphEdgeProjection. `projectedProperties` are the SELECTIVE filter set only (status/category/tenantId/createdAt) — never large text/blobs/full bodies; non-projected attributes are hydrated relationally (§5). Referenced property names are real properties of this object (PropRefer).

GraphProjection.__provider.doc: Name of the graphProvider this object projects into (must match a projectSettings.graphProvidersSettings.graphProviders[].name). May be omitted when the project declares at most one graph provider: the projection then uses that provider, or mainGraph when none is declared. Required when the project declares two or more (GRAPH_PROJECTION_PROVIDER_REQUIRED).
GraphProjection.__labels.doc: Neo4j node labels for the projected node (node mode), e.g. ['Document']. Every declared label is written on the node; the MERGE is keyed on the FIRST (primary) label and SETs the rest, e.g. labels ['Employee', 'Manager'] write `MERGE (n:Employee {identity}) SET n:Employee:Manager, n += $props`. Each label must be a plain Cypher identifier (letters, digits, `_`, not starting with a digit): any other label is a GRAPH_LABEL_INVALID validation error (the runtime would refuse it and skip the whole node write). A label later removed from this list is not removed from nodes already written. Leave null/absent in edge mode (use `projectsAsEdge`).
GraphProjection.__identity.doc: The node-key property used in `MERGE (n:Label {identity})` (PropRefer, defaults to `id`). It is also the hard-delete key: a hard delete runs `MATCH (n:Label {identity: $key}) DETACH DELETE n` with `$key` bound to the deleted row's own identity value (a row without one removes nothing). Node mode only.
GraphProjection.__projectedProperties.doc: Properties COPIED into the node (PropRefer[]). The SELECTIVE filter/identity set only — id, tenantId, and simple flat filter attributes (status, category, createdAt). Never large text, descriptions, blobs, or full document bodies (§5). Node mode only.
GraphProjection.__filterableProperties.doc: A subset of `projectedProperties` used in WHERE clauses — drives the Neo4j indexes the control plane creates so traversals filter in-graph (§5/§7). Node mode only.
GraphProjection.__projectsAsEdge.doc: When set, this object's rows project as RELATIONSHIPS rather than vertices (edge mode — e.g. a permissionGrant join/grant table). A GraphProjection is node-shaped OR edge-shaped, never both. See GraphEdgeProjection.

__GraphEdgeProjection.doc: Projects each row of the owning DataObject as a graph relationship. Edge-shaped graph projection: the owning DataObject's rows ARE relationships (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §4b) — e.g. a permissionGrant object with subjectId / resourceId / action projects as a `CAN_READ` relationship, not a vertex. On each write, the relationship is upserted between the `from` and `to` endpoints keyed by the named properties; on delete it is removed.

GraphEdgeProjection.__relationshipType.doc: The Neo4j relationship type the rows project as, e.g. `CAN_READ`.
GraphEdgeProjection.__from.doc: The source endpoint of the relationship (GraphEdgeEnd) — the candidate node labels and the property on THIS object whose value keys the source node.
GraphEdgeProjection.__to.doc: The target endpoint of the relationship (GraphEdgeEnd) — the candidate node labels and the property on THIS object whose value keys the target node.
GraphEdgeProjection.__edgeProperties.doc: Optional properties of this object copied onto the relationship (PropRefer[]), e.g. ['action','grantedAt'].

__GraphEdgeEnd.doc: One end of an edge-shaped projection (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §4b). `labels` are the candidate node labels the endpoint may resolve to (e.g. ['User','Group']); `key` is the property on the edge object whose value matches the target node's identity.

GraphEdgeEnd.__labels.doc: Candidate node labels this endpoint may resolve to, e.g. ['User','Group'] or ['Folder','Document'].
GraphEdgeEnd.__key.doc: The property on the owning edge object (PropRefer) whose value keys the node at this end of the relationship (matched against the node's identity).

__ObjectBasicSettings.doc: Basic configuration for a data object, including its identity, documentation, and deletion strategy. A data object acts as a logical model for a database table or MongoDB collection, and is central to defining how data is stored, queried, and managed within a microservice.

ObjectBasicSettings.__name.doc: A unique identifier for the data object used consistently across generated code, API routes, and documentation. The name must be a single, camelCase word without spaces or special characters, and should be unique within the project. Use a singular noun that clearly represents the entity (e.g., 'product', 'order', 'task').
ObjectBasicSettings.__description.doc: A descriptive explanation of what the data object represents. This description is used in documentation and helps clarify the business domain the object serves.
ObjectBasicSettings.__frontendDocument.doc: A text based information to inform the frontend developer or frontend AI agent about the data object specific UX behaviour of the data object logic based on user stories and use cases. The format may be either text or markdown(recommended). Write the document as an AI prompt and describe data object specific UX behaviours. Note that this document will be given to the AI agent or human developer combined with all technical details that is generated from the data object design,so this document should only focus on data object-specific behavioral UX business logic.
ObjectBasicSettings.__useSoftDelete.doc: Overrides the default data model setting to enable or disable soft deletion for this object. If enabled, records will not be physically deleted but marked inactive using an 'isActive' flag. These records will be excluded from normal queries unless explicitly requested.
ObjectBasicSettings.__virtual.doc: Declares a response-only (virtual) data object. Its properties describe a RESPONSE SHAPE only: no table or collection, no migration, no model, no db-layer module, no index, no seed and no Elasticsearch mapping is generated for it, and no tenant id column is injected. The object still yields its typed response record, so a BusinessApi bound to it keeps a typed response in the api layer, swagger and api docs. Such an api may only be a `get` or a `list` (create/update/delete is an ERROR); its main operation reads no database: `this.result` starts as an empty object (get, no id route parameter - so author its restSettings.routePath beside a default-routed list, or both take the bare resource path: ROUTE_COLLISION) or an empty array (list), and the api's own actions produce the response - AddToResponse / functionCall entries on a get, a ListMapAction with `replacesResult: true` in `afterMainListOperation` on a list. A relation, a crud or fetch action, a view, a seed or any other storage reference that points at a virtual object is an ERROR, and so is a storage-backed feature section (checkout, subscription, marketplace, invoicing, fiscalization, ledger, membership, graph or enterprise projection, geo, object moderation) activated on it. `useSoftDelete` and the access settings are ignored; indexes and entity cache settings are ignored with a WARNING. Leave false (the default) for every object that stores rows.
ObjectBasicSettings.__publishDbEvents.doc: Whether a write to this object publishes its row-level Kafka events: the db events `<serviceCodename>-dbevent-<object>-{created|updated|deleted}` and the elastic-index events `elastic-index-<codename>_<object>-{created|updated|deleted}`. `true` (the default) publishes both on every create, update and delete, bulk and by-query writes included. `false` turns both families off for an object nothing in the project consumes, such as an internal log or bookkeeping table: the Elasticsearch index of the object is STILL written (search, dynamic DataViews and cross-service reads keep working), only the Kafka copies stop, and their topics are no longer pre-created at boot. Route events of the object's apis follow each api's own `raiseApiEvent` and are not affected. Validation REFUSES `false` (ERROR DB_EVENTS_SWITCH_CONSUMED, naming the consumer) on an object that a stored DataView (main object, aggregate or stat source), an eventSubscription, a kafka-triggered business api, an edge controller kafka trigger, an agent kafka controller, a realtime hub (an `autoBridgeDataEvents` hub of its service, a hub kafkaEvent, or a hub `roomSettings.authSources` entry naming the object in any service, whose membership eviction is always on), an agent harness kafka trigger, a business api SSE `kafkaProgressListeners` topic, an event notification, an external feed or a content model consumes, because those consumers read exactly these events. A consumer that exists only at runtime (for example a dynamic agent's kafka controller stored by the agentHub) is not seen by validation. Framework system objects that nobody consumes (the agent run records, the tool catalog, the notification logs, the cron run log) ship with `false`; when a project does consume one of them, it keeps publishing and validation says so (DB_EVENTS_SWITCH_SYSTEM_OBJECT_CONSUMED). This is a separate setting from the retired api-level `raiseDbLevelEvents`, which still has no effect.
ObjectBasicSettings.__description.sample: User data object stores the user information like name, email, password and clientId etc.
ObjectBasicSettings.name: String

__ObjectAuthorization.doc: Defines access control scope for this data object, including tenant scoping and public accessibility. These settings are applied globally unless explicitly overridden at the Business API level.

ObjectAuthorization.__objectDataIsInTenantLevel.doc: Determines whether this object is scoped per tenant in a multi-tenant architecture. Only a stored true adds the implicit tenant ID field `<tenantName>Id` (e.g., clientId) that segregates data per tenant and filters the object's reads and scoped writes to the caller's tenant; a blueprint that omits the flag gets no tenant column and no tenant filter, although the pattern lists true as its default, so set it explicitly. Use this for tenant-owned data like projects or documents.
ObjectAuthorization.__dataObjectAccess.doc: Specifies the default access level for this DataObject and its related get/list APIs. The value is defined by the DataObjectAccess enum, which determines whether the object is private (restricted to owner/admins), protected (available to all authenticated project users), or public (open to everyone, including anonymous). API-level configurations may override this default.

__DataObjectAccess.doc.#: Defines the possible access levels for a DataObject. This type captures whether the object is only visible to its owner/admins (private), shared with authenticated project users (protected), or exposed to the public including anonymous users (public). The key difference is between restricted vs. shared access, and within shared access whether authentication is required.
__DataObjectAccess.doc.accessPrivate: Only the object owner and system administrators can access.
__DataObjectAccess.doc.accessProtected: All authenticated project users can access.
__DataObjectAccess.doc.accessPublic: All users, including anonymous, can access.

__RedisEntityCacheSettings.doc: Configuration for Redis-based entity-level caching. Enables fast access to frequently used data by storing and serving object-level records from Redis, with support for custom cache criteria and smart expiration.

RedisEntityCacheSettings.__useEntityCaching.doc: Enables Redis entity caching for this object. When active, individual records are cached in Redis, improving read performance for high-frequency access patterns.

__CompositeIndex.doc: Defines a composite index for a data object. Composite indexes improve database performance for queries that filter or sort based on multiple fields. Each index is created at the database level and can optionally handle duplicate conflicts during insert operations. Note that if you need unique constraints on a single field, you can use the `unique` property of the DataProperty instead. Composite indexes are particularly useful for optimizing complex queries that involve multiple fields, such as searching for users by email and client ID simultaneously or whne you need to ensure uniqueness across multiple fields (e.g., email and clientId). They are defined at the data object level and will be used across all related Business APIs.

CompositeIndex.__indexName.doc: Unique name of the database index. Used in DDL statements and must be unique within the scope of the current data object. Choose a descriptive name that reflects the indexed fields (e.g., userEmailIndex).
CompositeIndex.__onDuplicate.doc:
Defines the behavior when an insert operation encounters a duplicate key on this index. Options include updating the existing row or throwing an error. Useful for implementing upsert logic. By default (nullsNotDistinct: false), a key that carries a NULL is never a duplicate: the generated duplicate check skips a record with any null index field and the database unique index treats NULLs as distinct, so for such a row every option except doInsert does nothing and the write inserts a new row. Validation warns (COMPOSITE_INDEX_NULLABLE_MEMBER) when an index other than doInsert includes a non-required property; make every member required (with a defaultValue sentinel where needed) when the index must hold one row per combination. Alternatively set nullsNotDistinct: true on PostgreSQL 15+ (declare serviceOptions.postgresMajorVersion >= 15) or MongoDB to apply onDuplicate to NULL-bearing logical keys.

WHAT THE WORKFLOW SEES. `stopOperation` and `doUpdate` make a create api idempotent: a replay answers 2xx with the existing row. The api manager reports which happened as `this.createOutcome` — `'created'` when a row was really inserted, `'duplicateStopped'` when this index matched and NOTHING was written, `'duplicateUpdated'` when it matched and the row was updated in place. Post-main actions still run on a replay (the pipeline is not skipped), so gate any side effect that must not repeat — a child create, a counter allocation, a published event — with `condition: "this.createOutcome === 'created'"`. Without that gate the replay re-runs every one of them against the row that already has them, silently: the response body looks correct and only the database shows the duplicate children. Available from `afterMainCreateOperation` on, and only on a `create` api whose object declares an index with one of these two policies.
CompositeIndex.__indexFields.doc: List of field names that form the composite index. The order of fields matters for query optimization. For example, ['email', 'clientId'] allows fast lookups for email within a specific client context.
CompositeIndex.__nullsNotDistinct.doc: Opt-in NULL-equal logical keys, default false. Supported by nodejs, java, dotnet and rust on PostgreSQL 15+ (declare serviceOptions.postgresMajorVersion >= 15) and MongoDB only. A unique composite with this flag treats null members as equal; MongoDB also treats a missing member as null. create/createBulk apply onDuplicate to null-bearing keys. PostgreSQL emits NULLS NOT DISTINCT; MongoDB omits nullable-member type filters while retaining soft-delete and partialWhere predicates. Unsupported stores are rejected. Existing indexes require an explicit migration; reconcile never tightens an existing unique automatically. Cannot be combined with onDuplicate doInsert.
CompositeIndex.__partialWhere.doc: A PARTIAL-index predicate: an equality map from first-level declared property names of the owning data object to scalar literals, e.g. { "isDefault": true }. The index then covers ONLY the rows that match every entry, so a unique index enforces uniqueness inside that row set and nowhere else ("at most one default per (userId, providerName)" is indexFields [userId, providerName] with partialWhere { isDefault: true }). Each key must be a declared Boolean, Enum or String property (not a framework column, not the tenant column); each value must be a string or boolean literal matching the property type. The predicate is ANDed onto the soft-delete predicate the index already carries on a useSoftDelete object (sequelize `where`, MongoDB `partialFilterExpression`), and the boot reconcile compares it like any declared `where`. Leave it unset (the default) for an index over every live row. On a database that already holds rows violating a new partial UNIQUE index, the index build fails and the service boots without it (the table is reported degraded and /health lists the pending migration) unless a data repair runs first.

__OnDuplicate.doc.#: Enumeration that defines the conflict resolution strategy when a new record would violate a composite index constraint.
__OnDuplicate.doc.doUpdate: Update the existing record if a duplicate key is encountered. Equivalent to an upsert operation.
__OnDuplicate.doc.throwError: Throw a database error when a duplicate key is encountered. Prevents the insertion of conflicting data.
__OnDuplicate.doc.stopOperation: Stop the operation silently if a duplicate key is encountered. The existing record remains unchanged and no error is thrown.
__OnDuplicate.doc.doInsert: Proceed with the operation without checking for duplicates. Use this option when your composite index is designed for search purposes only and duplicates are allowed.

__PaymentResultMap.doc: Defines how normalized payment outcomes (started, success, failed, canceled) map to internal order status values using MScript expressions. The four buckets are provider-neutral — the framework normalizes provider-specific statuses into them. The mapping is declarative: the generated payment layer does not evaluate it or write the order row; a checkout lifecycle hook performs that write. The type was originally Stripe-specific but is now used by `CheckoutConfig.mapPaymentResultToOrderStatus` across all providers; the name is kept to avoid disrupting existing references.

PaymentResultMap.__paymentResultStarted.doc: MScript for mapping the Stripe 'started' status to an internal order status.
PaymentResultMap.__paymentResultCanceled.doc: MScript for mapping the Stripe 'canceled' status to an internal order status.
PaymentResultMap.__paymentResultFailed.doc: MScript for mapping the Stripe 'failed' status to an internal order status.
PaymentResultMap.__paymentResultSuccess.doc: MScript for mapping the Stripe 'success' status to an internal order status.

__OnPaymentError.doc.#: Enum options for handling errors that occur during the Stripe payment process.
__OnPaymentError.doc.continueRoute: Continue processing, log the error, and set status to 'failed'.
__OnPaymentError.doc.throwError: Throw an error and halt processing when a payment error occurs.

__DunningExhaustedState.doc.#: What the tokenized recharge scheduler does with a subscription whose refused recharges reached SubscriptionConfig.maxDunningAttempts. Hosted providers run their own dunning; this enum only governs the framework-driven cycle.
__DunningExhaustedState.doc.cancel: End the subscription: statusLiteral `canceled`, `canceledAt` stamped, trial entitlement revoked (a trialing row's `trialEnd` is clamped to now), recharge anchor cleared. The default.
__DunningExhaustedState.doc.pastDue: Park the subscription: statusLiteral `past_due` with the recharge anchor cleared, so no further charge is attempted until a payment method is restored and `nextRechargeAt` is re-stamped.

__SubscriptionRouteAccess.doc.#: Who may drive the INJECTED subscription lifecycle routes (POST /v1/subscribe<x>/:orderId, DELETE and PATCH /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId) of a DataObject with a subscription block. Those three routes are emitted by the framework, not authored, so there is no BusinessApi authOptions on them to gate: they carry the login gate and the per-row ownership gate, and nothing that separates privilege levels INSIDE one tenant. Tenancy is not that separation - the tenant filter legitimately admits every member of the workspace the subscription belongs to.
__SubscriptionRouteAccess.doc.inherit: The default. Use SubscriptionConfig.checkRoles when it is non-empty; otherwise DERIVE the gate from this object's own authored apis - when EVERY api bound to this data object declares a non-empty checkRoles, the injected routes require the UNION of those lists, and when even one does not, no role gate is emitted at all (the earlier ungated render). Deriving from the union, and only from a fully gated object, keeps the derived gate from ever being stricter than the object's own authored surface: a caller it refuses holds no role that any authored api on this object admits. `absoluteRoles` is NOT read - it is a bypass, not a gate.
__SubscriptionRouteAccess.doc.open: Emit NO role gate on the injected routes, whatever the authored apis declare. The explicit way to say that the subscribe / cancel / re-price routes are genuinely buyer-facing (a self-serve consumer plan, where the subscriber is an ordinary member rather than a billing operator). Login and ownership still apply.

__CheckoutRouteAccess.doc.#: Who may drive the INJECTED checkout payment routes (PATCH /v1/start<x>payment/:orderId, PATCH /v1/refresh<x>payment/:orderId, PATCH /v1/checkoutrefresh<x>/:orderId, GET /v1/<x>paymentbyorderid/:orderId, GET /v1/<x>paymentbypaymentid/:paymentId and POST /v1/<x>refundpayment/:orderId) of a DataObject with a checkout block. Those routes are emitted by the framework, not authored, so no BusinessApi authOptions gates them: they carry the login gate and the per-row ownership gate. When the order object's owner cannot be session-fed (no sessionSettings.isOwnerField, e.g. an object written only by cron or internal-call apis) the ownership gate cannot bind, and before this field there was no way at all to gate them. Leaving CheckoutConfig.routeAccess unset means `inherit` (as SubscriptionConfig.routeAccess); see CheckoutConfig.routeAccess. The refund route follows CheckoutConfig.refundRouteAccess (default `operator`) and takes this gate only under refundRouteAccess `inherit`.
__CheckoutRouteAccess.doc.inherit: The default (an unset routeAccess means inherit). Use CheckoutConfig.checkRoles when it is non-empty; otherwise DERIVE the gate from this object's own authored apis exactly as SubscriptionRouteAccess.inherit does - when EVERY authored api bound to this data object that can carry a human role answer declares a non-empty checkRoles, the injected routes require the UNION of those lists, and otherwise no role gate is emitted. The derived gate is never stricter than the object's own authored surface. `absoluteRoles` is NOT read - it is a bypass, not a gate.
__CheckoutRouteAccess.doc.open: Emit NO role gate on the injected checkout routes, whatever checkRoles or the authored apis declare. The explicit way to say that the start / refresh / read / refund routes are genuinely buyer-facing, and the acknowledgement that silences PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_ROUTES_UNGATED. Login and ownership still apply.

__CheckoutRefundRouteAccess.doc.#: Who may call the INJECTED refund route POST /v1/<x>refundpayment/:orderId of a DataObject with a checkout block. The route moves money back through the provider and is emitted by the framework, so no BusinessApi authOptions gates it, and the refund rules a designer authors on a RefundAction api (refund window, order-state preconditions, approval, earnings-hold checks) do not run on it. Previously it shared the buyer-facing gate of start / refresh (login, CheckoutConfig.checkRoles / routeAccess, and the per-row ownership gate that ADMITS the order owner), so on a buyer-facing checkout the buyer who owned a paid order could refund it through the raw route. This field separates the refund route from that gate; start / refresh / checkoutrefresh / paymentbyorderid / paymentbypaymentid are not affected by it.
__CheckoutRefundRouteAccess.doc.operator: The default (an unset refundRouteAccess means operator). The refund route requires a PLATFORM payment operator - a session whose role is superAdmin, admin or saasAdmin (superAdmin or saasAdmin in a multi-tenant project, which has no role named admin), or one holding the refund-specific paymentRefundOperator PBAC grant (the shared paymentOperator grant of the payment consoles does not admit here), plus the additive PAYMENT_ADMIN_TOKEN when the deployment sets it - or a verified, allow-listed inter-service (M2M) caller. Order ownership alone is never enough, and CheckoutConfig.checkRoles / routeAccess do not open it. A refusal is 403 OPERATOR_REQUIRED (401 LOGIN_REQUIRED without a session). The per-row ownership gate still runs in the handler, so a non-absolute operator refunds only orders the ownership gate admits; admin / superAdmin (superAdmin / saasAdmin in a multi-tenant project) and M2M callers bypass it. Buyer refunds go through an authored RefundAction api, where the designer's own rules run.
__CheckoutRefundRouteAccess.doc.inherit: The earlier behaviour, as an explicit opt-in: the refund route carries the same gate as the other injected checkout routes (login, CheckoutConfig.checkRoles / routeAccess, per-row ownership), so the order owner can refund their own order through it. Validation warns PAYMENT_REFUND_ROUTE_BUYER_REACHABLE when that gate is buyer-facing (routeAccess open, no role gate derived, or a role list that holds a role other than superAdmin / admin / saasAdmin; in a multi-tenant project other than superAdmin / saasAdmin).
__CheckoutRefundRouteAccess.doc.disabled: The refund route is not mounted (404). Refunds go only through an authored RefundAction api (or the provider dashboard).

__StripeOrderItemRelation.doc: Defines the relation between an order object and its order item object. This relation is used by payment-related automation patterns to fetch order items and run item-based operations. The type was originally Stripe-specific but is now provider-neutral; both `CheckoutConfig.orderItemRelation` and the legacy `StripeOrderConfig.orderItemRelation` reference this type. The name is kept to avoid disrupting existing references — a provider-neutral alias may be added in a future slice without removing this one.

StripeOrderItemRelation.__hasOrderItemRelation.doc: Enables order to orderItem relation mapping. When false, relation configuration is ignored.
StripeOrderItemRelation.__orderItemObject.doc: Order item data object name. This should be a local data object in the same service.
StripeOrderItemRelation.__orderForeignKey.doc: Property of the current order object that provides the value used to match order items. Commonly `id`.
StripeOrderItemRelation.__orderItemLocalKey.doc: Property of the order item object that stores the relation value to the order. Commonly `orderId`.
StripeOrderItemRelation.__quantityProperty.doc: Property of the order item object that stores item quantity for perOrderItemQuantity operations. Commonly `quantity` or `qty`.

__Checkout.doc: Provider-neutral one-time-payment activation for a DataObject. Mark a DataObject as billable by enabling `objectIsAnOrderObject` and pointing `configuration.providerName` at a configured PaymentProvider. The framework auto-generates the sys_<X>Payment system data object, the start/refresh/callback APIs, and wires the unified webhook router to the bound provider. This is the recommended shape for new billable objects, binding to any configured PaymentProvider via `providerName`.

Checkout.__objectIsAnOrderObject.doc: Enables one-time-payment logic for this object. When true, the object is treated as an order and integrated with the bound payment provider's payment flow.
Checkout.__configuration.doc: The CheckoutConfig describing how this object maps onto the provider's payment intent (amount property, currency property, status mapping, lifecycle hooks). Leave it null if objectIsAnOrderObject is false.

__CheckoutConfig.doc: Configuration for provider-neutral one-time payments. Provider-binding is explicit via `providerName` (lookup into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[]). Property bindings (amount / currency / status / owner) are PropRefer paths into the parent DataObject. Lifecycle hooks replace the legacy edgeFunctionOnStatusChange / edgeFunctionPaymentDone / afterPaymentCreations fields — designers can author multiple per-trigger MScript handlers in one place. HOSTED-CHECKOUT RETURN: when the bound provider settles through a hosted checkout form (iyzico Checkout Form), the vendor callback ALWAYS points at the service's own `/v1/payments/checkout-return/<provider>` route, derived from SERVICE_URL and never from a request body. That route settles the ticket and then redirects the buyer 303 to the ticket's `metadata.returnUrl`, which is stamped from the `return_url` supplied in the payment user params of the START call. With no `return_url` there is nothing to redirect to and the route answers a minimal JSON confirmation (`ok`, `orderId`, `paymentId`, `paymentStatus`, `statusLiteral`, `requestId`) - documented behaviour, but the buyer's browser stops there, so the buyer's return to the application depends entirely on `return_url` being present. The mounted payment route takes it as `body.paymentUserParams.return_url` on `PATCH /v1/start<object>payment/:orderId`; an api that drives the flow with a start-stage PaymentAction takes it from its OWN declared requestParameters (PAYMENT_START_NO_CALLER_PARAMS is the design-time finding when it declares none). A buyer who pays on the hosted form but never comes back (tab closed) is settled the same way, once, from iyzico's Checkout Form webhook (`CHECKOUT_FORM_AUTH`) on `/v1/payments/webhook/<provider>`, which the merchant points at the service in iyzico's panel. 3-D SECURE RETURN: a saved-card iyzico start (3dsecure/initialize) sends the service's own `/v1/payments/threeds-return/<provider>` as the vendor callback, likewise derived from SERVICE_URL. iyzico posts the bank-challenge outcome there; the route resolves the ticket by the posted paymentId plus the attempt's conversationId, calls 3dsecure/auth itself (forwarding conversationData) when the bank reports mdStatus=1, settles the ticket success / failed / amount_mismatch, runs the payment lifecycle hooks, and redirects 303 to `metadata.returnUrl` with `orderId` and `status` query parameters (the same JSON confirmation without one). The start answer for that shape is not a redirect: the frontend renders `next_action.threeDSHtmlContent`. No designer-authored complete stage is involved for either iyzico shape. 3-D SECURE BY PROVIDER: Stripe completes in the browser (Stripe.js) and the generated webhook route records it, with no return route; Adyen completes through the generated `PATCH /v1/complete<object>payment/:orderId` route with the `details` Adyen Web returns; iyzico through the two return routes above. A design never authors a complete, callback or webhook stage for these three providers.

CheckoutConfig.__providerName.doc: Name of the configured PaymentProvider that handles this object's payments. Must match an entry in projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. When omitted and exactly one stripe-typed provider is configured, the framework auto-binds to that one (single-provider convenience).
CheckoutConfig.__orderName.doc: Display name of the order as it appears in provider dashboards and receipts.
CheckoutConfig.__orderIdProperty.doc: The property name that holds the order's unique identifier.
CheckoutConfig.__amountProperty.doc: The property name that holds the order amount for payment. PLATFORM MONEY CONVENTION: every bound money property carries MAJOR currency units as a decimal (e.g. 250.00 TL, 10.00 USD) - never minor units (kurus/cents). Adapters convert to each provider's wire encoding themselves; a blueprint that stores minor units in a bound column will charge 100x. The bound column MUST be declared `type: "Decimal"`, so the framework rounds it to its `decimalScale` at every write boundary and before the amount reaches the provider. A bound column declared with another NUMERIC type (Integer/Short/Double/Float) is migrated by validation to Decimal (scale from the binding's static currency, default 2) and reported as an auto-fix; a non-numeric one is the ERROR `MONEY_BINDING_NOT_DECIMAL`. REQUIRED IN EFFECT: the generated REST start route (`PATCH /v1/start<object>payment/:orderId`) reads the amount off the persisted order row by LITERAL key, [amountProperty, `amount`] - there is no static amount and that route strips a body amount - so an activated checkout object that leaves amountProperty unset and declares no `amount` property is a design-time ERROR CHECKOUT_AMOUNT_UNBOUND (that route is refused 400 on every call, and a PaymentAction needs amountProperty anyway). A PaymentAction start resolves amountProperty more widely (request parameters, a dotted path into the persisted row such as `order.total`, then the manager scope), so a SET amountProperty that is not a declared property is only a WARNING CHECKOUT_AMOUNT_BINDING_NOT_A_COLUMN: the PaymentAction start works, the REST start route reads the literal key and NaNs (or charges the `amount` column when one exists).
CheckoutConfig.__currencyProperty.doc: The property name that holds the currency for the order.
CheckoutConfig.__currencyStaticValue.doc: The static currency value for the order. It is the LAST fallback, not an override: the currency is resolved from `currencyProperty` first (the request parameter of that name, then the persisted order row), or from a literal `currency` request parameter when `currencyProperty` is unset, and this static value applies only when that resolves to nothing.
CheckoutConfig.__orderStatusProperty.doc: The field name in the data object that holds the current order status. DECLARATIVE ONLY: the generated payment layer does NOT write this field. Payment results advance the payment ticket (`sys_<Object>Payment.statusLiteral`) and fire the checkout `lifecycleHooks`; an `afterPaymentCaptured` / `afterPaymentFailed` hook (or your own Business API) is what writes the order status.
CheckoutConfig.__orderStatusUpdateDateProperty.doc: The field name that records the timestamp of the last order status update. DECLARATIVE ONLY: the generated payment layer does NOT stamp it; write it from the same lifecycle hook that writes `orderStatusProperty`.
CheckoutConfig.__orderOwnerIdProperty.doc: The property name that holds the ID of the user who owns the order. Declarative: the generated payment ownership checks do not read it (they use the data object's owner field; see the PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_OWNERSHIP_UNBINDABLE warning), and it is never sent to a provider as a customer id.
CheckoutConfig.__description.doc: MScript expression for the order description, shown in provider dashboards and receipts.
CheckoutConfig.__mapPaymentResultToOrderStatus.doc: Declares how payment lifecycle outcomes (started, success, failed, canceled) map to internal order status values via MScript expressions. Same shape as the legacy mapping; the framework normalizes provider-specific statuses into these four buckets. DECLARATIVE ONLY: no generated route evaluates these expressions or writes `orderStatusProperty`; the table documents the intended mapping for the lifecycle hook that performs the write.
CheckoutConfig.__orderItemRelation.doc: How this order object relates to its order item object. Reused from StripeOrderItemRelation; the type is provider-neutral despite the legacy name.
CheckoutConfig.__lifecycleHooks.doc: Designer-authored MScript handlers fired by the payment dispatcher when the state machine advances. Each hook declares a `trigger` (e.g. afterPaymentCaptured, afterPaymentRefunded) and an MScript body. Replaces the legacy `afterPaymentCreations` + `edgeFunctionOnStatusChange` + `edgeFunctionPaymentDone` fields — a single hook with trigger=afterPaymentCaptured is the canonical replacement for both edge functions. Inside a hook `resource.metadata` values are `unknown`: narrow one with `typeof x === 'string'` or `String(x)` before passing it on (a truthiness check does not make it a string; see LifecycleHook.script).
CheckoutConfig.__onPaymentError.doc: Determines the system's behavior if a payment error occurs. Options are 'continueRoute' to proceed or 'throwError' to stop with an error.
CheckoutConfig.__idempotencyStrategy.doc: How idempotency keys are generated for retryable provider calls. `framework` (default) — the framework generates a UUIDv4 per intent and stamps it onto the provider call. `adapter` — the adapter uses the provider's native idempotency mechanism (e.g. Stripe's Idempotency-Key header with a provider-derived value). `framework` is simpler and more portable; `adapter` is more provider-idiomatic.
CheckoutConfig.__publishLifecycleEvents.doc: Opt-in (default false; only a literal `true` on an ACTIVE checkout block counts) that makes the generated payment layer publish this object's normalized PAYMENT lifecycle events to Kafka (family `payment`), one topic per event: `<projectCodename>-<service>-service-lcevent-payment-<object lowercased>-<suffix>`, where the FIXED event list and its suffixes are `payment.captured` -> `captured`, `payment.failed` -> `failed`, `payment.canceled` -> `canceled`, `refund.succeeded` -> `refund-succeeded`. On a nodejs service the list also carries `payment.requires_action` -> `requires-action` and `payment.authorized` -> `authorized` (state events: published only while the ticket is still `started`) and `refund.created` -> `refund-created` and `refund.failed` -> `refund-failed` (facts keyed on the refund), and the same flag also publishes the object's DISPUTES (family `dispute`, topic `...-lcevent-dispute-<object>-<suffix>`: `dispute.opened` -> `opened` and `dispute.evidence_required` -> `evidence-required` as facts, `dispute.won` -> `won` and `dispute.lost` -> `lost` only when the dispute row ends in that state; `data.dispute` = an allowlisted sys_<Object>Dispute projection, no metadata) and, when the object also has an ACTIVE marketplace block, its PAYOUTS (family `payout`, topic `...-lcevent-payout-<object>-<suffix>`: `payout.in_transit` -> `in-transit`, `payout.paid` -> `paid`, `payout.failed` -> `failed` (with failureReason), `payout.returned` -> `returned`, each only when the payout row ends in that state; `data.payout` = an allowlisted sys_<Object>Payout projection without the claim / lease columns or metadata, `record` null). The java and dotnet payment layers publish the fixed list only. Published by the payment intent machine AFTER the sys_<Object>Payment status write and AFTER the designer lifecycle hooks, and only when the ticket ENDS in the state the event names (captured -> success, failed -> failed, canceled -> canceled, refund.succeeded -> refunded or partially_refunded): a late cancel of a captured payment, or a capture the amount gate refused, publishes nothing. A tokenized renewal ticket (`metadata.recharge === true`) is not published on this family - the subscription family announces the renewal. `data` = { eventType, family, object, providerName, providerEventId, occurredAt, orderId, previousStatus, status, dedupeKey, failureReason (payment.failed only), payment (an ALLOWLISTED projection of the sys_<Object>Payment ticket: id, orderId, providerName, paymentId, providerIntentId, paymentStatus, statusLiteral, failureReason, amount, currency, fee, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt, the tenant column), refund (refund.succeeded: providerRefundId, providerIntentId, statusLiteral, amount, currency, reason), record (this object's own row read by `orderId`, in the shape and unit its db-change event publishes) }; never the raw provider payload, the client secret / next action, the refund evidence token or the ticket's metadata. Delivery is AT LEAST ONCE through the service's lifecycle outbox: each event is written to `sys_lifecycle_outbox` (one row per `data.dedupeKey`, the built envelope plus its retry state) before it is sent, the send is not awaited on the payment path, and a send the broker refuses (logged `PaymentLifecycleEventPublishFailed`) is re-sent by the outbox sweeper with the same envelope id and dedupeKey (every PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_OUTBOX_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, default 30 s; backoff up to one hour; parked `dead` after 50 refusals). A redelivery can repeat an event, and a process that dies between the status write and the outbox write loses that one event: dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`, and reconcile money from the rows, not from the stream. Envelope: `type` = the normalized event type; `actor.tenantId` = the row's tenant in a multi-tenant project. Off (the default) the generated code is byte-identical to a build without the field; the topics are listed by the kafka topic census and pre-created only while it is on.
CheckoutConfig.__storePaymentMethod.doc: An EXPLICIT opt-in (default false; only a literal `true` on an ACTIVE checkout block counts) to store the buyer's payment method while paying on this order object. It is the checkout twin of SubscriptionConfig.storePaymentMethod, for an order object that has no subscription block (a checkout-only order): either switch turns the behaviour on, and the framework reads them as ONE design-time rule (`storesPaymentMethodWhilePaying`), so the start routes, the PaymentAction enrolment, the webhook method mirror and the designer prompt cannot disagree. What it does: (1) a PaymentAction start / simple stage on the order object carries the stored-method enrolment (`storeMethod: true`) to the provider adapter (Adyen sends `storePaymentMethod: true`, Stripe `setup_future_usage: 'off_session'`), as under the subscription switch; (2) iyzico (save the card while paying on the hosted Checkout Form): the generated `PATCH /v1/start<order>payment/:orderId` and a PaymentAction start open the hosted form with the buyer's own card storage key (`sys_paymentCustomer.cardStorageKey`, read server-side from the buyer's payment-customer mapping, never from the request; none for a buyer who has no key yet), so iyzico lists the buyer's saved cards and offers to save the new one, and a card the buyer saves there is filed in the buyer's wallet (`sys_paymentMethod`) the moment the payment settles (the browser return or iyzico's Checkout Form webhook, once) through the identity owner's machine-only `attachPaymentMethodByCustomerIdForMachine`, which reads the buyer from the mapping; (3) it opens the RETENTION GATE of the webhook method mirror for the service: a provider-reported stored method (`method.attached` / `method.updated`) is filed for the user who owns the provider customer's mapping, through the same machine-only api. It is never read from a request body. The card saving needs an identity owner (the auth service holds sys_paymentCustomer) and a payment ticket that records its owner; without them nothing is saved. Default false: with both switches off the order renders exactly as before.
CheckoutConfig.__billingModel.doc: OBJECT-level billing model of this checkout object (docs/ADR-billing-model-reseller-intermediary.md). `reseller` (al-sat): the PLATFORM is seller of record — it issues the full-amount invoice + fiscal document to the buyer and the FULL amount enters the platform's account as a plain charge, so a marketplace block on the SAME object is refused at design time (BILLING_MODEL_RESELLER_WITH_MARKETPLACE_SPLIT — a PSP split under a platform-issued full invoice is an invoice/cash mismatch); seller earnings settle platform-side via the earnings ledger + payment instructions. `intermediary` (aracilik): the SUB-MERCHANT is seller of record — the platform NEVER fiscalizes the sale, so fiscalization on the SAME object is refused (BILLING_MODEL_INTERMEDIARY_WITH_PLATFORM_FISCALIZATION); the platform's only invoice is the COMMISSION invoice to the seller, and the PSP marketplace split is the natural money path. The selector is PER OBJECT because hybrid platforms mix models across objects of one project (e.g. events=reseller on a plain account, experiences=intermediary on a marketplace account — two paymentProviders entries of the same brand with different names). Null/absent = legacy behavior: no model-pairing validation fires and emitted code is unchanged (a marketplace-bearing object without a declared model gets the BILLING_MODEL_NOT_DECLARED warning nudge). Issuing sale documents in the SELLER's name from platform infrastructure is illegal in TR and permanently out of scope — neither model ever does it.
CheckoutConfig.__checkRoles.doc: Roles required on the INJECTED checkout payment routes of this object - PATCH /v1/start<x>payment/:orderId, PATCH /v1/refresh<x>payment/:orderId, PATCH /v1/checkoutrefresh<x>/:orderId, GET /v1/<x>paymentbyorderid/:orderId, GET /v1/<x>paymentbypaymentid/:paymentId and POST /v1/<x>refundpayment/:orderId (the checkout twin of SubscriptionConfig.checkRoles). Same meaning as BusinessApi authOptions.checkRoles: the list RESTRICTS (a caller holding none of these roles is refused 403 PAYMENT_ROLE_REQUIRED) and it is combined with OR. It is NOT absoluteRoles: the surface keeps its own separate BYPASS list (admin / superAdmin, PAYMENT_ABSOLUTE_ROLES), and a verified inter-service (M2M) caller that carries no user identity is admitted because the lifecycle routes are mounted allowM2M and a machine caller holds no role (an M2M caller that names a user - a forwarded user token - is that user and faces the list and the ownership gate). Login and the per-row ownership gate still run in front of and behind it. This is the way to gate the injected routes of an order object whose owner cannot be session-fed (written only by cron or internal-call apis), where the ownership gate cannot bind. A non-empty list applies unless routeAccess is `open`. The provider callback, the webhook and the mock 3-D Secure route are not gated by it. The refund route carries this gate only when refundRouteAccess is `inherit`: by default it carries the payment-operator gate instead, and `disabled` does not mount it.
CheckoutConfig.__routeAccess.doc: What to do when checkRoles is empty. `inherit` (the default: an UNSET routeAccess means inherit) derives the injected routes' role gate from this object's authored apis (see CheckoutRouteAccess for the rule; it is the SubscriptionConfig derivation): when every human-facing authored api on the object declares checkRoles the six routes require their union, otherwise no role gate is emitted, and when the object's owner cannot be session-fed the design-time WARNING PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_ROUTES_UNGATED says so. `open` emits no role gate at all, even over a non-empty checkRoles, and states that the checkout routes are meant to stay ungated (it silences PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_ROUTES_UNGATED). Previously an unset value meant no role gate: a buyer-facing checkout that relied on that keeps it with `open`, and the design-time WARNING PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_ROUTES_GATE_INHERITED names every block whose routes the new default gates while routeAccess is still unset (writing either value silences it).
CheckoutConfig.__refundRouteAccess.doc: Who may call the injected refund route POST /v1/<x>refundpayment/:orderId (see CheckoutRefundRouteAccess). `operator` (the DEFAULT: an unset value means operator) requires a platform payment operator (superAdmin / admin / saasAdmin; in a multi-tenant project superAdmin / saasAdmin only, as it has no role named admin; or the refund-specific paymentRefundOperator PBAC grant - the shared paymentOperator grant of the payment consoles does not admit here; plus PAYMENT_ADMIN_TOKEN when set) or a verified inter-service (M2M) caller - owning the order is not enough, and checkRoles / routeAccess do not apply to this one route. `inherit` restores the earlier behaviour (the refund route shares the start / refresh gate, so the order owner can refund) and warns PAYMENT_REFUND_ROUTE_BUYER_REACHABLE when that gate is buyer-facing. `disabled` does not mount the route. Buyer-initiated refunds belong on an authored RefundAction api, where the designer's refund rules run. UPGRADE NOTE: previously the refund route was reachable by the order owner under the checkout gate; a project whose buyers or non-operator staff called it directly now gets 403 OPERATOR_REQUIRED and must move that flow to a RefundAction api, or set `inherit` explicitly (unsafe on a buyer-facing checkout). No migration rewrites existing blueprints.

__BillingModel.doc.#: Who is the seller of record for a checkout-enabled DataObject (docs/ADR-billing-model-reseller-intermediary.md). Declared per OBJECT on CheckoutConfig.billingModel so a hybrid platform can run both models side by side in one project. Absent = undeclared (legacy behavior; no pairing validation fires).
__BillingModel.doc.reseller: Al-sat: the platform buys and re-sells — it is the seller of record, issues the full-amount invoice/fiscal document to the buyer, and takes the FULL amount as a plain charge (no PSP split). Seller earnings settle platform-side against the seller's incoming invoice via the earnings ledger + payment instructions.
__BillingModel.doc.intermediary: Aracılık: the sub-merchant is the seller of record — the platform never fiscalizes the sale; its only invoice is the commission invoice to the seller, and the PSP marketplace split is the natural money path.

__Subscription.doc: Provider-neutral subscription activation for a DataObject. When enabled, the framework auto-generates a sys_<X>Subscription table (or treats the parent DataObject as the subscription record if so configured) and emits subscribe/cancel/update APIs that route through the bound provider's subscriptions surface. Requires the bound PaymentProvider to have capabilities.supportsSubscriptions=true.

Subscription.__objectIsSubscriptionObject.doc: Enables subscription logic for this object. When true, the framework treats this object as a recurring-billing entity bound to a SubscriptionPlan.
Subscription.__configuration.doc: The SubscriptionConfig binding plan/customer/lifecycle properties to the provider. Leave null if objectIsSubscriptionObject is false.

__SubscriptionConfig.doc: Configuration for recurring subscriptions on a DataObject. Provider-binding via `providerName`. The framework wires up plan creation (where applicable), customer attachment, renewal webhooks, and cancellation flows. Requires the bound PaymentProvider to support subscriptions (capabilities.supportsSubscriptions=true). On a TOKENIZED provider (subscriptionSemantics 'tokenized', e.g. Adyen) the subscription opt-in also implies the object's `sys_<X>Payment` ticket table and the payment intent machine: the framework's recharge scheduler records every cycle's charge there (`orderId` = the subscription row id, `metadata.recharge: true`) and the provider webhook reconciles it, whether or not the object also opts into `checkout`. No checkout API (start / refresh / callback routes, ticket CRUD APIs) is added by the subscription opt-in alone; hosted and checkout-driven providers run their own cycle and get no extra table. 3-D SECURE ON STRIPE: a subscription whose FIRST payment needs the buyer (authentication, or a declined card) is created `incomplete`; the subscribe answer then carries `nextAction` (`requiresAction`, `clientSecret`, `paymentStatus`, `hostedInvoiceUrl`) for the frontend to finish with Stripe.js, and the row reads `past_due` (never an entitled state) until Stripe's `invoice.paid` makes it `active`; unfinished, Stripe expires it after 23 hours (`expired`). A RENEWAL that needs authentication reaches `afterInvoicePaymentFailed` with `resource.requiresAction: true` and `resource.hostedInvoiceUrl`, the page where the buyer authenticates. Grant the plan on `active` (`afterInvoicePaid` / `afterSubscriptionRenewed`), never on `afterSubscriptionCreated` alone. HOSTED SUBSCRIPTION FORM ON IYZICO: iyzico takes the card only on its hosted subscription Checkout Form, so a subscribe (the raw route or a SubscriptionAction `subscribe`) answers a row `pending_provider` under the `providerSubscriptionId` `pending:checkout:<token>`, plus `checkoutForm` (`token`, `checkoutFormContent`, `paymentPageUrl`, `tokenExpireTime`) for the frontend to show. iyzico POSTs the token to the service's own `/v1/payments/subscription-checkout-return/<provider>` (derived from SERVICE_URL), which reads the result from iyzico, never from the body: ACTIVE makes the row `active` and fires `afterSubscriptionCreated` once; another reported status (`past_due`, `trialing`) is stored without that hook; a refusal is `provider_failed`. The buyer's email, name and surname come from `metadata.buyer` or the caller's session (400 SUBSCRIPTION_BUYER_EMAIL_REQUIRED without an email). A `pending_provider` row grants nothing. A cancel first reads the form from iyzico: a form that produced no subscription closes locally, a confirmed subscription is canceled at iyzico under its real reference, and a failed read or provider cancel leaves the row available for retry.

SubscriptionConfig.__providerName.doc: Name of the configured PaymentProvider that handles subscriptions for this object. Must match an entry in projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name and the bound provider must have capabilities.supportsSubscriptions=true.
SubscriptionConfig.__planProperty.doc: Property on this object that holds the SubscriptionPlan reference — the plan `code`, the `providerPlanId`, or the plan row id. A SubscriptionAction with stage=subscribe falls back to this property when the action itself declares no planProperty; on that path, before the provider is called the action resolves the value against sys_<X>SubscriptionPlan, scoped to the bound provider (the same code can map to a different provider plan id on each provider), and sends the matched row `providerPlanId` to the provider. A reference that matches no row fails loudly instead of travelling to the provider raw. The value is passed through verbatim only when the object declares no subscription block at all, because no sys_<X>SubscriptionPlan catalog is generated in that case. GENERATOR SUPPORT for that action-level fallback is NOT universal: nodejs, python and dotnet implement it, while java, rust, golang and php do not, and on those four the subscribe stage fails at runtime (java with a 500 naming the missing planProperty, rust with 400 SUBSCRIPTION_PLAN_REQUIRED before reaching the provider). Design-time validation permits the design and warns with SUBSCRIPTION_ACTION_PLAN_PROPERTY_INHERITED, so set planProperty on the action itself when one of those four is a generation target.
SubscriptionConfig.__customerProperty.doc: Property on this object that holds the customer / owner reference. Used to attach the subscription to the provider-side customer record.
SubscriptionConfig.__trialDaysProperty.doc: Optional property holding the trial period length in days. When set, the subscription starts in `trialing` state and transitions to `active` after the trial.
SubscriptionConfig.__cancelAtPeriodEndProperty.doc: Optional property holding a boolean that, when true on subscription create or update, schedules cancellation at the end of the current period rather than immediately.
SubscriptionConfig.__statusProperty.doc: Optional property on this object that mirrors the subscription status (`trialing | active | past_due | paused | canceled | expired`). When set, the framework writes the new status onto THIS object's row (the row `sys_<X>Subscription.orderId` names) whenever the subscription status changes: when the subscribe route opens the subscription, as provider webhook events advance the subscription state machine and, on a tokenized provider (e.g. Adyen), at the recharge scheduler's own status writes (renewed, dunned, parked, dunning exhausted; never on a replay or a lost race). The write lands after the sys_<X>Subscription write and before the lifecycle hooks; a failed mirror write is logged as `SubscriptionStatusMirrorFailed` and never fails the event. It is a read model: sys_<X>Subscription.statusLiteral stays authoritative, and the framework-owned journal states `pending_provider` / `provider_failed` are never mirrored.
