An Enum property receives only the statuses among its options (an Enum naming none of them is not mirrored); bind a String or an Enum carrying these literals.
SubscriptionConfig.__lifecycleHooks.doc: Designer-authored MScript handlers fired on subscription lifecycle events (afterSubscriptionRenewed, afterSubscriptionCanceled, afterSubscriptionPastDue, etc.).
SubscriptionConfig.__maxDunningAttempts.doc: Tokenized providers only (subscriptionSemantics 'tokenized', e.g. Adyen), where the framework's recharge scheduler owns the billing cycle: the maximum number of refused recharges the dunning loop retries before the subscription is closed out. A refused charge moves the row to `past_due`, counts one attempt on `sys_<X>Subscription.dunningAttempts` and schedules a retry one day later; when the count reaches this cap the row goes to the terminal state named by `dunningExhaustedState` and the scheduler stops selecting it. A successful recharge resets the count. Transport errors (the provider could not be reached) do not count. Hosted and checkout-driven providers run their own dunning and ignore this field. Minimum 1.
SubscriptionConfig.__dunningExhaustedState.doc: Tokenized providers only: what the recharge scheduler does with a subscription whose refused recharges reached `maxDunningAttempts`. `cancel` (default) ends it: statusLiteral `canceled`, `canceledAt` stamped, a still-trialing row loses its trial entitlement (`trialEnd` clamped to now), and the recharge anchor is cleared. `pastDue` parks it: statusLiteral `past_due` with the recharge anchor cleared, so it is never charged again until an operator or a business API restores a payment method and re-stamps `nextRechargeAt`. Either way the exhausted row is logged once as `SubscriptionDunningExhausted`.
SubscriptionConfig.__storePaymentMethod.doc: An EXPLICIT opt-in (default false) to store the buyer's payment method while paying: Adyen enrols it for recharges, Stripe attaches it, iyzico's hosted form lets the buyer save it. On a tokenized provider (subscriptionSemantics 'tokenized', e.g. Adyen), where the framework's recharge scheduler charges a STORED method merchant-initiated, it makes the customer-initiated payment which opens the subscription (a PaymentAction start / simple stage on the order object that carries this subscription block) enrol the customer's payment method at the provider (`storeMethod: true`, sent by the Adyen adapter as `storePaymentMethod: true`), so the recharge has a method to reference (`ContAuth`). Stripe (save the card while paying) sends it as `setup_future_usage: 'off_session'`: Stripe attaches the confirmed card to the buyer's Stripe customer and reports `payment_method.attached`, which role (2) below persists into `sys_paymentMethod`; a caller can never send `setup_future_usage` itself (refused as a provider option, PAYMENT_PROVIDER_OPTION_NOT_ALLOWED). The card is enrolled for off-session use; by default the framework makes no off-session Stripe charge of its own: the stored card serves the buyer's later payments with `paymentMethodId` (buyer present, 3-D Secure possible) and Stripe's own subscription renewals. Only a Stripe entry that opts in (savedCardOffSession 'verified' beside savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce') charges a stored card already 3-D Secure verified off-session (merchant-initiated, no liability shift, buyer-absent use only), and only from a PaymentAction start / simple stage declared buyerAbsent. The stored-credential contract sent with the enrolment (`recurringModel`) is DERIVED from this configuration, never from the request body: `subscription` when `planProperty` binds the object to a plan with a billing interval (a fixed schedule), `unscheduled` (card on file) when it does not. Storing a card changes the cardholder-facing behaviour, so it is never a silent default: with the opt-in off the provider call carries no store flag even when the request body asks for one, any `recurringModel` / `initiatedBy` in the body is ignored, and `validate` warns (SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_PAYMENT_METHOD_OFF) that recharges on this tokenized provider will have no stored method. The field has TWO roles and only the first is provider-specific: (1) ADAPTER ENROLMENT, where the adapter supports sending a store flag with the opening payment (Adyen and Stripe today; for iyzico see below) - other hosted and checkout-driven providers store methods through their own checkout, so they send nothing extra; (2) the RETENTION GATE of the webhook method mirror, which applies to EVERY provider including the hosted and checkout-driven ones: a provider-reported stored method (`method.attached` / `method.updated`) is written into `sys_paymentMethod` only when a payment object of the service carries this opt-in, otherwise the event is acknowledged, logged as `PaymentMethodRetentionSkipped` and not retained (`method.detached` always syncs, and the cardholder's own `POST /v1/payment-methods/add` persists regardless). A checkout-only order object opts in with its own switch, CheckoutConfig.storePaymentMethod; either switch counts, read as one design-time rule. The mirror files the method for the user who OWNS the provider customer's payment-customer mapping, through the identity owner's machine-only `attachPaymentMethodByCustomerIdForMachine` (the webhook names no user; the api reads it from the mapping, idempotent per customer and method). iyzico (save the card while paying on the hosted Checkout Form): on an iyzico-bound order object carrying this opt-in (or CheckoutConfig.storePaymentMethod), the mounted start route and a PaymentAction start / simple stage open the hosted form with the buyer's own card storage key (`sys_paymentCustomer.cardStorageKey`, read server-side from the buyer's mapping; none for a buyer who has no key yet), so iyzico lists the buyer's saved cards and offers to save the new one. A card the buyer saves on the form is taken when the payment settles (the browser return or iyzico's Checkout Form webhook, once): a card filed under another key than the buyer's is refused, a first-time buyer's minted key is stored once through the machine-only `setPaymentCustomerCardStorageKeyForMachine` (a lost race deletes the card filed under the minted key), and the card is filed in the ticket owner's `sys_paymentMethod` right away through the machine-only `attachPaymentMethodByCustomerIdForMachine` (the owner is read from the buyer's payment-customer mapping, never from the request). Without either switch the iyzico form is opened without a key and nothing it saves is recorded.
SubscriptionConfig.__checkRoles.doc: Roles required on the INJECTED subscription lifecycle routes of this object - POST /v1/subscribe<x>/:orderId, DELETE /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId and PATCH /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId. Same meaning as BusinessApi authOptions.checkRoles: the list RESTRICTS (a caller holding none of these roles is refused 403 PAYMENT_ROLE_REQUIRED) and it is combined with OR. It is NOT absoluteRoles, and the two are never normalised into each other: the surface keeps its own separate BYPASS list (admin / superAdmin, PAYMENT_ABSOLUTE_ROLES), and a verified inter-service (M2M) caller that carries no user identity is admitted because the lifecycle routes are mounted allowM2M and a machine caller holds no role (an M2M caller that names a user - a forwarded user token - is that user and faces the list and the ownership gate). Leave empty to let routeAccess decide: `inherit` (the default) derives the gate from this object's authored apis, `open` emits none. Setting this is the way to gate the injected routes differently from the authored ones - for example when the authored billing apis are tenantOwner-only but a tenantAdmin must also be able to cancel. It is ONE list for the three routes; subscribeRoles, changeRoles and cancelRoles give a single route its own list, so a buyer may subscribe without being able to re-price or cancel.
SubscriptionConfig.__routeAccess.doc: What to do when checkRoles is empty: `inherit` (the default) derives the injected routes' role gate from this object's authored apis, `open` emits no role gate at all. See SubscriptionRouteAccess for the exact derivation rule and why it can never be stricter than the object's own authored surface. A project whose subscribe route is genuinely buyer-facing declares `open` here, which is also the one-key way to restore the earlier ungated render for an existing project.
SubscriptionConfig.__subscribeRoles.doc: Roles required on the injected subscribe route of this object, POST /v1/subscribe<x>/:orderId, and on that route only. Same meaning as checkRoles (it RESTRICTS, 403 PAYMENT_ROLE_REQUIRED, the same bypass and M2M rules). Non-empty: this list gates the subscribe route, whatever checkRoles and routeAccess say. Empty or unset: the route keeps the shared gate (checkRoles, else routeAccess). Use it to let a buyer subscribe without letting the same role re-price or cancel: put the buyer role here and keep checkRoles (or changeRoles / cancelRoles) for the operator roles. Declaring any of subscribeRoles / changeRoles / cancelRoles also makes nonOperatorReprice and nonOperatorImmediateCancel default to refusing.
SubscriptionConfig.__changeRoles.doc: Roles required on the injected CHANGE routes of this object: the re-price route `PATCH /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId` and, on a tokenized iyzico subscription object, the buyer's card change `POST /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId/payment-method` and its read `GET` on the same path (those two have no list of their own). Same meaning as checkRoles. Non-empty: this list gates these routes, whatever checkRoles and routeAccess say. Empty or unset: they keep the shared gate. A plan change on the PATCH (a providerPlanId in the body) is decided by nonOperatorReprice on top of this list. To let a buyer change the card, put the buyer role here and leave nonOperatorReprice unset: plan changes stay operator-only, and the buyer may also toggle cancelAtPeriodEnd on the PATCH. The card change serves only the subscription's own buyer (anyone else gets 404). See docs-site/integrations/payment/iyzico-field-notes.md (Who may subscribe, re-price and cancel).
SubscriptionConfig.__cancelRoles.doc: Roles required on the injected cancel route of this object, DELETE /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId, and on that route only. Same meaning as checkRoles. Non-empty: this list gates the DELETE route, whatever checkRoles and routeAccess say. Empty or unset: the route keeps the shared gate. An immediate cancel on that route (`?when=immediately`) is decided by nonOperatorImmediateCancel on top of this list.
SubscriptionConfig.__nonOperatorReprice.doc: May a caller who passes the PATCH /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId gate but is NOT a platform payment operator change the plan (send a providerPlanId)? `true` admits it. `false` refuses it with 403 SUBSCRIPTION_OPERATOR_REQUIRED before the handler runs; the same caller may still change the other fields (cancelAtPeriodEnd). Unset: refused when this block declares subscribeRoles, changeRoles or cancelRoles, and admitted otherwise (the earlier behaviour). A platform payment operator is a session holding superAdmin, admin or saasAdmin (superAdmin or saasAdmin on a multi-tenant project; the paymentOperator permission does not count), or a verified service caller that names no user. A plan change by a buyer otherwise moves the price without the project's own plan-change api, its rules and its events: keep it for operators unless the product means buyers to switch plans on this route.
SubscriptionConfig.__nonOperatorImmediateCancel.doc: May a caller who passes the DELETE /v1/<x>subscription/:subscriptionId gate but is NOT a platform payment operator cancel immediately (`?when=immediately`)? `true` admits it. `false` refuses it with 403 SUBSCRIPTION_OPERATOR_REQUIRED before the handler runs; the same caller may still cancel at period end (no `when`, or `when=period_end`). Unset: refused when this block declares subscribeRoles, changeRoles or cancelRoles, and admitted otherwise (the earlier behaviour). Platform payment operator: as for nonOperatorReprice. Provider caveat: PayPal and iyzico hosted subscriptions have no period-end cancel, so every DELETE on them cancels immediately; on those providers this setting cannot hold a buyer to a period-end cancel. Use cancelRoles to keep the buyer off the route instead.
SubscriptionConfig.__publishLifecycleEvents.doc: Opt-in (default false; only a literal `true` on an ACTIVE subscription block counts) that makes the generated payment layer publish this object's normalized SUBSCRIPTION lifecycle events to Kafka (family `subscription`), one topic per event: `<projectCodename>-<service>-service-lcevent-subscription-<object lowercased>-<suffix>`, where the FIXED event list and its suffixes are `subscription.created` -> `created`, `subscription.renewed` -> `renewed`, `subscription.payment_failed` -> `payment-failed`, `subscription.past_due` -> `past-due`, `subscription.canceled` -> `canceled`, `subscription.expired` -> `expired`, `invoice.paid` -> `invoice-paid`, `invoice.payment_failed` -> `invoice-payment-failed`; on a nodejs service also `subscription.paused` -> `paused` and `subscription.resumed` -> `resumed` (state events announced only when the event MOVED the row into `paused` / `active`, so a second report of a pause the row already carries announces nothing; java and dotnet publish the fixed list only). Published by the subscription machine (provider webhooks) AFTER the sys_<Object>Subscription write and AFTER the designer lifecycle hooks, and - for a tokenized provider - by the framework's recharge scheduler at its own status writes (renewed when a charged cycle is stamped, never on a replay; past_due when a row is parked for a missing payment method; payment_failed for every refused recharge attempt; canceled or past_due when dunning is exhausted, per dunningExhaustedState), and on nodejs by a SubscriptionAction: every status move its cancel or refresh writes runs the subscription machine and publishes the event the subscription FSM makes that move with (canceled, expired, past_due, paused, resumed, renewed, created), and its subscribe of a framework-owned (tokenized) subscription publishes `subscription.created` once per journal row. A STATE event (renewed, past_due, canceled, expired, paused, resumed) publishes only when the row ENDS in the state it names; a FACT event (created, payment_failed, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed) publishes whenever it is processed. `data` = { eventType, family, object, providerName, providerEventId, occurredAt, orderId, previousStatus, status, dedupeKey, failureReason (payment_failed / invoice.payment_failed only), subscription (an ALLOWLISTED projection of the sys_<Object>Subscription row: id, orderId, customerId, providerName, providerSubscriptionId, planId, statusLiteral, failureReason, currentPeriodStart, currentPeriodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, trialEnd, canceledAt, nextRechargeAt, dunningAttempts, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt, the tenant column), invoice (invoice.* events: providerInvoiceId, subscriptionId, amount, currency, statusLiteral, periodStart, periodEnd, paidAt), record (this object's own row read by `orderId`, in the shape and unit its db-change event publishes) }; never the raw provider payload or the row's metadata. Delivery is AT LEAST ONCE through the service's lifecycle outbox: each event is written to `sys_lifecycle_outbox` (one row per `data.dedupeKey`, the built envelope plus its retry state) before it is sent, the send is not awaited on the payment path, and a send the broker refuses (logged `PaymentLifecycleEventPublishFailed`) is re-sent by the outbox sweeper with the same envelope id and dedupeKey (every PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_OUTBOX_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, default 30 s; backoff up to one hour; parked `dead` after 50 refusals). A redelivery can repeat an event, and a process that dies between the status write and the outbox write loses that one event: dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`, and reconcile money from the rows, not from the stream. Envelope: `type` = the normalized event type; `actor.tenantId` = the row's tenant in a multi-tenant project. Off (the default) the generated code is byte-identical to a build without the field; the topics are listed by the kafka topic census and pre-created only while it is on.

__Marketplace.doc: Provider-neutral marketplace activation for a DataObject. When enabled, the framework auto-generates sys_<X>ConnectedAccount and sys_<X>Payout records and wires the connected-account KYC, transfer, and payout APIs through the bound provider. Requires the bound PaymentProvider to have capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true. In a multi-tenant project, the object carrying this marketplace block must declare objectSettings.authorization.objectDataIsInTenantLevel: true. Blueprint validation refuses non-tenant sellers with MARKETPLACE_SELLER_NOT_TENANT_LEVEL before code generation or PSP account creation; hosted onboarding, manual binding and sellerOnboarding provisioning share this rule. The connected-account ledger and charge lookup require the tenant persisted on the seller row. Single-tenant shapes are unchanged.

Marketplace.__objectIsMarketplaceObject.doc: Enables marketplace flows for this object. When true, the framework treats this object as a marketplace transaction with a connected sub-merchant account.
Marketplace.__configuration.doc: The MarketplaceConfig binding seller-account / amount / fee properties to the provider's marketplace surface. Leave null if objectIsMarketplaceObject is false.

__MarketplaceConfig.doc: Configuration for marketplace payouts on a DataObject. Provider-binding via `providerName`. Requires the bound provider to have capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true. In a multi-tenant project the seller-bearing object must be tenant-level (objectSettings.authorization.objectDataIsInTenantLevel: true); non-tenant sellers are refused at blueprint validation with MARKETPLACE_SELLER_NOT_TENANT_LEVEL before any PSP create call, whether onboarding is hosted or manual. Maps the object's seller-account / amount / fee properties onto the provider's marketplace primitives (Stripe Connect transfers, PayPal Hyperwallet, iyzico sub-merchant, Adyen MarketPay, Mangopay wallets).

MarketplaceConfig.__providerName.doc: Name of the configured PaymentProvider that handles marketplace payouts. Must match an entry in projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name and the bound provider must have capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true.
MarketplaceConfig.__sellerAccountProperty.doc: Property on this object that holds the connected sub-merchant account id (provider-side). The framework resolves this to a sys_<X>ConnectedAccount record for KYC state tracking: this object's own table, or the table of the seller object named in sellerAccountObject when the sellers onboard on another object.
MarketplaceConfig.__amountProperty.doc: Property holding the total marketplace transaction amount. PLATFORM MONEY CONVENTION: MAJOR currency units as a decimal - adapters own the provider wire conversion; never bind a minor-unit (kurus/cents) column. The bound column MUST be declared `type: "Decimal"`, so the framework rounds it to its `decimalScale` at every write boundary and before the amount reaches the provider. A bound column declared with another NUMERIC type (Integer/Short/Double/Float) is migrated by validation to Decimal (scale from the binding's static currency, default 2) and reported as an auto-fix; a non-numeric one is the ERROR `MONEY_BINDING_NOT_DECIMAL`.
MarketplaceConfig.__applicationFeeProperty.doc: Optional property holding the platform fee amount retained by the marketplace operator. When set, the framework subtracts this from the amount before transferring to the seller.
MarketplaceConfig.__currencyProperty.doc: Property holding the currency. Defaults to the parent Checkout block's currency when omitted.
MarketplaceConfig.__transferGroupProperty.doc: Optional property holding a transfer group identifier — used by some providers (e.g. Stripe) to group related transfers for reporting.
MarketplaceConfig.__settlementMode.doc: How the SELLER'S SHARE of a marketplace sale is settled (pairs with the billing-model choice - reseller pairs with platformSettled). `providerSplit` (and null, the legacy default - emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this knob): the PSP owns the money split - split-at-charge when this object is also a checkout object with sellerAccountProperty declared, PSP payouts via PayoutManager/payout-scheduler, optionally invoice-gated by payoutGate. `platformSettled` (the reseller/al-sat money path): the charge is PLAIN - the FULL amount enters the platform's account (a split there is an invoice/cash mismatch and a potential legal defect), the framework accrues seller earnings per capture on the sys_<X>EarningsEntry ledger (gross stays with the platform; the fee is ledgered as the platform's share, the remainder as the seller's earnings; refunds claw back), and settlement leaves as PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS (sys_<X>SettlementInstruction: draft -> approved -> instructed -> confirmed | failed) with an operator-gated export/API surface - see docs/ADR-platform-settlement-instructions.md. In platformSettled mode sellerAccountProperty is REQUIRED (it is the earnings ATTRIBUTION binding read off the persisted order row - not a split declaration) and an ACTIVE payoutGate is REFUSED (it gates PSP payouts, which do not exist on this path; invoice-gating lives on the instruction approve step instead - settlementGate). settlementGroupProperty / settlementEligibleAfterProperty scope the instructions per source (e.g. one per seller and event, only after the event ended).
MarketplaceConfig.__payoutGate.doc: Optional invoice-gate for payouts (the Turkish marketplace mutabakat flow). When `requiresIncomingInvoice` is true, a payout to a connected seller is RELEASED only after a matching INBOUND fiscal invoice from that seller has arrived (seller tax id = the connected account's tax id binding, amount within `matchTolerance`, reference/period correlation via transferGroup); until then the payout row sits in status `held` with a typed reason. Declarative like issuePolicy/submitPolicy: the designer declares the gate here and the framework wires PayoutManager + payout-scheduler + the fiscal inbound ingestion — no imperative glue. Leave null for ungated payouts (the default; emitted code is byte-identical to a project without this block). Requires a fiscalization context in the same service: inbound invoices arrive through a FiscalProvider whose capabilities include supportsInboundDocuments, landing as direction='inbound' rows on a fiscalized object's sys_<X>FiscalDocument ledger.
MarketplaceConfig.__lifecycleHooks.doc: Designer-authored MScript handlers fired on marketplace lifecycle events (afterPayoutPaid, afterPayoutFailed, afterPayoutHeld, afterKycUpdated, etc.).
MarketplaceConfig.__allowedSellerTypes.doc: PROJECT POLICY (docs/ADR-billing-model-reseller-intermediary.md §4): the seller legal forms this platform admits to sub-merchant onboarding, written in the bound provider brand's OWN sub-merchant type vocabulary (the onboarding matrix — iyzico: PERSONAL, PRIVATE_COMPANY, LIMITED_OR_JOINT_STOCK_COMPANY (input alias LIMITED_COMPANY); stripe: individual, company). Enforced at BOTH ends: design time validates every listed token against the bound brand's known types (MARKETPLACE_UNKNOWN_SELLER_TYPE, ERROR; brands the matrix does not cover are not judged), and the emitted onboarding route (POST /v1/payments/connected-accounts) refuses a request whose seller type is not in this list — or is missing while a policy is declared — with a typed 422 SELLER_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED naming the policy, before any provider call. Why a platform declares one: repeated high-volume sales by plain individuals can make the platform co-liable in TR (fiscal-advisor warning) — e.g. Masa's policy is sole-proprietorship minimum. Null/absent/empty = no policy (legacy behavior): the route is emitted byte-identically and every brand-known type is admitted.
MarketplaceConfig.__settlementRelease.doc: Optional settlement-RELEASE timing for a providerSplit marketplace object: WHEN the seller's split share of each captured sale is released to the seller. Today a split share is released only when a payout is created; with this block the framework books ONE payout row per captured sale at capture time (payment.captured), with the provider's settlement item ids of that sale persisted on it (iyzico: the split items' paymentTransactionIds, under the provider-neutral metadata.providerItemIds), and releases it on the declared condition: `onCapture` releases at once (the next scheduler tick sends it), `onDate` holds it until now >= the sale row's `releaseAtProperty` (e.g. the experience end date), `onStatus` holds it until the sale row's `statusProperty` reads one of `releaseOnStatus`, `manual` holds it until a payout is created for that sale (POST /v1/payments/payouts or a PayoutAction naming the sale by metadata.orderId / sourceOrderProperty). A held row is a payout-gate hold (statusLiteral `held`, metadata.payoutGate.holdReason awaiting_release_date / awaiting_release_status / awaiting_manual_release) re-checked on every payout-scheduler tick and released exactly once through the scheduler's claim / fence path; it composes with payoutGate (both must pass). The SALE is re-checked before every release (per tick and under the scheduler claim), from the payment layer's own ticket and dispute records: a fully refunded or canceled sale or a lost dispute cancels the row (statusLiteral failed, metadata.settlementRelease.canceledReason sale_refunded / sale_canceled / dispute_lost, no provider call, afterPayoutFailed fires); an open dispute holds it (holdReason dispute_open) until the dispute is won; a partially refunded sale holds it (holdReason sale_partially_refunded) until an operator creates a payout for the sale. REQUIREMENTS (validation ERRORS): settlementMode providerSplit (platformSettled has no PSP payouts), a framework-driven payoutCadence on the bound provider (`on_demand` or `scheduled`; the stripe / iyzico / adyen default `provider_driven` books no payout - set paymentProviders[].payoutCadence.mode), `releaseAtProperty` for onDate and `statusProperty` + `releaseOnStatus` for onStatus, each naming a property of THIS object; and a Node.js, .NET or Java service - the other backend languages do not emit the release yet and refuse the block (SETTLEMENT_RELEASE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED). PROVIDER PREREQUISITE (iyzico): the merchant account must NOT auto-approve split items - ask iyzico to switch the account's automatic item approval off; with auto-approval on, iyzico releases the seller share itself and no hold can apply. Replaces the authored-cron workaround (on_demand cadence + a cron that creates a payout per ended sale). Null / absent = today's behavior; emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this block.
MarketplaceConfig.__sellerAccountObject.doc: Optional: the name of ANOTHER data object of this same service that carries its own marketplace block and onboards the sellers (its sellerOnboarding, its sys_<X>ConnectedAccount table). Use it on an ORDER object (checkout + marketplace with sellerAccountProperty) whose seller lives on a separate seller/profile object - the standard shape of one seller object and many order objects. When set, every seller resolution of THIS object reads the named object's connected-account table instead of its own: the split-at-charge (subMerchantKey of the seller the order row names), payout destinations (PayoutManager), the payoutGate seller lookup, the settlementRelease booking, the platformSettled earnings ledger and the settlement instructions, with the same provider and tenant scoping (a seller id of another tenant matches nothing). The order row's sellerAccountProperty then holds the seller's provider account id (iyzico subMerchantKey) or the local id of the seller's connected-account row, exactly as before. REQUIREMENTS (validation ERRORS): the name resolves to a data object of this service other than this one (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_SELF); that object carries a marketplace block (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_NOT_MARKETPLACE) bound to the same providerName and the same settlementMode (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_PROVIDER_MISMATCH, SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_SETTLEMENT_MODE_MISMATCH); both objects sit on the same tenant level (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_TENANT_MISMATCH); this block does not also declare sellerOnboarding, which would provision a sub-merchant per ORDER row (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_WITH_ONBOARDING); and a Node.js service - the other backend languages refuse the key until they emit it (SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED). An order object with sellerAccountProperty and no own onboarding, in a service where another object onboards sellers on the same provider, gets the WARNING SELLER_ACCOUNT_OBJECT_SUGGESTED: without this key its charge looks the seller up in its own, empty table and is refused SELLER_ACCOUNT_UNRESOLVED. Null / absent = the object resolves sellers in its own table; emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this key.
MarketplaceConfig.__sellerOnboarding.doc: Optional role-to-property map that lets the FRAMEWORK PROVISION the seller's connected sub-merchant account (level 2) instead of a designer hand-pasting a provider-side key into `sellerAccountProperty`. `sellerAccountProperty` says where the minted account id LIVES; this block says where the facts it is minted FROM come from, named by provider-neutral ROLE and resolved as properties of the SAME data object that carries this marketplace block. Collection is the PRODUCT's job - a seller signup form, an admin screen or an import writes those properties through ordinary CRUD - and the requirements are the FRAMEWORK's: design time checks, for every legal form listed in `allowedSellerTypes`, that the roles that form needs are mapped, and NAMES the missing ones (MARKETPLACE_ONBOARDING_ROLE_UNMAPPED, ERROR). Leave it null for a HOSTED-onboarding provider (Stripe Connect onboarding, PayPal partner referrals - the provider collects the seller's identity on its own pages and the platform never holds these facts) and for a project that is not onboarding sellers yet; an absent block raises no role-map finding and changes no emitted code. Exception: sellers can only start and resume their OWN hosted onboarding (the nodejs, java and dotnet seller routes POST|GET /v1/payments/seller-onboarding/:sellerId) on an object that declares this block, an owner column and sellerAccountProperty, so a hosted provider that wants seller self-service binds at least one role here (emailProperty is enough). The multi-tenant seller must still be tenant-level (objectSettings.authorization.objectDataIsInTenantLevel: true), including hosted onboarding and manual account binding; a non-tenant seller is refused at blueprint validation before PSP account creation. Note that `ibanProperty` gates SETTLEMENT rather than registration, so it is never demanded by the coverage check.
MarketplaceConfig.__settlementGroupProperty.doc: Optional, settlementMode platformSettled only: a property of THIS (order) object whose value scopes the settlement instructions. Without it one instruction is drafted per (seller, currency); with it one per (seller, currency, value) - e.g. `eventId` on a ticket order, so each event of an organizer is paid by its own instruction. The value is read at generate time off the persisted order row each earnings entry names (sale accruals and refund clawbacks alike) and recorded on the instruction as metadata.settlementGroup; an order row with an empty value settles in the seller's ungrouped instruction. Validation ERRORS: an unknown property name, a non-platformSettled block (the key would be inert), and a service language other than Node.js, Java or .NET (SETTLEMENT_GROUPING_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED). Null / absent = one instruction per seller; emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this key.
MarketplaceConfig.__settlementEligibleAfterProperty.doc: Optional, settlementMode platformSettled only: a date property of THIS (order) object that gates WHEN a sale's earnings may be settled - an earnings entry is drafted into an instruction only once the current time has passed the value on its order row (e.g. the event's end date, so an organizer is paid per event only after the event). Read at generate time off the persisted order row, so a postponed event postpones its settlement. An order row with an empty or unparseable value is NOT eligible: its earnings stay accrued and the generate run logs SettlementEarningsWithoutEligibilityDate naming the order. Composes with the generate call's periodEnd (both must hold). Validation ERRORS: an unknown property name, a non-platformSettled block, and a service language other than Node.js, Java or .NET (SETTLEMENT_GROUPING_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED); a property that is not a Date / DateTime type is a WARNING. Null / absent = every accrued entry is eligible; emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this key.
MarketplaceConfig.__settlementGate.doc: Optional invoice gate on the APPROVE step of platformSettled settlement instructions (the reseller mutabakat step: the platform pays the seller only against the seller's incoming invoice). When `requiresIncomingInvoice` is true, POST /v1/payments/settlement/instructions/:id/approve is refused (409 INSTRUCTION_INVOICE_GATE_HELD, the typed hold reason on the instruction's metadata.settlementGate) until a matching INBOUND fiscal invoice from that seller is on the service's fiscal ledgers (the same matching rule as payoutGate: issuer tax id = the seller's connected-account tax id, currency, |total - instruction amount| within matchTolerance; when settlementGroupProperty is declared the group value is the reference an invoice note or document number may carry). A match stamps the instruction's invoiceRef with the invoice's document number and marks the invoice consumed by this instruction (one invoice settles one instruction or payout). Requires settlementMode platformSettled and a Node.js, Java or .NET service (validation ERRORS) and an inbound fiscal context in the same service (the payoutGate context WARNINGS apply). Null / absent = approve is the operator's act alone and invoiceRef is operator-filled; emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this block.

__SellerOnboardingConfig.doc: Role-to-property map that lets the FRAMEWORK PROVISION a seller's connected sub-merchant account (level 2), instead of a designer hand-pasting a provider-side key into `sellerAccountProperty`. `sellerAccountProperty` says where the minted account id LIVES; this block says where the facts it is minted FROM come from. Every entry is a PropRefer naming a property OF THE OWNING DATA OBJECT - the same object `sellerAccountProperty` resolves against, exactly like FiscalPartyConfig's party bindings - so the SELLER-BEARING object is the object that carries the marketplace block; a separate seller/profile object carries its OWN marketplace block rather than being reached through a relation (PropRefer has no cross-object resolution, and inventing one here would make the money bindings and the identity bindings resolve against different rows), and the order objects that charge to it name it in their own marketplace block's sellerAccountObject instead of declaring this block. The blueprint speaks ROLES; the payment adapters speak provider WIRE FIELDS (iyzico subMerchantType / legalCompanyTitle / gsmNumber, Stripe business_type, ...) and translate at the edge - no provider-specific field name may ever appear in this block. WHEN THE DATA IS COLLECTED: the PRODUCT owns the form and the FRAMEWORK owns the requirements. A seller signup screen, an admin back-office edit or an import writes these properties through the object's ordinary CRUD, long before any provisioning call; provisioning reads them off the persisted row. WHEN NOT TO DECLARE THIS BLOCK AT ALL: a HOSTED-onboarding provider (kycOnboarding mode hosted-url / partner-referrals - Stripe Connect onboarding, PayPal partner referrals) collects the seller's legal identity on ITS OWN pages, so the platform never holds these facts and the block stays null; declare it for the API-onboarding brands (iyzico sub-merchant, Mangopay document-api) whose account is minted from a payload the platform assembles. Absent/null = no provisioning declaration: no finding is raised and emitted code is byte-identical to a blueprint without this block.

SellerOnboardingConfig.__legalNameProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's LEGAL name - the registered company title for a company seller, the trading name for a sole proprietor. Adapters map it onto their own slots (iyzico: `name` plus `legalCompanyTitle`; Stripe: the company / individual naming fields). The API-onboarding brands require a name for every seller type.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__taxIdProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's CORPORATE tax number (Turkey: VKN). This is the COMPANY-tier identifier; an individual or sole proprietor is identified by `identityNumberProperty` instead, so a platform whose allowedSellerTypes admits both tiers binds BOTH roles.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__taxOfficeProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the tax office (Turkey: vergi dairesi) the seller's tax number is registered with. A company-tier fact: brands that mint an account from a payload require it alongside the tax id.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__addressProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's address as a single text value. iyzico requires it for EVERY sub-merchant type - proven by the MasaV6 sandbox probe, not inferred from the vendor docs.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__ibanProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's settlement IBAN. This role gates SETTLEMENT, NOT REGISTRATION: an account is created without it, but a SETTLEABLE sub-merchant needs it - approving a settlement for an IBAN-less sub-merchant is refused by the vendor (iyzico error 5068) and surfaces as a typed 422 naming this field (proven live 2026-09-08). Bind it whenever the platform pays sellers out; leave it null only for a marketplace that never settles through the PSP. Because it is not a registration requirement, an unmapped iban is never reported by the allowedSellerTypes coverage check.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__identityNumberProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's NATIONAL identity number (Turkey: TCKN). The INDIVIDUAL-tier identifier: required for a PERSONAL seller, and also for the sole-proprietorship tier (iyzico PRIVATE_COMPANY) whose owner is the taxable person.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__contactNameProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the contact person's given name. Required for the individual seller tier - the API-onboarding brands refuse a PERSONAL account without both contact name and surname.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__contactSurnameProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the contact person's family name. The twin of `contactNameProperty`; bind both or neither.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__sellerTypeProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's LEGAL FORM, written in the bound brand's own sub-merchant vocabulary - the SAME vocabulary `allowedSellerTypes` uses (iyzico: PERSONAL / PRIVATE_COMPANY / LIMITED_OR_JOINT_STOCK_COMPANY, input alias LIMITED_COMPANY; stripe: individual / company). It is the row-level fact the per-type mandatory-role matrix is selected BY, so a platform whose `allowedSellerTypes` admits MORE THAN ONE form MUST bind it - otherwise no row can say which form a given seller is, and design time reports MARKETPLACE_SELLER_TYPE_BINDING_UNMAPPED. A single-form policy may leave it null: the one admitted form is implied.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__emailProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's contact e-mail. The API-onboarding brands require it for every seller type, and it is the address the provider sends onboarding / KYC correspondence to.
SellerOnboardingConfig.__gsmProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the seller's mobile phone number in the vendor's expected format (iyzico wire field `gsmNumber`). Vendor-OPTIONAL at registration - bind it when the platform already collects it, not to satisfy a requirement.

__PayoutGateConfig.doc: Invoice-gated payout release (the TR marketplace MERCHANT model's mutabakat step). The platform invoices the end customer in its own name (outbound fiscalization); the SHOP invoices the PLATFORM for its receivable; the payout to the shop is conditional on that incoming invoice arriving and matching the computed amount. The generated payout gate consults this block before ANY release: PayoutManager.createPayout parks a gated payout as `held` instead of touching the provider, the payout-scheduler re-evaluates held rows each tick and fires released ones through the unchanged payout path, and the fiscal-inbound-cron supplies the inbound ledger the matching rule reads. The matching rule (fixed, declarative): the inbound invoice's issuer tax id must equal the connected account's tax id binding (the `taxId` column or `metadata.taxId` on sys_<X>ConnectedAccount); when the payout carries a transferGroup and an invoice references it (note or document number), that invoice is judged alone; currency must agree; |invoice total − payout amount| must be within `matchTolerance`. A payout held by the gate carries a typed reason (awaiting_inbound_invoice / seller_tax_id_unbound / amount_mismatch / currency_mismatch) on its row metadata and is visible on the payout list surfaces filtered by status=held.

PayoutGateConfig.__requiresIncomingInvoice.doc: The gate switch. True = a payout to a connected seller is released only after a matching inbound fiscal invoice from that seller arrives; absent/false = the block is inert and emitted payout code is byte-identical to an ungated project. The gate is consulted only where the owner's PayoutManager books the payout (on_demand / scheduled cadence): a PayoutAction on an owner whose provider resolves to a provider_driven cadence (the stripe / iyzico / adyen default when payoutCadence.mode is not set) pays synchronously and never consults it, so that design is a validation ERROR (PAYOUT_ACTION_PROVIDER_DRIVEN_RESERVE_OR_GATE) - set the provider's payoutCadence.mode to scheduled (or on_demand) or switch the gate off.
PayoutGateConfig.__matchTolerance.doc: Absolute amount tolerance (major units) for the invoice-total vs payout-amount comparison. Null takes the framework default (0.01 — the float-noise floor). Turkey rounds line VAT per line, so a small tolerance absorbs legitimate kurus-level drift; a larger one is a business decision, not a rounding aid.
PayoutGateConfig.__onMismatch.doc: What happens when an inbound invoice FROM THE RIGHT SELLER is present but mismatches (amount outside tolerance, or currency differs). `hold` (the default when null): the payout stays held with the typed mismatch reason until the operator resolves it. `notify`: the mismatch fires the afterPayoutHeld lifecycle hook and is logged, but the payout releases anyway — for platforms that reconcile out-of-band and refuse to block seller cash flow. A missing invoice ALWAYS holds regardless of this setting — that is what requiresIncomingInvoice means.

__SettlementGateConfig.doc: Invoice gate on the approve step of platformSettled settlement instructions (MarketplaceConfig.settlementGate). The platform approves a payment instruction to a seller only against the seller's matching incoming invoice. Same shape and matching rule as PayoutGateConfig, consulted on POST /v1/payments/settlement/instructions/:id/approve instead of on a PSP payout.

SettlementGateConfig.__requiresIncomingInvoice.doc: The gate switch. True = an instruction is approved only after a matching inbound fiscal invoice from its seller arrives; absent/false = the block is inert and the emitted instruction machine is byte-identical to an ungated project.
SettlementGateConfig.__matchTolerance.doc: Absolute amount tolerance (major units) for the invoice-total vs instruction-amount comparison. Null takes the framework default (0.01, the float-noise floor). Must be >= 0.
SettlementGateConfig.__onMismatch.doc: What happens when an inbound invoice FROM THE RIGHT SELLER is present but mismatches (amount outside tolerance, or currency differs). `hold` (the default when null): approve stays refused with the typed mismatch reason. `notify`: the mismatch is logged and recorded on the instruction's metadata.settlementGate, the approve succeeds without consuming the invoice and invoiceRef stays operator-filled. A missing invoice ALWAYS refuses the approve.

__SettlementReleaseConfig.doc: When a providerSplit marketplace sale's seller share is released (MarketplaceConfig.settlementRelease). The framework books one payout row per captured sale (payment.captured) carrying the provider's settlement item ids of that sale, holds it until the condition below holds, and the payout-scheduler releases it exactly once (its claim / fence path), re-checking the condition on every tick. Bindings are PropRefers naming properties of the SAME data object that carries the marketplace block (the sale row read back from the database, never a request body). Composes with payoutGate: a gated release still waits for the matching inbound invoice.

SettlementReleaseConfig.__mode.doc: Release trigger. `onCapture`: release as soon as the sale is captured (the next scheduler tick sends it). `onDate`: hold until now >= the sale row's releaseAtProperty (a Date); a row whose date is empty or unparseable stays held. `onStatus`: hold until the sale row's statusProperty reads one of releaseOnStatus. `manual`: hold until a payout is created for that sale (POST /v1/payments/payouts or a PayoutAction naming the sale by metadata.orderId / sourceOrderProperty), which releases the booked row instead of booking a second payout. Null is inert (no release machinery is emitted).
SettlementReleaseConfig.__releaseAtProperty.doc: (mode=onDate, REQUIRED) Property of this object holding the release date-time, e.g. the experience end. Read off the persisted sale row on every scheduler tick, so moving the date moves the release.
SettlementReleaseConfig.__statusProperty.doc: (mode=onStatus, REQUIRED) Property of this object holding the sale's business status (an Enum or String), e.g. the experience state.
SettlementReleaseConfig.__releaseOnStatus.doc: (mode=onStatus, REQUIRED) The status value(s) of statusProperty that release the share, compared exactly (case-sensitive) with the stored value.

__PayoutMismatchAction.doc.#: Gate behavior for a PRESENT-but-mismatching inbound invoice (PayoutGateConfig.onMismatch). A missing invoice always holds — this enum only governs mismatches.
__PayoutMismatchAction.doc.hold: Keep the payout held with the typed mismatch reason until an operator resolves it (the conservative default).
__PayoutMismatchAction.doc.notify: Fire the afterPayoutHeld hook and log the mismatch, but release the payout anyway (out-of-band reconciliation).

__SettlementMode.doc.#: Money path for a marketplace object's seller share (MarketplaceConfig.settlementMode). Null takes providerSplit - the legacy default, byte-identical emission.
__SettlementMode.doc.providerSplit: The PSP owns the split: split-at-charge, PSP payouts (PayoutManager / payout-scheduler), optional payoutGate. Today's behavior.
__SettlementMode.doc.platformSettled: The reseller (al-sat) path: plain charge - the full amount enters the platform's account; seller earnings accrue on the sys_<X>EarningsEntry ledger and settle via sys_<X>SettlementInstruction payment instructions (accounting export / ERP payment orders / bank orders). PSP payout creation for the object answers a typed 409.

__SettlementReleaseMode.doc.#: Release trigger of a providerSplit seller share (SettlementReleaseConfig.mode).
__SettlementReleaseMode.doc.onCapture: Release when the sale is captured (the next payout-scheduler tick sends the booked payout).
__SettlementReleaseMode.doc.onDate: Hold until now >= the sale row's releaseAtProperty.
__SettlementReleaseMode.doc.onStatus: Hold until the sale row's statusProperty reads one of releaseOnStatus.
__SettlementReleaseMode.doc.manual: Hold until a payout is created for that sale (POST /v1/payments/payouts or a PayoutAction naming the sale).

__Invoicing.doc: Provider-neutral accounts-receivable invoicing activation for a DataObject. Mark a DataObject as invoice-bearing by enabling `objectIsAnInvoiceObject` and (optionally) pointing `configuration.providerName` at a configured InvoiceProvider — when it is null, the framework-internal provider is the system of record (storage and lifecycle fully in the generated application; provider absence is not a special case but the `internal` adapter chosen implicitly). The framework generates the immutable invoice ledger (sys_<X>Invoice, sys_<X>InvoiceLine, sys_<X>CreditNote, sys_<X>InvoicePayment) and the issue/finalize/void/apply-payment surface around this object. The object itself stays the DOMAIN SURFACE: its schema is free, CRUD/UX/MScript live here, and it receives results through the PropRefer mirrors (statusProperty, ...) — it is never the financial record.

Invoicing.__objectIsAnInvoiceObject.doc: Enables accounts-receivable invoice logic for this object. When true, the object is treated as an invoice-bearing entity: the framework generates the sys_<X>Invoice ledger family and the invoice lifecycle surface bound to the configured (or internal) InvoiceProvider.
Invoicing.__configuration.doc: The InvoicingConfig describing how this object maps onto the invoice ledger (provider binding, customer/amount/currency bindings, line relation, issue policy, numbering, collection, lifecycle hooks). Leave it null if objectIsAnInvoiceObject is false.

__InvoicingConfig.doc: Configuration for provider-neutral accounts-receivable invoicing on a DataObject. Provider-binding is explicit via `providerName` (lookup into projectSettings.invoiceProvidersSettings.invoiceProviders[]); a null providerName binds the framework-internal provider. Property bindings (customer / amount / currency / due date / status) are PropRefer paths into the parent DataObject, same style as CheckoutConfig. The invoice flow is: draft (this object, freely editable) → finalize (line snapshot + number + FSM `open`) → payment allocation (sys_<X>InvoicePayment) → status mirrored back onto this object. Triggers are DECLARATIVE (`issuePolicy` / `issueCondition`) — the designer never writes imperative glue; `issuePolicy: manual` plus invoice actions is the imperative escape hatch.

InvoicingConfig.__providerName.doc: Name of the configured InvoiceProvider that is the SYSTEM OF RECORD for this object's invoices. Must match an entry in projectSettings.invoiceProvidersSettings.invoiceProviders[].name. When null, the framework-internal provider is used — storage and invoice lifecycle fully inside the generated application.
InvoicingConfig.__sourceObjectName.doc: Optional: the same-service DataObject this invoice is issued FROM (e.g. the order). When set, issuePolicy triggers read amount / lines / customer from the source object; when null, this object itself is both the domain surface and the source. Must be a local data object of the same service — a cross-service source is deliberately out of scope: there is no automatic cross-service invoice bridge. Unless `publishLifecycleEvents` is set, the invoice layer publishes no Kafka events of its own (every injected api has raiseApiEvent: false); the payment layer publishes only its payment-status events (`<object>-payment-updated` on every ticket status change, `<object>-payment-paymentdone` on a change into success). A separate billing service that must hear about an invoice fact either listens to this object's opt-in invoice lifecycle topics (`publishLifecycleEvents: true` - normalized events delivered at least once through the service's lifecycle outbox, see that field) or needs a designer-authored lifecycle hook that publishes it (a LIB function with a declared topic, or an internal-call api with a PublishEventAction); either way it listens with a standard EventSubscription. OWNERSHIP: every issued invoice row is stamped `ownerId` from the SOURCE object's owner column (the property flagged `sessionSettings.isOwnerField`). A source with no owner column stamps `ownerId: null` on every invoice, so no customer can read one (the document route answers 403 OWNER_UNRESOLVED_LEGACY, the owner-filtered list returns nothing) and only operator callers (absolute roles, M2M) see them; design-time WARNING INVOICE_OWNER_UNBINDABLE. The framework does not guess an owner column.
InvoicingConfig.__issuePolicy.doc: Declarative creation/finalization trigger — codegen wires the dispatcher accordingly, the designer never writes imperative glue. `manual` (default): invoices are created and finalized only through explicit calls. `onPaymentCaptured`: when the bound payment lifecycle reports a captured payment for the source object, the invoice is issued and finalized from the source snapshot (the B2C e-commerce flow). `onSourceCreate`: an open invoice with a due date is issued as soon as the source object is created — the B2B invoice-first-collect-later flow (pair with issueCondition to split B2B from B2C). onSourceCreate is wired through the in-process after-create seam: the db-layer create of the source object hands the committed row to the invoice manager automatically. `onSubscriptionInvoicePaid`: one invoice per provider subscription cycle, using the effective source subscription journal, including a cross-sourced object in this service; replay-safe and merchant-of-record aware.
InvoicingConfig.__issueCondition.doc: Optional MScript guard evaluated before an automatic issuePolicy trigger fires (e.g. only issue a legal invoice for B2B buyers). When present and falsy, the automatic trigger is skipped for that event; manual issuance stays available. BINDINGS: the guard runs with `this` bound to a context object, NOT the row - its only keys are `order` and `source` (both the source row the invoice is issued from: sourceObjectName, or this object itself) and `payment` (the sys_<X>Payment ticket on onPaymentCaptured, the sys_<X>Subscription row on a subscription capture, null on onSourceCreate); on onPaymentCaptured the lexical `event` / `resource` are in scope too. Write `order.buyerType === 'B2B'` (or `this.order.buyerType`), never `this.buyerType`: a `this.<field>` that is not one of those keys reads `undefined`, the guard is falsy on every event and no invoice is ever issued, so validation refuses it (CONDITION_THIS_NOT_IN_CONTEXT, ERROR).
InvoicingConfig.__customerProperty.doc: Property on this object referencing the buyer — an auth user id or a customer/party record reference. The invoice is attached to this customer for balance and collection purposes. It does NOT decide who may READ the invoice: read access is the invoice row's `ownerId`, stamped from the source object's owner column (see sourceObjectName).
InvoicingConfig.__amountProperty.doc: Optional property holding the invoice total, for objects whose total is not derived from lines. When invoiceLineRelation is active, line totals are authoritative and this binding serves as a mirror/cross-check. PLATFORM MONEY CONVENTION: MAJOR currency units as a decimal (the invoice family's native unit) - never bind a minor-unit (kurus/cents) column; line-relation bindings (unitPrice/lineTotal/vatAmount/...) follow the same convention. The bound column MUST be declared `type: "Decimal"`, so the framework rounds it to its `decimalScale` at every write boundary and before the amount reaches the provider. A bound column declared with another NUMERIC type (Integer/Short/Double/Float) is migrated by validation to Decimal (scale from the binding's static currency, default 2) and reported as an auto-fix; a non-numeric one is the ERROR `MONEY_BINDING_NOT_DECIMAL`.
InvoicingConfig.__vatRateStaticValue.doc: Optional static VAT rate (percent, e.g. 20) for RELATION-LESS invoice objects — the single implicit line built from amountProperty. Semantics: amountProperty is the VAT-INCLUSIVE gross; at snapshot time the implicit line is priced as a gross line (pricesIncludeVat) with the cart-parity gross-first formula (net = round(gross / (1 + rate/100)), vatAmount = gross - net, kurus rounding, so net + vatAmount equals the gross exactly), so invoice totals and fiscal document lines carry the real breakdown and the UBL emits a non-zero 0015 bucket with no exemption pair. Mutually exclusive with vatRateProperty (both set is a design-time ERROR) and meaningless next to invoiceLineRelation — the relation owns the per-line breakdown, so combining is a design-time ERROR. Rate 0 or key absent behaves exactly as before: zero bucket + the zero-VAT exemption fallback.
InvoicingConfig.__vatRateProperty.doc: Optional property ON THIS OBJECT holding the VAT rate (percent) for the relation-less single implicit line — the dynamic twin of vatRateStaticValue (both set is a design-time ERROR; combining with invoiceLineRelation is a design-time ERROR). Same VAT-inclusive-gross semantics; an unset/unreadable row value falls back to rate 0.
InvoicingConfig.__vatExemptionCodeProperty.doc: Optional property ON THIS OBJECT holding the GIB KDV exemption reason CODE of the relation-less single implicit line - the twin of invoiceLineRelation.vatExemptionCodeProperty for an object without a line relation, next to vatRateProperty. Read only when the line's VAT rate is 0: the code lands on the line's zero-VAT 0015 bucket of the Turkish fiscal document (cbc:TaxExemptionReasonCode), e.g. 335 for printed books (KDV 13/n), 301 for goods export, 351 for a 0% line that is NOT exempt. An unset or empty row value falls back to the invoice-wide / fiscal provider entry vatExemptionReasonCode, then to 350. The emitted codes decide the InvoiceTypeCode: any 2xx/3xx exemption code makes the document ISTISNA, 351 keeps SATIS. A code on a row whose rate is not 0 is refused when the document is prepared (typed 400). Combining it with a bound invoiceLineRelation is a design-time ERROR (the relation's own vatExemptionCodeProperty applies there).
InvoicingConfig.__vatExemptionReasonProperty.doc: Optional property ON THIS OBJECT holding the exemption reason TEXT that pairs vatExemptionCodeProperty on the relation-less single implicit line. Unset or empty: the platform writes the OFFICIAL GIB text of the code (UBL-TR Kod Listeleri, e.g. 335 -> 'KDV 13/n Basılı Kitap ve Süreli Yayınların Teslimleri'), so this binding is only needed for a code the GIB list does not carry yet. Meaningless without vatExemptionCodeProperty (WARNING).
InvoicingConfig.__currencyProperty.doc: Property on this object that holds the invoice currency.
InvoicingConfig.__currencyStaticValue.doc: Static currency fallback — applies only when currencyProperty is unset or resolves to nothing on the row.
InvoicingConfig.__dueDateProperty.doc: Optional property holding the payment due date stamped onto open invoices. When unbound, collection.daysUntilDue derives the due date at issue time.
InvoicingConfig.__statusProperty.doc: Optional property on this object that MIRRORS the invoice status (draft | open | paid | partially_paid | voided | uncollectible). The framework updates this property as the invoice state machine advances. It is a read model for UX/queries — the ledger's own statusLiteral on sys_<X>Invoice stays authoritative and is never writable through this object's update APIs.
InvoicingConfig.__invoiceLineRelation.doc: How this object relates to its LINE ITEM object — the editable SOURCE of invoice lines. Snapshot semantics: at finalize time the lines and their tax breakdown are copied into the immutable sys_<X>InvoiceLine ledger, so later edits to the source rows never change an issued invoice. The relation's per-line bindings align one-to-one with the line fields the shopping-cart pricing settings produce (unitPrice, quantity, lineTotal, discountAmount, vatRate, vatAmount, finalTotal), so a cart's tax breakdown flows into the invoice losslessly.
InvoicingConfig.__numbering.doc: Invoice numbering configuration (series / prefix / reset period). Authoritative for the internal provider (the framework's atomic sys_invoiceSequence assigns numbers) and for any provider with capabilities.supportsNumbering=false; when the bound provider owns the legal sequence (e.g. stripe), this block is ignored for number assignment.
InvoicingConfig.__collection.doc: How finalized invoices are collected: sent to the customer to be paid later (`sendInvoice`, with daysUntilDue deriving the due date), or charged automatically against a stored payment method (`chargeAutomatically` — requires the bound provider to have capabilities.supportsCollection=true).
InvoicingConfig.__lifecycleHooks.doc: Designer-authored MScript handlers fired as the invoice state machine advances (afterInvoiceFinalized, afterInvoicePaid, afterInvoiceVoided, afterCreditNoteIssued, afterPaymentApplied, ...). Invoice hooks carry their OWN trigger vocabulary (InvoiceLifecycleTrigger) — the payment LifecycleHook trigger enum is reconciled 1:1 with the payment lifecycle machines and deliberately stays untouched. A hook receives the normalized document (`invoice`: NormalizedInvoiceDetail; `allocation` / `creditNote` on their triggers), not the sys_<X>Invoice row - the source row id is `invoice.metadata.sourceObjectId`.
InvoicingConfig.__publishLifecycleEvents.doc: Opt-in (default false; only a literal `true` on an ACTIVE invoicing block counts) that makes the generated invoice layer publish this object's normalized INVOICE lifecycle events to Kafka (family `invoice`), one topic per event, 1:1 with the invoice lifecycle triggers: `<projectCodename>-<service>-service-lcevent-invoice-<object lowercased>-<suffix>`, where the FIXED event list and its suffixes are `invoice.finalized` -> `finalized` (afterInvoiceFinalized), `invoice.paid` -> `paid` (afterInvoicePaid), `invoice.partially_paid` -> `partially-paid` (afterInvoicePartiallyPaid), `invoice.voided` -> `voided` (afterInvoiceVoided), `invoice.uncollectible` -> `uncollectible` (afterInvoiceUncollectible), `invoice.payment_applied` -> `payment-applied` (afterPaymentApplied), `creditnote.issued` -> `creditnote-issued` (afterCreditNoteIssued). Published from the invoice lifecycle AFTER the designer lifecycle hooks of the same trigger, every time the trigger fires. `data` = { eventType, family, object, providerName, providerEventId (null: the triggers are not provider events), occurredAt, orderId (the source row id), status, dedupeKey, invoice (an ALLOWLISTED projection of the normalized invoice: providerInvoiceId, invoiceNumber, series, statusLiteral, currency, subtotal, vatTotal, total, amountPaid, amountRemaining, dueDate, issuedAt, lineCount, sourceObject, sourceObjectId, surfaceRowId), allocation (payment triggers: providerAllocationId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, appliedAt, paymentRef, invoiceStatus, amountPaid, amountRemaining), creditNote (creditnote.issued: providerCreditNoteId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, reason, issuedAt) }; never the buyer / seller party, the lines or the metadata wholesale. Delivery is AT LEAST ONCE through the service's lifecycle outbox: each event is written to `sys_lifecycle_outbox` (one row per `data.dedupeKey`, the built envelope plus its retry state) before it is sent, the send is never awaited by the transition that fired it, and a send the broker refuses (logged `PaymentLifecycleEventPublishFailed`) is re-sent by the outbox sweeper with the same envelope id and dedupeKey (every PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_OUTBOX_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, default 30 s; backoff up to one hour; parked `dead` after 50 refusals). The same fact processed twice (a redelivered invoice webhook) is sent once while its outbox row is kept; a redelivery can still repeat an event: dedupe on `data.dedupeKey`, and reconcile money from the invoice rows, not from the stream. Envelope: `type` = the normalized event type; `actor.tenantId` = the row's tenant in a multi-tenant project. Off (the default) the generated code is byte-identical to a build without the field; the topics are listed by the kafka topic census and pre-created only while it is on.

__InvoiceOperation.doc.#: The invoice lifecycle operation an InvoiceAction performs against the bound InvoiceProvider (through the generated per-object InvoiceManager — one code path for internal and external systems of record).
__InvoiceOperation.doc.create: Cut a DRAFT invoice from the source row: line snapshot through invoiceLineRelation (or a single line from amountProperty), buyer/currency/due-date from the declared bindings.
__InvoiceOperation.doc.finalize: draft → open: the number is assigned (internal: the atomic sys_invoiceSequence counter; supportsNumbering providers assign their own) and the document becomes immutable.
__InvoiceOperation.doc.void: Void a draft/open invoice. A settled or partially settled invoice is refused by the FSM — correct it with a credit note instead.
__InvoiceOperation.doc.applyPayment: Record a payment against an open invoice: allocation row + amountPaid/amountRemaining arithmetic + the partially_paid/paid transition.
__InvoiceOperation.doc.creditNote: Issue a credit note with amountProperty, reasonProperty and optional idempotencyKeyProperty. Use `refund-<providerRefundId>` for a refund-driven note. No automatic fiscal submission.

__FiscalOperation.doc.#: The fiscal document operation a FiscalizeAction performs against the bound FiscalProvider (through the generated per-object FiscalizationManager and the jurisdiction policy pipeline).
__FiscalOperation.doc.submit: Build and submit a fiscal document for the source row's FINALIZED invoice: the frozen snapshot is serialized (Turkey: UBL-TR), routed by the jurisdiction policy (buyer lookup picks e-invoice exchange vs e-archive reporting) and submitted to the provider. The sys_<X>FiscalDocument ledger row advances draft -> prepared -> submitted and onward with the provider's synchronous verdict.
__FiscalOperation.doc.cancel: Cancel an ACCEPTED document through the network's cancellation or objection flow (capabilities.supportsCancellation). Refused by the FSM for documents in any other state.
__FiscalOperation.doc.queryStatus: One-shot status poll for a submitted/pending document (capabilities.supportsStatusQuery). The verdict is recorded as a synthetic fiscal event and dispatched through the same path the status cron and webhooks use, so the FSM advances and lifecycle hooks fire exactly once.
__FiscalOperation.doc.resubmit: Resubmit a rejected or failed fiscal document by fiscalDocumentIdProperty through the same correction pipeline as the operator route.

__InvoiceIssuePolicy.doc.#: Declarative trigger deciding WHEN an invoice is created/finalized for an invoicing-enabled DataObject. The designer declares the trigger; codegen wires the dispatcher chain — no imperative glue.
__InvoiceIssuePolicy.doc.manual: Invoices are created and finalized only through explicit calls (invoice actions / admin surface). The default, and the imperative escape hatch.
__InvoiceIssuePolicy.doc.onPaymentCaptured: The invoice is issued and finalized from the source snapshot when the payment lifecycle reports a captured payment for the source object — the B2C e-commerce reference flow (checkout → payment.captured → invoice).
__InvoiceIssuePolicy.doc.onSourceCreate: An open invoice (with due date) is issued as soon as the source object is created — the B2B invoice-first flow; collection is allocated later as payments arrive.
__InvoiceIssuePolicy.doc.onSubscriptionInvoicePaid: Issue, finalize and settle one invoice per paid subscription cycle. sourceObjectName may name another subscription object of this service. Correlates the provider subscription through that source object's journal, uses the cycle amount/currency when supplied, and reuses the issuance claim on redelivery. Merchant-of-record events do not issue a second invoice.

__InvoiceLineRelation.doc: How an invoicing-enabled object relates to its line item object (provider-neutral sibling of StripeOrderItemRelation). The line item object is the EDITABLE SOURCE of invoice lines; at finalize time the bound fields are snapshotted into the immutable sys_<X>InvoiceLine ledger. The per-line bindings align with the line fields the shopping-cart pricing settings produce (quantity, unitPrice, lineTotal, discountAmount, vatRate, vatAmount, finalTotal), so a cart's tax breakdown flows into the invoice losslessly. Only quantity/unitPrice/description are commonly needed — the tax-breakdown bindings are for lines that already carry computed VAT.

InvoiceLineRelation.__hasLineItemRelation.doc: Enables invoice to line-item relation mapping. When false, relation configuration is ignored and the invoice total comes from amountProperty.
InvoiceLineRelation.__lineItemObject.doc: Line item data object name. This should be a local data object in the same service.
InvoiceLineRelation.__invoiceForeignKey.doc: Property of the current (invoicing-enabled) object that provides the value used to match line items. Commonly `id`.
InvoiceLineRelation.__lineItemLocalKey.doc: Property of the line item object that stores the relation value to this object. Commonly `orderId` or `invoiceId`.
InvoiceLineRelation.__quantityProperty.doc: Property of the line item object that stores the line quantity. Commonly `quantity`.
InvoiceLineRelation.__unitPriceProperty.doc: Property of the line item object that stores the unit price. Commonly `unitPrice`. Read as NET (VAT added on top) unless pricesIncludeVat is true, in which case it is the GROSS, VAT-inclusive price.
InvoiceLineRelation.__descriptionProperty.doc: Property of the line item object that stores the human-readable line description shown on the invoice.
InvoiceLineRelation.__lineTotalProperty.doc: Optional: property holding the NET line total AFTER the discount and before VAT - the same field the shopping cart writes as lineTotal in both of its VAT modes. When unbound, derived at snapshot time: quantity × unitPrice − discountAmount for a net-priced line, and (quantity × unitPrice − discountAmount) / (1 + vatRate/100) for a line with pricesIncludeVat. A bound value that disagrees with that derivation is refused at invoice creation.
InvoiceLineRelation.__discountAmountProperty.doc: Optional: property holding the per-line discount amount.
InvoiceLineRelation.__discountReasonProperty.doc: Optional: string property holding the per-line discount reason. Snapshotted onto the invoice line and emitted as cbc:AllowanceChargeReason inside a Turkish UBL discount allowance. Whitespace is trimmed and the text is XML-escaped; null or empty text emits no reason element.
InvoiceLineRelation.__vatRateProperty.doc: Optional: property holding the per-line VAT rate. Bind it when lines already carry computed tax (e.g. from shopping-cart pricing) so the invoice keeps the exact breakdown.
InvoiceLineRelation.__vatExemptionCodeProperty.doc: Optional: property of the line item object holding the line's GIB KDV exemption reason CODE - product data the merchant knows, e.g. 335 for printed books and periodicals (KDV 13/n), 301 for goods export, 351 for a 0% line that is NOT exempt. Snapshotted onto the invoice line (sys_<X>InvoiceLine.vatExemptionReasonCode) and threaded into the Turkish fiscal document, where it is the cbc:TaxExemptionReasonCode of that line's zero-VAT 0015 bucket; 0% lines are grouped per (rate, code), so two codes give two document TaxSubtotals. Read only for a 0% line: an unset or empty value falls back to the invoice-wide / fiscal provider entry vatExemptionReasonCode, then to 350; a code on a line whose VAT rate is not 0 is refused when the document is prepared (typed 400). The emitted codes decide the InvoiceTypeCode: any 2xx/3xx exemption code makes the document ISTISNA (taxed lines such as shipping at 20% stay on it), only 351 keeps SATIS; 7xx/8xx codes (IHRACKAYITLI / OZELMATRAH documents) are refused (typed 422).
InvoiceLineRelation.__vatExemptionReasonProperty.doc: Optional: property of the line item object holding the exemption reason TEXT that pairs vatExemptionCodeProperty. Unset or empty: the platform writes the OFFICIAL GIB text of the line's code (UBL-TR Kod Listeleri, e.g. 335 -> 'KDV 13/n Basılı Kitap ve Süreli Yayınların Teslimleri'), so bind it only for wording the list does not carry or for a code GIB added later. Meaningless without vatExemptionCodeProperty (WARNING).
InvoiceLineRelation.__vatAmountProperty.doc: Optional: property holding the per-line VAT amount.
InvoiceLineRelation.__finalTotalProperty.doc: Optional: property holding the final per-line total (after discount, including VAT). When unbound, derived at snapshot time: lineTotal + vatAmount for a net-priced line; for a line with pricesIncludeVat it IS the gross (quantity × unitPrice − discountAmount), the one field that carries the gross in that mode.
InvoiceLineRelation.__pricesIncludeVat.doc: Whether the bound unit prices (and discounts) are VAT-INCLUSIVE, the convention of a Turkish B2C catalogue and of a cart with pricingSettings.catalogPricesIncludeVat. Default false: prices are NET and VAT is added on top, so a 120 TRY price at 20% is invoiced as 120 + 24 = 144. When true, each line is priced GROSS-FIRST with the cart's rounding-exact extraction: gross = quantity × unitPrice − discountAmount, net lineTotal = gross / (1 + vatRate/100), vatAmount = gross − net (so net + VAT equals the gross exactly), finalTotal = gross; 120 at 20% is net 100 + VAT 20 = 120. lineTotal keeps ONE meaning in both modes, the net after discount (what the cart itself writes as lineTotal when it prices VAT-inclusive); in inclusive mode the gross is finalTotal. A bound lineTotal / vatAmount / finalTotal is validated against that extraction. Requires vatRateProperty: without a per-line rate there is no VAT to extract.

__InvoiceNumberingConfig.doc: Invoice numbering configuration for an invoicing-enabled DataObject. Effective when the framework owns the sequence — always for the internal provider, and for any provider entry with capabilities.supportsNumbering=false; a provider that owns the legal number (e.g. stripe) ignores it. Numbers come from the atomic sys_invoiceSequence counter, keyed by (series, period). NUMBERING IS PER SERVICE (the twin of the fiscal series rule). sys_invoiceSequence is injected once per service and every generated service has its own database, so its (series, year) unique constrains nothing ACROSS services: two services numbering under one series each keep a private counter and both mint the same invoice number, with no vendor to refuse the duplicate and no burn-and-retry to recover it. Two services of one project numbering through the framework under the same series is therefore REFUSED at design time (INVOICE_SERIES_SHARED_ACROSS_SERVICES, ERROR). Give each invoicing service its own numbering.series.

InvoiceNumberingConfig.__series.doc: Named series key the sequence counter is scoped by (e.g. 'A'). Multiple invoicing objects OF THE SAME SERVICE may share a series - they share one counter row in one database, which is correct. Two SERVICES may never share one: sys_invoiceSequence is per service and per database, so a shared series means two private counters minting the same number, and validation refuses it (INVOICE_SERIES_SHARED_ACROSS_SERVICES). Leaving series unset does NOT avoid this - the emitted allocator falls back to the constant 'INV', so two services that both omit it collide without anyone having configured anything shared. Within one service, sharing stays fine; jurisdictional series formats are applied by the fiscal policy layer, not here.
InvoiceNumberingConfig.__prefix.doc: Literal prefix prepended to the formatted number on the rendered invoice (e.g. 'INV-').
InvoiceNumberingConfig.__resetPeriod.doc: When the sequence counter resets: never (default), yearly, or monthly. Jurisdictions whose number format embeds the year typically reset yearly.

__InvoiceNumberingResetPeriod.doc.#: When an invoice numbering sequence counter resets.
__InvoiceNumberingResetPeriod.doc.never: One continuous sequence for the series. The default.
__InvoiceNumberingResetPeriod.doc.yearly: The counter restarts at 1 at the start of each year — for number formats that embed the year.
__InvoiceNumberingResetPeriod.doc.monthly: The counter restarts at 1 at the start of each month.

__InvoiceCollectionConfig.doc: How finalized invoices on an invoicing-enabled DataObject are collected. `sendInvoice` (the default) issues the invoice to the customer and waits for payment within daysUntilDue; `chargeAutomatically` charges a stored payment method at finalize time and requires the bound InvoiceProvider to have capabilities.supportsCollection=true (in practice: stripe). With external accounting providers, collection typically stays on the PaymentProvider side and this block keeps its sendInvoice default.

InvoiceCollectionConfig.__collectionMethod.doc: 'sendInvoice' — the invoice is delivered to the customer and paid later; the invoice opens with a due date. 'chargeAutomatically' — the provider charges the customer's stored payment method when the invoice is finalized; requires capabilities.supportsCollection on the bound provider.
InvoiceCollectionConfig.__daysUntilDue.doc: Days between issue date and due date under sendInvoice collection. Used to derive the due date when dueDateProperty is not bound. Ignored under chargeAutomatically.

__InvoiceCollectionMethod.doc.#: How a finalized invoice is collected.
__InvoiceCollectionMethod.doc.sendInvoice: Deliver the invoice to the customer and wait for payment until the due date. The default, and the only method external accounting providers use.
__InvoiceCollectionMethod.doc.chargeAutomatically: Charge the customer's stored payment method when the invoice is finalized. Requires the bound provider's capabilities.supportsCollection=true.

__InvoiceLifecycleHook.doc: A designer-authored MScript handler fired by the invoice dispatcher when the invoice state machine advances. Mirrors the payment LifecycleHook shape (name / trigger / condition / script) but carries its OWN trigger vocabulary — the payment PaymentLifecycleTrigger enum is reconciled 1:1 with the payment lifecycle machines and deliberately stays untouched by the invoice family. Hooks run after the FSM transition is persisted; a failure inside a hook does not roll back the transition. The hook context is the NORMALIZED document, not a ledger row: `invoice` is a NormalizedInvoiceDetail on every trigger, `allocation` (NormalizedPaymentApplication) and `creditNote` (NormalizedCreditNote) are set only on their own triggers - see `script` for every field and for where the source row id lives. A member read those shapes do not carry is reported at design time (INVOICE_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_UNKNOWN_FIELD_SILENT, WARNING), as is a read on a root the trigger never supplies (INVOICE_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_ROOT_NULL_ON_TRIGGER, WARNING).

InvoiceLifecycleHook.__name.doc: Unique name of this hook within its parent InvoicingConfig. Used in logs and the events table.
InvoiceLifecycleHook.__trigger.doc: Which invoice lifecycle event fires this hook.
InvoiceLifecycleHook.__description.doc: Human-readable explanation of what this hook does.
InvoiceLifecycleHook.__condition.doc: Optional MScript boolean - when present and falsy, the hook is skipped for this event.
