Sees the same names as `script` (`invoice`, `allocation`, `creditNote` - the normalized shapes, not ledger rows) and is checked for field reads the same way. `this` is the generated `_hookCtx` whose only keys are those three names: `this.total` reads `undefined` (write `invoice.total`), and validation warns on it (LIFECYCLE_HOOK_THIS_NOT_IN_CONTEXT).
InvoiceLifecycleHook.__script.doc: MScript body executed when the trigger fires. Runs from the invoice dispatcher, not from a request - there is no request, session or user in scope. The names in scope are the NORMALIZED provider shapes, NOT the sys_<X>Invoice row. `invoice` is a NormalizedInvoiceDetail on every trigger: providerInvoiceId, invoiceNumber, series, statusLiteral, currency, subtotal, vatTotal, total, amountPaid, amountRemaining, dueDate, issuedAt, buyer, seller, lines, vatExemptionReasonCode, vatExemptionReason, metadata - and nothing else: it has NO `id`, `sourceObjectId` or `customerId`. The sys_<X>Invoice row id is `invoice.providerInvoiceId` (on every provider binding - an external provider's own invoice id rides `invoice.metadata.__externalInvoiceId`). The SOURCE row id is `invoice.metadata.sourceObjectId` and its object name `invoice.metadata.sourceObject`; the invoicing object's own row (the one the statusProperty mirror writes) is `invoice.metadata.__surfaceRowId`, equal to the source row id when the object invoices its own rows; the buyer is `invoice.buyer?.partyId`. The framework stamps those metadata keys when it creates the draft, so an invoice created provider-side and imported without them carries none - guard the read. `allocation` is a NormalizedPaymentApplication (providerAllocationId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, appliedAt, paymentRef, invoiceStatus, amountPaid, amountRemaining, metadata) on afterPaymentApplied / afterInvoicePaid / afterInvoicePartiallyPaid when the payment was applied in-process, and `null` otherwise - including an external provider's invoice.paid webhook. `creditNote` is a NormalizedCreditNote (providerCreditNoteId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, reason, issuedAt, metadata) on afterCreditNoteIssued and `null` on every other trigger. The generated file binds these names through `any`, so a field that is not on the lists above compiles and reads `undefined` at every fire - and an `undefined` handed on as an api id or where-clause value finds no row; validation reports such a read (INVOICE_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_UNKNOWN_FIELD_SILENT, WARNING - the binding is `any`, so the build does not break) whether it is a direct member (`invoice.x`, `invoice?.x`, `this.invoice.x`), a string-literal key (`invoice['x']`), a key destructured off the root (`const { x } = invoice`) or one of those through ONE alias level (`const inv = invoice`, `((inv) => ...)(invoice)`). A field an earlier hook assigns onto `invoice` excuses the read only when that hook has the SAME trigger and comes EARLIER in the list. Names are resolved by scope: a parameter or local that reuses the root's or an alias's name is that local, so neither its reads nor its writes count. Lexical identity is respected in parameter defaults, switch discriminants, named classes and static blocks; this is not general dataflow analysis. Not checked (silence is not clean): a key computed at runtime, a spread or rest element, a `let` alias, an alias of an alias, a root renamed while destructuring `this`, a `this` rebound by a nested non-arrow `function`, and a root handed to any function other than an inline IIFE. Reach service logic through `LIB.<module>(...)` and other rows through `API.<apiName>(...)` (Node.js only: dotnet generation refuses an `API` read in invoice hook slots, use `LIB`) - the generated hook file does not import the dbLayer getters. Use hooks to fan out to other services (publish kafka events), update related records, or run application-side bookkeeping. Example: `await API.markOrderInvoiced({ orderId: invoice.metadata?.sourceObjectId, invoiceNumber: invoice.invoiceNumber })`.
InvoiceLifecycleHook.name: String

__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.#: Normalized invoice lifecycle events that can fire an InvoiceLifecycleHook. The invoice dispatcher maps state-machine transitions onto these values before invoking hooks, so the same hook definition works regardless of which provider is the system of record. A SEPARATE vocabulary from PaymentLifecycleTrigger on purpose: that enum is reconciled 1:1 with the payment lifecycle machines and stays untouched.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoiceFinalized: Fired when a draft invoice is finalized (draft → open): the number is assigned and the line snapshot is frozen. Use for delivery, notification, downstream document flows.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoicePaid: Fired when the invoice balance reaches zero (open/partially_paid → paid). Use for fulfillment gating, receipt emission.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoicePartiallyPaid: Fired when a payment is applied but a balance remains (open → partially_paid). Use for partial-payment bookkeeping and dunning.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoiceVoided: Fired when an invoice is voided (legal cancellation that keeps the number). Use to reverse downstream effects.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoiceUncollectible: Fired when an open invoice is marked uncollectible. Use for write-off bookkeeping and notification; the invoice can return to open if payment later arrives.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterCreditNoteIssued: Fired when a credit note is issued against a finalized invoice. Use to propagate the correction to bookkeeping.
__InvoiceLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentApplied: Fired on every payment allocation written against the invoice (the sys_<X>InvoicePayment row, handed to the hook as `allocation`, a NormalizedPaymentApplication). Fires alongside the resulting state trigger (afterInvoicePaid / afterInvoicePartiallyPaid), which describe the state outcome rather than the allocation event.

__Fiscalization.doc: Regulatory fiscalization activation for a DataObject. Mark a DataObject as fiscalized by enabling `objectIsFiscalized` and pointing `configuration.fiscalProviderName` at a configured FiscalProvider. The framework generates the sys_<X>FiscalDocument ledger around this object and routes each document through the jurisdiction's fiscal policy module (classify → prepare → validate → sign → submit → track → distribute → archive; which steps run is decided per document by the policy plus the provider's capabilities). Fiscalization is deliberately independent of `invoicing`: an invoicing-enabled object typically fiscalizes its finalized invoices, but a reporting-style regime may fiscalize transaction data on an object with no invoicing block at all — both shapes are supported. In a marketplace project the BILLING MODEL decides where this block goes: a reseller (merchant-model) platform fiscalizes the sale object itself, while an intermediary platform NEVER fiscalizes the sale — it fiscalizes only its commission object, whose buyerParty binds the seller's tax identity columns. The models, their legal pairing rules and the full commission composition are in the docs-site guide [Intermediation vs reseller billing](../mastering/intermediation-vs-reseller-billing.md).

Fiscalization.__objectIsFiscalized.doc: Enables fiscalization logic for this object. When true, the object is treated as the source of fiscal documents: the framework generates the sys_<X>FiscalDocument ledger and the submit/track surface bound to the configured FiscalProvider and jurisdiction policy.
Fiscalization.__configuration.doc: The FiscalizationConfig describing how this object maps onto the fiscal pipeline (provider binding, jurisdiction, party bindings, document typing, submit policy, lifecycle hooks). Leave it null if objectIsFiscalized is false.

__FiscalizationConfig.doc: Configuration for regulatory fiscalization on a DataObject. Provider-binding is explicit via `fiscalProviderName` (lookup into projectSettings.fiscalProvidersSettings.fiscalProviders[]); when null and EXACTLY ONE fiscal provider is declared, the framework binds that one implicitly (single-provider convenience) — with zero or several declared providers a null binding is a design error, because unlike invoicing there is no framework-internal fiscal authority to fall back to. `jurisdiction` selects the fiscal policy module compiled into the service (v1 ships the Turkish policy; other ISO codes are accepted with a roadmap warning). The trigger is DECLARATIVE (`submitPolicy` / `submitCondition`) — the designer never writes imperative glue; `submitPolicy: manual` plus fiscal actions is the imperative escape hatch (Faz 3 runtime slices). SERIES OWNERSHIP IS PER SERVICE. A fiscalProviders[] entry is one integrator account with ONE serialPrefix, and the wire-serial counter (sys_fiscalSerialSequence) lives in the EMITTING service's own database, so two services bound to one entry keep two private counters for what the vendor sees as a single series - and the integrator burn-and-retry hides the collision while it spends real serials out of a live account. Binding a second service to an entry another service already fiscalizes through is therefore REFUSED at design time (FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED, ERROR). The exception is an entry with serialAssignment "vendor" (uyumsoft, mock): the integrator numbers its documents and no service keeps a counter, so several services may bind it (a serialAssignment left blank for deploy time is judged as platform numbering; with supportsInboundDocuments on, the shared entry WARNS FISCAL_INBOUND_SHARED_ACCOUNT because every binding service polls the one inbox). To fiscalize from two services on platform numbering: register a second serial series with the integrator, declare a second entry with the same brand and the same credentials and its OWN serialPrefix, and bind that entry from the second service. The document number's human shape differs per service as a result; that is intended, not a defect. Inbound vendor documents are not supported on a tenant-scoped fiscal object: the fiscal ledger carries a tenant field even for a SaaS-level source or a fiscal-only object without an invoice, while vendor inbox documents carry none. Binding an inbound-capable provider there reports FISCAL_INBOUND_TENANT_UNSUPPORTED (WARNING), and codegen excludes the object from inbound ingestion; no inbound cron, mount or schedule is emitted when all inbound-capable objects are tenant-scoped. Outbound fiscalization remains valid. Tenant attribution for inbound documents is postponed.

FiscalizationConfig.__fiscalProviderName.doc: Name of the configured FiscalProvider this object's documents are submitted through. Must match an entry in projectSettings.fiscalProvidersSettings.fiscalProviders[].name. When null and exactly one fiscal provider is declared, that provider is bound implicitly; otherwise a null binding is reported at design time — there is no internal fiscal provider. SERIES OWNERSHIP IS PER SERVICE. A fiscalProviders[] entry is one integrator account with ONE serialPrefix, and the wire-serial counter (sys_fiscalSerialSequence) lives in the EMITTING service's own database, so two services bound to one entry keep two private counters for what the vendor sees as a single series - and the integrator burn-and-retry hides the collision while it spends real serials out of a live account. Binding a second service to an entry another service already fiscalizes through is therefore REFUSED at design time (FISCAL_SERIAL_NAMESPACE_SHARED, ERROR). The exception is an entry with serialAssignment "vendor" (uyumsoft, mock): the integrator numbers its documents and no service keeps a counter, so several services may bind it (a serialAssignment left blank for deploy time is judged as platform numbering; with supportsInboundDocuments on, the shared entry WARNS FISCAL_INBOUND_SHARED_ACCOUNT because every binding service polls the one inbox). To fiscalize from two services on platform numbering: register a second serial series with the integrator, declare a second entry with the same brand and the same credentials and its OWN serialPrefix, and bind that entry from the second service. The document number's human shape differs per service as a result; that is intended, not a defect.
FiscalizationConfig.__jurisdiction.doc: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code driving fiscal policy selection (e.g. 'TR'). The policy module is code compiled into the service, not blueprint data: it decides routing (Turkey: buyer-lookup splits e-invoice EXCHANGE from e-archive REPORTING), series formats and cancellation windows. Static for v1; a jurisdictionProperty PropRefer can be added later for multi-country sellers without breaking existing blueprints. v1 ships the 'TR' policy — other codes validate with a roadmap WARNING.
FiscalizationConfig.__sellerParty.doc: Identity of the document ISSUER (the platform operator or tenant company): tax id, legal name, address. OPTIONAL, and an OVERRIDE when present: the project's OWN seller identity lives on the bound fiscalProviders[] entry instead - configuration keys sellerTaxId / sellerName / sellerAddress / sellerDistrict / sellerCity, ops-supplied and env-backed exactly like the credentials that select the integrator account. It belongs there because it is one identity per project (declared per object it diverges - the same company was spelled two ways and omitted a third time on the first project that used the feature) and because it is ENVIRONMENT-VARYING: a sandbox integrator account has a different tax id than production, so a value baked into the blueprint cannot move between environments. Resolution order at emit time: this block, then the provider entry, then unbound. A tax id source must resolve at ONE of those two levels or the design is reported (FISCAL_SELLER_PARTY_UNBOUND) - a document that cannot name its issuer is rejected by every regime, so an unbound seller is a certainty of failure, not a runtime risk. Bind this block only when the issuer genuinely varies per row: a marketplace whose merchants invoice in their own name (taxIdProperty), or one object deliberately pinned to a different seller (taxIdStaticValue).
FiscalizationConfig.__buyerParty.doc: Identity of the document RECIPIENT: tax id, legal name, address. Typically bound with PropRefer paths into this object's properties (the buyer differs per row); static values are the fallback for fixed-counterparty setups. A NAME source is REQUIRED under the TR jurisdiction: bind nameProperty or nameStaticValue, or the design is reported at design time. Nothing downstream can supply the name - not the session, not the auth user, not the object's customer - and a Turkish e-Arsiv consumer document that names no buyer is rejected by the vendor, so an unbound name ships a nameless document. The buyer TAX ID by contrast stays optional on purpose: a sale that binds no buyer tax id is a consumer sale, and the policy routes it to the reporting scheme. The buyer tax id also feeds the policy's buyer-lookup (Turkey: is the buyer a registered e-invoice user?), which decides the document's route.
FiscalizationConfig.__lookupIndividuals.doc: Registry lookup for INDIVIDUAL (personal) buyer tax ids - ON by default. Buyer typing is derived from the bound tax id, never declared: an absent tax id is a consumer sale, an 11-digit personal id (Turkey: TCKN) is a person, a 10-digit company id (Turkey: VKN) is a company. Company ids are always looked up on the e-invoice network; personal ids are looked up too unless this is set to false, because an individual may be a sole proprietor registered on the network, and a registered buyer must receive the exchange document (Turkey: e-Fatura - the integrator refuses an e-Archive document for a registered buyer, a typed FISCAL_BUYER_REGISTERED_FOR_EINVOICE error). A registered personal id routes through exchange like a company's; an unregistered one goes to the reporting scheme (Turkey: e-Archive). Set false only to skip the lookup and send every individual straight to the reporting scheme. Ignored for consumer sales and when the bound provider cannot look buyers up.
FiscalizationConfig.__internetSale.doc: Bindings for the e-commerce (internet sales) content some reporting regimes require on the document. Turkey (VUK General Communique 509): an e-archive invoice for an internet sale must carry the sale's website, the payment method and date, the shipment date, and a COMPLETE carrier party - the carrier company's legal title and VKN with the shipment tracking number, or the seller itself when it delivers with its own vehicle or courier. Bind them here from the order object's properties, the designer's carrier data object (carrierMode / carrierDataObject) or static values where the platform is fixed. Optional: when absent the document is built without the internet-sales section; the validator recommends these bindings when fiscalization rides an object that also has checkout (the e-commerce signal), and once the block binds anything under TR it must declare a carrier source (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_UNBOUND, ERROR) unless it ships nothing: with carrierMode empty and no shipment slot bound (website / payment only - a digital good, a service, a subscription) the sale is treated as noShipment with a WARNING instead (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_DEFAULTED_NO_SHIPMENT, maintainer ruling 2026-10-03). The block is an OBJECT-level declaration (maintainer ruling 2026-10-03): an object whose fiscalization declares an internetSale block is an internet-sale object, so EVERY row is fiscalized as an internet sale - the internet-sale phrase, cac:Delivery per carrierMode and the ELEKTRONIK sending type - even a row whose own bound slots are empty. An object that sells both in store and online must be split into two objects or two fiscalization configurations.
FiscalizationConfig.__documentTypeMap.doc: Optional MScript expression that overrides the fiscal document type per row (e.g. mapping a transaction kind to invoice, creditNote or receipt). When null, the jurisdiction policy derives the type from the document's own data. Runs at classify time, before the route is resolved. A creditNote must name the invoice it returns: declare originalRefProperty, the property holding the id of the original row, and set it on the return row; Turkey writes the original's 16-character serial and issue date as cac:BillingReference on the IADE document. A TR map that can yield 'creditNote' without originalRefProperty is refused at design time (FISCAL_CREDIT_NOTE_ORIGINAL_UNBOUND, ERROR). A matching map: source.originalOrderId ? 'creditNote' : 'invoice'.
FiscalizationConfig.__originalRefProperty.doc: Property of this object holding the id of the ORIGINAL row a credit-note row returns: another row of this object, the one whose invoice was fiscalized. Required on a TR fiscalization whose documentTypeMap can yield 'creditNote' (FISCAL_CREDIT_NOTE_ORIGINAL_UNBOUND, ERROR): GIB requires every IADE document to name the invoice it returns (cac:BillingReference). The value is the original row's id, NOT a sys invoice id: the generated FiscalizationManager reads that row's issued outbound fiscal document (status submitted, pending, accepted or completed; not itself a credit note) for its 16-character serial and the row's invoice for its issue date (written as the Turkey-local date). A list of row ids names several originals, one reference each. On a multi-tenant object only documents of the return row's tenant are read. A credit note whose original does not resolve - empty value, no issued document, or a row with more than one issued invoice (ambiguous) - is refused with a typed fiscal error before the integrator call. Read only for rows the documentTypeMap classifies as creditNote; needs the invoicing block on the same object. To model a TR return: create the return as a row of this object, set this property to the original row's id, and let documentTypeMap classify it (source.originalOrderId ? 'creditNote' : 'invoice').
FiscalizationConfig.__useCommercialInvoiceProfile.doc: Selects the jurisdiction's COMMERCIAL exchange profile for network-delivered documents. Turkey: true stamps ProfileID TICARIFATURA on e-invoice (TR_EFATURA) documents — the commercial profile with the buyer accept/reject flow; null or false stays on the base TEMELFATURA profile. Ignored on reporting routes (Turkey: e-archive documents always carry the EARSIVFATURA profile) and by jurisdictions without a commercial-profile concept.
FiscalizationConfig.__submitPolicy.doc: Declarative submission trigger — codegen wires the dispatcher accordingly. `onInvoiceFinalized` (the default): the fiscal pipeline runs when this object's invoice is finalized (requires the invoicing block on the same object; the finalize snapshot is the document source). `manual`: documents are submitted only through explicit calls (fiscal actions / admin surface) — the imperative escape hatch, and the natural mode for reporting-only objects without invoicing.
FiscalizationConfig.__submitCondition.doc: Optional MScript guard evaluated before an automatic submitPolicy trigger fires (e.g. only fiscalize domestic sales). When present and falsy, the automatic trigger is skipped for that event; manual submission stays available. BINDINGS: the guard runs with `this` bound to a context object, NOT the row - its only keys are `invoice` (the finalized NormalizedInvoiceDetail: total, currency, buyer, metadata, ...) and `source` (this object's row, when resolvable). Write `source.country === 'TR'` or `invoice.total > 0` (or `this.invoice.total`), never `this.country`: a `this.<field>` that is not one of those keys reads `undefined`, the guard is falsy on every event and nothing is ever submitted, so validation refuses it (CONDITION_THIS_NOT_IN_CONTEXT, ERROR).
FiscalizationConfig.__onFiscalError.doc: Determines the system's behavior when a fiscal pipeline step fails. 'continueRoute' logs the failure on the fiscal document and lets the surrounding flow proceed; 'throwError' halts the flow. Fiscal rejection by the authority is NOT a pipeline error — it is a normal FSM outcome (rejected, resubmittable).
FiscalizationConfig.__lifecycleHooks.doc: Designer-authored MScript handlers fired as the fiscal document state machine advances (afterFiscalSubmitted, afterFiscalAccepted, afterFiscalRejected, afterFiscalCanceled, afterFiscalFailed). A row that mirrors the fiscal outcome (e.g. a fiscalStatus property) needs a hook on EVERY outcome it shows: afterFiscalAccepted and afterFiscalRejected cover the authority verdicts, afterFiscalFailed covers a technical failure (integrator 5xx, transport, a prepare step that throws) - without it the row keeps its old value while the document sits failed until an operator resubmits. The owning row id is fiscalDocument.metadata.sourceObjectId. Fiscal hooks carry their OWN trigger vocabulary (FiscalLifecycleTrigger) — the payment LifecycleHook trigger enum is reconciled 1:1 with the payment lifecycle machines and deliberately stays untouched, and the invoice family's InvoiceLifecycleTrigger likewise stays invoice-only.

__FiscalPartyConfig.doc: Identity of one party (seller or buyer) on a fiscal document. Each of the three identity slots (tax id, legal name, address) binds EITHER a property of the owning DataObject (PropRefer — per-row identity) OR a static value (fixed identity); when both are set the property wins and the static value is the row-level fallback. The tax id is the load-bearing slot: it keys buyer-lookup routing and appears verbatim on the document; name and address are document content. Kept deliberately lean — structured address breakdowns, registration numbers and scheme ids are jurisdiction concerns the policy module derives, not blueprint fields.

FiscalPartyConfig.__taxIdProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the party's tax identifier (Turkey: VKN or TCKN). For the buyer this is the usual binding — every row carries its own counterparty.
FiscalPartyConfig.__taxIdStaticValue.doc: Static tax identifier — the usual binding for the seller party, whose identity is fixed per project. Used when taxIdProperty is unset or resolves to nothing on the row.
FiscalPartyConfig.__nameProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the party's legal name.
FiscalPartyConfig.__nameStaticValue.doc: Static legal name. Used when nameProperty is unset or resolves to nothing on the row.
FiscalPartyConfig.__addressProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the party's address as a single text value.
FiscalPartyConfig.__addressStaticValue.doc: Static address text. Used when addressProperty is unset or resolves to nothing on the row.

__FiscalInternetSaleConfig.doc: Bindings sourcing the internet-sales content of a fiscal document from the owning DataObject. Some reporting regimes demand extra content for e-commerce sales (Turkey, VUK General Communique 509: an e-archive invoice for an internet sale must state the website, the payment method and date, the shipment date and a complete carrier party). Each slot binds a property of the owning object (PropRefer — per-row values) and, where the value is fixed per project, a static fallback; the website is static-only, since the sales channel does not vary per row. The carrier is declared by carrierMode: carrierCompany reads the carrier's legal title and VKN/TCKN from the designer's carrier data object (the carrier-company settings; OpenAPPL has no carrier system table) or from static values for a single-carrier shop, plus the tracking number; selfDelivery names the seller as the carrier; noShipment declares that nothing physical is shipped. An empty carrierMode reads as noShipment when no shipment slot (carrier source, legacy carrier name, shipment date, tracking number) is bound - a digital or service sale, with a WARNING - and as carrierCompany otherwise (maintainer ruling 2026-10-03). Never a name-only or empty carrier: a TR configuration without a carrier source is refused at design time and a carrier whose tax id does not resolve is refused before the integrator call. Slots left null are simply omitted from the document. The block is object-level (maintainer ruling 2026-10-03): once it binds anything, every row of the owning object is an internet sale - the phrase, the carrier per carrierMode, the ELEKTRONIK sending type - whatever that row's own slot values; an object that sells both in store and online is split into two objects or two fiscalization configurations. Kept deliberately lean per the FiscalPartyConfig doctrine — WHERE the values land on the document is the jurisdiction policy module's concern, not blueprint fields.

FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__paymentMethodProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding how the buyer paid. Carried verbatim onto the document (Turkey: the GIB vocabulary — KREDIKARTI/BANKAKARTI, EFT/HAVALE, KAPIDAODEME, ODEMEARACISI, DIGER).
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__paymentMethodStaticValue.doc: Static payment method — for single-method shops. Used when paymentMethodProperty is unset or resolves to nothing on the row.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__paymentDateProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the payment date (a date property or ISO 8601 text). Written as the Turkey-local cbc:PaymentDueDate; a value that is not an ISO date or instant is refused with a typed fiscal error before the integrator call.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__shipmentCarrierProperty.doc: Legacy: property of the owning object holding the carrier's name. The carrier party is now declared by carrierMode and the carrier* slots; this name still marks the document as an internet sale and serves as the carrier TITLE fallback when no carrierTitle source resolves, but it is never a carrier party on its own - a carrier tax id source is required, because a name-only cac:CarrierParty fails the GIB schema and is not a legal carrier record (VUK 509).
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__shipmentCarrierStaticValue.doc: Legacy: static carrier name for single-carrier shops, used when shipmentCarrierProperty is unset or empty on the row. Like shipmentCarrierProperty it is only the carrier TITLE fallback now: declare the carrier with carrierMode and bind carrierTaxIdStaticValue (or a carrier data object) next to it, otherwise a TR internet-sale configuration is refused (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_UNBOUND).
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__shipmentDateProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the shipment (despatch) date (a date property or ISO 8601 text). Written as cac:Delivery/cac:Despatch/cbc:ActualDespatchDate in Turkey local time; not written with carrierMode noShipment. A value that is not an ISO date or instant is refused with a typed fiscal error before the integrator call.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__websiteStaticValue.doc: The sales website address the document reports (e.g. www.example.com). Static only: the sales channel is a project-level fact, not row data.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierMode.doc: How the goods of an internet sale reach the buyer, which decides the carrier party (cac:CarrierParty) the document names. carrierCompany: a shipping company carries the goods, and its legal title and VKN/TCKN come from the designer's carrier data object (carrierDataObject reached through carrierRefProperty) or, for a single-carrier shop, from carrierTitleStaticValue / carrierTaxIdStaticValue; the tracking number comes from trackingNumberProperty. selfDelivery: the seller delivers with its own vehicle or courier, so the carrier party is the seller's own title, VKN/TCKN and address - the same identity the document names as supplier (VUK 509). noShipment: nothing physical is shipped (a service, a subscription, a digital good), so the document carries no carrier party and no cac:Delivery; declare it only when that is true. The slot has no default (new blocks, including the default project's, leave it empty). Left EMPTY, the block decides (maintainer ruling 2026-10-03): carrierCompany when any shipment slot is bound (a carrier source, the legacy carrier name, shipmentDateProperty or trackingNumberProperty), otherwise noShipment - a digital or service sale - with a design-time WARNING (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_DEFAULTED_NO_SHIPMENT) asking to declare the mode. A TR internet-sale configuration whose carrierMode resolves no carrier is refused at design time (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_UNBOUND, ERROR), and a document whose carrier tax id does not resolve on the row is refused with a typed fiscal error before the integrator call.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierDataObject.doc: The designer's carrier data object - the carrier-company settings, one row per shipping company - the carrier party is read from. It must be a LOCAL data object of the same service. The owning row references one of its rows through carrierRefProperty, and carrierTitleProperty / carrierTaxIdProperty / carrierAddressProperty / carrierDistrictProperty / carrierCityProperty name its columns. OpenAPPL has no carrier system table: this binding IS the carrier settings, and the generated FiscalizationManager reads the referenced row when it builds the document. Read only when carrierMode is carrierCompany, or empty: a bound carrier data object is itself a shipment slot, so an empty carrierMode then reads as carrierCompany. Tenancy: a tenant-level carrier data object (it carries the project's tenant id) is read only within the owning row's tenant - a carrier row of another tenant is treated exactly like a missing row, so the document is refused before the integrator call; a shared carrier object (not tenant-level) is read for every tenant. Under an owning object that has no tenant, a tenant-level carrier object could never be read, so that combination is refused at design time (FISCAL_INTERNET_SALE_CARRIER_TENANT_UNREACHABLE, ERROR): make the carrier object shared, or the owning object tenant-level. A stale build of such a design reads no carrier row and only the carrier static values count.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierRefProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the id of the carrier row (a row of carrierDataObject) that ships this sale. Required with carrierDataObject: the generated FiscalizationManager reads the carrier row by this id, and a row whose reference is empty or points at no carrier row resolves no carrier tax id, which refuses the document before the integrator call unless carrierTaxIdStaticValue backs it.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierTitleProperty.doc: Property of the carrier data object holding the carrier's legal title (unvan), written as the carrier party's name in cac:PartyName (an 11-digit TCKN carrier also gets cac:Person when the title splits into a first and a family name). Falls back to carrierTitleStaticValue, then to the legacy shipmentCarrier name; a carrier whose title resolves nowhere is refused like a missing tax id.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierTaxIdProperty.doc: Property of the carrier data object holding the carrier's tax id - a 10-digit VKN for a company or an 11-digit TCKN for a person. The load-bearing slot: VUK 509 forbids a name-only carrier, so a carrier row whose tax id is empty or not 10/11 digits is refused with a typed fiscal error before the integrator call. Falls back to carrierTaxIdStaticValue.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierAddressProperty.doc: Optional: property of the carrier data object holding the carrier's street address (cbc:StreetName of the carrier party's PostalAddress). Omitted when empty.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierDistrictProperty.doc: Optional: property of the carrier data object holding the carrier's district (ilce, cbc:CitySubdivisionName). When empty the UBL-TR safe default applies ('Merkez'), which keeps the document schema-valid.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierCityProperty.doc: Optional: property of the carrier data object holding the carrier's city (il, cbc:CityName). When empty the UBL-TR safe default applies (the country code), which keeps the document schema-valid.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierTitleStaticValue.doc: Static carrier legal title - for a single-carrier shop that needs no carrier data object. Used when no carrier data object is bound or the bound title column is empty on the carrier row.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__carrierTaxIdStaticValue.doc: Static carrier tax id (10-digit VKN or 11-digit TCKN) - for a single-carrier shop that needs no carrier data object. Used when no carrier data object is bound or the bound tax id column is empty on the carrier row; together with a title source it is a complete carrier source for carrierMode carrierCompany.
FiscalInternetSaleConfig.__trackingNumberProperty.doc: Property of the owning object holding the shipment tracking number the carrier issued, written as cac:Delivery/cbc:TrackingID. Optional on purpose: an invoice issued before the parcel is handed over has no tracking number yet, and the element is then omitted.

__FiscalCarrierMode.doc.#: How the goods of a Turkish internet sale reach the buyer - the choice that decides the carrier party the e-archive document names (VUK 509).
__FiscalCarrierMode.doc.carrierCompany: A shipping company carries the goods: the carrier party is that company's legal title and VKN/TCKN, read from the designer's carrier data object or the carrier static values, with the shipment tracking number. Also the meaning of an empty carrierMode when a shipment slot is bound.
__FiscalCarrierMode.doc.selfDelivery: The seller delivers with its own vehicle or courier: the carrier party is the seller's own title, VKN/TCKN and address.
__FiscalCarrierMode.doc.noShipment: Nothing physical is shipped (a service, a subscription, a digital good): the document carries no carrier party and no cac:Delivery. Also the meaning of an empty carrierMode when no shipment slot is bound (a design-time WARNING asks to declare it).

__FiscalSubmitPolicy.doc.#: Declarative trigger deciding WHEN a fiscal document is prepared and submitted for a fiscalization-enabled DataObject. The designer declares the trigger; codegen wires the dispatcher chain — no imperative glue.
__FiscalSubmitPolicy.doc.onInvoiceFinalized: The fiscal pipeline runs when the object's invoice is finalized — the finalize snapshot (immutable lines plus tax breakdown) is the document source. The default, and the standard commercial flow; requires the invoicing block on the same object.
__FiscalSubmitPolicy.doc.manual: Documents are submitted only through explicit calls (fiscal actions / admin surface). The imperative escape hatch, and the natural mode for reporting-only objects that carry no invoicing block.

__OnFiscalError.doc.#: Enum options for handling a technical failure inside the fiscal pipeline (transport error, provider outage, signing failure). Authority REJECTION is not covered here — a rejected document is a normal state-machine outcome (rejected, correctable and resubmittable), not a pipeline error.
__OnFiscalError.doc.continueRoute: Record the failure on the fiscal document (statusLiteral failed, retryable), log it, and let the surrounding flow proceed. The safer default for commerce flows — a fiscal outage should not block order completion.
__OnFiscalError.doc.throwError: Throw an error and halt the surrounding flow when a fiscal pipeline step fails. For regimes or flows where proceeding without fiscal clearance is not acceptable.

__FiscalLifecycleHook.doc: A designer-authored MScript handler fired by the fiscal dispatcher when the fiscal document state machine advances. Mirrors the InvoiceLifecycleHook shape (name / trigger / condition / script) but carries its OWN trigger vocabulary — the payment PaymentLifecycleTrigger enum is reconciled 1:1 with the payment lifecycle machines and the invoice family's InvoiceLifecycleTrigger is invoice-only; both deliberately stay untouched. Hooks run after the FSM transition is persisted; a failure inside a hook does not roll back the transition. The runtime dispatcher, the normalized resource surface and the per-trigger resource-field checks ship with the fiscal runtime slice.

FiscalLifecycleHook.__name.doc: Unique name of this hook within its parent FiscalizationConfig. Used in logs and the events table.
FiscalLifecycleHook.__trigger.doc: Which fiscal document lifecycle event fires this hook.
FiscalLifecycleHook.__description.doc: Human-readable explanation of what this hook does.
FiscalLifecycleHook.__condition.doc: Optional MScript boolean — when present and falsy, the hook is skipped for this event. Sees the same name as `script`: `fiscalDocument`. `this` is the generated `_hookCtx` whose only key is `fiscalDocument`, so `this.uuid` reads `undefined` (write `fiscalDocument.uuid`), and validation warns on it (LIFECYCLE_HOOK_THIS_NOT_IN_CONTEXT).
FiscalLifecycleHook.__script.doc: MScript body executed when the trigger fires. Runs from the fiscal dispatcher, not from a request - there is no request, session or user in scope. The document is reachable as `fiscalDocument`, a StoredFiscalDocument - the NORMALIZED fiscal document plus its ledger row id, not the raw sys_<X>FiscalDocument row: fiscalDocumentId (the sys_<X>FiscalDocument row id), invoiceId, providerName, network, scheme, documentType, direction, providerDocumentId, uuid (the ETTN), documentSerial, statusLiteral, rawStatus, submittedAt, clearedAt, rejectionReason, artifacts, metadata - and nothing else. The generated file binds it through `any`, so a field that is not on this list compiles and reads `undefined` at every fire. Service library helpers are reachable as `LIB.<module>(...)` and other rows through `API.<apiName>(...)` - the generated hook file does not import the dbLayer getters. Use hooks to fan out to other services (publish kafka events), update related records, or run application-side bookkeeping - e.g. stamping the assigned ETTN (`fiscalDocument.uuid`) back onto a domain record after acceptance. The owning row's id is `fiscalDocument.metadata.sourceObjectId`. On afterFiscalFailed `fiscalDocument.metadata.lastFiscalError` is `{ step, message }` when the engine's pipeline failed (bounded integrator text), and `fiscalDocument.rejectionReason` carries the integrator's text when a poll or webhook reported the failure.
FiscalLifecycleHook.name: String

__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.#: Normalized fiscal document lifecycle events that can fire a FiscalLifecycleHook. The fiscal dispatcher maps state-machine transitions onto these values before invoking hooks, so the same hook definition works regardless of which provider or network carried the document. A SEPARATE vocabulary from PaymentLifecycleTrigger and InvoiceLifecycleTrigger on purpose: those enums are reconciled 1:1 with their own machines and stay untouched.
__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterFiscalSubmitted: Fired when a document is handed to the provider or authority (prepared → submitted). Use for operator notification and correlation bookkeeping; acceptance is NOT implied yet.
__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterFiscalAccepted: Fired when the authority (or the network on its behalf) accepts the document. Use for stamping the fiscal identifiers back onto domain records, unlocking fulfilment, or archiving flows.
__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterFiscalRejected: Fired when the authority rejects the document. Use for operator alerting and correction workflows — a rejected document can be corrected and resubmitted.
__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterFiscalCanceled: Fired when an accepted document is canceled through the provider's cancellation flow (requires the provider's supportsCancellation). Use to reverse downstream effects.
__FiscalLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterFiscalFailed: Fired when a TECHNICAL failure moves the document to failed (draft/prepared/submitted/pending -> failed): an integrator 5xx or transport error, a prepare step that throws, or a failed status the integrator reports on a poll or webhook. Not an authority rejection (that is afterFiscalRejected). Use it to mirror `failed` on the owning row (fiscalDocument.metadata.sourceObjectId) and alert operators - a failed document waits for an operator resubmit. When the engine's own pipeline failed, fiscalDocument.metadata.lastFiscalError is { step, message } (the step that threw and its message; integrator-authored text is bounded); a failed poll / webhook verdict carries the integrator's text on fiscalDocument.rejectionReason instead. Fires once per transition: a resubmit that fails again after re-preparing takes a new failed transition and fires again, while a resubmit that dies before its first transition only refreshes lastFiscalError in place and does not fire.

__LifecycleHook.doc: A designer-authored MScript handler fired by the payment dispatcher when a normalized payment event advances the state machine. Hooks replace the legacy edge-function-driven post-payment plumbing — instead of writing a Kafka edge controller plus an edgeFunction, the designer writes the trigger + script inline. The dispatcher invokes hooks after the FSM transition completes and the state has been persisted; failures inside a hook DO NOT roll back the state transition and DO NOT fail the dispatch — they are logged loudly as PaymentLifecycleHookFailed (hook name, trigger, event id, error) and the event still settles processed, so the hook's effect is operator-reconcilable from the log. An internal API call made from a hook (await API.<name>(...)) that answers a non-2xx now raises a typed ApiError instead of resolving the error envelope as data, so a refused call lands in that same log instead of vanishing.

LifecycleHook.__name.doc: Unique name of this hook within its parent config (CheckoutConfig / SubscriptionConfig / MarketplaceConfig). Used in logs and the events table.
LifecycleHook.__trigger.doc: Which lifecycle event fires this hook. The framework normalizes provider-specific events into the PaymentLifecycleTrigger enum before dispatching. The trigger also fixes which fields `resource` carries in the script/condition (single source: the Normalized* interfaces in the generated `src/common/payment-providers/types.ts`; a read the interface does not declare is rejected at design time — LIFECYCLE_HOOK_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE_FIELD). Each trigger delivers EXACTLY ONE of those interfaces and the generated hook branch casts `resource` to it, so a field belonging to a different trigger's arm does not compile — `orderId` is readable on afterPaymentCaptured and not on afterPaymentRefunded, `providerRefundId` the other way round, `paidAt` on afterInvoicePaid / afterInvoicePaymentFailed and not on the other subscription triggers. Per trigger family: afterPaymentCaptured / afterPaymentFailed / afterPaymentCanceled / afterPaymentStarted / afterPaymentAmountMismatch / afterPaymentCapturedAfterCancel → NormalizedIntent → providerIntentId, providerStatus, statusLiteral, amount, currency, providerSurcharge, customerId, paymentMethodId, description, orderId, metadata, failureReason, settlementItems, nextAction; afterPaymentRefunded / afterRefundFailed → NormalizedRefund → providerRefundId, providerIntentId, statusLiteral, amount, currency, reason, failureReason, metadata; afterDisputeOpened / afterPaymentDisputed / afterDisputeEvidenceRequired / afterDisputeWon / afterDisputeLost → NormalizedDispute → providerDisputeId, providerIntentId, amount, currency, reason, statusLiteral, evidenceDueBy, evidenceSubmittedAt, outcome; afterSubscriptionCreated / afterSubscriptionRenewed / afterSubscriptionPaymentFailed / afterSubscriptionPastDue / afterSubscriptionCanceled → NormalizedSubscription → providerSubscriptionId, customerId, planId, statusLiteral, failureReason, currentPeriodStart, currentPeriodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, trialEnd, canceledAt, metadata, nextAction; afterInvoicePaid / afterInvoicePaymentFailed → NormalizedInvoice → providerInvoiceId, subscriptionId, amount, currency, statusLiteral, failureReason, billingReason, periodStart, periodEnd, paidAt, hostedInvoiceUrl, requiresAction; afterPayoutPaid / afterPayoutFailed / afterPayoutHeld → NormalizedPayout → providerPayoutId, destinationAccountId, amount, currency, statusLiteral, scheduledFor, arrivedAt, failureReason, transferGroup; afterKycUpdated → NormalizedConnectedAccount → providerAccountId, kycStatus, payoutEnabled, country, email, businessName, metadata. The normalized resource never has an `id` field: the provider-side id is the `provider…Id` member, and the stored row's own id is on the loaded row (`payment.id` / `subscription.id` / `payout.id`). The trigger must belong to the family of the hook list it sits in - CheckoutConfig: the payment, refund and dispute triggers; SubscriptionConfig: the subscription and invoice triggers; MarketplaceConfig: the payout triggers and afterKycUpdated - because no other lifecycle ever receives that event: a payout trigger in a checkout hook list would never fire and its `resource` would be typed for the payment machine, so it is rejected at design time (LIFECYCLE_HOOK_TRIGGER_WRONG_FAMILY).
LifecycleHook.__description.doc: Human-readable explanation of what this hook does.
LifecycleHook.__script.doc:
MScript executed when the trigger fires. Like every MScript it is ONE expression, not a statement list: to run two calls in sequence, wrap them in an inline async IIFE - `(async () => { await API.reserveSeats({ bookingId: resource.orderId }); await API.issueReceipt({ bookingId: resource.orderId }); })()`. A bare `a; b` sequence is refused at validation (INVALID_MSCRIPT_SYNTAX): the generated handler wraps the script in parentheses, where it cannot compile. The script is placed inside the generated lifecycle handler, so the names below are plain bare identifiers: write `payment.id`, not `this.payment.id`. Every trigger gets the normalized event payload (`event`) and the normalized resource that event carries (`resource`) — provider ids and amounts live on the RESOURCE (`resource.providerIntentId`), not on the event. The row this service loaded is named for WHICH row it is, and that depends on the owning config: checkout triggers (payment, refund and dispute) get `payment`, the sys_<X>Payment ticket, with `order` kept as a deprecated alias of it; subscription triggers get `subscription`; marketplace triggers get `payout`. On a dispute trigger the sys_<X>Dispute row is reached as `this.dispute`, because the same checkout hook list is also emitted into the payment handler where that name does not exist. A row can be null (an `account.*` payout event, a dispute on an intent this service does not own), so guard it. `resource.metadata` values are `unknown`: a value is whatever the provider or the framework stored there, not necessarily a string. A read below `resource.metadata` compiles (`resource.metadata.lateCapture.orderId`, `resource.metadata?.amountMismatch?.expected`): the nodejs hook types `metadata` as `Record<string, any>`, and the java and dotnet hooks read members dynamically; a missing level reads null / undefined, so guard it. Nothing checks a value's type, so narrow a metadata value before passing it on, with `typeof x === 'string'` or `String(x)`: a truthiness guard does not make it a string. Write `typeof resource.metadata?.bookingId === 'string' && f(resource.metadata.bookingId)` or `f(String(resource.metadata?.bookingId ?? ''))`, not `resource.metadata?.bookingId && f(resource.metadata.bookingId)`. There is no request, session or user: a hook runs from a provider webhook, not from a call. Service library helpers are reached as `LIB.<module>(...)`, other rows through the generated dbLayer getters. Same-service Business APIs that declare `internalCallSettings.hasInternalCallController` are reached as `await API.<apiName>({ ...params })` — awaitable, runs the API's full manager pipeline asSystem, and resolves to the API's response resource. On nodejs, java and dotnet the optional second argument `API.<apiName>(params, { session: this.session })` carries a session explicitly when the hook has one and wants the caller's tenant (required for ledger APIs on a tenant-scoped owner object). Provider webhook hooks have no caller session and keep their explicit-param calls. Omitting the argument leaves the session null, with no inheritance through AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager; language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature; only internal-controller APIs are members of `API`, and the called API's own hooks may run but cannot make further `API.*` calls (depth is limited to one). Use hooks to fan out to other services (publish kafka events), invoke internal APIs, update related records, or run application-side bookkeeping.

The design-time checks over this script — unknown `resource` field, undefined `this.<X>`, unbound `API.<apiName>`, `LIB.<module>` existence, and the case-mismatch report — are STATIC and read the syntax you wrote. A field read on `event` or `resource` is seen as a direct member (`resource.x`, `resource?.x`, `this.resource.x`), a string-literal key (`resource['x']`), a key destructured off the root (`const { x } = resource`, also as an inline IIFE parameter pattern) and through ONE alias level (`const r = resource`, `((r) => r.x)(resource)`); each keeps the tier of the root it came from (bare = build break, ERROR; through `this.` = silent `undefined`, WARNING). A field another hook assigns onto the shared context excuses a read only when that hook runs in the SAME fire and comes EARLIER in the list: the same trigger, or the dispute alias pair `afterDisputeOpened` / `afterPaymentDisputed`, which both fire on `dispute.opened` over one context. Hooks of one fire run in list order; any other trigger fires on a different event and never shares the context. The checks are still blind to anything whose name is not literally in the source: a computed member (`this[key]`, `API[name]`, `LIB.mod[fn]`), a name reached through a spread or rest element (`{ ...payment }`), a key built at runtime, a `let` alias, an alias of an alias, a root renamed while destructuring `this` (`const { resource: r } = this`), a `this` rebound by a nested non-arrow `function`, and a root handed to any function other than an inline IIFE. Names are resolved by scope: a parameter or local that reuses the root's or an alias's name is that local, not the root. Lexical identity is respected in parameter defaults, switch discriminants, named classes and static blocks; this is not general dataflow analysis. Silence on such a read means NOT CHECKED, not checked-and-clean — and a TypeScript-annotated body skips the AST passes altogether. Spell member reads out literally if you want the checker to see them.
LifecycleHook.__condition.doc: Optional MScript boolean — when present and falsy, the hook is skipped for this event. Use this for fine-grained filtering (e.g. only fire on certain amounts or certain payment methods). It sees the same names as `script` (`event`, `resource`, and the row names of the owning config), bare. `this` is the generated `_hookCtx` context object, NOT the row: `this.amount` reads `undefined`, so the condition is falsy and the hook never runs - write `resource.amount > 0`. Validation warns on a `this.<name>` that is not a context key of the machine the trigger runs in and that no hook of the config assigns (LIFECYCLE_HOOK_THIS_NOT_IN_CONTEXT).
LifecycleHook.name: String

__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.#: Normalized lifecycle events that can fire a LifecycleHook. The dispatcher maps each provider's native event taxonomy onto these values before invoking hooks, so the same hook definition works regardless of which provider emitted the event. Every member is mapped by exactly one lifecycle machine — a hook authored on any of these values executes (this enum was reconciled with the machine templates in both directions; the retired afterAnyStatusChange catch-all, which no machine ever mapped, is gone — author one hook per specific trigger instead).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentCaptured: Fired when a one-time payment transitions to the captured state. Use for fulfillment, receipt emission, post-payment record creation. Idempotent: may fire more than once for the same payment if the provider retries its webhook — hooks should be safe under replay.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentFailed: Fired when a payment fails terminally. Use for cleanup, notification, retry scheduling.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentCanceled: Fired when a one-time payment intent is CANCELED before it was captured: the normalized `payment.canceled` event (stripe `payment_intent.canceled`, iyzico CANCEL, adyen CANCELLATION / CANCEL_OR_REFUND / EXPIRE, and the other adapters that report a voided or expired intent) moved the sys_<X>Payment ticket to its terminal `canceled` status. The hook runs only when the ticket IS `canceled` after the transition, so a late cancel report for an intent that was already captured (which the state machine ignores) does not fire it; a redelivered cancel of an already-canceled ticket does, so the hook must be safe under replay. `resource` is a NormalizedIntent, exactly as on afterPaymentCaptured / afterPaymentFailed. Use it to release reserved stock, reopen the order, or notify the buyer.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentRefunded: Fired when a refund is captured against a prior payment. Use to reverse fulfillment or update bookkeeping.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterRefundFailed: Fired when a refund of this service's payment FAILS: the normalized `refund.failed` event, from the provider's webhook or from a RefundAction / refund route the provider answered `failed` at once. `resource` is the NormalizedRefund (providerRefundId, providerIntentId, statusLiteral, amount, currency, reason, failureReason, metadata) and `payment` the sys_<X>Payment ticket. `reversal` (a boolean, bare in the script and the condition, or `this.reversal`) is true when the failed refund had already SUCCEEDED: the provider reported it `succeeded` and later `failed` (Stripe), the refund was reversed and the money is back with the merchant. The framework has then undone the refund's own effects (the refund row reads `failed`, the ticket is back at its earlier status, a settlement clawback is reversed), but `afterPaymentRefunded` already ran for it: undo what that hook did here (re-open fulfilment, correct a credited wallet, tell the buyer). `reversal` is false for a refund that failed without having succeeded, which changed nothing. It runs once per refund failure; a replayed failure report does not run it again. Generated for the nodejs, java and dotnet targets; the python, rust and golang targets do not fire it yet (validation warns PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_TRIGGER_NODEJS_ONLY there).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentStarted: Fired when a start records a NEW payment intent on the order's sys_<X>Payment ticket: the generated start route (`/v1/start<x>payment/:orderId`) and an in-workflow PaymentAction with stage start or simple, which share one recording seam. It runs AFTER the ticket is written and BEFORE the synchronous capture lifecycle of the same start, so a design that mirrors the payment state onto its order sees the start first and then afterPaymentCaptured / afterPaymentFailed. It runs once per new intent: a start that resumes the order's still-open intent (the answer carries `pendingIntentReused: true`, e.g. a 3-D Secure challenge or an iyzico hosted form the buyer has not finished) creates nothing and does not fire it, and a declined charge records no intent and does not fire it. FRAMEWORK NOTICE, not provider-emitted: `event.eventType` is `payment.started`, `event.providerEventId` is `framework:payment.started:<providerIntentId>`, `event.rawPayload` is `{ source, orderId }`. `resource` is the created NormalizedIntent with `resource.orderId` set to the ticket's order (`resource.statusLiteral` is the provider's answer, e.g. started / requires_action / success); `payment` is the ticket row as written. A hook failure is logged `PaymentLifecycleHookFailed` and never fails the start. Generated for the nodejs, dotnet, java and python targets (python fires the notice, but like every python payment hook its script is not lowered yet: validation warns PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_NOT_LOWERED on an authored script or condition); the rust and golang targets do not fire it yet (validation warns PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_TRIGGER_NODEJS_ONLY there).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentAmountMismatch: Fired when a capture report is REFUSED by the capture amount gate and the sys_<X>Payment ticket is written `amount_mismatch`: the amount, currency or order the provider reports does not match what the framework charged for the order. Every path that writes that state fires it: the provider webhook, the start / complete / refresh routes and an in-workflow PaymentAction, the hosted Checkout Form return (and its webhook) and the 3-D Secure return. It runs once, on the write that moved the ticket into review; a replayed webhook, a second return or any later report for a ticket already `amount_mismatch` does not fire it again. No success lifecycle runs for the refused capture (no afterPaymentCaptured, no invoice, no settlement). FRAMEWORK NOTICE, not provider-emitted: `event.eventType` is `payment.amount_mismatch`, `event.providerEventId` is `framework:payment.amount_mismatch:<providerIntentId>`, `event.rawPayload` is `{ source, orderId }`. `resource` is the reported NormalizedIntent with `resource.orderId` set to the TICKET's order (never the provider's claim) and `resource.metadata.amountMismatch` = the record written on the ticket (`payment.metadata.amountMismatch`: expected and reported amount / currency / order, the source, the time). Use it to mark the order as under review ("payment received, amount under review, do not retry") and notify an operator; an operator resolves the payment. A hook failure is logged `PaymentLifecycleHookFailed` and never changes the review state. Generated for the nodejs, dotnet and java targets; the python, rust and golang targets do not fire it yet (validation warns PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_TRIGGER_NODEJS_ONLY there).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentCapturedAfterCancel: Fired when a CAPTURE is recorded on a payment the order no longer expected: a payment a start of the order left behind (a retired iyzico hosted Checkout Form, or a 3-D Secure step a new attempt superseded) that the buyer paid after all, or the payment a `canceled` sys_<X>Payment ticket records. Every path that records such a capture fires it, once per recorded capture, right after the write that recorded it: the hosted Checkout Form return and its webhook, the 3-D Secure return, the complete / refresh routes (and the provider review sweeper, which refreshes), an in-workflow PaymentAction, the callback seam, the provider webhook through the intent machine, and the retired-form expiry backstop (one detail read of each retired hosted form after its token life, run by the review sweeper). It fires from the write, never from a scan of the ticket, so two late captures recorded at the same moment run it twice, and one capture arriving by two paths at once runs it once (the listing write is a compare-and-set). FRAMEWORK NOTICE, not provider-emitted: `event.eventType` is `payment.captured_after_cancel`, `event.providerEventId` is `framework:payment.captured_after_cancel:<paymentId>`, `event.rawPayload` is `{ source, orderId, ticketId }`. `resource` is the CAPTURED payment as a NormalizedIntent (`providerIntentId` its id, which may differ from the payment the ticket names; `statusLiteral` success; `amount`, `currency`, `orderId`) and `resource.metadata.lateCapture` is the notice: `case` (`capturedAfterCancel`: the order was not paid and the ticket moved to the `captured_after_cancel` review; `paidTwice`: the order already held a capture and this one is listed under `payment.metadata.retiredAttemptCaptures`, the one to refund; `pending`: listed beside an attempt of the order still being charged or decided (a start claim, or an attempt the provider holds for its review: the order is not known unpaid, so the ticket is not moved); when that attempt is decided, by whichever writer lands the decision, the hook runs ONCE more for the same capture with `resolves: 'pending'` and the decided case, `paidTwice` (the entry gains `orderPaidTwice: true`) or `capturedAfterCancel` (the ticket moved into the review); a listing never decided gets no follow-up), `origin` (`retiredAttempt` or `canceledPayment`), `orderId`, `ticketId`, `providerName`, `paymentId`, `ticketPaymentId`, `ticketStatus`, `amount`, `currency`, `amountMatches`, `providerStatus`, `capturedAt` (when this service recorded the capture, not the provider's payment time) and `source`. `payment` is the order's ticket the capture was recorded on. It runs no capture lifecycle (no afterPaymentCaptured, no invoice, no settlement accrual), never moves the order and refunds nothing: bind it to a notification or an operator task, and refund or fulfil by hand. A hook failure is logged `PaymentLifecycleHookFailed` and never changes the review. Generated for the nodejs target; the dotnet, java, python, rust and golang targets do not fire it yet (validation warns PAYMENT_LIFECYCLE_TRIGGER_NODEJS_ONLY there).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPaymentDisputed: Fired when a chargeback / dispute is opened against a one-time payment — the checkout-perspective alias of afterDisputeOpened (both fire on the same normalized dispute-opened event, handled by the dispute machine). Use for notification + evidence preparation.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterSubscriptionCreated: Fired when a new subscription is created. Creation is not payment: on Stripe a subscription whose first payment still needs 3-D Secure fires it while it reads `past_due`; grant a plan on afterInvoicePaid / afterSubscriptionRenewed or a `statusLiteral` of `active`.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterSubscriptionRenewed: Fired when a subscription's billing period rolls over and the next invoice is paid. Use for entitlement extension, receipt emission.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterSubscriptionPaymentFailed: Fired when a renewal charge attempt on a subscription fails. Use for retry messaging, grace-period handling.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterSubscriptionCanceled: Fired when a subscription reaches a terminal state. This is BOTH terminal events: `subscription.canceled` (canceled immediately or at period end) and `subscription.expired` (provider-reported natural end or final non-payment). Hook it for entitlement revocation and you cover every way a subscription ends.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterSubscriptionPastDue: Fired when the provider reports the subscription as past due (delinquent after failed renewal attempts). Use for dunning, notification.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoicePaid: Fired when a subscription invoice is paid. Use for receipt emission, entitlement bookkeeping.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterInvoicePaymentFailed: Fired when the provider reports a subscription INVOICE whose payment failed (the normalized `invoice.payment_failed` event; the stripe and iyzico adapters produce it, while paypal, paddle and lemonsqueezy report a failed renewal only at the subscription level, so on those brands use afterSubscriptionPaymentFailed / afterSubscriptionPastDue). The subscription machine moves an `active` row to `past_due` on the same event, and this hook runs after that write. `resource` is a NormalizedInvoice (providerInvoiceId, subscriptionId, amount, currency, statusLiteral, failureReason, billingReason, periodStart, periodEnd, paidAt, hostedInvoiceUrl, requiresAction), NOT a NormalizedSubscription: `resource.providerSubscriptionId` is rejected at design time, the parent id is `resource.subscriptionId` and the stored row is `subscription`. Use for invoice-level dunning (which invoice, for how much). It is not a second name for afterSubscriptionPaymentFailed, which fires on the SUBSCRIPTION-level failure report (`subscription.payment_failed`) and never on this event; a provider that sends both reports fires both hooks, once each. On Stripe it also fires for `invoice.payment_action_required`, a payment that waits on the BUYER (3-D Secure on a renewal): that report carries `resource.requiresAction: true` and `resource.hostedInvoiceUrl` (the Stripe page where the buyer authenticates); send the buyer that link from this report. Stripe may report the same attempt as `invoice.payment_failed` too, so the hook can run twice for one invoice; key a notification on `resource.providerInvoiceId`.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterDisputeOpened: Fired when a chargeback / dispute is opened against a payment. Use for notification + evidence preparation.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterDisputeEvidenceRequired: Fired when the provider requests evidence for an open dispute. Use to alert operators ahead of the evidenceDueBy deadline.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterDisputeWon: Fired when a dispute resolves in the merchant's favor.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterDisputeLost: Fired when a dispute resolves against the merchant — funds are returned to the cardholder.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPayoutPaid: Fired when a marketplace payout to a connected account completes successfully.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPayoutFailed: Fired when a marketplace payout fails (e.g. bank rejection).
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterPayoutHeld: Fired when the invoice gate (marketplace payoutGate) parks a payout as `held` — the matching inbound fiscal invoice is missing or mismatches. GATE-INTERNAL, not provider-emitted: the generated payout gate synthesizes the payout.held event. The held row's metadata carries the typed reason (awaiting_inbound_invoice / seller_tax_id_unbound / amount_mismatch / currency_mismatch). Use for operator notification.
__PaymentLifecycleTrigger.doc.afterKycUpdated: Fired when a connected account's KYC / verification status changes. Use to gate payouts or prompt re-verification.

__IdempotencyStrategy.doc.#: How idempotency keys are generated for retryable provider calls.
__IdempotencyStrategy.doc.framework: Framework generates a UUIDv4 per intent and stamps it onto the provider call. Simpler and more portable across providers.
__IdempotencyStrategy.doc.adapter: Adapter uses the provider's native idempotency mechanism (e.g. Stripe's Idempotency-Key header with a provider-derived value).

__AfterPaymentEmitMode.doc.#: Defines record emission strategy for AfterPaymentCreation.
__AfterPaymentEmitMode.doc.perOrder: Create a single record for the full order.
__AfterPaymentEmitMode.doc.perOrderItem: Create one record for each order item.
__AfterPaymentEmitMode.doc.perOrderItemQuantity: Create multiple records per order item using checkout.orderItemRelation.quantityProperty.

__ShoppingCartConfig.doc: Shopping cart configuration chapter. When enabled, auto-generates the Cart and CartItem DataObjects (plus the Campaign store when promotionSettings.dynamicPromotions is enabled) with Redis-first architecture for hyper-scalable cart management. No Coupon or CampaignUsageLog object is ever generated: a coupon is the couponCode column of a campaign row.

ShoppingCartConfig.__basicSettings.doc: Core cart settings including activation, naming, currency, and guest cart support. The useShoppingCartFeature flag activates the entire shopping cart functionality.
ShoppingCartConfig.__pricingSettings.doc: Price calculation settings including VAT handling, rounding, discounts, shipment, and extra charges.
ShoppingCartConfig.__itemSettings.doc: Cart item configuration including what item properties to generate.
ShoppingCartConfig.__productCatalogSettings.doc: Optional product catalog integration for automatic item population when adding products.
ShoppingCartConfig.__reservationSettings.doc: Opt-in TTL stock reservation. When enabled on a catalog-bound cart with a stock mapping, adding a line reserves units against a Redis capacity counter seeded from the catalogue row; holds expire on their own short TTL, are released on remove/clear, and are consumed inside the claimed checkout window.
ShoppingCartConfig.__logisticsSettings.doc: Shipping logistics settings for weight, dimensions, and volume tracking.
ShoppingCartConfig.__loyaltySettings.doc: Loyalty program settings for points earning and redemption.
ShoppingCartConfig.__promotionSettings.doc: Promotion engine configuration including static and dynamic promotions.
ShoppingCartConfig.__redisSettings.doc: Redis caching configuration for hyper-scalable cart management.
ShoppingCartConfig.__checkoutSettings.doc: Checkout settings for cart-to-order conversion. Configures how checkout creates orders, property mappings, and event publishing.

__ShoppingCartBasicSettings.doc: Core shopping cart settings with activation flag. When useShoppingCartFeature is true, the Cart and CartItem DataObjects are auto-generated.

ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__useShoppingCartFeature.doc: Enables shopping cart functionality for this service. When true, auto-generates Cart and CartItem DataObjects with all pricing, status, and calculation properties. In a multi-tenant project the two generated objects are tenant-level (objectDataIsInTenantLevel true, with the injected <tenantName>Id column): every cart and cart line row, and a local-mode order written into a tenant-level order object, carries the tenant of the request that created it, and a designer read api over them runs the tenant filter, so a tenant administrator reads its own tenant's carts only. This is decided when the code is generated, from the project's tenancy (nodejs today, the other languages follow their port); a single-tenant project is unchanged, and the Campaign store always stays platform-level.
ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__cartObjectName.doc: Name for the auto-generated Cart DataObject (e.g., 'cart', 'shoppingCart'). Related objects are named based on this: {name}Item, {name}Campaign, etc.
ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__currency.doc: The currency code for this cart (e.g., USD, EUR, TRY). All monetary calculations use this currency.
ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__supportGuestCart.doc: Whether to support anonymous/guest carts before user login. Adds sessionId property for session binding. An anonymous shopper IS its session id (the X-Session-Id header), and the guest-to-login transition is ROTATION, NOT ADOPTION: the active-cart pointer is owner-sliced (user:{userId} wins over session:{sessionId} the moment the session carries a userId), so logging in moves the shopper to a different owner slot and they start from 'no cart'. The guest basket is neither merged nor adopted - it stays intact under its session slot until the cart TTL expires, and dropping back to the same session id finds it again. Cart adoption/merge on login is a possible FUTURE feature, not configurable behavior.
ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__supportNotes.doc: Whether to include a notes field for customer special instructions.
ShoppingCartBasicSettings.__supportMetadata.doc: Whether to include a metadata JSON field for custom extensibility.

__CartStatus.doc.#: Fixed status values for shopping cart lifecycle. These values are used by the system and should not be customized.
__CartStatus.doc.active: Cart is in active use. The user is adding/modifying items.
__CartStatus.doc.churning: Reserved lifecycle value. No framework automation writes it: the inactivity period settings that once described it were retired and cart lifecycle automation is a postponed feature. A project worker may write it by hand through the cart object's CRUD API.
__CartStatus.doc.abandoned: Written by an explicit cart delete: deleteCart stamps the DB row abandoned while removing the live Redis cart. No inactivity automation writes it (the period settings were retired).
__CartStatus.doc.checkedOut: Cart has been successfully checked out. Order creation process has started.
__CartStatus.doc.convertedToOrder: Cart has been fully converted to an order. The order record now exists.

__AutoGeneratedCartDataObject.doc.#: Documentation for the auto-generated Cart DataObject. Created based on ShoppingCartBasicSettings and feature flags.

properties.userId: ID - Owner's user ID (nullable for guest carts)
properties.status: CartStatus - Cart lifecycle status (active, churning, abandoned, checkedOut, convertedToOrder)
properties.lastActivityAt: DateTime - Timestamp of last cart activity, used for churning/abandonment detection
properties.linesCount: Integer - Number of distinct line items
properties.itemsCount: Integer - Total quantity of all items
properties.appliedCampaignIds: Array - Applied campaign IDs (if promotions enabled)
properties.earnedPoints: Integer - Loyalty points earned (if loyalty enabled)
properties.pointsValue: Double - Monetary value of redeemed points (if loyalty enabled)

__ShoppingCartPricingSettings.doc: Price calculation settings. Controls VAT handling, rounding, and which charge types are supported.

ShoppingCartPricingSettings.__catalogPricesIncludeVat.doc: Whether product prices include VAT. When true the engine prices GROSS-FIRST: the customer-facing line total is unitPrice x quantity exactly (a 250-inclusive item twice is 500.00, never 499.99), any line discount is taken off that gross, and the ex-VAT/VAT split is DERIVED from the discounted gross with the same rounding-exact extraction the invoice layer uses. When false, prices are ex-VAT and VAT is added on top.
ShoppingCartPricingSettings.__defaultVatRate.doc: Default VAT rate when an item doesn't specify its own. UNIT CONTRACT: this knob speaks PERCENT, like every public vatRate boundary - write 18 for 18% VAT. The cart engine converts it to its internal fraction exactly once, at ingress: any value >= 1 is a percent and is divided by 100; any value below 1 is accepted as a legacy FRACTION and passes through unchanged (0.18 also means 18%), so existing fraction-speaking projects keep computing identical totals. BE LOUD ABOUT THE BOUNDARY: a bare 1 means ONE PERCENT (0.01), never 100% - author 1% VAT as 1; and a sub-1% rate has no percent spelling, author it as a fraction (0.005 = 0.5%).
ShoppingCartPricingSettings.__roundingStrategy.doc: When to round monetary values: perLine (recommended), perItem, or atTotal.

__RoundingStrategy.doc.#: Defines when monetary rounding is applied during price calculations.
__RoundingStrategy.doc.perLine: Round each line total after calculating (quantity × unit price). Recommended for most cases.
__RoundingStrategy.doc.perItem: Round each item's unit price before multiplication. May cause small discrepancies in line totals.
__RoundingStrategy.doc.atTotal: Only round the final grand total. Keeps maximum precision but may show odd line totals.

CartDiscountConfig.__supportType.doc: What level of discounts are supported: none, cartLevel, itemLevel, or bothLevels.
CartDiscountConfig.__allocationMode.doc: How cart-level discounts are allocated to items: proportional, byQuantity, lastItem, or customRule.

__DiscountSupportType.doc.#: Defines what types of discounts the cart supports.
__DiscountSupportType.doc.cartLevel: Only cart-level discounts (applied to entire cart, then allocated to items).
__DiscountSupportType.doc.itemLevel: Only item-level discounts (applied directly to individual items).
__DiscountSupportType.doc.bothLevels: Both cart-level and item-level discounts supported.

__DiscountAllocationMode.doc.#: Defines how cart-level discounts are allocated to individual items for accounting and tax purposes.
__DiscountAllocationMode.doc.proportional: Allocate discount proportionally based on each item's contribution to subtotal.
__DiscountAllocationMode.doc.byQuantity: Allocate discount equally per item quantity.
__DiscountAllocationMode.doc.lastItem: Apply entire discount to the last item (simplest, least accurate).
__DiscountAllocationMode.doc.customRule: Use custom allocation logic defined in event handler.

CartShipmentConfig.__supportShipment.doc: Whether the cart supports shipment charges.
CartShipmentConfig.__defaultShipmentVatRate.doc: Default VAT rate for shipping (may differ from product VAT). Uses defaultVatRate if not specified. Same unit contract as defaultVatRate: PERCENT (18 = 18%), with values below 1 read as legacy fractions.

__CartExtraChargeConfig.doc: Configuration for additional charges like handling, packaging, insurance, etc.

CartExtraChargeConfig.__supportExtraCharges.doc: Whether the cart supports extra charges beyond shipment.
CartExtraChargeConfig.__storeBreakdown.doc: Whether to store breakdown of individual extra charges as JSON array.

__ShoppingCartItemSettings.doc: Configuration for cart line items. The CartItem DataObject is auto-generated based on these settings.

ShoppingCartItemSettings.__itemObjectSuffix.doc: Suffix for the auto-generated CartItem DataObject name (default: 'Item'). E.g., 'cart' + 'Item' = 'cartItem'.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportCategory.doc: Whether items track category for filtering and promotions.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportBrand.doc: Whether items track brand for filtering and promotions.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportProductGroup.doc: Whether items track product group ID for variant grouping in promotions.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportVendor.doc: Whether items track vendor/supplier for marketplace scenarios.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportGiftItems.doc: Whether items can be marked as promotional gifts.
ShoppingCartItemSettings.__supportItemMetadata.doc: Whether items have a metadata JSON field for custom data.

__AutoGeneratedCartItemDataObject.doc.#: Documentation for the auto-generated CartItem DataObject. Created based on ShoppingCartItemSettings and pricing settings.

properties.cartId: ID - Foreign key to parent Cart
properties.productId: ID - Product reference (if using product catalog)
properties.name: String - Item display name
