properties.vatRate: Double - VAT rate for this item
properties.earnedPoints: Integer - Points from this item (if loyalty enabled)
properties.bonusPoints: Integer - Bonus points allocated (if loyalty enabled)

__ShoppingCartProductCatalogSettings.doc: Optional product catalog integration. When enabled, adding a product by ID/barcode resolves the line against the bound product DataObject and the SERVER becomes authoritative for the money fields AND for every promotion qualifier: unitPrice and vatRate, and productId, category, brand, productGroup and vendor (read through productMappings), always come from the catalog row - a client-sent value is ignored, never trusted, and when the catalog row has no value for one of these fields the client value is dropped, not kept, so a client cannot move a line into a discounted category, brand or product group. The display-only fields productName and description fill only when the client left them blank, and a product the catalog does not hold is refused with a typed 404 CART_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND. The binding is PRICING-ONLY: it does not read, reserve, or verify stock/capacity - a scarce-stock deployment must enforce capacity in its own purchase/checkout flow (atomic conditional update, e.g. soldCount + qty <= capacity); see docs/ADR-shopping-cart-capacity-reservation.md. LANGUAGE NOTE: the qualifier authority is implemented by the nodejs target; the dotnet catalog resolve still overrides only unitPrice/vatRate (when the row carries them) and fills productName/description, and keeps client-sent qualifier fields (port pending).

ShoppingCartProductCatalogSettings.__useProductCatalog.doc: Whether to integrate with a product DataObject for automatic item population. When true the cart's add/update-item routes price from the catalog (server-authoritative): unitPrice is no longer required from the client, a client-sent unitPrice/vatRate is overridden by the catalog values, and an unknown lookup value answers 404 CART_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND. When false, pricing stays client-supplied under the strict ingress guard.
ShoppingCartProductCatalogSettings.__productDataObject.doc: The product catalog DataObject to fetch product details from. Required when useProductCatalog is true; ignored while the catalog integration is off.
ShoppingCartProductCatalogSettings.__lookupField.doc: Field to use for product lookup: 'id' or 'barcode'.
ShoppingCartProductCatalogSettings.__productMappings.doc: Which product fields to map to cart items. Configure only if your product uses non-standard property names.

__ProductLookupField.doc.#: Field used to look up products when adding to cart.

__ProductFieldMappings.doc: Maps product DataObject property names to expected names. Only configure if your product uses non-standard names. All fields are optional - only specify overrides.

ProductFieldMappings.__vatRateField.doc: Product property for VAT rate (default: 'vatRate'). The column speaks PERCENT (18 = 18%), per the platform-wide vatRate unit contract; the cart engine normalizes the resolved value once at ingress, with values below 1 read as legacy fractions. A bare 1 means 1 percent, never 100%.
ProductFieldMappings.__stockField.doc: OPT-IN stock mapping: product property holding the directly available stock (units that may still be reserved). No default - leaving it unset means the catalogue exposes no stock and the cart cannot reserve. Mutually exclusive with capacityField; the mapped column is only ever read to SEED and RECONCILE the Redis capacity counter, never per-request (and never through the DB cart mirror).
ProductFieldMappings.__capacityField.doc: OPT-IN stock mapping: product property holding the TOTAL capacity (availability is capacity minus soldCountField, or capacity alone when no soldCountField is mapped). No default. Mutually exclusive with stockField. Read only to seed/reconcile the Redis capacity counter.
ProductFieldMappings.__soldCountField.doc: OPT-IN stock mapping: product property counting units already sold; only meaningful together with capacityField (availability = capacity - soldCount). No default.

__ShoppingCartReservationSettings.doc: Opt-in TTL stock reservation. Requires productCatalogSettings.useProductCatalog plus exactly one stock mapping (productMappings.stockField or capacityField). Adding a line atomically reserves its units against a per-product Redis capacity counter seeded from the catalogue row; the counter is the ONLY runtime availability authority (the DB cart mirror is never consulted), holds expire on ttlSeconds (guestTtlSeconds for session-owned carts), are released on remove/clear/expiry, consumed inside the claimed checkout window, and restored by a compensating release when order creation definitively fails. A shortfall is the typed 409 CART_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED naming the short lines.

ShoppingCartReservationSettings.__enabled.doc: Turns TTL stock reservation on for this cart. Off by default; when off nothing about the emitted service changes.
ShoppingCartReservationSettings.__ttlSeconds.doc: Reservation hold TTL in seconds for authenticated (user-owned) carts. Deliberately decoupled from redisSettings.cartTtlSeconds and MUCH shorter (minutes, not hours): an abandoned basket must not starve stock for the cart's whole lifetime.
ShoppingCartReservationSettings.__guestTtlSeconds.doc: Reservation hold TTL in seconds for guest (session-owned) carts - the SHORT anti-hoarding hold. Should not exceed ttlSeconds.
ShoppingCartReservationSettings.__guestQuota.doc: Per-session hold quota for guest carts - the second half of the anti-hoarding defense (a rotating session can still multiply holds, but each rotation is bounded and short-lived).
ShoppingCartReservationSettings.__reconcileIntervalSeconds.doc: How long a seeded counter is trusted before it is lazily re-seeded (reconciled) from the catalogue row on the next reservation touch. The reconcile re-reads the row's stock mapping and resets the counter's consumed tally - the row is the durable truth the counter re-anchors to.

__CartGuestHoldQuota.doc: Bounds on the reservation holds one guest session may accumulate. Applied only to session-owned carts; authenticated carts are not quota'd here.

CartGuestHoldQuota.__maxLines.doc: Maximum distinct reserved lines (products) per guest session.
CartGuestHoldQuota.__maxUnits.doc: Maximum total reserved units (sum of quantities) per guest session.

__ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.doc: Configuration for shipping logistics. When enabled, adds weight/dimension properties to Cart and CartItem.

ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.__supportLogistics.doc: Whether to track logistics data (weight, dimensions, volume) for shipping calculations.
ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.__supportDimensions.doc: Whether to track length, width, height in addition to weight.
ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.__supportVolume.doc: Whether to auto-calculate and store volume.
ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.__supportDimensionalWeight.doc: Whether to calculate dimensional weight for shipping carriers.
ShoppingCartLogisticsSettings.__dimFactor.doc: Dimensional weight factor (default: 5000 for cm/kg, 139 for in/lb).

__ShoppingCartLoyaltySettings.doc: Loyalty program configuration. When enabled, adds points properties to Cart and CartItem.

ShoppingCartLoyaltySettings.__supportLoyalty.doc: Whether to enable loyalty points functionality.
ShoppingCartLoyaltySettings.__supportPointsRedemption.doc: Whether customers can redeem points for discounts.
ShoppingCartLoyaltySettings.__pointsToMoneyRate.doc: How many points equal 1 currency unit (e.g., 100 points = $1).
ShoppingCartLoyaltySettings.__pointsAllocationMode.doc: How cart-level bonus points are allocated to items.

__PointsAllocationMode.doc.#: Defines how cart-level bonus points are allocated to individual items.
__PointsAllocationMode.doc.proportional: Allocate points proportionally based on item value contribution.
__PointsAllocationMode.doc.lastItem: Assign all bonus points to the last item.
__PointsAllocationMode.doc.highestPrice: Assign all bonus points to the highest-priced item.
__PointsAllocationMode.doc.firstMatch: Assign all bonus points to the first qualifying item.

__ShoppingCartPromotionSettings.doc: Promotion engine configuration. The promotions that price a cart are the dynamic ones (the generated {cart}Campaign store read by the full promotion engine); static promotions are accepted by the schema but no generated service reads them.

ShoppingCartPromotionSettings.__supportPromotions.doc: Whether to enable promotion functionality. Adds couponCode and appliedCampaignIds fields to Cart.
ShoppingCartPromotionSettings.__staticPromotions.doc: Static promotion tiers. Accepted by the schema but not applied: no generated service reads them, in any language. Use dynamic promotions (campaigns) for discounts that must change a price.
ShoppingCartPromotionSettings.__dynamicPromotions.doc: Complex promotions loaded from the generated {cart}Campaign store (one DataObject; coupons are its couponCode column).
ShoppingCartPromotionSettings.__conflictResolution.doc: How to handle conflicts between multiple applicable promotions.

__ConflictResolutionMode.doc.#: Defines how to handle multiple applicable promotions.
__ConflictResolutionMode.doc.bestForCustomer: Automatically select the promotion(s) that give the customer the highest benefit.
__ConflictResolutionMode.doc.applyAll: Apply all applicable promotions that are stackable.
__ConflictResolutionMode.doc.priorityOrder: Apply promotions in priority order until max is reached.
__ConflictResolutionMode.doc.exclusive: Only apply the highest-priority exclusive promotion.

__StaticPromotionSettings.doc: Simple cart-level promotion tiers (free-shipping threshold, cart total and quantity discounts, membership discounts, a loyalty points multiplier). Not applied: no template or runtime library in any language reads these settings, so a static promotion changes no price. Kept so stored blueprints stay valid; author the same tiers as dynamic campaigns instead (for example a minCartTotal rule with a freeShipping reward, or a tieredDiscount reward).

StaticPromotionSettings.__freeShippingThreshold.doc: Free shipping when cart total exceeds a threshold. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).
StaticPromotionSettings.__cartTotalDiscount.doc: Tiered percentage or fixed discount based on cart total. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).
StaticPromotionSettings.__cartQuantityDiscount.doc: Tiered discount based on total item quantity. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).
StaticPromotionSettings.__membershipDiscounts.doc: Discounts based on customer membership level. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).
StaticPromotionSettings.__loyaltyPointsMultiplier.doc: Points multiplier based on membership level. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

__FreeShippingPromotion.doc: Static promotion: Free shipping when cart total exceeds threshold. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

FreeShippingPromotion.__minCartTotal.doc: Minimum cart total (ex-VAT) to qualify for free shipping.
FreeShippingPromotion.__customerMessage.doc: Message to display to customer when promotion applies.

__CartTotalDiscountPromotion.doc: Static promotion: Tiered discount based on cart total. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

CartTotalDiscountPromotion.__tiers.doc: Array of discount tiers. Evaluated top-down, first matching tier applies.
CartTotalDiscountPromotion.__maxDiscountAmount.doc: Optional cap on the maximum discount amount.
CartTotalDiscountPromotion.__stackableWithDynamic.doc: Whether this discount can stack with dynamic promotions.

__CartTotalDiscountTier.doc: A single tier in cart total discount promotion.

CartTotalDiscountTier.__name.doc: The tier's identifying name (e.g. 'over-100'). Identifies the tier in designer lists and duplicate detection — thresholds stay purely functional.
CartTotalDiscountTier.name: String
CartTotalDiscountTier.__minCartTotal.doc: Minimum cart total to activate this tier.
CartTotalDiscountTier.__discountPercent.doc: Percentage discount to apply (e.g., 10 for 10%). Mutually exclusive with discountAmount.
CartTotalDiscountTier.__discountAmount.doc: Fixed discount amount to apply. Mutually exclusive with discountPercent.
CartTotalDiscountTier.__customerMessage.doc: Message to display when this tier applies.

__CartQuantityDiscountPromotion.doc: Static promotion: Tiered discount based on total item quantity. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

CartQuantityDiscountPromotion.__stackableWithDynamic.doc: Whether this discount can stack with dynamic promotions.

__CartQuantityDiscountTier.doc: A single tier in cart quantity discount promotion.

CartQuantityDiscountTier.__name.doc: The tier's identifying name (e.g. 'bulk-5'). Identifies the tier in designer lists and duplicate detection — thresholds stay purely functional.
CartQuantityDiscountTier.name: String
CartQuantityDiscountTier.__minQuantity.doc: Minimum total items to activate this tier.
CartQuantityDiscountTier.__customerMessage.doc: Message to display when this tier applies.

__MembershipDiscountPromotion.doc: Static promotion: Discount based on customer membership level. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

MembershipDiscountPromotion.__membershipProperty.doc: Session property that holds the customer's membership level.
MembershipDiscountPromotion.__levels.doc: Array of membership levels and their discount percentages.
MembershipDiscountPromotion.__stackableWithDynamic.doc: Whether this discount can stack with dynamic promotions.

__MembershipDiscountLevel.doc: Discount configuration for a specific membership level.

MembershipDiscountLevel.__membershipLevel.doc: The membership level name (e.g., silver, gold, platinum).
MembershipDiscountLevel.__discountPercent.doc: Percentage discount for this membership level.

__LoyaltyPointsMultiplierPromotion.doc: Static promotion: Points multiplier based on membership level. Not applied (see StaticPromotionSettings).

LoyaltyPointsMultiplierPromotion.__membershipProperty.doc: Session property that holds the customer's membership level.
LoyaltyPointsMultiplierPromotion.__levels.doc: Array of membership levels and their point multipliers.

__PointsMultiplierLevel.doc: Points multiplier configuration for a specific membership level.

PointsMultiplierLevel.__multiplier.doc: Points multiplier for this level (e.g., 2 for double points).

__DynamicPromotionSettings.doc: Configuration for complex, database-driven promotions evaluated by the Promotion Engine at runtime. When enabled, the service gets ONE promotion DataObject, the campaign store {cartObjectName}Campaign (e.g. cartCampaign), and the generated cart manager loads its enabled rows into the engine. The loader contract: it reads rows with the query { isEnabled: true } and maps the columns name, priority, exclusive, stackable, requiresCoupon, couponCode, rules ([{ ruleType, config }]) and rewards ([{ rewardType, config }]) onto the engine, plus usageCount, the usage counter a usageLimit rule reads. There is NO Coupon object and NO CampaignUsage / UsageLog object: a coupon is the couponCode of a campaign row whose requiresCoupon is true, and usage is the usageCount column of the same row. A service may author {cartObjectName}Campaign itself (the authored object replaces the generated one), but it must then declare isEnabled, rules and rewards (validation ERROR SHOPPING_CART_CAMPAIGN_STORE_SHAPE otherwise, because the loader would read an empty catalog) and should declare couponCode and requiresCoupon (WARNING SHOPPING_CART_CAMPAIGN_STORE_COUPON_COLUMNS: without them no coupon can match).

DynamicPromotionSettings.__enabled.doc: Whether dynamic promotions are enabled. Generates the {cartObjectName}Campaign store (the only promotion DataObject) and wires the promotion engine to it. Every designer-authored surface on the store is operator-only: in a multi-tenant project restricted to the platform operator (superAdmin / saasAdmin; CART_CAMPAIGN_WRITE_NOT_PLATFORM_OPERATOR / CART_CAMPAIGN_READ_NOT_PLATFORM_OPERATOR), in a single-tenant project to the campaign operator the generated /campaigns routes admit (checkRoles of superAdmin / admin / saasAdmin / tenantOwner / tenantAdmin only, loginRequired true, M2MAllowed false; CART_CAMPAIGN_WRITE_NOT_CAMPAIGN_OPERATOR / CART_CAMPAIGN_READ_NOT_CAMPAIGN_OPERATOR) - a create / update / delete or get / list api on the store, a crud or read action on it in any api, an internal call, an api serving a DataView that reads it, and an event notification bound to such a view. All four codes are non-bypassable.
DynamicPromotionSettings.__supportCoupons.doc: Whether the cart takes coupon codes: emits the cart router's POST /<cart>/coupons and DELETE /<cart>/coupons/:code routes. No Coupon DataObject is generated: a coupon is a campaign row with requiresCoupon true and its couponCode. Runtime verdicts on the coupon routes are typed: applying an UNKNOWN code answers 404 COUPON_NOT_FOUND; a code whose campaign matched but whose rules refuse the cart (expired window, minimums, usage caps) answers 400 COUPON_NOT_ELIGIBLE - it is never silently 'applied' with a zero discount. Removing one coupon re-evaluates every remaining applied code, so the surviving coupons keep their discounts.
DynamicPromotionSettings.__supportMultipleCoupons.doc: Whether multiple coupon codes can be applied to a single cart.
DynamicPromotionSettings.__campaignSettings.doc: Configuration for the auto-generated Campaign DataObject.
DynamicPromotionSettings.__cacheSettings.doc: Redis caching settings for campaign data.

__AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.doc: Configuration for the auto-generated Campaign DataObject. Controls which features are available for campaigns.

AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__generateAdminApis.doc: RETIRED: no template in any language has ever read this flag, so the campaign/coupon admin CRUD APIs it advertised were never emitted — in nodejs, java, python, rust, golang, dotnet or php. It is kept only so stored blueprints that carry it stay valid; do not set it. To administer campaigns and coupons, author ordinary BusinessApis against the campaign/coupon data objects. The coupon RUNTIME surface is unaffected and is not gated by this flag: the cart router's POST /<cart>/coupons and DELETE /<cart>/coupons/:code are emitted from promotionSettings.dynamicPromotions.supportCoupons.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportBudgetLimits.doc: NOT IMPLEMENTED: no runtime reads this flag and no budget counter exists, so it caps nothing; true is reported as the validation warning SHOPPING_CART_CAMPAIGN_LIMIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportUsageLimits.doc: Whether campaigns can have usage limits (max total redemptions). When true: every cart-router checkout records promotion usage - inside the checkout claim, the usageCount column of each campaign the checkout used (its reward campaigns and the coupon campaigns of the cart's codes) is incremented once - and a campaign rule { ruleType: 'usageLimit', config: { maxUses: n } } is enforced: coupon evaluation refuses the campaign once usageCount reaches n (COUPON_NOT_ELIGIBLE), and the checkout increment is guarded in the database (usageCount + 1 <= n), so two checkouts racing for the last use cannot both win - the loser is refused 409 PROMOTION_USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED with its cart unchanged and retryable. A definite order-create failure gives the use back. When false: nothing is recorded by the cart router, and a usageLimit rule fails with USAGE_LIMITS_DISABLED. A CartCheckoutAction records usage per its own recordPromotionUsage option either way.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportCustomerLimits.doc: NOT IMPLEMENTED: no runtime reads this flag and no per-customer counter exists, so it caps nothing; true is reported as the validation warning SHOPPING_CART_CAMPAIGN_LIMIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The implemented cap is the total one: supportUsageLimits with a usageLimit rule.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportDailyLimits.doc: NOT IMPLEMENTED: no runtime reads this flag and no daily counter exists, so it caps nothing; true is reported as the validation warning SHOPPING_CART_CAMPAIGN_LIMIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportScheduling.doc: Informational: the dateRange and timeOfDay campaign rules are evaluated whether or not this flag is set; no runtime reads it.
AutoGeneratedCampaignSettings.__supportCustomerTags.doc: Informational: no runtime reads this flag. The customerTag campaign rule has no built-in evaluator; register one with registerRule('customerTag', ...).

__PromotionCacheSettings.doc: Redis caching configuration for promotion campaign data.

PromotionCacheSettings.__cacheInRedis.doc: Whether to cache active campaigns in Redis for performance.
PromotionCacheSettings.__cacheTtlSeconds.doc: TTL for campaign cache in Redis (default: 3000 seconds = 50 minutes).
PromotionCacheSettings.__cacheKeyPrefix.doc: Authored prefix for campaign cache keys (default: 'promo:'). Node.js appends campaigns: followed by the resolved project, service, campaign store and cart, individually encodeURIComponent-encoded and colon-joined. One key serves load, write and invalidation; no tenant/user scope is added.

__AutoGeneratedPromotionDataObjects.doc.#: The promotion DataObject generated when dynamicPromotions.enabled is true, and the rule / reward vocabulary its rows speak. There is exactly ONE promotion object: the campaign store {cartObjectName}Campaign. No Coupon, PromotionCampaign or CampaignUsageLog object is generated - a coupon is a campaign row with requiresCoupon true and a couponCode, and usage is the usageCount column of that row.

CampaignStore.description: {cartObjectName}Campaign - one row per campaign. The generated cart manager loads the rows whose isEnabled is true into the promotion engine (through the dynamicPromotions.cacheSettings Redis cache). Admins manage rows through the cart router's /campaigns routes.

properties.name: String (required) - Display name of the campaign
properties.description: Text - Free-form description for campaign administrators
properties.isEnabled: Boolean (required, default true) - Admin activation toggle; the loader queries { isEnabled: true }. Not the soft-delete isActive: a paused campaign stays stored and editable
properties.priority: Integer (required, default 0) - Evaluation priority, higher runs first
properties.exclusive: Boolean (default false) - When true, no further campaign is evaluated after this one applies
properties.stackable: Boolean (default true) - When false, this campaign does not combine with another non-stackable campaign
properties.requiresCoupon: Boolean (default false) - When true the campaign applies only through its couponCode; when false it is an auto campaign applied whenever its rules match
properties.couponCode: String - The coupon code that triggers this campaign (requiresCoupon campaigns)
properties.rules: Object[] - Eligibility rules [{ ruleType, config }]; every rule must pass
properties.rewards: Object[] - Rewards [{ rewardType, config }]; each one applies when the rules pass
properties.usageCount: Integer (default 0) - How many checkouts used this campaign: incremented inside the checkout claim when promotion usage is recorded; read by the usageLimit rule

CampaignRuleType.#: Rule types the promotion engine evaluates, with the config each one reads.
CampaignRuleType.minCartTotal: Cart subtotal must reach a minimum. Config: { minTotal: number }
CampaignRuleType.minQuantity: Total quantity in the cart must reach a minimum. Config: { minQuantity: number }
CampaignRuleType.productCategory: At least one line's category is listed; the matching lines qualify. Config: { categories: string[] }
CampaignRuleType.brand: At least one line's brand is listed; the matching lines qualify. Config: { brands: string[] }
CampaignRuleType.productList: At least one line's productId is listed; the matching lines qualify. Config: { productIds: string[] }
CampaignRuleType.customerTag: No built-in evaluator (needs a CRM lookup): register one with registerRule('customerTag', ...), otherwise evaluation fails with RULE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
CampaignRuleType.firstPurchase: No built-in evaluator (needs an order-history lookup): register one with registerRule('firstPurchase', ...), otherwise RULE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
CampaignRuleType.membershipLevel: No built-in evaluator (needs a membership lookup): register one with registerRule('membershipLevel', ...), otherwise RULE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
CampaignRuleType.buyXGetY: Minimum quantity of the target lines. Config: { buyQuantity: number, targetProductIds?: string[] }
CampaignRuleType.dateRange: The current date must be inside the window. Config: { startDate?: string, endDate?: string }
CampaignRuleType.timeOfDay: The current server hour must be inside [fromHour, toHour). Config: { fromHour: number, toHour: number }
CampaignRuleType.usageLimit: The campaign's usageCount must be below maxUses. Config: { maxUses: number } (a non-negative integer, else INVALID_RULE_CONFIG). Evaluated when usage limits are on (campaignSettings.supportUsageLimits, or checkUsageLimits true on a CouponValidationAction); while they are off the rule fails with USAGE_LIMITS_DISABLED. The checkout claim enforces the cap atomically on the usageCount column (409 PROMOTION_USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED for the checkout that would pass it)

CampaignRewardType.#: Reward types the promotion engine applies, with the config each one reads.
CampaignRewardType.percentDiscount: Percentage off the qualifying lines (all lines when no rule narrowed them). Config: { percent: number }
CampaignRewardType.fixedDiscount: Fixed amount off, allocated over the qualifying lines. Config: { amount: number, allocation?: 'proportional' | 'equal' | 'firstItem' }
CampaignRewardType.freeShipping: Marks the cart for free shipping. Config: {}
CampaignRewardType.freeItem: Adds free lines. Config: { items: [{ barcode, productName, quantity, unitPrice }] }
CampaignRewardType.buyXGetY: The cheapest qualifying units become free. Config: { getQuantity: number }
CampaignRewardType.bundlePrice: The qualifying lines cost a fixed bundle total. Config: { bundleTotal: number }
CampaignRewardType.pointsMultiplier: Multiplies loyalty points earned. Config: { multiplier: number }
CampaignRewardType.tieredDiscount: Percentage that grows with the cart subtotal. Config: { tiers: [{ minTotal: number, percent: number }] }

__ShoppingCartRedisSettings.doc: Redis caching configuration for cart data enabling hyper-scalable, Redis-first architecture. Redis is the AUTHORITATIVE live store; the cart/cartItem DB rows are a best-effort MIRROR that may lag. The mirror has full delete parity: removing a line purges its mirrored row in the same request, and clearing the cart purges the cart's WHOLE mirrored line set - including any ghost row an earlier delete-blind build left behind, so the mirror self-heals on the next clear. Never treat the mirror as the live cart; read the cart routes for live state.

ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__enabled.doc: Whether to use Redis for cart caching.
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__keyPrefix.doc: Prefix for all Redis keys related to this cart type (e.g., 'cart:').
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__cartTtlSeconds.doc: TTL for cart data in Redis. After this time inactive carts are evicted.
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__itemsTtlSeconds.doc: TTL for cart items data in Redis.
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__persistStrategy.doc: When to persist cart data to database: 'onEveryChange', 'onCheckout', 'periodic', 'never'.
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__persistIntervalSeconds.doc: Interval for periodic persistence (if persistStrategy is 'periodic').
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__useHashForCart.doc: Use Redis HASH for cart data (better for partial updates) vs STRING (simpler).
ShoppingCartRedisSettings.__useListForItems.doc: Use Redis LIST for items (ordered) vs SET (unordered, faster lookups).

__RedisPersistStrategy.doc.#: Defines when cart data in Redis is persisted to the database.
__RedisPersistStrategy.doc.onEveryChange: Persist to DB on every cart modification. Most durable but highest DB load.
__RedisPersistStrategy.doc.onCheckout: Only persist when cart is checked out. Abandoned carts may be lost if Redis fails.
__RedisPersistStrategy.doc.periodic: Persist on a schedule (see persistIntervalSeconds). Balance of durability and performance.
__RedisPersistStrategy.doc.never: Never persist to DB automatically. Use for pure Redis carts (e.g., anonymous sessions).

__ShoppingCartApiSettings.doc: Configuration for auto-generated cart management API routes.

ShoppingCartApiSettings.__routePrefix.doc: Not read: no generator uses this value, so the cart routes always mount at /{cartObjectName} (basicSettings.cartObjectName, default 'cart'). Kept so stored blueprints stay valid; do not set it.
ShoppingCartApiSettings.__authenticationRequired.doc: RETIRED: no template in any language has ever read this flag — it has zero hits under _in/**/*.ts and _in/**/*.ejs — so setting it changes nothing about the cart's auth gate. It is kept only so stored blueprints that carry it stay valid; do not set it. The flag that ACTUALLY decides whether the cart router rejects an anonymous caller is basicSettings.supportGuestCart (cart-router.ejs: `const guestCartEnabled = basic?.supportGuestCart === true;`) — true allows guest carts, false/absent requires a session. Two fields cannot own one gate, and supportGuestCart is the one that does.
ShoppingCartApiSettings.__rateLimiting.doc: Enable rate limiting on cart APIs.
ShoppingCartApiSettings.__maxRequestsPerMinute.doc: Rate limit: max requests per minute per user/session.
ShoppingCartApiSettings.__enabledRoutes.doc: Which cart routes to generate. Required when basicSettings.useShoppingCartFeature is true; ignored while the shopping-cart feature is off.

__CartApiRoutes.doc: Which cart API routes to generate. All default to true: an omitted flag counts as true and false drops the route. The routes mount at /{cartObjectName} (basicSettings.cartObjectName, default 'cart'); apiSettings.routePrefix is not read. applyCoupon and removeCoupon are generated only when the coupon feature is on, and redeemPoints only when points redemption is on (see each flag). The Go runtime ignores these flags and has no recalculate or redeemPoints route.

CartApiRoutes.__getCart.doc: GET /{cartObjectName} - Retrieve current cart with items and totals.
CartApiRoutes.__addItem.doc: POST /{cartObjectName}/items - Add an item to the cart by barcode (required); quantity defaults to 1.
CartApiRoutes.__clearCart.doc: DELETE /{cartObjectName}/items - Clear all items from cart.
CartApiRoutes.__applyCoupon.doc: POST /{cartObjectName}/coupons - Apply a coupon code (body { couponCode }). Generated only when promotionSettings.supportPromotions, dynamicPromotions.enabled and dynamicPromotions.supportCoupons are all on.
CartApiRoutes.__removeCoupon.doc: DELETE /{cartObjectName}/coupons/:code - Remove an applied coupon. Same coupon gate as applyCoupon.
CartApiRoutes.__redeemPoints.doc: POST /{cartObjectName}/redeemPoints - Redeem loyalty points (body { points }). Generated only when loyaltySettings.supportLoyalty and supportPointsRedemption are both on (Node.js and Rust; the Java, .NET, Python and PHP routers check only this flag).

__ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.doc: Configuration for cart-to-order checkout process. Defines how checkout converts a cart into an order, including property mapping, order creation mode, and event publishing.

ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__orderCreationMode.doc: How to create orders from cart: 'local' creates order in same service, 'remote' publishes event for external order service, 'none' skips order creation. In 'local' mode the order row's money is the SERVER's checkout snapshot (a catalog-bound cart prices from the catalog; money keys in the request's checkoutData cannot move it), a settled cart becomes terminal ('convertedToOrder') and refuses further mutation, and a FAILED order create answers a typed 502 ORDER_CREATION_FAILED, publishes no checkout event, and leaves the cart retryable. A 'none'-mode cart still keeps server pricing from a bound catalog even though it creates no order.
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__orderDataObjectName.doc: Name of the order DataObject in this service. Required when orderCreationMode is 'local'. The system will auto-detect if there's a DataObject with isOrder flag.
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__autoMapProperties.doc: Local mode only: in orderCreationMode 'remote' no order is built here and this has no effect (validation warning SHOPPING_CART_REMOTE_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY_SETTING when false there). If true, automatically copy the canonical cart fields onto the order payload. The full list is ownerId, currency, subtotal, discountTotal, vatTotal, grossTotal, total, couponCodes, redeemedPoints, pointsValue and appliedPointsValue, plus userId taken from the cart owner. Order properties the order DataObject does not declare are dropped (and logged), so declare the columns you want to keep. Note that total is NET of any loyalty redemption: to keep an order row whose total is reconstructable from its own columns, declare grossTotal and appliedPointsValue too, since total = grossTotal - appliedPointsValue.
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__propertyMappings.doc: Override specific cart-to-order property mappings when autoMapProperties isn't sufficient. Local mode only: in orderCreationMode 'remote' the cart builds no order, so the mappings are not applied to the checkout event (validation warning SHOPPING_CART_REMOTE_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY_SETTING); map the order fields in the consuming service.
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__orderDataClause.doc: Local mode only (in orderCreationMode 'remote' it has no effect: validation warning SHOPPING_CART_REMOTE_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY_SETTING). JavaScript injected into order creation for custom properties, written as an object-literal BODY (`prop: expr, prop: expr`) and merged onto the order payload last, so it outranks autoMapProperties, propertyMappings and initialOrderStatus. Exactly three bindings are in scope: the frozen cart as 'cart', its lines as 'cartItems', and the generated cart manager as 'this' - whose per-request context is 'this.userId', 'this.sessionId', 'this.clientId' and 'this.requestId'. The checkout request body is NOT in scope here; read it with a propertyMappings entry whose cartProperty is 'checkoutData.<field>'. A member that does not exist yields undefined rather than a value. Example: `{ "js": "salesChannel: 'web', referralCode: this.userId" }`
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__publishCheckoutEvent.doc: Whether to publish a checkout completed event to Kafka. Always true when orderCreationMode is 'remote'.
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__checkoutEventTopic.doc: Kafka topic for checkout events. Default: '{serviceCodename}-cart-checkout-completed'. An explicit topic is PROJECT-SCOPED on the wire like a PublishEventAction topic: it is published as '<projectCodename>-<topic>', and a name that already starts with '<projectCodename>-' is left unchanged, so the preview and stage instances of one project never share it. A consumer in the project may name it with or without the prefix. The event carries { cartId, checkoutId, cart, items, rewards, orderId, orderCreationMode, checkoutData } under data (the unified event envelope, type '<cartObjectName>.checkoutCompleted').
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__initialOrderStatus.doc: Initial status to set on created orders. Usually 'pending' or 'awaiting_payment'. Local mode only: in orderCreationMode 'remote' the consuming service sets the status (a non-default value there is the validation warning SHOPPING_CART_REMOTE_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY_SETTING).
ShoppingCartCheckoutSettings.__externalCheckoutConsumer.doc: Declares that the order service consuming this cart's checkout topic lives OUTSIDE this project (another project, an external system). It only matters in orderCreationMode 'remote': a remote checkout publishes the checkout topic and creates no order itself, so design time requires an order-creating consumer of that exact topic - a create Business API whose controllers.kafkaSettings consumes it (requestTopicName) - and reports CART_CHECKOUT_TOPIC_NO_CONSUMER (ERROR) when the project has none. An event subscription, an event notification (a receipt mail), a kafka controller of another kind or an edge function on the topic creates no order and does not count. Set this flag to true to state that the consumer is external: the finding is then satisfied and the project validates and builds. Leave it false (the default) when the order service is part of this project. In 'local' and 'none' mode the flag is ignored (no finding, nothing emitted), and it never changes generated code in any mode.

__OrderCreationMode.doc.#: How checkout creates orders from the shopping cart.
__OrderCreationMode.doc.local: Create the order directly in this service using the specified orderDataObjectName.
__OrderCreationMode.doc.remote: Publish a checkout event for an external order service to consume and create the order.
__OrderCreationMode.doc.none: Do not create an order automatically. Use this when custom order creation logic is needed.

__CartToOrderPropertyMapping.doc: Maps a cart property to an order property, optionally with a transformation.

CartToOrderPropertyMapping.__cartProperty.doc: The cart property path to read from (e.g., 'grandTotalIncVat', 'userId', 'items'). Two extra roots are addressable by path: 'cart.<field>' (an explicit alias of the cart itself) and 'checkoutData.<field>', the checkout request body - which is the only way to put a request field on the order. The request body IS the checkout data: POST { "shippingMethod": "express" } is read as 'checkoutData.shippingMethod'; a body whose only key is checkoutData ({ "checkoutData": { ... } }) is unwrapped once, so both shapes read the same.
CartToOrderPropertyMapping.__orderProperty.doc: The order property to write to (e.g., 'totalAmount', 'customerId').
CartToOrderPropertyMapping.__transform.doc: Optional MScript expression to transform the value. Use 'value' to reference the cart property value (e.g. `Math.round(Number(value) * 100)`). The expression is emitted as `(value) => <expr>` inside the generated cart manager class, so `this` is the MANAGER - not the cart, a cart line or the order row: `this.discount` fails the generated service's build (TS2339) unless it happens to be a manager member. Only the per-request members `this.userId` / `this.sessionId` / `this.clientId` / `this.requestId` are meaningful; any other `this.<name>` is reported (CART_TRANSFORM_THIS_READ, WARNING). Read another cart field through its own mapping, or put the value on the order with checkoutSettings.orderDataClause.

__MembershipSettings.doc: Configuration settings for membership-based access control of a data object. This object does not define access itself but relies on a separate membership data object to manage which users can access this data object. For example, an 'organization' object might have access control defined through an 'organizationMember' object, which holds references to both the user and the organization.

MembershipSettings.__hasMembership.doc: Indicates whether this data object uses an external membership object to manage access rights. If set to true, access to this object is governed by entries in another object. Default is false.
MembershipSettings.__configuration.doc: The configuration object for membership settings. Leave it null if hasMembership is false.

__MembershipSettingsConfig.doc: Configuration settings for membership-based access control of a data object. This object does not define access itself but relies on a separate membership data object to manage which users can access this data object. For example, an 'organization' object might have access control defined through an 'organizationMember' object, which holds references to both the user and the organization.

MembershipSettingsConfig.__membershipObjectName.doc: Specifies the name of the external data object used to manage membership. This object contains membership entries linking users to this object.
MembershipSettingsConfig.__membershipObjectIdProperty.doc: The field name in the membership object that refers back to this data object (e.g., organizationId). It links the membership entry to this object.
MembershipSettingsConfig.__membershipUserIdProperty.doc: The field name in the membership object that refers to the user who holds membership. This is typically linked to the user's session during authorization checks.
MembershipSettingsConfig.__membershipStatusCheck.doc:
OPTIONAL extra validity filter on a membership row, and a QUERY FILTER rather than a row test — it is folded into the membership lookup itself (`$and`-ed onto the user/scope clause), so the database never returns a row that fails it. That is why it cannot be a predicate: a predicate can only be judged AFTER a row is fetched, which is exactly the shape that broke (`this` at that point is the service manager, not the row, so it evaluated to a bare boolean and every lookup answered "no membership").

The field is an MScript, and MQuery is a special MScript — `{ memberStatus: { $in: this.includePending ? ['pending','active'] : ['active'] } }` is a JavaScript object, not a language-neutral one, which is why it is typed this way rather than as a separate MQuery type.

WHAT TO AUTHOR: a static MQuery dict — `{ memberStatus: 'active' }`, `{ age: { $gte: 18 } }`, `{ $and: [{ memberStatus: 'active' }, { expiresAt: { $gt: '2026-01-01' } }] }`. Write it as the bare dict (the neutral, portable form every language lowers through its own MQuery converter) or as an MScript source whose js expression EVALUATES to such a dict. Either way it is resolved ONCE at codegen time and baked into the query.

TODAY'S LIMITS, stated because the shape suggests more than it does: only the `js` source is read, so a per-language source map is accepted but its non-js entries are ignored; and because the evaluation happens at build time, an expression referencing runtime state (`this.*`) throws and the filter is OMITTED rather than applied. A PREDICATE (`this.memberStatus === 'active'`) is REJECTED at design time (`MEMBERSHIP_STATUS_CHECK_NOT_A_FILTER`). Express a condition on the row's ROLE with `roleField` + `rolePermissions` (or a MembershipCheckAction's `requiredRoles`), not here.
MembershipSettingsConfig.__roleField.doc: OPTIONAL (ADR-native-permission-system §9.3). The field on the membership object whose value carries the member's role (e.g. `role`). It is the ONE place a member's role is read from, by both consumers: the permission resolver's membership layer (L4) reads `membershipRow[roleField]` and looks the role up in `rolePermissions`, and a MembershipCheckAction's `requiredRoles` compares against the same field. ABSENT ⇒ plain ROLELESS membership: the existence check still works, every member is treated as the built-in `member` role for permission binding, and `requiredRoles` cannot be used (there is no field to compare).
MembershipSettingsConfig.__rolePermissions.doc:
OPTIONAL (ADR-native-permission-system §9.3). The membership-role → permission-list map: which permissions each membership role grants on this scope object. CONFIG-ONLY — read straight from the blueprint at request time; NEVER seeded into the `givenPermission` store and NEVER runtime-DB-managed (contrast the GLOBAL role→permission map of RBACSettings.configuration.rolePermissions, which IS seeded). Use the built-in `member` role for permissions common to all members (plain roleless membership resolves to it). Each entry binds a role to declared PermissionGroup permission names.

REQUIRES PERMISSION MANAGEMENT. Exactly one thing reads this map — the permission resolver's membership layer — and that resolver is generated only when `authentication.accessControl.permissionBasics.pbacIsActive` is on. With PBAC off the grants are stored and NOTHING can ever read them: they read like live authorization and are inert, which is a design-time ERROR (`MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_PERMISSIONS_WITHOUT_PBAC`). A MembershipCheckAction does NOT consult this map either — it gates on the member ROLE (`requiredRoles`), not on permissions. So in a project without permission management, keep the member roles and express what each role may do as `requiredRoles` on each gated api; a rule needing a finer distinction wants a finer MEMBER ROLE, not a permission.

__MembershipRolePermission.doc: A single CONFIG-ONLY membership-role-to-permission binding (ADR-native-permission-system §9.3). Binds a membership role (the value of the membership object's `roleField`, or the built-in `member` default) to a list of permission names declared under a PermissionGroup. Read straight from the blueprint at request time by the L4 resolver — NEVER seeded into the `givenPermission` store, NEVER runtime-DB-managed.

MembershipRolePermission.__role.doc: The membership role this binding grants permissions to. Matches the value carried in the membership object's `roleField`, or the built-in `member` role (the default applied to plain roleless membership and any row with no role value).
MembershipRolePermission.__permissions.doc: The list of permission names this membership role grants on the scope object. Each must resolve to a permission declared under a PermissionGroup.

__LedgerSettings.doc:
Append-only-ledger activation for a DataObject. When enabled, each ROW of the decorated object OWNS a ledger: the framework generates the satellite objects (sys_<X>LedgerEntry lots, sys_<X>LedgerMovement append-only log, sys_<X>LedgerReservation when reservations are enabled) and the earn/consume/reserve/commitReservation/releaseReservation/getBalance/listEntries/adjust API roster, all bound to the owner row by a single FK.

OWNERSHIP IS THE ROW. There is no divider machinery inside the ledger — dividers are owner-IDENTITY columns on the decorated object itself. Multi-store stock is a `storeStockItem` object (storeId + productId with a unique composite index — without it, two ledger rows can exist for the same (store, product) and each carries half the truth); a multi-asset wallet is a `walletAccount` object (userId + assetCode), where 50+ crypto assets are 50+ rows and listing a new asset is an INSERT, never a schema change; the tenant divider comes free via `objectDataIsInTenantLevel`. Polymorphic owners (a payee that may be a user or an organization) declare a thin owner object rather than a polymorphic FK. Per-asset scales use `unit.scaleProperty` (an owner-row column seeded from an app-declared asset catalog — BTC rows carry 1e8, USD rows carry 100) instead of a global `unit.scale`; exactly one of the two is declared.

SESSION NEVER ENTERS THE LEDGER CORE. Mutating ledger APIs are fully parametric internal-call APIs: ownerId and operation inputs stay explicit, with no session-injected columns or ownership checks. User-facing spends are thin WRAPPER APIs the designer declares — e.g. `spendMyPoints` (REST, session-injected) resolves the caller's wallet row, then on nodejs, python, rust, java or dotnet calls `await API.consumeWalletLedger({ ownerId, amount, target, idempotencyKey }, { session: this.session })`. For a tenant-scoped owner object the second argument is required so the generated manager resolves the caller's tenant. A nodejs hook that has a caller session passes it in the same way. Omitting it leaves the session null and preserves the existing asSystem behavior, with no implicit inheritance through AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager. Language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature. Teach the wrapper, never session-inject the core.

Requires a RELATIONAL dbType on the owning service — every balance mutation is a multi-row compare-and-set in one transaction, which has no document-store emulation; mongodb is refused at design time (LEDGER_REQUIRES_RELATIONAL_DB).

OUT OF SCOPE in v1, stated so the boundary is designed rather than inferred: atomic cross-ledger conversion/swap (a two-legged consume+earn wrapper is TWO transactions; `transfer()` is the named v2 candidate); aggregate/portfolio reads (a DataView/list over owner rows, never materialized ledger state); and retry/attempt semantics (attempt counters, MAX_ATTEMPTS, retry crons are OUTBOX/delivery machinery about external providers, not ledger arithmetic — the outbox/delivery pattern is their future home). Integration recipes: earn-on-capture, clawback-on-refund, payout-via-reservation (see the pattern docs). Java supports the qualified relational ledger owner and its outbound response, stream, replay and event read boundary. Raw database reads and mutation amounts stay minor-unit integers. Projected outward Integer/Short columns use major-unit Double documentation; scale-one, CAS and non-ledger columns retain storage types, and per-asset satellites remain raw.

__LedgerSettings.useCase.description: Decorate a wallet-style object so every row owns an append-only points ledger: integer amounts at a fixed scale, FIFO consumption, a one-year expiry with a 30-day reminder window, and two-phase holds keyed by a business reference. The framework generates the lot/movement/reservation satellites, the earn/consume/reserve/commit/release/getBalance/listEntries roster (mutating APIs internal-call only — user-facing spends go through a designer wrapper API that resolves the caller's row from the session and calls `await API.consumePoints({ ownerId, amount, idempotencyKey, ... })`), and the expire/remind/sweep crons.

LedgerSettings.__objectOwnsALedger.doc: Enables the append-only ledger for this object. When true, every row of this object owns a ledger and the framework generates the satellite lot/movement(/reservation) objects, the configured API roster, and the configured cron jobs.
LedgerSettings.__configuration.doc: The LedgerConfig describing the ledger's unit, balance contract, consumption policy, parties, source refs, maturity, expiry, reservations, extra columns, events, and generated APIs. Auto-initialized to an empty config when objectOwnsALedger flips true; leave it null if objectOwnsALedger is false.

__LedgerConfig.doc: Configuration for the append-only ledger owned by each row of the decorated DataObject. Property bindings (`ownerKeyProperty`, `balance.*Property`, `unit.scaleProperty`) are PropRefer paths into the OWNER object's declared properties. Column-name fields on the satellite blocks (`parties`, `entrySource`, `entryMaturity`, `reservation`) NAME generated columns on the satellite tables and must not collide with the framework-owned generated fields (LEDGER_RESERVED_FIELD_COLLISION). Every balance mutation is a compare-and-set on the owner row's generated version column inside ONE transaction with the lot writes and the movement row; consumption applies each allocation with compare-and-set on `remaining = previousRemaining`.

LedgerConfig.__ledgerName.doc: CodeName of this ledger, used to name the generated satellite objects, the API roster (earn<LedgerName>, consume<LedgerName>, ...), and the event topic prefix. Defaults to the owner object's name at build time when omitted.
LedgerConfig.__unit.doc: The unit of account (name + fixed-point scale). Amounts are integers at a fixed scale. Exactly ONE of `unit.scale` (global) or `unit.scaleProperty` (per-asset, owner-row column) must be declared — validator-enforced (LEDGER_UNIT_SCALE_CONFLICT / LEDGER_UNIT_SCALE_MISSING).
LedgerConfig.__ownerKeyProperty.doc: The property whose value keys the satellite ownerId columns. Defaults to `id`. An alternate key must be a required, non-array ID (UUID) with a full-domain, globally unique index; tenant-scoped property uniques and soft-delete/partial uniques do not qualify. Unsupported keys fail with LEDGER_OWNER_KEY_UNSUPPORTED; no key is substituted.
LedgerConfig.__balance.doc: The THREE-NUMBER balance contract (available / pending / reserved) and how the numbers are maintained (materialized owner-row columns vs derived-at-read). See LedgerBalance.
LedgerConfig.__consumptionPolicy.doc: Order in which lots are drawn down by consume/reserve: fifo (default), fefo, or lifo. Ties are broken by (createdAt, id) so allocation is deterministic.
LedgerConfig.__allowNegative.doc: Whether the owner's available balance may go below zero. Default false — consume/reserve beyond the available number is refused. A derived-mode balance cannot ENFORCE the non-negative floor (no materialized number to compare-and-set against), so derived mode requires allowNegative: true (LEDGER_DERIVED_NEGATIVE_UNENFORCEABLE).
LedgerConfig.__parties.doc: Names of the generated party-reference columns on movement rows — earn carries a SOURCE ref, consume/reserve carry a TARGET ref. Movement METADATA, never FK-resolved by the ledger. See LedgerParties.
LedgerConfig.__entrySource.doc: The coarse source-reference line on the LOTS — the optional (owner, sourceRef) unique second idempotency line behind the movement-level idempotencyKey. See LedgerEntrySource.
LedgerConfig.__entryMaturity.doc: Lot maturity: credited value that counts as PENDING until its availableAt instant passes. See LedgerEntryMaturity.
LedgerConfig.__expiry.doc: Lot expiry sweep + pre-expiry reminders. The sweep consumes the UNRESERVED remainder only. See LedgerExpiry.
LedgerConfig.__reservation.doc: Two-phase holds (reserve / commitReservation / releaseReservation) with a stale-hold sweep. See LedgerReservation.
LedgerConfig.__additionalProperties.doc: Designer-declared extra columns on the generated satellite objects — full DataProperty declarations, relations included. This is where REAL FKs live (party refs are metadata-only). See LedgerAdditionalProperties.
LedgerConfig.__events.doc: Event emission settings — topic prefix, the opt-in balance-changed event, and event signing. See LedgerEvents.
LedgerConfig.__generatedApis.doc: Per-API bindings for the generated roster, with the internal-call-first defaults and the idempotency contract. See LedgerGeneratedApis.

__LedgerUnit.doc: The ledger's unit of account. `name` labels the unit (points, credits, cents, stock units); amounts are integers at a fixed-point scale. EXACTLY ONE of `scale` or `scaleProperty` must be declared (validator-enforced): `scale` is a single global scale for the whole ledger; `scaleProperty` names an owner-row column carrying the per-asset scale — the multi-asset divider form, where the scale is seeded from an app-declared asset catalog (BTC rows carry 100000000, USD rows carry 100).

LedgerUnit.__name.doc: Name of the unit of account (e.g. 'points', 'credits', 'cents'). Used in documentation, events, and generated API docs.
LedgerUnit.__scale.doc: Global fixed-point scale for the whole ledger — the integer amounts stored are `real value × scale` (100 = two decimal places; 1 = whole units). Declare exactly one of scale | scaleProperty.
LedgerUnit.__scaleProperty.doc: Owner-row column (PropRefer into the decorated object) carrying the per-asset fixed-point scale, for multi-asset dividers where each owner row is one asset. Declare exactly one of scale | scaleProperty.
LedgerUnit.name: String

__LedgerBalanceMode.doc.#: How the owner row's balance numbers are maintained.
__LedgerBalanceMode.doc.materialized: The owner row carries running balance columns, updated by compare-and-set in the same transaction as every lot write and movement row. The default, and required for enforcing a non-negative floor.
__LedgerBalanceMode.doc.derived: Balances are computed from the lots at read time; the owner row carries no running numbers. Cheaper writes, but the non-negative floor cannot be enforced (there is no materialized number to compare-and-set against), so allowNegative must be true.

__LedgerBalance.doc: Defines the available, pending and reserved balances returned by getBalance. The THREE-NUMBER balance contract: getBalance returns `available` (mature + unreserved), `pending` (unmatured), and `reserved` (held by open reservations) — and maturity is filtered IN THE QUERY, never post-query in application code. In materialized mode the named owner-row columns carry the running numbers and every mutation compare-and-sets them atomically with the lot and movement writes; `invariantCheckCron` schedules the verifyInvariants job that re-derives the numbers from the lots and reports drift.

LedgerBalance.__mode.doc: materialized (owner-row columns, CAS-updated — the default) or derived (computed from lots at read time; requires allowNegative: true).
LedgerBalance.__availableProperty.doc: Owner-row column (PropRefer) carrying the running AVAILABLE number — mature and unreserved value, the only number a spend may draw on. Materialized mode.
LedgerBalance.__pendingProperty.doc: Owner-row column (PropRefer) carrying the running PENDING number — credited but unmatured value (lots whose availableAt has not passed). Materialized mode.
LedgerBalance.__reservedProperty.doc: Owner-row column (PropRefer) carrying the running RESERVED number — value held by open reservations. Materialized mode.
LedgerBalance.__lifetimeCreditedProperty.doc: Optional owner-row column (PropRefer) accumulating every credit ever earned (never decremented). Materialized mode.
LedgerBalance.__lifetimeConsumedProperty.doc: Optional owner-row column (PropRefer) accumulating every consumption ever committed (never decremented). Materialized mode.
LedgerBalance.__invariantCheckCron.doc: Cron expression for the verifyInvariants job: re-derive available/pending/reserved from the lots and compare against the materialized columns, reporting drift. Leave null to disable the job.

__LedgerConsumptionPolicy.doc.#: Order in which lots are drawn down by consume/reserve. Ties are broken by (createdAt, id) so allocation is deterministic under concurrency.
__LedgerConsumptionPolicy.doc.fifo: First-in-first-out — oldest lot by createdAt first. The default.
__LedgerConsumptionPolicy.doc.fefo: First-expired-first-out — soonest-expiring lot first (lots without an expiry come last); ties broken by (createdAt, id). Use with expiring value so about-to-expire lots are spent first.

__LedgerParties.doc: Names of the generated party-reference columns on the movement rows: earn carries a SOURCE ref (what granted the value), consume/reserve carry a TARGET ref (what the value was spent on). Party refs are movement METADATA — the lot stores its source, movement rows store both sides, and the values arrive as explicit API parameters. They are NEVER FK-resolved by the ledger: cross-service values are legal (an order id from another service, a promotion code, a support-ticket ref). When a real FK relation is wanted, declare it under additionalProperties instead. When this block or a side is omitted, the columns default to sourceId/sourceType and targetId/targetType.

LedgerParties.__source.doc: Column names for the SOURCE side (set by earn; also stored on the lot). Defaults to sourceId/sourceType.
LedgerParties.__target.doc: Column names for the TARGET side (set by consume/reserve). Defaults to targetId/targetType.

__LedgerPartyRef.doc: Column names for one party side of a movement. Pure metadata: the ledger stores and returns these values but never resolves, validates, or joins them — no FK is created (declare a real relation under additionalProperties when referential integrity is wanted).

LedgerPartyRef.__idProperty.doc: Name of the generated column carrying the party's id value (metadata, not a relation).
LedgerPartyRef.__typeProperty.doc: Name of the generated column carrying the party's type discriminator (e.g. 'order', 'promotion', 'refund', 'payout').

__LedgerEntrySource.doc: Configures the source-reference column and optional owner/source uniqueness of credited lots. The coarse source-reference line on the LOTS: `referenceProperty` names a generated lot column storing the originating business ref of each credited lot, and with `unique: true` (the default) the framework adds a unique (owner, sourceRef) index — the optional COARSE second idempotency line behind the movement-level idempotencyKey (one credit per business source, e.g. one earn per order).

LedgerEntrySource.__referenceProperty.doc: Name of the generated lot column carrying the originating business reference. Default 'sourceRef'.
LedgerEntrySource.__unique.doc: When true (the default), the framework adds a unique (owner, sourceRef) index on the lots — the same business source cannot credit the same owner twice.
LedgerEntrySource.__sourceTypeProperty.doc: Optional name of a generated lot column carrying the source's type discriminator. Default 'sourceType'.

__LedgerEntryMaturity.doc: Lot maturity. There is NO separate pending-lot concept — 'pending points with an abandonment sweep' is exactly 'unmatured lot + maturity deadline', one concept. Each lot carries a nullable availableAt: set from `defaultDelay` at credit time (or supplied per earn call); until it passes, the lot counts toward the balance's PENDING number and cannot be consumed or reserved — and consume/getBalance filter maturity IN THE QUERY, never post-query in application code. The maturity cron matures due lots (pending → available) and publishes `<prefix>.entry.matured`.

LedgerEntryMaturity.__availableAtProperty.doc: Name of the generated lot column carrying the maturity instant. Default 'availableAt'.
LedgerEntryMaturity.__defaultDelay.doc: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. 'P14D', 'PT1H') added to the credit instant when the earn call does not supply availableAt. Leave null for immediate maturity unless the caller supplies availableAt explicitly.
LedgerEntryMaturity.__cronExpression.doc: Cron expression for the maturity job that flips due lots from pending to available and publishes the matured event. Default '0 * * * *' (hourly).

__LedgerExpiry.doc: Lot expiry sweep and pre-expiry reminders. When enabled, lots whose expiry falls due are swept in batches by the expire cron. THE SWEEP CONSUMES THE UNRESERVED REMAINDER ONLY: value held by an OPEN reservation survives expiry until the reservation commits or releases — a hold must never be silently voided by the calendar (framework-owned subtlety). `reminderLeadDays` + `reminderCron` drive the notifyExpiring job that publishes a pre-expiry reminder event.

LedgerExpiry.__enabled.doc: Enables lot expiry for this ledger. When false, the other fields in this block are inert (LEDGER_EXPIRY_CONFIG_INERT).
LedgerExpiry.__ttl.doc: ISO-8601 duration a lot lives from its credit instant (e.g. 'P365D'). The lot's expiry instant is computed at credit time.
LedgerExpiry.__cronExpression.doc: Cron expression for the expire sweep. Default '15 2 * * *' (nightly at 02:15).
LedgerExpiry.__batchSize.doc: Maximum lots swept per cron run. Default 500.
LedgerExpiry.__reminderLeadDays.doc: Days before expiry at which the notifyExpiring job publishes a reminder event. Leave null to disable reminders.
LedgerExpiry.__reminderCron.doc: Cron expression for the notifyExpiring job. Default '0 8 * * *' (daily at 08:00).

__LedgerCommitPolicy.doc.#: What commitReservation may consume relative to the reserved amount. The allocation plan is computed at reserve time, persisted on the reservation row, and REPLAYED at commit — never recomputed; every transition is a compare-and-set.
__LedgerCommitPolicy.doc.exact: Commit consumes exactly the reserved amount. The default.
__LedgerCommitPolicy.doc.partial: Commit may consume less than the reserved amount; the unconsumed remainder is released back to available in the same transaction.

__LedgerReservation.doc: Two-phase holds: reserve places a hold (available → reserved), commitReservation consumes it, releaseReservation returns it. This is the payout recipe — payout initiation → reserve (referenceProperty = the payout item's ref, so double-reserve is structurally impossible); afterPayoutPaid → commitReservation; afterPayoutFailed → releaseReservation — and it keeps the retry/attempt boundary clean: attempt chaos stays on the payout/outbox side while the ledger sees only reserve/commit/release. The sweep releases holds stale past `staleAfterSeconds`, restoring BOTH sides — the lots and the balance — in one transaction.

LedgerReservation.__enabled.doc: Enables two-phase holds for this ledger (generates the sys_<X>LedgerReservation object and the reserve/commitReservation/releaseReservation APIs). When false, the other fields in this block are inert (LEDGER_RESERVATION_CONFIG_INERT).
LedgerReservation.__staleAfterSeconds.doc: Seconds after which an open hold counts as stale and the sweep releases it. Default 172800 (48 hours).
LedgerReservation.__sweepCron.doc: Cron expression for the sweepReservations job. Default '0 * * * *' (hourly).
LedgerReservation.__referenceProperty.doc: Name of the generated reservation column carrying the caller's business ref for the hold. The framework adds a UNIQUE PARTIAL INDEX over OPEN holds on (owner, reference) — the same ref cannot hold twice concurrently, while committed/released history keeps its refs.
LedgerReservation.__kindProperty.doc: Optional name of a generated reservation column carrying a caller-defined kind discriminator (e.g. 'payout', 'checkout').
LedgerReservation.__commitPolicy.doc: exact (commit consumes exactly the reserved amount — the default) or partial (commit may consume less; the remainder is released in the same transaction).

__LedgerAdditionalProperties.doc: Designer-declared extra columns on the generated satellite objects — full DataProperty declarations, relations included. This is where REAL FKs live, in contrast to the metadata-only party refs. Names must not collide with the framework-owned generated fields of each satellite table (LEDGER_RESERVED_FIELD_COLLISION) nor with the column names configured on parties/entrySource/entryMaturity/reservation.

LedgerAdditionalProperties.__entry.doc: Extra columns on the sys_<X>LedgerEntry lot object.
LedgerAdditionalProperties.__movement.doc: Extra columns on the sys_<X>LedgerMovement append-only log object.
LedgerAdditionalProperties.__reservation.doc: Extra columns on the sys_<X>LedgerReservation object (only meaningful when reservation.enabled).

__LedgerEvents.doc: Event emission for the ledger. Topics are prefixed with `prefix` (default: the ledger name) — e.g. `<prefix>.entry.matured`, `<prefix>.entry.expired`, `<prefix>.reservation.released`. `publishBalanceChanged` opts into a balance-changed event on EVERY mutation (default false — high volume; prefer the specific lifecycle events). `secure` requires the project's Ed25519 signature on the ledger's events for cross-trust-boundary consumers (same mechanism as serviceOptions.secureEvents).

LedgerEvents.__prefix.doc: CodeName prefix for the ledger's event topics. Defaults to the ledger name.
LedgerEvents.__publishBalanceChanged.doc: Implemented by nodejs, java, dotnet and python: when true, each committed ledger operation publishes `<prefix>.balance.changed` through ServicePublisher. Its data is `{ ownerId, available, pending, reserved, movementId, idempotencyKey, version }`: ownerId is the configured owner key; balances are major units, using unit.scale or the owner row's unit.scaleProperty. Identity is (topic alias, ownerId, movementId); version is null for derived mode. Capture is inside the winning transaction after writes, delivery is best effort after commit; rollback, retry attempts and idempotent replays emit nothing extra. A maturity/expiry batch emits once per owner transaction; stale holds emit once per hold transaction. Default false emits nothing. events.secure signs this alias through the existing project Ed25519 mechanism. Ledgers require a relational database; MongoDB is rejected. See mastering/ledger for wire topic scope and delivery limits.
LedgerEvents.__secure.doc: When true, the ledger's events are Ed25519-signed by the project (publish side) and signature-verified by framework consumers (subscribe side). Default false.

__LedgerGeneratedApis.doc:
Per-API bindings for the generated roster. Declaring a binding on an API the ledger does not generate raises LEDGER_API_BINDING_INERT; enable its emit flag and prerequisites before overriding its transport. ROSTER DEFAULTS: the five mutating APIs (earn, consume, reserve, commitReservation, releaseReservation) emit as INTERNAL-CALL APIs only (internalCall: true, rest: false) — the integration story is a lifecycle hook or a designer-declared wrapper API awaiting `API.<api><LedgerName>({ ... })`; getBalance emits rest + internalCall and returns the available/pending/reserved triple plus the computed spendable; listEntries emits rest; adjust is OFF by default (emit: false) — an operator instrument, enable deliberately and gate it with checkRoles; voidBySource (reverse the lots one source credited, e.g. a refund before maturity) is OFF by default too and defaults to internalCall only.

TRANSPORT RULING: the rest flag is honoured in BOTH directions — rest: false emits hasRestController: false and mounts NOTHING, rest: true mounts the route — and the safe default for a MUTATING member is exactly that non-mounted shape. A mutating member bound to REST with an empty checkRoles admits any authenticated caller to a mint/burn operation and raises LEDGER_REST_MUTATION_UNGATED; either name a role in checkRoles, or keep the mutation internal and call it from a wrapper API that carries its own gate.

IDEMPOTENCY CONTRACT: `idempotencyKey` is a REQUIRED caller-supplied parameter on earn/consume/reserve, unique-indexed on the movement table by the framework. A REPLAY returns the ORIGINAL movement's result with `alreadyProcessed: true` — never a 409, because a network retry must not alarm the caller. The key identifies the OPERATION, not the attempt — derive it from the business fact (e.g. `pay:<providerIntentId>`), never suffix it with an attempt counter.

SESSION CANON: the mutating APIs run asSystem and are fully parametric — session-injected values never enter the ledger core. User-facing spends go through designer-declared wrapper APIs (REST, session-injected) that resolve the owner row from the session and call the internal API with explicit parameters. On nodejs, python, rust, java and dotnet, ledger APIs on a tenant-scoped owner object require `{ session: this.session }` as the optional second argument so their generated manager resolves the caller's tenant. A nodejs hook with a caller session uses the same argument. Omitting it leaves the session null; no session is inherited from AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager. Language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature.

LedgerGeneratedApis.__earn.doc: Credit a lot to an owner (source ref + required idempotencyKey; optional availableAt). Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest false.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__consume.doc: Consume available value from an owner's lots per the consumptionPolicy (target ref + required idempotencyKey). Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest false.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__reserve.doc: Place a two-phase hold on available value (target ref + required idempotencyKey; requires reservation.enabled). Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest false.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__commitReservation.doc: Consume a hold by replaying its persisted allocation plan (per commitPolicy). Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest false.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__releaseReservation.doc: Release a hold, restoring lots and balance in one transaction. Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest false.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__getBalance.doc: Read the three-number balance — available (mature + unreserved), pending (unmatured), reserved — plus the computed spendable. Default binding: emit true, internalCall true, rest true.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__listEntries.doc: List an owner's lots (remaining, maturity, expiry, source). Default binding: emit true, rest true.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__adjust.doc: Operator correction: credit or debit outside the normal earn/consume flow, always with a required reason and idempotencyKey. Default binding: emit FALSE — enable deliberately and gate with checkRoles.
LedgerGeneratedApis.__voidBySource.doc: Reverse what ONE source credited to an owner (`void<LedgerName>BySource({ ownerId, sourceRef, sourceType?, idempotencyKey?, reason? })`), e.g. a refund of an order whose earning has not matured yet. Every lot stamped with that source ref that is still pending or available loses its UNRESERVED remainder (unmatured lots leave pending, matured lots leave available, a drained lot becomes `voided`), recorded as ONE `void` movement. What the source credited but the ledger no longer holds (spent, held by an open reservation, expired) is answered as `shortfall` and is never booked as a debt or a negative lot. Idempotent by the source: an omitted idempotencyKey is derived from the owner and the source ref. A source with no lot on the owner is a typed 404 (LEDGER_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND). Emitted by the nodejs, java, dotnet and python ledger layers; other languages refuse an enabled binding (LEDGER_VOID_BY_SOURCE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED). Default binding: emit FALSE, internalCall true, rest false.

__LedgerApiBinding.doc: Binding overrides for one generated ledger API. A binding on an API the ledger does not generate raises LEDGER_API_BINDING_INERT. Per-API defaults live on LedgerGeneratedApis — the five mutating APIs default to internal-call only, getBalance to rest + internal, listEntries to rest, adjust to emit: false.

LedgerApiBinding.__emit.doc: Whether this API is generated at all. Default true for every roster member except adjust and voidBySource (see LedgerGeneratedApis).
LedgerApiBinding.__internalCall.doc: Expose the API on the service's in-process `API` namespace (fully parametric, runs asSystem) — the integration surface for lifecycle hooks and wrapper APIs. Per-API default: true for the five mutating APIs, adjust and getBalance, false for listEntries. adjust defaults to internalCall: true even though its emit default is false.
LedgerApiBinding.__rest.doc: Expose the API as a REST endpoint. Per-API default: false for the five mutating APIs and adjust (adjust defaults to rest: false; session never enters the ledger core — declare a wrapper API for user-facing spends), true for getBalance and listEntries. HONOURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: rest: false emits `restSettings.hasRestController: false`, so the operation has NO router entry, no swagger path, no MCP tool and no route-manifest row — it stays callable on the internal-call namespace and from actions; rest: true emits the route at routePath. It was not always so: the emitter used to DROP the restSettings block for rest: false, and every route-emitting surface reads an absent block as MOUNTED, so a binding authored rest: false shipped the route anyway behind nothing but loginRequired.
LedgerApiBinding.__routePath.doc: Custom REST path override (only meaningful when rest is true). Leave null to auto-generate.
LedgerApiBinding.__checkRoles.doc: Roles required to call the REST endpoint (OR logic, same semantics as ApiAuthOptions.checkRoles). Only meaningful when rest is true. SAFE DEFAULT FOR A MOUNTED MUTATION: the generated roster API carries loginRequired: true and no other gate, so a value-writing member (earn, consume, reserve, commitReservation, releaseReservation, adjust) bound to REST with an empty checkRoles is a mint/burn surface behind 'be logged in' — any authenticated caller of the service reaches it. The framework's default answer is therefore NOT to mount it at all (rest: false on every mutating member); binding one anyway raises LEDGER_REST_MUTATION_UNGATED until checkRoles names a role. It is a warning rather than a refusal because checkRoles needs RBAC and a project may run with accessControl.roleSettings.rbacIsActive: false, where no role can be named — there the only honest fix is to drop the rest binding and call the internal API from a wrapper that carries its own ownership or permission gate.

__DataProperty.doc: The definition of a data property within a data object. A data property is not just a storage field—it encapsulates the logic, behavior, and metadata associated with a specific piece of data. Through its settings, a data property can define relationships, context-aware values, session-based defaults, computed formulas, access filters, enums, and more. It serves as a powerful unit of business logic tightly integrated with the data model.

__DataProperty.useCase.description: Use a DataProperty to define one field of a DataObject — its type, constraints, indexing, and behavior (relation, session-binding, static-join). This example is a required foreign-key reference to a customer, indexed for fast lookups; the relation is activated by the populated relationSettings block.

DataProperty.__basicSettings.doc: Defines the foundational attributes of the data property — name, type, isRequired, isFilterParameter, enumOptions (when type === 'Enum'), defaultValue, and the rest of the per-property flags. The activation booleans for relation, filter, and enum live here so a property's design lives in one place.
DataProperty.__indexSettings.doc: Controls how the property is indexed in storage systems to optimize lookup and uniqueness behaviors. Optional — omit (or null) when unused; never [].
DataProperty.__relationSettings.doc: Defines relationship mappings when `basicSettings.hasRelation === true`. Foreign-key target object, key, on-delete behavior, etc. Leave null/absent when hasRelation is false.
DataProperty.__sessionSettings.doc: Specifies how the property's value is derived from the session context when this block is populated. Setting `sessionSettings.sessionParam` activates session-bound mode; leave the wrapping object null/absent otherwise.
DataProperty.__staticJoin.doc: Defines the static-join configuration when this block is populated. Setting `staticJoin.jointSource` activates the join; leave the wrapping object null/absent otherwise.
DataProperty.__graphEdge.doc: Opt-in graph edge for an FK-relation property (docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §4a/§5). When this property has `basicSettings.hasRelation: true` (a 1-hop FK declared in `relationSettings`), populating `graphEdge` projects that relationship as a graph edge: on every write of the owning row, `MERGE` the relationship to the target node by key (and the target row projects as its own node). Also the §5 PROMOTION mechanism — a flat filter attribute kept in `projectedProperties` becomes a node+edge by adding a `graphEdge` block here. Leave null/absent when the relation is not projected.
DataProperty.__decisionSource.doc: Opt-in WRITE-TIME CLASSIFICATION of this property (decision layer binding point B, docs/ADR-decision-layer-system-one.md section 5). When populated, the property's value is not written by callers: a calibrated decision provider answers ONE typed question about the row after a create and after every update that touches a `recomputeOn` property, and the DECISION is stored in this column, so every later query is a plain indexed predicate with no model in the path. Three companion columns are added next to it and written with every decision: `<prop>DecisionConfidence` (Double), `<prop>DecidedBy` (String, the exact model version that answered, or `manual`) and `<prop>DecidedAt` (Date); a fourth, `<prop>DecisionOverridden` (Boolean), pins an operator's correction against recomputation. The value type must match the question: noul -> Boolean, choice -> Enum (every option key an enum option) or String, score -> Double / Float / Integer. A provider outage never fails the write: the column is left unset and the backfill picks the row up. Never use it on a property an authorization predicate reads (DECISION_ON_AUTHZ_SURFACE). Leave null/absent for an ordinary property.
