__ApiAuthOptions.doc: Defines core authentication and authorization settings for a Business API. These settings cover session validation, role and ownership checks, and access scope (e.g., tenant vs. SaaS-level). While these options are sufficient for most use cases, more fine-grained access control—such as conditional permissions or contextual ownership—should be implemented using explicit access control actions (e.g., `PermissionCheckAction`, `MembershipCheckAction`, `ObjectPermissionCheckAction`).

ApiAuthOptions.__apiInSaasLevel.doc: If true, this API is a SaaS-LEVEL (cross-tenant) surface, and the CONSEQUENCE is the point: it removes tenant isolation from this api's reads. In a multi-tenant project every read and every scoped write (get/list/update/delete) on a tenant-level DataObject is otherwise AND-ed with `{ <tenantName>Id: this._tenantId }` (the MANAGER slot - there is no generic `session.tenantId`) (and the tenant ROOT object is pinned to the caller's own row by `id`); `apiInSaasLevel: true` drops that term entirely, so this api reads - and, on a scoped write, mutates - rows belonging to EVERY tenant. That is exactly how a deliberate cross-tenant surface is built (a public catalogue or job board, a SaaS-admin console, cross-tenant analytics), and it is also indistinguishable in the blueprint from the same flag left behind by accident - copying a board api as the template for a tenant-scoped list is the shape that bites. So when the api reads tenant-level data, NAME what you are exposing in `crossTenantScopeOf`: an undeclared pairing is reported as SAAS_LEVEL_TENANT_READ_UNDECLARED, and a declaration naming a source the api does not read is refused as CROSS_TENANT_READ_DECLARATION_MISMATCH. Gate the api itself with `checkRoles`/`absoluteRoles` naming SaaS-level roles unless the surface is genuinely public.
ApiAuthOptions.__crossTenantScopeOf.doc: DECLARES that this api's cross-tenant reads are deliberate, by NAMING the read source whose tenant isolation `apiInSaasLevel` waives. Write the api's own `apiOptions.dataViewName` when the api reads a DataView, otherwise its `apiOptions.dataObjectName`; matching is case-insensitive and a `service:` prefix on an object name is ignored. WHY A NAME AND NOT A YES/NO FLAG: the accident this guards against is copying a deliberate cross-tenant api as the template for a tenant-scoped one, and a boolean would be copied along with it unchanged, still reading `true`. A name is not - retarget the copy at another view or object and the declaration no longer matches what the api reads, which is refused as CROSS_TENANT_READ_DECLARATION_MISMATCH. Leave null when this api is not a cross-tenant surface: declaring it without `apiInSaasLevel: true` waives nothing and is reported as CROSS_TENANT_READ_WITHOUT_SAAS_LEVEL. NAMED FOR THE COMMON CASE, NOT A LIMIT: `apiInSaasLevel` lifts the tenant term from an api's scoped WRITES too (a SaaS-level update/delete addresses any tenant's row), and one declaration covers whichever the api does - the source named is the `dataViewName`/`dataObjectName` the api is pointed at, not the verb.
ApiAuthOptions.__M2MAllowed.doc:
If true, this API ACCEPTS machine callers: a caller presenting a VERIFIED `x-m2m-token` and no user identity passes checkValidLogin / checkBasicAuth instead of being refused. It WIDENS the login gate; it is not a gate of its own, and it is a statement about what the API ALLOWS, never about who called (the CALLER-side answer is `this.isM2M`, and a guard reading `M2MAllowed` instead is true for every caller of an M2M-allowed api). `loginRequired: true` + `M2MAllowed: true` IS NOT A MACHINE-ONLY FORM. This doc called it one until the consequence was measured: six apis authored in exactly that pair, with no `checkRoles` beside it, let a plain tenantOwner read ANOTHER tenant's plan, seat and quota state. The login gate opens for a user session exactly as it does for a machine token, so anonymous is the only caller the pair excludes. To REFUSE human callers, declare `requiredCallerKind` beside it — that is the flag that narrows, this one only widens.

THE FOUR CALLERS. "Machine vs human" is two rows; the runtime has four, and the fourth is the one a designer cannot predict and the one their traffic actually carries — `InterService.call` attaches `x-m2m-token` unconditionally and forwards the caller's bearer when `forwardCallerToken` is set, so an ordinary end user proxied through a service-to-service hop arrives carrying BOTH signals:

| caller | isM2M | session owner | loginRequired:true + M2MAllowed:true | ... + requiredCallerKind: machine | ... + requiredCallerKind: machineWithoutUserIdentity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| anonymous | false | null | 401 | 401 | 401 |
| an INTERACTIVE user session | false | set | PASSES (the hole) | 403 | 403 |
| a session-less machine token | true | null | passes | passes | passes |
| a user FORWARDED on an InterService hop | true | set | passes | PASSES | 403 |

`loginRequired: false` does the OPPOSITE of what it looks like here — it switches the whole authorization pipeline off (ApiManager short-circuits every role, permission and ownership check on that flag, checkValidLogin included, and no checkBasicAuth override is emitted), so the endpoint answers ANONYMOUS callers and M2MAllowed beside it demands nothing. There is no M2M-ONLY gate for a Business API; `loginRequired: false` means PUBLIC. Declaring the pair explicitly is reported as PUBLIC_API_WITH_M2M_ONLY_INTENT. (EdgeControllers are a different pattern with a different runtime and do carry an m2m auth mode — see EdgeControllerOptions.)
ApiAuthOptions.__requiredCallerKind.doc:
WHO may call this api, as a demand on the CALLER — the narrowing counterpart to `M2MAllowed`, which only widens. `M2MAllowed` is what the API DECLARES it tolerates; `requiredCallerKind` is what the caller must TURN OUT TO BE, measured at runtime from the verified `isM2M` identity or the Kafka dispatch transport. Default `any` — no caller-kind demand, exactly the behaviour every api had before this field existed, so a project on the old spelling is unaffected.

`machine` is the machine-only gate the platform used to have no way to express. It refuses an INTERACTIVE user session with 403 `M2M_CALLER_REQUIRED` and admits a machine caller — INCLUDING an end-user identity forwarded on an ordinary InterService hop, which carries `x-m2m-token` and is therefore `isM2M`. That is the DEFAULT reading of "machine callers only" on purpose: measured live on the reporting project, the narrow line would have cut invitation-accept and job publishing, which reach these apis through exactly such a hop.

`machineWithoutUserIdentity` is the labelled EXCEPTION: machine caller AND no user identity resolved at all, so it ALSO REFUSES the forwarded hop (403 `M2M_CALLER_WITHOUT_USER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`). Declare it only for an api that must never run on behalf of a person — a key-rotation or tenant-provisioning surface — and expect it to refuse any internal caller that forwards its bearer. If you are unsure which you want, you want `machine`.

BOTH refuse before any role, permission or ownership gate and are NOT bypassed by `absoluteRoles`: an absolute role is a statement about a PERSON, and the point of this field is that no person may call. Cron and in-process `internal` triggers are exempt — they have no HTTP caller and already run as a trusted system job, the same exemption `checkValidLogin` makes. A KAFKA dispatch (the api's `kafkaSettings` consumer) satisfies the machine half of this gate too: no human stands behind a consumed event, and framework-published events (dbEvents, route events) carry no `x-m2m-token`, so `machine` admits every message the kafka controller dispatches instead of answering 403 `M2M_CALLER_REQUIRED` and dropping it. That is the ONLY gate kafka satisfies — it is not a trusted system job: `loginRequired`, the role, permission and ownership gates still run against the session the event carries (its `actor`), and `machineWithoutUserIdentity` still refuses an event whose `actor` names a user, which a framework dbEvent usually does (it carries the originating user). Current design-time validation requires `M2MAllowed: true` beside a machine kind on a `loginRequired: true` api (MACHINE_CALLER_KIND_WITHOUT_M2M_ALLOWED). This admits session-less token callers through the login gate; Kafka events carrying a user actor still undergo ordinary user login checks. A `checkRoles` list beside a machine kind currently produces MACHINE_CALLER_KIND_WITH_ROLE_GATE. That warning does not disable roles: a Kafka actor or a user forwarded on an InterService hop can carry a role, and the runtime still enforces the declared role gate for that identity. See `M2MAllowed` for the four-caller table. The auth role-write door needs `machineWithoutUserIdentity`: an authored auth api may write the user's `roleId` only when no session-bearing caller, forwarded identity included, can reach it; `machine` does not open it. Lane status: this gate is enforced in nodejs, python, dotnet, java, rust and golang. Its carry onto the JobStream enqueue edge (JobStreamAccess.enqueueAccess) is enforced in all of them except golang, whose enqueue gate does not carry the caller-kind field yet.
ApiAuthOptions.__loginRequired.doc: Specifies whether the user must be authenticated to access the API. By default, this inherits the login requirement from the associated data object, but it can be overridden here. `false` means PUBLIC, and it is not one relaxed flag beside the others: it turns the WHOLE authorization pipeline off. No checkBasicAuth override is generated, the role lists never reach the manager, and ApiManager short-circuits checkValidLogin, every role, permission, ownership and parent-ownership check on this single flag — including the M2M demand, so `M2MAllowed: true` beside it gates nothing. Pairing it with a role/permission/ownership gate is refused as PUBLIC_API_WITH_ROLE_GATE, and pairing it with an explicit `M2MAllowed: true` is reported as PUBLIC_API_WITH_M2M_ONLY_INTENT.
ApiAuthOptions.__queueTokenRequired.doc: The name of a `WaitingRoom` (services.waitingRooms[].roomBasics.name or its codeName in THIS service; the stamp is the room key, codeName when set, else name) whose admission `QueToken` this API requires. An ADDITIONAL gate beyond login/M2M (M2M-parity in shape): when set, the API stays publicly routed but the caller must present a valid, unexpired, queue-scoped QueToken minted by that WaitingRoom; the codegen pass emits a Redis one-shot check (token exists + not consumed + matches this room) that consumes the token on success (per the room's QueTokenSettings.singleUse). Empty/absent = no admission gate. This is the only BusinessApi change a WaitingRoom binding implies (the WaitingRoom binding sets this automatically when it fronts the API; it can also be declared by hand). Combine with loginRequired/checkRoles as usual.
ApiAuthOptions.__ownershipCheck.doc: Defines whether ownership should be enforced on the main data object. This check restricts access to the object’s owner and will be applied via the query in list operations and after the instance is fetched in others. On golang a DataView read (apiOptions.dataViewName on a list or get api) and a serviceLayerCall api carry no ownership gate, so declaring it there is the non-bypassable validation error API_AUTH_GATE_NOT_GENERATED (the same for permissionCheck and foreignPermissionCheck).
ApiAuthOptions.__parentOwnershipChecks.doc: A list of PARENT-ownership gates. Where `ownershipCheck` gates on the caller owning THIS object, each entry here gates on the caller owning a PARENT record the request is created under or acts on. At runtime the generated manager fetches the parent row named by `parentObject` using the id carried in the request field `parentIdField`, and DENIES (403) unless the parent row's `ownerField` equals the session userId (a missing parent row is also a 403). This expresses the create-under-parent / modify-child-if-you-own-the-parent case that `ownershipCheck` cannot (no target row exists yet on a create) and that `permissionCheck` cannot (RBAC/membership, not ownership). Runs right after `checkBasicAuth`, before the main operation. Empty = no parent-ownership gate.
ApiAuthOptions.__absoluteRoles.doc: A list of role names that grant unconditional access to this API in terms of authentication and authorization. Users with any of these roles will bypass all auth checks—including role, permission, ownership, and membership and custom 401-403 validations. However, business-level validations (e.g., required fields, value constraints) will still apply to ensure domain correctness. NOT THE WHOLE LIST THE GENERATED CODE GETS: every login-required api is EMITTED with `superAdmin` in its absolute-role list whether or not it appears here, and `tenantOwner` is added automatically wherever the tenant filter is in force on the api (a tenant-scoped object, and not a SaaS-level api). Exactly those two roles are automatic - not `tenantAdmin`. Those operator roles live one layer BELOW the blueprint on purpose - a blueprint default invites exceptions and drifts, and a designer or an agent that forgets them is exactly how a legitimate operator, or a tenant owner on their own tenant, ends up refused - so do not add them here and do not expect to read them back here. Whatever you DO declare survives: the emitted list is the UNION of your entries with the automatic ones, de-duplicated case-insensitively (the same case-folded role identity the runtime compares with), never a substitution. The `tenantOwner` arm RIDES THE TENANT FILTER for a reason: an absolute role bypasses every authorization check but NEVER the tenant scope, so on a tenant-scoped api the owner reaches its own tenant and nothing else. Where no tenant filter stands behind the gate - a SaaS-level api (`apiInSaasLevel: true`), an api over a non-tenant-scoped object such as a shared catalog, or a CREATE api (a create emits no where clause at all, so no tenant term ever rides it - only the create-time session stamp, which an authored tenant-column `dataClauseItems` entry overrides by design) - `tenantOwner` is NOT automatic, because that is exactly the surface where making it automatic once produced a live privilege escalation (anyone who registered their own tenant listing all tenants, editing the shared plan catalog, writing billing rows, or minting a row straight into another tenant through a provisioning create); there, only `superAdmin` is automatic and you declare any tenant role you need yourself. The automatic roles are added only where the gate can run: `loginRequired: false` switches the whole authorization pipeline off, so a public api still emits exactly what it authored. None of this reaches tenant isolation - the tenant filter is assembled separately and is never bypassed by an absolute role, and `apiInSaasLevel` remains the only declared cross-tenant surface. The bypass includes the FOREIGN permission gate (`foreignPermissionCheck`): a session holding an absolute role - authored here or one of the automatic `superAdmin` / `tenantOwner` pair - skips the project's `foreignPermissionProvider` exactly as it skips the native role, permission and ownership gates; the provider is never called for it (no round-trip, so an unreachable provider does not refuse it either), and there is no per-api opt-out. absoluteRoles ALONE IS NOT A GATE: with no checkRoles, enforceable ownershipCheck, permission check, liveCheck membership check, 401/403 validation, session-scoped whereClause, membershipFilters entry (list apis) or well-formed parentOwnershipChecks entry (only where the generated manager carries that gate: not on the retired php lane) beside it, every other logged-in user falls through and can call the api. The validator reports that shape as ABSOLUTE_ROLES_WITHOUT_GATE - an ERROR everywhere: validateProject / validateService fail, every build and regeneration fails, and a normal save of the project, service, api or its auth block is refused - for an api saved long ago exactly as for a new one. Add checkRoles (usually the same roles, e.g. absoluteRoles: ["admin"] with checkRoles: ["admin"]) to make it operator-only, set an enforceable ownershipCheck if the row's owner may call it, declare a parentOwnershipChecks entry (parentObject, parentIdField, ownerField) if the owner of the PARENT row may call it, or remove absoluteRoles (keep loginRequired: true) if it is meant to be open to every logged-in user. A save that must land before the fix (two errors blocking each other's fix) may pass skipValidation: true, which skips every save-time check; validate and build still report it. CART READS: on a get / list api over the shopping cart object this list holds operator roles only - superAdmin, admin, saasAdmin in a single-tenant project; superAdmin, saasAdmin in a multi-tenant one, plus tenantOwner / tenantAdmin only where the api's tenant filter is in force (a tenant-level cart object and no apiInSaasLevel; the auto-generated cart is tenant-level in a multi-tenant project generated in nodejs, and platform-level elsewhere), because a tenant administrator bypasses the owner gate but not the tenant scope and would otherwise read every tenant's carts. Anything else is CART_READ_API_SHOPPER_ABSOLUTE_ROLE (ERROR, non-bypassable). CART LINES AND CART READ ACTIONS: the same rule holds on a get / list api over the cart item object and on an api holding a read action onto the cart or its lines - tenantOwner / tenantAdmin count as operators only where that read's tenant filter is in force (the item api's own filter, or the action's tenant pin on its target; the auto-generated cart item is tenant-level in a multi-tenant nodejs service), and the tenantOwner the generated gate adds on its own counts too; anything else is CART_READ_SURFACE_NOT_SCOPED (ERROR, non-bypassable). Undefined designer gate roles receive the UNDEFINED_GATE_ROLE warning, including entries in absoluteRoles.
ApiAuthOptions.__checkRoles.doc: A list of roles that are required to pass basic role checks for this API. These are not absolute—users with these roles still undergo other validations and access control checks unless also included in `absoluteRoles`. Multiple roles are combined using OR logic. CART LINES AND CART READ ACTIONS: on a get / list api over the cart item object, or an api holding a read action onto the cart or its lines, this list holds operator roles only - superAdmin / admin / saasAdmin single-tenant; superAdmin / saasAdmin multi-tenant, plus tenantOwner / tenantAdmin only where that read's tenant filter is in force (the auto-generated cart item is tenant-level in a multi-tenant nodejs service); anything else is CART_READ_SURFACE_NOT_SCOPED (ERROR, non-bypassable). Designer API gates naming a role absent from the project receive UNDEFINED_GATE_ROLE as a warning; on a login-required api a list whose EVERY name is undefined is UNDEFINED_GATE_ROLE as an error (the api admits no defined-role session), unless `absoluteRoles` names a defined role, which keeps the warning. A business membership accessLevel is not a session role. Framework-injected APIs and project-free validation are exempt.
ApiAuthOptions.__defaultPermissions.movedNote: `defaultPermissions` was RETIRED on 2026-08-01. It was declared and shape-validated but read by no emitter and no runtime library, so a caller was never asked to hold the named permissions — the declaration enforced nothing. The supported route is `permissionCheck` (ADR-native-permission-system §9.5), whose gate the generated route-manager arms and `ApiManager.checkPermission` runs. It takes ONE permission name, not an AND-set: declare the permission that actually gates this API and express any further condition with a `PermissionCheckAction` / `ObjectPermissionCheckAction` in the workflow.
ApiAuthOptions.__foreignPermissionCheck.doc: Opt this API into the project's FOREIGN permission server (declared once on `authentication.foreignPermissionProvider`). When both this and the project provider are present, the runtime gate sends a request shaped from `foreignPermissionCheck.params` (a free MScript map evaluated against the api context `this`) plus the provider's `sessionBindings` to the foreign policy engine and denies (403 by default) when the server's response trips the provider's `denyWhen`. The params are whatever the permission server expects — the framework does not interpret the keys. Leave null for no foreign check. Not asked for an absolute-role session: `absoluteRoles`, including the automatic `superAdmin` / `tenantOwner` pair, bypasses this gate like every other authorization check, with no per-api opt-out; the tenant filter still applies.
ApiAuthOptions.__machineSessionRetirement.doc: Grants this api ONE machine capability: retiring every session of the user the api itself resolved. Only on an authored auth api (`authentication.businessLogic`) whose main data object is `user`, with crudType `get` or `update`, `M2MAllowed: true` and `loginRequired` left on; the validator refuses it anywhere else (MACHINE_SESSION_RETIREMENT_OUTSIDE_AUTH, MACHINE_SESSION_RETIREMENT_SHAPE) and on an auth service generated in a language that does not emit it yet (MACHINE_SESSION_RETIREMENT_LANGUAGE; nodejs, java, dotnet and rust emit it). The framework then binds a retire action right after the main operation (`afterMainGetOperation` / `afterMainUpdateOperation`, which run only when the operation resolved a row), so EVERY successful call retires the addressed user's sessions: access sessions, refresh families and owner-index entries, plus the user's invalidation epoch, which also ends cached api-key sessions and any session the owner index never held; the userSession rows of the retired sessions are marked loggedOut. WHO may retire: a VERIFIED, ADMITTED `x-m2m-token` caller that names no user (a token naming a user is that user, not a machine), and only within the target's own tenant: in a multi-tenant project the user's tenant must be the tenant the request resolved, and a token that signs a `callerTenantId` must name that same tenant; a superAdmin account is refused (403 MACHINE_SESSION_RETIREMENT_REFUSED). A person calling the same api keeps the self / admin gate of the session store, unchanged. The target is never a request value: it is the row the api's own (tenant-pinned) main operation read. Typical use: a machine-only `blockAccount` update api that writes the blocked state and, with this flag, ends the account's sessions in the same call.
ApiAuthOptions.__permissionCheck.doc:
Opt this API into the project's NATIVE permission resolver (ADR-native-permission-system §10). When set, the runtime gate calls `decide(permission, objectId, on, ctx)` on the project's permission manager and DENIES (403) when the layered resolution (object/user override → membership → global role → ownership) returns `{ effect: 'DENY' }`. `permission` is a declared `PermissionGroup` permission name; the optional `on` is a PropRefer to a request field carrying the parent/scope object id (for membership-role checks against a parent). Runs at a TYPE level right after `checkBasicAuth` (covers create/list — no objectId) AND at an OBJECT level after the instance fetch (get/update/delete — objectId available). Null = no native check (legacy `checkRoles`/`ownershipCheck` resolve byte-identically to today).

REQUIRES PERMISSION MANAGEMENT — `authentication.accessControl.permissionBasics.pbacIsActive` must be on. With it off the permission resolver IS NEVER GENERATED, so the gate is emitted against nothing and answers DENY (deny-by-default) before ANY layer runs: not the store-backed layers, not the CONFIG-ONLY membership layer, not even the absolute-role bypass. Every caller is refused — the record's own owner and superAdmin included — with a message that reads like a policy decision rather than a missing resolver, and a guarded `list` narrows to zero rows through the same deny-closed filter. This is a design-time ERROR (`PERMISSION_CHECK_WITHOUT_PBAC`). Enabling PBAC is a project-wide decision to adopt permission management, not the local fix for one api: without it, gate on `checkRoles`/`absoluteRoles`, `ownershipCheck`, or a MembershipCheckAction's `requiredRoles`.

REACHED FROM AN AI AGENT TOOL: an agent tool bound to this api on the same service (an `apiTools` entry, or a `crudScopes` CRUD tool whose operation this api serves) runs this gate with the CALLER's session manager, so the verdict is the one the same caller gets over REST. A run with no HTTP caller (a Kafka- or cron-triggered agent, a run resumed after an approval pause or a restart) carries no session manager, and the gate then REFUSES the tool call (403) instead of passing it. Gate an api that an event-driven agent must call with `checkRoles` / `ownershipCheck` instead. REACHED FROM A KAFKA CONTROLLER OR A JOBSTREAM WORKER: neither door carries a session manager (the identity is the event envelope's actor, or the session the enqueue gate forwarded), so the permission cannot be decided there and the call is REFUSED (403) - a JobStream job is marked failed - after the api's absoluteRoles and a verified machine caller it admits, which still pass; cron and internal calls keep their bypass. Validation warns about such an api (PERMISSION_CHECK_ON_CALLERLESS_DOOR). Gate an event-driven api with `checkRoles` / `absoluteRoles`, or `ownershipCheck` where it applies. REACHED FROM A GRPC CONTROLLER: the session manager is attached to a gRPC call only when its credential resolves a session, and such a call is decided exactly as over REST; a call that resolved no session is REFUSED (403, PERMISSION_DENIED) after the same absoluteRoles and machine-caller arms. It reaches the gate only when `loginRequired` is false, and validation warns about that combination with a gRPC controller (PERMISSION_CHECK_ON_CALLERLESS_DOOR, door grpc); set `loginRequired: true` to have every gRPC caller decided.
ApiAuthOptions.__requireApproval.doc:
Step-up APPROVAL for a critical operation: the api answers its first call with 403 APPROVAL_REQUIRED and sends a one-time code to the caller's own verified email or mobile. The caller repeats the SAME request with `api-approval-id` and `api-approval-code` (REST: headers, or the same two fields in the JSON body; gRPC / MCP: the request envelope; never the query string) and the api runs. The 403 is the EXPECTED first answer of such an api, not a failure: a frontend shows a code input and retries, a test treats it as a step. The challenge rides the problem body's `errors` member: `{ approvalId, channel, codeIndex, expireTime, expiresAt, actionName, actionDescription }`.

WHERE THE GATE SITS: a fixed milestone of the api pipeline, never a designer stage. It runs AFTER every authorization check (login, checkRoles / absoluteRoles, permissionCheck, ownershipCheck, parentOwnershipChecks, the parameter checks and every hook up to afterCheckBasicAuth) and BEFORE the first stage that may write: for create / list / a get that fetches no instance, right before buildWhereClause / buildDataClause; for update / delete and an ownership-checked get, right after afterCheckInstance and the object-level permission check, before buildDataClause and the main operation. So a caller who is not allowed to run the api can never make it send a code, and nothing from buildDataClause on runs before the approval. An action that writes the database in a stage BEFORE the milestone runs on the challenged first call too, which is reported as APPROVAL_GATE_AFTER_WRITE.

BOUND TO THE INPUT (`bindInput`, default true): the code approves exactly this user, this api of this service and the canonical digest of the api's declared request parameters (the `useIdempotencyKey` hash rule). A retry with a changed parameter, another api, another user, a wrong, expired or already used code is refused with ONE failure shape, 403 APPROVAL_INVALID. A wrong code or a changed input counts an attempt; the fifth destroys the approval, and a new call without `api-approval-id` starts a new one. A second first call inside 60 seconds with the same input answers the same challenge again without a second message; with another input it answers 429 APPROVAL_RESEND_WINDOW.

TEST MODE: on the preview and dev deployments the challenge also carries the code (`errors.secretCode`), so a harness or a designer completes it without a mailbox; on stage and production it never does. DOORS: cron and in-process internal calls pass; a kafka-consumed or job-stream call, a machine caller with no user and an agent run with no caller are refused 403 APPROVAL_NOT_AVAILABLE (nobody there can receive a code); an idempotent replay (`useIdempotencyKey`) answers the response the approved execution stored. Over SSE the stream's error frame carries APPROVAL_REQUIRED but not the approvalId, so a streaming client takes the challenge from the REST route first (APPROVAL_ON_SSE_CONTROLLER). Requires `loginRequired: true` (APPROVAL_REQUIRES_LOGIN), no machine-only `requiredCallerKind` (APPROVAL_ON_MACHINE_API), a channel whose identity is REQUIRED on the project's users (APPROVAL_ON_OPTIONAL_IDENTITY) and, until the remaining language lanes port it, a nodejs, dotnet, java or rust service (APPROVAL_NOT_PORTED: another lane would run the api unapproved). It is the ONLY approval surface: the standalone action-approve verification flows are retired, and approving from another device by a link is not supported yet. Leave null for an ordinary api.

__ApiForeignPermissionCheck.doc: Per-BusinessApi foreign-permission question. `params` is a FREE MScript map (arbitrary keys; each value MScript evaluated against the api context `this`) sent to the project's `foreignPermissionProvider`. `denyMessage` is an optional manual 403 message overriding the provider's `messageFrom`.

ApiForeignPermissionCheck.__params.doc: The free MScript map sent to the permission server. Each entry maps a request key to an MScript expression evaluated against the api context (`this.session`, the read params, the fetched instance, etc.) — exactly the pattern GrpcCallAction.request.fields / ApiCallAction body params use. It is whatever the permission server expects; the framework does not interpret the keys. Merged with the provider's `sessionBindings` to form the request.
ApiForeignPermissionCheck.__denyMessage.doc: Optional manual user-facing 403 message. Takes precedence over the provider's `messageFrom(result)` when the check denies. Omit to let the provider derive the message.

__ApiPermissionCheck.doc: Per-BusinessApi NATIVE permission gate (ADR-native-permission-system §9.5). `permission` is a declared `PermissionGroup` permission name the caller must hold for this API; the runtime resolver decides it through the layered model (object/user override → object-role → multi-scope membership → global role → ownership). `scopeFields` is an OPTIONAL multi-scope channel: the request/instance FK fields whose ids form the `scopeMap` the resolver checks object-roles (L3) + memberships (L4) on. This is the native counterpart to `foreignPermissionCheck` (the two are mutually exclusive per API).

ApiPermissionCheck.__permission.doc: The permission name the caller must hold. Must resolve to a permission declared in a `PermissionGroup` (RBACSettings). The resolver checks it against the subject's overrides, object-roles, memberships, global role grants, and ownership per the ADR §5 precedence.
ApiPermissionCheck.__scopeFields.doc:
OPTIONAL multi-scope channel (ADR-native-permission-system §5.0/§9.5). The target object's own declared scope-FK fields whose ids form the `scopeMap` ({scopeName→scopeObjectId}) the resolver checks object-roles (L3) and memberships (L4) on (union across scopes). Two forms: an ARRAY of FK field names (`['orgId','projectId']`) — each scope name is the field minus a trailing `Id` (`orgId→org`); or a MAP of explicit `{ scopeName: fkField }` (`{ org: 'orgId', project: 'parentProjectId' }`) when the scope name must differ from the field. The runtime gate reads each field off the request/fetched instance and threads `decide(permission, scopeMap, objectId)`. Omit for a single-object check (scopeMap empty → L4 abstains, L3 falls back to the objectId).

THE SCOPE NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: it must equal the SCOPE OBJECT'S OWN NAME, because that is the key the compiled membership config is built with. `['organizationId']` derives `organization`, which works only if the membership-bearing object is named `organization`; when it is not, name it explicitly (`{ org: 'orgId' }` for an object called `org`). A name that matches no membership-bearing object is silently fatal at runtime — the membership layer abstains, a single record falls through to deny-by-default and a list narrows to zero rows, with no diagnostic anywhere — so it is a design-time ERROR (`PERMISSION_CHECK_SCOPE_UNKNOWN`).

__ApiParentOwnershipCheck.doc: One PARENT-ownership gate for a Business API. At runtime the generated manager fetches the parent row and DENIES (403) unless the caller owns it. `parentObject` names the parent DataObject (in THIS service) whose row is fetched by id; `parentIdField` is the request field carrying that parent row's id; `ownerField` is the session-bound owner property ON the parent object compared against the caller's session userId. Distinct from `ownershipCheck` (which gates the target row itself) — use this for create-under-parent and modify-child-if-you-own-the-parent. LANGUAGE NOTE: every selectable service language emits this gate (nodejs, java, python, dotnet, golang and rust), on every api shape, golang DataView reads (apiOptions.dataViewName on a list or get api) and serviceLayerCall apis included. On the retired php lane, which carries no such gate, a declared parentOwnershipChecks list is the non-bypassable validation error PARENT_OWNERSHIP_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE. The language is the one the service is built in, a build-language override included.

ApiParentOwnershipCheck.__parentIdField.doc: The request field (body param or url segment) holding the id of the parent row to authorize against. Read off the api context (`this.<field>`) at gate time.
ApiParentOwnershipCheck.__parentObject.doc: The parent DataObject name (a data object in THIS service) whose row is fetched by id to check ownership.
ApiParentOwnershipCheck.__ownerField.doc: The session-bound owner property ON `parentObject` (a property flagged sessionSettings.isOwnerField=true) compared against the caller's session userId. 403 when they differ, when the parent row is missing, or when the owner column is null.

__ApiApprovalChannel.doc.#: The channel a Business API step-up approval code is sent through, the `channel` of ApiApprovalRequirement. The caller's session must carry that identifier, verified.
__ApiApprovalChannel.doc.email: The code goes to the caller's verified email address (session `email` with `emailVerified: true`). Default code lifetime 900 seconds.
__ApiApprovalChannel.doc.mobile: The code goes to the caller's verified mobile number by SMS (session `mobile` with `mobileVerified: true`); the project's user must have a mobile identifier. Default code lifetime 300 seconds.

__ApiApprovalRequirement.doc: The step-up approval requirement of one Business API: the channel of its one-time code, the input binding, the code lifetime and the action text the message shows. It is the value of `authOptions.requireApproval`. The api answers 403 APPROVAL_REQUIRED until the caller repeats the same request with `api-approval-id` and `api-approval-code`; see ApiAuthOptions.requireApproval for the pipeline position, the doors and the failure shapes.

ApiApprovalRequirement.__channel.doc: Where the code is sent: `email` (the caller's verified email) or `mobile` (the caller's verified mobile, by SMS). The message is the framework's approval message, sent through the notification service like the verification codes (event `apiApprovalByEmail` / `apiApprovalByMobile` on the `<codename>-auth-service-<channel>-actApp-start` topic, derived whenever an api declares the channel). The channel's identity must be a REQUIRED identity of the project's users (APPROVAL_ON_OPTIONAL_IDENTITY otherwise). A caller whose session has no VERIFIED identifier of this channel is refused 403 APPROVAL_NOT_AVAILABLE and nothing is sent.
ApiApprovalRequirement.__bindInput.doc: When true (the default), the approval is bound to the api's declared request parameters: the retry must carry the same values, or it is refused 403 APPROVAL_INVALID. The binding is the canonical digest the `useIdempotencyKey` check uses, so a changed amount or target can never ride an approval given for another one. False binds the approval to the user and the api only, which lets the retry change the input the user approved; it is reported as APPROVAL_UNBOUND_INPUT.
ApiApprovalRequirement.__expireTimeWindow.doc: How long the code stays valid, in seconds. Null takes the channel default: 900 (15 minutes) for email, 300 (5 minutes) for mobile. A positive integer; the record is stored with this TTL and is gone afterwards.
ApiApprovalRequirement.__actionName.doc: A short name of the operation the user approves (at most 64 characters), shown in the approval message and returned in the challenge. The client reads it from the challenge's `errors` member to say what is being approved. Plain text; the message escapes markup.
ApiApprovalRequirement.__actionDescription.doc: An optional longer description of the operation (at most 256 characters), shown in the approval message and returned in the challenge. Plain text; the message escapes markup.

__BusinessApiActionStore.doc: Represents the centralized registry of all executable logic units (actions) that can be used inside a Business API's workflow. Each action is categorized by purpose and referenced by name within the workflow stages. This store enables declarative composition of API behavior, including data manipulation, inter-service communication, access control, AI operations, and more. Every array here is optional — include only the action-type arrays you use; omitted arrays normalize to [] server-side.

BusinessApiActionStore.__fetchObjectActions.doc: Actions that fetch a related or foreign object instance from another data object, based on a matching key or query.
BusinessApiActionStore.__fetchStatsActions.doc: Actions that perform aggregate computations (count, sum, min, max) across a data object, often for contextual summaries or conditional logic.
BusinessApiActionStore.__fetchParentActions.doc: Actions that retrieve parent object data of the current context, typically for display enrichment or validation.
BusinessApiActionStore.__searchObjectActions.doc: Actions that searches the main object or a related object in elastic search index with a keyword and returns an id array
BusinessApiActionStore.__fetchFromElasticActions.doc: Actions that make a fetch from elastic using a raw elastic query, the result is returned as a normalized `{ items: [], aggregations: {} }` object.
BusinessApiActionStore.__collateListsActions.doc: Actions that collate objects of a source array to a target array's objects using key matching like collating an address list with a user list.
BusinessApiActionStore.__functionCallActions.doc: Actions that invoke a custom or reusable library function written in MScript. Useful for transformation, derived value computation, or conditional logic.
BusinessApiActionStore.__arrowFunctionActions.doc: Actions that defines an arrow function to be called with its context name in other MScripted areas.
BusinessApiActionStore.__listMapActions.doc: Actions that defines a list map, to create a new list out of a current list by mapping its items. Renders a js array map function.
BusinessApiActionStore.__interserviceCallActions.doc: Actions that perform a call to another Business API defined in a different microservice. These enable inter-service orchestration.
BusinessApiActionStore.__interProjectCallActions.doc: Actions that call a Business API published by a LINKED SIBLING PROJECT (same organization, linked via addSiblingProject). These enable inter-project orchestration across separately deployed OpenAPPL projects.
BusinessApiActionStore.__createCrudActions.doc: Actions that create related records in other data objects during or after the main operation. Often used in cascading aggregations — cascading, NOT transactional: each child write commits on its own and is never rolled back when a later action throws (see the failure-semantics section of BusinessWorkflow).
BusinessApiActionStore.__createBulkCrudActions.doc: Actions that create multiple related child or linked objects in bulk. Useful when creating multiple child records at once, such as bulk creating child tasks, audit logs, or attachments. The objects parameter is an MScript expression that evaluates to an array of objects to be created.
BusinessApiActionStore.__upsertBulkCrudActions.doc: Actions that write an array of rows into a data object with insert-or-update semantics: each row is matched to an existing row by the matchBy key and inserted, updated, skipped or rejected according to matchMode, with per-column onExisting policies for enrichment (fillIfEmpty, keep, compute). The bulk import twin of createBulkCrudActions.
BusinessApiActionStore.__deleteCrudActions.doc: Actions that delete related child or linked objects. Useful in cleanup workflows or cascade logic.
BusinessApiActionStore.__updateCrudActions.doc: Actions that update properties of related objects using a conditional query. Used for post-processing or child updates.
BusinessApiActionStore.__apiCallActions.doc: Actions that make external or internal HTTP API requests. Often used to integrate with third-party systems or auxiliary internal services.
BusinessApiActionStore.__grpcCallActions.doc: Actions that call a FOREIGN (non-OpenAPPL) gRPC server declared in this service's `serviceSettings.grpcClients[]` (docs/ADR-grpc-interservice-and-grpccall.md, Part B). The gRPC analogue of ApiCallAction: instead of a URL it targets a named grpcClient + rpc method, builds the proto Request from compiled MScript fields, and rides the shared grpcUnaryCall engine.
BusinessApiActionStore.__aiCallActions.doc: Actions that call an LLM (e.g., OpenAI or Anthropic) with structured prompts and fetch textual or JSON responses. Used for generation, enrichment, or inference.
BusinessApiActionStore.__decisionActions.doc: Actions that ask a calibrated decision provider typed questions about a piece of state and get back typed answers with honest probabilities - classification, routing, scoring and gating without text generation. Cheaper and faster than aiCallActions for a decision, and its answer is always one of the declared values (which is not the same as always right); it cannot explain itself, so it never decides authorization.
BusinessApiActionStore.__agentCallActions.doc: Actions that invoke a configured AI Agent defined in the service's aiAgents section. The agent is executed internally with a data payload built from the current API context via MScript. The result is stored in the workflow context and optionally written to the response.
BusinessApiActionStore.__membershipCheckActions.doc: Actions that validate whether a user is a member of a related object (e.g., organization, team) using configured membership rules.
BusinessApiActionStore.__permissionCheckActions.doc: Actions that verify whether the current user has a global (non-object-scoped) permission before continuing workflow logic.
BusinessApiActionStore.__objectPermissionActions.doc: Actions that check object-scoped permissions, validating whether a user has specific rights on an instance loaded into the context.
BusinessApiActionStore.__readJwtTokenActions.doc: Actions that read a JWT encoded token from a reference and write its back to context as a validatedd and decoded payloa dobject.
BusinessApiActionStore.__validationActions.doc: Custom validation logic actions that run MScript boolean checks and optionally block further execution based on result.
BusinessApiActionStore.__addToContextActions.doc: Actions that write computed or fixed values to the runtime context (`this`) for later use in logic, conditions, or response shaping.
BusinessApiActionStore.__addToResponseActions.doc: Actions that explicitly add computed values or context properties to the final API response payload.
BusinessApiActionStore.__removeFromResponseActions.doc: Actions that remove properties from the API response before it is sent to the client. Used for cleanup or filtering.
BusinessApiActionStore.__renderDataActions.doc: Actions that apply a template (e.g., EJS/Markdown) to context data to generate rendered output.
BusinessApiActionStore.__dataToFileActions.doc: Actions that serialize a context object into a downloadable file format (e.g., CSV, JSON, TXT). For PDF rendering, use renderPdfActions instead.
BusinessApiActionStore.__fileToDataActions.doc: Actions that parse an uploaded or stored tabular file (csv, tsv, xlsx, json, ndjson) into an array of row objects keyed by data-model property names, coercing and validating every cell against the target DataObject's properties. The parsed rows land in the context for a following upsertBulkCrudActions / createBulkCrudActions step; rejected rows are collected with their row index and reasons.
BusinessApiActionStore.__renderPdfActions.doc: Actions that render a PDF from a PdfTemplate (or pre-rendered HTML) and store the resulting buffer in the context for use by later actions — typically attached to a SendMailAction or returned to the client as a download.
BusinessApiActionStore.__redirectActions.doc: Actions that redirect the API response to another URL or internal API path. Typically used in post-auth flows or chained APIs.
BusinessApiActionStore.__createJWTTokenActions.doc: Actions that create JWT tokens with a payload and store them in context or response.
BusinessApiActionStore.__signDataWithProjectKeyActions.doc: Actions that sign arbitrary data with the project's Ed25519 key and return a verifiable envelope (`{ sig, kid, jwks_url }`). Use the result anywhere — webhook headers, response bodies, downstream API calls — to let receivers confirm the data originated from this project by fetching the project JWKS.
BusinessApiActionStore.__createObjectActions.doc: Actions that create javascript objects in the context.
BusinessApiActionStore.__publishEventActions.doc: Actions that emit custom domain events to a message bus or pub/sub system. Used for decoupled workflows, domain events, or business-specific notifications. The action's message is published inside the unified event envelope — consumers find it under the envelope's `data` key (`{ id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data }`); the declared topic is PROJECT-SCOPED on the wire as `<projectCodename>-<topic>`, so a consumer inside the project subscribes to the same declared name and the framework scopes both ends, while a hand-written consumer passes the declared name to KafkaListener and lets the runtime resolve it. Note: When `raiseApiEvent` under `ApiOptions` is true, a standard API-level event is automatically emitted, so this should only contain additional custom events beyond the default API event.
BusinessApiActionStore.__readFromRedisActions.doc: Actions that read a Redis key directly and store its value into the context. This enables other actions—limited to context scope—to access Redis-sourced values.
BusinessApiActionStore.__writeToRedisActions.doc: Actions that write a value to Redis under a computed key, either for session continuity or caching.
BusinessApiActionStore.__sendMailActions.doc: Actions that send an email using a configured provider — or on behalf of a project MailAccount (with reply threading) via the mcpbff mail bridge — with dynamic subject/body/to fields.
BusinessApiActionStore.__checkMailboxActions.doc: Actions that pull filtered message summaries (envelope metadata, no bodies) from a project MailAccount's mailbox on demand, via the mcpbff mail bridge.
BusinessApiActionStore.__readMailActions.doc: Actions that fetch one full message — bodies plus attachment content — from a project MailAccount's mailbox by RFC 5322 messageId, via the mcpbff mail bridge.
BusinessApiActionStore.__sendSmsActions.doc: Actions that send an SMS message to a target phone number with a given body and sender info.
BusinessApiActionStore.__sendPushNotificationActions.doc: Actions that send push notifications to mobile or web clients with title and content.
BusinessApiActionStore.__sendWhatsAppActions.doc: Actions that send a WhatsApp Business message via a configured WhatsApp provider (Meta Cloud API or Twilio's WhatsApp channel). Supports both free-form text inside the 24-hour session window and template sends for re-engagement.
BusinessApiActionStore.__paymentActions.doc: Actions to start, to complete or to refresh a payment operation using the native integrated payment systems. Every provider registered in the PaymentProviderRegistry is supported (stripe, paypal, adyen, iyzico, paddle, lemonsqueezy, mangopay, plus the `custom` escape hatch); the action binds to an entry of projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[]. For a gateway with no native adapter use integration actions.
BusinessApiActionStore.__refundActions.doc: Actions that issue a refund (full or partial) against a previously captured payment via the bound PaymentProvider. The action writes a sys_<X>Refund record and advances the parent payment state machine.
BusinessApiActionStore.__invoiceActions.doc: Actions that drive the accounts-receivable invoice lifecycle (create draft / finalize / void / apply payment) for an invoicing-enabled DataObject through the generated InvoiceManager — the imperative escape hatch for issuePolicy: manual workflows (ADR-invoice-fiscalization §7.5). All operations go through the bound InvoiceProvider adapter, so the framework-internal ledger and an external system of record are one code path.
BusinessApiActionStore.__fiscalizeActions.doc: Actions that drive the regulatory fiscalization lifecycle (submit / cancel / queryStatus) for a fiscalization-enabled DataObject through the generated FiscalizationManager - the imperative escape hatch for submitPolicy: manual workflows (ADR-invoice-fiscalization sec. 7.5). Every operation goes through the bound FiscalProvider adapter and the compiled jurisdiction policy; there is no framework-internal fiscal provider.
BusinessApiActionStore.__payoutActions.doc: Actions that trigger a marketplace payout to a connected sub-merchant account via the bound PaymentProvider. Requires the provider to advertise supportsMarketplace=true. The action writes a sys_<X>Payout record whose status is later advanced via webhook events.
BusinessApiActionStore.__subscriptionActions.doc: Actions that create, cancel or refresh a recurring subscription against the bound PaymentProvider. The `stage` field on the action picks the operation (subscribe / cancelSubscription / refresh). Requires the provider to advertise supportsSubscriptions=true.
BusinessApiActionStore.__verifyWebhookActions.doc: Actions to verify a webhook call of a provider using the signature material held by the bound adapter. Every provider registered in the PaymentProviderRegistry is supported (stripe, paypal, adyen, iyzico, paddle, lemonsqueezy, mangopay, plus the `custom` escape hatch); the verification scheme comes from that provider's PaymentCapabilities.webhookStyle. An adapter that cannot verify at all (no signing secret yet) refuses with a `webhook_verification_unconfigured` 401 rather than reporting a signature failure.
BusinessApiActionStore.__integrationActions.doc: Actions that call third-party API integrations managed in the platform integration catalog (e.g., AWS S3, Stripe, Google Maps). Each integration exposes predefined actions and is selected by its provider key.
BusinessApiActionStore.__loopActions.doc: Actions that repeat a sequence of workflow steps for each item in a list (defined by an MScript expression).
BusinessApiActionStore.__parallelActions.doc: Actions that execute multiple child actions in parallel without waiting for each to finish sequentially. Ideal for non-dependent logic flows.
BusinessApiActionStore.__cartValidationActions.doc: Actions that validate a shopping cart before checkout. Checks for item existence, stock availability, price validity, and minimum order requirements.
BusinessApiActionStore.__cartCheckoutActions.doc: Actions that process shopping cart checkout. Handles inventory reservation, promotion recording, order creation, and cart clearing.
BusinessApiActionStore.__couponValidationActions.doc: Actions that validate coupon codes. Checks eligibility, usage limits, expiration, and calculates discount amounts.
BusinessApiActionStore.__emitSseEventActions.doc: Actions that emit custom SSE events to the client during the workflow. No-op when called via REST.
BusinessApiActionStore.__iteratorActions.doc: Generic streaming actions whose methods return async iterables. Used for custom streaming logic that isn't covered by AiCallAction. Can be referenced in streamSource.iteratorAction or used inline in the workflow.
BusinessApiActionStore.__videoRoomTokenActions.doc: VideoRoomTokenAction actions — run a declared service videoRooms[] room's authorization flow and mint the provider join credential (SFU join token with media grants, or an HLS playback grant for broadcast viewers). See docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §9.
BusinessApiActionStore.__videoRoomControlActions.doc: VideoRoomControlAction actions — control-plane operations against a declared service videoRooms[] room via its provider's server API (create/end room, remove/mute participant, start/stop recording or broadcast). See docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §9.
BusinessApiActionStore.__contentTransitionActions.doc: ContentTransitionAction actions — drive the publishing lifecycle of a declared service contentModels[] content record (publish / unpublish / schedule / unschedule / archive / restore) from inside a composed workflow. See docs/ADR-content-platform-pattern-family.md §7.
BusinessApiActionStore.__writeToElasticLogActions.doc: WriteToElasticLogAction actions — append an object to a declared ElasticLog (projectSettings.elasticLogsSettings.elasticLogs[]) by name, written directly to ES.
BusinessApiActionStore.__fetchFromElasticLogActions.doc: FetchFromElasticLogAction actions — query a declared ElasticLog by name with a raw Elasticsearch search body, read directly from ES.
BusinessApiActionStore.__graphQueryActions.doc: GraphQueryAction actions — run a parameterized graph traversal (a declared service.graphLayer.queries[] by name, or inline Cypher) against the service's Bolt driver pool, written/read directly (no interservice hop). See docs/ADR-graph-database-layer.md §8a.

__BusinessApiAction.doc: Abstract base class for all Business API actions. Every action in a Business API workflow inherits from this type. It defines shared fields such as name, execution condition, and response behavior. This class is never instantiated directly—subclasses implement specific logic units like fetch, validation, or API calls. Any subclass is distinguished from the array (in actions property of the business api) it is inserted

BusinessApiAction.__id.doc: The unique identifier of the action, used to reference this action from within a Business API workflow step.
BusinessApiAction.__name.doc: A unique human readable camle case name for the action , will also be used as the method name of the api context class.
BusinessApiAction.__description.doc: An optional text to describe the purpose and logic of the action, what it does and why it does.
BusinessApiAction.__condition.doc: An MScript boolean expression. If provided, the action will only run when this condition evaluates to true.
BusinessApiAction.__contextPropertyName.doc: The name of the property under which the result of the action will be written to the context. The result of an business api action can be accessed by other actions using `this.<contextPropertyName>`. Leave this field null if your action result will not be used by further actions. The value exists only AFTER this action runs: an MScript scheduled earlier — in an earlier stage, or earlier in the same stage's array — reads `undefined`, which in a `shouldBeTrue: false` validation action passes the guard vacuously. See the `workflow` ordering rules.
BusinessApiAction.__writeToResponse.doc: If true, the result of the action will be written to the API response directly, typically under the property matching the contextPropertyName.
BusinessApiAction.__onActionError.doc: Defines what happens when the action throws an error. `throwError` (default) re-throws, aborts the remaining pipeline and answers the caller with the error — but it rolls NOTHING back: every write this api already performed (the main CRUD operation, earlier crud actions, `interserviceCallAction` writes on other services, published events, sent mails) stays committed, so the request ends half-applied. See the failure-semantics section of `BusinessWorkflow`, and prefer ordering a failure-prone write into a pre-main stage. `completeApi` catches the error, stores it as `this.<actionName>Error` on the context so subsequent actions can inspect the failure, and lets the API continue. An `updateCrudAction` / `deleteCrudAction` whose selector matched NO row does not throw at all unless it also sets `onNoRows: throwError`, so `completeApi` alone cannot observe an empty match. Do not combine `completeApi` with a guard that is meant to abort the flow (a `validationActions`, `permissionCheckActions`, `objectPermissionActions` or `membershipCheckActions` entry whose effective `checkType` throws): the failure is only logged and the api continues into the branch the guard exists to prevent, and validation reports `GUARD_ACTION_NEUTRALIZED_BY_COMPLETE_API`. What an UNSET `checkType` means depends on the target language: the nodejs, java, dotnet, python, rust and golang emitters read it as `storedCheck` (no throw) for the permission/membership families; ValidationAction keeps its `liveCheck` (throwing) default, and the warning names the lane it judged; a saved project is judged on the lane its services are actually built for, and only a language-blind run (an offline or file-loaded validation) is fail-safe, warning as if the lane were one of the throwing ones. Use an explicit `checkType: "storedCheck"` for a check that is genuinely advisory.
BusinessApiAction.__emitProgressInSSEContext.doc: When true and the API is running in SSE context, this action automatically emits a progress event before and after execution. When false (default) or when called via REST, no progress is emitted.
BusinessApiAction.name: String

__BusinessApiActionErrorOption.doc.#: The option that defines what to do if a specific action causes an error.
__BusinessApiActionErrorOption.doc.throwError: Use this option if you want to fail the compile api in case of this specific action fails
__BusinessApiActionErrorOption.doc.completeApi: Use this option if you want your api to be completed even this specific action fails.

__BusinessApiActionNoRowsOption.doc.#: What an `updateCrudAction` / `deleteCrudAction` does when its whereClause matched NO row. The db-layer helpers resolve the affected rows as an array, so a selector that matched nothing resolves `[]` and, without this option, is indistinguishable from success: no error is raised, `onActionError` never fires and no `<actionName>Error` slot is written.
__BusinessApiActionNoRowsOption.doc.ignore: Default. A zero-row update / delete completes normally with an empty result (`this.<actionName>` is `[]`). Keep this for a deliberately broad selector that may legitimately match nothing.
__BusinessApiActionNoRowsOption.doc.throwError: A zero-row update / delete raises a typed 404 (`errorCode: ACTION_NO_ROWS_MATCHED`, an operator log line correlated by requestId) exactly like any other action error, so `onActionError` decides what happens next: `throwError` aborts the api with that 404, `completeApi` stores it as `this.<actionName>Error` and the api continues. Use it when the action addresses ONE specific row whose absence is a defect (a status stamp, a compensation, an owner binding).

__FetchObjectAction.doc: Fetches one or more records from a foreign or related data object and stores the result in the context or response. Supports key-based lookup or complex query filtering. Commonly used to enrich the current object with external data before proceeding with workflow logic. It can return null or raise a 404 error when no objects found according to isRequired property.

__FetchObjectAction.useCase.description: Use when a workflow needs to load a related or foreign record (and optionally enforce its existence) before continuing — e.g. fetch the customer behind an order so later steps can read its tier or email.

example.name: fetchCustomer
example.description: Load the customer that placed this order and 404 if it no longer exists.

FetchObjectAction.__targetObject.doc: Specifies the name of the foreign data object to fetch data from. Can reference a data object in the same service or any service within the same OpenAPPL application.
FetchObjectAction.__matchValue.doc: An MScript expression whose result will be used as the key to match against the target object's property. For example, `{ "js": "this.customerId" }`.
FetchObjectAction.__localKey.doc: The property of the target object used for matching — `id`, or any unique/indexed field like `email` or `slug`. There is NO compile-time default: the generated fetch adds its match term only when BOTH `matchValue` and `localKey` are set, so leaving `localKey` empty while `matchValue` is authored silently drops the match from the query. Validation REFUSES the blueprint with FETCH_MATCH_VALUE_WITHOUT_LOCAL_KEY (ERROR). Always set it when `matchValue` is used. An MScript slot is EMPTY when no language source in it carries anything: an absent slot, `null`, and the untouched multilanguage envelope the authoring panel scaffolds (`{ "js": null, "java": null, ... }`) all count as empty, so a section you have not authored yet is never refused.
FetchObjectAction.__properties.doc: An array of field names to include in the result. Leave empty to fetch all fields. Dot notation is allowed for nested fields (e.g., `profile.name`).
FetchObjectAction.__whereClause.doc: Optional MScript query to define an advanced condition for the fetch. It does NOT override `matchValue`/`localKey` — the generated fetch MERGES them: the whereClause query is evaluated first and the `localKey: matchValue` term is added on top (AND semantics; if the whereClause constrains the same key as `localKey`, the match term wins for that key). Leave `matchValue` empty when the whereClause alone should select the record.
FetchObjectAction.__isRequired.doc: Set to true if you want to use this fetch also for an existince validation. If isRequired is true, a null or empty result will create a 404 error, however this error either can be thrown or logged according to the onError property of the main action configuration.
FetchObjectAction.__isArray.doc: If true, the action will return a list of objects. If false, a single object is expected. This affects both response shape and loop behavior.

__SearchObjectAction.doc: Searches one or more records from the main data object or a foreign or related data object and stores the result in the context as an id array. The search is made in elastic search index and the returned id array can be used in the where clause of the main query.

__SearchObjectAction.useCase.description: Use when you need a full-text / keyword search over an Elasticsearch index to produce a list of matching record ids that a later query's where clause can filter on — e.g. resolve a user's search box input into candidate product ids.

example.name: searchProducts
example.description: Full-text search products by the caller's keyword to narrow the main listing query.

SearchObjectAction.__targetObject.doc: Specifies the name of the data object to make the search data from. Can reference to the main data object, a different data object in the same service or any service within the same OpenAPPL application.
SearchObjectAction.__keyword.doc: An MScript expression whose result will be used as the key to match against the target object's searched properties. For example, `{ "js": "this.keyword" }`.
SearchObjectAction.__searchProperties.doc: The properties of the target object used for matching. A stored-DataView-bound list accepts projected field and aggregate column paths from the view. Searchability warnings use each resolved source column mapping; bare stat or aggregate object names are not searchable columns.

__FetchFromElasticAction.doc: Fetches data object data from its elastic search index with a raw elastic search body, and stores a normalized ENVELOPE in the action's context property: `{ items, aggregations, total }`. `items` is the normalized hits array (each entry is the hit's `_source`, and top_hits style aggregations are normalized into it as well), `aggregations` is the elastic aggregation result or null, and `total` is the Elasticsearch total (`hits.total`, as a `{ value }` object or a bare number), falling back to the number of returned items only when the response carries no numeric total. The envelope is NOT unwrapped to a single hit, so a one-row lookup reads `this.<contextPropertyName>.items[0]?.<field>`; `this.<contextPropertyName>.<field>` is undefined by construction and is rejected at design time (CONTEXT_ENVELOPE_MEMBER_UNDEFINED).

__FetchFromElasticAction.useCase.description: Use when you need a raw Elasticsearch query (aggregations, custom scoring, collapsing, etc.) that the abstract query layer can't express — returns normalized items plus the raw aggregations object for dashboards and analytics.

example.name: topCategoriesByRevenue
example.description: Aggregate order revenue grouped by category for the storefront dashboard.

body.js: { size: 0, query: { range: { createdAt: { gte: this.fromDate } } }, aggs: { byCategory: { terms: { field: 'categoryId', size: 10 }, aggs: { revenue: { sum: { field: 'totalAmount' } } } } } }

FetchFromElasticAction.__targetObject.doc: Specifies the name of the data object to make the fetch data from. Can reference to the main data object, a different data object in the same service or any service within the same OpenAPPL application.
FetchFromElasticAction.__body.doc: An MScript expression which is evaluated a js object representing the elastic search api body. Note that this object uses elastics own operators and own query format not the abstract MScript query format.
FetchFromElasticAction.__properties.doc: The properties of the target object that is extracted from the _source of an hit.

__CollateListsAction.doc: Use CollateListsAction to collate a list of objects to another list of objects like aggregating an adress list to a user list.

__CollateListsAction.useCase.description: Use to stitch one fetched list onto another by a shared key — e.g. attach each user's address records onto the matching user object so the response carries nested data without N+1 queries.

example.name: attachAddressesToUsers
example.description: Group fetched addresses under each user by userId.

CollateListsAction.__sourceList.doc: An Mscript that will be evaluated to the source object array where the source objects will be collected from.
CollateListsAction.__targetList.doc: An MScript that will be evealuted to the target object array that the collected objects will be aggregated to.
CollateListsAction.__sourceKey.doc: The name of the property of the source object to match with the target object. If multiple objects are collected and targetIsArray is afalse, only the first object  will be aggregated.
CollateListsAction.__targetKey.doc: The name of the property of the target object to match with the osurce object. If multiple targets are found the source objects will be copied to all matching targets.
CollateListsAction.__nameInTarget.doc: The name of the property that will be created in the target object to store the copied source object or objects.
CollateListsAction.__targetIsArray.doc: Make this option true if you want the target property to be an array that will expect multiple source objects.

__FetchStatsAction.doc: An action used to compute inline aggregate statistics (e.g., count, min, max, sum) from a data object. Ideal for Business APIs that need quick numerical insights tied to context. Use for simple stat enrichment for single or multiple bindings; for complex use cases, consider dedicated stat APIs or BFF services. Note that this action collects the stat values from elastc search using aggregations features.

__FetchStatsAction.useCase.description: Use for quick inline aggregate metrics tied to the current context — counts, sums, min/max — optionally bucketed by a field, computed from Elasticsearch aggregations without a dedicated stats API.

example.name: projectTaskStats
example.description: Compute open-task counts and total estimated hours for the project in context.

FetchStatsAction.__targetObject.doc: The name of the data object from which statistical metrics will be aggregated. Can be a local or foreign object.
FetchStatsAction.__matchValue.doc: MScript expression for the value to match on the target object. Typically references a foreign key like `this.projectId`.
FetchStatsAction.__localKey.doc: The property of the target object to be matched against — `id`, or any indexed field. There is NO compile-time default: the stats query adds its match term only when BOTH `matchValue` and `localKey` are set (an authored `matchValue` with an empty `localKey` is silently dropped). Validation REFUSES the blueprint with FETCH_MATCH_VALUE_WITHOUT_LOCAL_KEY (ERROR). An MScript slot is EMPTY when no language source in it carries anything: an absent slot, `null`, and the untouched multilanguage envelope the authoring panel scaffolds (`{ "js": null, "java": null, ... }`) all count as empty, so a section you have not authored yet is never refused.
FetchStatsAction.__stats.doc: An array of stat operations like `count`, `sum(price)`, `min(quantity)`, or `max(score)`. Each must be a valid SQL-style aggregate expression.
FetchStatsAction.__whereClause.doc: Optional MScript query for compound stat filters or joins. It does NOT replace the match logic — the generated stats query MERGES them: the whereClause is evaluated first and the `localKey: matchValue` term is added on top (AND semantics; on a shared key the match term wins). Leave `matchValue` empty when the whereClause alone should scope the stats.
FetchStatsAction.__bucketBy.doc: Optional property reference to group the scoped items and calculate the stat(s) in buckets as an array. Keep null to have a total single reseult. The array result can be collated with main or any other data list in fyrther actions.

__FetchParentAction.doc: Fetches selected properties from a parent object related to the current object in context. Typically used to enrich the response or inform access and validation logic with values inherited from a higher-level entity (e.g., organization, project). The parentObject can be a local data object (same service) or a remote data object (different service). For remote parent objects, the action automatically fetches from Elasticsearch, enabling seamless inter-service parent data retrieval. **Important**: A relation to the parent object must be defined in the current dbObject's properties for this action to work.

__FetchParentAction.useCase.description: Use to pull inherited values from a parent entity (organization, project, tenant) into context for access checks or response enrichment — requires a relation to the parent on the current dbObject; remote parents are resolved from Elasticsearch automatically.

example.name: fetchOrganization
example.description: Load the owning organization's plan and billing status to gate later quota validations.

FetchParentAction.__parentObject.doc: Specifies the parent data object to fetch from. This can be a local data object (belonging to the same service) or a remote data object (belonging to another service). For local parent objects, the action calls the service's dbLayer utility function directly. For remote parent objects, the action automatically fetches from Elasticsearch, which contains data from remote services via CQRS joins. This is used when a child object in context needs data inherited or referenced from its parent. **Requirement**: A relation property must be defined in the current dbObject's properties that establishes the child-to-parent relationship. The action uses this relation to determine the foreign key and local key for querying the parent object.
FetchParentAction.__properties.doc: List of property names to fetch from the parent object. Leave empty to retrieve all fields. Uses dot notation for nested fields when needed.

__FunctionCallAction.doc: Defines a reusable logic step that calls a library-defined function using MScript syntax. This action allows for custom transformation, enrichment, or computation during the execution of a Business API. It is often used to prepare derived values, calculate totals, or apply shared service logic prior to validation or response shaping.

__FunctionCallAction.useCase.description: Use to invoke a shared service-library function for a derived computation or transformation — e.g. compute an order total with tax and shipping from line items before validation or response shaping.

example.name: computeOrderTotal
example.description: Calculate the grand total via the shared pricing library.

FunctionCallAction.__callScript.doc: An MScript expression that defines the function call. The script may reference a predefined library function and pass contextual arguments. Example: `{ "js": "LIB.calculateTotal(this.items)" }`.

__EmitSseEventAction.doc: Emits a custom SSE event during the workflow. The event name and payload are declaratively configured. When the API is called via REST (no SSE context), this action is a silent no-op.

__EmitSseEventAction.useCase.description: Use to push a named progress / status event to a connected SSE client mid-workflow (long-running jobs, multi-phase pipelines); it is a silent no-op when the API is invoked over plain REST.

example.name: notifyPhaseComplete
example.description: Tell the client the import phase finished and how many rows were processed.

EmitSseEventAction.__eventName.doc: The SSE event name to emit to the client (e.g., 'jobCreated', 'phaseComplete').
EmitSseEventAction.__data.doc: MScript expression evaluated against the pipeline context to build the event payload.

__ArrowFunctionAction.doc: This action defines a reusable function and sets it to the context with the contextPropertyName name. Java supports a non-empty authored body only when it has at least one named parameter and exactly one return of a supported literal, parameter, or string concatenation; for example, parameterNames: ["tier"] with functionBody: "{ return 'Tier ' + tier; }". Callbacks, object/array literals, accumulators, and general JavaScript statements refuse generation with JAVA_ARROW_FUNCTION_BODY_UNPORTABLE and the actions.arrowFunctionActions[<name>].functionBody slot. An empty body remains a noop. The Intl currency formatter use-case is for Node.js; Java designers should use the supported formatter subset.

__ArrowFunctionAction.useCase.description: Use to define a small reusable inline function and store it on the context, so later actions (especially mapping or filtering steps) can call it — e.g. a formatter applied across several lists.

example.name: defineCurrencyFormatter
example.description: Build a reusable currency formatter bound to the request locale.
example.functionBody: { return new Intl.NumberFormat(this.session.locale || 'en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: currency || 'USD' }).format(amount); }

ArrowFunctionAction.__parameterNames.doc: An array of strings to represent the names of the function parameters
ArrowFunctionAction.__functionBody.doc: The JavaScript function body, enclosed in a block ({}). For Java, use a parameterized single-return formatter such as { return 'Tier ' + tier; }; unsupported authored bodies are refused with their functionBody slot named. An empty block remains a noop.

__ListMapAction.doc: This action creates a new list out of a current list by mapping its items with MScript. By default the new list is stored under `contextPropertyName` for later actions to read — it does NOT change the api response. On a `list` api set `replacesResult: true` to make the mapped rows BE the response rows: this is the supported way to add a derived field to every row (or to reshape rows) of a list, and it must run in the `afterMainListOperation` stage, before `buildOutput` composes the envelope. To only DROP fields per row, prefer `RemoveFromResponseAction` with `applyToListRows: true` — it is declarative and needs no MScript.

__ListMapAction.useCase.description: Use to transform a list into a reshaped list — projecting, renaming, or deriving fields per item. Without `replacesResult` the new array is stored in context for downstream actions; with `replacesResult: true` on a list api it replaces the rows the response ships.

example.name: deriveGatheringStatus
example.description: Add a computed derivedStatus to every row of the gathering list response.

ListMapAction.__sourceList.doc: An MScript expression to reference the source array to map from. On a `list` api the rows the main operation fetched are bound under the PLURALIZED object name — `this.gatherings` for a `gathering` list — which is the source to use together with `replacesResult`.
ListMapAction.__itemName.doc: A codesafe string which will be used in code to reference the item of the source array. eg. user
ListMapAction.__mapScript.doc: An MScript to return the new item based on the source item. Reference to the source item using the itemName given. eg. `{ name: user.name, email: user.Email, firstName: user.name.split(' ')[0] }`. If you need a multi-lined script to make precalculations use an arrow function definition called inline. eg: `((user) => { /* your code here */ })(user)`
ListMapAction.__replacesResult.doc: List apis only. When true, the mapped array is assigned back to the api's result rows, so `buildOutput` ships THEM — this is how a derived field reaches every row of a list response. Without it the mapped array only lands on the workflow context (and `contextPropertyName: "result"` does NOT replace the response — it is a reserved name and an ERROR). The action must be wired into the `afterMainListOperation` stage: earlier there are no rows yet, and from `afterBuildOutput` on the envelope is already composed. The map is 1:1, so the paging totals stay correct. To drop fields rather than add them, `RemoveFromResponseAction.applyToListRows` is the simpler construct.

__InterserviceCallAction.doc: Calls another Business API defined in a different microservice. This enables inter-service coordination within an OpenAPPL application. The response can be extracted into the context or added to the API response. This action supports dynamic parameters and flexible response handling.

__InterserviceCallAction.useCase.description: Use to call a Business API in another microservice within the same OpenAPPL application — set forwardCallerToken=true when the downstream must apply the original user's role/ownership checks (e.g. cartService asking orderService to create an order for the buyer).

example.name: createOrderInOrderService
