example.description: Hand the validated cart to orderService.createOrder under the buyer's identity.

InterserviceCallAction.__targetService.doc: The logical name of the microservice where the target Business API is defined.
InterserviceCallAction.__targetApi.doc: The name of the target Business API to call in the foreign service.
InterserviceCallAction.__apiParameters.doc: A list of key-value MScript expressions passed as input parameters to the target API. These are dynamically evaluated using the current context. Every `:segment` of the target's REST route (its explicit routePath, or the calculated default such as `/orders/:orderId`) MUST be bound by an entry whose `name` matches the segment exactly (case included): the generated action substitutes the URL from that entry, and an unbound segment is a design-time ERROR (INTERSERVICE_PATH_PARAM_UNBOUND) because the call would otherwise send the literal `:segment` and the target would answer 400. At runtime, a bound segment whose value is null, undefined or blank (empty or whitespace-only) refuses the call before any token or I/O with 400 INTERSERVICE_PATH_PARAM_UNBOUND, naming the action, the target, the route and the segment. Not required when the call really rides gRPC (the target declares a gRPC controller and `transport` is `grpc` or `auto`); a `transport: "grpc"` call against a target WITHOUT a gRPC controller falls back to REST and is checked like any REST call. An `applyField` call declares no apiParameters at all: its one id segment is bound through `applyField.recordId`.
InterserviceCallAction.__responseProperty.doc: If defined, only the specified property will be extracted from the target API response; otherwise the full response body is stored. It indexes the PRODUCER'S RESPONSE BODY, which under the unified response contract is the record itself at the root (with `_type`) for a single-item target — there is NO resource-named wrapper, so a value like `order` or `profile` on a get/create/update/delete target matches nothing and silently falls back to the whole body. Valid values are a record property (or an `addToResponse`/`writeToResponse` key) on a single-item target, or `data` / `paging` on a LIST target, whose body is the AIP `{ data, paging }` envelope. Leave it unset to store the whole record — that is the normal choice for a single-item call. Over REST, the stored result is decoded by the target's SUCCESS content-type (its bare media type: parameters ignored, any case): `application/json` and the `application/json-*` family are the parsed body; any other textual type (`text/*`, a `+json` type such as `application/problem+json`, a `+xml` type, `application/xml`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) or no content-type at all is the body STRING; any other type (a file download: `application/pdf`, an xlsx or zip vendor type, `application/octet-stream`, `image/*`) is a Buffer holding the exact bytes. The file's filename and content-type are not exposed. Leave responseProperty unset on a file-download target.
InterserviceCallAction.__isArray.doc: If true, the result is expected to be an array. This influences how the response is processed and stored.
InterserviceCallAction.__forwardCallerToken.doc: When `true`, forward the inbound caller's session token to the downstream service as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` so the call runs under the user's identity (downstream sees the actual `session.userId` / `roleId` / ownership context). The M2M token still rides alongside as `x-m2m-token` for server-to-server trust, so both checks pass and the downstream can prefer whichever its auth middleware reads first. When `false` (default) the call goes M2M-only and the downstream sees no user session — appropriate for system-level audit writes, background jobs invoked by cron, or other contexts where the original caller's identity is irrelevant. Set `true` whenever the downstream API should apply user-role / ownership checks (e.g. an orderService.createOrder call from cartService should preserve the buyer's identity, not run as the cartService service account).
InterserviceCallAction.__transport.doc: Selects the transport for the interservice call. `auto` (default) uses gRPC automatically when the target Business API has a gRPC controller (`grpcSettings.hasGrpcController`), otherwise REST — for a gRPC-only target this is the only path that works. `rest` forces the HTTP/REST path (the target's normal REST route, with the forwarded caller bearer). `grpc` forces the gRPC path (requires the target to expose a gRPC controller; against a target without one the generated action silently falls back to REST, which draws the INTERSERVICE_GRPC_TRANSPORT_FALLBACK warning). The designer rarely needs to set this — `auto` picks the fastest available transport with no other blueprint changes.
InterserviceCallAction.__tenantContext.doc: An MScript expression yielding the CODENAME of the tenant this call must run inside, on a multi-tenant project. The generated call lowers it onto the outbound request as the tenant selector the receiving service's auth pipeline reads (the `mbx-<tenantName>-codename` header, or the project's `tenantNameHeaderName` override), NOT into the request body - so it reaches the receiver's tenant resolution rather than its parameter validation, which is where a hand-placed `_<tenantName>` apiParameters entry lands and is discarded (INTERSERVICE_PARAM_UNPLACEABLE). Use it when the hop has to act inside a tenant that is not the caller's own, or that the caller has no session in: provisioning an invited user into the workspace the invitation names, a cron sweep acting per tenant. A hop that declares no tenantContext and forwards no caller token signs the calling manager's own VERIFIED tenant (the session's tenant, a kafka event actor's tenant, a verified machine caller's claim) into its machine token as the `callerTenantId` claim, so it runs in the caller's own tenant and never in another; a caller with no verified tenant (the root floor, a tenant named only by an anonymous request's header) signs nothing, and the receiver then refuses a tenant-level api (the framework's own payment machine twins included) with 403 `M2M_TENANT_REQUIRED` or, on a platform-level api, serves the ROOT tenant's rows. A hop that forwards the caller's token (`forwardCallerToken`) runs in the tenant of that session. A declared tenantContext wins over the signed claim's default and rides the codename header; an expression that evaluates to null or an empty string REFUSES the call at runtime rather than sending it tenant-less. Leave it unset on a single-tenant project and on any hop that should run in the caller's own tenant.
InterserviceCallAction.__timeoutMs.doc: Optional positive integer timeout in milliseconds, at most 2147483647 (the Node.js timer maximum), for REST and gRPC inter-service calls. Overrides the service default INTER_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS (a positive integer at most 2147483647); an unset environment variable uses 10000 ms, and an invalid environment value logs a warning and falls back to 10000 ms. When omitted, the generated action carries no timeout override.
InterserviceCallAction.__applyField.doc: Applies ONE data-determined field on one record of the target service through the target's own typed update API (InterserviceApplyField). Use it when the NAME of the field to set is data, for example `this.proposedChange.targetField`: an apiParameters entry's `name` is static, so apiParameters cannot express that call. `targetApi` must be an `update` API of `targetService` whose REST route carries exactly one `:segment`, its id segment; `recordId` binds it, `field` names the target update API's request parameter to set, `value` is the value, and `allowedFields` is the design-time whitelist of names `field` may evaluate to. Every `allowedFields` entry must be in the target update API's write set (a caller-supplied request parameter that one of its dataClauseItems stores into an update-writable property), otherwise INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_UPDATABLE. At runtime a `field` outside `allowedFields` refuses the call with 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED and an undefined `value` with 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_VALUE_UNDEFINED, both before any token is minted or any request is sent; an accepted call is an ordinary update request, so the target runs its normal guard pipeline (authorization, ownership, lifecycle hooks) on it. Exclusive with `apiParameters` (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_WITH_API_PARAMETERS). Always rides REST, so `transport: "grpc"` is refused (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_TRANSPORT_UNSUPPORTED). Generated by the nodejs emitter only for now: a calling service whose language is java, dotnet, python, rust or golang is refused with INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED. Null or absent = an ordinary static-name call.

__InterserviceApplyField.doc: A guarded single-field update on another service's record, applied through that service's typed update API, where the field NAME is computed at runtime and whitelisted at design time. It is the `applyField` block of an InterserviceCallAction and replaces its `apiParameters`: the generated request carries exactly one data key, the field `field` evaluated to, set to `value`, on the record `recordId` names. Design-time rules: the target API must be an `update` API (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_TARGET_NOT_UPDATE) whose effective REST route carries exactly one `:segment` and that segment is its id segment, `:id` or `:` followed by the data object name and `Id` (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_TARGET_NOT_ID_ADDRESSED); its write set must be statically known, so an update API with no dataClauseItems, an action-carried write, an unresolvable data object or no declared request parameters is refused (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_TARGET_SURFACE_UNKNOWN); every `allowedFields` entry must be in that write set (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_UPDATABLE); `apiParameters` must be empty (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_WITH_API_PARAMETERS); `transport` must not be `grpc` (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_TRANSPORT_UNSUPPORTED); the calling service must generate in nodejs (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED; the other emitters do not implement it yet). Runtime refusals, all before any token or I/O: 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED for a `field` result that is not a string or not exactly one of the allowed fields, 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_VALUE_UNDEFINED for an undefined `value`, 400 INTERSERVICE_PATH_PARAM_UNBOUND for a null or blank `recordId`. The target's own authorization still decides whether the call may update the record.

InterserviceApplyField.__recordId.doc: MScript yielding the id of the record to update on the target service. It binds the one `:segment` of the target update API's REST route, its id segment (`:id` or the data object name followed by `Id`). A null or blank result refuses the call at runtime with 400 INTERSERVICE_PATH_PARAM_UNBOUND before any token or I/O.
InterserviceApplyField.__field.doc: MScript that evaluates at runtime to the NAME of the single target request parameter to set; it must be one of `allowedFields`. The name lives in the same namespace as `apiParameters[].name`: the request parameters of the target update API, which for a generated update API are the data object property names. A result that is not a string, or not exactly (case-sensitive) one of `allowedFields`, refuses the call with 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED; the message names the refused field name, never the value.
InterserviceApplyField.__value.doc: MScript yielding the value to apply to the chosen field. `null` is a value and is sent (it clears a nullable property, subject to the target's own checks). `undefined` refuses the call with 400 INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_VALUE_UNDEFINED, because a request without the key would reach the target as an update of nothing.
InterserviceApplyField.__allowedFields.doc: The design-time whitelist: the names `field` may evaluate to. It must hold at least one non-blank string (INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_ALLOWED_FIELDS_EMPTY). Each entry must be in the target update API's write set, matched exactly and case-sensitively: a request parameter the caller can send, declared at httpLocation body or query (not `id`, not the id segment, not contractOnly; an omitted location, bearer, session, header, cookie, request or urlpath is refused, a cookie one as UNSUPPORTED_LOCATION) that one of the target's dataClauseItems reads as `this.` plus the parameter name and stores into a property that is writable on update (not `allowUpdate: false`), whose wire key (its `dataPath`, else its name) is not `__proto__` (UNSAFE_WIRE_KEY: a request body cannot carry it; give the parameter another dataPath), and whose wire key no other request parameter of the target reads from the request (WIRE_KEY_SHARED: the one value would be stored twice; only a parameter at urlpath, session, header or request is read elsewhere, every other location, cookie included, is read from the body or the query string). An entry outside that set is INTERSERVICE_APPLY_FIELD_NOT_UPDATABLE, which names the entry, the target and the accepted set, with the reason UNKNOWN_AT_TARGET, NOT_STORED, IMMUTABLE, SERVER_POPULATED_LOCATION, RECORD_ID, UNSUPPORTED_LOCATION, WIRE_KEY_SHARED or UNSAFE_WIRE_KEY.

__InterProjectCallAction.doc: Calls a Business API in a linked sibling project in the same organization. Calls a Business API exposed by a LINKED SIBLING PROJECT — another OpenAPPL project in the same organization that was linked via addSiblingProject and therefore appears in the blueprint's `siblingProjects[]` registry. It is the cross-project counterpart of InterserviceCallAction (which calls a service inside the SAME project) and IntegrationAction (which calls a catalog integration). `targetProject` references the sibling by its codename (the designer-friendly form) or by its projectId; `targetApi` names a Business API published by that sibling. Parameters are passed as dynamically evaluated MScript key-value pairs, and the response — optionally narrowed to a single `responseProperty` — is stored in the context and can be written to the API response.

__InterProjectCallAction.useCase.description: Use to call a Business API published by a linked sibling project (same organization) — first link the target with addSiblingProject, then reference it here by its codename (or projectId). Parameters are MScript-computed and the result lands on context.

example.name: fetchCustomerProfile
example.description: Fetch the shared customer profile from the linked crmbackend project.

InterProjectCallAction.__targetProject.doc: The linked sibling project that exposes the target Business API. Reference the sibling by its codename (designer-friendly) or by its projectId — it must resolve to an entry of the blueprint's `siblingProjects[]` registry, i.e. the project must first be linked with addSiblingProject.
InterProjectCallAction.__targetApi.doc: The name of the Business API published by the sibling project to call.
InterProjectCallAction.__apiParameters.doc: A list of key-value MScript expressions passed as input parameters to the target API. These are dynamically evaluated using the current context.
InterProjectCallAction.__responseProperty.doc: If defined, only the specified property will be extracted from the target API response; otherwise the full response body is stored. It indexes the PRODUCER'S RESPONSE BODY, which under the unified response contract is the record itself at the root (with `_type`) for a single-item target — there is NO resource-named wrapper, so a value like `order` or `profile` on a get/create/update/delete target matches nothing and silently falls back to the whole body. Valid values are a record property (or an `addToResponse`/`writeToResponse` key) on a single-item target, or `data` / `paging` on a LIST target, whose body is the AIP `{ data, paging }` envelope. Leave it unset to store the whole record — that is the normal choice for a single-item call.
InterProjectCallAction.__isArray.doc: If true, the result is expected to be an array. This influences how the response is processed and stored.
InterProjectCallAction.__forwardCallerToken.doc: When `true`, the caller forwards the inbound end-user's identity to the sibling project alongside the cross-project M2M trust token: the raw caller bearer rides `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the verified session identity (userId / email / roleId / tenantId / sessionId) is embedded as a claim inside the project-key-signed `x-project-m2m-token`. Forwarding it does NOT decide that it is applied. The receiving project decides, and by default it refuses: the claim is applied only when the callee sets `ACCEPT_FORWARDED_IDENTITY` (default unset = reject, the call runs as pure machine-to-machine), and even then three rules bound it. (1) The claim is an identity or it is nothing: a claim that names no user contributes NO field at all, so a forwarded `roleId`, `tenantId` or `sessionId` without a `userId` grants nothing, scopes nothing and cannot make the caller non-anonymous to the ownership gates. (2) Only scalar slots cross; a non-scalar value in any slot is dropped before the claim is read. (3) The claim is never applied over an identity boundary: if the receiving request ALREADY carries its own authenticated session and that session is not provably the same user, the claim is refused whole and the request proceeds exactly as it would have with the opt-in switched off, under the local user, with `ForwardedIdentityNotPropagated` logged. An optional `FORWARDED_ROLE_CEILING` allowlist additionally caps which roleIds may be assumed. (4) A claim that MOVES the tenant does not bring the previous tenant's scoped members with it: `tenantCodename` and `userGroupIdList` are CLEARED on the merged session, because a tenant codename that no longer matches the tenant id is a false binding and a user-group id issued inside one tenant grants nothing inside another. Both clear fail-closed - the codename falls back to the request's own resolved tenant and an empty group list simply matches no group-scoped permission - so a workflow reading `this.session.userGroupIdList` on a forwarded cross-tenant call must treat the empty list as no group-scoped authority rather than as an error. When the claim IS applied the sibling acts on the user's identity (audit fields, ownership checks, user-scoped business logic). When `false` (default) the call is pure machine-to-machine: the sibling sees no user session and the target API must allow M2M callers (`M2MAllowed`). Set `true` whenever the sibling API should run under the original user's identity rather than as a machine caller, and remember that the sibling must opt in for it to have any effect.

__ApiCallAction.doc: Calls an external or internal HTTP API during Business API execution. This is ideal for integrating with third-party services or internal utility endpoints. The fetched result is stored in context and optionally written to the response. Input and output transformation are supported.

__ApiCallAction.useCase.description: Use to call an external or internal HTTP endpoint and capture the result into context — third-party lookups, webhooks, utility services. Set signBody=true for outbound calls whose receiver must verify origin via the project JWKS.

example.name: geocodeAddress
example.description: Resolve a shipping address to lat/lng via the maps provider.

ApiCallAction.__apiCallRequest.doc: Configuration object defining the HTTP call. Includes method, URL, headers, query parameters, and body.
ApiCallAction.__isArray.doc: If true, the result is expected to be an array and will be treated as such during response and context processing.
ApiCallAction.__apiFetchProperty.doc: Used when the response is a complex object but only one specific property is needed. The extracted property will be stored in context.
ApiCallAction.__signBody.doc: When true, the outbound request body is signed with the project's Ed25519 private key. The receiver verifies that the call originated from this project by fetching the project JWKS. Three headers are added: `Mindbricks-Signature` (base64url EdDSA signature over the raw body bytes), `Mindbricks-Kid` (key id), and `Mindbricks-Jwks-Url` (where to resolve the public key). Use this for outbound webhooks to receivers that need to verify the call's origin — the inverse of how Stripe-style callbacks are verified coming IN.
ApiCallAction.__httpRequestPath.doc: Values for the `{name}` placeholders in the PATH of `apiCallRequest.httpRequestUrl`, e.g. `https://api.example.com/v1/projects/{projectId}/stats` with `[{ "name": "projectId", "value": { "js": "this.project.id" } }]`. Each value is MScript, evaluated at call time, converted to a string and URL-encoded as ONE path segment (`encodeURIComponent`: a `/`, `?` or `#` in the value cannot add a segment or a query). Names match the placeholder exactly, case included. Every path placeholder must have an entry and every entry must have a placeholder: an unbound placeholder (API_CALL_PATH_PLACEHOLDER_UNBOUND), an unused entry (API_CALL_PATH_PARAM_UNUSED) and a placeholder in the host or the query string (API_CALL_PATH_PLACEHOLDER_OUTSIDE_PATH) are design-time errors, and the generated call refuses to run with them; a value that evaluates to null, undefined, an empty string or an object, or to the dot segment `.` / `..` (which a URL parser would collapse, moving the call to another path), is refused at run time before the request is sent; an entry is refused as unused whether or not it has a value. The URL itself stays a static literal (not MScript). Only ApiCallAction has this family: the shared HTTPRequest of RemoteSessionConfig, RemoteServiceAuthenticationConfig and RedirectAction sends its URL verbatim.

__GrpcCallAction.doc: Calls a FOREIGN (non-OpenAPPL) gRPC server during Business API execution (docs/ADR-grpc-interservice-and-grpccall.md, Part B). The gRPC counterpart of `ApiCallAction`: instead of a URL it targets a named gRPC client (declared in `serviceSettings.grpcClients[]`) and an rpc method. The request message is built from compiled MScript `request.fields` (like ApiCallAction compiles its body/headers); the call rides the shared `grpcUnaryCall` engine (the same engine the interservice gRPC path uses) with the grpcClient's static metadata attached; the decoded Response is extracted by `responsePath` and stored in context (and optionally written to the response). For an OpenAPPL target, prefer `InterserviceCallAction` (transport auto-selects gRPC with zero proto config); use `GrpcCallAction` for third-party gRPC services whose proto you supply via the grpcClient.

__GrpcCallAction.useCase.description: Use to integrate a third-party / non-OpenAPPL gRPC service. Declare the foreign server once under serviceSettings.grpcClients[] (endpoint + inline proto + package/service + any static auth metadata), then call one of its rpc methods here, mapping the request fields from context via MScript and extracting the part of the response you need with responsePath.

example.name: createCharge
example.description: Charge the buyer via the external payments gRPC service.

GrpcCallAction.__grpcClientName.doc: Codename of the foreign gRPC client to call. Must match an entry in this service's `serviceSettings.grpcClients[].name`. The grpcClient supplies the proto (package/service), endpoint, static metadata, and TLS.
GrpcCallAction.__grpcMethodName.doc: The rpc method name to invoke on the grpcClient's `service` (must be declared in the grpcClient's proto, e.g. `CreateCharge`). Unary by default; set `streaming: true` for a SERVER-streaming method (`rpc X(Req) returns (stream Resp)`). Client-streaming and bidi are not yet supported.
GrpcCallAction.__request.doc: The request message sent to the gRPC method. Its `fields` map proto field names to MScript expressions evaluated against the current API context — exactly like ApiCallAction's body parameters. A method that takes no arguments may omit this or leave `fields` empty.
GrpcCallAction.__responsePath.doc: Optional dotted path into the decoded Response message to extract the value of interest (e.g. `charge.id`, `result.items`). When null, the full decoded Response message is stored. Applied after the call returns. For a `streaming` call it is applied PER streamed message.
GrpcCallAction.__isArray.doc: If true, the extracted value (`responsePath` result, or the whole Response) is expected to be an array and is treated as such during response and context processing. Ignored when `streaming` is true (a streamed result is always the collected array).
GrpcCallAction.__streaming.doc: If true, the `grpcMethodName` is a SERVER-streaming rpc (`rpc X(Req) returns (stream Resp)`). The call collects every streamed Response message into an array and returns it (the simplest result for a BusinessApi value; `responsePath` is applied per-item and `isArray` is implied). When false/absent the call is unary. Client-streaming/bidi and an async-iterator (stream-to-client) consumption mode are follow-ons.

__GrpcCallRequest.doc: The request message for a `GrpcCallAction` — a list of proto-field-to-MScript mappings. Mirrors how ApiCallAction expresses its body: each field's value is compiled MScript evaluated against the API context at runtime and assigned to the named proto field of the gRPC Request message.

GrpcCallRequest.__fields.doc: The proto Request fields to send. Each entry maps a proto field name to an MScript expression. Fields whose value evaluates to undefined are still assigned (proto-loader applies defaults); omit a field by not listing it.

__AiCallAction.doc: Invokes an AI model such as OpenAI or Anthropic to perform text generation, refinement, classification, or summarization. The prompt is composed from a template and context, and the result is stored in the context and optionally exposed in the response.

__AiCallAction.useCase.description: Use to call an LLM for generation, classification, or summarization — bind it to a named project AI provider via providerName, and when a later action reads a field of the result (a decision, a category, a moderation verdict) declare a responseSchema: the reply is then enforced natively where the provider can, validated, and a reply that does not match fails the action instead of silently taking a default branch.

example.name: classifyTicket
example.description: Classify an incoming support message into a category and urgency.

promptTemplate.systemPrompt: You are a support triage assistant. Respond ONLY with JSON: category is one of billing, technical, account, other; urgency is one of low, medium, high; summary is one sentence.

AiCallAction.__providerName.doc: Reference to a project-level AI provider by codeName. Must match an entry in projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name. When set, the action's request is routed to that provider's adapter at runtime (credentials read from AI_PROVIDER_<NAME>_* env vars). When null, the runtime falls back to model-name sniffing (gpt-* → openai, claude-* → anthropic) against the project's legacy `aiSettings.openAiApiKey` / `anthropicApiKey` keys — works for back-compat but emits a deprecation warning at validation. New actions should set providerName.
AiCallAction.__promptTemplate.doc: Defines both the static system message and dynamic user message. These are passed to the AI model to guide its behavior. Supports MScript in the user prompt.
AiCallAction.__isArray.doc: Descriptive: marks an action whose result is a list of items. The runtime does not reshape the result on this flag. A responseSchema must have an object root, so a list result under a schema is declared as an array property of that object (e.g. {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{...}}},"required":["items"]}) and read as this.<contextPropertyName>.items.
AiCallAction.__responseFormat.doc: Expected format of the model's output: `json` for structured output or `text` for plain text. With `json` the reply is parsed after stripping ONE surrounding markdown fence (```json / ```) and its whitespace; a reply that still does not parse FAILS the action with a 502 coded AI_CALL_RESPONSE_NOT_JSON, and so does one that parses to a scalar or null (a bare string, number, boolean or null) when no responseSchema is declared, because the actions after it read fields (the raw text is never passed on; declare onActionError: completeApi to branch on this.<actionName>Error.code instead). `text` returns the reply unchanged. Pair `json` with responseSchema to enforce a specific shape - plain `json` is not enforced on the wire by every provider (the Anthropic adapter enforces only a schema).
AiCallAction.__responseSchema.doc: JSON Schema (as a JSON string) that the model's reply must validate against - the same form as AIAgent.modelSettings.responseSchema. Implies JSON output: the reply is parsed and validated whatever responseFormat says (set responseFormat to 'json' to silence the design-time warning). Providers with native structured output (openai-compatible json_schema strict, anthropic current-gen output_config, google responseSchema) receive the schema on the wire; other providers do not see it, so spell the shape out in the prompt as well. The runtime strips one surrounding markdown fence, parses, and validates with the agent runtime's JSON-Schema subset (type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties:false, items); a reply that does not parse or does not validate FAILS the action with a 502 coded AI_CALL_RESPONSE_NOT_JSON / AI_CALL_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH. There is no repair retry (unlike AIAgent): declare onActionError: completeApi to handle the failure in the workflow. Object-root schemas only. Declare one on every decision, moderation or classification call whose result a later action branches on. Example: '{"type":"object","properties":{"decision":{"type":"string","enum":["approve","reject","escalate"]},"reason":{"type":"string"}},"required":["decision","reason"]}'.
AiCallAction.__model.doc: The identifier of the LLM model to be used, such as `gpt-4`, `claude-3`, or any provider-accessible variant.

__AgentCallAction.doc: Invokes an AI Agent from within a Business API workflow. The agent must be defined under `agentHub/aiAgents` (recommended — runtime-managed agents); legacy in-service `aiAgents` are also resolved when present. The agent is executed using a data payload constructed from the current API context via an MScript expression, and its result is stored in the workflow context for subsequent actions or response writing. This enables tight integration between structured API logic and AI agent capabilities.

__AgentCallAction.useCase.description: Use to invoke a defined AI Agent (from agentHub/aiAgents) inside a workflow, building its input payload from context — for multi-tool / multi-step reasoning that a single AiCallAction can't express.

example.name: runContentAnalyzer
example.description: Run the contentAnalyzer agent over the submitted article plus the author's prior context.

inputData.js: { text: this.data.body, authorBio: this.author.bio, locale: this.session.locale }

AgentCallAction.__agentName.doc: The name of the AI Agent to invoke. Must match the `agentBasics.name` of an agent defined under `agentHub/aiAgents` (recommended) or in the service's local `aiAgents` array. Codegen auto-detects the dispatch target: local-first, then AgentHub. An agent the calling service deploys itself (its own `aiAgents`, or an `agentHub/aiAgents` entry whose `agentBasics.assignedService` names that service) runs in-process; any other agent is called on the agentHub service (`SERVICE_AGENTHUB_URL`). Example: 'contentAnalyzer', 'summarizer'.
AgentCallAction.__inputData.doc: An MScript expression that builds the data object to pass to the agent as its request body. Has access to `this` (the API context), including `this.data`, `this.session`, and any context properties set by previous actions. Example: `{ "js": "{ message: this.data.description, context: this.fetchedProfile.bio }" }`. If null, the agent receives an empty object `{}` on both dispatch routes; `this.data` is not forwarded implicitly, so pass it explicitly (`{ "js": "this.data" }`) to forward it.

__IteratorAction.doc: A generic streaming action whose method returns an async iterable. The sourceScript MScript expression must evaluate to an object with Symbol.asyncIterator (async generator, readable stream, etc.). Designed for custom streaming logic that isn't covered by AiCallAction.

__IteratorAction.useCase.description: Use for custom streaming output not covered by AiCallAction — sourceScript must evaluate to an async-iterable (async generator, readable stream) whose chunks are streamed to the SSE client.

example.name: streamReport
example.description: Stream a large report row-by-row from a custom library generator.

IteratorAction.__sourceScript.doc: MScript expression that evaluates to an async iterable. Example: LIB.streamProcessor(this.data)

__AIPromptTemplate.doc: Defines the structure of an AI prompt using a two-part design: a static system-level instruction and a dynamic user message populated via MScript from the current context. Used in AiCallAction to guide AI model behavior.

AIPromptTemplate.__systemPrompt.doc: A fixed instruction string that sets the tone or role for the AI model. Examples include guidance like 'You are a helpful assistant' or 'You are a strict validator'.
AIPromptTemplate.__userPrompt.doc: A dynamic MScript expression that generates the user-facing part of the prompt. This often references contextual variables such as `this.username`, `this.itemName`, or `this.description` to personalize or situate the model's response. It is an EXPRESSION, not prompt text: codegen splices it into `await Promise.resolve(<userPrompt>)`, so write prompt text as a template literal in backticks, e.g. { "js": "`Classify this customer message: ${this.data.message}`" }. Bare text (or a template literal that is never closed) is refused at validation with INVALID_MSCRIPT_SYNTAX and a wrap-it-in-backticks hint; a blueprint that reaches codegen anyway has its text emitted as a template literal.

__CreateCrudAction.doc: Defines an embedded creation operation for a related data object—typically a child or associated entity—within a Business API. These actions enable CASCADING (never transactional) object creation as part of a larger business operation: the child row is committed on its own as soon as the action completes, and nothing rolls it back if a later action of the same api throws — see the failure-semantics section of `BusinessWorkflow`. When the child write can legitimately fail (a unique index with `onDuplicate: throwError`), place the action in a PRE-MAIN stage — `afterBuildDataClause` for `create`/`update`, `afterCheckInstance` for `update`/`delete` — so it fails before the parent row is written. Often used when the main API creates or updates a parent object and simultaneously needs to initialize dependent records (e.g., child tasks, audit logs, attachments). The childObject must be a data object of the same service: the action writes through this service's dbLayer, and a `<otherService>:<Object>` reference is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL). To create a row another service owns, call that service's create API with an `InterserviceCallAction` (its `tenantContext` names the tenant on a multi-tenant project).

__CreateCrudAction.useCase.description: Use to create a single related/child record as part of a larger operation — e.g. write an audit-log entry after the main object is updated. The child object belongs to the same service and is written through its dbLayer; a row another service owns is created by calling that service's API with an InterserviceCallAction.

example.name: createAuditLog
example.description: Record an audit entry for the status change just applied to the order.

CreateCrudAction.__childObject.doc: Specifies the related data object to be created. It must be a data object of the same service, named bare or with this service's own name as prefix: the action calls the service's dbLayer utility function (`create{ObjectName}`) directly. A reference to another service's object (`<otherService>:<Object>`) is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL); to create a row another service owns, call that service's create API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.
CreateCrudAction.__dataClause.doc: An array of property-value mappings that define what data to write into the new object. Each entry uses MScript to evaluate a value from the current context. The child row is written from these mappings PLUS the two auto-fills the generator applies to a column the mappings do not name: the tenant column, stamped from the session tenant, and every child property carrying `sessionSettings.sessionParam`, filled from the caller's session. In dotnet, mapped tenant aliases are collapsed before the resolved session tenant overrides an authored tenant for ordinary callers; superAdmin and root-tenant callers retain an authored tenant. Other authored mappings retain precedence, and an unresolvable auto-fill leaves the key ABSENT, so a NOT NULL column refuses the row instead of being written null. A child property carrying a `staticJoin` block that the mappings do not name is resolved on this path too: it is read from the joint source row exactly as the main create resolves it - local or cross-service source, and the `staticJoin.defaultValue` fallback when the join cannot supply a value. A required child column with none of these sources is a design-time error (CHILD_CREATE_MISSING_VALUE_SOURCE).

__CreateBulkCrudAction.doc: Defines a bulk creation operation for multiple related data objects—typically child or associated entities—within a Business API. These actions enable CASCADING (never transactional) bulk object creation as part of a larger business operation: the bulk insert is committed on its own as soon as the action completes, and nothing rolls it back if a later action of the same api throws — see the failure-semantics section of `BusinessWorkflow`. When the bulk write can legitimately fail (a unique index), place the action in a PRE-MAIN stage — `afterBuildDataClause` for `create`/`update`, `afterCheckInstance` for `update`/`delete` — so it fails before the parent row is written. Often used when the main API needs to create multiple child records at once (e.g., bulk creating child tasks, audit logs, or attachments). The objects parameter is an MScript expression that evaluates to an array of objects, where each object contains the property-value mappings for a single record to be created. The childObject must be a data object of the same service: the action writes through this service's dbLayer, and a `<otherService>:<Object>` reference is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL). There is no cross-service bulk write; to create rows another service owns, call that service's API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.

__CreateBulkCrudAction.useCase.description: Use to create many child records at once from an array built in context — e.g. fan out order line items into individual orderItem rows in a single bulk write.

example.name: createOrderItems
example.description: Bulk-create one orderItem per validated cart line.

objects.js: this.lineItems.map(li => ({ orderId: this.createdOrder.id, productId: li.productId, quantity: li.quantity, unitPrice: li.unitPrice }))

CreateBulkCrudAction.__childObject.doc: Specifies the related data object to be created in bulk. It must be a data object of the same service, named bare or with this service's own name as prefix: the action calls the service's dbLayer bulk create utility function (`createBulk{ObjectName}`) directly. A reference to another service's object (`<otherService>:<Object>`) is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL); there is no cross-service bulk write, so call the owning service's API with an `InterserviceCallAction` instead.
CreateBulkCrudAction.__objects.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to an array of objects. Each object in the array represents a single record to be created, with property-value mappings that define what data to write into the new object. Each property value can use MScript to evaluate from the current context. The child row is written from these mappings PLUS two generator fills, which follow different precedence rules. The TENANT column of a tenant-scoped child is not an authored-wins fill: for an ordinary caller the resolved session tenant is written OVER any tenant an entry supplies (in dotnet, mapped tenant aliases are collapsed first), so a row cannot name another tenant; a superAdmin or root-tenant caller acts across tenants and keeps an authored tenant, and only an absent one is stamped from its session tenant; with no resolved session tenant nothing is stamped and no tenant is invented. Every child property carrying `sessionSettings.sessionParam`, filled from the caller's session, is written ONLY when the entry does not name it: there an authored mapping wins, and a session that carries no value leaves the key ABSENT, so a NOT NULL column refuses the row instead of being written null. `staticJoin` columns are still NOT resolved on this path, so map those explicitly: an entry the `objects` source shows (an array of object literals, or a `.map` callback that returns object literals) and that leaves a joined column unmapped is a design-time warning (CREATE_BULK_STATIC_JOIN_UNMAPPED), because that column is written NULL. Required columns are NOT checked at design time on this path (CHILD_CREATE_MISSING_VALUE_SOURCE is the single-row CreateCrudAction's check): an entry that leaves a required column without a value is refused by the database at run time.

__UpdateCrudAction.doc: Defines an embedded update operation for related data objects—typically child or connected entities—within a Business API. This action is used when the API needs to selectively update external records based on a condition. It is commonly applied after creating or modifying a parent object to ensure consistency or to propagate business state changes across related objects. The childObject must be a data object of the same service: the action updates through this service's dbLayer, and a `<otherService>:<Object>` reference is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL). To update rows another service owns, call that service's update API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.

__UpdateCrudAction.useCase.description: Use to conditionally update related records as part of a business operation — propagate state changes across linked objects via a where clause plus a data clause.

example.name: markRelatedTasksDone
example.description: Close every open task tied to the project once the project is archived.

UpdateCrudAction.__childObject.doc: The name of the related data object that will be updated. It must be a data object of the same service, named bare or with this service's own name as prefix: the action calls the service's dbLayer update utility function (`update{ObjectName}ByMQuery`) directly. A reference to another service's object (`<otherService>:<Object>`) is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL); to update rows another service owns, call that service's update API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.
UpdateCrudAction.__dataClause.doc: A list of key-value assignments to apply to the matched records. Each item in the list defines a property of the child object and its new value (evaluated via MScript). Required fields must be included explicitly, and all values are resolved in the current context.
UpdateCrudAction.__whereClause.doc: An MScript-based query that determines which records in the child object should be updated. This is a required field and must uniquely or conditionally identify the target set of records.
UpdateCrudAction.__onNoRows.doc: What to do when the whereClause matched NO row. `ignore` (default) completes the action with an empty result exactly as before, so an existing blueprint is unchanged; `throwError` raises a typed 404 (`errorCode: ACTION_NO_ROWS_MATCHED`) that `onActionError` then routes like any other action error - aborting the api, or stored as `this.<actionName>Error` under `completeApi`. Set it when this update addresses one specific row whose absence is a defect; leave it for a deliberately broad selector that may match nothing.

__DeleteCrudAction.doc: Defines an embedded delete operation to remove related records—typically child or connected entities—within a Business API. This action allows declarative, conditional deletion of external data objects that are linked to the primary object. It is typically used for cascading deletes, cleanup logic, or enforcing referential integrity in business processes. The childObject must be a data object of the same service: the action deletes through this service's dbLayer, and a `<otherService>:<Object>` reference is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL). To delete rows another service owns, call that service's delete API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.

__DeleteCrudAction.useCase.description: Use to remove related records by a where clause for cascading deletes or cleanup — e.g. delete all cart items once a cart is converted to an order.

example.name: clearCartItems
example.description: Delete every item in the cart that was just checked out.

DeleteCrudAction.__childObject.doc: The name of the related data object from which records will be deleted. It must be a data object of the same service, named bare or with this service's own name as prefix: the action calls the service's dbLayer delete utility function (`delete{ObjectName}ByMQuery`) directly. A reference to another service's object (`<otherService>:<Object>`) is refused at design time (CRUD_ACTION_CHILD_OBJECT_NOT_LOCAL); to delete rows another service owns, call that service's delete API with an `InterserviceCallAction`.
DeleteCrudAction.__whereClause.doc: An MScript-based query that defines the selection condition for records to be deleted. This field is required and must identify which records in the child object will be affected.
DeleteCrudAction.__onNoRows.doc: What to do when the whereClause matched NO row. `ignore` (default) completes the action with an empty result exactly as before, so an existing blueprint is unchanged; `throwError` raises a typed 404 (`errorCode: ACTION_NO_ROWS_MATCHED`) that `onActionError` then routes like any other action error - aborting the api, or stored as `this.<actionName>Error` under `completeApi`. Set it when this delete addresses one specific row whose absence is a defect (a compensation that must undo a row the request just wrote); leave it for a cascading cleanup that may legitimately find nothing.

__ApiAggregateData.doc: Defines a single property-value pair used to populate a related data object during an aggregated operation. This structure is used in `CreateCrudAction` and `UpdateCrudAction` to specify how each property of the child object should be assigned—either statically or dynamically—from the API execution context.

ApiAggregateData.__dataProperty.doc: The name of the target property on the child object that will be set during the operation. This must match a valid property name defined in the child data object schema.
ApiAggregateData.__dataValue.doc: The MScript expression or static value used to assign a value to the specified property. This can reference current context (`this`), a parameter (`this.input`), or the loop iteration variable when executed inside a `LoopAction` — by the name configured on `LoopAction.loopItemName` (e.g. if `loopItemName` is `customerItem`, reference `customerItem.id`). The legacy name `crudItem` is also bound as an alias for backward compatibility with older specs.

__LoopAction.doc: Defines a repeated execution block within a Business API workflow. It loops over the result of an MScript expression and executes a list of actions for each item. The current item is exposed as a local variable named by `loopItemName`, directly accessible in MScript, and also as the aliases `loopItem` and `crudItem`. Every action executed under a loop additionally receives the loop-step context as ordinary bindings: `stepIndex`, the zero-based index of the current iteration, and `stepResults`, an accumulator carrying the results of this loop level's earlier steps keyed `<innerActionName>_<stepIndex>`. Referencing `stepIndex` in a dataValue is the canonical way to persist an order derived from the input list. Loop actions can be nested to support multi-level iteration: each level gets its OWN fresh counter and accumulator, so an inner level can never advance or overwrite its parent's. Inside a nested loop `stepIndex` and `stepResults` always name the INNERMOST enclosing loop — the outer level's index and results are shadowed and unreachable by name — while every enclosing level's `loopItemName` stays reachable, so a grid-like write addresses its rows and columns through the item names rather than through two indexes. An inner action that declares a `contextPropertyName` publishes its result in TWO places: on the manager as `this.<contextPropertyName>`, the access path that property documents, and — when the loop item is an object — back onto the item itself as `<loopItemName>.<contextPropertyName>`. The `this` slot names the last step in which that inner action RAN: normally the CURRENT step, exactly like `loopItemName` and `stepIndex`, so once the loop has finished it holds the LAST step's value — but an inner action carrying a `condition` writes nothing on a step it skips, so the slot then still holds the PREVIOUS iteration's value. Read the per-item copy whenever you need a specific iteration's value, or to tell a skipped step from a stale one.

__LoopAction.useCase.description: Use to run a set of previously-defined actions once per item of an iterable, exposing the current item under loopItemName — set isParallel only when iterations don't write shared context or contend on the same records.

example.name: notifyEachParticipant
example.description: Send a confirmation email to every participant of the booking, sequentially.

LoopAction.__loopFor.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to an iterable (such as an array). Each element of the result will be bound to the variable defined by `loopItemName` and processed through the listed actions.
LoopAction.__loopItemName.doc:
The name of the variable representing the current item in each loop iteration. This variable is directly accessible in MScript without `this.`. For example, if `loopItemName` is `customerItem`, you can reference `customerItem.id` or `customerItem.status` inside any action executed in the loop.

The loop's step binder publishes `this.<loopItemName>` plus the aliases `this.crudItem`, `this.loopItem`, `this.stepIndex` and `this.stepResults` BEFORE EVERY action inside the loop. Two consequences the validator now reports as WARNINGS:

- An action whose `contextPropertyName` spells one of those names writes its result into the same slot and the next step overwrites it, on every iteration, with no error anywhere (`LOOP_STEP_BINDING_SHADOWED`). Pick a name of your own, e.g. `<name>Result`. A `contextPropertyName` that collides with an inherited ApiManager member is a separate, blocking error (`RESERVED_CONTEXT_PROPERTY`).
- A loop nested inside another loop that spells the SAME `loopItemName` shadows its parent's item for the whole inner body, so an action inside the inner loop cannot reach the outer item under any spelling (`NESTED_LOOP_ITEM_NAME_SHADOWED`). Give each nesting level its own name.

Defaults to `item` when unset, which participates in both checks.
LoopAction.__actions.doc: An array of action names (as strings) to execute during each loop iteration. These actions must be previously defined in the Business API's action store.
LoopAction.__isParallel.doc: A boolean value to control the non-blocking behaviour of the loop steps. If `isParallel` is true, all loop steps are scheduled asynchronously and awaited as a group. If false, steps are awaited and executed one by one. Warning: parallel mode can cause race conditions when actions write to shared context (`this.*`) or perform conflicting read-modify-write updates on the same record. Prefer item-local writes, `stepResults`, or database concurrency controls when enabling parallel mode.

__ParallelAction.doc: Defines a non-blocking execution group in which multiple actions are executed in parallel. Each action runs independently using the same input context. Parallel actions are useful for concurrent fetches, validations, or other side-effect-free logic. Warning: avoid parallel branches that mutate the same shared fields or the same database records without concurrency controls, because final state can become non-deterministic. This action can also include nested `ParallelAction` or `LoopAction` steps, enabling concurrent or branched execution across multiple layers of the workflow.

__ParallelAction.useCase.description: Use to run several independent, side-effect-free actions concurrently for latency — typically parallel fetches/enrichments — avoiding branches that mutate the same context fields or records.

example.name: enrichOrderConcurrently
example.description: Fetch customer, shipping rates, and inventory levels at the same time.

ParallelAction.__actions.doc: An array of action names (as strings) to be executed concurrently. Each action in this list will run using the shared context. Nested parallel and loop actions are supported for composing deeply concurrent workflows.

__MembershipCheckAction.doc: Defines access control based on membership rules configured on a data object. This is used when access to a Business API operation depends on whether the current user is a member of a related entity, such as a project, team, or organization. The `dataObjectName` field specifies which object’s membership rules should be applied—if omitted, the main data object of the Business API is used by default. This action supports direct and nested membership checks, such as validating access to a parent organization while updating a child project.

__MembershipCheckAction.useCase.description: Use to gate an operation on whether the current user is a member (optionally with a required role) of a related entity such as a team, project, or organization — liveCheck enforces immediately, storedCheck defers the decision.

example.name: requireProjectMembership
example.description: Caller must be an admin or editor member of the project to update it.
example.errorMessage: You must be an admin or editor of this project to modify it.

MembershipCheckAction.__dataObjectName.doc: The name of the data object whose membership configuration should be used to validate access. If omitted, the Business API’s main data object is assumed. Use this field when you need to check access against a related or parent object (e.g., checking `Organization` membership when updating a `Project`).
MembershipCheckAction.__objectKey.doc: An MScript expression that returns the ID of the object whose membership should be checked. For example, if checking access to a project, this would return a `projectId`.
MembershipCheckAction.__userKey.doc: An MScript expression that returns the user ID to check against the target object’s membership configuration. Typically `this.session.userId`, but may also reference delegated users or owners.
MembershipCheckAction.__requiredRoles.doc: OPTIONAL. The member roles that satisfy this check — the declarative answer to "which members may do this?", and the form to REACH FOR FIRST. The membership row passes when the value of the scope object's `membershipSettings.configuration.roleField` is any one of these (case-sensitively, as authored). `['owner','admin']` reads exactly as the rule does. Requires the scope object to declare a `roleField`; each name must be one the membership object's role field can actually carry — a role that appears in no `rolePermissions` entry and in no enum on that field is a design-time ERROR (`MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED_ROLE_UNKNOWN`). Leave BOTH this and `checkFor` empty to gate on membership EXISTENCE alone. Mutually exclusive with `checkFor`.
MembershipCheckAction.__checkFor.doc: OPTIONAL escape hatch for a membership condition that is not a role list — reach for `requiredRoles` first. An MScript expression evaluated ONCE the row is fetched, with the row bound as `membership`: `membership.seatCount > 0`, `membership.expiresAt > this.now`. THE RECEIVER MATTERS: `membership.<field>` reads the membership row; bare `this.<field>` reads the API MANAGER, NOT the row — `this.memberRole === 'owner'` therefore evaluates to `undefined === 'owner'` → false and refuses every caller, and `this.membership.<field>` is undefined and throws. Both mistakes are design-time ERRORs (`MEMBERSHIP_CHECK_FOR_WRONG_RECEIVER`). An expression that does NOT mention `membership` is treated as a VALUE compared against the row's `roleField` — use `requiredRoles` for that instead; it says the same thing without a receiver to get wrong. Mutually exclusive with `requiredRoles`.
MembershipCheckAction.__errorMessage.doc: A message to display when the membership check fails. Use this to provide a meaningful explanation to the user, such as 'You must be a member of this team to perform this action.'
MembershipCheckAction.__checkType.doc: Specifies whether this membership check should enforce access immediately (`liveCheck`) or simply write the result to context (`storedCheck`). Use `storedCheck` when the result will be used later in a conditional or validation flow.

__ReadJwtTokenAction.doc: Defines a read jwt token operation from either context, session or request and write its payload to the context with the contextPropertyName after validating it. The token signature should be in HMAC format. The token payload may be used for allowing access to an object via a signed token instead of standard authentication. This is typically used for public or limited-access sharing workflows (e.g., view-only links). Once the token payload is in context any other validations may be performed using the payload values in further actions.

__ReadJwtTokenAction.useCase.description: Use to validate an HMAC-signed JWT (from request, context, or session) and place its payload on context — typically to authorize access via a signed share link instead of a standard session.

example.name: readShareToken
example.description: Validate the view-only share token and expose its scope claims for later checks.

ReadJwtTokenAction.__readTokenFrom.doc: An MScript value that evaluates to the encoded JWT string. It may be in the context through parameters like `this.accessToken`, it may be read directly from controller request like `this.request.query.payToken` or it may be read from the session in cases where users have their own tokens for authorization like this.session.userSubscription.
ReadJwtTokenAction.__isRequired.doc: A Boolean value to define if the token is required. Set it true if you want the application throw an error if the token is null or can not be validated.
ReadJwtTokenAction.__jwtKey.doc: An MScript value that evaluates to the Jwt key to validate the token signature. It may be an hardcoded value like `1234560987abcdef` or a reference to context like this.jwtKey or a env reference like process.env.SUBS_KEY.
ReadJwtTokenAction.__statusCheck.doc: An optional check script that runs after the signature is verified and before the payload is written to the context, so it cannot read the payload: `this.<contextPropertyName>` is not set yet and no other name is bound to it. Use it for general status checks on other context, session or request values; if the check fails the token is considered invalid (a 400 when isRequired, otherwise the action stores null). To check values inside the payload, use a later action, such as a ValidationAction, that reads `this.<contextPropertyName>`.

__PermissionCheckAction.doc: Defines a global permission check that evaluates whether the user holds specific platform or service-level permissions. This check is not tied to any particular object instance and is useful for validating roles such as `canAccessAdminPanel`, `canExportData`, or `canSendEmails`. You can either enforce the result immediately or store it in context for conditional usage later in the flow.

__PermissionCheckAction.useCase.description: Use for a global, instance-independent permission gate — verify the user holds a platform/service-level capability such as exporting data or accessing an admin panel.

example.name: requireExportPermission
example.description: Only users with the data-export capability may run this bulk export.

PermissionCheckAction.__permissionName.doc: The name of the permission that the user must possess. The check will only succeed if the user has the given permission.
PermissionCheckAction.__checkType.doc: Specifies how the result of the check should be handled. When set to `liveCheck`, the Business API will immediately throw an authorization error if the check fails, halting execution. When set to `storedCheck`, the result is stored in context and does not interrupt execution—even if the check fails. This allows for advanced, combinational authorization logic where multiple checks may be evaluated together later in the workflow.

__ObjectPermissionCheckAction.doc: Performs a permission check scoped to a specific object instance. It evaluates whether the current user has the required permissions on the resolved object, based on all applicable sources: directly assigned object permissions, inherited permissions from parent contexts (e.g., user or role permissions), and dynamic ABAC rules that intersect with the object’s attributes. This check is used when fine-grained, instance-level authorization is required.

__ObjectPermissionCheckAction.useCase.description: Use for fine-grained, instance-level authorization — confirm the user holds the required permission(s) on a specific resolved object, considering direct grants, inherited role permissions, and ABAC rules.

example.name: requireDocumentEditPermission
example.description: Caller must hold editDocument (and shareDocument when sharing) on this exact document.

ObjectPermissionCheckAction.__permissionName.doc: The name of the permission that the user must possess on the resolved object instance.
ObjectPermissionCheckAction.__checkType.doc: Specifies how the result of the check is handled. If set to `liveCheck`, the API will immediately throw a permission error if the check fails. If set to `storedCheck`, the result is stored in the context and does not interrupt execution—allowing you to combine multiple permission checks later in the workflow.
ObjectPermissionCheckAction.__readObjectIdFrom.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the ID of the specific instance whose permissions should be checked. This could reference input parameters, session values, or context-fetched records (e.g., `{ "js": "this.projectId" }` or `{ "js": "this.parent.organizationId" }`).

__ApiCheckType.doc.#: Defines how the result of a validation, permission, or membership check is used within the Business API lifecycle.
__ApiCheckType.doc.storedCheck: The result of the check is written to the context and does not interrupt API execution. This allows deferred decision-making or combining the result with other checks later in the workflow (e.g., in conditionals or response shaping).
__ApiCheckType.doc.liveCheck: If the check fails, the Business API will immediately throw an authorization or validation error and halt execution. Use this mode when the check outcome must strictly control access or behavior.

__ValidationAction.doc: Defines a flexible business rule that performs a dynamic condition check during Business API execution. Unlike permission or membership checks, a ValidationAction is fully script-based and domain-specific, allowing complex logical conditions such as subscription status, object states, quota limits, feature flags, or compliance rules. If the validation fails, the system either throws an error (liveCheck) or stores the result in context for later decision-making (storedCheck).

__ValidationAction.useCase.description: Use for a script-based domain rule — quota limits, object state, subscription status, eligibility — that throws (liveCheck) or records its result (storedCheck) with a semantically chosen error status.

example.name: checkProjectQuota
example.description: Block creation when the organization is at its plan's project limit.
example.errorMessage: Your plan does not allow creating more projects. Upgrade to add more.

ValidationAction.__description.doc: A short, human-readable description explaining the intent of the validation—such as 'User must be active subscriber', 'Quota must not be exceeded', or 'Document must be in draft state'.
ValidationAction.__shouldBeTrue.doc: Indicates the expected outcome of the validation logic. If `true`, the validation passes when the condition evaluates to `true`. Set to `false` when the validation should pass on a `false` condition (e.g., `!isUserBanned`).
ValidationAction.__checkType.doc: Specifies how the result of the validation is handled. If `liveCheck`, the API throws an error immediately when the validation fails. If `storedCheck`, the result is saved to context and execution continues—allowing deferred or compound logic.
ValidationAction.__validationScript.doc: An MScript expression that returns a boolean value based on current API context. This defines the actual validation condition. If the result does not match `shouldBeTrue`, the validation fails.
ValidationAction.__errorMessage.doc: Message returned to the client if the validation fails and `checkType` is `liveCheck`. This should be clear and relevant to the context, e.g., 'Your plan does not allow creating more projects.'
ValidationAction.__errorStatus.doc: The HTTP status code to return when the validation fails and `checkType` is set to `liveCheck`. Choose by semantic: `400` for malformed/invalid input, `401`/`403` for authorization failures (the generated service bypasses these for users with absolute roles like `superAdmin`), `404` for missing resources, `409` for uniqueness/duplicate conflicts (a team is already registered, a stage window already exists, an active application is already submitted — prefer 409 over 403 when the issue is conflict, not auth), `422` for semantic / business-rule violations on otherwise valid input (eligibility not confirmed, prerequisite not met), `429` for a rate-limit or quota refusal that clears with time (errorCode TOO_MANY_REQUESTS), `500` for internal errors, `503` when a dependency the api needs is down right now (errorCode SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, the authored message is kept). Callers retry 429 and 503, so never use either for a permanent refusal. There is no `402`: a payment-required refusal is `422`. Default `400`.

__AddToContextAction.doc: Adds one or more calculated values to the runtime context (`this`) at a specific point in the Business API flow. This is typically used to prepare values that will be referenced in later actions, such as computed totals, enriched properties, or temporary flags. The values are evaluated via MScript and written under the names you specify.

__AddToContextAction.useCase.description: Use to compute and stash one or more intermediate values on the context (this.*) so later actions can reference them — totals, flags, normalized inputs.

example.name: prepareTotals
example.description: Compute subtotal and a high-value flag for use by validation and the response.

AddToContextAction.__context.doc: An array of `ContextData` objects. Each defines a property name and an MScript expression to compute its value. These values will be written to the runtime context (`this.<contextName>`), making them accessible in subsequent steps. A contextName that spells a member of the generated API manager (`session`, `result`, `output`, `dataClause`, a pipeline method - the same reserved set RESERVED_CONTEXT_PROPERTY uses) is refused (RESERVED_CONTEXT_NAME): the assignment would REPLACE that member for the rest of the workflow. To feed an owner column on an internal create, declare `sessionSettings.ownerProvenance: "payload"` instead of writing `session`.

__ContextData.doc: ContextData is a container object to represent any key-value pair to write or read to/from context.

ContextData.__contextName.doc: The name of the variable to store in the context (e.g., `totalCost`, `userQuota`). The value will be accessible in later steps as `this.<contextName>`.
ContextData.__contextValue.doc: An MScript expression used to compute the value for this property. Can reference other context fields, parameters, session values, or constants (e.g., `{ "js": "this.items.length * this.price" }`).

__AddToResponseAction.doc:
Adds one or more properties from the current context to the final response object after the main operation completes. This is useful when some values are computed or fetched indirectly (e.g., session-based, Redis-loaded, or generated) and need to be exposed in the API response explicitly.

ON A LIST API, `this.data` IS NOT THE ROW ARRAY. `this.data` is the main-operation alias of `this.result`, which on a db-backed list is the db-layer RESULT OBJECT `{ rows, count }`; the response envelope's `data` key is built from it later, by `buildOutput()`. An array idiom written against it (`(this.data ?? []).map(r => r.id)` at `afterBuildOutput`) therefore throws `this.data.map is not a function` and answers 500 on EVERY call, not just on an empty result, because `??` does not fall back on an object. The row array has exactly two documented spellings: the plural binding `this.<objects>` (e.g. `this.users` for a `user` object) and `this.data.rows`. Validation reports the wrong idiom as the warning `LIST_DATA_ALIAS_OBJECT_SHAPE`, naming both spellings and the api. A DataView list is exempt: its main operation answers the row array itself, so `this.data` IS the array there.

__AddToResponseAction.useCase.description: Use to copy computed or indirectly-fetched context values into the final response object that wouldn't otherwise be exposed — e.g. a generated download URL or a derived total.

example.name: exposeTotals
example.description: Surface the computed subtotal and the rendered receipt URL in the response.

AddToResponseAction.__context.doc: An array of `ContextData` entries. Each defines a name-value pair to be copied from the evaluated MScript into the response object. The property will appear in the final API output.

__RemoveFromResponseAction.doc: Removes one or more properties from the final API response before it is returned to the client. This is useful for eliminating internal, sensitive, or unnecessary fields that were added by earlier actions or populated from context. Commonly used to enforce privacy, avoid leaking implementation details, or to conform to specific output schemas. On a `list` api set `applyToListRows: true` — this is THE supported way to redact fields from every row of a list response, and the only construct that can do it conditionally (an `isSecret` property is hidden from the owner and the admin too, and `contextPropertyName` never replaces the response). Place the action in the `afterBuildOutput` workflow stage: the response object it edits does not exist before `buildOutput` composes it.

__RemoveFromResponseAction.useCase.description: Use to strip internal or sensitive fields from the response before it returns to the client — passwords, internal flags, raw provider payloads. On a list api, `applyToListRows: true` strips the same fields from EVERY row; `condition` gates the whole action once per request (session/role), `rowCondition` decides per row (ownership).

example.name: stripPendingFieldsFromRows
example.description: On the anonymous gathering list, hide the moderation fields on every row the caller does not own.

RemoveFromResponseAction.__properties.doc: An array of property names (strings) that will be removed from the final API response. Use this to clean up sensitive or internal fields before the response is returned. Each entry is a dot-notation path resolved against the RESPONSE ROOT (`customer.internalNotes`, `addresses[0].postalCode`) — or, when `applyToListRows` is true, against EACH ROW of the list response (`pendingPayload`), never against the envelope.
RemoveFromResponseAction.__applyToListRows.doc: List responses only. When true, every path in `properties` is deleted from EACH ROW of the list envelope (`output.data[i]`) instead of from the response root — the supported way to redact a list. Leave false (the default) on non-list apis: the row loop has nothing to walk there, and design-time validation rejects the combination. The rows are the composed response rows, so the action must run in the `afterBuildOutput` stage.
RemoveFromResponseAction.__itemName.doc: List-row redaction only. A code-safe identifier bound to the current row inside `rowCondition`, e.g. `row` (the default) lets you write `row.creatorUserId`. Ignored unless `applyToListRows` is true.
RemoveFromResponseAction.__rowCondition.doc: List-row redaction only. An MScript boolean evaluated ONCE PER ROW, with the row bound under `itemName`. The properties are removed only from the rows where it returns true — this is how a field stays visible on the caller's OWN rows and is hidden on everyone else's (`row.creatorUserId !== this.session?.userId`). Leave it null to redact every row. Note the division of labour with the inherited `condition`: `condition` is evaluated ONCE PER REQUEST and gates the whole action (session/role questions — 'is this caller an admin?'), `rowCondition` is evaluated ONCE PER ROW (per-row questions — 'does this caller own this row?'). Requires `applyToListRows: true`.

__RedirectAction.doc: Redirects the client to a new URL after the API execution. This is often used in web-based flows like OAuth callbacks, login success handlers, or conditional navigation.

__RedirectAction.useCase.description: Use to redirect the browser after execution — OAuth callbacks, post-login landing, or conditional navigation — with a URL that may be templated from context.

example.name: redirectAfterOAuth
example.description: Send the user back to the app with their freshly minted session token.

RedirectAction.__redirectUrl.doc: The URL to redirect the client to. Supports templated HTTPRequest objects, which may include path parameters or query strings dynamically generated using MScript.

__CreateObjectAction.doc: Constructs an in-memory JavaScript object from key-value pairs and writes it to the context. This action does not persist data to the database. It is typically used to prepare structured data for use in other actions such as sending emails, rendering templates, API calls, or forming response objects.

__CreateObjectAction.useCase.description: Use to assemble an in-memory object (not persisted) for use by later actions — an email model, a template payload, or an API request body — optionally merging in a computed object.

example.name: buildWelcomeEmailModel
example.description: Compose the data model passed to the welcome-email template.

CreateObjectAction.__payload.doc: An array of key-value pairs (as `ObjectData`) representing the base fields of the constructed object. Values are evaluated using MScript.
CreateObjectAction.__mergeObject.doc: An optional MScript expression that returns an object. Its keys and values will be shallow-merged into the base object after `payload` is evaluated. This allows for dynamic or computed properties.

__ObjectData.doc: Represents a single property assignment used when constructing a new object via `CreateObjectAction`. The value is evaluated dynamically from context.

ObjectData.__key.doc: The name of the property to assign on the created object (e.g., `status`, `createdBy`).
ObjectData.__value.doc: An MScript expression used to compute the value assigned to this property. Can include references to `this`, `session`, or other computed context.

__CreateJWTTokenAction.doc: Generates a signed JWT token from a given payload. This token can be stored in context or included in the API response for client use. Typically used for authentication or temporary session flows.

__CreateJWTTokenAction.useCase.description: Use to mint a signed JWT from a context-built payload — share links, temporary sessions, or single-use action tokens — to return to the client or store for later validation.

example.name: issueShareToken
example.description: Create a view-only token scoped to a single document, valid for one hour.

payload.js: { documentId: this.document.id, scope: 'view', iat: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000), exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 3600 }

CreateJWTTokenAction.__JWTKey.doc: An MScript expression that defines the value of the JWT key to sign the payload. It is mostly an environement variable reference.
CreateJWTTokenAction.__payload.doc: An MScript expression that defines the object payload to be encoded inside the JWT. May include user ID, scopes, expiration, or other claims.

__SignDataWithProjectKeyAction.doc: Signs an arbitrary value with the project's Ed25519 private key and stores a verifiable envelope on the workflow context. The envelope shape is `{ sig, kid, jwks_url }`. Any receiver (in this project or another trusted one) can verify the signature by fetching the project JWKS at `jwks_url` — defense against payload spoofing for webhooks, downstream API calls, or anywhere a designer wants to attach an origin proof to data. The signing form is canonical JSON with recursively sorted keys, so both sides reproduce identical bytes regardless of insertion order.

__SignDataWithProjectKeyAction.useCase.description: Use to attach an Ed25519 origin proof to data before sending it downstream (outbound webhooks, cross-project calls); the receiver verifies via the project JWKS. Produces an envelope { sig, kid, jwks_url } on context.

example.name: signWebhookPayload
example.description: Sign the order-shipped event so the partner can verify it came from this project.

SignDataWithProjectKeyAction.__inputData.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the value being signed. May be an object (canonicalized via the shared canonicalize() helper), a string (used as-is), or a Buffer-like (used as-is). Has access to `this` — the API context.
SignDataWithProjectKeyAction.__contextPropertyName.doc: Context property to write the resulting envelope under. Other actions can reference the signature via `this.<contextPropertyName>.sig`, the kid via `.kid`, and the JWKS URL via `.jwks_url`. If null, the envelope is appended to the action's default result slot.

__PublishEventAction.doc: Publishes a message to an event topic (such as a message bus, queue, or pub/sub channel) as part of the Business API flow. This action is used to emit domain events or trigger asynchronous workflows that are consumed by other services or systems. The payload is defined using MScript and can include structured data from the API context. On the wire the message rides inside the unified event envelope — consumers that receive the RAW wire message (an AIAgent `kafkaController.dataMapping`) read it from the envelope's `data` key (`{ id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data }`), while consumers the framework unwraps for them (an EventNotification `targetPathInData`, whose listener reads `record = event.data`) address the authored message's own keys directly and must NOT add a `data.` prefix.
