The declared topic doubles as the default envelope `type`, and on the WIRE it is project-scoped as `<projectCodename>-<topic>` - every framework-derived topic family already carried that prefix, and authored topics now do too, so two projects on one broker cannot share a topic by both authoring the same name. Subscribe by the declared name: the framework scopes producer and consumer with the same helper.

__PublishEventAction.useCase.description: Use to emit a domain event onto a topic so other services or async consumers can react — decoupling side effects from the request lifecycle.

example.name: publishOrderPlaced
example.description: Announce a placed order for fulfillment and analytics consumers.

message.js: { orderId: this.order.id, customerId: this.order.customerId, total: this.order.totalAmount, placedAt: new Date().toISOString() }

PublishEventAction.__topic.doc: The name of the topic, channel, or event key to which the message will be published. This string typically matches the naming convention of the consuming system (e.g., `project.created`, `user.signup`).
PublishEventAction.__message.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the message payload to send. This can be a primitive value, object, or string and may reference `this`, session data, or previous action results.
PublishEventAction.__allowEmptyKeys.doc: Comma-separated TOP-LEVEL keys of `message` that are allowed to be empty or absent ON PURPOSE. A deliberately-empty optional fan-out field had no way to say so, and the two checks that judge a publish payload then contradicted each other: `{ recipients: [] }` raised PAYLOAD_EMPTY_ARRAY ("the target always receives no data"), while sourcing the same key from an `isRequired: false` fetch raised PUBLISH_OPTIONAL_CONTEXT_UNGUARDED ("the payload silently carries null fields") — so the only escape was a ceremonial AddToContextAction setting the key to `[]` a second time. Naming a key here states the intent directly and silences BOTH findings for that key alone; every other key is judged exactly as before. Design-time only: no generator reads it, and the published payload is byte-identical with or without it.
PublishEventAction.__actorTenantId.doc: Optional MScript tenant id for session-less cron or system APIs publishing tenant-scoped events, for example { js: 'this.row.companyId' }. Evaluated only when the publishing session carries no tenant. A non-null result replaces eventTenantFallback() as the envelope actor tenant fallback; null uses the existing fallback. A session tenant always wins and suppresses evaluation of this expression. Consumers derive tenant scope from the envelope actor, so set this per processed tenant row on SaaS-level APIs. It does not override a tenant user's session, change the message payload, or grant tenant access. Nodejs supports this slot; other language publishers require the corresponding port.

__ReadFromRedisAction.doc: Reads a value from Redis using a dynamically computed key and writes the result into the context under a specified property name (contextPropertyName). This action is typically used to retrieve session data, temporary values, or cached results that are needed later in the API flow. The retrieved value becomes accessible to other actions using `this.<contextName>`.

__ReadFromRedisAction.useCase.description: Use to read transient state from Redis by a computed key — verification tokens, cached results, rate-limit counters — into context for later steps.

example.name: readOtpAttempts
example.description: Load the current OTP attempt count for this phone number.

ReadFromRedisAction.__redisKey.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the Redis key to fetch. Can include values from the current context, session, or request (e.g., `{ "js": "this.session.userId" }`).

__WriteToRedisAction.doc: Writes a value to Redis under a computed key. The value is defined via MScript and can include dynamic data from the current context. This is typically used for storing transient data such as verification tokens, process state, or temporary API results.

__WriteToRedisAction.useCase.description: Use to write transient state to Redis under a computed key — store a verification code, process state, or short-lived cache value (objects are JSON-serialized automatically).

example.name: storeOtpCode
example.description: Persist the generated OTP keyed by phone for later verification.

WriteToRedisAction.__redisKey.doc: An MScript expression that resolves to the Redis key where the message will be stored. You can use contextual values to create scoped or namespaced keys.
WriteToRedisAction.__message.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the value to store. This can be a string, number, or object. Complex objects will be serialized to JSON automatically.
WriteToRedisAction.__ttl.doc: Optional MScript expression that evaluates to a time-to-live in seconds. When set, the cached value expires after this many seconds (e.g. a session cache). Omit it, or set it to null, for a non-expiring key: the action then issues a plain SET with no expiry (which also clears any expiry an earlier write set on the same key). A value that is present must be a number of seconds, at least 1: a static zero, negative, boolean or non-numeric literal is refused at design time (REDIS_TTL_NOT_NUMERIC) and a static literal below one second (e.g. 0.5) is refused too (REDIS_TTL_BELOW_ONE_SECOND). At runtime the value is coerced with Number(...) and floored to whole seconds; a positive value below one second rounds UP to 1 (an expiry was asked for, so it never falls to a non-expiring write), and a value that is not a finite positive number (NaN, 0, negative, Infinity, a non-numeric string) degrades to the same no-expiry SET.

__RenderDataAction.doc: Renders a literal string with flat ${key} substitutions from inputData on nodejs. The inputData expression is evaluated as MScript; the template itself is literal text. Placeholders use word-character top-level keys. Missing or undefined values become empty text; present values use String(), including null as 'null'. There is no file lookup, EJS, Mustache, expression evaluation, nested-key lookup or HTML escaping. The rendered result is saved into context with contextPropertyName and can be reused by later actions.

__RenderDataAction.useCase.description: Substitute a top-level name into literal text from the evaluated user profile.

example.name: renderGreeting
example.description: Render literal text with the top-level name.

RenderDataAction.__inputData.doc: MScript expression producing the value map used for flat ${key} substitutions in the literal template.
RenderDataAction.__template.doc: Literal text containing ${key} placeholders; keys use word characters and read top-level inputData properties. Missing/undefined values become empty text; present values use String() (null becomes 'null'). No file lookup, EJS/Mustache, expressions, nested keys or HTML escaping is performed.

__DataToFileAction.doc: Converts a given input into a downloadable file such as CSV, JSON, or XLSX. Two modes: VERBATIM writes a pre-rendered string from `inputData` as text; ROWS serializes structured rows—an array of objects from `inputData`, or, when `inputData` is empty on a `list` api, the api's own list result—into csv, tsv, xlsx, json or ndjson, selecting and computing output columns through `columns`. The ROWS mode with an empty `inputData` is the one-declaration table export: the list api's select/where/order and the caller's filter parameters decide the rows, the action decides the file. PDF is not a DataToFileAction format - use RenderPdfAction instead. ROWS mode, like the xlsx arm, is nodejs-only: the other lanes refuse it with a typed 501 and the design gets the TABULAR_ACTION_NOT_PORTED warning.

__DataToFileAction.useCase.description: Use to turn a pre-rendered string (or object) into a downloadable text-based file (CSV, JSON, etc.) and optionally stream it straight to the client. For PDFs use RenderPdfAction instead.

example.name: exportOrdersCsv
example.description: Export the queried orders as a CSV download.

DataToFileAction.__inputData.doc: An MScript expression that resolves to the content to save. In VERBATIM mode (no `columns`, a text format) it is a pre-rendered string—such as a rendered CSV, JSON string, or HTML body; a raw object is JSON-stringified. In ROWS mode it resolves to structured ROWS: an array of objects (keys become columns) or `{ sheets: [{ name, rows }] }` for a multi-sheet xlsx. ROWS mode is taken when `columns` is declared, when the format is `xlsx` or `ndjson`, or when `inputData` is left empty: an empty `inputData` on a `list` api exports the api's own list result (`this.<pluralDataName>`, i.e. the rows the api's select/where/order and the caller's filter parameters produced), which is the one-declaration table export.
DataToFileAction.__outputFormat.doc: The format of the file to be generated, one of the `FileFormats` enum values (e.g. `json`, `csv`, `xlsx`). In VERBATIM mode every format writes the input as utf8 text. In ROWS mode only the tabular formats are valid—`csv`, `tsv`, `xlsx`, `json`, `ndjson`—and the generated service serializes the rows itself (RFC 4180 csv/tsv with a header row, one exceljs worksheet per sheet, a JSON array, or one JSON object per line). For PDF use RenderPdfAction instead.
DataToFileAction.__sendToClient.doc: If true, the generated file will be sent to the client as a downloadable attachment in the API response. If false, the file is only generated internally.
DataToFileAction.__columns.doc: ROWS mode column selection, in output order. Each entry names the output `header` and either a row `property` to copy or a `value` MScript computed per row with `item` (the row) in scope, e.g. a formatted date or a joined label. Leave empty to emit every key of the rows as its own column.
DataToFileAction.__sheetName.doc: ROWS mode, xlsx only: the worksheet name when the rows are a plain array (a `{ sheets }` input names its own sheets). Defaults to the action's context property name.
DataToFileAction.__maxRows.doc: ROWS mode: a hard cap on the number of rows written; extra rows are dropped and the truncation is logged. Protects the service from an unbounded export. Null means no cap beyond the api's own pagination.
DataToFileAction.__fileName.doc: An MScript for the download / stored file name (without the extension, which follows `outputFormat`), with `rows` (the rows about to be written) in scope, e.g. `` `stock-${new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)}` ``. Defaults to the action's context property name. The temp file the action writes is always uniquely named per request, whatever the download name.
DataToFileAction.__rowFilter.doc: ROWS mode: an MScript boolean evaluated per row with `item` in scope; rows answering false are left out of the file. The place for a condition the list api's where clause cannot express.
DataToFileAction.__beforeWrite.doc: ROWS mode: an MScript evaluated ONCE after the column projection, with `rows` (the projected rows, keyed by output header) in scope; its result replaces the rows written. Sort, group, add a manual summary row, or reshape freely.
DataToFileAction.__sheetLayout.doc: ROWS mode, xlsx only: how the table is laid out on the worksheet - title, start cell, header style, freeze / filter, widths, a totals row, and `cells`, the free area for any address and any MScript.
DataToFileAction.__textOptions.doc: ROWS mode, csv / tsv / json / ndjson: delimiter, header row, BOM (Excel opens a UTF-8 csv with Turkish text correctly only with a BOM), json wrapper key and pretty printing.

__FileFormats.doc.#: Specifies supported output formats for content generation, serialization, or export. These are primarily text-based formats, suitable for structured data, document rendering, and developer-facing outputs; `xlsx` is the one binary, structured exception (see its entry). For PDF rendering, use RenderPdfAction (which targets PdfTemplate) instead of DataToFileAction.
__FileFormats.doc.json: JavaScript Object Notation — structured, widely used for API and machine-readable exports.
__FileFormats.doc.xml: Extensible Markup Language — structured, verbose format common in enterprise and legacy systems.
__FileFormats.doc.csv: Comma-Separated Values — simple flat data format, best for spreadsheets or tabular exports.
__FileFormats.doc.tsv: Tab-Separated Values — like CSV but uses tabs, better for escaping commas in data.
__FileFormats.doc.txt: Plain Text — raw string content without formatting.
__FileFormats.doc.html: HyperText Markup Language — suitable for browser rendering and templated output.
__FileFormats.doc.md: Markdown — lightweight markup language for documentation and developer-friendly reports.
__FileFormats.doc.yaml: YAML Ain’t Markup Language — human-readable config format, commonly used in CI/CD pipelines and devops.
__FileFormats.doc.svg: Scalable Vector Graphics — XML-based vector image format used in charts and exports.
__FileFormats.doc.rtf: Rich Text Format — supports basic styling, used in word processors.
__FileFormats.doc.log: Log file — typically used for line-based event or debug data.
__FileFormats.doc.tex: LaTeX — markup format used for academic or mathematical document generation.
__FileFormats.doc.xlsx: Excel Workbook (Office Open XML spreadsheet) — BINARY format for spreadsheet exports and template downloads. Unlike the text formats, a DataToFileAction with `outputFormat: xlsx` expects its `inputData` MScript to return structured ROWS (an array of objects, one worksheet with keys as columns, or `{ sheets: [{ name, rows }] }` for multiple worksheets) rather than a pre-rendered string; the generated service builds the workbook and writes binary. Prefer this over `csv` when formatting or non-ASCII text (e.g. Turkish characters) must survive a spreadsheet round-trip.
__FileFormats.doc.ndjson: Newline-delimited JSON — one JSON object per line, the streaming-friendly tabular text format. ROWS mode only: a DataToFileAction writes each row as one line, and a FileToDataAction reads one row per line.

__TabularFormats.doc.#: The tabular file formats a FileToDataAction can parse: every one is a header row plus records, which is what lets a spreadsheet, a csv export and an ndjson dump share one import contract.
__TabularFormats.doc.csv: Comma-separated values with a header row (RFC 4180 quoting, optional BOM).
__TabularFormats.doc.tsv: Tab-separated values with a header row.
__TabularFormats.doc.xlsx: Excel workbook (Office Open XML); one worksheet is read, selected by sheetName or the first sheet.
__TabularFormats.doc.json: A JSON array of objects; keys are the columns.
__TabularFormats.doc.ndjson: Newline-delimited JSON, one object per line; keys are the columns.

__BulkMatchModes.doc.#: How an UpsertBulkCrudAction treats each incoming row against the rows already stored, after matching on matchBy.
__BulkMatchModes.doc.upsert: Update the matched row, insert when there is no match (the default).
__BulkMatchModes.doc.insert: Insert every row; no matching is performed.
__BulkMatchModes.doc.update: Update the matched row; a row with no match is rejected (errorRowHandling decides whether that aborts). The enrichment mode.
__BulkMatchModes.doc.skipExisting: Insert only the rows with no match; matched rows are left untouched and counted as skipped.

__BulkOnExistingPolicies.doc.#: Per-column policy applied when an UpsertBulkCrudAction updates a MATCHED row. Columns absent from the incoming row are never touched on update.
__BulkOnExistingPolicies.doc.fillIfEmpty: Write only when the stored value is null or an empty string; an existing value is kept.
__BulkOnExistingPolicies.doc.keep: Never written on update; the column is insert-only (the seed-data insertOnly rule).
__BulkOnExistingPolicies.doc.skipIfEmpty: Write only when the INCOMING value is not empty (null or an empty string); an empty cell leaves the stored value alone. The paste / partial-sheet guard.
__BulkOnExistingPolicies.doc.compute: The column's value MScript runs with `existing` (the stored row) and `row` (the incoming row) in scope and its result is written, e.g. `existing.stock + row.qty`.

__BulkEmptyCellPolicies.doc.#: What an UpsertBulkCrudAction does with an EMPTY incoming cell (null or an empty string) on a column that has no policy of its own, when updating a matched row.
__BulkEmptyCellPolicies.doc.write: Write the null - the file says the value is gone (the default, and what an insert always does).
__BulkEmptyCellPolicies.doc.skip: Leave the stored value alone - a blank cell in a pasted or partial sheet means "no change", never "erase".

__ErrorRowHandlings.doc.#: What a row-oriented action does with a row it cannot process.
__ErrorRowHandlings.doc.collect: Skip the row, record it under `rejected` with its row index and reasons, and continue (the default).
__ErrorRowHandlings.doc.fail: Throw on the first bad row; nothing after it is processed. Rows already written by an earlier row of the same action stay written (the bulk actions are cascading, never transactional).

__TabularColumnMap.doc: One column of a tabular import or export. On a FileToDataAction it binds a file column to a data-model property: `header` names the column in the file (defaults to the property name), and `value` optionally computes the property from the whole file row instead (`row`, `rowIndex` and `existing` in scope). On a DataToFileAction it names one output column: `header` is the column title, `property` copies a row key, and `value` computes the cell from `item` (the row).

TabularColumnMap.__property.doc: The data-model property this column maps to (import) or copies (export). Optional on export when `value` is given.
TabularColumnMap.__header.doc: The column title in the file. Import: the header cell to read, defaulting to the property name. Export: the header cell to write, defaulting to the property name.
TabularColumnMap.__value.doc: Optional MScript computing the cell. Import scope: `row` (the parsed file row keyed by header), `rowIndex`, and `existing` (null on parse; the matched stored row inside an UpsertBulkCrudAction compute policy). Export scope: `item` (the row being written).
TabularColumnMap.__valueMap.doc: Import only. A dictionary from the raw file value to the property value, applied before type coercion: `{ "Sr": "senior", "Jr": "junior", "Aktif": true }`. Matched exactly first, then case-insensitively on the trimmed text; a value with no entry passes through unchanged (use a `value` MScript when an unmapped value must be rejected).
TabularColumnMap.__format.doc: Export only, xlsx: the Excel number / date format applied to the column's cells, e.g. `#,##0.00`, `0%`, `yyyy-mm-dd`, `dd.mm.yyyy hh:mm`.
TabularColumnMap.__width.doc: Export only, xlsx: the column width in characters. Overrides `sheetLayout.columnWidths` for this column.

__BulkColumnPolicy.doc: The onExisting policy of one column when an UpsertBulkCrudAction updates a matched row. A column without a policy is overwritten by the incoming value.

BulkColumnPolicy.__property.doc: The child object property the policy applies to.
BulkColumnPolicy.__onExisting.doc: One of the BulkOnExistingPolicies values: overwrite, fillIfEmpty, keep or compute.
BulkColumnPolicy.__value.doc: Required for the `compute` policy: an MScript evaluated per matched row with `existing` (the stored row) and `row` (the incoming row) in scope; its result is written to the column.

__SheetHeaderStyles.doc.#: How the header row of an exported worksheet is styled.
__SheetHeaderStyles.doc.bold: Bold text on a light grey fill, the default.

__SheetTotalFunctions.doc.#: The Excel function a totals-row cell carries; written as a real formula over the column's data range, never a baked number.

__SheetColumnWidths.doc.#: How exported worksheet columns are sized.
__SheetColumnWidths.doc.auto: Fit each column to its longest header or cell text (capped at 60 characters), the default.

__SheetCell.doc: One free cell of an exported worksheet: any address, any MScript. Written before the table, so it can sit above, beside or below it (the table's own cells win on overlap).

SheetCell.__value.doc: An MScript for the cell value, with `rows` (the rows being written) in scope; a number stays a number, a Date a date, a string starting with `=` is written as a formula.

__SheetTotal.doc: One cell of the totals row written under the exported table.

SheetTotal.__column.doc: The column the total is for, by output header or by source property name.
SheetTotal.__fn.doc: One of the SheetTotalFunctions values; sum by default.
SheetTotal.__label.doc: Optional text written in the first column of the totals row (e.g. `Total`) when that column carries no total itself.
SheetTotal.label: String

__SheetLayout.doc: The layout of an exported xlsx worksheet around the data table. It covers a title block, where the table starts, header styling, freeze pane and auto filter, column widths, a totals row of real formulas, and `cells` - the free area where any address takes any MScript.

SheetLayout.__title.doc: An MScript for a title written in the first cell of the start column, two rows above the header (the row between stays empty), bold and larger; `rows` in scope. Leave empty for no title.
SheetLayout.__startCell.doc: Where the header row starts, e.g. `B3`. Defaults to `A1` (or `A3` when a title is set).
SheetLayout.__freezeHeader.doc: Freeze the rows above and including the header so it stays visible while scrolling. Default true.
SheetLayout.__autoFilter.doc: Put an Excel auto filter on the header row. Default true.
SheetLayout.__columnWidths.doc: One of the SheetColumnWidths values; a column's own `width` overrides it.
SheetLayout.__totals.doc: Totals-row cells written directly under the table as formulas over the column's data range.
SheetLayout.__cells.doc: The free area: any cell, any MScript. Report metadata, a generated-by line, a filter summary, a note - whatever the layout needs and the table does not carry.
SheetLayout.title: MScript

__TabularTextOptions.doc: Serializer options for the text formats of a ROWS mode export.

TabularTextOptions.__delimiter.doc: csv: the field delimiter, `,` by default; `;` is what a Turkish / German Excel expects.
TabularTextOptions.__includeHeader.doc: csv / tsv: write the header row. Default true.
TabularTextOptions.__bom.doc: csv / tsv / json / ndjson: prefix the file with a UTF-8 byte order mark. Excel needs it to read non-ASCII text in a csv correctly. Default false.
TabularTextOptions.__jsonWrapper.doc: json: wrap the array in an object under this key, e.g. `data` gives `{ "data": [ ... ] }`. Empty writes the bare array.
TabularTextOptions.__pretty.doc: json: indent the output. Default true.

__FileToDataAction.doc: Parses a tabular file into an array of row objects keyed by data-model property names, and stores `{ rows, rejected, total }` in the action's context property. The file may be an uploaded spreadsheet, a csv or tsv export, a JSON array or an ndjson dump. `fileSource` resolves to the file bytes (a Buffer, a base64 or utf8 string) or to a bucket reference `{ bucket, storageKey }` returned by a bucket upload route, which the action reads in process. When `targetObject` names a DataObject, every column is bound to a property by header (or by the `columns` map), each cell is coerced to the property's type (numbers, booleans, dates, enums, arrays) and validated (required, enum membership), and a cell that cannot be coerced rejects its row. The rows are the input of an UpsertBulkCrudAction (`objects: this.<contextPropertyName>.rows`), the import twin of DataToFileAction. Language lanes: implemented by the nodejs generator only (NJS-first); java, dotnet, golang and rust emit a typed 501 and python raises NotImplementedError, and a design on such a service gets the TABULAR_ACTION_NOT_PORTED warning.

__FileToDataAction.useCase.description: Use to import a spreadsheet or csv into a data object: upload the file to a bucket, pass its storageKey to the api, parse it with this action and write the rows with an UpsertBulkCrudAction.

example.name: parseProductSheet
example.description: Read the uploaded xlsx into product rows validated against the Product object.

FileToDataAction.__fileSource.doc: MScript resolving to the file to parse: a Buffer, a base64 string, a utf8 text string, or a bucket reference `{ bucket, storageKey }` (a Remote/Native bucket of this service, read in process through the bucket layer's readBucketObject).
FileToDataAction.__inputFormat.doc: The tabular format of the file, one of the TabularFormats values. Defaults to xlsx.
FileToDataAction.__targetObject.doc: The DataObject whose properties the rows are bound to and validated against. Without it the rows are returned as parsed, keyed by header, with no coercion.
FileToDataAction.__sheetName.doc: xlsx only: the worksheet to read. Defaults to the first worksheet.
FileToDataAction.__headerRow.doc: 1-based index of the header row; rows above it are ignored. Defaults to 1.
FileToDataAction.__delimiter.doc: csv only: the field delimiter when it is not a comma (e.g. `;` for locale csv exports).
FileToDataAction.__columns.doc: Explicit column bindings. A property without an entry is bound automatically from the header with the same name (case-insensitive); an entry with `header` renames, an entry with `value` computes the property from the whole row.
FileToDataAction.__maxRows.doc: Hard cap on the number of data rows read; a file with more rows is rejected with a typed 400 before any row is parsed.
FileToDataAction.__errorRowHandling.doc: collect (default): a row that fails coercion or validation is skipped and listed under `rejected`. fail: the action throws a typed 400 on the first bad row.
FileToDataAction.__recordPath.doc: json / ndjson: the dot path to the array of records inside a wrapper document, e.g. `data.orders` or `payload.items`. Without it the root array is used, then a root-level `rows`, `items` or `data` array; a single root object becomes one record. Nested values inside a record are reached from `columns[].header` with the same dot / index syntax (`address.city`, `lines[0].qty`).
FileToDataAction.__range.doc: xlsx: the cell range holding the table, e.g. `B3:H200`, when the sheet carries a title block or side notes. The header row is the first row of the range (`headerRow` is then relative to it). Without it the whole sheet is read.
FileToDataAction.__rowFilter.doc: An MScript boolean evaluated per RAW row before binding, with `row` (the raw record keyed by header / key) and `rowIndex` in scope. A false result skips the row silently (counted in `skipped`, never in `rejected`): a subtotal line, a comment row, an inactive flag.
FileToDataAction.__rowTransform.doc: An MScript evaluated per RAW row before binding, with `row` and `rowIndex` in scope; its result REPLACES the raw row. The free hand for a shape the column map cannot express: rename or merge keys, flatten a nested record, split one cell into several, build a composite key. Return the same object when nothing changes.
FileToDataAction.__afterParse.doc: An MScript evaluated ONCE after every row is parsed, with `rows` (the accepted, typed rows), `rejected` and `total` in scope. Its result replaces `rows`: deduplicate, sort, aggregate several lines into one record, or drop what an earlier row already covered. The context property still carries `rejected` and `total` unchanged.

__UpsertBulkCrudAction.doc: Writes an array of rows into a data object with insert-or-update semantics—the bulk import twin of CreateBulkCrudAction. Each row is matched to a stored row on the `matchBy` key (the id, a unique property or a declared composite index); `matchMode` decides whether a match is updated, skipped or rejected and whether a miss is inserted; `columnPolicies` refine an update per column (overwrite, fillIfEmpty, keep, compute). Every write goes through the service's db-layer create/update helpers, so hashed columns, db events, elastic indexing and the entity cache behave exactly as on a single create or update. Columns absent from an incoming row are never touched on update. The action stores `{ inserted, updated, skipped, rejected }` in its context property. Like CreateBulkCrudAction it is CASCADING, never transactional: rows written before a failure stay written. Language lanes: implemented by the nodejs generator only (NJS-first); java, dotnet, golang and rust emit a typed 501 and python raises NotImplementedError, and a design on such a service gets the TABULAR_ACTION_NOT_PORTED warning.

__UpsertBulkCrudAction.useCase.description: Use after a FileToDataAction to load or enrich a table from a spreadsheet: match on a business key and update what the file carries, insert what is new.

example.name: upsertProducts
example.description: Upsert the parsed product rows by SKU; never overwrite a stored price with an empty cell and add incoming stock to the stored stock.

UpsertBulkCrudAction.__childObject.doc: The LOCAL data object the rows are written into. Remote objects are not supported on this action: an import writes through the owning service's db-layer so the per-row match and the column policies see the stored row.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__objects.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the array of row objects to write, keyed by property name—typically `this.<parsed>.rows` from a FileToDataAction, or any array built by an earlier action.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__matchBy.doc: The property names that identify a stored row: `id`, one `unique` property, or the fields of a declared composite index. Defaults to ["id"]. A row whose key values are all empty cannot be matched and is treated as a miss.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__matchMode.doc: One of the BulkMatchModes values: upsert (default), insert, update or skipExisting.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__columnPolicies.doc: Per-column onExisting policies applied when a matched row is updated. A column without an entry is overwritten by the incoming value.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__errorRowHandling.doc: collect (default): a row that fails (no match in update mode, a db refusal, a compute error) is listed under `rejected` and the action continues. fail: the action throws on the first failed row.
UpsertBulkCrudAction.__emptyCells.doc: On UPDATE of a matched row, what an empty incoming cell means for a column without its own policy: `write` (default) writes the null, `skip` leaves the stored value alone. Set `skip` for pasted or partial sheets so a blank cell can never erase a value; inserts always write the row as parsed.

__PaperSize.doc.#: Standard paper sizes for PDF rendering.
__PaperSize.doc.A4: ISO A4 — 210 × 297 mm. International default for invoices and business documents.
__PaperSize.doc.A3: ISO A3 — 297 × 420 mm. Larger reports, posters, fold-out spreads.
__PaperSize.doc.A5: ISO A5 — 148 × 210 mm. Small documents such as receipts or booklets.
__PaperSize.doc.Letter: US Letter — 8.5 × 11 in. North American standard.
__PaperSize.doc.Legal: US Legal — 8.5 × 14 in. North American legal documents.

__PaperMargin.doc: Page margins for PDF rendering, in millimeters. When supplied on a PdfTemplate, applies to every render of that template; per-call overrides on RenderPdfAction take precedence.
__PdfMetadata.doc: Document-level metadata embedded in the generated PDF (visible in PDF readers' document-properties pane and used by some catalog/search systems).

PdfMetadata.__title.doc: PDF document title. Shown in PDF readers and as the browser tab title when viewed inline.
PdfMetadata.__author.doc: Author or organization name embedded in the PDF metadata.
PdfMetadata.__subject.doc: Short description of the document's subject.
PdfMetadata.__keywords.doc: Comma-separated keywords for indexing or search.
PdfMetadata.title: String
PdfMetadata.author: String
PdfMetadata.subject: String

__RenderPdfAction.doc: Renders a PDF from a `PdfTemplate` + input data, or from pre-rendered HTML. The result (an object `{ fileName, content: Buffer, contentType: 'application/pdf' }`) is stored in the action context under `contextPropertyName` and can be referenced by subsequent actions — most commonly attached to a `SendMailAction` or returned as a downloadable response via `sendToClient`. Page setup defaults come from the PdfTemplate; per-call overrides win when supplied. The PDF rendering layer (Gotenberg) is provisioned automatically by the deployer whenever any service declares a PdfTemplate or RenderPdfAction — no provider configuration is exposed at design time.

__RenderPdfAction.useCase.description: Use to render a PDF from a PdfTemplate + input data (or pre-rendered HTML); the result object is stored in context for attaching to a SendMailAction or returned directly when sendToClient is true.

example.name: renderInvoicePdf
example.description: Render the invoice PDF in A4 portrait for emailing to the customer.

RenderPdfAction.__pdfTemplate.doc: Name of a PdfTemplate defined in this service's ServiceLibrary. Required unless `html` is supplied: a RenderPdfAction with neither `pdfTemplate` nor `html` is a validation error, and so is a `pdfTemplate` that names no PdfTemplate in the owning service's library. The authentication module has no ServiceLibrary, so a RenderPdfAction there must use `html` and leave `pdfTemplate` empty. When set, the template's bodyTemplate is rendered with `inputData` to produce the HTML before PDF conversion.
RenderPdfAction.__inputData.doc: An MScript expression evaluating to the data passed into the EJS template. Should be set when `pdfTemplate` is used and `html` is not (validation warns otherwise; the template is then rendered with an empty object). Typically constructed from context (e.g., `{ "js": "this.invoice" }`).
RenderPdfAction.__html.doc: An MScript expression evaluating to a fully-rendered HTML string. Use this when the HTML was produced by a prior action (e.g., a `RenderDataAction` whose output you also use as an email body). When `html` is provided, `pdfTemplate`/`inputData` are not used for body rendering — but `pdfTemplate` may still be referenced to inherit page setup, header, and footer.
RenderPdfAction.__paperSize.doc: Optional per-call override of the template's paper size.
RenderPdfAction.__orientation.doc: Optional per-call override of the template's orientation.
RenderPdfAction.__margin.doc: Optional per-call override of the template's margins.
RenderPdfAction.__fileName.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the file name used both when the PDF is attached to an email and when it is sent to the client (e.g., `` `Invoice-${this.invoice.number}.pdf` ``). Defaults to the template name with a `.pdf` extension.
RenderPdfAction.__sendToClient.doc: If true, the generated PDF is returned to the client as a downloadable attachment in the API response. If false (default), the PDF is only stored in context for use by later actions.

__CheckMailboxAction.doc: Checks a MailAccount's mailbox on demand and stores the matching message summaries in the context. Summaries are the canonical mail envelope WITHOUT bodies or attachment content (`account`, `messageId`, `inReplyTo`, `references`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `subject`, `attachments` metadata, `receivedAt`) — use `ReadMailAction` with a summary's `messageId` to fetch the full message. The mailbox is reached through the mcpbff mail bridge over signed M2M; the account's credentials never enter this service (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md §4/§10). Complements the account's `autoListen` Kafka push: use this when a workflow needs to PULL from the mailbox at a specific moment (a cron sweep, an on-request inbox view) instead of reacting to the `new-email-arrived` topic.

__CheckMailboxAction.useCase.description: Use to pull filtered message summaries from a MailAccount's inbox inside a workflow — e.g. a nightly cron that sweeps unseen invoices, or an API that lists a support mailbox before assigning tickets.

example.name: checkSupportInbox
example.description: List today's unseen support mails about invoices.

CheckMailboxAction.__mailAccount.doc: Codename of a `projectSettings.mailAccountsSettings.mailAccounts[]` entry — the mailbox to check. An unresolvable name is rejected at project-validation time (`UNKNOWN_MAIL_ACCOUNT`). A mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user) may be named too (nodejs): `mailbox` then says which connected mailbox.
CheckMailboxAction.__mailbox.doc: Optional MScript expression naming ONE connected mailbox when `mailAccount` is a mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user); refused on a project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_MAILBOX_ON_PROJECT) and required on a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_STATIC_REFERENCE without it). It evaluates either to the `mailbox` object a connected-mailbox event carries (`{ credentialKey, ownerId, scope, tenantId }`, for example `this.mailbox` when the api declares a body parameter `mailbox`, or `this.request.event.data.mailbox`), or to a string, the mailbox key (its lowercase address) of a mailbox the SESSION owner connected to the template (the user for a user template, the session's tenant for a tenant template). The mcpbff admits the call only when the caller owns the mailbox: the session user for a user template; a tenantOwner / tenantAdmin of that tenant for a tenant template; or the event context of a Kafka-triggered run whose actor is the owner (the system session minted in the event's tenant, acting for the event's user). Any other caller gets MAILBOX_NOT_FOUND, whether the mailbox exists or not. nodejs only; other languages refuse a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED).
CheckMailboxAction.__unseenOnly.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to a boolean. When true (the default), only messages without the `\Seen` flag are returned — 'what's new since the mailbox was last touched'. Set to `false` to search the whole INBOX.
CheckMailboxAction.__since.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to an ISO-8601 date string or `Date` — only messages the server received on/after that date match (IMAP SINCE, day granularity).
CheckMailboxAction.__from.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to a string matched against the From header (case-insensitive substring, e.g. `{ "js": "'@acme.com'" }`).
CheckMailboxAction.__subjectContains.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to a string matched against the Subject header (case-insensitive substring).
CheckMailboxAction.__limit.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to the maximum number of summaries to return. The NEWEST n matches are kept, returned oldest-first. Default 20, ceiling 100.

__ReadMailAction.doc: Fetches ONE full message from a MailAccount's mailbox by its RFC 5322 `messageId` — bodies (`text`/`html`) plus attachment content — and stores it in the context. This is the on-demand content path of the mail family (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md §3): the `new-email-arrived` Kafka envelope and CheckMailboxAction summaries carry attachment METADATA only, and a consumer that needs the bytes reads them through this action. Attachment items arrive as `{ filename, mimeType, size, contentBase64 }`. The mailbox is reached through the mcpbff mail bridge over signed M2M; credentials never enter this service (§4/§10).

__ReadMailAction.useCase.description: Use inside a mail-triggered workflow (or after a CheckMailboxAction) to load a message's bodies and attachment bytes by messageId — e.g. reading the PDF out of an invoice mail before booking it.

example.name: readInvoiceMail
example.description: Fetch the full invoice mail (including the attached PDF) that triggered this workflow.

ReadMailAction.__mailAccount.doc: Codename of a `projectSettings.mailAccountsSettings.mailAccounts[]` entry — the mailbox to read from. An unresolvable name is rejected at project-validation time (`UNKNOWN_MAIL_ACCOUNT`). A mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user) may be named too (nodejs): `mailbox` then says which connected mailbox.
ReadMailAction.__mailbox.doc: Optional MScript expression naming ONE connected mailbox when `mailAccount` is a mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user); refused on a project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_MAILBOX_ON_PROJECT) and required on a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_STATIC_REFERENCE without it). It evaluates either to the `mailbox` object a connected-mailbox event carries (`{ credentialKey, ownerId, scope, tenantId }`, for example `this.mailbox` when the api declares a body parameter `mailbox`, or `this.request.event.data.mailbox`), or to a string, the mailbox key (its lowercase address) of a mailbox the SESSION owner connected to the template (the user for a user template, the session's tenant for a tenant template). The mcpbff admits the call only when the caller owns the mailbox: the session user for a user template; a tenantOwner / tenantAdmin of that tenant for a tenant template; or the event context of a Kafka-triggered run whose actor is the owner (the system session minted in the event's tenant, acting for the event's user). Any other caller gets MAILBOX_NOT_FOUND, whether the mailbox exists or not. nodejs only; other languages refuse a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED).
ReadMailAction.__messageId.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the RFC 5322 Message-ID of the message to fetch (angle brackets optional) — typically `this.newMail.messageId` from the `new-email-arrived` envelope, or a CheckMailboxAction summary's `messageId`. An unknown id makes the action fail with `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`.
ReadMailAction.__markSeen.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to a boolean. When true, the message's `\Seen` flag is set after a successful read. Default FALSE: on an autoListen account the seen flag is the listener's delivery cursor (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md §6) — marking a not-yet-published message seen would eat its Kafka delivery.
ReadMailAction.__includeAttachments.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluating to a boolean. When true (the default), each attachment's bytes are returned base64-encoded in `contentBase64`; set to `false` to fetch bodies only (attachment items then carry metadata with `contentBase64: null`).

__SendMailAction.doc: Sends an email using a configured email provider — or, when `mailAccount` is set, ON BEHALF OF a project MailAccount through the mcpbff mail bridge (docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md). The subject, body, and recipient addresses are defined via MScript and can be dynamically constructed from context. With `inReplyTo`/`references` the send becomes a threaded reply that real mail clients keep inside the original conversation. This action is commonly used for transactional notifications, confirmations, alerts, and mailbox replies.

__SendMailAction.useCase.description: Use to send a transactional email via a configured email provider — subject/body/recipients built from context, with optional attachments such as a rendered invoice PDF from a prior RenderPdfAction.

example.name: sendInvoiceEmail
example.description: Email the customer their invoice with the rendered PDF attached.

SendMailAction.__provider.doc: Codename of the configured email provider. Must match an entry in `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` with `kind: 'email'` (or `kind: 'multi'`). The action handler imports the matching native-integration client from `_common/notification-providers/email/<resolvedProvider>` and calls `provider.send(payload)` directly — no kafka hop, no interservice call. When omitted, the project default `notificationService.serviceSettings.serviceOptions.defaultEmailProviderName` is used. An unresolvable name throws `UnknownNotificationProvider`; a kind mismatch throws `IncompatibleProviderKind` at project-validation time. Exactly one transport must be chosen: set `provider` OR `mailAccount`, never both.
SendMailAction.__mailAccount.doc: Codename of a `projectSettings.mailAccountsSettings.mailAccounts[]` entry. When set, the mail goes out ON BEHALF OF that mailbox identity through its own connector (SMTP for v1) instead of a NotificationProvider: the runtime calls the mcpbff mail bridge over signed M2M (the account's credentials exist only in the mcpbff deployable — see docs/ADR-mail-account-family.md §4/§10), the `From` header is ALWAYS the account's `address` (any `from` expression is ignored), and the account's `sendEnabled`/`replyEnabled` gates are enforced at send time. Mutually exclusive with `provider`. A mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user) may be named too (nodejs): `mailbox` then says which connected mailbox, and the reply goes out from that owner's own mailbox.
SendMailAction.__mailbox.doc: Optional MScript expression naming ONE connected mailbox when `mailAccount` is a mailbox TEMPLATE (ownerScope tenant or user); refused on a project account (MAIL_ACCOUNT_MAILBOX_ON_PROJECT) and required on a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_STATIC_REFERENCE without it). It evaluates either to the `mailbox` object a connected-mailbox event carries (`{ credentialKey, ownerId, scope, tenantId }`, for example `this.mailbox` when the api declares a body parameter `mailbox`, or `this.request.event.data.mailbox`), or to a string, the mailbox key (its lowercase address) of a mailbox the SESSION owner connected to the template (the user for a user template, the session's tenant for a tenant template). The mcpbff admits the call only when the caller owns the mailbox: the session user for a user template; a tenantOwner / tenantAdmin of that tenant for a tenant template; or the event context of a Kafka-triggered run whose actor is the owner (the system session minted in the event's tenant, acting for the event's user). Any other caller gets MAILBOX_NOT_FOUND, whether the mailbox exists or not. nodejs only; other languages refuse a template (MAIL_ACCOUNT_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED).
SendMailAction.__subject.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the email subject. Can include context variables like `this.user.name`.
SendMailAction.__body.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the email content, usually a rendered HTML or plaintext string. Often prepared using `RenderDataAction`.
SendMailAction.__to.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the recipient email address (or a list of addresses).
SendMailAction.__from.doc: An MScript expression defining the sender email address. Can be static or context-driven. Ignored on the `mailAccount` path — an on-behalf send is always From the account's own address.
SendMailAction.__cc.doc: Optional MScript expression to specify CC recipients. Can be a single address or array.
SendMailAction.__attachments.doc: Optional MScript expression that resolves to an array of attachment objects. Each item must have the shape `{ fileName: string, content: Buffer | base64-string, contentType: string }`. Typically populated from upstream actions — most commonly `RenderPdfAction`, whose stored context object already matches this shape (e.g., `{ "js": "[this.invoicePdf]" }`).
SendMailAction.__inReplyTo.doc: Optional MScript expression that evaluates to the RFC 5322 Message-ID of the message being replied to (as delivered in the `new-email-arrived` envelope or a ReadMailAction result, e.g. `{ "js": "this.newMail.messageId" }`). When set, the send is a REPLY: the id is emitted as the `In-Reply-To` header (and appended to `References`) so real mail clients thread the reply under the original. On the `mailAccount` path the account's `replyEnabled` gate applies; on the provider path the header is passed through where the provider supports custom headers.
SendMailAction.__references.doc: Optional MScript expression that evaluates to the full thread chain of RFC 5322 Message-IDs, oldest first (e.g. `{ "js": "this.newMail.references" }`). Emitted as the `References` header; when `inReplyTo` is set and missing from the list, it is appended automatically so the chain stays RFC-complete.
SendMailAction.subject: MScript

__SendSmsAction.doc: Sends an SMS message using a configured SMS provider. The recipient phone number, message content, and sender ID are defined using MScript expressions. Useful for OTPs, short notifications, or alerts.

__SendSmsAction.useCase.description: Use to send a short SMS via a configured provider — OTPs, delivery alerts, reminders — to a phone number in international format.

example.name: sendOtpSms
example.description: Text the one-time verification code to the user's phone.

body.js: `Your Example verification code is ${this.otpCode}. It expires in 5 minutes.`

SendSmsAction.__provider.doc: Codename of the configured SMS provider. Must match an entry in `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` with `kind: 'sms'` (or `kind: 'multi'`). The action handler imports the matching native-integration client from `_common/notification-providers/sms/<resolvedProvider>` and calls `provider.send(payload)` directly — no kafka hop, no interservice call. Required (REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING) when the project declares an sms-capable (sms / multi) provider. May be omitted only in a project that declares NO sms provider: the action then sends to the built-in SMS sink on every deployment, production included (wired at build time), and validation warns once with SMS_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK. An unresolvable name throws `UnknownNotificationProvider`; a kind mismatch throws `IncompatibleProviderKind` at project-validation time. A service whose action sends to the SMS sink this way gets the mail sink coordinate (MAILSINK_PORT / MAILSINK_USER / MAILSINK_PASS) on preview and stage like a notification-sending service, so nothing is configured for it.
SendSmsAction.__subject.doc: Optional subject line, if supported by the SMS provider. Otherwise ignored. Can be used for internal categorization or template labeling.
SendSmsAction.__body.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the message body. This should be a short, plaintext message suitable for mobile delivery.
SendSmsAction.__to.doc: An MScript expression that resolves to the recipient's phone number (in international format).
SendSmsAction.__from.doc: The sender identifier, either a short code or alphanumeric sender name, depending on provider capabilities.
SendSmsAction.subject: MScript

__SendPushNotificationAction.doc: Sends a push notification using a configured provider (e.g., Firebase, OneSignal). Subject and body are rendered via MScript and sent to the recipient device or user ID. Suitable for in-app or mobile alerts.

__SendPushNotificationAction.useCase.description: Use to send a mobile/in-app push via a configured provider (Firebase, OneSignal) to a user or device id — order updates, mentions, alerts.

example.name: pushOrderShipped
example.description: Notify the customer's devices that their order has shipped.

body.js: `Order ${this.order.number} has shipped and will arrive in 2-3 days.`

SendPushNotificationAction.__provider.doc: Codename of the configured push provider. Must match an entry in `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` with `kind: 'push'` (or `kind: 'multi'`). The action handler imports the matching native-integration client from `_common/notification-providers/push/<resolvedProvider>` and calls `provider.send(payload)` directly — for `targetKind: 'userId'` it first fetches DeviceToken rows via cross-service RPC to the notification service. Required (REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING) when the project declares a push-capable (push / multi) provider: there is no project-default fallback on this action. May be omitted only in a project that declares NO push provider: the action then sends to the built-in push sink on every deployment, production included (wired at build time), validation warns once with PUSH_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK listing the action, and the service gets the mail sink coordinate (MAILSINK_*) on preview and stage. An unresolvable name throws `UnknownNotificationProvider`; a kind mismatch throws `IncompatibleProviderKind` at project-validation time. When the named provider's credentials are not set, the send goes to the built-in push sink on the dev, preview and stage deployments (stored in the mail sink as a mail to `push-<token hash>@push-sink.invalid`) and fails on production.
SendPushNotificationAction.__subject.doc: The notification title or heading, rendered via MScript. This typically appears as the bold title on a mobile push alert.
SendPushNotificationAction.__body.doc: The body text of the notification, defined via MScript. Should be concise and actionable.
SendPushNotificationAction.__to.doc: The recipient device ID or user identifier, evaluated from context. Format depends on the configured provider.
SendPushNotificationAction.__from.doc: Optional sender or topic ID. Used to label or route notifications by source when supported by the provider.
SendPushNotificationAction.subject: MScript

__SendWhatsAppAction.doc: Sends a WhatsApp Business message using a configured WhatsApp provider — either Meta WhatsApp Cloud API (provider='whatsapp') or Twilio's WhatsApp channel (provider='twilio' with kind='whatsapp'). Supports free-form text sends inside the 24-hour customer-service window AND template-based sends (mandatory outside the window). With `template` set the provider sends the approved template: Meta sends `{ type: 'template', template: { name, language: { code }, components } }`, Twilio sends `{ contentSid, contentVariables }` with no body. Without it the message is free-form text, which Meta (131047) and Twilio (63016) refuse outside the window after accepting the request - design-time warning WHATSAPP_FREEFORM_OUTSIDE_WINDOW. LANGUAGE NOTE: the template send is implemented by the nodejs, dotnet and java actions and providers; the other language targets still send free-form text (ports pending).

__SendWhatsAppAction.useCase.description: Use to send a WhatsApp Business message — free-form text inside the 24h session window, or a registered template (with variables) for re-engagement outside it.

example.name: sendShippingWhatsApp
example.description: Send a templated shipping-update WhatsApp with order number and tracking link.

SendWhatsAppAction.__provider.doc: Codename of the configured WhatsApp provider. Must match an entry in `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` with `kind: 'whatsapp'` (or `kind: 'multi'`). The action handler imports the matching native-integration client from `_common/notification-providers/whatsapp/<resolvedProvider>` and calls `provider.send(payload)` directly. Required (REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING) when the project declares a whatsapp-capable (whatsapp / multi) provider: there is no project-default fallback on this action. May be omitted only in a project that declares NO whatsapp provider: the action then sends to the built-in WhatsApp sink on every deployment, production included (wired at build time), validation warns once with WHATSAPP_FLOWS_GO_TO_SINK listing the action, and the service gets the mail sink coordinate (MAILSINK_*) on preview and stage. An unresolvable name throws `UnknownNotificationProvider`; a kind mismatch throws `IncompatibleProviderKind` at project-validation time. When the named provider's credentials are not set, the send goes to the built-in WhatsApp sink on the dev, preview and stage deployments (stored in the mail sink as a mail to `whatsapp-<digits>@whatsapp-sink.invalid`) and fails on production.
SendWhatsAppAction.__subject.doc: Optional subject prefix for the message — combined with `body` when supported by the provider variant. Most WhatsApp clients ignore subject lines; safe to leave null.
SendWhatsAppAction.__body.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the free-form message body. Used as the WhatsApp text payload when no `template` is set. Required for session-window sends.
SendWhatsAppAction.__to.doc: An MScript expression that resolves to the recipient phone in E.164 format (with or without the leading '+'). Must be a WhatsApp-opted-in number.
SendWhatsAppAction.__from.doc: Optional sender override. For Twilio variant: a WhatsApp-enabled sender like 'whatsapp:+14155238886'; falls back to env-configured default.
SendWhatsAppAction.__template.doc: Optional approved WhatsApp template. Required for sends outside the 24-hour customer-service window; absent, the message is sent as free-form text, which is delivered only inside the window (WHATSAPP_FREEFORM_OUTSIDE_WINDOW warning). For a Meta Cloud API provider it is the approved template name (`^[a-z0-9_]+$`, e.g. `order_shipped`); for a Twilio provider it is the Content SID (`^HX[0-9a-f]{32}$`). Case-sensitive and never rewritten; the format is checked against the resolved provider at design time (WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME_INVALID, ERROR). When set, `body` / `subject` are not sent.
SendWhatsAppAction.__templateVariables.doc: Optional MScript that resolves to the template parameters. Used only when `template` is set. For Meta it becomes `template.components`: an array of component objects (`[{ type: 'body', parameters: [...] }]`) is sent as is, and an array of plain values (`[this.order.number, this.order.trackingUrl]`) is the shorthand for the body text parameters {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in order. For Twilio it becomes `contentVariables` (JSON-stringified): an object (`{ '1': ..., '2': ... }`) as is, an array numbered from 1.
SendWhatsAppAction.__templateLanguage.doc: Optional MScript that resolves to the Meta template language code (`'en'`, `'tr'`, `'pt_BR'`, or a per-recipient read such as `this.customer.language`). Used only when `template` is set; empty or null means `en`. Twilio ignores it (a Content SID names one language).
SendWhatsAppAction.subject: MScript

__PaymentAction.doc: Calls the proper native payment provider functions according to the current stage of payment lifecycle. The bound provider is selected by `providerName` (lookup into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[]). The legacy `gateway` field is preserved for back-compat with pre-PaymentProvider-refactor configs — when only `gateway` is set, it resolves to a `legacyStripe` provider via the runtime compat shim. WHERE THE CALLER'S PAYMENT CONTROLS COME FROM: a `start` stage builds the provider intent from the OWNING API'S BOUND REQUEST PARAMETERS - the emitted action spreads that request-parameter blob into the intent input and PaymentManager reads `return_url`, `paymentMethodId` and `providerOptions` off it. The money facts (amount / currency / orderId / customer) come from the parent DataObject's checkout block bindings against the PERSISTED order row, never from the caller, so those three keys are the only values a caller ever contributes. An api that declares no requestParameter at a caller-supplied `httpLocation` (`body`, or `query` on a bodyless method) can receive none of them - design-time finding PAYMENT_START_NO_CALLER_PARAMS. The consequence that bites hardest is `return_url`: with a hosted-checkout provider (iyzico Checkout Form) the buyer's browser leaves for the provider and returns to the service's own `/v1/payments/checkout-return/<provider>` route, which redirects 303 to the ticket's `metadata.returnUrl` - stamped from `return_url` at start - and, when the ticket carries none, answers a minimal JSON confirmation instead. That JSON is documented behaviour, not an error: the payment succeeds and the buyer's browser simply stops on it. An iyzico saved card's 3-D Secure ends the same way on the generated `/v1/payments/threeds-return/<provider>` route, which calls 3dsecure/auth itself, so an iyzico design authors no `complete` stage. Neither does a Stripe design (Stripe.js finishes the intent and the generated webhook route records it) nor an Adyen design (its details step is the generated `PATCH /v1/complete<object>payment/:orderId` route); of the native providers only PayPal's capture after the buyer approved needs an authored `complete` stage.

__PaymentAction.useCase.description: Use to drive the one-time payment lifecycle (start/complete/refresh/callback/simple) against a named PaymentProvider — e.g. create a payment intent at checkout that the frontend then confirms.

example.name: startOrderPayment
example.description: Create a payment intent for the order so the client can confirm it.

PaymentAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. Selects which native adapter handles this action. When null/omitted, falls back to the legacy `gateway` field for back-compat (resolves to `legacyStripe` if only `gateway` is set).
PaymentAction.__stage.doc: The type of the stage call that the action will make. It can start, complete or refresh a payment, or read back a provider callback. New stages (refund, subscribe, payout, dispute) are handled by their dedicated Action types; PaymentAction itself only owns the original one-time-payment stages (simple, start, complete, refresh, callback). Any other PaymentStage value on a PaymentAction (refund, dispute, subscribe, cancelSubscription, payout) is a design-time ERROR PAYMENT_STAGE_OFF_CONTRACT: the generated action has no arm for it and would fall back to starting a payment, i.e. CHARGE the buyer; use a RefundAction, SubscriptionAction or PayoutAction (disputes arrive on the provider webhook). Every stage reads the caller's payment USER PARAMS from ONE blob: this api's bound request parameters at a caller-supplied httpLocation (`body`, or `query` on a bodyless method), one flat key per declared parameter plus the keys of a declared Object parameter named `paymentUserParams`. `start` passes that blob through as the one `return_url`, `paymentMethodId` and `providerOptions` are read off (see the class description), so declare those keys whenever the flow needs them - without a caller-supplied parameter the api can receive none of them and validation reports PAYMENT_START_NO_CALLER_PARAMS. `complete` and `refresh` address an intent that already exists and read its id off the SAME blob (`providerIntentId`, or `paymentId`; `complete` also reads `return_url` and `paymentMethodId`), so declare that id as a caller-supplied requestParameter too: without it the nodejs emission of the stage throws on every call, and validation reports PAYMENT_STAGE_NO_INTENT_ID_PARAM (a warning, not an error: the other language runtimes read the id off the raw request). `callback` reads the provider's own request. On a checkout order object `complete`, `refresh` and `callback` are GATED before the provider is called, exactly as the generated payment routes are: the `sys_<X>Payment` ticket recorded for the addressed id must exist (400 PAYMENT_NOT_STARTED), its order row must exist (404 NOT_FOUND), and the caller must own that order (another user is 403 NOT_OWNER, a request with no session is 401 LOGIN_REQUIRED; only a trusted system caller or a kafka consumer declared `loginRequired: false` skips the owner check, never the ticket check). A ticket that is still a start claim (a start of the order is in flight) is 409 PAYMENT_START_IN_FLIGHT, as on the generated complete / refresh routes. An anonymous hosted-checkout browser return or a provider webhook therefore cannot drive these stages: those arrive on the generated `/v1/payments/checkout-return/<provider>` and webhook routes, and an iyzico saved card's 3-D Secure callback on the generated `/v1/payments/threeds-return/<provider>` route, which completes the payment (3dsecure/auth) without any stage. Stripe needs no `complete` stage either (the browser finishes the intent through Stripe.js and the webhook route records it), and Adyen's details step is the generated `PATCH /v1/complete<object>payment/:orderId` route. Of the native providers only PayPal's capture after the buyer approved needs an authored `complete` stage, in a session api the return page calls. `start` and `simple` on a checkout order object authorize the persisted order BEFORE anything reaches the provider, with the generated start route's ownership rule: the order's owner (the order row first, then the payment ticket), a payment admin (`admin` / `superAdmin`; `superAdmin` / `saasAdmin` in a multi-tenant project) or a verified inter-service caller the api admits may start it; another user is 403 NOT_OWNER and a request with no caller 401, before any intent, ticket or charge (a trusted system caller is not asked). On an order object with no `sessionSettings.isOwnerField` a buyer cannot start it at all, and validation reports PAYMENT_START_ORDER_OWNERSHIP_UNBOUND (a warning) for a start api a non-admin can reach. The check covers the payment action only, not what an earlier action of the same workflow read.
PaymentAction.__buyerAbsent.doc: Declares that this action charges while the BUYER IS NOT IN SESSION: a scheduled or merchant-triggered charge made on the buyer's behalf (a renewal or card-on-file charge a cron job or an event consumer runs, an agreed top-up, a later charge the buyer agreed to in advance, such as one an AI assistant confirmed for them earlier), never a checkout the buyer is clicking through. The off-session charge still needs a proven stored card: a scheduled or system run (a cron or internal transport, or a Kafka consumer declared loginRequired false, recognised from the transport and never from the request) proves it from the order owner through the identity owner's machine-only reads (needs an owner column on the order object), an HTTP call proves it with the caller's forwarded token, and an anonymous HTTP call proves none and stays on-session; the framework does not check which user calls the API over HTTP, so never put such an action on an API the buyer calls while paying. Default false. It is a design fact, read at generation time; no request value can set it. It matters on a Stripe entry with savedCardOffSession 'verified' (beside savedCardThreeDSMode 'verifyOnce'): only a start / simple charge of an action declared buyerAbsent, on a checkout order object, on a proven stored card (the order owner's on a system run, the caller's on an HTTP call) whose row is 3-D Secure verified, is sent off_session (a merchant-initiated transaction, no buyer step, no 3-D Secure liability shift). Every other action stays on-session on that entry and Stripe may still ask the buyer to authenticate. Card-network rules allow a merchant-initiated charge only while the buyer is absent, under the stored-credential agreement accepted when the card was saved, so a buyer-present checkout (a one-click purchase included) must NOT declare it. Declared on another provider, on a Stripe entry without savedCardOffSession 'verified', on a complete / refresh / callback stage, on a marketplace order object, on an order object bound to a provider entry of another brand, or with no checkout order object behind it, it does nothing and draws the warning PAYMENT_ACTION_BUYER_ABSENT_INERT. nodejs services only for now.

__VerifyWebhookAction.doc: Verifies a webhook call of a provider with its signature secret and reads the parameters and writes them to the context. The bound provider is selected by `providerName` (lookup into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[]); the verification scheme (hmac / rsa-pub / cert / signature) is derived from the provider's PaymentCapabilities.webhookStyle. A 'refetch' provider (Mangopay) sends unsigned GET hooks and has no signature to verify, so this action refuses it; its hooks are received by the generated GET /v1/payments/webhook/<provider> route. The legacy `provider: 'stripe'` field is preserved for back-compat with pre-PaymentProvider-refactor configs. Payment-lifecycle webhooks need no api: the generated `/v1/payments/webhook/<provider>` route verifies them, stores the event and runs the lifecycle hooks. An authored api running this action cannot drive payment stages either (PaymentAction `complete` / `refresh` / `callback` refuse an anonymous caller), so use it only for a provider notification the design consumes outside the payment lifecycle.

__VerifyWebhookAction.useCase.description: Use at the top of a provider-webhook API to verify the inbound call's signature against the bound PaymentProvider and place the parsed event on context for subsequent handling.

example.name: verifyStripeWebhook
example.description: Verify the incoming Stripe webhook signature and expose the parsed event.

VerifyWebhookAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. Selects which adapter verifies this webhook. When null/omitted, falls back to the legacy `provider` field.
VerifyWebhookAction.__secretKey.doc: An MScript value to represent or to reach the secret key of the webhook signature. Kept for back-compat; new designs let the framework resolve the secret from the PaymentProvider entry's configuration block automatically.

__RefundAction.doc: Issues a refund against a prior captured payment via the bound PaymentProvider. Supports full refunds (omit `refundAmountProperty`) and partial refunds (set `refundAmountProperty` to a PropRefer that resolves to a numeric value at runtime). Provider must have capabilities.supportsRefundsFull=true for full refunds and supportsRefundsPartial=true for partial. The action writes a sys_<X>Refund record and advances the parent sys_<X>Payment state machine to `partially_refunded` or `refunded` accordingly. The action needs a checkout target in its own service (the api's object, a related checkout object, or the service's single one); keep the RefundAction on the service that owns the checkout object. A refund-only service that owns none sets `providerOnly: true` with an explicit `providerName`, a `paymentIntentIdProperty` and a mandatory `ownershipGuard` (403 NOT_OWNER when false, before any provider call); it then writes no local refund record.

__RefundAction.useCase.description: Use to refund a captured payment — omit refundAmountProperty for a full refund, or point it at a numeric property for a partial refund; writes a refund record and advances the payment state machine.

example.name: refundOrder
example.description: Issue a partial refund for a returned item against the order's payment intent.

RefundAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. When null/omitted, the framework reads the providerName from the parent DataObject's CheckoutConfig.
RefundAction.__paymentIntentIdProperty.doc: Property holding the payment intent / payment ticket id to refund. Resolves at runtime against the request context. When no binding resolves an intent id, the action refunds the payment recorded on the sys_<Order>Payment ticket of the order the api acts on (its own row, or the row's single relation to the order); an order without a payment ticket answers 404.
RefundAction.__refundAmountProperty.doc: Optional property holding the partial refund amount. When omitted, a full refund is issued. Provider must support supportsRefundsPartial when this is set.
RefundAction.__reasonProperty.doc: Optional property holding a refund reason (one of duplicate, fraudulent, requested_by_customer, other). Passed through to the provider when supported.
RefundAction.__providerOnly.doc: Opt-in (default false) for a refund-only service that owns no checkout object: the action refunds a payment another service charged, straight through the provider, with no local `sys_<Order>Payment` ticket and no `sys_<Order>Refund` ledger row. Requires an explicit `providerName` (a declared paymentProvidersSettings provider), a `paymentIntentIdProperty` and an `ownershipGuard`; validation refuses providerOnly without any of the three (REFUND_PROVIDER_ONLY_GUARD_REQUIRED, REFUND_PROVIDER_ONLY_BINDING_INCOMPLETE). With providerOnly the service's checkout objects are ignored by this action (no ticket lookup, no ownership preflight, no close-out), so the ownershipGuard is the only check that the caller may refund the intent. Unset, the action needs a checkout target in its service and a service without one is refused PAYMENT_NOT_CONFIGURED. The preferred alternative keeps the RefundAction on the service that owns the checkout object, where the ticket preflight (404 for an unknown intent, 403 NOT_OWNER for a foreign owner, 409 for a terminal or fully refunded payment) runs. nodejs, python, rust, java and dotnet: on another service language providerOnly is refused (REFUND_PROVIDER_ONLY_NOT_PORTED).
RefundAction.__ownershipGuard.doc: Required when `providerOnly` is true, ignored otherwise. An MScript boolean expression, evaluated at runtime BEFORE the provider is resolved or called, that answers whether this caller may refund the intent (for example `this.session.userId === this.charge.ownerId`, after an earlier action fetched the charge from the service that owns it, or `this.session.roleId === 'admin'`). A falsy result refuses the call with 403 NOT_OWNER and no provider call is made. No role bypasses it: grant operators inside the expression.

__InvoiceAction.doc: Drives the accounts-receivable invoice lifecycle for an invoicing-enabled DataObject through the generated per-object InvoiceManager. `operation` picks the step: create (draft from the source row, line snapshot through invoiceLineRelation), finalize (number assignment, draft → open), void, or applyPayment (allocation + the partially_paid/paid transition). The PaymentAction family's invoicing twin (ADR-invoice-fiscalization §7.5) and the imperative escape hatch for `issuePolicy: manual` designs — the declarative issuePolicy triggers (onPaymentCaptured) run without any action. The framework-internal ledger and an external system of record are one code path; the effective provider binding is the owning DataObject's InvoicingConfig (providerName → the project's single declared provider → the implicit internal adapter). RESULT: `contextPropertyName` receives the provider's NORMALIZED result, not a sys_<X>Invoice row - create, finalize and void store a NormalizedInvoiceDetail (providerInvoiceId, invoiceNumber, series, statusLiteral, currency, subtotal, vatTotal, total, amountPaid, amountRemaining, dueDate, issuedAt, buyer, seller, lines, vatExemptionReasonCode, vatExemptionReason, metadata), applyPayment stores a NormalizedPaymentApplication (providerAllocationId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, appliedAt, paymentRef, invoiceStatus, amountPaid, amountRemaining, metadata). There is no `id`: the invoice id is `providerInvoiceId`, and the source row id travels on `metadata.sourceObjectId`. Chaining a create into a finalize: `{ name: cutInvoice, operation: create, contextPropertyName: inv }` then `{ name: finalizeIt, operation: finalize, invoiceIdProperty: inv.providerInvoiceId }`, scheduled in that order. A read of a member the result type does not declare (`this.inv.id`, `invoiceIdProperty: inv.id`) is reported as INVOICE_ACTION_RESULT_UNKNOWN_FIELD (WARNING). creditNote issues a NormalizedCreditNote (providerCreditNoteId, providerInvoiceId, amount, currency, reason, issuedAt, metadata) through CreditNoteManager, with optional idempotencyKeyProperty. For refunds reuse `refund-<providerRefundId>`. Credit notes do not create a new fiscal source or submit automatically.

__InvoiceAction.useCase.description: Use inside a manual invoicing workflow — cut a draft from an order, finalize it with a legal number, record an out-of-band payment, or void a mis-issued document.

example.name: finalizeContractInvoice
example.description: Assign the legal number and open the invoice issued for this contract.

InvoiceAction.__operation.doc: The invoice lifecycle operation to perform: create | finalize | void | applyPayment | creditNote. creditNote issues a credit adjustment; its result is NormalizedCreditNote.
InvoiceAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.invoiceProvidersSettings.invoiceProviders[].name — a design-time capability check. When null/omitted (the normal shape), the binding falls back to the owning DataObject's invoicing.configuration.providerName and ultimately the framework-internal provider. At RUNTIME the object's InvoiceManager always executes against the object-level binding; declaring a DIFFERENT provider here than the object resolves is a design error the validator reports.
InvoiceAction.__sourceIdProperty.doc: operation=create: property holding the SOURCE row id the invoice is issued from (invoicing.configuration.sourceObjectName, or the invoicing object itself). When omitted, the api's own persisted row id is used.
InvoiceAction.__invoiceIdProperty.doc: Required for finalize / void / applyPayment / creditNote: property holding the invoice id to operate on - the `providerInvoiceId` of a NormalizedInvoiceDetail (for the internal provider that IS the sys_<X>Invoice row id). Resolved params -> the api row -> the context, one dotted segment at a time, so an earlier create action's result is addressed as `<its contextPropertyName>.providerInvoiceId` (e.g. `inv.providerInvoiceId`). The create result has NO `id`: `inv.id` (or an addToContext `this.inv?.id`) resolves nothing and the action throws "invoiceIdProperty did not resolve an invoice id" at runtime, after the main write has committed; validation warns INVOICE_ACTION_RESULT_UNKNOWN_FIELD on that read.
InvoiceAction.__amountProperty.doc: operation=applyPayment or creditNote: required property holding a positive amount in major units.
InvoiceAction.__paymentRefProperty.doc: operation=applyPayment: optional property holding the payment reference (provider intent id, bank transfer reference, receipt no).
InvoiceAction.__reasonProperty.doc: operation=void or creditNote: optional property holding the reason.
InvoiceAction.__idempotencyKeyProperty.doc: operation=creditNote: optional property holding the complete idempotency key. For a refund-driven note bind `refund-<providerRefundId>`, the same key the automatic refund bridge uses. A replay returns the original note without another issuance hook.

__FiscalizeAction.doc: Drives the regulatory fiscalization lifecycle for a fiscalization-enabled DataObject through the generated per-object FiscalizationManager. `operation` picks the step: submit (serialize the finalized invoice snapshot and submit it through the jurisdiction policy pipeline), cancel (the network's cancellation flow for an accepted document), or queryStatus (a one-shot provider poll dispatched through the same event path the status cron uses). The InvoiceAction family's fiscal twin (ADR-invoice-fiscalization sec. 7.5) and the imperative escape hatch for `submitPolicy: manual` designs - the declarative submitPolicy trigger (onInvoiceFinalized) runs without any action. The effective provider binding is the owning DataObject's FiscalizationConfig (fiscalProviderName -> the project's single declared fiscal provider); there is NO framework-internal fiscal provider. resubmit retries a rejected or failed fiscal document through the existing correction pipeline using fiscalDocumentIdProperty; the operator route remains available.

__FiscalizeAction.useCase.description: Use inside a manual fiscalization workflow - submit the fiscal document for an order's finalized invoice on an operator's approval, cancel an accepted document inside the legal window, or poll the authority verdict on demand.

example.name: submitOrderFiscalDocument
example.description: Submit the e-document for this order's finalized invoice.

FiscalizeAction.__operation.doc: The fiscal operation to perform: submit | cancel | queryStatus | resubmit.
FiscalizeAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.fiscalProvidersSettings.fiscalProviders[].name - a design-time capability check. When null/omitted (the normal shape), the binding is the owning DataObject's fiscalization.configuration.fiscalProviderName (or the project's single declared fiscal provider).
