At RUNTIME the object's FiscalizationManager always executes against the object-level binding; declaring a DIFFERENT provider here than the object resolves is a design error the validator reports.
FiscalizeAction.__sourceIdProperty.doc: operation=submit: property holding the SOURCE row id whose finalized invoice is fiscalized. When omitted, the api's own persisted row id is used.
FiscalizeAction.__fiscalDocumentIdProperty.doc: Required for cancel / queryStatus / resubmit: property holding the fiscal document id (the sys_<X>FiscalDocument row id) to operate on.
FiscalizeAction.__reasonProperty.doc: operation=cancel: optional property holding the cancellation reason.

__SubscriptionAction.doc: Creates, updates, cancels, or refreshes a recurring subscription against the bound PaymentProvider. The `stage` field picks the operation: `subscribe` creates a new subscription, `cancelSubscription` cancels an existing one, `refresh` pulls the latest provider state. Provider must have capabilities.supportsSubscriptions=true. The action writes / updates a sys_<X>Subscription record. A `subscribe` can need the buyer: on Stripe a first payment that needs 3-D Secure answers `statusLiteral: 'past_due'` with `nextAction` for Stripe.js; on iyzico every subscribe answers `pending_provider` with `checkoutForm`, iyzico's hosted subscription form. The Business API must return that answer to the frontend. A PROVIDER REFUSAL AFTER THE MAIN WRITE never leaves a silent half-commit: a `subscribe` placed after the main operation of a CREATE api with onActionError `throwError` deletes the row that create just wrote and answers the refusal (502, no row stands, an event already queued about the row is cancelled); in every other post-write placement (a `cancelSubscription` or `refresh` after an update, or `completeApi`) the row the main write committed stands, the api answers 2xx with that row and the refusal in `actionFailures` (action name, errorCode such as SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER_REFUSED, detail) and its route event is still published - check `actionFailures` before treating the change as done at the provider.

__SubscriptionAction.useCase.description: Use to manage a recurring subscription against the bound provider — stage=subscribe to start a plan (planProperty required on the action, or inherited from the DataObject subscription config), cancelSubscription or refresh on an existing subscription.

example.name: subscribeToPlan
example.description: Subscribe the customer to the selected plan.

SubscriptionAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. When null/omitted, the framework reads providerName from the parent DataObject's SubscriptionConfig.
SubscriptionAction.__planProperty.doc: Property holding the SubscriptionPlan reference (plan code or plan id). Required when stage=subscribe UNLESS the DataObject this api targets sets objectSettings.subscription.configuration.planProperty, which a subscribe-stage action falls back to when it declares none of its own. Design-time validation accepts either one and reports SUBSCRIPTION_ACTION_MISSING_PLAN_PROPERTY only when NEITHER is set. Setting it here overrides the DataObject-level property for this action. Inheriting it raises the design-time WARNING SUBSCRIPTION_ACTION_PLAN_PROPERTY_INHERITED, because the fallback is implemented by the nodejs, python and dotnet generators ONLY: on java, rust, golang and php the emitted subscribe stage has no fallback path, so java fails every call with a 500 naming the missing planProperty and rust refuses every call with 400 SUBSCRIPTION_PLAN_REQUIRED before reaching the provider. Set it on the action itself when any of those four is a generation target.
SubscriptionAction.__subscriptionIdProperty.doc: Property holding the subscription id to operate on. Required when stage=cancelSubscription or stage=refresh.
SubscriptionAction.__cancelAtPeriodEndProperty.doc: Optional property holding a boolean. When stage=cancelSubscription and this resolves true, cancellation is scheduled at period end; otherwise immediate.

__PayoutAction.doc: Triggers a marketplace payout to a connected sub-merchant account via the bound PaymentProvider. Provider must have capabilities.supportsMarketplace=true. The action writes a sys_<X>Payout record and the payout's progress is then tracked via webhook events that advance through scheduled → in_transit → paid | failed | returned.

__PayoutAction.useCase.description: Use to pay out marketplace earnings to a connected sub-merchant account via a provider that supports marketplace; the payout's progress is then tracked through webhook events.

example.name: payoutSeller
example.description: Transfer the seller's settled earnings to their connected account.

PayoutAction.__providerName.doc: Lookup key into projectSettings.paymentProvidersSettings.paymentProviders[].name. When null/omitted, the framework reads providerName from the parent DataObject's MarketplaceConfig.
PayoutAction.__connectedAccountProperty.doc: Property holding the connected sub-merchant account id. Resolves at runtime against the request context.
PayoutAction.__amountProperty.doc: Property holding the payout amount. Required: the action refuses a payout whose amount does not resolve. On a sourceOrderProperty payout that releases a settlementRelease row, the value is not used and not compared: the payout sends the amount booked for that sale at capture (for a partially refunded sale, the pro-rata remainder the payout scheduler recomputes under its claim). See docs-site/integrations/payment/iyzico-field-notes.md (Refunds and disputes while held).
PayoutAction.__currencyProperty.doc: Property holding the currency. Defaults to the parent MarketplaceConfig's currency when omitted.
PayoutAction.__transferGroupProperty.doc: Optional property holding a transfer group identifier for provider-side reporting (Stripe).
PayoutAction.__metadataProperty.doc: Optional property (or context value) holding an OBJECT passed to the provider as the payout's `metadata`, e.g. iyzico `{ paymentId }` / `{ paymentId, paymentTransactionIds }` (named transaction ids travel with the paymentId of their charge). A value that is not a plain object is ignored. Null/absent: no metadata is sent.
PayoutAction.__scheduledForProperty.doc: Optional property holding the date-time the payout is scheduled for (`scheduledFor`). On a scheduled cadence (or a reserve) the booked row is not sent before it. Null/absent: the cadence decides, as before.
PayoutAction.__sourceOrderProperty.doc: Optional property holding the id of the marketplace SALE row this payout settles, sent as `metadata.orderId`. On a marketplace owner that declares `settlementRelease`, the payout then RELEASES the payout row the framework booked for that sale at capture - with the provider item ids persisted on it (iyzico paymentTransactionIds) - instead of booking a second payout: `manual` releases it, `onDate` / `onStatus` release it only once the condition holds (it stays held otherwise). A sale with no booked row is refused 409 SETTLEMENT_RELEASE_NOT_BOOKED. Null/absent: an ordinary payout, as before.

__CartValidationAction.doc: Validates a shopping cart before checkout. Checks that items exist, stock is available, prices are valid, and minimum order requirements are met. The validation results are written to the context for use in subsequent actions.

__CartValidationAction.useCase.description: Use before checkout to validate a cart — items present, stock available, prices current, minimum order met — writing the results to context. Set failFast=false to collect all failures at once.

example.name: validateCart
example.description: Run pre-checkout cart validations and collect every failure for the client.

CartValidationAction.__validations.doc: Array of validation types to perform. Valid options: 'itemsExist', 'stockAvailable', 'pricesValid', 'minimumOrderMet', 'shippingAddressValid'.
CartValidationAction.__failFast.doc: If true, stop validation on first failure. If false, collect all failures before returning.

__CartValidationType.doc.#: Types of validations that can be performed on a shopping cart before checkout.
__CartValidationType.doc.itemsExist: Verify the cart has at least one item.
__CartValidationType.doc.stockAvailable: Check that all items have sufficient inventory/stock.
__CartValidationType.doc.pricesValid: Verify item prices haven't changed since added to cart.
__CartValidationType.doc.minimumOrderMet: Check that the cart meets the minimum order threshold (params.minimumOrderTotal). In the Node.js runtime the comparison reads the cart's persisted pre-redemption figure (grossTotal), falling back to subtotal - discountTotal + vatTotal for a snapshot written before that field existed, so paying part of the basket with loyalty points never shrinks it below the minimum - points are a payment method, not a discount on the goods; a snapshot that carries none of those figures is answered MINIMUM_ORDER_UNDETERMINABLE rather than measured against a net total. The Java, .NET, PHP and Rust runtimes still compare the post-redemption total. Python accepts this validation name, echoes it back and never evaluates it (its validate implements only itemsExist, unitPrice, quantity and promotionsValid). Go answers valid:true unconditionally and drops the requested validation list at the call site. Aligning them is tracked as a porting task.
__CartValidationType.doc.shippingAddressValid: Validate that a valid shipping address is provided.
__CartValidationType.doc.promotionsValid: Verify that applied promotions are still valid and eligible.

__CartCheckoutAction.doc: Processes shopping cart checkout. Handles inventory reservation, promotion usage recording, order creation, and cart clearing. The checkout result is written to the context.

__CartCheckoutAction.useCase.description: Use to process a cart checkout — reserve inventory, record promotion usage, create the order, and clear the cart — choosing the stage (validate/process/finalize) appropriate to the step.

example.name: processCheckout
example.description: Run full checkout processing and clear the cart afterward.

CartCheckoutAction.__stage.doc: The checkout stage: 'validate' for validation only, 'process' for full checkout processing, 'finalize' for final order creation.
CartCheckoutAction.__clearCartAfterCheckout.doc: If true, clear the cart after successful checkout.
CartCheckoutAction.__recordPromotionUsage.doc: If true, record promotion usage at checkout: inside the checkout claim, the usageCount of each campaign the checkout used is incremented once (guarded by its usageLimit cap when campaignSettings.supportUsageLimits is on; 409 PROMOTION_USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED when the cap is reached). Needs dynamic promotions with the generated campaign store; otherwise nothing is recorded.

__CartCheckoutStage.doc.#: Stages of the shopping cart checkout process.
__CartCheckoutStage.doc.validate: Only validate the cart without processing. Used to check if cart is ready for checkout.
__CartCheckoutStage.doc.process: Full checkout processing including inventory reservation and order creation.
__CartCheckoutStage.doc.finalize: Final order finalization after payment confirmation.

__CouponValidationAction.doc: Validates a coupon code for eligibility against the active cart and optionally calculates the discount amount. The code must name a campaign (requiresCoupon, couponCode) of the campaign store, and every rule of that campaign must pass (date windows, minimums, a usageLimit cap, ...). Results are written to the context as { valid, couponCode, discountAmount?, reason?, rewards? } - an unknown or ineligible code is valid false with a reason, not an error. An EMPTY or missing couponCode is the one error: 400 'couponCode is required', by design (there is nothing to validate).

__CouponValidationAction.useCase.description: Use to validate a coupon code — checking expiration, usage limits, and minimum-order eligibility — and compute the discount amount into context for the checkout total.

example.name: validateCoupon
example.description: Validate the applied coupon and compute its discount before checkout.

CouponValidationAction.__checkUsageLimits.doc: How this validation treats a usageLimit rule of the coupon's campaign: true enforces it against the campaign's usageCount (even when campaignSettings.supportUsageLimits is off), false skips it (the rule passes).
CouponValidationAction.__checkExpiration.doc: Has no effect: the campaign's dateRange rule, which is what expires a coupon, is always evaluated.
CouponValidationAction.__calculateDiscount.doc: If true, calculate and include the discount amount in the result.

__PaymentStage.doc.#: The target stage of the payment lifecycle on which the action's decision for next step to be executed is based. The original five values (simple/start/complete/refresh/callback) are owned by `PaymentAction` and cover the one-time payment lifecycle. The newer values (refund/dispute/subscribe/cancelSubscription/payout) are owned by dedicated Action types (RefundAction, SubscriptionAction, PayoutAction) — they share this enum for consistency but are not invoked through PaymentAction: a PaymentAction that declares one of them is refused at design time (PAYMENT_STAGE_OFF_CONTRACT).
__PaymentStage.doc.simple: The lifecycle is simple it is just one sync call to handle everything, creating the charge immediately.
__PaymentStage.doc.start: The payment operation is wanted to be started, mostly an intent is created on the frontend side, but also it can be started in the server side.
__PaymentStage.doc.complete: The payment operation is wanted to be completed, the intent will be a real charge.
__PaymentStage.doc.refresh: The payment operation data in the gateway server will be fetched and the application payment tickets and order status will be refreshed according to the server. Use this if you dont want to use a webhook.
__PaymentStage.doc.callback: The api is called by the gateway webhook, so the refresh operation will be held asynchronously. Use this option if you provide your api as a webhook to the provider.
__PaymentStage.doc.refund: Issue a refund against a prior captured payment. Owned by RefundAction. Supports full or partial refunds depending on PaymentCapabilities.supportsRefundsPartial.
__PaymentStage.doc.dispute: Fetch or respond to a dispute / chargeback. There is no dispute action type: disputes arrive on the provider webhook and are advanced by the generated dispute machine (checkout dispute lifecycle hooks such as afterDisputeOpened). Not a PaymentAction stage.
__PaymentStage.doc.subscribe: Create a subscription against a SubscriptionPlan. Owned by SubscriptionAction. Requires PaymentCapabilities.supportsSubscriptions.
__PaymentStage.doc.cancelSubscription: Cancel an existing subscription, either immediately or at the end of the current billing period. Owned by SubscriptionAction.
__PaymentStage.doc.payout: Trigger a marketplace payout to a connected sub-merchant account. Owned by PayoutAction. Requires PaymentCapabilities.supportsMarketplace.

__IntegrationAction.doc: Calls a third-party API integration from the platform integration catalog (e.g., AWS S3, Stripe, Google Maps). The provider is identified by its string key matching an integration picked for the project. Each integration exposes a set of predefined actions, and this object triggers one of them with dynamically computed parameters. The result is stored in the context and can be used in follow-up steps.

__IntegrationAction.useCase.description: Use to invoke a catalog integration (e.g. amazonS3, googleMaps) by its provider key and action method, passing dynamically-computed named parameters; the result lands on context.

example.name: uploadReceiptToS3
example.description: Upload the generated receipt PDF to the receipts bucket.

IntegrationAction.__provider.doc: The provider key identifying the integration to call (e.g., `amazonS3`, `Stripe`, `googleMaps`). Must match the providerKey of an integration that has been picked for the current project.
IntegrationAction.__action.doc: The specific action or method to invoke on the integration provider. For example: `uploadFile`, `createRecord`, `deleteObject`, `listItems`. Action names must match the methods exposed by the integration class code.
IntegrationAction.__parameters.doc: An array of parameter objects that define the inputs to pass to the integration action. Each parameter includes a name and a dynamically evaluated value from context.

__IntegrationParameter.doc: Defines a single named input to be passed to a native integration provider action. Parameter values are evaluated using MScript and can be derived from session, context, or external input.

IntegrationParameter.__parameterName.doc: The name of the parameter as expected by the integration action (e.g., `bucketName`, `filePath`, `email`).
IntegrationParameter.__parameterValue.doc: An MScript expression that resolves to the parameter value. This can reference current context, session variables, request parameters, or computed logic.

__BusinessApiParameter.doc: Defines a customizable input parameter for a Business API. Parameters are extracted from the incoming request, transformed and validated, and then written directly to the API context under `this.<name>`. These parameters may originate from any request part (e.g., body, query, session), and can be combined with Redis-based or auto-generated parameters.

BusinessApiParameter.__name.doc: The name of the parameter in the API context. The value will be available at `this.<name>` during Business API execution. This does not need to match the incoming request key. Because the value binds as `this.<name>` on the generated manager, the name must not collide with a member of the manager base class chain (e.g. `request`, `output`, `execute`, `checkRoles`) - such a parameter would overwrite the manager's own member and break the request pipeline, so validation refuses it (BUSINESS_API_PARAM_RESERVED_NAME). Exception: a parameter that writes a same-named data property of the api's object is allowed - that is the normal explicit-mode write path. That exception is not free: the emitted field still overwrites the base member at construction, so validation reports it as a warning (PARAM_SHADOWS_MANAGER_MEMBER) naming what the manager loses - rename the DATA PROPERTY to clear it. Only members the runtime captures privately are silent, and today those are `name` (the api name is read from a private slot, so a `name` parameter no longer disarms idempotent replay or the login gate exemptions), `controllerType` (the transport is read from a private slot, so a `controllerType` parameter cannot make a caller a trusted system job) and `auth` (the caller's session manager is read from a private slot, so an `auth` column is plain data and never stands in for the caller at any gate). The name `session` is refused outright, in every language (ERROR PARAM_NAMED_SESSION): designer MScript reads `this.session` as the caller's session, and a parameter of that name would bind the request's value there. That covers a parameter writing a `session` data property too - rename the data property (e.g. `sessionValue`) and the parameter with it. The ERROR blocks saving the slice and building; it is not in the non-bypassable security list, because the framework's own gates read the caller's session from a private slot.
BusinessApiParameter.__type.doc: The expected data type of the parameter, selected from the standard `DataTypes` enum (e.g., String, Number, Boolean). Used for validation and casting.
BusinessApiParameter.__required.doc: Indicates whether the parameter must be present in the incoming request. If true and the parameter is missing, the API will return a validation error.
BusinessApiParameter.__isArray.doc: Set to `true` when the parameter accepts an array of values (e.g. `String[]`, `ID[]`, `Integer[]`). In nodejs, a present non-array value for a caller-authored array parameter is refused with HTTP 400 `INVALID_PARAMETER_TYPE`, naming the parameter, before vocabulary validation; this also applies on MongoDB and on Kafka, internal-call and streaming paths. Optional null or absent values and array values are unchanged. Query and header scalars retain their one-element-array read lift; session, header, cookie and request locations and geo or row-id parameters are excluded from this shape gate. This flag MUST match the `isArray` setting on the matching data property to avoid a codegen mismatch error. For auto-generated parameters bound to a data property, this is backfilled automatically when omitted.
BusinessApiParameter.__enumOptions.doc: When `type === 'Enum'`, the ordered list of string values the parameter accepts. For auto-generated parameters bound to an Enum data property, this is backfilled from the property automatically when omitted.
BusinessApiParameter.__defaultValue.doc:
Optional fallback used when the request omits this parameter — an MScript expression evaluated at request time and spliced into the generated handler as a PRESENCE test on the read (`(<read>) !== undefined ? (<read>) : <default>`): the default applies only when the key is ABSENT, and a caller that sends an explicit `null` binds `null`. One transport exception: on the gRPC arm a singular parameter whose type maps to a proto3 message (Object / Json / GeoPoint as `google.protobuf.Struct`, Date / DateTime / Time as `google.protobuf.Timestamp`) decodes as `null` when omitted and cannot carry an explicit null at all, so there a `null` read takes the default. Because it is an expression (not a raw literal), it can be a plain literal (`{ "js": "1" }`, `{ "js": "'USD'" }`) OR computed/context code (`{ "js": "this.session.userId" }`, `{ "js": "new Date()" }`, `{ "js": "LIB.common.uuid()" }`). Author literals with the value's own syntax (strings quoted); supply per-language sources when a native form is needed. Leave null for no default.

ENUM MEMBER SHORTHAND. When `type` is `Enum`, a defaultValue whose JS source is a SINGLE BARE IDENTIFIER textually equal to one of the `enumOptions` — `{ "js": "participant_cancel" }`, or the legacy plain-string form `"participant_cancel"` — is accepted as authoring shorthand: the shared pattern parse normalizes it to the quoted string literal (`{ "js": "'participant_cancel'" }`) and validation reports the rewrite through the autoFixes tier, never silently. Precedence when names collide: for an Enum-typed parameter the ENUM-MEMBER reading WINS over a slot binding or JS global of the same name — a bare `LIB` on a parameter whose enumOptions include `"LIB"` normalizes to `"'LIB'"`; anything more than a bare identifier (`LIB.today()`, `this.x ?? 'a'`) keeps its expression meaning and never normalizes. A bare identifier that is NOT an enum member does not normalize — in the `{ "js": … }` form it is a design-time ERROR (`MSCRIPT_UNKNOWN_ROOT_BINDING`: the splice scope is `this`, `LIB` and the JS/Node globals, so any other root identifier is a guaranteed TS2304 in the generated manager).
BusinessApiParameter.__httpLocation.doc: The section of the HTTP request to extract the parameter from (e.g., `body`, `query`, `session`). Chosen from the `RequestLocations` enum. REQUIRED, and there is no schema default: an absent value is reported as REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING, and a cased spelling (`Body`) is auto-corrected to the canonical enum member. Where a value nevertheless has to be resolved for a parameter that never passed validation (a legacy import, a partial subtree write), the fallback is METHOD-AWARE: an api whose effective HTTP method is GET or DELETE binds the parameter from the QUERY STRING, every other method from the BODY. Declaring `body` on a GET or DELETE is refused at design time (BODY_PARAM_ON_BODYLESS_METHOD) because no caller can send a body on those methods, so the parameter would read undefined on every call. One more override applies before any of this: when the parameter NAME matches a `:segment` of the api's effective route, the URL is the source of truth and the built api rebinds the location to `urlpath` (reported as an autoFix, REQUEST_PARAM_REBOUND_TO_URLPATH); give such a parameter no `dataPath`, or a `dataPath` equal to the segment name, or the generated reader looks up a key `req.params` does not carry.
BusinessApiParameter.__hidden.doc: Make a parameter hidden to hide it in Swagger, Mcp or other API automation tools. This is usefull when you want to define a higly technical parameeter which will be used by frontend or other integration developers for specific reasons in rare cases.
BusinessApiParameter.__contractOnly.doc: If `true`, the parameter is a CONTRACT-SURFACE declaration that the API intentionally does not consume: it is validated, typed and documented (REST doc, Swagger, MCP, test tooling) and the value is bound into the request context, but no whereClause, dataClause or action MScript is expected to read it and it is not expected to be stored. Typical uses: carrying a producer envelope key on an event-sourced API to document/enforce the producer's payload contract, reserving a field for a consumer that is wired later, or accepting a correlation token the framework handles elsewhere. Setting it suppresses the PARAM_UNUSED / PARAM_NOT_STORED / REQUIRED_PARAM_NOT_STORED advisories for this parameter and keeps it out of the UPDATE_WRITES_NOTHING dropped-parameter count. It is also THE sanctioned declaration for a parameter that carries the contract of a fully-parametric API whose work is done by an action: for example an M2M update that takes `orderId` / `lines` / `idempotencyKey`, has no dataClause (its columns may be `allowUpdate: false`) and hands the values to a LIB action that reads them as `this.<param>`. The wire contract and the `this.<param>` reads are unchanged; the parameter just stops implying a column write. Do NOT set it on a parameter that is supposed to be written to a column or to select the row: that would silence the exact finding that catches a silently dropped caller value. Defaults to `false`.
BusinessApiParameter.__dataPath.doc: OPTIONAL - when omitted (or null) the parameter's own name is the path, which is what every read site already computes (`dataPath ?? name` in BusinessApiParameter); the field only needs authoring when the source key DIFFERS from the parameter name. It was formerly required, which made every flat parameter repeat its own name and made the framework's own injected builders (and the auth module) nonconforming. A dot-path expression to locate the parameter value in its specified source (e.g., `user.email`, `input.cart.total`). For flat parameters this is simply the parameter's own name (e.g. `phaseId` → dataPath `phaseId`). KAFKA-TRIGGERED APIs — read scope 'record': when the API is invoked through `controllers.kafkaSettings`, the source is the pseudo-request the generated Kafka controller builds as `body: _payload?.data ?? _payload`, i.e. the event record ALREADY UNWRAPPED out of the unified event envelope. Use the BARE key (`contentType`), NEVER a `data.` prefix: the envelope is stripped before `readKafkaParameters` runs, so `data.contentType` reads through a second, non-existent envelope and resolves to undefined at runtime. Note this is the opposite binding from an AIAgent `kafkaControllers[].dataMapping` that declares a mapping — that one is read scope 'envelope' (it is handed the raw wire message) and therefore does read `message.data.<key>`. The wire is enveloped for every topic without exception; what changes is whether your reader unwrapped it for you. ENVELOPE scope on kafka: a parameter whose `httpLocation` is `request` resolves against the RAW envelope instead of the record — the generated controller carries it on `_req.event` — so `old.archived` reads the pre-change row the framework publishes on every `.updated` db-change event, which is the only way to author an act-only-if-it-actually-changed consumer. Dotted paths are TRAVERSED on kafka and on the REST `request` location; every OTHER location on every other protocol brackets the whole string as a single key. Where a path is traversed, every hop is optional-chained, so a missing intermediate object binds undefined instead of throwing out of the parameter read.
BusinessApiParameter.__transform.doc: An optional MScript expression to post-process the raw input before validation. This is useful for trimming, normalizing, or coercing types. THE VALUE IS `this.<parameterName>`, not `this`: the expression is spliced into a method of the generated api manager (`this.<name> = await Promise.resolve(<expr>)`), so `this` is the MANAGER. Write `this.title?.trim()`, never a bare `this` — a bare `this` does not throw, it writes the manager object into the column, and validate refuses it (`MSCRIPT_PARAMETER_BARE_THIS`). Reading another parameter as `this.<otherName>` is fine.
BusinessApiParameter.__description.doc: Human-readable explanation of the parameter’s purpose. For auto-generated parameters, this inherits the description from the linked data object property. For manually defined parameters, the developer should provide one.
BusinessApiParameter.__dataExample.doc: Realistic example value the caller would send for this parameter. Required-by-convention when `type` is `Object` or `Object[]` so downstream consumers (REST API doc, populate worker, test-plan slot filler, frontend forms) know the inner shape — `Object` alone tells the caller it's a JSON blob but not what keys to put in it. For scalars use the example to clarify edge cases the type+description don't cover (e.g. `"YYYY-MM-DD"` for a Date, an enum value the caller should default to). Stored verbatim and rendered into the REST API doc as a fenced-JSON code block. Spec-auditor warns when an Object-typed parameter has no dataExample, errors when the parameter is also `required: true`.
BusinessApiParameter.name: String

__RedisApiParameter.doc: Defines a parameter whose value is fetched from Redis before Business API execution begins. The result is written directly to the context as `this.<name>`, making it accessible like any other parameter. This is useful for injecting server-side or cached state without requiring the client to send it explicitly.

RedisApiParameter.__name.doc: The name under which the Redis value will be stored in the context. For example, setting this to `tenantConfig` makes it accessible as `this.tenantConfig`. Like request parameters, the name binds as `this.<name>` on the generated manager and therefore must not collide with a manager base-chain member (validation refuses it with BUSINESS_API_PARAM_RESERVED_NAME; the name `session` with PARAM_NAMED_SESSION).
RedisApiParameter.__type.doc: The expected data type for the Redis value (e.g., String, Boolean, Object). Used for validation and type enforcement.
RedisApiParameter.__required.doc: If true, the API will throw an error if the Redis key is missing or the value is null. If false, the value is optional and `defaultValue` may apply.
RedisApiParameter.__defaultValue.doc: Optional fallback if the Redis lookup fails — an MScript expression evaluated at request time (not a raw literal). A literal is authored with the value's own syntax (`{ "js": "'default'" }`, `{ "js": "0" }`); computed/context forms (`{ "js": "this.session.userId" }`) are also allowed. Leave null to keep the Redis parameter strictly required-or-null. The expression is spliced into the generated manager's `readRedisParameters()` method, so its scope is `this` (the manager), `LIB` and the JS/Node globals — in the `{ "js": … }` form any other root identifier is a design-time ERROR (`MSCRIPT_UNKNOWN_ROOT_BINDING`), because it would be a guaranteed TS2304 at build.
RedisApiParameter.__redisKey.doc: An MScript expression that evaluates to the Redis key from which to read the value. This can include dynamic tokens like `this.session.userId` or a request parameter such as `this.socialCode` — raw request parameters are already bound when redis parameters are read, and the fetched value is available to `requestParameters` transforms.
RedisApiParameter.name: String

__ApiRestSettings.doc: Defines the REST controller configuration for a Business API. REST is the default HTTP interface in OpenAPPL. These settings allow enabling/disabling REST access and customizing the endpoint path. Fields are flat — set `routePath` and `forcePOSTMethod` directly on this block (the legacy `configuration: { ... }` wrapper is still accepted on input but lifted at validate time).

ApiRestSettings.__hasRestController.doc: Controls whether the Business API is exposed as a REST endpoint. Set to false to disable HTTP access.
ApiRestSettings.__routePath.doc:
Custom REST path override. Leave as `$default` to auto-generate.

## Default-route calculation

Given the API's crudType, name, dataObjectName, and whereClause.selectBy, the calculator produces:

  create / list                   →  /<resourcePath>
  get / update / delete           →  /<resourcePath>/:<param>          (unless the where clause, not the URL, addresses the row - see below)

The `<param>` segment is chosen in this order:
  1. If `whereClause.selectBy` has exactly one entry and that entry is NOT `id`,
     the param uses that field name, even when a `fullWhereClause` is also set. Example: selectBy=['slug'] → /<resource>/:slug.
  2. Otherwise, if `whereClause.fullWhereClause` is set, there is NO param: the route is the bare `/<resourcePath>` (see the next section).
  3. If `whereClause.selectBy` has several entries and none is `id`, there is NO param either.
  4. Otherwise the param is the data-object's natural id, formatted as `<dataObjectName>Id`.
     Example: dataObject=`User` → /<resource>/:userId.

`<resourcePath>` is derived from the API name + dataObjectName, ALWAYS lowercased:
  - Default-shape APIs (e.g. getUser/listUsers/createUser/updateUser/deleteUser on the User
    object) collapse to the plural object name: `/users`.
  - Non-default APIs (custom verbs like `archiveUser`, `closeOrder`) concatenate verb + singular
    object name (no plural): `/archiveuser`, `/closeorder`.

The path parameter follows the standard OpenAPPL naming convention — `dataObject.objectName` is lowercase camelCase (e.g. `user`, `orderItem`), and the param appends `Id`: `:userId`, `:orderItemId`. (The resource segment is additionally lowercased; the param name passes the input case through.)

## fullWhereClause removes the path parameter: author routePath

A get/update/delete API that sets `whereClause.fullWhereClause` (and no single non-`id` selectBy entry, which still names the segment) gets NO path parameter from the default calculator: the where clause, not the URL, addresses the row, so there is no segment to derive, and a `:<dataObjectName>Id` nothing reads would only make every caller send a dummy id. The calculated route is therefore the bare `/<resourcePath>`, which for a `get` is the same `GET /<resource>` the list API mounts. Validation reports that shape once, as the ERROR `SINGLE_ACCESS_ROUTE_MISSING_ID`, whose message names the route to author (the list-endpoint `ROUTE_COLLISION` warning stands down for it). So an API with a fullWhereClause sets `routePath` explicitly: with a `:segment` named after the request value the where clause reads (`/orders/:invoiceNbr`), or as a static path distinct from the collection (`/orders/current`, `/getactivebasket`) when the record is resolved from the session or other context. The same applies to a multi-entry selectBy without `id`.

## Custom routePath rules

  - Always start with `/`.
  - If your custom path includes a parameter (`:something`) AND `selectBy` is unset, the parameter name is inferred as the selectBy field. Example: `routePath: '/orders/:invoiceNbr'` with no selectBy → effective selectBy is `invoiceNbr`.
  - If your custom path's parameter name conflicts with the configured `selectBy`, an ambiguity warning is raised at validation.
  - A custom routePath without any `:`-style parameter IS allowed for single-record get/update/delete APIs — useful for verb-style endpoints (e.g. `/getActiveBasket`, `/closeMyOrder`) where the record is resolved from auth context or `fullWhereClause` rather than the URL. Just be aware the route cannot vary per record, so it must not collide with the list/create path on the same resource.

## Version prefixes

The generated service mounts every Business API route twice: at the bare path and under a fixed `/v1` alias (`/feeds` and `/v1/feeds` are the same route). Because of that alias, a leading `/v1` in a custom routePath is redundant and is STRIPPED at validate time as an auto-fix (`/v1/feeds` becomes `/feeds`, still reachable at both `/feeds` and `/v1/feeds`). Any OTHER version prefix (`/v2`, `/v3`, ...) is part of the route you authored and is kept verbatim: `/v2/me/settings` is mounted exactly as written (and, through the alias, at `/v1/v2/me/settings`). There is no per-API version field; a version is simply a path segment.

## Verifying the calculated route

After writing your business APIs, the apply worker can call `getServiceBusinessApiList(serviceName)` to get the structured list of `{name, crudType, method, routePath, source}` for every API in the service — useful to confirm the auto-calculator produced the route shape you expected before triggering a build. Custom create/list routes also bind an undeclared :<dataObjectName>Id into this.<dataObjectName>Id for actions, even when the API does not address its main row by id.
ApiRestSettings.__forcePOSTMethod.doc: The http method will be set according to the crud type, use this setting if you want to force the HttpMethod to POST. Not recommended if you don't have a specific reason.
ApiRestSettings.__acknowledgedShadowedFilterParams.doc: Per-API acknowledgment for the `FILTER_PARAM_SHADOWED_BY_ROUTE` warning. `isFilterParameter` is a PROPERTY-level flag, so a dual-use property — a route `:param` on one API and a genuine query filter on another (e.g. `creatorProfile.userId`: `:userId` on a nested get API, real filter on `adminListCreatorProfiles`) — would otherwise warn forever on the route-param API: clearing the property flag to silence it would break the filter on the sibling API. List the property name(s) here, on the API whose route deliberately shadows them, to record the dual use as intentional; the warning is silenced for the named segments on THIS API only and stays silenced through re-validation. Names that do not currently match a shadowed filter property on this API raise `FILTER_PARAM_ACK_STALE` so stale acknowledgments cannot rot silently. Leave null/empty when no route segment shadows a filter property. On list APIs the shadow warning is suppressed when queryFiltersActive is false or the route segment is an authored selectBy/custom request parameter.

__ApiCronSettings.doc: Schedules the Business API for periodic execution using a cron expression. Ideal for background jobs or recurring tasks. Fields are flat — set `cronExpression` directly (the legacy `configuration: { ... }` wrapper is still accepted on input but lifted at validate time).

ApiCronSettings.__hasCronController.doc: Enables or disables the cron controller. If true, the API will run at the interval defined by `cronExpression`, on ONE replica per tick (`singleReplica`, default true, nodejs) or on every replica when `singleReplica` is false.
ApiCronSettings.__cronExpression.doc: Cron expression defining the schedule (e.g., '0 * * * *' for hourly execution). NodeJS schedules reject Quartz last-day (L) tokens in day-of-month or day-of-week fields because node-cron cannot register them. Java and dotnet keep their native Quartz support.
ApiCronSettings.__singleReplica.doc: Default true: each scheduled tick runs on ONE replica of the service instead of on every replica. Every replica's scheduler still fires the tick, but before running the API it inserts a claim row into the service's `sys_cronJobRun` table (job name `api:<apiName>`, tick key `tick:<fire time>`: the minute for a 5-field expression, and for a seconds schedule the latest second the expression fires at, the current one or the one before, so a replica whose scheduler read the clock just after the second turned names the same tick); the unique (jobName, tickKey) index lets exactly one insert win, and only that replica runs the API. The row then records the run (status, timings, replica, masked error), and a failed run is recorded as failed. A database that cannot be reached skips the tick on that replica (logged as CronJobStoreUnavailable) instead of running it unclaimed. An out-of-band run (the test transport's run-now) is not claimed. Set it to false only for work that must run on every replica (a per-replica cache refresh): every replica then runs every tick, the behaviour before patterns 1.87.0. NodeJS only; other languages run every tick on every replica whatever the setting, and an explicit `singleReplica: true` there is warned about (API_CRON_SINGLE_REPLICA_NOT_PORTED).

__ApiInternalCallSettings.doc:
Marks the Business API as callable IN-PROCESS from ANY MScript-evaluated designer script of the same service, not only from payment lifecycle hooks. The call reads `await API.<apiName>({ ...params })`, and the same in-process namespace is reachable from action expressions and `query.dataClauseItems`, the api-level WHERE-clause helpers, the list-option filters, `BusinessApiParameter.transform` and `defaultValue`, and the hub, video, event-subscription, bucket-auth and notification script slots: `API` is an AMBIENT GLOBAL of the generated service — `src/index.ts` installs the registry on `globalThis` at boot and the emitted `src/global.d.ts` declares its type — so every slot reaches it with no import machinery at all, exactly the way it reaches `LIB`, and the `library.functions` / `library.edgeFunctions` bodies that are emitted as verbatim CommonJS reach it too. (The post-render import pass, src/codegen/transforms/inject-ts-api-import.ts, still adds the `internalApis` import to generated TypeScript for back-compat; it is no longer the mechanism that makes the name resolve, and it never reached a `js` library body.) Unbound `API.<apiName>` references are statically checked in EVERY designer-code slot listed above, and in library and edge-function module bodies, and a miss is an ERROR (`INTERNAL_API_NOT_FOUND` / `INTERNAL_API_NO_CONTROLLER`). A COMPUTED access (`API[expr]`) cannot be resolved at design time and carries a warning instead — write the member literally, because a name reached that way that is not a registry member still surfaces as a runtime TypeError. (This closes the per-slot check gap: there is no longer a slot where the check does not run.) No transport is involved: the internal call controller invokes the API's manager directly, and the FULL manager pipeline still runs — parameter validation, actions, workflow, events, audit — through a trusted-system controller. Internal calls always execute asSystem with the system authorization posture. By default the session is null, so the API must be FULLY PARAMETRIC — every input it needs must be an explicit request parameter. On nodejs, python, rust, java and dotnet the optional second argument explicitly supplies a session: `await API.<apiName>(params, { session: this.session })`. Native Java callers pass a map context to `InternalApis.call(apiName, params, context)`; native C# callers pass a dictionary context as the optional second argument to `API.<apiName>`. A BusinessApi action (and, on nodejs, a hook) that has a caller session and wants the caller's tenant must pass it; ledger internal APIs on a tenant-scoped owner object need it too. No session is implicitly inherited through AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager. A `session` property inside params is only input data. Language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature. Session-dependent declarations are still flagged by the validator because it judges the sessionless default call; passing a session does not change the internal call's system authorization posture: role and ownership gates remain bypassed.

Name resolution is EXACT and CASE-SENSITIVE. The generated `API` barrel is keyed by the api's declared `name` verbatim, so `API.getOrder` does not resolve an api declared `getorder`, `GetOrder` or `getOrderById` — a case variant is a MISS, never a near-hit. The miss is reported as `INTERNAL_API_NOT_FOUND` — or, when the names differ only in case, as `INTERNAL_API_NAME_CASE_MISMATCH`, whose message names the declared spelling it found — in every designer-code slot and in library / edge-function module bodies alike. The same exactness applies to `targetApi` bindings.

ApiInternalCallSettings.__hasInternalCallController.doc: Enables or disables the internal call controller. If true, the API becomes a member of its service's in-process `API` namespace and can be awaited as `API.<apiName>(params)` from ANY designer script that service emits — payment lifecycle hooks, action expressions, `query.dataClauseItems`, the api-level WHERE-clause helpers, the list-option filters, `BusinessApiParameter.transform` / `defaultValue`, the hub, video, event-subscription, bucket-auth and notification script slots, AND the `library.functions` / `library.edgeFunctions` module bodies — not from lifecycle hooks alone. The registry is an ambient global of the service, so no slot needs an import. The call runs the full manager pipeline asSystem and resolves to the API's response resource. On nodejs, python, rust, java and dotnet, `API.<apiName>(params, { session: this.session })` explicitly carries the caller's session and tenant; this is required for ledger APIs on a tenant-scoped owner object. Omitting the optional second argument leaves the session null, with no inheritance through AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager. The system authorization posture is unchanged: role and ownership gates remain bypassed even with an explicit session. Language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature.

__ApiGrpcSettings.doc: Enables gRPC interface for the Business API. Useful for high-performance service-to-service communication. Response shapes follow Google AIP conventions and are not configurable: single-item methods return the resource message directly, list methods return `<Method>Response { repeated <Model> data = 1; Paging paging = 2; }` (1-based paging), and errors surface as gRPC status codes — never inside the response message.

ApiGrpcSettings.__hasGrpcController.doc: Controls whether this API exposes a gRPC method. The gRPC controller resolves the caller's session from the `authorization` metadata; a `permissionCheck` api answers a call whose credential resolved no session with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, so pair a gRPC-exposed `permissionCheck` api with `loginRequired: true` (validation warns otherwise, PERMISSION_CHECK_ON_CALLERLESS_DOOR).
ApiGrpcSettings.__responseType.doc: Specifies whether the gRPC method returns a single result or a stream of results.

__GrpcApiResponseType.doc.#: Controls whether the gRPC method returns a single message or a stream.
__GrpcApiResponseType.doc.stream: Returns multiple streamed messages (for list-type APIs).

__SseResponseMode.doc.#: Defines how the SSE endpoint delivers data to the client.
__SseResponseMode.doc.stream: Sends data in sequential chunks. Use for large datasets, file exports, or LLM token streaming where each chunk is a piece of the final result.
__SseResponseMode.doc.events: Sends progress events followed by a final result. Use for long-running operations where the client needs status updates during processing.

__StreamSourceType.doc.#: Reserved: the intended kind of custom stream source for SSE streaming. Not read by the code generator yet, so no value changes what a stream sends.
__StreamSourceType.doc.libFunction: Intended: a registered async generator lib function as the stream source (not wired yet).
__StreamSourceType.doc.iteratorAction: Intended: a declared iterator action pattern as the stream source (not wired yet; schedule an IteratorAction in the workflow to stream today).
__StreamSourceType.doc.sseRelay: Intended: relay an external SSE endpoint's events as chunks (not wired yet).
__StreamSourceType.doc.wsRelay: Intended: relay an external WebSocket endpoint's messages as chunks (not wired yet).

__StreamSourceConfig.doc: Reserved: not read by the code generator yet. Describes a custom source of chunked SSE data (lib function, iterator action, SSE or WebSocket relay), but no generated SSE route reads it in any service language, so declaring it has no effect; the schema only validates its shape so stored blueprints stay valid. To stream custom items, schedule an `IteratorAction` in the workflow instead.

StreamSourceConfig.__sourceType.doc: Reserved, not read by the code generator yet. The intended kind of stream source: libFunction (async generator), iteratorAction (declared pattern), sseRelay (external SSE), wsRelay (external WebSocket). Validation only checks the enum value.
StreamSourceConfig.__libFunctionName.doc: Reserved, not read by the code generator yet. Name of the registered async generator lib function intended as the stream source for sourceType 'libFunction'.
StreamSourceConfig.__iteratorAction.doc: Reserved, not read by the code generator yet. Name of the declared iterator action intended as the stream source for sourceType 'iteratorAction'; to stream from an IteratorAction today, schedule it in the workflow instead.
StreamSourceConfig.__relayUrl.doc: Reserved, not read by the code generator yet. MScript expression intended to evaluate to the URL of the external SSE or WebSocket endpoint to relay (sourceType 'sseRelay' or 'wsRelay'); nothing connects to it.
StreamSourceConfig.__relayAuth.doc: Reserved, not read by the code generator yet. MScript expression intended to evaluate to the authorization header value for the relay connection. Optional.

__KafkaProgressListener.doc: Configures a Kafka topic subscription for receiving progress updates from remote processes during an SSE connection. Messages are filtered by a correlation ID and relayed as SSE events to the client.

KafkaProgressListener.__topic.doc: The Kafka topic to subscribe to for receiving progress messages.
KafkaProgressListener.__correlationField.doc: MScript expression evaluated against the pipeline context to extract the correlation ID (e.g., `{ "js": "dbResult.jobId" }`).
KafkaProgressListener.__kafkaFilterField.doc: The field name in the incoming Kafka message payload to match against the correlation ID.
KafkaProgressListener.__eventName.doc: The SSE event name to emit to the client when a matching Kafka message is received.
KafkaProgressListener.__payloadMapping.doc: Optional MScript expression to extract or transform data from the Kafka message payload. If null, the entire message payload is forwarded.
KafkaProgressListener.__completeWhen.doc: Optional MScript expression evaluated against the Kafka message (as msg). When it evaluates to true, the Kafka listener stops and the SSE connection closes.

__ApiKafkaSettings.doc: Configures Kafka as a trigger mechanism for the Business API. This supports both asynchronous processing and integration-based event handling (e.g., storage triggers, audit flows). Fields are flat — set `requestTopicName` and `responseTopicName` directly (the legacy `configuration: { ... }` wrapper is still accepted on input but lifted at validate time).

ApiKafkaSettings.__hasKafkaController.doc:
Enables the Kafka controller for this API. When true, the API can be triggered by Kafka messages. The generated controller unwraps the unified event envelope before the manager reads parameters — `body: _payload?.data ?? _payload` — so this API's `requestParameters[].dataPath` values are read scope 'record' and must be BARE keys, never `data.`-prefixed. The envelope's `actor` becomes the session and its `requestId` the correlation id.

PARAM_UNUSED semantics on kafka-consumer APIs: on an event-sourced API (hasKafkaController true, hasRestController false) a request parameter binds a key of the PRODUCER's payload, not a caller-supplied value. Binding a producer envelope key the manager never reads (e.g. `caseId`, `decidedAt`, `idempotencyKey`) is often DELIBERATE carriage — keeping `required: true` on the binding documents and enforces the producer contract even when the consumer's logic ignores the key. The validator therefore reports such bindings as informational (`PARAM_UNUSED` with `details.severity: 'info'` and consumer-specific text) instead of the REST-tier 'caller value silently dropped' warning; dropping the binding to silence it would silently loosen the contract check.

PERMISSION CHECK ON THIS ENTRY: a consumed message carries no session manager, so an api that declares `authOptions.permissionCheck` answers every message with 403 (logged as KafkaMessageRejected, dead-lettered when enabled) unless the event actor holds one of the api's `absoluteRoles` or the message is a verified machine call the api admits. Validation warns (PERMISSION_CHECK_ON_CALLERLESS_DOOR); gate a Kafka consumer with `checkRoles` / `absoluteRoles` instead.
ApiKafkaSettings.__requestTopicName.doc: Name of the main Kafka topic this API listens to. Can be custom or auto-generated from the API name. It stays required when the Kafka controller is enabled, also when `requestTopicNames` lists further topics: it is the FIRST topic of the api's effective topic list, and the default dead-letter topic (`<wireRequestTopicName>-deadletter`) is derived from it unless deadLetterPerTopic is true.
ApiKafkaSettings.__requestTopicNames.doc: Additional Kafka topics this API listens to, next to `requestTopicName`. The effective topic list is `requestTopicName` (or the generated default request topic when it is unset) followed by these names, exact-match de-duplicated in order, and the generated controller subscribes to EVERY topic of that list while routing all of them into the same handler and the same manager - one BusinessApi, one handling logic, several topics, instead of one near-identical api per topic. Each nodejs subscription gets its own consumer group (`<SERVICE_CODENAME>-<topic>-<apiName>`), where SERVICE_CODENAME is the lowercased `<projectCodename>-<serviceName>-service`. The response topic stays shared by all the topics. By default the dead-letter topic stays shared too: an explicit `deadLetterTopicName` is used for every topic, and the default dead-letter topic stays derived from the main topic. Opt into deadLetterPerTopic to derive the default from each incoming topic instead; an explicit name still wins. In the log lines and the dead-letter record the `topic` field names the topic the message actually came in on. Each entry must be a valid Kafka topic name (`KAFKA_TOPIC_NAME_INVALID` otherwise, a blank entry included) and a non-string entry is refused. Kafka topic names are case-sensitive: Orders and orders remain distinct subscriptions. Only exact duplicates within this list are removed, reported as an autofix. Leave empty (the default) for a single-topic api; an entry equal to `requestTopicName` changes nothing.
ApiKafkaSettings.__responseTopicName.doc: Topic name to which the API response will be published. Optional. Only an APPLIED outcome (manager `httpStatus < 400`) is published here; a message the pipeline REJECTED never rides the response topic, it is logged as `KafkaMessageRejected` and, when `deadLetterEnabled` is true, published to the dead-letter topic instead.
ApiKafkaSettings.__deadLetterEnabled.doc: Opt-in dead-letter publishing for messages the manager pipeline REJECTS. The generated kafka controller treats any consumed message whose pipeline answers `httpStatus >= 400` (parameter vocabulary, required parameter, auth, ownership, a stale-version 409, a 5xx) as a REJECTED outcome: it logs an ERROR-level `KafkaMessageRejected` line (status, errorCode, detail, the api name and the redacted inbound message) instead of the INFO `KafkaMessageResponded` an applied mutation gets, and it commits the offset either way, so the message is not redelivered. With this flag true the controller ALSO publishes the original inbound message plus the problem body to the dead-letter topic (`deadLetterTopicName`, or, when unset, `<wireRequestTopicName>-deadletter` - the request topic AS THE CONSUMER SUBSCRIBES TO IT, which is project-scoped whenever a publishEventAction of this project authors it) through the service publisher, so a rejected message is preserved somewhere replayable. A dead-letter publish failure is logged as `KafkaDeadLetterPublishFailed` and never stalls the partition. Default false: an api that does not opt in emits no dead-letter code at all.
ApiKafkaSettings.__deadLetterPerTopic.doc: Opt-in per-incoming-topic default dead-letter names. Default false preserves the shared main-topic dead-letter stream (K5). With deadLetterEnabled true and no explicit deadLetterTopicName, true derives <scopeEventTopic(incomingTopic)>-deadletter for each effective request topic; the declared-topic census lists each stream for provisioning and ACLs. An explicit deadLetterTopicName always wins and remains shared. A single-topic controller is unchanged. This flag does not enable dead-letter publishing by itself.
ApiKafkaSettings.__deadLetterTopicName.doc: Topic the rejected messages are published to when `deadLetterEnabled` is true. Optional: unset means `<wireRequestTopicName>-deadletter`, derived from the main request topic by default, or from each incoming topic when deadLetterPerTopic is true, as the consumer subscribes to it (project-scoped whenever a publishEventAction of this project authors that topic), so a scoped topic and its dead-letter stream stay in one namespace. Set explicitly, the name is baked exactly as authored - no suffix, no composition, never re-derived - and it still takes the publish door like any other topic: it is scoped to `<projectCodename>-<name>` when it is itself an authored PublishEventAction topic of this project, and stays verbatim otherwise. The census reports the string that reaches the wire in both arms. Must be a valid Kafka topic name. Ignored when `deadLetterEnabled` is false - and setting it without that flag raises the design-time warning `KAFKA_DEAD_LETTER_TOPIC_INERT`, because the generated controller then emits no dead-letter code at all and a rejected message's payload is preserved nowhere: set `deadLetterEnabled: true` to publish to this topic, or remove this field so the blueprint stops promising a dead-letter stream that does not exist.

__ApiSseSettings.doc: Enables Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming for a Business API, allowing the API to stream its response as chunks or emit progress events over an SSE connection. The REST endpoint continues to serve single request-response. The SSE endpoint is a companion for responses that are too large or too slow for a single HTTP response. Fields are flat — set `responseMode`, `timeout`, `chunkSize`, `streamSource`, and `kafkaProgressListeners` directly (the legacy `configuration: { ... }` wrapper is still accepted on input but lifted at validate time).

ApiSseSettings.__hasSseController.doc: Enables the SSE controller for this API. The SSE route is mounted at the API's own route path and HTTP method, on a separate SSE router; no `/stream` suffix is derived. For a distinct streaming path, declare a sibling API with its own `restSettings.routePath`.
ApiSseSettings.__responseMode.doc: Defines how the SSE endpoint delivers data. 'stream' sends data in chunks (for large datasets, file exports, LLM token streaming). 'events' sends progress updates followed by a final result (for long-running operations).
ApiSseSettings.__timeout.doc: Maximum duration in milliseconds for an SSE connection before the server closes it. Defaults to 300000 (5 minutes).
ApiSseSettings.__chunkSize.doc: Number of rows per chunk when streaming list results. Defaults to 100.
ApiSseSettings.__streamSource.doc: Reserved: not read by the code generator yet. No generated SSE route wires this block into execution, so a declared source (lib function, iterator action, SSE or WebSocket relay) changes nothing: in `stream` mode a list API is walked in keyset chunks of `chunkSize` rows and any other API sends its single result as one chunk. To stream items of your own, schedule an `IteratorAction` in the workflow; each item it yields is written as a `chunk` frame. Leave this null.
ApiSseSettings.__kafkaProgressListeners.doc: Optional array of Kafka topic listeners for receiving progress updates from remote processes. After the pipeline completes, the SSE connection stays open and listens to configured Kafka topics, relaying filtered messages as SSE events. Works with both 'stream' and 'events' response modes.

__SelectClauseSettings.doc: Defines which fields are included in the response of a Business API. Use this to limit returned properties for performance or visibility. On `get` and `list` APIs it shapes the read and its output; on `create`, `update` and `delete` APIs only `selectProperties` is read, as the boundary of the answer (the written row narrowed to the declared properties + `id`, the write itself never projected). The system `id` column is always kept: an explicit selection that omits `id` still returns it, so rows remain addressable. A declared select list is always the response boundary; the runtime may read more columns but never returns them.

SelectClauseSettings.__selectProperties.doc: An array of property names to return in the response. Leave empty to return all fields. The system `id` column is always included in the response even when the list omits it — a projected row stays addressable on every language lane. The projection is applied AT THE QUERY (`attributes` on sequelize, `projection` on mongo), so a property left out of this list is not merely hidden downstream: the fetched row never carried it, and the row is bound under `this.<objectName>` for every workflow action on the api. An MScript slot that dereferences an omitted property therefore reads `undefined` — reported as `SELECT_PROJECTION_HIDES_MSCRIPT_READ`. When that slot is a VALIDATION GUARD, the consequence is not a wrong value but a closed door: a must-be-true guard throws on `undefined` for every request, so the api refuses its entire audience while a sibling api with a wider projection answers 200 (MasaV6 `GET /events/:id`). That case is the ERROR-tier `GATE_READS_REDACTED_FIELD`; fix it by gating on a criterion this list carries, or by adding the property to this list for that audience. A declared select list is always the response boundary; the runtime may read more columns but never returns them: where framework code must read a column the list omits - the owner column an instance `ownershipCheck` on a `get` compares, the foreign key a selectJoin reads, or (full row) the attributes a `permissionCheck` ABAC condition names on an ownership-gated get or a permission-filtered list - and, on those same shapes, every column the api's own actions read off the row (the full row when such a read is dynamic) - the READ is widened by exactly that, the gate, the join and every workflow action see the widened row, and the RESPONSE is narrowed back to this list + `id` + the selectJoin payload keys. On a get/list api bound to a DataView (apiOptions.dataViewName) this list is INERT: the read returns the view document, whose columns are decided by the view's viewBasics.properties alone (DATAVIEW_SELECT_PROPERTIES_INERT); on an unauthenticated api, a view that projects a column this list withholds is the ERROR DATAVIEW_PUBLIC_PROJECTION_LEAK, so narrow the view, not this list. On a `create` / `update` / `delete` api this list bounds the ANSWER only: the write, the instance fetch, the ownership check and every action see the full row, and the response record carries this list + `id` (the api's route event keeps the full row). Declare it on a buyer-facing write behind an ownership check so the caller does not receive internal columns; without it the write answers the full row.
SelectClauseSettings.__selectJoins.doc: An array of join definition to a related object with the properties to be selected from the join. The result is encapsulated in the result with the `joinName` of the SelectJoin.

__SelectJoin.doc: Select join is a definition object for a join from the main object to another related data object to select additional properties from it.

__SelectJoin.useCase.description: Use a SelectJoin in a get/list API's selectClause to pull selected fields from a related object into the response under joinName — using the mainKey->joinedKey selector to disambiguate the relation. This example joins each order's customer fields onto the order.

SelectJoin.__joinName.doc: A human readable single code safe word to name the SelectJoin definition. This name is also used as the property name of the joined object or object list in the main data object.
SelectJoin.__joinedDataObject.doc: The name of the data object to be joined. Note that this object should be defined as a related object in the relation settings of one of the main object properties. Or the joined object should have got a relation defined in one of its properties. If the relation is to the main object form another object, the join result will be an array for an object list. The relation may be either in the same service or in a remote service. The compiler will arrange the code to make the join either through db or the elastic search index.
SelectJoin.__selector.doc: The selector defines how the main (operating) object is related to the joined object when more than one relation exists. It uses the syntax mainObjectKey-\>joinedObjectKey. The left side (mainObjectKey) MUST be a property of the main object being operated on. The right side (joinedObjectKey) MUST be a property of the joined (target) object. Example: main object = user, joined object = project → id-\>ownerId (user projects). Example: main object = project, joined object = user → ownerId-\>id (project owner). If selector is null or empty, the first detected relation is used. Optional shorthand forms are supported: '-\>' or empty selects the first relation, '-\>someKey' selects the first relation matching the joined object's property, 'someKey-\>' selects the first relation originating from the given main object property. For clarity and to avoid ambiguity, the full mainObjectKey-\>joinedObjectKey syntax is strongly recommended.
SelectJoin.__condition.doc: An MScript expression evaluates to Boolean and specifies whether this join should be made or not in code level, e.g (this.includeProductData). Note that this condition can not reference to the main object or main object list, for complex joins use a BFF View.
SelectJoin.__properties.doc: An array of property names to return in the join response. Leave empty to return all fields.
SelectJoin.__sortBy.doc: A sort definition to sort if result fetched by join is an array in case the tarrget has a parental relation with the main object. Leave it null for one to one joins where only one or no object will be fetched.
SelectJoin.__topPick.doc: A number to limit the number of objects in array result fecthed in case the tarrget has a parental relation with the main object. Leave it null for one to one joins where only one or no object will be fetched. If top pick is 1, the result will be a single object even though teh fetch is an array. Example usage, to get the older member of a club in a getClub api, the member join will be sorted by -age desc- and topPick will be 1.

__WhereClauseSettings.doc: Defines how records are filtered in a Business API. This includes:- `selectBy`: strict selection logic based on required field equality. It also drives the default route path and parameter creation for single-record APIs (`get`, `update`, `delete`). When a non-ID field is set as `selectBy`, the route uses that field instead of the object ID, and the ID parameter is suppressed. - `fullWhereClause`: an optional override for complex, flexible query logic. When set, no ID parameter is auto-created and the route path defaults to the resource base path. - `additionalClauses`: optional conditional query fragments that are always appended to the WHERE clause, whether it is derived from `selectBy` or `fullWhereClause`. Use `selectBy` when your selection logic is static and business-critical (e.g., `['slug']`). Use `fullWhereClause` when the WHERE clause needs to be built dynamically using MScript. `additionalClauses` allow context-aware filtering such as role-based visibility or soft-delete exclusion. For `update` and `delete` operations, the actual database mutation always targets the single record fetched by `fetchInstance`, regardless of the WHERE clause breadth. Selector resolution order for `get`/`update`/`delete`: (1) explicit `fullWhereClause`; (2) explicit `selectBy`; (3) inferred `selectBy` from non-id `:` segments in the route path; (4) the standard `:{objectName}Id` (or `:id`) URL parameter; (5) latest-record fallback — when none of the above apply the pipeline sets `fullWhereClause = "{}"` and dbLayer's single-record fetcher returns the most recent record (ordered by `createdAt` DESC). The fallback is intentional support for current-context endpoints (`GET /snapshots/latest`, `DELETE /drafts/current`); when it triggers automatically, validate emits a `LATEST_RECORD_FALLBACK` warning so the designer can confirm intent. Suppress the warning by setting `fullWhereClause: { "js": "{}" }` explicitly when latest-record semantics is desired.

__WhereClauseSettings.useCase.description: Use WhereClauseSettings to locate the target record(s) of a get/list/update/delete API — selectBy for a static unique selector (which also shapes the route path), fullWhereClause for dynamic MScript queries, and additionalClauses for always-appended conditional fragments such as soft-delete exclusion or role-based visibility. This example selects a project by slug and hides archived projects from non-admins.

WhereClauseSettings.__selectBy.doc: A list of fields that must be matched exactly as part of the WHERE clause. This is not a filter — it is a required selection rule. In single-record APIs (`get`, `update`, `delete`), it defines how a unique record is located. In `list` APIs, it scopes the results to only entries matching the given values. When a single non-ID field is specified (e.g., `['slug']`), the default route path is built as `/:slug` instead of `/:objectId`, and the ID parameter is not auto-created. If a custom route path contains non-ID parameters and no `selectBy` is configured, the route parameters are automatically inferred as `selectBy`. For the `id` field, both `/:objectId` and `/:id` are accepted as valid parameter sources.
WhereClauseSettings.__fullWhereClause.doc: An MScript query expression that overrides all default WHERE clause logic. Use this for fully customized queries.
WhereClauseSettings.__additionalClauses.doc: A list of conditionally applied MScript query fragments. These clauses are appended only if their conditions evaluate to true.
WhereClauseSettings.__fuzzyDomainFilters.doc: Query-time fuzzy filters (FuzzyDomainFilter): each one classifies the distinct values of one property of the API's data object against a criterion with a decision provider, caches every decision, and ANDs `property IN (<qualifying values>)` onto the where clause. List APIs only. A provider outage fails the request (or answers empty), never the unfiltered list.

__ExtendedClause.doc: Defines an optional filtering clause that is dynamically included in the query when a single MScript condition is met. Enables route-level filtering to adapt to session, context, or other logic at runtime.

ExtendedClause.__name.doc: A descriptive label used for internal documentation or UI purposes. Does not impact runtime behavior.
ExtendedClause.__condition.doc: An MScript expression that gates whether `whereClause` is merged into the query at runtime. The clause applies when the expression evaluates truthy. Leave null to apply the clause unconditionally. To express an exclusion (apply when X is NOT true), negate the expression yourself, e.g. `{ "js": "!this.session?.isAdmin" }`.
ExtendedClause.__whereClause.doc: The conditional query fragment to include, written as an MScript Query. The clause is merged into the final query when `condition` is truthy (or when `condition` is null, in which case the clause always applies).
ExtendedClause.name: String

__DataClauseSettings.doc: Defines additional data values to be used in create or update operations. This clause augments the auto-generated data object by injecting or overriding values from context.
__DeleteOptions.doc: Options block of a `delete`-type Business API. NOTE: it does NOT decide soft-vs-hard delete — that choice belongs to the data object (see `useSoftDelete` below).

DeleteOptions.__useSoftDelete.doc: OPTIONAL and INERT — no code generator reads this flag, and it is no longer a REQUIRED field. It was required-but-inert: every delete api had to carry a value whose only observable behaviour was raising DELETE_OPTIONS_SOFTDELETE_IGNORED when it disagreed with the data object, and a designer who trusted it hit the unique index at runtime. Whether a delete archives the row (sets `isActive: false`) or physically removes it is decided ONLY by the target data object's `objectSettings.basicSettings.useSoftDelete`, which defaults to true; there is no per-API override. Writing `useSoftDelete: false` here does NOT turn one delete API into a hard delete — the row is still archived — so validation reports it (DELETE_OPTIONS_SOFTDELETE_IGNORED, warning) when it contradicts the object flag. To hard-delete, set `useSoftDelete: false` on the data object itself, which applies to every API that deletes it. Omit this field unless you are deliberately restating the object's flag.

__GetOptions.doc: Options specific to `get`-type Business APIs for customizing how a single record is fetched.

GetOptions.__setAsRead.doc: RETIRED — leave this empty. The post-read write it describes was never emitted by any lane; the declaration validated and did nothing. A NON-EMPTY value is now refused at design time (RETIRED_LIST_SETTING) rather than silently ignored; an empty array stays legal because it asks for nothing. Declare an `update` BusinessApi and call it after the read, so the mutation carries its own auth, its own contract and its own errors.

__ListOptions.doc: Behavioral options for Business APIs of type `list`. These control sorting, grouping, filtering, and caching logic.

__ListOptions.useCase.description: Use ListOptions to control sorting, capping, caching, and runtime filter/search behavior of a list API. This example sorts orders by newest first, enables auto query filtering, and opts the API into runtime filters, search, and sort.

ListOptions.__totalCount.doc: Optional MScript for list APIs only, evaluated after afterMainListOperation. Returns a finite non-negative integer, including 0, preferred over the database count. The row producer owns requested-page selection; this does not slice rows or change ListMapAction.replacesResult (a 1:1 map). topPick caps the declared total; paginationOptions.unpaged:true retains returned-row accounting. Cursor mode is incompatible. Query cache stores the main result; this expression runs again after post-main actions on hits and misses.
ListOptions.__listSortBy.doc: Sort order definitions for the result set. Multiple fields can be provided with direction (asc/desc). This is the static default order; to let a declared request parameter pick one of several named orders per request, declare `listOrderSets` + `listOrderSelector`.
ListOptions.__listOrderSets.doc: Named alternative orders for this list, each `{ key, sortBy: SortByItem[] }`. At request time the value of the declared request parameter named by `listOrderSelector` is matched against the keys and the matching set's `sortBy` becomes the row order; a value that matches no key (or an absent value) falls back to `listSortBy`. Every property named in a set must exist on the api's data object. A unique `id ASC` tie-break is appended to whichever order is chosen so equal keys page stably. Honoured on the sequelize and mongo list paths, on a DataView (Elasticsearch) list, and in the query-cache identity (a different selected order is a different cache entry). Precedence when `runtimeFilters.sortEnabled` is also on: a selector value that matches a key wins; otherwise a runtime `?sortBy=` naming an allowed field applies; otherwise `listSortBy`. Requires `listOrderSelector`. Honoured by the nodejs lane; the other language lanes are tracked by port records.
ListOptions.__listOrderSelector.doc: The name of one of this api's declared `requestParameters` whose request value selects an entry of `listOrderSets` by `key`. Typically an Enum parameter whose `enumOptions` are product vocabulary such as `newest` / `popular`: at design time every enum option must map to a key (LIST_ORDER_SET_ENUM_VALUE_UNMAPPED) and a key no option can reach is warned about (LIST_ORDER_SET_KEY_UNREACHABLE); a parameter that is not declared on the api is an error (LIST_ORDER_SELECTOR_UNKNOWN). Requires `listOrderSets`. Naming it `sortBy` while `runtimeFilters.sortEnabled` is on makes the runtime property sort unreachable behind the enum vocabulary check (LIST_ORDER_SELECTOR_SHADOWS_RUNTIME_SORT).
ListOptions.__listGroupBy.doc: RETIRED — leave this empty. Grouping was declared and shape-validated here, and no emitter and no runtime library, in any lane, ever compiled it into a query: a GROUP BY on a list api that returns whole rows is not expressible without aggregates this pattern cannot declare, and visual grouping is a client concern the list envelope does not carry. The only consumer it ever had was a property-existence cross-check that validated the entries and threw them away. A NON-EMPTY value is now refused at design time (RETIRED_LIST_SETTING) rather than silently ignored; an empty array stays legal because it asks for nothing. For report-shaped grouping use a DataView (BFF), or group the rows in the client.
ListOptions.__topPick.doc: Optional maximum number of sorted records to consider for this list API. If null or 0, no cap is applied. Works with pagination by limiting the full ranked set first, then paging within that capped set: the page LIMIT never reaches past the cap, a page that starts beyond the cap is empty, and the reported total (and therefore totalPages) never exceeds the cap. Honoured by the nodejs api-layer; the other language lanes still ignore it.
ListOptions.__queryCache.doc:
Author `queryCache` as the boolean `true`. This list api then caches its ANSWER in Redis and serves a repeat of the identical query from the cache until the entry expires or an entity write invalidates it. Supported in nodejs and dotnet. This declaration guard still warns with QUERY_CACHE_LANE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for java, golang, python and rust. The shared getQueryCacheEnabled accessor enables only a list whose RESOLVED queryCache value is boolean true. Existing ListOptions hydration also converts the authored string "true" to boolean true before emission; this support declaration does not change that raw-input policy. Direct unresolved strings and numbers do not enable the accessor.

This is a DIFFERENT cache from `objectSettings.redisEntityCacheSettings.useEntityCaching`: that one keys ONE ROW by its id and backs `get<Object>ById`; this one keys ONE ANSWER TO ONE QUERY. Both may be on at once.
