Cache identity is the RESOLVED query — the where clause (which is where a list's session-derived narrowing lands: the tenant filter, the ownership filter, the compiled permission/membership filters), the page window, the sort order, the runtime filter/search terms and the declared request parameters. Two callers entitled to different rows therefore never share an entry.

Invalidation is driven by writes to the api's DataObject: every create/update/delete on it drops the cached answers the written row could appear in. Flag the column the list is normally filtered by (a tenant, owner or parent id) with `indexSettings.clusterInRedis` to make that SLICED — otherwise a single write flushes every cached answer for the object, and the design-time warning QUERY_CACHE_UNSLICED points it out.

Entries expire after 60 seconds by default (`QUERY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` overrides it per deployment), which is also the backstop for the one thing invalidation cannot see: a list whose rows are enriched from OTHER objects, or a DataView-backed list, only refreshes those parts on expiry. Do not enable it on a list that must be read-your-writes consistent with a different object's writes.
ListOptions.__setAsRead.doc: RETIRED — leave this empty. A write side-effect fired from a read api, with no declared transaction, ordering, failure or idempotency semantics, and no emitter or runtime library in any lane ever emitted it. A NON-EMPTY value is now refused at design time (RETIRED_LIST_SETTING) rather than silently ignored; an empty array stays legal because it asks for nothing. Declare an `update` BusinessApi and call it after the read, so the mutation carries its own auth, its own contract and its own errors.
ListOptions.__permissionFilters.doc: Optional filter array that applies permission constraints to the query dynamically based on session or object roles. If given more than one permission filter, all will be applied with @and operator.
ListOptions.__membershipFilters.doc: An array for membership settings to filter to the WHERE clause of the list. If given more than one membership, one of all will be enough to select the object.
ListOptions.__searchFilter.doc: A ListSearchFilter object that collects an id list from ElasticSearch main object index search and appends to the where clause so that db select is done according to the search results of ElasticSearch
ListOptions.__jointFilters.doc: A setting for one or more ListJointFilter to filter the list result with a criteria in a joined data object, more than one filters will be combined by (AND) or (OR) according to the operator parameter
ListOptions.__queryFiltersActive.doc: When set to true, the compiler automatically add filter parameters (the properties that have filter settings enabled) to the request query, and add whereClause items if any query filter is given. If any property is set as selectBy or in custom parameters, it will be omitted in filter parameetrs. Leave this value as true unless you have reason to deactivate query filtering in the list api. Honoured now: an explicit false now suppresses the auto-added filter parameters and their where-clause terms for every lane, because the gate lives on the pattern (BusinessApi.getFilterProperties) rather than in one template. Before that it was declared and validated but read by nothing, so false was silently ignored.
ListOptions.__runtimeFilters.doc: Runtime filter / sort / search / saved-filter behavior for this list API. Operates uniformly on DataObject-sourced and DataView-sourced APIs — codegen compiles to SQL where-clauses or ES queries depending on the API's data source (see porting-docs/closed/PROPOSAL-list-api-runtime-filters.md). Four opt-in flags: filtersEnabled (accept operator-based POST body filters), searchEnabled (accept `?q=` runtime search), sortEnabled (accept runtime `?sortBy=&sortOrder=`), savedFiltersEnabled (auto-generate /filters aux endpoints + a per-service listSavedFilter table).

__ListRuntimeFilterSettings.doc: Per-list-API runtime filter behavior. Four independent opt-in flags. The same block applies to DataObject-sourced and DataView-sourced lists (codegen compiles to SQL/ES per source).

ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__filtersEnabled.doc: When true, the API accepts a structured `filters` POST body with operator-based per-field criteria. Operator vocabulary is shared across DataObject and DataView sources (see RuntimeFilterOperator).
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__searchEnabled.doc: When true, the API accepts a runtime `?q=` query parameter for full-text search across fields configured in `searchedFields`. For DataObject sources the framework routes the search through the existing ListSearchFilter ES bridge; for DataView sources native ES multi_match is used.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__sortEnabled.doc: When true, the API accepts runtime `?sortBy=&sortOrder=` query parameters. The static `listSortBy` becomes the default; runtime sort overrides it. `sortBy` must name a column of `allowedSortFields` (or its computed default); any other value is refused with 400 `INVALID_SORT_FIELD`.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__savedFiltersEnabled.doc: When true, the api-layer auto-generates three auxiliary endpoints next to this API at <routePath>/filters (GET, POST) and <routePath>/filters/:filterId (DELETE), plus a per-service `listSavedFilter` DataObject. Saved-filter rows are scoped to the calling user, and the aux endpoints are never more permissive than this API: they inherit its checkRoles, absoluteRoles and permissionCheck without scopeFields (checkRoles is not copied beside permissionCheck). Where the parent API has a tenant filter in force, only superAdmin and saasAdmin remain in the auxiliary absoluteRoles because the preset table is not tenant-scoped; other inherited absolute roles join a non-empty checkRoles only when no permissionCheck is inherited, retaining ownership checks. Other parents keep the existing inheritance. The auxiliary endpoints always require a login, and never inherit M2MAllowed, apiInSaasLevel or requiredCallerKind.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__allowedFields.doc: Optional explicit allow-list of fields the runtime filter body may target; a declared list is used verbatim (the validator warns, RUNTIME_FILTER_SECRET_FIELD, when it names a `hashed` / `isSecret` column). If null or empty on a `filtersEnabled` api, codegen computes the default from the data source: for DataObject, every property with isFilterParameter=true; for DataView, every projected mainObject property plus every aggregate name plus every stat name; never a `hashed` / `isSecret` or storage-internal column. A body naming a field outside the effective list is refused with 400 `INVALID_FILTER_FIELD`; a default that comes out empty refuses every field.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__allowedSortFields.doc: Optional explicit allow-list for runtime sort; a declared list is used verbatim. If null or empty on a `sortEnabled` api, codegen computes the default: `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` plus every non-array property of a sortable type (ID, String, Integer, Short, Float, Double, Decimal, Boolean, Date, Enum; on a stored DataView, every ES-sortable field of the view index), restricted to `allowedFields` only when `allowedFields` is declared, and never a `hashed` / `isSecret` or storage-internal column. A `?sortBy=` outside the effective list is refused with 400 `INVALID_SORT_FIELD`.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__searchedFields.doc: Fields searched by the runtime `?q=` parameter. If null, defaults to fields whose property type is text-like.
ListRuntimeFilterSettings.__allowedOperators.doc: Optional explicit subset of the operator vocabulary this API supports. If null, the full set is allowed EXCEPT regexp, which is default-deny and must be named here to be reachable (on nodejs, a caller-supplied regular expression runs on a backtracking engine on the SQL and MongoDB read paths; on java and python the DataObject path does not reach a regex engine at all and lowers regexp to a literal $like substring test instead; on go, rust and php the runtime-filter feature has no codegen call site at all, so regexp is unreachable there, not merely degraded).

__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.#: Per-field runtime filter operator vocabulary shared by DataObject-sourced and DataView-sourced list APIs. Matches FILTER_OPERATORS in _common/nodejs/src/common/dynamic-filter.ts (slice 6.2 — single source of truth for codegen + runtime).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.noteq: Field does not equal value (must_not term / SQL <>).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.in: Field matches any of values[] (terms / SQL IN).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.notin: Field matches none of values[] (must_not terms / SQL NOT IN).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.range: values[] = [low, high]; matches gte low AND lte high.
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.match: Full-text match (ES match / SQL ILIKE pattern).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.matchPhrasePrefix: Phrase prefix match (ES match_phrase_prefix / SQL starts).
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.contains: With a SCALAR value, wildcard *value* (case-insensitive substring). With a LIST value, array superset containment on both legs; an EMPTY list is the explicit match-nothing filter and a null element is NULL_IN_VALUES.
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.notContains: Negation of contains. With a LIST value the negation is around the WHOLE conjunction (at least one is missing), not per element; a null element is NULL_IN_VALUES.
__RuntimeFilterOperator.doc.regexp: Caller-supplied regular expression. DEFAULT-DENY: unreachable unless the API lists it in allowedOperators, and even then the pattern is refused with UNSAFE_REGEX_PATTERN if it is over 256 characters or its quantifiers can trade characters with each other more than one pair's worth. See docs-site/business-apis/list-api.md.

__ListPermissionFilter.doc: Permission-based filter that operate on list queries before execution. This is used for object based permissions assigned to a specific role or user

ListPermissionFilter.__name.doc: A human readable and source-code safe to define the permission filter.
ListPermissionFilter.__condition.doc: An optional MScript expression that skips the permission check entirely if it evaluates to false. Useful for exempting trusted users such as object owners or platform admins.
ListPermissionFilter.__permission.doc: The name of the permission that the filter wil be built for
ListPermissionFilter.__on.doc: An optional request-field name carrying the parent/scope object id passed to the native resolver's `compileListFilter(permission, on, …)` for membership-role checks against a parent (ADR-native-permission-system §7.2). Null = a flat type-level check.
ListPermissionFilter.__ownershipCheck.doc: When true, the L5 ownership fallback applies to the compiled list filter — a row the subject owns is included even when no override/role/membership grants it (ADR-native-permission-system §5 layer 5). Mirrors `ApiAuthOptions.ownershipCheck`.
ListPermissionFilter.name: String

__ListOrderSet.doc: One named row order a list api can switch to per request: the `key` a `listOrderSelector` request value is matched against, and the `sortBy` items that become the order when it matches. Declared under `ListOptions.listOrderSets`.

ListOrderSet.__key.doc: The value of the `listOrderSelector` request parameter that selects this order (for an Enum selector, one of its `enumOptions`). Code-safe and unique within the list.
ListOrderSet.__sortBy.doc: The row order applied when this set is selected: one or more SortByItem entries over the api's main data object, in priority order. Must not be empty. A unique `id ASC` tie-break is appended at runtime.

__SortByItem.doc: Sort clause configuration for list operations. Used by `ListOptions.listSortBy` (the static default order), `ListOptions.listOrderSets[].sortBy` (a selectable named order) and `SelectJoin.sortBy` (order over a joined object).

SortByItem.__property.doc: A property reference to define the field that the sort will be done by. On a stored-DataView-bound list, use a projected field, aggregate column path, or declared stat/aggregate name from the view; the underlying data object is not the sort namespace.
SortByItem.__order.doc: The sort order, it should be either asc or desc
SortByItem.__name.doc: A human readable code safe name to define the sort item
SortByItem.name: String

__SortOrder.doc.#: Defines sorting direction — ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

__ListMembershipFilter.doc: A settings object to add a membership filter to the WHERE clause of the list. If given more than any one membership of all will be enough to select the object.

ListMembershipFilter.__name.doc: A human readable and source-code safe to define the membership filter.
ListMembershipFilter.__dataObjectName.doc: The name of the data object whose membership configuration should be used to validate access. If omitted, the Business API’s main data object is assumed. Use this field when you need to check access against a related or parent object (e.g., checking `Organization` membership when updating a `Project`).
ListMembershipFilter.__objectKeyIdField.doc: An property reference that returns the ID of the object from the expected list item whose membership should be checked. Typically it will the id of the list item, but you may want to apply filter through another field of the list item like projectId of a task.
ListMembershipFilter.__userKey.doc: An MScript expression that returns the user ID to check against the target object’s membership configuration. Typically `this.session.userId`, but may also reference delegated users or owners.
ListMembershipFilter.__checkFor.doc: An optional MScript expression to validate specific aspects of the membership (such as role or permissions). If omitted, any valid membership grants access.
ListMembershipFilter.__condition.doc: An optional MScript expression that skips the membership check entirely if it evaluates to false. Useful for exempting trusted users such as object owners or platform admins.
ListMembershipFilter.name: String

__ListSearchFilter.doc: Searches one or more records from the main data object and uses the id array in the where clause of the list. The search is made in elastic search index and the result id array is appended to the where clause of the main query.

ListSearchFilter.__hasSearchFilter.doc: A Boolean value to define if a search filter definition is active in the api or not
ListSearchFilter.__condition.doc: An optional MScript which evaluates to a boolean that defines id the search filter will be used or not
ListSearchFilter.__keyword.doc: An MScript expression whose result will be used as the key to match against the target object's searched properties. For example, `{ "js": "this.keyword" }`.
ListSearchFilter.__searchProperties.doc: The properties of the target object used for matching.

__ListJointFilterSettings.doc: The settings definition for a list api to define any joint filter and combine them with an AND or OR operator

ListJointFilterSettings.__operator.doc: The combination operator of multi joint filters, will be used if there are more than one joint filter, default value is `AND`
ListJointFilterSettings.__filters.doc: The ListJointFilter array to define one or more joint filter to a related object

__FilterOperator.doc.#: Filter combination is used to define how any multiple id arrayy based list filters will be combined
__FilterOperator.doc.AND: Combine the multiple filters by AND operator
__FilterOperator.doc.OR: Combine the multiple filters by OR operator

__ListJointFilter.doc: ListJointFilter definition object for a joint filter from the main object to another related data object to filter the main list result. This is like lefy join in the where clause. If you want to filter your list result with a criteria which is evaluated in a related object other than main object, you can use joint filter.

ListJointFilter.__name.doc: A human readble single code safe word to name the JointFilter deifnition.
ListJointFilter.__joinedDataObject.doc: The name of the data object to be joined. Note that this object should be defined a s a related object in the relation settings of one of the main object properties. Or the joined object should have got a relation defined in one of its properties. The relation may be either in the same service or in a remote service. The compiler will arrange the code to make the join either through db or the elastic search index.
ListJointFilter.__condition.doc: An MScript expression evaluates to Boolean and specifies wheather this filtering should be made or not in code level. Note that this condition can not reference to the main object list, for complex joint filters use a BFF View.
ListJointFilter.__whereClause.doc: An Mscript query to select the object id array from th target object. Note that the result object id list will be used in the main where clause.
ListJointFilter.__selector.doc: The selector defines how the main (operating) object is related to the joined object when more than one relation exists. It uses the syntax mainObjectKey-\>joinedObjectKey. The left side (mainObjectKey) MUST be a property of the main object being operated on. The right side (joinedObjectKey) MUST be a property of the joined (target) object. Example: main object = user, joined object = project → id-\>ownerId (user projects). Example: main object = project, joined object = user → ownerId-\>id (project owner). If selector is null or empty, the first detected relation is used. Optional shorthand forms are supported: '-\>' or empty selects the first relation, '-\>someKey' selects the first relation matching the joined object's property, 'someKey-\>' selects the first relation originating from the given main object property. For clarity and to avoid ambiguity, the full mainObjectKey-\>joinedObjectKey syntax is strongly recommended.
ListJointFilter.name: String
ListJointFilter.__fuzzyDomainFilters.doc: Fuzzy filters on the JOINED object (FuzzyDomainFilter): each narrows the joined rows this joint filter selects by `property IN (<qualifying values>)` before their keys are collected, with `targetProperty` naming a property of `joinedDataObject`. Optional.

__PaginationOptions.doc: Defines how pagination is handled in list-type Business APIs. Paginated lists take 1-based `page` and `pageSize` request parameters (legacy `pageNumber`/`pageRowCount` spellings are accepted as aliases) and respond with the list envelope `{ data: [...], paging: { page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages } }`.

PaginationOptions.__paginationEnabled.doc: RETIRED and IGNORED. No code generator reads this flag: a list api is always paginated unless it declares `unpaged: true`. The UI scaffolder writes `paginationEnabled: false` on every api, so a stored `false` cannot be told apart from the scaffold default, and reading it as "return the full set" would unpage every existing list. Leave the stored value as it is; to answer a list's whole result set, set `unpaged: true`.
PaginationOptions.__unpaged.doc: Opt this list api OUT of pagination. This is the ONLY switch that does; the retired `paginationEnabled` is ignored. An unpaged list answers its WHOLE filtered result set in one response, `{ data: [...], paging: { page: 1, pageSize: N, totalCount: N, totalPages: 1 } }` (an empty set reports `totalPages: 0`), and ignores `page`/`pageSize` request parameters. The runtime walks the store in keyset chunks of 1000 rows, so rows come back in the fixed order `createdAt ASC, id ASC` and `listOptions.listSortBy` does not apply (the validator warns when both are declared). A set larger than the runtime ceiling is REFUSED with 422 `UNPAGED_LIST_TOO_LARGE`, never truncated; the ceiling is the `UNPAGED_LIST_MAX_ROWS` environment variable (a positive integer, default 10000). `listOptions.topPick` still caps the set. A validation ERROR together with `cursorMode` (a caller-driven keyset walk is the opposite contract) and with `apiOptions.dataViewName` (an Elasticsearch read cannot walk past its result window). The ceiling applies to the one-response answer: an SSE stream (`responseMode: 'stream'`) of an unpaged list sends the whole set chunk by chunk and is NOT capped. A store that returns a cursor it already returned ends the walk with 500 `UNPAGED_LIST_WALK_STALLED` instead of hanging. Meant for internal, kafka, cron and library callers: the validator warns when external callers can reach an unpaged list (`UNPAGED_LIST_REST_EXPOSED` with a REST controller, `UNPAGED_LIST_EXPOSED` with only SSE, gRPC or `apiOptions.mcpExposed`), because every caller that passes the api's gates receives the whole table; for such a list, page it and size the page with `defaultPageRowCount`. Honoured by the nodejs lane; the other language lanes still serve one page at the default size.
PaginationOptions.__defaultPageRowCount.doc: Default page size (rows per page) applied when the caller does not send a `pageSize` (or legacy `pageRowCount`) request parameter. Must be a positive integer; null or 0 means the framework default of 25. The resolved window is still clamped to 1000 rows by the runtime. Honoured by the nodejs api-layer; the other language lanes still emit their own default.
PaginationOptions.__cursorMode.doc: Opt this list api into KEYSET (cursor) pagination instead of page/offset. A cursor list is ordered by the fixed keyset `createdAt ASC, id ASC` — `listOptions.listSortBy` and a runtime `?sortBy=` no longer apply — takes an opaque `cursor` request parameter instead of `page`, and answers with `{ data: [...], paging: { pageSize, nextCursor } }`. `nextCursor` is null when the walk is exhausted; feed it back as `?cursor=` for the next page. NO COUNT query runs, so `totalCount` and `totalPages` are ABSENT from the envelope — that skipped table scan is the point of the mode. Use it for deep walks, exports and any list where rows are inserted while the caller is paging: offset paging skips and duplicates rows under concurrent inserts, keyset does not. `listOptions.topPick` is meaningless here (there is no ranked window to cap) and is ignored. Honoured by the nodejs, dotnet and java lanes (PostgreSQL and MongoDB); the other language lanes still ignore it and serve page/offset. A validation ERROR together with `unpaged: true`.

__BusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the execution flow milestones of a Business API. Only one of the sub-flows (create, update, delete, get, list) will be populated, based on the `crudType` of the API. Each workflow contains ordered arrays of action names to be executed at predefined lifecycle milestones (e.g., after reading parameters, after the main DB operation). Actions are referenced by NAME — the canonical workflow-ref form; legacy action ids remain accepted as input (older projects may still store them) but are never required. These workflows allow complete control of the API's logic and are fully compatible with visual workflow editors. When authoring, send only the api's own crudType with only its populated phases; omitted sections are equivalent to empty.

## Failure semantics — a workflow is NOT a transaction

The milestones of a workflow run as a plain sequential async pipeline. There is NO transaction, NO savepoint, NO automatic rollback and NO automatic compensation across the actions of an api. Every write an action performs — the main CRUD operation, a `createCrudAction` / `createBulkCrudAction` / `updateCrudAction` / `deleteCrudAction`, an `interserviceCallAction` write on another service, a published event, a sent mail, an external `apiCallAction` — is COMMITTED ON ITS OWN the moment that action completes.

When an action throws with `onActionError: throwError` (the default), the api aborts and the caller receives an error response, but every write that already happened STAYS COMMITTED. An `update` whose `afterMainUpdateOperation` child create fails therefore answers 4xx/5xx while the parent row is already updated — a half-applied request the caller cannot distinguish from a total failure. This is deliberate: the framework is choreographic (see `docs/ADR-project-saga-document.md`), so recovery is the designer's job, not the runtime's.

Design for it:

- **Order failure-prone writes BEFORE the main operation.** Actions placed in a pre-main stage run before `mainOperation()`, so a throw there leaves the database untouched. The pre-main write stages per crudType are: `afterBuildDataClause` for `create` and `update`; `afterCheckInstance` (or `afterFetchInstance`) for `update` and `delete`. A child create carrying a unique index, or an `interserviceCallAction` create on another service that may reject, belongs there — not in `afterMain<Crud>Operation`.
- **Keep post-main stages for work that is idempotent, retryable or genuinely optional.** In `afterMain<Crud>Operation`, `afterBuildOutput`, `afterSendResponse` and `afterApiEvent` the main row is already committed (and the last two run ONLY on a success response — see below); `onActionError: completeApi` is usually the honest setting there, since it stores the failure as `this.<actionName>Error` and still answers the caller. Note that a zero-row `updateCrudAction` / `deleteCrudAction` is NOT a failure by default: the db-layer helper resolves `[]` when the selector matched nothing, no error is raised and no `<actionName>Error` is written, so a post-main stamp or compensation that matched nothing looks successful to `completeApi`. Set `onNoRows: throwError` on such an action to turn the empty match into a typed 404 (`errorCode: ACTION_NO_ROWS_MATCHED`) that `completeApi` stores exactly like any other action error.
- **When a write must be allowed to fail after the main write, split the flow.** Use separate apis plus an explicit compensating api (for example a status-reverting update) or a saga-style retry, and record the intent in a `ProjectSaga` document. Remote/M2M and non-db actions (`sendMailAction`, `publishEventAction`, `apiCallAction`) could never be enrolled in a database transaction anyway.

## The post-response phase is SUCCESS-ONLY

`afterSendResponse` and `afterApiEvent` run only when the api answered a SUCCESS status. If the pipeline aborted and the response is 4xx/5xx, the runtime skips the whole post-response tail — `afterSendResponse`, the api event and `afterApiEvent` — so no action authored there runs and no event is published: events are domain facts, and a request that failed produced none. The skip is recorded as a `PostResponseSuppressedOnAbort` warning naming the withheld actions, so it is visible rather than silent.

What that means when authoring:

- **Never place failure cleanup or compensation in `afterSendResponse` / `afterApiEvent`.** On a failed request those milestones do not run at all. Compensating work belongs in the stage that owns the failure, or in a separate compensating api (see above).
- **A `publishEventAction` in `afterSendResponse` announces only operations that actually happened.** It cannot fire for a request that aborted at `afterCheckParameters` or `afterBuildDataClause`.
- **An explicitly completed missing-instance response (`onNotFound: complete`) is a SUCCESS branch.** It answers 2xx and still runs `afterSendResponse`; only its api event stays suppressed, because no CRUD operation took place.
- **An idempotency-key replay skips the post-response phase too.** The ORIGINAL execution already ran it; a cached replay is a response, not a second execution.

BusinessWorkflow.__create.doc: The milestone execution flow for a `create`-type API. Contains action arrays tied to standard lifecycle stages of record creation.
BusinessWorkflow.__update.doc: The milestone execution flow for an `update`-type API. Contains action arrays tied to record lookup, validation, mutation, and response shaping.
BusinessWorkflow.__delete.doc: The milestone execution flow for a `delete`-type API. Contains action arrays for lookup, conditional deletion, side-effects, and cleanup.
BusinessWorkflow.__get.doc: The milestone execution flow for a `get`-type API. Contains actions that run at fixed read-only stages like parameter validation, access checks, and enrichment.
BusinessWorkflow.__list.doc: The milestone execution flow for a `list`-type API. Enables filtering, paging, sorting, and post-query actions such as formatting or permission-based shaping.

__UpdateBusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the execution milestones for an `update`-type Business API, used to modify an existing record. Each field represents a fixed lifecycle milestone. Custom action names placed under a milestone will be executed in order after that point. These workflows enable full customization of business logic without overriding default update behavior, and they support visual modeling of logic steps.

**Failure semantics — NO ROLLBACK.** The milestones run sequentially with no transaction. Everything up to and including `afterBuildDataClause` (and before it `afterFetchInstance` / `afterCheckInstance`) runs BEFORE the row is updated, so an action that throws there leaves the database untouched. From `afterMainUpdateOperation` onward the parent row is already committed, and an action that throws (`onActionError: throwError`, the default) aborts the remaining pipeline WITHOUT reverting that update or any write an earlier action already made — the classic corruption is a status-advancing update whose `afterMainUpdateOperation` child create 409s, leaving the record advanced and the child missing. Put child writes that may legitimately fail in `afterCheckInstance` or `afterBuildDataClause`; use `onActionError: completeApi` for post-main work that must not fail the api, and an explicit compensating api when a post-main write really can fail. `completeApi` alone is INCOMPLETE for an `updateCrudAction`: a selector that matched no row resolves `[]` without raising anything, so nothing lands in `this.<actionName>Error`; add `onNoRows: throwError` to the action when the row it addresses must exist. See `BusinessWorkflow` for the full contract.

UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterStartBusinessApi.doc: Executed first, just after the api is started by the controller and BEFORE the login check (pipeline step 0): the context has the raw request, and a session the caller sent is populated, but the api's login requirement has not been enforced yet, so an anonymous caller reaches this stage. Use it for login-independent work - fundamental request validations or preparing the context. On an api that requires a login (authOptions.loginRequired, default true) an InterserviceCallAction, AgentCallAction, IntegrationAction, InterProjectCallAction, SendMailAction, CheckMailboxAction, ReadMailAction, PublishEventAction, SendSmsAction, SendWhatsAppAction or SendPushNotificationAction may not be scheduled here, directly or inside a loop/parallel container: each acts with the service's or the project's own authority (a machine-identity forward, a mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push send or a mailbox read with the project's credentials, or a Kafka event its consumer treats as a machine caller), so an anonymous caller would borrow that authority. Design time refuses that shape (PRE_AUTH_MACHINE_AUTHORITY_ACTION); schedule those actions at afterReadParameters (the first milestone after the login check) or later.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterReadParameters.doc: Triggered after all parameters are read from the request or Redis. Use this to perform early validation or context enrichment based on raw input.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterTransposeParameters.doc: Executed after parameters are normalized or transformed. Use this for logic that depends on preprocessed values (e.g., derived inputs or structure remapping).
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckParameters.doc: Runs after parameter validations complete. Use this for business logic checks or to raise field-specific errors (e.g., pricing thresholds, invalid combinations).
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckBasicAuth.doc: Fires after role and permission validations. Typically used to enforce fine-grained access checks or audit preparation logic.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildWhereClause.doc: Occurs once the main `WHERE` clause is generated for the query. Insert actions here to log or modify query conditions or add scoped audit logic. This where clause will be first used to fetch the instance to be updated.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterFetchInstance.doc: Fires after manager fetches the target record before it is updated and written to the context for pre-operation checks. Insert your own actions here to add your own checks or to mnanipulate default instance check which will be executed next.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckInstance.doc: Triggered after the instance is dispatched and check for basic requirements like existence or ownership. Insert actions here to make your own checks on the instance that will be updated.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildDataClause.doc: Executed after the update data clause object is constructed and before the actual update operation. Use this to inject additional fields or adjust payload structure.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterMainUpdateOperation.doc: Runs immediately after the database update operation completes. Ideal for events, side-effects, or chained actions based on the updated record.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterMissingInstance.doc: Alternate branch for basics.apiOptions.onNotFound=`complete`. Runs when update prefetch finds no target (so no mutation is attempted) or when a prefetched-row mutation affects zero rows. The normal afterMainUpdateOperation branch and API event are skipped, then execution rejoins at afterBuildOutput.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildOutput.doc: Allows final shaping of the response payload before it is sent. You can inject, modify, or strip fields at this stage.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterSendResponse.doc: Triggered after the response is sent to the client. Use for post-response operations like analytics, logging, or delayed workflows. This milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that aborted and answered 4xx/5xx skips it entirely, along with the api event and `afterApiEvent`, so nothing authored here runs and no event is published.
UpdateBusinessWorkflow.__afterApiEvent.doc: Triggered after the Business API emits an API-level event (if configured). This is the final milestone in the API execution flow and is typically used for cleanup, async queues, or chained notifications that depend on event dispatch success. Like `afterSendResponse`, this milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that answered 4xx/5xx never reaches it.

__workflowDesign.name: startBusinessApi
__workflowDesign.internalBehaviour: Manager initializes context, prepares request and session objects, and sets up internal structures for parameter handling and milestone execution.

__workflowDesign.name: readParameters
__workflowDesign.internalBehaviour: Manager reads parameters from the request or Redis, applies defaults, and writes them into context for downstream milestones.

__workflowDesign.name: transposeParameters
__workflowDesign.internalBehaviour: Manager executes parameter transform scripts and derives any helper values or reshaped payloads into the context.

__workflowDesign.name: checkParameters

__DeleteBusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the execution milestones for a `delete`-type Business API, which removes or soft-deletes a single record. Each field corresponds to a lifecycle milestone. Custom actions inserted at any milestone are executed in order after that point. This enables fine-grained control over logic such as confirmation checks, permission gating, logging, or external integrations—without needing to override the default deletion behavior.

**Failure semantics — NO ROLLBACK.** The milestones run sequentially with no transaction. Everything up to and including `afterCheckInstance` runs BEFORE the row is deleted, so an action that throws there leaves the database untouched. From `afterMainDeleteOperation` onward the delete is already committed, and an action that throws (`onActionError: throwError`, the default) aborts the remaining pipeline WITHOUT restoring the deleted row or undoing any write an earlier action already made — a cascade cleanup that fails half-way stays half-done. Put dependent deletes and guard-style child writes that may legitimately fail in `afterFetchInstance` / `afterCheckInstance`; use `onActionError: completeApi` for post-main cleanup that must not fail the api. `completeApi` alone is INCOMPLETE for a `deleteCrudAction`: a selector that matched no row resolves `[]` without raising anything, so nothing lands in `this.<actionName>Error`; add `onNoRows: throwError` to the action when the row it addresses must exist. See `BusinessWorkflow` for the full contract.

DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterStartBusinessApi.doc: Executed first, just after the api is started by the controller and BEFORE the login check (pipeline step 0): the context has the raw request, and a session the caller sent is populated, but the api's login requirement has not been enforced yet, so an anonymous caller reaches this stage. Use it for login-independent work - fundamental request validations or preparing the context. On an api that requires a login (authOptions.loginRequired, default true) an InterserviceCallAction, AgentCallAction, IntegrationAction, InterProjectCallAction, SendMailAction, CheckMailboxAction, ReadMailAction, PublishEventAction, SendSmsAction, SendWhatsAppAction or SendPushNotificationAction may not be scheduled here, directly or inside a loop/parallel container: each acts with the service's or the project's own authority (a machine-identity forward, a mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push send or a mailbox read with the project's credentials, or a Kafka event its consumer treats as a machine caller), so an anonymous caller would borrow that authority. Design time refuses that shape (PRE_AUTH_MACHINE_AUTHORITY_ACTION); schedule those actions at afterReadParameters (the first milestone after the login check) or later.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterReadParameters.doc: Triggered after all parameters are read from the request or Redis. Use this to perform early validation or context enrichment based on raw input.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterTransposeParameters.doc: Executed after parameters are normalized or transformed. Use this for logic that depends on preprocessed values (e.g., derived inputs or structure remapping).
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckParameters.doc: Runs after parameter validations complete. Use this for business logic checks or to raise field-specific errors (e.g., pricing thresholds, invalid combinations).
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckBasicAuth.doc: Fires after role and permission validations. Typically used to enforce fine-grained access checks or audit preparation logic.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildWhereClause.doc: Occurs once the main `WHERE` clause is generated for the query. Insert actions here to log or modify query conditions or add scoped audit logic. This where clause will be first used to fetch the instance to be deleted.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterFetchInstance.doc: Fires after manager fetches the target record before it is deleted and written to the context for pre-operation checks. Insert your own actions here to add your own checks or to mnanipulate default instance check which will be executed next.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckInstance.doc: Triggered after the instance is dispatched and check for basic requirements like existence or ownership. Insert actions here to make your own checks on the instance that will be deleted.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterMainDeleteOperation.doc: Runs immediately after the database delete operation completes. Ideal for events, side-effects, or chained actions based on the deleted record.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterMissingInstance.doc: Alternate branch for basics.apiOptions.onNotFound=`complete`. Runs when delete prefetch finds no target (so no mutation is attempted) or when a prefetched-row mutation affects zero rows. The normal afterMainDeleteOperation branch and API event are skipped, then execution rejoins at afterBuildOutput.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildOutput.doc: Allows final shaping of the response payload before it is sent. You can inject, modify, or strip fields at this stage.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterSendResponse.doc: Triggered after the response is sent to the client. Use for post-response operations like analytics, logging, or delayed workflows. This milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that aborted and answered 4xx/5xx skips it entirely, along with the api event and `afterApiEvent`, so nothing authored here runs and no event is published.
DeleteBusinessWorkflow.__afterApiEvent.doc: Triggered after the Business API emits an API-level event (if configured). This is the final milestone in the API execution flow and is typically used for cleanup, async queues, or chained notifications that depend on event dispatch success. Like `afterSendResponse`, this milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that answered 4xx/5xx never reaches it.

__CreateBusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the standard execution milestones for a `create`-type Business API. Each field represents a milestone (a fixed lifecycle stage), and its value is an ordered list of action names executed by the API manager. These steps include all default, hardcoded logic (e.g., session handling, parameter extraction, DB insert) while leaving space for user-defined actions after each milestone. You can modify this workflow programmatically or visually.

**Failure semantics — NO ROLLBACK.** The milestones run sequentially with no transaction. Everything up to and including `afterBuildDataClause` runs BEFORE the row is inserted, so an action that throws there leaves the database untouched. From `afterMainCreateOperation` onward the new row is already committed, and an action that throws (`onActionError: throwError`, the default) aborts the remaining pipeline WITHOUT undoing that insert or any write an earlier action already made. Put child writes that may legitimately fail — a unique-index child create, an `interserviceCallAction` create on another service, an external api call — in `afterBuildDataClause`; use `onActionError: completeApi` for post-main work that must not fail the api. See `BusinessWorkflow` for the full contract.

CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterStartBusinessApi.doc: Executed first, just after the api is started by the controller and BEFORE the login check (pipeline step 0): the context has the raw request, and a session the caller sent is populated, but the api's login requirement has not been enforced yet, so an anonymous caller reaches this stage. Use it for login-independent work - fundamental request validations or preparing the context. On an api that requires a login (authOptions.loginRequired, default true) an InterserviceCallAction, AgentCallAction, IntegrationAction, InterProjectCallAction, SendMailAction, CheckMailboxAction, ReadMailAction, PublishEventAction, SendSmsAction, SendWhatsAppAction or SendPushNotificationAction may not be scheduled here, directly or inside a loop/parallel container: each acts with the service's or the project's own authority (a machine-identity forward, a mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push send or a mailbox read with the project's credentials, or a Kafka event its consumer treats as a machine caller), so an anonymous caller would borrow that authority. Design time refuses that shape (PRE_AUTH_MACHINE_AUTHORITY_ACTION); schedule those actions at afterReadParameters (the first milestone after the login check) or later.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterReadParameters.doc: Triggered after all parameters are read from the request or Redis. Use this to perform early validation or context enrichment based on raw input.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterTransposeParameters.doc: Executed after parameters are normalized or transformed. Use this for logic that depends on preprocessed values (e.g., derived inputs or structure remapping).
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckParameters.doc: Runs after parameter validations complete. Use this for business logic checks or to raise field-specific errors (e.g., pricing thresholds, invalid combinations).
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckBasicAuth.doc: Fires after role and permission validations. Typically used to enforce fine-grained access checks or audit preparation logic.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildDataClause.doc: Executed after the data clause object is constructed and before the actual create operation. Use this to inject additional fields or adjust payload structure.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterMainCreateOperation.doc:
Runs immediately after the database insert operation completes. Ideal for events, side-effects, or chained actions based on the created record.

This stage also runs when NO ROW WAS INSERTED. If the object declares a unique index with `onDuplicate: 'stopOperation'` (the sanctioned way to make a create retry-safe), a replay returns the EXISTING row and the pipeline continues normally — `this.result` and `this.<objectName>` are that prior row. Read `this.createOutcome` to tell the cases apart: `'created'` (a row was inserted), `'duplicateStopped'` (the index matched and nothing was written) or `'duplicateUpdated'` (`onDuplicate: 'doUpdate'` matched and the row was updated in place). Gate every action here whose effect must not repeat — child creates, counter allocations, published events — with `condition: "this.createOutcome === 'created'"`. The value is bound by `executeMainOperation()` at this stage, so it is `undefined` in any earlier stage and must not be read there.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildOutput.doc: Allows final shaping of the response payload before it is sent. You can inject, modify, or strip fields at this stage.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterSendResponse.doc: Triggered after the response is sent to the client. Use for post-response operations like analytics, logging, or delayed workflows. This milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that aborted and answered 4xx/5xx skips it entirely, along with the api event and `afterApiEvent`, so nothing authored here runs and no event is published.
CreateBusinessWorkflow.__afterApiEvent.doc: Triggered after the Business API emits an API-level event (if configured). This is the final milestone in the API execution flow and is typically used for cleanup, async queues, or chained notifications that depend on event dispatch success. Like `afterSendResponse`, this milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that answered 4xx/5xx never reaches it.

__GetBusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the execution milestones for a `get`-type Business API, which retrieves a single record. Each milestone represents a predefined point in the API lifecycle. Action names listed under a milestone will be executed in the given order immediately after that point is reached. This structure enables customized behaviors like access control, derived property enrichment, or API shaping without overriding core logic.

**Failure semantics — NO ROLLBACK.** The milestones run sequentially with no transaction. The main operation of a `get` api only reads, but any WRITING action you place in these stages (a `createCrudAction`, `updateCrudAction`, `publishEventAction`, `sendMailAction`, an external api call — e.g. an access-log or view-counter write) is committed on its own as soon as it completes. A later action that throws (`onActionError: throwError`, the default) aborts the remaining pipeline and answers the caller with an error, but does NOT undo those writes. See `BusinessWorkflow` for the full contract.

GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterStartBusinessApi.doc: Executed first, just after the api is started by the controller and BEFORE the login check (pipeline step 0): the context has the raw request, and a session the caller sent is populated, but the api's login requirement has not been enforced yet, so an anonymous caller reaches this stage. Use it for login-independent work - fundamental request validations or preparing the context. On an api that requires a login (authOptions.loginRequired, default true) an InterserviceCallAction, AgentCallAction, IntegrationAction, InterProjectCallAction, SendMailAction, CheckMailboxAction, ReadMailAction, PublishEventAction, SendSmsAction, SendWhatsAppAction or SendPushNotificationAction may not be scheduled here, directly or inside a loop/parallel container: each acts with the service's or the project's own authority (a machine-identity forward, a mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push send or a mailbox read with the project's credentials, or a Kafka event its consumer treats as a machine caller), so an anonymous caller would borrow that authority. Design time refuses that shape (PRE_AUTH_MACHINE_AUTHORITY_ACTION); schedule those actions at afterReadParameters (the first milestone after the login check) or later.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterReadParameters.doc: Executed after parameters are extracted from the request. This is the earliest milestone and is ideal for initial validation, normalization, or preprocessing.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterTransposeParameters.doc: Runs after parameter transformation, such as type coercion or merging Redis parameters. Use this stage to derive dependent values or reformat inputs.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckParameters.doc: Triggered after core validations on required or custom parameters complete. Insert validation actions here to enforce business-specific input rules.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckBasicAuth.doc: Executed after basic role and permission checks are performed. Use this for object-level access guards or dynamic access logic based on user roles.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildWhereClause.doc: Occurs once the main `WHERE` clause is generated for the query. Insert actions here to log or modify fetch conditions or add scoped audit logic.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterMainGetOperation.doc: Runs immediately after the object is fetched from the database. This is the best point for enrichment actions like fetching related data or computing derived properties.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckInstance.doc: Triggered after the instance is dispatched and check for basic requirements like existence or ownership. Insert actions here to make your own checks on the instance that was fetched.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterMissingInstance.doc: Alternate branch for basics.apiOptions.onNotFound=`complete`. Runs only when the get target is missing; the normal afterMainGetOperation branch and API event are skipped, then execution rejoins at afterBuildOutput.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildOutput.doc: Executes after the response payload is constructed but before it is sent. Use this to adjust formatting, inject extra context, or remove sensitive fields.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterSendResponse.doc: Triggered after the response is dispatched. Use for non-blocking post-response actions like logging, analytics, or starting asynchronous flows. This milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that aborted and answered 4xx/5xx skips it entirely, along with the api event and `afterApiEvent`, so nothing authored here runs and no event is published.
GetBusinessWorkflow.__afterApiEvent.doc: Runs after the optional API-level event has been emitted. This is the final milestone and is ideal for actions that should occur after the workflow is complete. Like `afterSendResponse`, this milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that answered 4xx/5xx never reaches it.

__ListBusinessWorkflow.doc:
Defines the execution milestones for a `list`-type Business API, which returns a paginated set of records. Each field represents a fixed lifecycle milestone. Action names added to a milestone will be executed in order after that point. This structure enables modular extension of logic for filtering, permission enforcement, data enrichment, and more—without overriding the main query behavior.

**Failure semantics — NO ROLLBACK.** The milestones run sequentially with no transaction. The main operation of a `list` api only reads, but any WRITING action you place in these stages (a `createCrudAction`, `updateCrudAction`, `publishEventAction`, `sendMailAction`, an external api call — e.g. an audit or export record) is committed on its own as soon as it completes, and per-item writes inside a `loopAction` commit one by one. A later action that throws (`onActionError: throwError`, the default) aborts the remaining pipeline and answers the caller with an error, but does NOT undo the writes that already succeeded. See `BusinessWorkflow` for the full contract.

ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterStartBusinessApi.doc: Executed first, just after the api is started by the controller and BEFORE the login check (pipeline step 0): the context has the raw request, and a session the caller sent is populated, but the api's login requirement has not been enforced yet, so an anonymous caller reaches this stage. Use it for login-independent work - fundamental request validations or preparing the context. On an api that requires a login (authOptions.loginRequired, default true) an InterserviceCallAction, AgentCallAction, IntegrationAction, InterProjectCallAction, SendMailAction, CheckMailboxAction, ReadMailAction, PublishEventAction, SendSmsAction, SendWhatsAppAction or SendPushNotificationAction may not be scheduled here, directly or inside a loop/parallel container: each acts with the service's or the project's own authority (a machine-identity forward, a mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push send or a mailbox read with the project's credentials, or a Kafka event its consumer treats as a machine caller), so an anonymous caller would borrow that authority. Design time refuses that shape (PRE_AUTH_MACHINE_AUTHORITY_ACTION); schedule those actions at afterReadParameters (the first milestone after the login check) or later.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterReadParameters.doc: Executed immediately after request and Redis parameters are read into context. Use this stage for early validations or transformations on raw inputs.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterTransposeParameters.doc: Runs after parameter reshaping or normalization logic. Use this for refining structured inputs or deriving helper values for downstream use.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckParameters.doc: Executed after required and custom parameters have been validated. Place custom validation or cross-field logic actions here.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterCheckBasicAuth.doc: Runs after role-based access checks. Use this milestone to insert actions that enforce access based on session, membership, or other dynamic conditions.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildWhereClause.doc: Triggered after the main query’s `WHERE` clause has been finalized. Insert logic here for audit logging or external query construction monitoring.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterMainListOperation.doc: Runs after the paginated list has been retrieved from the database. Use this milestone for data enrichment, parallel fetches, or computed fields.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterBuildOutput.doc: Executed after the response payload has been shaped. This is the best point to inject additional context, sanitize outputs, or apply output transformations.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterSendResponse.doc: Runs after the list result has been sent to the client. Use this for analytics, usage tracking, or triggering asynchronous actions. This milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that aborted and answered 4xx/5xx skips it entirely, along with the api event and `afterApiEvent`, so nothing authored here runs and no event is published.
ListBusinessWorkflow.__afterApiEvent.doc: Executed after the optional API-level event is published (if configured). This is the final milestone for clean-up or system-level broadcasting. Like `afterSendResponse`, this milestone is SUCCESS-ONLY: an api that answered 4xx/5xx never reaches it.

__AgentExecutionMode.doc.#: Defines how the AI agent processes requests.
__AgentExecutionMode.doc.task: One-shot execution: receives input, processes it, returns result. No conversation history.
__AgentExecutionMode.doc.chat: Multi-turn conversation: maintains history across requests using a session identifier.
__AgentExecutionMode.doc.orchestrator: Coordinates multiple sub-agents in sequential, parallel, or adaptive workflows.

__AgentModality.doc.#: Defines the primary input/output modality of the agent.
__AgentModality.doc.text: Text-in, text/JSON-out. Supports tool calling and streaming.
__AgentModality.doc.vision: Text + image(s) in, text/JSON-out. Supports tool calling and streaming.
__AgentModality.doc.image: Text prompt in, image URL(s) out. No tool calling.
__AgentModality.doc.audio: Text-to-speech or speech-to-text depending on direction setting.
__AgentModality.doc.video: Text/image prompt in, video URL out. No tool calling.

__AgentResponseFormat.doc.#: Defines the expected response format from the AI model.
__AgentResponseFormat.doc.json: Structured JSON response (uses JSON mode where supported).
__AgentResponseFormat.doc.url: A URL pointing to a generated resource (image, audio, video).
__AgentResponseFormat.doc.binary: Raw binary data (e.g., audio stream chunks).

__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.#: How much internal reasoning a reasoning-capable model spends before it answers. Sent to OpenAI-family reasoning models (the o-series and the gpt-5 family) as reasoning_effort; other providers ignore it.
__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.none: No reasoning. Function tools on the gpt-5 family over chat/completions need this on models whose default effort is above none.
__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.minimal: The smallest reasoning budget the model offers.
__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.low: Low reasoning effort: faster and cheaper answers.
__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.medium: Medium reasoning effort (the usual provider default).
__AgentReasoningEffort.doc.high: High reasoning effort: slower, more thorough answers.

__AgentHistoryStorage.doc.#: Defines where conversation history is stored for chat-mode agents.
__AgentHistoryStorage.doc.memory: In-memory storage. Fast but lost on restart. Suitable for development or ephemeral sessions.
__AgentHistoryStorage.doc.database: Persistent database storage. History survives restarts. Required for production chat agents.

__AgentCostCeilingScope.doc.#: Which spend guardrails.dailyCostCeilingUsd is compared with.
__AgentCostCeilingScope.doc.project: The combined spend of every agent of the service process in the project (single-tenant) or in the caller's tenant (multi-tenant). The default.
__AgentCostCeilingScope.doc.agent: This agent's own spend only (per tenant on a multi-tenant project): the spend of the project's other agents never counts against this agent's ceiling.

__AgentOrchestrationStrategy.doc.#: Defines how orchestrator agents execute their steps.
__AgentOrchestrationStrategy.doc.sequential: Steps run one after another in defined order.
__AgentOrchestrationStrategy.doc.parallel: Steps marked as parallel run concurrently; others run sequentially.
__AgentOrchestrationStrategy.doc.adaptive: The orchestrator AI decides which steps to run next based on intermediate results, looping until completionCondition is met.

__AgentAudioDirection.doc.#: Defines whether the audio agent performs text-to-speech or speech-to-text.
__AgentAudioDirection.doc.tts: Text-to-speech: converts text input into audio output.
__AgentAudioDirection.doc.stt: Speech-to-text: converts audio input into text output.

__AgentAudioOutputFormat.doc.#: Defines the output format for text-to-speech audio generation.
__AgentAudioOutputFormat.doc.mp3: MP3 format. Widely supported, good compression.
__AgentAudioOutputFormat.doc.opus: Opus format. Excellent compression, low latency.

__AgentImageQuality.doc.standard: Standard quality. Faster generation, lower cost.
__AgentImageQuality.doc.hd: High-definition quality. Slower generation, higher detail.

__AgentImageStyle.doc.#: Defines the artistic style for image generation.

__AgentApiFormat.doc.raw: Raw HTTP request/response. Full control over payload shape.

__AgentContextSourceType.doc.#: Defines how a context source fetches its data.
__AgentContextSourceType.doc.dataObject: Queries a DataObject from the service's database.

__AgentContextSourceType.doc.apiCall: Invokes a BusinessApi or external HTTP endpoint.

__AIAgent.doc:
Defines a standalone AI agent at the service level. Each agent encapsulates a model configuration, system prompt, input/output pipeline, optional tool access, and conversation management. Agents support multiple execution modes (task, chat, orchestrator) and modalities (text, image, audio, video, vision). They are exposed as dedicated REST and/or SSE endpoints and can be invoked by other agents as tools.

### Field support matrix

Every AIAgent field is either WIRED into the generated runtime or was REMOVED from the schema — no field validates-and-no-ops.

| Field | Status |
| --- | --- |
| agentBasics (name, description, modality, executionMode task/chat/orchestrator) | wired |
| agentBasics.executionMode = 'orchestrator' | wired (supervisor/worker orchestration driven by orchestrationSettings: sequential/parallel step pipelines and an adaptive planner loop; steps are durable child runs) |
| modelSettings (providerName, model, systemPrompt, temperature, maxTokens) | wired |
| modelSettings.responseFormat = 'json' | wired on EVERY provider family (native JSON/structured mode where available, prompt-based emulation + repair loop elsewhere) |
| modelSettings.responseSchema, strictOutput | wired (schema-validated structured output with bounded repair loop) |
| modelSettings.fallbackProviders | wired (retry with backoff, then fall down the declared provider chain) |
| modelSettings.toolChoice, parallelToolCalls | wired (mapped to each provider's native tool-choice control) |
| modelSettings.reasoningEffort | wired (sent as reasoning_effort to OpenAI-family reasoning models; on Anthropic models it switches thinking on and sets its effort or budget, unset = thinking off; ignored by other providers) |
| modelSettings.contextWindowTokens | wired (context-compaction trigger override) |
| modelSettings.systemPromptSources | wired (fetched into the system message as named context segments; cached per chatSettings.refreshSystemPrompt + per-source cacheTtlSeconds; fetch failures are fail-soft) |
| inputSettings.promptTemplate, acceptsUpload, maxFiles | wired (uploads reach the model as image/document content blocks on vision-capable providers) |
| inputSettings.contextSources | wired (fetched per run; variables bind into promptTemplate — without a template they append as a context block on the user message; fetch failures are fail-soft) |
| inputSettings.autoResize / autoConvert | removed (auto-migrated off existing blueprints) |
| outputSettings.responseProperty, postProcess | wired |
| outputSettings.requiresApproval | wired (draft-then-approve: the final output is held as a draft in the 'paused_approval' run state until an approver releases or rejects it via the hub approval API) |
| outputSettings.storeTo | removed (auto-migrated off existing blueprints) |
| toolSettings (enableCrudTools, crudScopes, apiTools, agentTools, libraryTools, customTools, integrationTools) | wired; list entries are existence-checked at design time |
| toolSettings.approvalRequiredTools | wired (human-in-the-loop: the run pauses BEFORE the tool fires; the hub approval API approves — the run resumes through its tool journal — or rejects with a clean rejection tool_result) |
| chatSettings.historyStorage, maxHistoryMessages | wired |
| chatSettings.summarizeAfter, pinnedRecentMessages | wired (context compaction: sliding window or recursive summarization with a pinned recent window) |
| chatSettings.refreshSystemPrompt | wired (per-turn re-evaluation vs once-per-instance caching of the whole system message pipeline, dynamic systemPromptSources included) |
| orchestrationSettings (strategy, maxIterations, completionCondition, orchestrationSteps incl. cross-service 'service:agent' steps) | wired (durable supervisor/worker graph: steps dispatch as child runs keyed by originKey — idempotent retries; a paused/failed child pauses/fails the parent coherently) |
| imageSettings / audioSettings / videoSettings | wired |
| customEndpoint | wired (legacy direct-endpoint binding; prefer a 'custom'-type project AI provider) |
| endpointSettings (REST/SSE/basePath/authRequired/chatSurfaces) | wired |
| guardrails.maxToolCalls, maxFileSizeMb, timeout, allowedMimeTypes, maxAgentDepth | wired |
| guardrails.maxTokenBudget, maxToolResultChars | wired (cumulative token budget from provider usage feedback; tool-result truncation) |
| guardrails.inputValidation, outputValidation | wired (MScript gates: input rejection is a clean 4xx-style error before any provider call; output failure repairs once in strict mode, else annotates) |
| guardrails.dailyTokenBudgetPerUser, dailyCostCeilingUsd | wired (per-user/day token and per-tenant/day USD ceilings enforced before every provider call — deny-before-checkpoint; cost from the model price table, run records carry tokenUsage.costUsd) |
| guardrails.logPreviewChars, logMaskFields | wired (configurable redaction of the tool-call audit trail; default 0 = metadata/sizes only — the WS2 posture) |
| evalSettings.evalCases | wired (declared eval suite; executed by the hub's role-gated POST /agents/:agentName/eval runner, which requires guardrails.dailyCostCeilingUsd) |
| kafkaControllers (name, topic, groupId, dataMapping, enabled) | wired |

AIAgent.__approvalExpiryDays.doc: Agent-level approval expiry in days, shared by approvalRequiredTools and requiresApproval. Null or unset on stored agents disables expiry; newly created agents start at 30 days through the new-instance defaults registry only. A configured value must be a positive safe integer number. Node.js and Rust only for now: every deployment host, including assignedService, must emit the sweep or validation refuses it. Pauses older than the window become terminal expired without executing tools or releasing drafts. The independent hourly UTC sweep is claimed by one replica and bounded to 200 rows per page and 10 pages per agent per tick, with a cursor across ticks. Approve/reject of an expired run returns 410 AGENT_APPROVAL_EXPIRED; polling retains terminal metadata. Expired runs are eligible for conversation retention and user erasure.
AIAgent.__agentBasics.doc: Core identity and execution mode of the agent, including its name, description, modality, and how it processes requests.
AIAgent.__modelSettings.doc: AI provider and model configuration, including the system prompt and optional dynamic prompt sources that inject context into the system message.
AIAgent.__inputSettings.doc: Defines how incoming request data is transformed into the agent's prompt or input, including file upload support and dynamic context enrichment.
AIAgent.__outputSettings.doc: Controls how the AI model's response is transformed before returning to the client.
AIAgent.__toolSettings.doc: Configures which tools the agent can call during execution. Only applicable for text and vision modality agents. Includes CRUD tools, API tools, sub-agent tools, library function tools, and custom tool definitions.
AIAgent.__chatSettings.doc: Conversation history management settings. Only applicable when executionMode is 'chat'.
AIAgent.__orchestrationSettings.doc: Multi-agent orchestration configuration. Only applicable when executionMode is 'orchestrator'. Defines the execution strategy and the steps to coordinate. Steps run as DURABLE child runs (sub-agent executions keyed by '<supervisor-run-id>:<step-name>' — a crashed or re-driven supervisor never re-executes a completed step) under the ORIGINAL caller's identity (per-step scoped permissions); a paused child (human-in-the-loop) pauses the supervisor, a failed child fails it.
AIAgent.__imageSettings.doc: Image generation parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'image'.
AIAgent.__audioSettings.doc: Audio generation or transcription parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'audio'.
AIAgent.__videoSettings.doc: Video generation parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'video'.
AIAgent.__customEndpoint.doc: Custom provider endpoint configuration — binds the agent directly to an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint when no project-level AI provider is referenced. Ignored when modelSettings.providerName is set (declare a 'custom'-type provider in projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[] instead). Every agent must have either modelSettings.providerName or this customEndpoint.
AIAgent.__endpointSettings.doc: Controls how the agent is exposed as an API endpoint, including REST/SSE toggles, path customization, and authentication.
AIAgent.__guardrails.doc: Safety limits and cost controls including token budgets, timeouts, file size limits, and input/output validation.
AIAgent.__evalSettings.doc: Declarable evaluation suite for the agent: named prompt/assertion cases executed on demand by the hub's role-gated eval runner (POST /agents/{name}/eval). Each case runs the agent for real (a normal durable run with source 'eval') and passes/fails on expectedContains and/or an MScript assertion. The runner requires guardrails.dailyCostCeilingUsd on the agent: without it the suite is refused with 409 AGENT_EVAL_COST_CEILING_REQUIRED.
AIAgent.__kafkaControllers.doc: Kafka-triggered controllers for the agent. Each controller listens on a Kafka topic and maps the incoming message payload to the agent's input format before executing the agent. Multiple controllers can be defined for different topics with different data mappings.

__AgentBasics.doc: Core identity, execution mode and service placement of the AI agent. The name serves as the asset identifier and is used in endpoint paths, inter-agent references, and code generation.

AgentBasics.__name.doc: Unique agent name within the service. Used in endpoint paths (/agents/{name}), inter-agent tool references, and generated code file names. Must be camelCase.
AgentBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this agent does. Used in documentation, MCP tool descriptions, and the design UI.
AgentBasics.__executionMode.doc: How the agent processes requests: 'task' for one-shot execution, 'chat' for multi-turn conversations with history, 'orchestrator' for coordinating multiple sub-agents.
AgentBasics.__modality.doc: The primary input/output modality: 'text' for text generation with tool calling, 'vision' for text+image input, 'image'/'audio'/'video' for media generation.
AgentBasics.__assignedService.doc: Service assignment for a project-level agentHub agent (agentHub.aiAgents). When set to a service name, this hub agent ALSO fans out into that service's agent-layer — it is generated there exactly like a service-local aiAgents entry and can be referenced hub-wide (e.g. by a videoRooms[].meetingAgents[].agentName). Null (default) keeps the agent hub-only. Ignored on service-level aiAgents.
AgentBasics.name: String

__AgentModelSettings.doc: AI provider and model configuration for the agent. Defines which LLM or generative model to use, its parameters, and optional dynamic system prompt sources that inject contextual data into the system message at runtime.

AgentModelSettings.__providerName.doc: Reference to a project-level AI provider by codeName. Must match an entry in projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name — the runtime looks up the provider's type + env-var-driven credentials from the per-service providers-manifest (codegen-emitted). This is the canonical (and only) provider binding: every agent must set providerName OR declare a customEndpoint section. A legacy raw `provider` type string (pre-aiProviders[] blueprints) is accepted and auto-migrated into providerName at validation time. The referenced provider's family must match the agent's modality (LLM for text/vision, image/audio/video providers for media agents).
AgentModelSettings.__model.doc: Provider-specific model name. Current latest model IDs (as of mid-2026): Anthropic — 'claude-opus-4-8' (most capable), 'claude-sonnet-5' (balanced default), 'claude-haiku-4-5' (fast). OpenAI — 'gpt-5', 'gpt-5-mini'. Google — 'gemini-2.5-pro', 'gemini-2.5-flash'. Image — 'dall-e-3' (OpenAI), 'flux-pro' (fal). Audio TTS — 'eleven_multilingual_v2' (ElevenLabs). Always pick the latest model from the provider's docs unless the project explicitly requires an older version — older Claude IDs like 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-5' or 'claude-3-5-sonnet-...' are out of date.
AgentModelSettings.__systemPrompt.doc: Static system instructions that define the agent's persona, constraints, and output format. This text is sent as the system message in every request.
AgentModelSettings.__temperature.doc: Controls randomness in model output. Range 0.0-2.0 (anthropic/bedrock providers accept 0.0-1.0 — validated against the bound provider). Lower values (0.1-0.3) for deterministic tasks, higher values (0.7-1.0) for creative tasks. Default: 0.7.
AgentModelSettings.__maxTokens.doc: Maximum number of output tokens per model call (thinking tokens count against it). Leave null for the provider default (Anthropic: model-aware, 16384 on current Claude models, 8192 on Claude 3.5, 4096 on the Claude 3 base models and on a non-Claude model id behind a custom Anthropic-format endpoint). On Anthropic models thinking is off unless reasoningEffort is set; with an effort on Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.6+ the limit covers thinking AND the answer (no separate budget exists there), so give it room (16000 or more for tool-heavy chat agents). A final turn that spends the whole limit on thinking is retried once with thinking off before it fails with AGENT_EMPTY_OUTPUT.
AgentModelSettings.__responseFormat.doc: Expected response format: 'text' for plain text, 'json' for structured JSON, 'url' for media URLs, 'binary' for raw binary data. 'json' is wired for EVERY provider family: providers with a native JSON/structured-output mode (openai-compatible, anthropic current-gen, google) receive it natively; the rest get prompt-based emulation with a bounded validate-and-repair loop. Pair with responseSchema to enforce a specific JSON shape.
AgentModelSettings.__systemPromptSources.doc: Dynamic data sources fetched at runtime and injected into the system prompt as named context segments (appended under a '## Context' block, one segment per source). Refresh semantics: the whole system message pipeline is built once per runtime instance unless chatSettings.refreshSystemPrompt is true (re-evaluated every turn); each source may additionally cache its fetched value for cacheTtlSeconds. A source that fails to fetch is FAIL-SOFT: the run continues without that segment (logged warning). Useful for injecting user profiles, configuration, or domain knowledge.
AgentModelSettings.__fallbackProviders.doc: Comma-separated ordered list of project-level AI provider names (aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name) to fall back to when the primary provider fails with a retryable error (429 rate-limit, 5xx, network) after its retry budget is exhausted. The conversation is provider-neutral, so history carries over losslessly to the next provider in the chain. Each entry is existence- and family-checked at design time. Example: 'backupOpenai,localOllama'.
AgentModelSettings.__responseSchema.doc: JSON Schema (as a JSON string) that the agent's final response must validate against. Implies JSON output. Providers with native structured output (openai-compatible json_schema, anthropic current-gen output_config, google responseSchema) receive the schema natively; other providers get a schema instruction in the system prompt. Either way the runtime validates the final answer and runs a bounded repair loop (validation errors are fed back to the model) before failing. Object-root schemas only. An EMPTY schema ('{}', or an object schema that declares no property) means NO structured output: it is never sent to the provider (anthropic refuses it), the agent falls back to its responseFormat, and validation warns (AGENT_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_EMPTY). Provider schema limits: anthropic compiles the schema into a decoding grammar and documents at most 24 optional properties (not listed in required) and 16 union-typed properties (anyOf / oneOf or a type array) across a request's strict schemas, plus an internal grammar-size limit ('Schema is too complex for compilation'); validation warns when an agent bound to an anthropic provider exceeds the two counts (AGENT_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_TOO_COMPLEX). When the provider refuses the schema as too complex to compile, the runtime retries that call ONCE in JSON mode: the schema rides the system prompt instead of the wire, native enforcement stays off for that provider instance from then on, and the answer is validated locally by the same repair loop (a still-invalid answer fails naming the fallback). Prefer required fields and flat structures. Example: '{"type":"object","properties":{"sentiment":{"type":"string","enum":["pos","neg"]}},"required":["sentiment"]}'.
AgentModelSettings.__strictOutput.doc: Controls what happens when structured output (responseFormat 'json' and/or responseSchema) still fails validation after the bounded repair loop. true (default): the run fails with a clean validation error — the caller NEVER receives schema-violating raw text. false: the raw text is returned with a logged warning (legacy fail-open behavior).
AgentModelSettings.__toolChoice.doc: Controls how the model may use tools on the first call of a run: 'auto' (default — model decides), 'any' (model MUST call some tool), 'none' (tool calling disabled), or the exact name of a tool the model MUST call. Mapped to each provider's native control (openai tool_choice, anthropic tool_choice, google functionCallingConfig.mode, bedrock toolConfig.toolChoice).
AgentModelSettings.__parallelToolCalls.doc: When false, the model is instructed to issue at most ONE tool call per assistant turn (openai parallel_tool_calls:false, anthropic disable_parallel_tool_use). Default: true (parallel tool calls allowed). Providers without a native control ignore this.
AgentModelSettings.__contextWindowTokens.doc: Override of the model's context-window size (in tokens) used by the runtime's context compaction — when the estimated conversation size approaches this window, older turns are compacted (sliding window or summarization per chatSettings). Leave null to use the provider family's default estimate.
AgentModelSettings.__reasoningEffort.doc: Reasoning effort: 'none', 'minimal', 'low', 'medium' or 'high'. OpenAI-family reasoning models (o-series, gpt-5 family) receive it as reasoning_effort. Anthropic models receive it as thinking configuration: adaptive thinking with output_config.effort on current models, a budget_tokens clamped below maxTokens on older ones; unset or 'none' turns thinking off where the model allows it. Other providers ignore it. Leave null for no thinking on Anthropic and the model's own default elsewhere. On a gpt-5 family model whose default effort rejects function tools on chat/completions, a tool-bearing request that the provider refuses for that reason is resent once with reasoning_effort 'none' when this field is null; set it explicitly to choose the effort yourself. Not every model accepts every value (older gpt-5 models do not accept 'none').

__AgentInputSettings.doc: Defines how incoming request data is transformed into the agent's prompt or input. Includes the prompt template (an MScript expression that builds the user message from request body, params, and context), file upload support for vision/audio agents, and dynamic context sources that fetch additional data to enrich the prompt. The legacy autoResize/autoConvert flags were removed (never consumed by any generator) — the migrator drops them from old blueprints.
