AgentInputSettings.__promptTemplate.doc: MScript expression that builds the user message from request data. Has access to 'this.request.body', 'this.request.params', and any context source variables. Example: `{ "js": "this.request.body.message" }` or a template literal combining multiple fields. Plain prose that is not a JS expression is read as a template-literal body, so 'Summarize ${this.request.body.ticket}' interpolates and text without interpolations is sent as written. A template that throws while it is evaluated (for example `${this.request.body.company.id}` on a request whose body has no company - an orchestration step or kafka body of another shape) FAILS the run with a 422 AGENT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_EVAL_FAILED error naming agent.<name>.promptTemplate and the error class (the full evaluation message is written to the service log only, never to the response or the run row); the template source is never sent to the model. A designer-thrown typed 4xx keeps its own status and message, and the run row prefixes the path. An async template (one that returns a Promise, e.g. an awaited LIB call inside an async function) is awaited before any provider call; a rejection is handled exactly like a thrown error. One exception, kept for compatibility: a template that is a single bare word that does not resolve (e.g. Summarize, or session - only this.session is bound) is sent as that literal text; validation warns about it (AGENT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_BARE_IDENTIFIER) - quote it or use a template literal. Words that resolve (request, this, JavaScript/Node globals such as JSON or Math) are evaluated, and reserved words are read as prose. Guard optional fields with ?. / ?? when the agent is invoked with more than one body shape.
AgentInputSettings.__acceptsUpload.doc: When true, the agent's endpoint accepts multipart/form-data with file uploads. A dedicated upload manager middleware is generated to handle validation and temporary storage. NOT required for an audio STT agent: an stt agent ALWAYS gets the upload pipeline, whatever this flag says, because its runtime leg cannot run without audio bytes. Set it for vision (image) agents, or for any other agent that should accept a file. The upload pipeline is served on the agent's own route (`POST <basePath>` and `<basePath>/stream`) only; the agent hub wildcard `POST /agents/:agentName` reads no multipart body.
AgentInputSettings.__maxFiles.doc: Maximum number of files accepted per request. Default: 1. Relevant whenever the agent has an upload pipeline - that is acceptsUpload = true OR an audio STT agent, which gets one regardless. Exceeding it answers 400 TOO_MANY_FILES.
AgentInputSettings.__contextSources.doc: Dynamic data sources fetched at runtime to enrich the user prompt. Each source provides a named variable accessible in the promptTemplate via MScript (e.g. 'this.userProfile.email'); when the agent declares NO promptTemplate the fetched values are appended to the user message as a bounded '[Context]' block. Sources are fetched per run (honoring each source's cacheTtlSeconds); a fetch failure is FAIL-SOFT — the run continues without that variable (logged warning). Use these to inject database records, computed values, or external data into the conversation.

__AgentOutputSettings.doc: Controls how the AI model's response is transformed before returning to the client. Supports extracting a specific property from JSON responses and applying post-processing transformations. The legacy storeTo field (bucket persistence of generated media) was removed — never consumed by any generator; the migrator drops it from old blueprints.

AgentOutputSettings.__responseProperty.doc: When the model returns JSON, extract this property as the response value. Example: 'result' extracts the 'result' field from the model's JSON output. Leave null to return the full response.
AgentOutputSettings.__postProcess.doc: MScript expression to transform the model's output before sending to the client. The raw response is available as 'result'. Example: `{ "js": "result.trim().toUpperCase()" }` or a more complex transformation function.
AgentOutputSettings.__requiresApproval.doc: Draft-then-approve execution mode: when true, the agent's FINAL output is held as a DRAFT — instead of returning (and post-processing) the answer, the run pauses in the 'paused_approval' state with the draft riding the pending-approval entry. An approver (hubSettings.hubBasics.approvalRoles) releases it via the hub approval API: approve delivers the output (postProcess runs at approval time, and for chat agents the conversation history persists then), reject terminates the run with status 'rejected'. The common top-level agent.approvalExpiryDays controls how long this draft may wait; null/unset disables expiry. Default: false.

__AgentToolSettings.doc: Configures which tools the agent can invoke during its execution loop. Only applicable for text and vision modality agents. Tools follow the OpenAI/Anthropic function calling convention. The agent's tool-calling loop continues until the model stops requesting tools or the maxToolCalls guardrail is hit.

AgentToolSettings.__enableCrudTools.doc: When true, auto-generates tool definitions from the service's DataObjects, exposing create/read/update/delete/list operations. Uses the same schema generation as the MCP layer.
AgentToolSettings.__crudScopes.doc: Comma-separated allow-list of DataObject names to expose as CRUD tools. Empty means NO CRUD tools are generated (explicit opt-in per object — the old expose-everything default was removed with the WS2 security floor). Each entry must name a DataObject of the host service (existence-checked at design time). Example: 'User,Order,Product'. A CRUD operation with a matching BusinessApi runs through that api with the CALLER's identity (roles, ownership and `permissionCheck` decided as over REST; a `permissionCheck` api refuses a run with no HTTP caller).
AgentToolSettings.__apiTools.doc: Comma-separated list of BusinessApi names to expose as callable tools. Each API becomes a tool the agent can invoke. Example: 'sendNotification,calculatePrice'. A tool bound to a BusinessApi of the agent's own service runs that api's auth gates for the CALLER, exactly as the same caller's REST call: a `permissionCheck` api is decided by the caller's session manager, and is refused (403) on a run with no HTTP caller (Kafka- or cron-triggered, or resumed). Only a run started by the agent's own HTTP request carries the session manager, so the same refusal applies, even with a real user behind the run, to a Telegram or WhatsApp chat-surface message, the hub's eval suite and a programmatic executeAgent run (an in-process AgentCallAction, the video live pipeline); gate the apis such runs call with checkRoles, absoluteRoles or ownershipCheck.
AgentToolSettings.__m2mTools.doc: Comma-separated SUBSET of apiTools that must execute over a MACHINE (M2M) identity instead of the caller's own. This is the per-tool AUTH ARM declaration and it is the DESIGNER'S security decision — the agent never chooses, is never offered a credential, and cannot widen its own authority by reasoning about it; the arm is resolved from this list before the model is shown the tool. DEFAULT (a name absent here) is the USER arm: the tool call runs under the identity the agent itself is running as — the `actor` carried on the triggering event, or the session of the HTTP caller — so the target BusinessApi's own checkRoles/ownership gates keep deciding exactly as they would for that user calling directly. Name a tool here ONLY when the operation is a background or elevated one the acting user is not entitled to perform (an approval, a moderation verdict, a system reconciliation): the M2M arm carries roleId 'system' and therefore passes NO role gate, so the target api must be reachable over M2M — an entry whose api is not M2M-allowed is a design-time error, and the target service's serviceSettings.serviceOptions.allowedM2MClients still decides whether this project's agent host is an admitted caller. Every entry must also appear in apiTools. Example: apiTools 'getOrder,approveRefund' with m2mTools 'approveRefund'.
AgentToolSettings.__agentTools.doc: Comma-separated list of other AI agent names to expose as tools. Enables cross-agent delegation — a text agent can invoke an image agent to generate visuals. Example: 'imageGenerator,translator'.
AgentToolSettings.__libraryTools.doc: Comma-separated list of service library function names to expose as tools. Each function becomes a callable tool with auto-generated parameter schemas. Example: 'formatCurrency,geocodeAddress'.
AgentToolSettings.__customTools.doc: Custom tool definitions with explicit name, description, JSON Schema parameters, and a handler function reference. Use when you need tools that don't map to existing CRUD, API, or library functions.
AgentToolSettings.__integrationTools.doc: Integration providers to expose as agent tools. Each entry maps a project integration to tool definitions. Explicit method names create individual tools with full JSON Schema parameters. Wildcard '*' creates a single dispatcher tool with a getIntegrationMethodDoc helper for looking up exact signatures on demand.
AgentToolSettings.__approvalRequiredTools.doc: Comma-separated list of TOOL names (as registered on the agent's tool registry) that require HUMAN APPROVAL before they execute. When the model calls one of these tools the run PAUSES in the 'paused_approval' state — persisted ending at the assistant tool-call turn, the tool has NOT fired — and surfaces on the approval API of the service that ran it (GET /agent-runs/pending): the hub's for a run started on the hub, and on nodejs the serving business service's own for a run started on that service's agent route. An approver (hubSettings.hubBasics.approvalRoles) then approves (the tool executes and the run resumes through its tool journal — already-completed tools are never re-executed) or rejects (the model receives a clean rejection tool_result and the run continues without the tool's effect). Use the REGISTERED tool names: CRUD tools are '<op>_<objectName>' (e.g. 'delete_order'), api tools use the BusinessApi name, agent tools are 'invoke_agent_<agentName>', integration tools 'integration_<provider>_<method>' (or 'integration_<provider>' for a wildcard dispatcher), custom and library tools their declared names. The common top-level agent.approvalExpiryDays controls this pause duration, shared with outputSettings.requiresApproval; null/unset disables expiry. Example: 'delete_order,refundPayment,integration_stripe_createRefund'.
AgentToolSettings.__enableBatchApiCall.doc: When true, the agent also gets the built-in `batch_api_call` tool: one tool call that runs up to guardrails.maxToolCalls (default 25, never more than 50) calls of this agent's own apiTools (in-process and cross-service; not CRUD, agent, library, custom or integration tools) in one step, `{ calls: [{ tool, args }], stopOnError? }`, at most 4 at a time. Each inner call runs exactly as a direct call would: under the caller's session, with the same guest, role and required-argument checks, the api's own gates and its `fields` projection, and gets its own `{ index, tool, ok, result | error }` entry. A tool listed in approvalRequiredTools, or one the guardrails.decisionGate covers, cannot run inside a batch (that item is refused, the call is not made); put `batch_api_call` itself in approvalRequiredTools to approve a whole call list at once. Use it for bulk work the user has already confirmed. Node.js only for now. Default: false.

__AgentChatSettings.doc: Conversation history management for chat-mode agents. Controls how messages are stored, truncated, and optionally summarized. Only applicable when executionMode is 'chat'.

AgentChatSettings.__historyStorage.doc: Where conversation history is persisted: 'memory' for in-process storage (fast but lost on restart), 'database' for persistent storage (survives restarts, required for production).
AgentChatSettings.__maxHistoryMessages.doc: Read window of the conversation history: the most recent stored messages read into a new run (turn-aware: the window starts on a user message and never splits a tool call from its result). With historyStorage database nothing is trimmed when a turn is saved: every message stays stored as an appended transcript row, and older messages are only left out of what the next run reads (or folded into a summary if summarizeAfter is set). The in-process memory store still keeps at most this many. Default: 100.
AgentChatSettings.__summarizeAfter.doc: When the conversation exceeds this many messages, the runtime summarizes the OLDER turns (everything except the pinned recent window) into a single context message via the agent's own provider. With historyStorage database the summary is stored as one transcript row and the next turn's history starts at it (the summarized messages stay stored, they are only no longer read); with historyStorage memory the compacted history is saved. Set to 0 to disable summarization and use simple sliding-window truncation instead. Also used as the compaction strategy selector when the estimated conversation size approaches the model's context window. Recommended for chat agents with long tool loops (for example 40): the default 0 only drops the oldest messages once the window is nearly full.
AgentChatSettings.__refreshSystemPrompt.doc: When true, the system message pipeline is re-evaluated on every conversation turn. When false, the system message is built once per runtime instance and cached. Dynamic systemPromptSources (SCHEDULED) will ride the same switch once wired.
AgentChatSettings.__pinnedRecentMessages.doc: Number of most-recent conversation messages that are ALWAYS kept verbatim (never summarized or dropped) during context compaction, in addition to the system prompt. Default: 4.
AgentChatSettings.__maxToolResultCharsInHistory.doc: Cap for tool results in the conversation history a chat agent REPLAYS. When > 0, every tool result of the history is cut to this many characters with the same row-aware truncation as guardrails.maxToolResultChars (a JSON list keeps whole leading rows and a note naming how many were left out). With historyStorage database the cap is applied when a new run READS the history; the stored transcript rows keep the results the run saw. With historyStorage memory it is applied when the turn is saved. The run that produced the results still read them whole; the cap keeps the NEXT turns, which replay the history, from carrying old bulk results. 0 (default) = off.
AgentChatSettings.__retentionDays.doc: Retention window in days for the stored conversations of this chat agent (historyStorage database). A positive integer enables a periodic, single-replica sweep that hard-deletes every conversation whose last activity (its newest message) is older than the window: the session row, every transcript row of the conversation (sys_agentMessage), the conversation's runs with their stored inputs and outputs, the run events of those runs, and the search-index documents of the deleted rows. A conversation with a run that is still running or paused for approval is kept until that run is decided or expires. Every deletion writes an audit record (who or what deleted it, the conversation, the agent, row counts; never message content). Unset or null keeps conversations indefinitely and emits no sweep; new projects get no default, because erasure is the project owner's choice. Users can list and delete their own conversations through the agent's conversation routes independently of this setting. Validation refuses the window when historyStorage is not database (nothing is stored, so nothing can be swept) and, for now, on an agent that a generator other than nodejs or rust emits (the agentHub, an assignedService or the declaring service in java, dotnet, python or golang), because those lanes have no sweep yet.

__AgentOrchestrationSettings.doc: Multi-agent orchestration configuration for orchestrator-mode agents. Defines the execution strategy and the steps to coordinate. Only applicable when executionMode is 'orchestrator'. Steps dispatch as durable, idempotent child runs — see AIAgent.orchestrationSettings.

AgentOrchestrationSettings.__strategy.doc: How steps are executed: 'sequential' runs steps in declaration order (consecutive steps marked parallel form a concurrent group), 'parallel' runs every step concurrently, 'adaptive' exposes each step as a run_step_<name> tool to the orchestrator's own model, which plans/delegates/collates within maxIterations.
AgentOrchestrationSettings.__maxIterations.doc: Safety limit for the orchestrator: in 'adaptive' mode the maximum provider turns of the planner loop; in sequential/parallel mode the maximum total step dispatches. Default: 10.
AgentOrchestrationSettings.__completionCondition.doc: MScript expression evaluated after each completed step (adaptive: after each tool turn). The orchestrator stops early and collates when this evaluates to true. Has access to 'stepResults' (all completed step outputs). Example: `{ "js": "stepResults.validation?.approved === true" }`.
AgentOrchestrationSettings.__orchestrationSteps.doc: The sequence of steps the orchestrator executes. Each step invokes a sub-agent with mapped input, captures its output, and optionally runs conditionally or in parallel with other steps.

__AgentImageSettings.doc: Image generation parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'image'. These settings are passed to the provider's image generation API (e.g., DALL-E, Fal AI).

AgentImageSettings.__size.doc: Output image dimensions. Common values: '1024x1024' (square), '1792x1024' (landscape), '1024x1792' (portrait). Available sizes depend on the provider and model.
AgentImageSettings.__quality.doc: Image quality level: 'standard' for faster/cheaper generation, 'hd' for higher detail. Not all providers support quality control.
AgentImageSettings.__style.doc: Artistic style: 'natural' for realistic output, 'vivid' for hyper-real/dramatic output. Provider-specific.
AgentImageSettings.__count.doc: Number of images to generate per request. Default: 1. Some providers support batch generation.

__AgentAudioSettings.doc: Audio generation or transcription parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'audio'. Supports text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT) directions.

AgentAudioSettings.__direction.doc: The audio processing direction: 'tts' converts text to speech audio, 'stt' converts speech audio to text.
AgentAudioSettings.__voice.doc: Voice identifier for TTS. Provider-specific (e.g., 'alloy', 'echo' for OpenAI; voice IDs for ElevenLabs). Leave null for provider default.
AgentAudioSettings.__outputFormat.doc: Audio output format for TTS: 'mp3', 'wav', 'opus', or 'flac'. Defaults to 'mp3'; the adapters then map that onto each provider's own spelling (ElevenLabs sends 'mp3_44100_128').
AgentAudioSettings.__language.doc: Language code for STT transcription (e.g., 'en', 'tr', 'de'). Leave null for auto-detection.

__AgentVideoSettings.doc: Video generation parameters. Only applicable when modality is 'video'. Video generation is typically asynchronous — the agent polls for completion and streams progress events via SSE.

AgentVideoSettings.__duration.doc: Target video duration in seconds. Available range depends on the provider and model. Common: 4-16 seconds.
AgentVideoSettings.__resolution.doc: Video resolution. Common values: '720p', '1080p'. Higher resolution may cost more and take longer.

__AgentCustomEndpoint.doc: Custom provider endpoint configuration. Only applicable when provider is 'custom'. Allows connecting to any OpenAI-compatible API (self-hosted models, vLLM, Ollama, etc.) or Anthropic-compatible endpoints.

AgentCustomEndpoint.__baseUrl.doc: Base URL of the custom API (e.g., 'https://my-model.example.com/v1' or 'http://localhost:11434/v1').
AgentCustomEndpoint.__apiKeyEnvVar.doc: Name of the environment variable containing the API key for the custom endpoint (e.g., 'CUSTOM_AI_API_KEY'). The key is read from process.env at runtime.
AgentCustomEndpoint.__apiFormat.doc: API format to use: 'openai' for OpenAI-compatible chat completions, 'anthropic' for Anthropic Messages format, 'raw' for full control over request/response shape.

__AgentEndpointSettings.doc: Controls how the agent is exposed as an API endpoint. Each agent can have a REST endpoint (synchronous) and/or an SSE endpoint (streaming). Authentication requirements and path customization are configured here.

AgentEndpointSettings.__hasRestEndpoint.doc: When true, generates a POST REST endpoint at /agents/{name} (or custom basePath). Returns the full response synchronously. False closes the agent's public REST route (user and anonymous callers); an AgentCallAction from another service of the project still reaches the agent on a nodejs agentHub, since that call carries a verified service token.
AgentEndpointSettings.__hasSseEndpoint.doc: When true, generates a POST SSE endpoint at /agents/{name}/stream. Streams tokens (text), progress events (media generation), or step results (orchestrator) in real-time.
AgentEndpointSettings.__basePath.doc: Custom base path override for the agent's endpoints. Default: '/agents/{name}'. Example: '/ai/chat' generates POST /ai/chat and POST /ai/chat/stream.
AgentEndpointSettings.__authRequired.doc: When true, the agent's endpoints require a valid JWT token. Set to false for public-facing agents (e.g., a chatbot widget). A public agent has no per-client or per-IP rate limit and a guest has no user id, so `dailyTokenBudgetPerUser` does not apply: bound it with `dailyCostCeilingUsd` and a rate limit in front of the route.
AgentEndpointSettings.__chatSurfaces.doc: Chat-surface interfaces for the agent - exposes it over messaging apps (Telegram, WhatsApp) alongside the REST/SSE interfaces. Each entry names a CHANNEL PROVIDER (`provider` -> a `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` of kind `whatsapp` (Meta Cloud) or `telegram`); the surface type comes from the provider kind and every credential is the provider's, so one agent reached over Telegram and WhatsApp at once declares two entries naming a telegram and a whatsapp provider. The entry itself only carries the surface-specific binding (the identity strategy + an optional webhook-path override for Telegram + typingIndicator (default on)). A WhatsApp surface has no webhook: Meta calls the provider's one door on the notification service and the agent consumes the provider's inbound messages over Kafka (`<codename>-whatsapp-inbound-message`), replying with the provider's access token, phone number id and Graph API version. A Telegram surface is a webhook of the host service (`/agents/<agent>/telegram/webhook`), verified with the provider's `telegramWebhookSecret` and answered with its `telegramBotToken`. A provider backs at most ONE conversational consumer (an agent surface or an mcpbff exposure); the validator errors on a second one (CHAT_PROVIDER_MULTI_CONSUMER). The retired `chatProvider` (a chat-bot name) is converted on load to `provider`.
AgentEndpointSettings.__surfaces.doc: Declarative surface registry for the agent (docs/ADR-aiagent-chat-surfaces.md 'Surface registry'). ABSENT or EMPTY = implicit mode (fully backward compatible): every surface is enabled by whatever wiring references the agent — REST/SSE from hasRestEndpoint/hasSseEndpoint, telegram/whatsapp from chatSurfaces[], kafka from kafkaControllers[], videoRoom from a room's meetingAgents[]. NON-EMPTY = declared mode: the list is the authority on which surfaces the agent is reachable over — REST/SSE routes, chat webhooks and kafka listeners are emitted only for declared surfaces, and the validator requires each declared surface's prerequisites (telegram/whatsapp need a chatSurfaces[] entry bound to a provider of that kind, kafka needs an enabled kafkaController, videoRoom needs a videoRooms[].meetingAgents[] reference in the service the agent deploys to). Wiring present for an UNdeclared surface is warned and suppressed (videoRoom: errored on the room, since its emission is room-driven). On the agentHub service the declared list also binds the hub wildcard routes: POST /agents/:agentName answers 404 (the same body as an unknown agent) for an agent whose list leaves out 'rest', and POST /agents/:agentName/stream for one that leaves out 'sse', so a kafka-only agent (surfaces ['kafka']) cannot be run by a signed-in caller over REST or SSE; the role-gated eval suite (fixed evalCases) still runs. In implicit mode the hub derives the same list from the legacy flags: hasRestEndpoint false leaves out 'rest' and hasSseEndpoint false leaves out 'sse', so those wildcard routes answer the same 404 (an implicit-mode agent with both flags on is served). These refusals govern PUBLIC exposure (user and anonymous callers): a call from another service of the project (an AgentCallAction, or any InterService call) carries an x-m2m-token, and a token the hub verifies and its caller lists admit runs any design-time agent on POST /agents/:agentName whatever its surfaces (the stream route and dynamic agents keep their rule). The agentHub service's own AgentCallActions run an agent it deploys without 'rest' in-process. An agentHub generated in java, dotnet or python still refuses such a service call, and an AgentCallAction that reaches such an agent over that hub is warned (AGENT_CALL_SURFACE_NOT_REST).

__AgentSurfaceType.doc.#: A surface an agent is reachable over. Only surfaces with real generated wiring are enumerated — a value is added here when its wiring lands, not before.
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.rest: Synchronous POST endpoint at basePath (agent-router). Implicit driver: endpointSettings.hasRestEndpoint (default true).
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.sse: Streaming POST endpoint at basePath/stream (agent-router). Implicit driver: endpointSettings.hasSseEndpoint (default true).
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.telegram: Telegram chat surface (webhook + inline sender). Prerequisite: a chatSurfaces[] entry referencing a telegram bot.
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.whatsapp: WhatsApp chat surface (a Kafka consumer of the WhatsApp provider's inbound messages + inline Meta-Cloud sender; the webhook door is the provider's, on the notification service). Prerequisite: a chatSurfaces[] entry referencing a whatsapp bot that names a WhatsApp provider.
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.videoRoom: Live video-room surface — the agent joins rooms as a meeting agent (video-layer live pipeline). Prerequisite: a videoRooms[].meetingAgents[] entry referencing the agent in the service it deploys to (its own service, or its assignedService for hub agents).
__AgentSurfaceType.doc.kafka: Event surface — synthetic requests from kafka topics. Prerequisite: at least one enabled kafkaControllers[] entry.

__ChatSurfaceType.doc.#: The messaging app a chat surface binds the agent to.
__ChatSurfaceType.doc.telegram: Telegram Bot API. Inbound updates carry a stable from.id but no phone unless the user shares it — defaults to the 'link' identity strategy.
__ChatSurfaceType.doc.whatsapp: WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API / Twilio). Inbound messages carry the sender's E.164 phone — defaults to the 'phone' identity strategy.

__ChatSurfaceIdentityStrategy.doc.#: How a chat surface resolves an inbound message's surfaceUserId to an application user.
__ChatSurfaceIdentityStrategy.doc.link: Explicit account-link only — the user runs a short-lived link code (minted by linkChatSurface) from an authenticated in-app session. The only path that works when the surface redacts the phone (Telegram).
__ChatSurfaceIdentityStrategy.doc.phone: Auto-bind via the ES read-model — the channel-asserted phone is matched against an existing user (HexaAuth.getUserByIdentity) and sys_chatIdentity is written lazily. Suitable for surfaces that expose a trustworthy phone (WhatsApp).

__ChatSurfaceSettings.doc: Binds a chat consumer (an aiAgent, or the mcpbff assistant through `mcpbffSettings.chatSurfaces[]`) to one messaging surface by naming a CHANNEL PROVIDER. The provider (`projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[]`, kind `whatsapp` with provider `whatsapp`, or kind `telegram`) supplies the surface type and ALL credentials (WhatsApp: whatsappAccessToken / whatsappPhoneNumberId / whatsappApiVersion / whatsappApiBase / whatsappAppSecret / whatsappVerifyToken; Telegram: telegramBotToken / telegramWebhookSecret), read at runtime from NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER_<PROVIDER>_<key>; this entry only carries the surface-specific binding - the identity strategy, an optional Telegram webhook-path override and the typingIndicator activity preference (default on). Outbound replies are sent with the provider's credentials only; a WhatsApp reply posts through the provider's Graph API version (the adapter default v20.0 when unset). The retired `chatProvider` (a chat-bot name) is converted on load.

ChatSurfaceSettings.__provider.doc: Name of the channel provider this surface binds to - must match a `projectSettings.notificationProvidersSettings.notificationProviders[].name` whose kind is `whatsapp` (provider `whatsapp`, Meta Cloud) or `telegram`. The provider's kind IS the surface type and its configuration holds every credential. Also the asset identifier within the chatSurfaces list. Validation: a missing or unknown provider, or one of another kind, is an error (CHAT_SURFACE_PROVIDER_UNBOUND); a provider bound by two conversational consumers (two agent surfaces, or an agent surface and an mcpbff exposure) is an error (CHAT_PROVIDER_MULTI_CONSUMER).
ChatSurfaceSettings.__chatProvider.doc: RETIRED (patterns 1.60.0). The legacy chat-bot name. A surface still carrying it is converted on load: the bot's provider becomes `provider` and this field is dropped. Leave it null.
ChatSurfaceSettings.__webhookPath.doc: TELEGRAM only — optional override of the webhook path the provider calls to deliver inbound messages. Default: a per-consumer distinct path, /agents/{agent}/telegram/webhook for an aiAgent surface and /chat/{provider}/webhook for an mcpbff exposure (so several Telegram surfaces on one service never collide). The path serves POST only (inbound receive); Telegram has no GET verification handshake, and the secret token header is checked on each POST. A WhatsApp surface has NO webhook of its own: Meta calls the WhatsApp provider's one door `/v1/whatsapp-webhooks/meta/<providerName>` on the notification service and the agent consumes the provider's inbound messages over Kafka; a value set here for a whatsapp surface is ignored (the validator warns).
ChatSurfaceSettings.__identityStrategy.doc: How inbound senders are resolved to an application user: 'link' (explicit link-code only) or 'phone' (auto-bind via the channel-asserted phone). Defaults to 'link' on EVERY surface, WhatsApp included — phone auto-bind is an explicit opt-in, which is what the agent-hub prompt doc promises. The per-surface fallback some generators still carry (telegram → 'link', whatsapp → 'phone') is therefore unreachable from a hydrated ChatSurfaceSettings, and now also unreachable for a present-but-null key (the validator writes the declared default back into the raw config); it survives only where a generator reads a RAW blueprint whose key is OMITTED entirely. Removing that dead fallback is tracked as follow-up work.
ChatSurfaceSettings.__typingIndicator.doc: Show best-effort activity while the agent or MCP BFF assistant runs. Enabled by default (including null/unset); false disables it. WhatsApp marks the inbound message id read and requests typing_indicator type text, refreshing every 20 seconds; Telegram sends sendChatAction typing every 4 seconds. Both use only the channel provider credentials and stop refreshing on reply or failure. Status-call errors are logged safely and never delay or fail the turn. WhatsApp dismisses its indicator on reply or after approximately 25 seconds.

__AgentGuardrails.doc: Safety limits and cost controls for the agent. Prevents runaway costs, excessive tool usage, and enforces input/output validation. These limits are enforced at runtime by the agent execution loop.

AgentGuardrails.__maxToolCalls.doc: Maximum number of tool invocations allowed per request. Prevents infinite tool-calling loops. Default: 25.
AgentGuardrails.__maxTokenBudget.doc: Maximum total tokens (input + output) allowed per request, cumulative across every provider call of the run (tool loop + structured-output repair loop). Enforced by the runtime from provider usage feedback (estimates where the provider reports none). The gate is PRE-CALL. On the FIRST call of a run (nothing produced yet) an over-budget estimate is refused before any spend with a typed 429 problem+json (errorCode AGENT_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXCEEDED) carrying the budget and the usage. Once the run has produced at least one model turn, reaching the budget FINISHES the run gracefully instead of aborting it: no further model turn is issued (tool calls the last model turn already requested still complete, so the conversation stays well-formed), and the run returns, on the same surfaces as a normal finish (the API response data, the SSE done event, the execution row output), a partial result { truncated: true, truncatedReason: 'tokenBudget', partial: <the last assistant text or null>, tokenBudget: { budget, used, estimated } } (plus validationErrors when the budget ran out before a structured-output or outputValidation repair turn; such a partial is never passed to outputValidation and never reported as a validation failure). The partial text is NOT schema-validated, responseProperty does not apply to it, and postProcess is skipped; the requiredToolCalls gate and the output approval hold still apply. An overshoot discovered only AFTER a provider call returned does not discard the finished answer: it is recorded and warned, and the run finishes before its next model turn. The daily per-user / per-tenant ceilings are separate guardrails and keep refusing with their own 429. Prevents excessive cost on a single request.
AgentGuardrails.__maxToolResultChars.doc: Maximum size (in characters of the serialized result) a single tool result may occupy in the conversation. Larger results are truncated with an elision marker before being fed back to the model — a runaway list/query result cannot blow the context window. Default: 16000.
AgentGuardrails.__elideToolResultsAfter.doc: Tool-result elision, by count. When > 0, before EACH provider call of a run the runtime keeps the newest N tool results whole and replaces the content of every older one with a one-line stub (`[result of listOrders elided: 140 rows, 58213 chars; call the tool again if you need it]`). The tool_result itself stays in place (same tool-use id), so every tool call keeps its answer and no provider rejects the sequence; the results of the latest tool turn are never elided, and a stub is never re-elided. Use it on agents whose turns read large lists: each provider call re-sends every earlier result, so without elision the input of a long tool loop grows superlinearly. Combine with elideToolResultsOverChars to elide only the large ones. The elided conversation is also what the run checkpoints and a chat agent stores as history. The SSE client and the run event log still receive the full results. 0 (default) = off: the provider payload is unchanged.
AgentGuardrails.__elideToolResultsOverChars.doc: Tool-result elision, by size. When > 0, only an older tool result longer than this many characters is replaced with its one-line stub (see elideToolResultsAfter). With elideToolResultsAfter at 0, every result before the latest tool turn is a candidate; with both set, a result is elided when it is older than the newest N AND longer than this. 0 (default) = off.
AgentGuardrails.__maxFileSizeMb.doc: Maximum file size in MB for uploaded files. Enforced by the upload manager middleware.
AgentGuardrails.__timeout.doc: Maximum execution time in milliseconds for a single agent request. Includes all tool calls and provider API calls. Default: 120000 (2 minutes).
AgentGuardrails.__maxAgentDepth.doc: Maximum agent-as-tool recursion depth. A direct caller (REST/SSE/kafka/internal) runs at depth 0; every sub-agent invocation (invoke_agent_* tools, orchestration steps) adds 1. Bounds cyclic/self-referential agent chains. Default: 3.
AgentGuardrails.__inputValidation.doc: MScript expression that validates the request input BEFORE any provider call. Return true to allow; false or a string error message to reject — a rejection is a clean 4xx-style error (statusCode 422), no tokens are spent and no run starts. Has access to 'this.request.body' / 'this.session', to 'this.source' and to 'this.onBehalfOf'. 'this.source' is the entry point the FRAMEWORK started the run from - 'rest' (the agent's REST route or the hub wildcard POST /agents/:agentName), 'sse' (a /stream route), 'kafka' (a kafkaControllers[] listener), 'eval' (the hub eval suite), 'internal' (programmatic executeAgent, e.g. an in-process AgentCallAction), 'telegram' / 'whatsapp' (chat surfaces), 'agent' / 'agent-tool' (an orchestration step or sub-agent tool). It is set from the route or listener that started the run and is never read from the request body or headers, so a body or header field named 'source' cannot set it: `this.source === 'kafka'` is a trustworthy gate for an event-only agent. 'this.onBehalfOf' is the identity a run acts for when it is NOT the run's session - on a Kafka run the event author ({ userId, roleId?, roles?, tenantId? } from the envelope actor; the run's session is the minted system session) - as data only, null on every other run. An expression that THROWS fails closed (the request is rejected with the evaluation error logged).
AgentGuardrails.__outputValidation.doc: MScript expression that validates the model's final output before returning/persisting. Return true to allow; false or a string to flag. Has access to 'result' (and 'this.request'). On failure: when modelSettings.strictOutput is true (default) the validation feedback is fed back to the model ONCE for repair, and a still-failing answer aborts the run with a clean error; when strictOutput is false the original output is returned with a logged annotation (AgentOutputValidationFailed). When guardrails.maxTokenBudget is reached before or inside that repair turn, the run finishes with the token-budget partial result (truncated: true, validationErrors) instead of a validation error.
AgentGuardrails.__dailyTokenBudgetPerUser.doc: Maximum total tokens (input + output) a single userId may consume per UTC day before this agent refuses to run for it. The tally is the service's: the in-process daily ledger is keyed by the userId and the UTC day only, so the provider usage of every agent of the same service process under that userId counts toward it. The userId is the run's SESSION identity: a Kafka-triggered run executes under the minted system session, so it is charged to that controller's system scope ('system:kafka:<agent>.<controller>', one shared daily bucket per controller), never to the event author's budget. Enforced BEFORE every provider call from the in-process daily ledger fed by real provider usage (the per-replica floor — cross-replica exactness is a deployment concern, like the run coordinator's session lock). Exceeding denies with a clean 429-style error before any further spend. Null = no per-user daily ceiling.
AgentGuardrails.__dailyCostCeilingUsd.doc: Maximum estimated spend in USD per tenant per UTC day before this agent refuses to run (single-tenant projects, and tenant-less runs, use one global bucket). The tally is the service's: the in-process daily ledger is keyed by the tenant and the UTC day only, so by default the spend of every agent of the same service process in that tenant (or project) counts toward it; set costCeilingScope to 'agent' to compare it with this agent's own spend only. It is the guard that bounds a Kafka-triggered agent's daily spend, because its token budget is one shared bucket per controller. Cost is computed per provider call from the model price table — a versioned, dated built-in table (input, output, prompt-cache read and write prices per model, so cached prompt tokens are billed at their own rates), overridden by the blueprint's projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.modelPrices entries and then by the AGENT_MODEL_PRICES env var (JSON map of model key → { inputPerMTok, outputPerMTok, cacheReadPerMTok, cacheWritePerMTok }), which merges last. The figure is an approximation from list prices. A model that matches no entry is priced by the '*' fallback (3/15 USD per 1M input/output tokens) and its cost is marked estimated: the runtime warns once per such model, the budget refusal names the model and the fallback, and validation warns (AGENT_COST_CEILING_UNPRICED_MODEL) when this ceiling is set on a model with no price entry. Enforced at the same deny-before-checkpoint seam as the token budgets; run records carry the accumulated tokenUsage.costUsd. Null = no cost ceiling. The hub eval runner (POST /agents/{name}/eval) runs an agent's evalSettings.evalCases only when this ceiling is declared (a value >= 0): eval cases are real runs charged to the calling approver's tenant, and this is their per-tenant bound.
AgentGuardrails.__costCeilingScope.doc: Which spend guardrails.dailyCostCeilingUsd is compared with. 'project' (the default, also when empty) compares it with the combined spend of all agents of the service process in the project, or in the caller's tenant on a multi-tenant project, so other agents' spend can exhaust this agent's ceiling. 'agent' keeps a ledger per agent (per tenant on a multi-tenant project) and compares the ceiling with this agent's own spend, calls in flight included. The refusal names the scope and the spend it counted.
AgentGuardrails.__logPreviewChars.doc: Redaction control for the tool-call AUDIT TRAIL (every tool execution logs an AgentToolCallAudit entry: who/what/tenant/cost/traceId). 0 (default) = WS2 posture: metadata and byte sizes only, no payload content. > 0 = include argument/result previews truncated to this many characters: every preview first goes through the framework log redaction (the request-log credential vocabulary, including tokens, client secrets, m2m and session-token names and credentials inside string values or plain text), then logMaskFields is masked; a preview that cannot be redacted is omitted.
AgentGuardrails.__logMaskFields.doc: Comma-separated field names that are masked ('***') at ANY depth inside audit-trail previews when logPreviewChars > 0. Case-insensitive. Built-in always-masked names: password, token, secret, apiKey, authorization, accessToken. These masks are applied on top of the framework log redaction every preview already runs, so list only project-specific names. Example: 'ssn,cardNumber,iban'.
AgentGuardrails.__allowedMimeTypes.doc: Comma-separated list of allowed MIME types for file uploads. Example: 'image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp' for vision agents. Each entry is an exact 'type/subtype', a family wildcard 'type/*' (so 'image/*' accepts every image subtype) or '*/*'; matching is case-insensitive and ignores ';' parameters, and any other shape fails generation naming the agent and the entry. Enforced by the upload manager.
AgentGuardrails.__requiredToolCalls.doc: Comma-separated list of TOOL names (as registered on the agent's tool registry - exact, case-sensitive) that MUST each have at least one SUCCESSFUL call in the run's own tool-call journal before the run may end 'success'. Enforced at the run FINISH path from the RUNTIME's journal (the per-run tool record persisted on sys_agentExecutions), never from the model's self-report: a run whose journal lacks a successful call to every listed tool ends 'failed' with an error naming ALL missing tools (code AGENT_REQUIRED_TOOL_NOT_CALLED). A call that returned an error, was rejected by a human approver, or was skipped does NOT satisfy the gate; a run that fails for any other reason keeps its own error (the gate only turns would-be successes into failures). Empty/absent = no mandated tools (default - nothing changes). Each entry must name a tool this agent's toolSettings actually registers (crud op names like 'create_order', apiTool names, invoke_agent_*, library/custom tool names, integration_* tools) - checked at design time (AGENT_REQUIRED_TOOL_NOT_REGISTERED). Use for agents whose job ends in a mandatory write: e.g. 'applyReplyAnalysis' on an agent whose entire purpose is that one write - the write skipped can no longer end green.
AgentGuardrails.__decisionGate.doc: An optional calibrated decision gate over this agent's tool calls (AgentDecisionGate). Null = no gate, and the agent behaves exactly as before. Where `inputValidation` answers a question MScript can express about the whole request, this answers one it cannot about a single tool call - is this about to destroy something - and routes the call to deny, human approval, or a warning.

__AgentDecisionGateAction.doc: What happens to a tool call the gate judges unsafe, and - with the same vocabulary - what happens when the decision provider fails instead of answering. `deny` returns a typed refusal to the model loop so the agent can choose another tool; it does NOT abort the run, because a run-level abort is what the other guardrails are for and an agent that can self-correct should be allowed to. `requireApproval` routes the call into the EXISTING human-in-the-loop seam (the run pauses in `paused_approval`, as `toolSettings.approvalRequiredTools` already does) rather than inventing a second approval queue. `warn` records the verdict in the audit trail and lets the call through - for measuring a policy against real traffic before enforcing it.
__AgentDecisionGate.doc: A calibrated decision gate over an agent's tool calls. Declared on `guardrails.decisionGate`, it asks the bound decision provider about each tool call BEFORE the tool runs, with the tool name and its arguments as the state. It answers the question an MScript `inputValidation` cannot: is this particular call about to do damage. The gate runs after the static `toolSettings.approvalRequiredTools` check, so a call that would pause for approval anyway never costs a provider request, and before the tool registry's own guest and role guards; a denied call returns a typed refusal to the model loop rather than aborting the run. It is NOT an authorization check - it judges the ACTION, never the caller's right to act, and the verdict never reaches a permissionCheck.

AgentDecisionGate.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry that judges this agent's tool calls. Required when the gate is declared.
AgentDecisionGate.__model.doc: Optional PINNED model version for the gate's decisions, overriding the provider entry's. A floating tag is refused (DECISION_MODEL_NOT_PINNED): a gate whose model can change answers differently on two days, and a tool call allowed yesterday and denied today with no code change is the hardest kind of agent behaviour to debug. The model reaches the provider call; the gate audit records the model that actually answered. Null inherits the provider entry.
AgentDecisionGate.__questions.doc:
The questions asked about each tool call. The STATE is built by the framework - the tool name plus its arguments - not by the designer, because the gate must see exactly what is about to execute. All questions ride ONE provider request, so asking several (destructive? exfiltrates data? touches production?) costs barely more than one.

Every gate question must be a `noul`: a statement about the call ('this call deletes data the user did not ask to delete') whose AFFIRMATIVE probability the gate thresholds at 0.5. A `choice` or `score` question is refused (AGENT_DECISION_GATE_QUESTION_NOT_NOUL) because its answer is an option key or a level on a scale, and neither has an "unsafe" reading - state each concern as its own noul instead.

Write the instructions for YOUR project. Measured in testing: `git stash` was answered as not destructive, which is defensible since a stash is recoverable - and in one repository a bare `git stash` is banned for having destroyed a lane's uncommitted work. Both readings are right for different repositories, so a shipped universal tool-safety bundle would be wrong for most of them.
AgentDecisionGate.__confidenceThreshold.doc: Confidence at or above which the gate's verdict is acted on. Below it the call is treated as failing the gate and follows `onGateFail`, because a gate that is unsure must not be the thing that lets a destructive call through. Must sit outside the provider's advertised `probabilityDriftBand` of the 0.5 boundary (DECISION_THRESHOLD_IN_DRIFT_BAND): the probability is not reproducible across identical requests, so a threshold inside the band would allow a tool call on one run and deny the identical one on the next.
AgentDecisionGate.__onGateFail.doc: What happens when the gate judges the call unsafe (AgentDecisionGateAction). Default `deny`.
AgentDecisionGate.__onProviderError.doc: What happens when the decision provider fails instead of answering. Default `deny` - a guard that fails open is not a guard, and this is the one place in the decision family where no other posture is defensible by default. `warn` is available for a gate being trialled, and makes the fail-open choice explicit rather than implicit.
AgentDecisionGate.__appliesToTools.doc: Comma-separated tool names the gate judges. Null or empty = EVERY tool the agent can call, which is the safe default: a gate that covers only the tools somebody remembered to list is the failure mode this field invites. Narrow it only to spare the latency on tools that cannot do harm.
AgentDecisionGate.__exemptTools.doc: Comma-separated tool names the gate never judges, applied after `appliesToTools`. Use for the read-only tools an agent calls constantly, where the gate's 250-400 ms would dominate the run for no safety gain.

__AgentKafkaController.doc: Defines a Kafka-triggered controller for the AI agent. When enabled, a KafkaListener is created that subscribes to the specified topic. Incoming messages are mapped to the agent's request format using the dataMapping expression, then the agent is executed under a minted SYSTEM session (roleId 'system', userId 'system:kafka:<agent>.<controller>', in the event's tenant). The event author (the envelope actor) is never the run's session and the run is not charged to the author's dailyTokenBudgetPerUser; the author is kept as onBehalfOf data (guardrails.inputValidation this.onBehalfOf, tool handlers' ctx.onBehalfOf, request.onBehalfOf). A controller can decline events that are not its own - an optional condition that evaluates falsy, or a declared dataMapping that returns null - and a declined event is skipped (no run, no retry, no dead-letter). Optionally, the agent's response can be published to a response topic. Multiple controllers can be defined per agent for different topics with different data mappings.

AgentKafkaController.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this Kafka controller within the agent. Used in generated code and log correlation. Must be camelCase. For services resolved to Java, authored Kafka listener names and group IDs are limited to 249 Unicode code points; longer values are refused at design time before Spring listener startup. This Java-specific bound does not refuse other service languages or unresolved contexts.
AgentKafkaController.__topic.doc: Kafka topic to subscribe to, written as the full topic name. When a message arrives on this topic, the agent is executed with the mapped data. There is no alias syntax: a string such as 'order.created' is subscribed under exactly that name, and validation warns KAFKA_TOPIC_UNKNOWN_PRODUCER when nothing in the project publishes it. The only rewrite is the project scope: a topic a PublishEventAction of this project authors, or a framework topic of this project written without its `<projectCodename>-` prefix, is consumed under the prefixed wire name. `getKafkaEventTopicsOfService` lists the exact names.
AgentKafkaController.__groupId.doc: Optional Kafka consumer group ID. If not specified, a default group ID is generated from the service codename and controller name. Use a custom group ID for shared consumption across service instances. For services resolved to Java, authored Kafka listener names and group IDs are limited to 249 Unicode code points; longer values are refused at design time before Spring listener startup. This Java-specific bound does not refuse other service languages or unresolved contexts.
AgentKafkaController.__dataMapping.doc: MScript expression that transforms the incoming Kafka message into the agent's request body. Has access to 'message' (parsed JSON payload), 'session' (the minted SYSTEM session the run executes under: roleId 'system', userId 'system:kafka:<agent>.<controller>', the event's tenant; the event author is message.actor and reaches the agent as onBehalfOf, never as the session), 'topic' (topic name), and 'headers' (Kafka message headers). Should return an object matching the agent's expected input shape (e.g., { message: message.text, context: message.metadata }). A declared mapping (any authored source, the literal `null` included) whose RESULT is null or undefined DECLINES the event: the agent is not run, nothing is retried or dead-lettered, the event is marked processed and an info-level AgentKafkaEventSkipped log (reason 'dataMapping') is written - so 'return null' is the way a mapping says 'this event is not mine'. An object result with at least one field, EVERY field undefined (the shape an unconditional mapping produces when the envelope does not carry the fields it reads; JSON drops undefined keys, so it would reach the agent as an empty input), also declines on the Node.js service target, under its own reason 'dataMappingEmpty' with the undefined field names in the skip log's emptyFields - that is how a malformed or foreign envelope stays distinguishable from a deliberate filter (reason 'dataMapping'). A field set to null, a literal {} and an array are bodies and run. When the dataMapping PROPERTY itself is left null (not authored), NO mapping runs and the listener forwards the envelope's payload — `message.data ?? message` — as the request body, so an UNMAPPED controller's input fields are addressed BARE (read scope 'record'), exactly opposite to the mapped form described next. IMPORTANT — a declared dataMapping is read scope 'envelope': it is the one built-in Kafka consumer the framework does NOT unwrap for you, because the MScript is evaluated over the WHOLE raw wire message. And EVERY framework-raised event is a unified ENVELOPE — db-level, API-level AND explicit PublishEventAction messages alike, since ServicePublisher wraps its `data` argument unconditionally with no kind-dependent branch: `{ id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data, old? }`, where `data` is `{ _type, ...record }` for a db/API event and the authored message object for a PublishEventAction topic. The payload ALWAYS rides under `data` — map fields as `message.data.field` (e.g. `message.data.status`), never from the envelope root (`message.type` is the domain fact like `user.created`, not your object's field); the pre-change row of an update is under `message.old`. Do NOT carry this `data.` prefix to other consumer surfaces: an EventNotification `targetPathInData` and a Kafka-triggered BusinessApi's `requestParameters[].dataPath` are read scope 'record' — the framework unwrapped `event.data` for them — and must use the bare key. Events carry no session and no HTTP status — `message.actor.userId` is the minimal identity. Use the `getKafkaEventPayloadStructure` tool to see the exact per-topic shape. IMPORTANT — the mapping must be a SINGLE EXPRESSION: statement sequences like 'if (…) { return {…}; } return null;' do not compile in the generated listener. For conditional logic use an inline function — '() => { if (…) { return {…}; } return null; }' or '(message, session, topic, headers) => ({ … })' — which the Node.js service target invokes with (message, session, topic, headers); unannotated function parameters are auto-annotated ': any' at codegen so both forms compile under the generated service's strict tsconfig (other language targets are being brought to inline-function parity). On the Node.js service target, a Promise or thenable mapping result is awaited before decline checks and before the request body reaches the agent. Async inline-function forms and bare API calls can return the body asynchronously. Top-level 'await' remains unsupported; place it inside an async function expression. A rejected mapping fails the Kafka handler like a synchronous mapping error. Root identifiers may use those four bindings, generated service bindings such as API, and JS/Node globals such as process, URL and crypto; unknown roots fail validation with MSCRIPT_UNKNOWN_ROOT_BINDING.
AgentKafkaController.__condition.doc: Optional MScript predicate that decides whether this controller handles an incoming event at all. It is evaluated for every message BEFORE the dataMapping and BEFORE any agent run, with the same four bindings as dataMapping: 'message' (the WHOLE raw wire message - the unified event envelope, so read the payload as message.data.field), 'session', 'topic' and 'headers'; the inline-function form '(message, session, topic, headers) => ...' is invoked with them positionally. A truthy result runs the controller exactly as if no condition were declared. A falsy result DECLINES the event: the dataMapping is not evaluated, no agent run starts (no sys_agentExecutions row), nothing is retried or published to the dead-letter topic, the event is marked processed for dedup, and an info-level AgentKafkaEventSkipped log with reason 'condition' is written. Use it on a shared topic where only some events belong to this agent (e.g. message.data.contentType === 'invoice'). Must be a single synchronous expression: an async function form is refused at validation (AGENT_KAFKA_CONDITION_ASYNC), and a condition that returns a Promise at runtime throws instead of being read as truthy. An authored literal source counts as declared - `null` or `false` declines every event, only an untouched (all-null) slot means no condition. A condition that THROWS is an error of the controller (logged by the Kafka listener, the event is not marked processed), not a decline. Null = every event is handled. A guardrails.inputValidation refusal is NOT a decline: it still fails the run (once, without retries) and dead-letters it.
AgentKafkaController.__enabled.doc: Set to true to activate this Kafka controller. When false, the listener is not created during service startup. Default is true.
AgentKafkaController.__concurrency.doc: Maximum number of agent runs this controller executes AT ONCE on one service replica. Default 1: the controller handles one message at a time, and the next message is delivered only after the current run has finished and its offset is committed (a topic created by the framework has KAFKA_DEFAULT_PARTITIONS partitions, default 1, so one replica sees every message; more replicas in the same group only help when the topic has more partitions). Above 1, the Node.js listener consumes in batches and runs up to this many messages of a batch in parallel: the committed offset only moves past messages that have finished together with every earlier one, messages that carry the same Kafka key still run one after another, and after a crash the group resumes at the first unfinished message; a message that had already finished beyond it is redelivered and recognised as a duplicate by the run guard, so it is not run again. Every per-run guard (condition, dataMapping, maxTokenBudget, timeout) applies to each run, and the daily token budget and cost ceiling reserve each provider call's estimated cost before it is made, so runs in flight together cannot overspend them. The trade-off is cost and load: N runs in flight spend N times as fast and put N times the load on the model provider (also capped process-wide by AGENT_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY, default 4, so a value above it only queues more runs on the provider slots) and on the tools the agent calls. The alternatives without this setting are sharding the work over several topics, each with its own controller, or running more replicas on a topic with more partitions. Range 1 to 64.
AgentKafkaController.name: String

__AgentContextSource.doc: Defines a dynamic data source that fetches context at runtime. Used in both systemPromptSources (injected into the system message) and contextSources (injected into the user prompt). Each source produces a named variable accessible via MScript in templates.

AgentContextSource.__name.doc: Variable name used to reference this source's data in MScript templates. Example: if name is 'userProfile', access it as 'userProfile.email' in the promptTemplate.
AgentContextSource.__sourceType.doc: How data is fetched: 'dataObject' queries a DataObject, 'libraryFunction' calls a library function, 'apiCall' invokes a BusinessApi or external endpoint.
AgentContextSource.__config.doc: Source-specific configuration as an MScript expression evaluated per fetch (access to 'this.request' / 'this.session'). It must return: for 'dataObject' → { object: '<DataObjectName>', query: {...}, list?: boolean } (runs get<Object>ByQuery / list); for 'libraryFunction' → { function: '<moduleName>', args?: [...] } (calls the service library function); for 'apiCall' → { url: 'https://…', method?, headers?, body?, timeoutMs? } (bounded HTTP fetch, JSON parsed when possible). A missing config makes the source unfetchable — flagged at design time.
AgentContextSource.name: String
AgentContextSource.__cacheTtlSeconds.doc: Cache the fetched value for this many seconds (per runtime instance). 0 or null = no caching: contextSources re-fetch every run; systemPromptSources re-fetch whenever the system message pipeline re-evaluates (see chatSettings.refreshSystemPrompt).

__AgentCustomTool.doc: Defines a custom tool that the agent can invoke during its execution loop. Custom tools are used when existing CRUD, API, or library tools are not sufficient. Each tool has a name, description (shown to the AI), a JSON Schema defining its parameters, and a handler pointing to a library function.

AgentCustomTool.__name.doc: Tool name as exposed to the AI model. Should be descriptive and unique within the agent's tool set. Example: 'searchProducts', 'sendEmail'.
AgentCustomTool.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what the tool does. This text is included in the tool definition sent to the AI model and helps it decide when to use the tool.
AgentCustomTool.__parameters.doc: JSON Schema defining the tool's input parameters. The AI model uses this schema to generate valid arguments. Example: '{"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"}},"required":["query"]}'. Validated at design time: must parse to a structurally valid JSON Schema object with a root type of 'object'.
AgentCustomTool.__handler.doc: Name of the service library function that implements the tool — e.g. 'searchProducts' (a `library.functions[].moduleName`). A leading 'lib.' prefix is accepted and stripped by the codegen. The function receives the parsed parameters as its argument.
AgentCustomTool.name: String

__AgentIntegrationToolConfig.doc: Configures an integration provider as a tool source for the agent. Explicit method names (comma-separated) create individual tools with full JSON Schema parameters. Wildcard '*' creates a single dispatcher tool per integration plus a shared getIntegrationMethodDoc helper for looking up exact method signatures on demand.

AgentIntegrationToolConfig.__integrationName.doc: The provider key of the integration (e.g., 'stripe', 'amazonS3'). Must match a provider added to the project's integrations.
AgentIntegrationToolConfig.__methods.doc: Comma-separated list of method names to expose as individual tools, or '*' to register a single dispatcher tool with a documentation lookup helper. Examples: 'createCustomer,getPaymentIntent' or '*'.

__AgentOrchestrationStep.doc: Defines a single step in an orchestrator agent's workflow. Each step invokes a sub-agent with mapped input and captures its output. Steps can be conditional and can run in parallel with other steps.

AgentOrchestrationStep.__name.doc: Unique step identifier within the orchestration workflow. Used in logging, progress events, and result references.
AgentOrchestrationStep.__agentName.doc: Name of the sub-agent to invoke for this step. Either a local agent name (an AIAgent of the same service / the agent hub — checked against the declared agents at design time) or 'serviceName:agentName' for CROSS-SERVICE delegation: the step is dispatched over the signed inter-service path (x-m2m-token) to that service's /agents/<agentName> route, with the supervisor's originKey forwarded so retries stay idempotent.
AgentOrchestrationStep.__inputMapping.doc: MScript expression that prepares the input for the sub-agent. Has access to 'this.request' (original request) and 'stepResults' (outputs from previously completed steps). Example: `{ "js": "{ message: stepResults.research.summary }" }`.
AgentOrchestrationStep.__outputMapping.doc: MScript expression that transforms the sub-agent's output before storing it in stepResults. Has access to 'result' (the sub-agent's raw response). Example: `{ "js": "result.choices[0].message.content" }`.
AgentOrchestrationStep.__condition.doc: MScript expression evaluated before executing this step. The step is skipped if it evaluates to false. Has access to 'stepResults'. Example: `{ "js": "stepResults.triage?.needsReview === true" }`.
AgentOrchestrationStep.__parallel.doc: When true, this step can run concurrently with other parallel steps. Sequential steps wait for all preceding parallel steps to complete before running.
AgentOrchestrationStep.name: String

__AgentEvalSettings.doc: Declarable evaluation suite for the agent. Cases are executed by the hub's role-gated eval runner (POST /agents/{name}/eval — same approver roles as the human-in-the-loop API): each case runs the agent for real and reports pass/fail per case plus suite totals. Each case is charged to the calling approver's tenant, so the runner requires the agent to declare guardrails.dailyCostCeilingUsd (the per-tenant daily spend bound): without it the route answers 409 AGENT_EVAL_COST_CEILING_REQUIRED before any provider call, and design time warns AGENT_EVAL_WITHOUT_COST_CEILING.

AgentEvalSettings.__evalCases.doc: The evaluation cases of this agent's suite. Each is executed as a REAL agent run (source 'eval', durable run row, normal guardrails/budgets apply) by the hub eval runner.

__AgentEvalCase.doc: One evaluation case: an input to run the agent with and what to assert about the answer. A case passes when EVERY declared check passes; a case with no check at all is flagged at design time.

AgentEvalCase.__name.doc: Unique case identifier within the suite. Used in the eval report. Must be camelCase.
AgentEvalCase.__input.doc: The request body for the run: either a JSON object string (e.g. '{"message":"hi"}') or a plain string (wrapped as { message: <text> }).
AgentEvalCase.__expectedContains.doc: Substring the (stringified) agent answer must contain for the case to pass. Case-sensitive. Combine with assertion for stronger checks.
AgentEvalCase.__assertion.doc: MScript assertion evaluated against the answer — 'result' is the agent output. Must return true for the case to pass; false/string (or a thrown error) fails the case with that message. Example: `{ "js": "result.sentiment === 'positive'" }`. Must be a SINGLE EXPRESSION rooted at 'result' — statement sequences do not compile. For multi-step logic use an inline function — '() => { if (!result) return "no output"; return result.decision !== "reject"; }' — which the Node.js service target invokes with (result); 'function' forms may read 'this' (bound to the eval case), and unannotated parameters are auto-annotated ': any' at codegen so the form compiles under strict tsc (other language targets are being brought to inline-function parity). The assertion is synchronous — top-level 'await' fails validation. Other root identifiers (beyond JS/Node globals) fail validation with MSCRIPT_UNKNOWN_ROOT_BINDING.
AgentEvalCase.name: String

__HubRoomAuthRule.doc.#: Legacy enum kept for backward compatibility. New hubs should use authSources/authScripts arrays.
__HubRoomAuthRule.doc.membership: User must have a record in a membership/participant DataObject linking them to the room.
__HubRoomAuthRule.doc.ownership: User must be the owner (createdBy) of the room DataObject record.
__HubRoomAuthRule.doc.public: Any authenticated user can join the room.
__HubRoomAuthRule.doc.custom: A library function handles authorization logic.

__HubEventDirection.doc.#: Defines the direction of a custom hub event.
__HubEventDirection.doc.clientToRoom: Client emits to the server, which broadcasts to all room members.
__HubEventDirection.doc.serverToClient: Server emits directly to a specific client (e.g., presence updates).
__HubEventDirection.doc.serverToRoom: Server emits to all members of a room (e.g., system messages, deletions).

__HubMessageType.doc.#: Built-in message content types for hub messages. Each type defines a known content schema stored in the message's content JSONB column.
__HubMessageType.doc.image: Image message. Content: { mediaUrl, thumbnail, caption, width, height }.
__HubMessageType.doc.video: Video message. Content: { mediaUrl, thumbnail, caption, duration }.
__HubMessageType.doc.audio: Audio/voice message. Content: { mediaUrl, duration, waveform }.
__HubMessageType.doc.document: File/document message. Content: { mediaUrl, fileName, fileSize, mimeType }.
__HubMessageType.doc.contact: Shared contact card. Content: { contactName, contactPhone, contactUserId }.
__HubMessageType.doc.location: Location pin. Content: { lat, lng, address, label }.
__HubMessageType.doc.system: Auto-generated system message (member joined, room renamed, etc.). Content: { systemAction, systemData }.

__HubCustomFieldType.doc.#: Data types for fields in custom message type definitions.
__HubCustomFieldType.doc.Enum: One of a fixed set of string values (defined in enumValues).

__EventSubTransport.doc.#: Defines the transport protocol for a client event subscription.
__EventSubTransport.doc.websocket: Socket.IO WebSocket connection. Best for long-lived subscriptions (dashboards, tickers, admin panels) where clients dynamically subscribe/unsubscribe to topics.
__EventSubTransport.doc.sse: Server-Sent Events over HTTP. Best for short-lived, page-scoped subscriptions (product pages, order tracking) that open on page load and close on navigation.

__InterserviceTransport.doc.auto: Default — uses gRPC automatically when the target Business API has a gRPC controller (`grpcSettings.hasGrpcController`), otherwise REST; the only path that works for a gRPC-only target.
__InterserviceTransport.doc.rest: Forces the HTTP/REST path (the target's normal REST route, with the forwarded caller bearer).
__InterserviceTransport.doc.grpc: Forces the gRPC path — requires the target to expose a gRPC controller.

__GrpcTlsMode.doc.#: TLS mode for a generated gRPC client channel.
__GrpcTlsMode.doc.insecure: Plaintext credentials (default) — fine for dev / trusted networks.

__ForeignPermissionProviderType.doc.#: Transport for the foreign permission server a `ForeignPermissionProvider` calls.
__ForeignPermissionProviderType.doc.grpc: Call a foreign gRPC `service.method` via the shipped grpcUnaryCall machinery; proto emitted from `protoSource`.

__ForeignPermissionRestMethod.doc.#: [rest only] HTTP method used to call the foreign permission server.

__ForeignPermissionRequestIn.doc.#: [rest only] Where the merged permission request (params + sessionBindings) is placed on the HTTP call.
__ForeignPermissionRequestIn.doc.body: JSON body — the default, for POST.

__ForeignPermissionBindingIn.doc.#: Where a resolved session-binding value is placed on the foreign permission request.
__ForeignPermissionBindingIn.doc.bearer: Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` — REST header / gRPC `metadata.authorization`; `as` is ignored.
__ForeignPermissionBindingIn.doc.header: A REST request header / gRPC metadata entry named `<as>`.
__ForeignPermissionBindingIn.doc.body: A JSON body field / gRPC proto message field `<as>` — the default, alongside the per-api params.
__ForeignPermissionBindingIn.doc.query: A REST query-string param `<as>`; ignored for grpc.

__HubScalingAdapter.doc.#: Defines the Socket.IO adapter for multi-instance scaling.
__HubScalingAdapter.doc.redis: Uses @socket.io/redis-adapter for broadcasting across multiple service instances. Required for production deployments.
__HubScalingAdapter.doc.memory: In-memory adapter. Only works with a single service instance. Suitable for development.

__RealtimeConfig.doc: Service-level configuration for the Socket.IO server powering realtime hubs. Only active when the service has at least one RealtimeHub. Controls the scaling adapter, heartbeat timings, and connection limits.

RealtimeConfig.__adapter.doc: The Socket.IO adapter for multi-instance scaling. Use 'redis' for production (broadcasts events across instances via Redis pub/sub) or 'memory' for single-instance development.
RealtimeConfig.__heartbeatInterval.doc: How often the Socket.IO server sends heartbeat pings to connected clients, in milliseconds. Default: 25000 (25 seconds).
RealtimeConfig.__heartbeatTimeout.doc: How long the server waits for a heartbeat response before considering the client disconnected, in milliseconds. Must be less than heartbeatInterval. Default: 20000 (20 seconds).
RealtimeConfig.__maxConnectionsPerUser.doc: Maximum number of concurrent Socket.IO connections allowed per authenticated user. Prevents resource exhaustion from excessive client connections. Default: 10.

__RealtimeHub.doc: Defines a bidirectional realtime communication hub powered by Socket.IO. Each hub provides room-based messaging with built-in message types (text, image, video, audio, document, sticker, contact, location, system) and optional custom message types for app-specific structured data. Messages are always persisted to an auto-generated DataObject. The hub auto-bridges the create, update and delete events of every DataObject of its service via Kafka, and provides standard events (typing, read receipts, presence) as toggles. Hubs are mounted as Socket.IO namespaces and expose auto-generated REST endpoints.

RealtimeHub.__hubBasics.doc: Core identity of the realtime hub including its name and description. The name determines the Socket.IO namespace path (`/<service>-api/hub/{name}`) and, kebab-cased, the REST endpoint prefix (`/{kebab-name}` under the service's `/<service>-api` route).
RealtimeHub.__roomSettings.doc: Configures room management, join authorization, and role assignment. Defines which DataObject represents rooms, eligibility conditions, and a layered authorization flow (absoluteRoles → checkRoles → checkScript → authSources → authScripts) that determines each user's hub role.
RealtimeHub.__hubRoles.doc: Named permission sets that control what users can do inside a room. Each role specifies read, send, moderate, delete, and manage permissions. Roles are assigned to users by the room authorization flow defined in roomSettings.
RealtimeHub.__messageSettings.doc: Controls message structure, built-in message types (text, image, video, audio, etc.), cross-cutting features (reply threading, reactions, forwarded flag), and custom app-specific message types. An auto-generated Message DataObject persists all messages.
RealtimeHub.__eventSettings.doc: Configures standard events (typing, presence, read/delivery receipts), auto-bridged DataObject CRUD events via Kafka, and custom or external Kafka events. Standard events are toggleable and the framework generates the socket handlers automatically.
RealtimeHub.__historySettings.doc: Controls whether message history is sent to clients when they join a room and how many recent messages to include.
RealtimeHub.__guardrails.doc: Safety limits, rate controls, moderation settings, and auth caching for the hub. Includes rooms per user, message rate limits, payload size limits, and moderation modes; maxUsersPerRoom is enforced only by the Java and Python runtimes, and connectionTimeout by none.
RealtimeHub.__hubLogic.doc: Server-side logic hooks for intercepting custom messages with MScript, providing room state on join, and running scheduled interval actions. Enables game loops, collaborative editing, auction countdowns, and other stateful hub behaviors.
RealtimeHub.__contentModeration.doc: Decision-moderated messages for this hub: objectModeration applied to hub messages. When `enabled`, every message a user sends (socket `hub:send` or REST POST) is judged by a calibrated decision provider before it reaches the room. An `accept` is delivered as usual, a `review` is HELD (nothing is stored or broadcast) in a framework-generated `sys_<hubName>HubMessageModerationReview` object until a reviewer accepts it, and a `reject` is dropped with a typed error to the sender. Message types a HubLogic handler processes and system-authored messages are never judged. Optional - omit (or null) when unused.

__HubBasics.doc: Core identity of the realtime hub. The name is used in the Socket.IO namespace path (`/<service>-api/hub/{name}`), kebab-cased as the REST endpoint prefix (`/{kebab-name}` under the service's `/<service>-api` route), and as the code identifier.

HubBasics.__name.doc: Unique hub identifier within the service. Used in the Socket.IO namespace (`/<service>-api/hub/{name}`) and, kebab-cased, as the REST endpoint prefix ('chatHub' serves `/chat-hub/...`). Must be a valid code name (camelCase, no spaces). Examples: 'chatHub', 'gameLobby', 'liveDashboard'.
HubBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the hub's purpose. Used in documentation and AI assistant context.
HubBasics.name: String

__HubRoomSettings.doc: Configures how rooms are managed and who can join them. Every hub requires a roomDataObject -- an existing DataObject that represents rooms. Authorization uses a layered flow: (1) roomEligibility checks if the room supports real-time features, (2) absoluteRoles bypass all checks, (3) checkRoles gates access to specific user roles, (4) checkScript applies a custom condition, (5) authSources and authScripts (OR-logic) determine the user's hub role. The first matching authSource/authScript wins (ordered highest-privilege first).

HubRoomSettings.__roomDataObject.doc: Name of the existing DataObject that represents rooms in this hub. The DataObject must be defined in the same service. Examples: 'Chat', 'ChessMatch', 'SupportTicket'. Clients join rooms by referencing the ID of this DataObject.
HubRoomSettings.__roomEligibility.doc: MScript condition evaluated against the room record (fetched from Elasticsearch) BEFORE any authorization. The context variable name is the roomDataObject name (e.g., if roomDataObject is 'catalogEvent', use 'catalogEvent.chatEnabled'). The generic alias 'room' is also available. If false, the room does not support real-time features and NOBODY can join -- including absoluteRoles. Examples: `{ "js": "catalogEvent.chatEnabled == true" }`, `{ "js": "catalogEvent.status == 'published'" }`.
HubRoomSettings.__absoluteRoles.doc: List of role names (from session.roleId) that bypass ALL authorization checks.
