Users with any of these roles get the built-in 'system' hub role with full permissions. Checked AFTER roomEligibility (even superAdmins cannot join ineligible rooms). Examples: ['superAdmin'], ['superAdmin', 'systemAdmin'].
HubRoomSettings.__checkRoles.doc: List of role names that are REQUIRED to proceed to auth sources. If defined, users whose roleId is NOT in this list are immediately denied. Use to restrict hub access to specific user tiers. Examples: ['premiumUser', 'subscriber']. Leave empty to allow all roles.
HubRoomSettings.__checkScript.doc: MScript condition evaluated after checkRoles and before authSources. Context variables: 'user' (session data) and the roomDataObject name for the room record (e.g., 'catalogEvent'). The generic alias 'room' is also available. Must return true to proceed. Examples: `{ "js": "user.city == catalogEvent.city" }`, `{ "js": "user.subscriptionLevel >= catalogEvent.minLevel" }`.
HubRoomSettings.__authSources.doc: Ordered array of DataObject-based authorization sources. Each source queries Elasticsearch for a record matching the user and room. Sources are checked top-to-bottom (highest-privilege first). The FIRST matching source determines the user's hub role -- remaining sources are skipped. Each source can have an optional 'condition' MScript evaluated against the found record (context variable: 'record').
HubRoomSettings.__authScripts.doc: Ordered array of MScript-based authorization sources. Checked after authSources if no authSource matched. Each script is evaluated with 'user' (session) and 'room' (room record) context. The FIRST script returning true determines the user's hub role. Use for complex authorization logic that can call library functions.

__HubMessageSettings.doc: Controls message structure and persistence. Every hub auto-generates a Message DataObject with system fields (id, roomId, senderId, timestamp), a messageType enum column, and a content JSONB column. Designers select which built-in message types to support (text, image, video, etc.) and can define custom message types with app-specific field schemas. Cross-cutting features (reply threading, reactions, forwarded flag) are toggleable across all message types.

HubMessageSettings.__dataObjectName.doc: Name for the auto-generated Message DataObject. Must be a valid code name. Convention: '{HubName}Message'. Example: 'ChatHubMessage', 'GameLobbyMessage'. If omitted, defaults to '{hubName}Message'.
HubMessageSettings.__messageTypes.doc: Built-in message types to support in this hub. Each type has a known content schema managed by the framework. Select the types relevant to your use case. The messageType column in the DataObject becomes an enum of all selected built-in types plus any custom message type names.
HubMessageSettings.__enableReplyTo.doc: When true, adds a 'replyTo' JSON field to all messages for threading/reply support. Contains { id, preview }. Works across all message types.
HubMessageSettings.__enableReaction.doc: When true, adds a 'reaction' JSON array field to all messages for emoji reactions. Each entry has emoji, userId, timestamp. Works across all message types.
HubMessageSettings.__enableForwarded.doc: When true, adds a 'forwarded' Boolean field to all messages indicating if the message was forwarded from another room. Works across all message types.
HubMessageSettings.__customMessageTypes.doc: App-specific message types beyond the built-in set. Each custom type defines a name (added to the messageType enum) and a field schema validated at runtime. Use for structured payloads like game moves, bids, polls, or domain-specific actions. The fields are stored in the message's content JSONB column.

__HubEventSettings.doc: Configures standard events, auto-bridged DataObject events, custom events, and external Kafka events. Standard events (typing, recording, read receipts, delivery receipts, presence) are toggleable -- the framework generates the socket handlers; they are broadcast only, never persisted. Auto-bridge relays the create, update and delete events of every DataObject of the hub's service to hub rooms. Custom events and Kafka events remain for app-specific signals and external sources. Event names in these fields are the Node.js runtime's: Java and Python emit the same typing, recording and receipt events but no `hub:online` or `hub:offline`, .NET has no recording, delivery-receipt, online or offline events, and the Go hub implements none of these settings.

HubEventSettings.__enableTypingIndicator.doc: When true, enables built-in typing/stopTyping events. Clients emit 'hub:event' with event 'typing' and the server broadcasts 'hub:typing' / 'hub:stopTyping' to room members. Ephemeral (not persisted).
HubEventSettings.__enableRecordingIndicator.doc: When true, enables built-in recording/stopRecording events for voice message recording state. Clients emit `hub:event` with event 'recording' or 'stopRecording' and the server broadcasts `hub:recording` or `hub:stopRecording` { roomId, userId } to the other room members. Ephemeral (not persisted).
HubEventSettings.__enableReadReceipts.doc: When true, enables built-in read receipt events. Clients emit `hub:event` with event 'messageRead' and data { lastReadTimestamp }, and the server broadcasts `hub:messageRead` { roomId, userId, lastReadTimestamp } to room members, the sender included (server time when no timestamp is sent). Ephemeral (not persisted): a client that needs read state across sessions must store it itself.
HubEventSettings.__enableDeliveryReceipts.doc: When true, enables built-in delivery receipt events. Clients emit `hub:event` with event 'messageDelivered' and data { messageId } when a message is received, and the server broadcasts `hub:messageDelivered` { roomId, userId, messageId } to room members, the sender included. Ephemeral (not persisted).
HubEventSettings.__enablePresence.doc: When true, enables built-in online and offline presence events: the server broadcasts `hub:online` { roomId, userId } to a room on a socket's first join of it, and `hub:offline` { roomId, userId } to every room the socket had joined when it disconnects. There is no away state. Ephemeral. The `hub:presence` joined and left frames are sent whatever this flag says.
HubEventSettings.__autoBridgeDataEvents.doc: When true (default), the hub subscribes to the Kafka create, update and delete events of every DataObject of its service (the room object, membership objects, the hub's own message and moderation objects and any other) and relays each one to one room as `hub:<objectName>.<verb>` (declared object name; verb created, updated or deleted) with the payload `{ roomId, ...record }`. The room is the record's `<roomDataObject>Id` field, else its roomId, else its own id; a record without one is not relayed. If 'system' message type is enabled, each relayed event is also stored as a system message `{ systemAction: '<objectName>.<verb>', systemData: record }` in the room's history (stored, not broadcast).
HubEventSettings.__customEvents.doc: App-specific events beyond the standard set, each declared with a name, a direction and an ephemeral flag. The declarations are informational: a client's `hub:event` `{ roomId, event, data }` whose event no enabled standard toggle handles is relayed to room members, the sender included, as `hub:<event>` `{ roomId, userId, ...data }`, declared or not; direction and ephemeral change nothing at runtime, and custom events are never persisted. Use for domain-specific interactions like collaborative cursor tracking or custom notifications that don't fit built-in standard events.
HubEventSettings.__kafkaEvents.doc: External Kafka topic events to bridge into hub rooms. Use for events from other services or topics not covered by auto-bridge (which handles only the DataObjects of the hub's own service). Each entry specifies a topic, an optional filter expression, and a target room expression (default `data.roomId || data.id`); room members receive `hub:<name>` `{ roomId, ...record }`. Nothing is persisted.

__HubHistorySettings.doc: Controls whether message history is sent to clients when they join a room. When enabled, the server queries the message DataObject for the most recent messages and emits them as a 'hub:history' event immediately after join confirmation.

HubHistorySettings.__historyEnabled.doc: When true, sends the most recent messages to a client when they join a room. Requires autoDataObject to be true in messageSettings.
HubHistorySettings.__historyLimit.doc: Number of most recent messages to send when a client joins a room. Default: 50.

__HubGuardrails.doc: Safety limits, rate controls, moderation settings, and caching for the hub. Prevents resource exhaustion, abuse, and oversized payloads. All values have sensible defaults but should be tuned for production use cases. Not every field is enforced on every runtime: see maxUsersPerRoom and connectionTimeout.

HubGuardrails.__maxUsersPerRoom.doc: Maximum number of concurrent users allowed in a single room. Enforced only by the Java ('Room is at capacity') and Python ('Room is full') runtimes, which reject a join over the cap; the Node.js, .NET and Go runtimes never check it, so their rooms are uncapped. Default: 1000.
HubGuardrails.__maxRoomsPerUser.doc: Maximum number of rooms a single user can be joined to simultaneously. Prevents memory exhaustion from users joining too many rooms. Default: 50.
HubGuardrails.__messageRateLimit.doc: Maximum number of messages a single user can send per minute across all rooms; hub:send and the REST send share the budget. A message over the limit is refused ('Rate limit exceeded', REST 429) until older messages leave the sliding 60-second window. The Node.js runtime counts per service instance. Default: 60.
HubGuardrails.__maxMessageSize.doc: Maximum message payload size. A hub:send frame or REST send body whose JSON text is longer is rejected ('Message too large', REST 413); the Node.js runtime counts characters of the whole frame, and its Socket.IO transport also drops any frame over 1 MB. Default: 65536 (64 KB).
HubGuardrails.__connectionTimeout.doc: Not enforced: no runtime reads this value, so an idle connection is never disconnected for inactivity. In the Node.js runtime a dead connection is dropped by the Socket.IO heartbeat, which serviceSettings.realtimeConfig.heartbeatInterval and heartbeatTimeout configure. Kept so stored blueprints stay valid. Default: 300000 (5 minutes).
HubGuardrails.__authCacheTTL.doc: Time-to-live in seconds for the Redis auth cache. After a user's authorization for a room is resolved, the resulting hubRole name is cached in Redis. Subsequent joins and REST calls for that room within the TTL skip the role checks (absoluteRoles, checkRoles, checkScript, authSources, authScripts); the room, eligibility and block checks still run, and a block or unblock clears the entry. 0 disables caching only on the .NET and Java runtimes; the Node.js and Python runtimes read 0 as the default 300. Default: 300 (5 minutes).
HubGuardrails.__globalModeration.doc: When true, ALL messages in the hub require moderator approval before being broadcast, regardless of the sender's hubRole. When false, only messages from roles with 'moderated: true' go through moderation. Messages a hubLogic messageHandler processes and server or system messages are never held. Default: false.
HubGuardrails.__defaultSilenced.doc: When true, all users join rooms in a silenced state (canSend overridden to false) regardless of their hubRole. Users with canModerate permission are exempt. Other users must request speak permission (`hub:requestSpeak`), which a moderator can grant (`hub:grantSpeak`). In the Node.js runtime a grant lives on the user's connected sockets only: it is lost on reconnect or re-join, and the REST send stays refused. Useful for webinar/classroom/town-hall scenarios. Default: false.

__HubAuthSource.doc: A DataObject-based authorization source for hub room access. Queries Elasticsearch for a record in the specified DataObject where userField matches the authenticated user and roomField matches the target room. If a record is found (and the optional condition passes), the user is granted the specified hubRole. Sources are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins.

HubAuthSource.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this authorization source. Used as a reference name in logs and documentation. Examples: 'ticketHolder', 'eventOwner', 'hostAssignment'.
HubAuthSource.__sourceObject.doc: Name of the DataObject to query in Elasticsearch. Can be the room DataObject itself (for ownership checks), a membership/join-table DataObject, or any other DataObject. The query searches for a record where userField = current userId AND roomField = roomId. Examples: 'issuedTicket', 'eventHost', 'catalogEvent'.
HubAuthSource.__userField.doc: Property on the DataObject that holds the user identifier. Matched against the authenticated user's userId. Examples: 'userId', 'ownerUserId', 'createdBy', 'playerId'.
HubAuthSource.__roomField.doc: Property on the DataObject that holds the room identifier. Matched against the room's ID. Use 'id' when checking the room DataObject itself (ownership pattern). Examples: 'eventId', 'chatId', 'id'.
HubAuthSource.__condition.doc: Optional MScript condition evaluated against the found record. The context variable name matches the 'sourceObject' name (e.g., if sourceObject is 'issuedTicket', use 'issuedTicket.status'). The generic alias 'record' is also available. If the condition returns false, this source does not match and the next source is tried. Examples: `{ "js": "issuedTicket.status == 'active'" }`, `{ "js": "eventHost.role == 'lead'" }`.
HubAuthSource.__hubRole.doc: The hub role assigned to the user if this source matches. Must correspond to a role defined in the hubRoles section. If null, the user is authorized but gets no specific role (all members have equal permissions). Examples: 'owner', 'moderator', 'attendee'.
HubAuthSource.name: String

__HubAuthScript.doc: An MScript-based authorization source for hub room access. The script is evaluated with 'user' (session data) and 'room' (room record from Elasticsearch) as context variables. Scripts can call library functions for complex logic. If the script returns true, the user is granted the specified hubRole. Scripts are evaluated after authSources, top-to-bottom; the first match wins.

HubAuthScript.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this authorization script. Used as a reference name in logs and documentation. Examples: 'vipAccess', 'geoRestriction', 'publicRoomGuest'.
HubAuthScript.__script.doc: MScript expression that must evaluate to a boolean. Context variables: 'user' (authenticated session with userId, roleId, etc.) and 'room' (the room DataObject record). Can call library functions. Examples: `{ "js": "lib.checkVIPAccess(user, room)" }`, `{ "js": "user.tier == 'gold' && room.isPublic" }`.
HubAuthScript.__hubRole.doc: The hub role assigned to the user if this script returns true. Must correspond to a role defined in the hubRoles section. If null, the user is authorized but gets no specific role (all members have equal permissions).
HubAuthScript.name: String

__HubRole.doc: Defines a named permission set for hub users. Each role controls what actions a user can perform within a room. Roles are assigned by authSources, authScripts, or absoluteRoles. A built-in 'system' role (all permissions true) is automatically used for absoluteRoles users. When globalModeration or the role's 'moderated' flag is true, messages require moderator approval before broadcast.

HubRole.__name.doc: Unique role name. Referenced by authSources and authScripts via their hubRole property. Convention: lowercase descriptive names. Examples: 'owner', 'moderator', 'attendee', 'viewer'.
HubRole.__canRead.doc: When true, the user receives the room: hub:history on join, hub:state, room broadcasts, and REST GET messages. When false the role is write-only: the user joins the room and may send (canSend), and moderation commands still reach it, but it gets no history, no state, no broadcasts, and REST GET messages answers 403 HUB_READ_FORBIDDEN. A role with canModerate true always reads (it must see pending messages), so canRead false has no effect on it and validation warns (HUB_ROLE_MODERATOR_READS). Default: true.
HubRole.__canSend.doc: When true, the user can send messages. When false, the user is read-only (viewer). Default: true.
HubRole.__allowedMessageTypes.doc: Comma-separated list of message types this role can send. If empty, all hub message types are allowed. Use to restrict certain roles to text-only or exclude media types. Examples: 'text', 'text,image'.
HubRole.__moderated.doc: When true, messages from users with this role are saved as 'pending' and require moderator approval before being broadcast to the room. Default: false.
HubRole.__canModerate.doc: When true, the user can approve/reject pending messages, and block/silence other users. Default: false.
HubRole.__canDeleteAny.doc: When true, the user can delete any message in the room (not just their own). Default: false.
HubRole.__canManageRoom.doc: When true, the user can update room settings and kick users from the room. Default: false.
HubRole.name: String

__HubCustomMessageType.doc: Defines a custom (app-specific) message type for the hub. Custom message types extend the built-in types with designer-defined names and field schemas. Each custom type adds its name to the messageType enum in the generated DataObject. The content JSONB column stores the fields defined here, validated at runtime. Examples: 'chessMove' with from/to/piece fields, 'nudge' with animation field, 'bid' with amount/currency fields.

HubCustomMessageType.__name.doc: Unique name for this custom message type. Becomes an entry in the messageType enum alongside built-in types. Must be a valid code name (camelCase). Examples: 'chessMove', 'nudge', 'bid', 'pollVote'.
HubCustomMessageType.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this message type represents and when it is used.
HubCustomMessageType.__fields.doc: Typed fields that make up this custom message type's content schema. Each field has a name, type, and optional constraints. Fields are validated before broadcast and persistence. The entire set is stored in the message's content JSONB column.
HubCustomMessageType.name: String

__HubCustomField.doc: Defines a single field in a custom message type's content schema. Fields are stored inside the message's content JSONB column and validated before persistence and broadcast. For Enum types, provide comma-separated allowed values in enumValues.

HubCustomField.__name.doc: Field name in the custom message content JSON. Must be a valid JavaScript identifier. Example: 'from', 'piece', 'bidAmount', 'animation'.
HubCustomField.__fieldType.doc: Data type of this field. Determines validation and serialization. Use 'Enum' with enumValues for fixed-choice fields.
HubCustomField.__required.doc: When true, messages of this custom type must include this field. Validated before persistence and broadcast.
HubCustomField.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the field's purpose. Used in documentation and AI context.
HubCustomField.__enumValues.doc: Comma-separated list of allowed values when fieldType is 'Enum'. Example: 'pawn,rook,knight,bishop,queen,king'. Ignored for other field types.
HubCustomField.__defaultValue.doc: Default value for this field if not provided in the message payload. Stored as a string and coerced to the field type at runtime.
HubCustomField.name: String

__HubCustomEvent.doc: Declares an app-specific event that clients emit within the hub, for signals like game actions, cursor positions or custom notifications. A client sends `hub:event` `{ roomId, event: '<name>', data }` and room members receive `hub:<name>` `{ roomId, userId, ...data }`. The declaration is informational: the runtime relays undeclared event names the same way, does not validate the payload, and never persists custom events. There is no server-side emitter for custom events; server traffic reaches rooms through hubLogic server messages, kafkaEvents or the auto-bridge.

HubCustomEvent.__name.doc: Event name. Clients send it as the event of a `hub:event` frame and the room receives it as `hub:<name>`. Examples: 'gameOver', 'cursorMove', 'reactionBurst'. Do not reuse a standard event name (typing, stopTyping, recording, stopRecording, messageRead, messageDelivered), which an enabled toggle handles first, or a built-in hub frame name such as 'presence' or 'messageArrived'. Convention: camelCase.
HubCustomEvent.__description.doc: Human-readable description of when and why this event is emitted.
HubCustomEvent.__ephemeral.doc: Not read by any runtime: custom events are always broadcast only and never persisted, whatever this flag says. Kept so stored blueprints stay valid.
HubCustomEvent.__direction.doc: Intended sender and audience. Only 'clientToRoom' generates code, in the Node.js runtime: a handler that relays the client's `hub:event` to the room as `hub:<name>`, which the hub does for undeclared names anyway. 'serverToClient' and 'serverToRoom' generate nothing in any runtime; server traffic reaches clients through hubLogic server messages (`hub:messageArrived`, to the room or to listed users), kafkaEvents (`hub:<name>`) or the auto-bridge.
HubCustomEvent.name: String

__HubKafkaEvent.doc: Bridges a Kafka topic message into the hub as a room-scoped event. When a matching message arrives on the configured Kafka topic, the filterExpression is evaluated. If it passes, the targetRoomExpression extracts the room ID, and the event is broadcast to all clients in that room. Use for backend-driven updates like participant changes, status transitions, or external system notifications.

HubKafkaEvent.__name.doc: Event name emitted to room clients when a matching Kafka message arrives. Example: 'participantAdded', 'statusChanged'.
HubKafkaEvent.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this Kafka-bridged event represents.
HubKafkaEvent.__topic.doc: Kafka topic to subscribe to. The hub creates a consumer for this topic and evaluates incoming messages against the filterExpression.
HubKafkaEvent.__filterExpression.doc: MScript expression evaluated against each Kafka message to decide if it should be bridged. Has access to 'data' (the parsed message payload). Example: `{ "js": "data.eventType === 'participant.added'" }`. If omitted, all messages on the topic are bridged.
HubKafkaEvent.__targetRoomExpression.doc: MScript expression to extract the target room ID from the Kafka message. Has access to 'data'. Example: `{ "js": "data.chatId" }`. The event is broadcast only to clients in this room.
HubKafkaEvent.name: String

__HubLogic.doc: Server-side logic hooks for the hub. Allows intercepting custom message types with MScript before broadcast, fetching room state on join or on demand, and running scheduled actions on an interval. MScript hooks can call service library functions, Redis, DB, Business APIs, or external services -- the hub just provides the hook points and acts on the return values. Intercepted messages are queued per-room to prevent race conditions.

HubLogic.__stateScript.doc: MScript called when a user joins a room or emits 'hub:requestState'. Must return the current room state (any shape). The return value is sent to the requesting client only via 'hub:state' event. Context: 'session' (user session), 'roomId', 'room' (room DataObject record), 'lib' (service library). Example: `{ "js": "lib.chess.getState(roomId)" }`. Leave empty if the hub doesn't need state management.
HubLogic.__messageHandlers.doc: Array of message type interceptors. When a client sends a custom message type that matches a handler, the message is NOT broadcast immediately. Instead, the handler's script is called and the return value determines accept/reject, broadcast behavior, and server-generated messages. Unmatched message types follow the standard flow (immediate broadcast + persist). Handlers are processed sequentially per room (no race conditions).
HubLogic.__scheduledActions.doc: Array of interval-based actions that run while a room has connected users (or always if keepAlive is true). Each action calls its script on the configured interval. The script can return serverMessages to broadcast to the room. Use for game ticks, world updates, auction countdowns, or periodic state broadcasts.

__HubMessageHandler.doc: Intercepts a specific custom message type and routes it through an MScript before broadcast. The script receives the message, sender session, room record, and service library, and returns an object controlling accept/reject, broadcast targets, message modifications, persistence, and server-generated messages. Use for game moves, bids, collaborative edits, or any message that needs server-side validation or state management.

HubMessageHandler.__messageType.doc: The custom message type name to intercept. Must match a name from customMessageTypes in HubMessageSettings. When a client sends a message of this type, the handler script is called instead of the standard broadcast flow.
HubMessageHandler.__script.doc: MScript called when a message of this type is received. Context: 'session' (sender session), 'message' ({ type, content }), 'roomId', 'room' (room DataObject record), 'lib' (service library). Must return an object: { accept: Boolean, rejectReason?: String, broadcast?: Boolean, broadcastTo?: 'all'|'others'|'sender'|String[], modifiedContent?: Object, persist?: Boolean, serverMessages?: [{ type: String, content: Object, to: 'all'|'others'|'sender'|String[], persist?: Boolean }] }. Example: `{ "js": "lib.chess.processMove(roomId, session, message)" }`.

__HubScheduledAction.doc: A recurring action that runs on an interval for each active room. The script is called every intervalMs milliseconds and can return serverMessages to broadcast. The interval starts when the first user joins the room and stops when the last user disconnects, unless keepAlive is true. Use for game world ticks, NPC movement, countdown timers, or periodic state sync.

__HubScheduledAction.useCase.description: Use to run a recurring server-side tick per active realtime room — game world updates, countdown timers, NPC movement, periodic state sync — returning serverMessages to broadcast each interval.

HubScheduledAction.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this scheduled action. Used for logging and lifecycle management.
HubScheduledAction.__intervalMs.doc: Interval in milliseconds between script invocations. Example: 1000 for a 1-second game tick, 60000 for a 1-minute cycle. Minimum recommended: 100ms.
HubScheduledAction.__keepAlive.doc: When true, the scheduled action keeps running even when no users are connected to the room. Use for game worlds that need to evolve independently of player presence. When false (default), the action starts on the first join and stops on the last disconnect.
HubScheduledAction.__script.doc: MScript called on each interval tick. Context: 'roomId', 'room' (room DataObject record), 'lib' (service library). Must return an object: { serverMessages?: [{ type: String, content: Object, to: 'all'|String[], persist?: Boolean }] }. Example: `{ "js": "lib.world.tick(roomId)" }`.
HubScheduledAction.name: String

__VideoRoom.doc: Defines a video-conference / live-broadcast room surface for the service (docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md). A VideoRoom binds an EXISTING DataObject (the room record — a meeting, a lesson, a live event) to a media provider from projectSettings.videoProvidersSettings. The `roomKind` folds the whole family into one chapter: interactive SFU kinds (oneToOne, groupMeeting, webinar) where authorized participants publish camera/mic, and the broadcast kind (one/few publishers → RTMP/HLS/CDN, massive viewer scale) where viewers only watch. Key rule: if viewers only watch → broadcast; if they join with camera/mic → an interactive kind. The generated service is the CONTROL PLANE only — it mints capability-scoped join tokens (via the RealtimeHub-style layered auth flow), drives the provider's room API, persists auto-generated Session/Participant DataObjects, and runs the optional AI pipeline (transcription → meeting analysis → smart search); media itself never passes through the service. Lifecycle events are published on Kafka; recordings land in a service bucket.

VideoRoom.__roomBasics.doc: Core identity of the video room: name, room kind (the family discriminator), and the video provider it runs on.
VideoRoom.__roomSettings.doc: Binds the room to an existing DataObject and configures the layered join-authorization flow (roomEligibility → absoluteRoles → checkRoles → checkScript → authSources → authScripts) that determines each user's roomRole. Mirrors the proven RealtimeHub room authorization shape.
VideoRoom.__roomRoles.doc: Named media-capability sets (publish audio/video, screen share, subscribe, data channel, moderate, record, manage). Roles are assigned to users by the roomSettings authorization flow; the minted join token carries exactly the role's grants. When absent, every authorized user gets the room kind's default capabilities (oneToOne/groupMeeting: full publish+subscribe; webinar/broadcast: subscribe-only audience, absoluteRoles publish).
VideoRoom.__sessionSettings.doc: Controls the auto-generated session persistence DataObjects ({name}RoomSession per room session, {name}RoomParticipant per join). They are real DataObjects (db-layer, ES indexing); on a nodejs service the framework also injects read-only list/get Business APIs on them (and on {name}MeetingInsight) under /videoroom-history/<room>/, gated by the room's own join authorization and, for a tenant-level room record, pinned to the caller's tenant. No create/update/delete API is generated: the runtime writes these rows.
VideoRoom.__recordingSettings.doc: Recording configuration — mode (composite / individual tracks / audio only) and the service bucket (remoteBuckets / nativeBuckets entry) recording artifacts land in. Recording artifacts are also the input of the postSession AI transcription.
VideoRoom.__broadcastSettings.doc: Live-broadcast delivery configuration — HLS output, DVR window, RTMP ingest for external encoders (OBS), latency mode, and simulcast push targets (YouTube Live / Twitch / LinkedIn Live style RTMP endpoints). Only meaningful for the webinar (optional broadcast output of an interactive session) and broadcast room kinds.
VideoRoom.__aiPipeline.doc: The AI layer on top of the room: speech-to-text transcription, LLM meeting analysis (summary, action items, decisions, topics, custom prompts), and smart search over transcripts + insights via Elasticsearch. Providers are referenced BY NAME from projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings — no new provider system.
VideoRoom.__eventSettings.doc: Kafka lifecycle event publication for the room (roomStarted, roomEnded, participantJoined/Left, recordingReady, broadcastStarted/Stopped, transcriptReady, insightsReady).
VideoRoom.__guardrails.doc: Safety limits for the room: participant/publisher caps, duration cap, empty-room timeout, and join-token TTL.
VideoRoom.__meetingAgents.doc: AI meeting/voice agents that JOIN the room as participants (docs/ADR-video-live-ai-layer.md §4). Each entry references an aiAgents agent deployed in the owning service; the in-session live worker joins it as a participant, feeds it addressed turns from the caption stream (or direct data-channel messages), relays its text reply on the room data channel, and — when voiceEnabled — speaks the reply through a published audio track. Only meaningful on interactive rooms on an AI_PIPELINE_BRANDS provider (native/livekit); mention/always turn policies require live transcription.

__VideoRoomBasics.doc: Core identity of the video room. The name is used as the code identifier, the auto route prefix (/videoroom/{name}/), and the prefix of the auto-generated DataObjects ({name}RoomSession, {name}RoomParticipant, {name}Transcript, {name}MeetingInsight).

VideoRoomBasics.__name.doc: Unique room identifier within the service. Used as the auto REST route prefix (/videoroom/{name}/) and the auto-generated DataObject prefix. Must be a valid code name (camelCase). Examples: 'teamMeeting', 'lessonRoom', 'townHall'.
VideoRoomBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the room's purpose. Used in documentation and AI assistant context.
VideoRoomBasics.__roomKind.doc: The family discriminator. 'oneToOne' = SFU call capped at 2 participants, everyone publishes. 'groupMeeting' = interactive SFU meeting, everyone may publish. 'webinar' = SFU with few publishers and a silenced audience (via roomRoles); may ALSO enable broadcastSettings to stream the session out to HLS/simulcast. 'broadcast' = YouTube-Live-style: one/few publishers (SFU or RTMP ingest) → HLS/CDN playback for massive viewer scale; viewers receive playback grants, not SFU join tokens. Key rule: viewers only watch → broadcast; viewers join with camera/mic → an interactive kind.
VideoRoomBasics.__providerName.doc: Name of the video provider this room runs on (must match a projectSettings.videoProvidersSettings.videoProviders[].name). Interactive kinds (oneToOne/groupMeeting/webinar) require an interactive-capable brand; the broadcast kind requires a broadcast-capable brand — see the VideoProvider capability list.
VideoRoomBasics.__mediaRouting.doc: ADVANCED — how media is routed for interactive kinds. OpenAPPL is SFU-native: 'sfu' (default) routes ALL interactive rooms (including oneToOne) through the provider's SFU, which is what enables recording, moderation, server-side events, and the AI pipeline. 'p2p' is an escape hatch for oneToOne rooms ONLY (ultra-low-cost or privacy-sensitive calls where media must not touch a server) on providers that support it — it DISABLES recordingSettings and aiPipeline for the room. 'auto' lets the provider decide (e.g. P2P for 2 participants, SFU beyond). Ignored by the broadcast kind. Leave absent unless you know you need it.
VideoRoomBasics.name: String

__VideoMediaRoutingMode.doc.#: How media is routed for an interactive video room (docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §5). the generated video stack is SFU-native; P2P is a documented-as-advanced escape hatch, and MCU is intentionally NOT a routing mode (server-side mixing exists only as composite recording layout and broadcast program output).
__VideoMediaRoutingMode.doc.sfu: Server-routed WebRTC through the provider's SFU — the default for every interactive kind. Required for recording, moderation, server-side events, and the AI pipeline.
__VideoMediaRoutingMode.doc.p2p: Direct peer-to-peer WebRTC, oneToOne rooms only, on providers that support it. Media never touches a server: recordingSettings and aiPipeline are unavailable.
__VideoMediaRoutingMode.doc.auto: Provider decides (e.g. P2P while 2 participants, SFU beyond).

__VideoRoomKind.doc.#: The video room family discriminator (docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §5). Interactive kinds ride the provider's SFU (WebRTC, low latency, limited participants); the broadcast kind rides live-streaming delivery (RTMP/HLS/CDN, higher latency, massive scale).
__VideoRoomKind.doc.oneToOne: Two-party SFU call (consultation, support, interview). Both participants publish; maxParticipants is effectively 2.
__VideoRoomKind.doc.groupMeeting: Interactive SFU meeting — every authorized participant may publish camera/mic/screen (team meeting, classroom, board call).
__VideoRoomKind.doc.webinar: SFU with few publishers and a large silenced audience (roles decide who publishes). May additionally enable broadcastSettings to stream the session out to HLS / simulcast targets.
__VideoRoomKind.doc.broadcast: Live-broadcast room — one/few publishers (SFU publish or external RTMP encoder) → transcode/package → HLS/CDN playback at massive viewer scale. Viewers only watch.

__VideoRoomSettings.doc: Binds the video room to an existing DataObject and configures who may join and with which roomRole. Every video room requires a roomDataObject — an existing DataObject that represents the room (a meeting, a lesson, a live event); clients request tokens by referencing the ID of this DataObject. Authorization uses the RealtimeHub layered flow: (1) roomEligibility checks the room record supports video, (2) absoluteRoles bypass all checks (full-capability system role), (3) checkRoles gates access to specific user roles, (4) checkScript applies a custom condition, (5) authSources and authScripts (OR-logic, ordered highest-privilege first) determine the user's roomRole — the first match wins.

VideoRoomSettings.__roomDataObject.doc: Name of the existing DataObject that represents rooms of this video room. Must be defined in the same service. Examples: 'Meeting', 'Lesson', 'LiveEvent'. Clients request join tokens by referencing the ID of this DataObject.
VideoRoomSettings.__roomEligibility.doc: MScript condition evaluated against the room record BEFORE any authorization. The context variable name is the roomDataObject name (generic alias 'room' also available). If false, the room does not support video and NOBODY can join — including absoluteRoles. Examples: `{ "js": "meeting.videoEnabled == true" }`, `{ "js": "liveEvent.status == 'live'" }`.
VideoRoomSettings.__absoluteRoles.doc: List of role names (from session.roleId) that bypass ALL authorization checks. Users with any of these roles get the built-in 'system' room role with full media capabilities. Checked AFTER roomEligibility. Examples: ['superAdmin'].
VideoRoomSettings.__checkRoles.doc: List of role names REQUIRED to proceed to auth sources. If defined, users whose roleId is NOT in this list are immediately denied. Leave empty to allow all roles.
VideoRoomSettings.__checkScript.doc: MScript condition evaluated after checkRoles and before authSources. Context variables: 'user' (session data) and the roomDataObject name for the room record (generic alias 'room'). Must return true to proceed. Example: `{ "js": "user.tenantId == meeting.tenantId" }`.
VideoRoomSettings.__authSources.doc: Ordered array of DataObject-based authorization sources. Each source queries for a record matching the user and room; sources are checked top-to-bottom (highest-privilege first) and the FIRST match determines the user's roomRole. Example: a 'host' source on an eventHost join-table, then an 'attendee' source on issuedTicket.
VideoRoomSettings.__authScripts.doc: Ordered array of MScript-based authorization sources, checked after authSources if none matched. Each script is evaluated with 'user' and 'room' context; the FIRST script returning true determines the user's roomRole.

__VideoRoomAuthSource.doc: A DataObject-based authorization source for video room access. Queries for a record in the specified DataObject where userField matches the authenticated user and roomField matches the target room. If a record is found (and the optional condition passes), the user is granted the specified roomRole. Sources are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins. Mirrors HubAuthSource.

VideoRoomAuthSource.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this authorization source. Examples: 'eventHost', 'ticketHolder', 'roomOwner'.
VideoRoomAuthSource.__sourceObject.doc: Name of the DataObject to query. Can be the room DataObject itself (ownership check), a membership/join-table DataObject, or any other DataObject. Examples: 'issuedTicket', 'eventHost', 'meeting'.
VideoRoomAuthSource.__userField.doc: Property on the DataObject that holds the user identifier, matched against the authenticated user's userId. Examples: 'userId', 'ownerUserId', 'hostId'.
VideoRoomAuthSource.__roomField.doc: Property on the DataObject that holds the room identifier, matched against the room's ID. Use 'id' when checking the room DataObject itself (ownership pattern). Examples: 'meetingId', 'eventId', 'id'.
VideoRoomAuthSource.__condition.doc: Optional MScript condition evaluated against the found record. The context variable name matches the 'sourceObject' name (generic alias 'record'). If false, this source does not match and the next source is tried. Example: `{ "js": "issuedTicket.status == 'active'" }`.
VideoRoomAuthSource.__roomRole.doc: The roomRole assigned to the user if this source matches. Must correspond to a role defined in the roomRoles section. If null, the user is authorized with the room kind's default capabilities.
VideoRoomAuthSource.name: String

__VideoRoomAuthScript.doc: An MScript-based authorization source for video room access, evaluated with 'user' (session data) and 'room' (room record) as context variables. If the script returns true, the user is granted the specified roomRole. Scripts are evaluated after authSources, top-to-bottom; the first match wins. Mirrors HubAuthScript.

VideoRoomAuthScript.__name.doc: Unique identifier for this authorization script. Examples: 'vipAccess', 'publicRoomGuest'.
VideoRoomAuthScript.__script.doc: MScript expression that must evaluate to a boolean. Context variables: 'user' (authenticated session) and 'room' (the room DataObject record). Can call library functions. Example: `{ "js": "user.tier == 'gold' && room.isPublic" }`.
VideoRoomAuthScript.__roomRole.doc: The roomRole assigned to the user if this script returns true. Must correspond to a role defined in the roomRoles section. If null, the user is authorized with the room kind's default capabilities.
VideoRoomAuthScript.name: String

__VideoRoomRole.doc: Defines a named media-capability set for video room users. Each capability maps 1:1 onto a grant in the minted provider join token (e.g. LiveKit video grants) — the SFU enforces them, the service only declares them. Roles are assigned by authSources, authScripts, or absoluteRoles (which get a built-in full-capability 'system' role). Examples: a webinar 'speaker' (publish all), 'attendee' (subscribe + data channel), a broadcast 'presenter' vs 'viewer' (playback only).

VideoRoomRole.__name.doc: Unique role name, referenced by authSources/authScripts via their roomRole property. Examples: 'host', 'speaker', 'attendee', 'viewer'.
VideoRoomRole.__canPublishAudio.doc: When true, the user may publish their microphone. Default: true.
VideoRoomRole.__canPublishVideo.doc: When true, the user may publish their camera. Default: true.
VideoRoomRole.__canScreenShare.doc: When true, the user may publish a screen-share track. Default: false.
VideoRoomRole.__canSubscribe.doc: When true, the user receives other participants' tracks (or the HLS playback grant in a broadcast room). Default: true.
VideoRoomRole.__canUseDataChannel.doc: When true, the user may send data-channel messages (in-room chat, reactions, live caption relay). Default: true.
VideoRoomRole.__canModerate.doc: When true, the user can mute/remove other participants and approve pending speakers. Default: false.
VideoRoomRole.__canRecord.doc: When true, the user can start/stop recording (when recordingSettings is enabled and autoRecord is false). Default: false.
VideoRoomRole.__canManageRoom.doc: When true, the user can start/end the room session and start/stop broadcast outputs. Default: false.
VideoRoomRole.__hidden.doc: When true, the user joins invisibly (not listed to other participants) — for observers, QA monitors, or service bots. Default: false.
VideoRoomRole.name: String

__VideoRoomSessionSettings.doc: Controls the auto-generated session persistence DataObjects. {name}RoomSession holds one row per room session (start/end, peak participant count, recording storage keys, broadcast playback URL); {name}RoomParticipant holds one row per participant join (identity, roomRole, join/leave timestamps, publish stats). They are real DataObjects (db-layer, Elasticsearch indexing). On a nodejs, java or dotnet service the framework injects read-only list<Object>s / get<Object> Business APIs on them for meeting-history and attendance screens: GET /videoroom-history/<room>/rooms/{roomId}/sessions (or /participants) lists one room record's rows, GET /videoroom-history/<room>/sessions/{id} (or /participants/{id}) reads one row. Every call runs the room's own join authorization for that room record (and requires a tenant-level room record to belong to the caller's tenant), answering 403 VIDEO_ROOM_HISTORY_ACCESS_DENIED otherwise. No create/update/delete API is generated: the runtime writes these rows.

VideoRoomSessionSettings.__persistSessions.doc: When true (default), a {name}RoomSession DataObject is auto-generated and one record is written per room session (created on roomStarted, finalized on roomEnded).
VideoRoomSessionSettings.__persistParticipants.doc: When true (default), a {name}RoomParticipant DataObject is auto-generated and one record is written per participant join (finalized on leave with duration and publish stats).
VideoRoomSessionSettings.__sessionDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the auto-generated session DataObject. Defaults to '{roomName}RoomSession'. Must be a valid code name.
VideoRoomSessionSettings.__participantDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the auto-generated participant DataObject. Defaults to '{roomName}RoomParticipant'. Must be a valid code name.

__VideoRoomRecordingSettings.doc: Recording configuration for the room. Recording runs on the provider's egress (never through the service) and artifacts land in the configured service bucket; the storage keys are written to the {name}RoomSession record and a recordingReady event is published. Recording artifacts are the input of the postSession AI transcription.

VideoRoomRecordingSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for recording capability on this room. When false, recording controls and the recording section are inert. Default: false.
VideoRoomRecordingSettings.__autoRecord.doc: When true, every room session records automatically from start to end. When false, recording is started/stopped by roles with canRecord (or a VideoRoomControlAction). Default: false.
VideoRoomRecordingSettings.__mode.doc: What the egress records. 'composite' = one mixed grid video of the whole session (default); 'individual' = one file per participant track (best transcription diarization quality); 'audioOnly' = composite audio track only (cheapest, sufficient for the AI pipeline).
VideoRoomRecordingSettings.__bucketName.doc: Name of the service bucket (a remoteBuckets[] or nativeBuckets[] entry in the SAME service) recording artifacts are uploaded to. The bucket's storage credentials are handed to the provider egress at start-recording time.
VideoRoomRecordingSettings.__retentionDays.doc: Days recording artifacts are kept before cleanup. Null/absent = keep forever.

__VideoRecordingMode.doc.#: What the provider egress records for a room session.
__VideoRecordingMode.doc.composite: One mixed video of the whole session (speaker/grid layout). The default.
__VideoRecordingMode.doc.individual: One file per participant track — larger, but gives the best speaker-diarization quality to the AI transcription.
__VideoRecordingMode.doc.audioOnly: Composite audio only — cheapest artifact, sufficient when recording exists only to feed the AI pipeline.

__VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.doc: Live-broadcast delivery for webinar and broadcast room kinds. Configures the HLS output viewers play, the DVR window, RTMP ingest for external encoders (OBS/vMix) as publishers, the latency mode, and simulcast push targets — external RTMP endpoints (YouTube Live, Twitch, LinkedIn Live) the provider egress pushes the program feed to in parallel. Broadcast viewers authorize through the SAME roomSettings flow but receive an HLS playback grant instead of an SFU join token.

VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__hlsEnabled.doc: When true (default), the room session is packaged to HLS and viewers receive the playback URL (written to the session record and returned by the token route for subscribe-only roles). Default: true.
VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__dvrWindowMinutes.doc: Minutes of rewindable DVR window kept in the HLS output. 0 (default) = live edge only.
VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__rtmpIngestEnabled.doc: Declares that the room's publisher streams from an external RTMP encoder (OBS, vMix, hardware). Only the broadcast-only brands (mux, awsIvs, cloudflareStream) serve it: their publisher /token answer is the RTMP(S) ingest URL + stream key. A LiveKit (native/livekit) or other SFU-brand room returns no ingest URL or stream key from /token or /control, so the flag is config data only there. Default: false.
VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__latencyMode.doc: Delivery latency/scale trade-off for the HLS output. 'standard' = normal HLS latency (~10-30s), maximum CDN compatibility (default); 'low' = low-latency HLS (~2-6s) where the provider supports it.
VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__maxViewers.doc: Optional cap on concurrent broadcast viewers (playback grants). Null/absent = unlimited (CDN scale).
VideoRoomBroadcastSettings.__simulcastTargets.doc: External RTMP endpoints the provider egress pushes the program feed to in parallel with (or instead of) HLS — this is where YouTube Live / Twitch / LinkedIn Live live. Each target is a named rtmpUrl + secret streamKey.

__VideoBroadcastLatencyMode.doc.#: Delivery latency/scale trade-off of the broadcast HLS output.
__VideoBroadcastLatencyMode.doc.standard: Normal HLS latency (~10-30s), maximum CDN compatibility. The default.
__VideoBroadcastLatencyMode.doc.low: Low-latency HLS (~2-6s) where the provider supports it.

__VideoSimulcastTarget.doc: One external RTMP push target of a broadcast (e.g. a YouTube Live / Twitch / LinkedIn Live endpoint). The provider egress pushes the program feed to rtmpUrl using the secret streamKey.

VideoSimulcastTarget.__rtmpUrl.doc: The target's RTMP(S) ingest URL, e.g. 'rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2'.
VideoSimulcastTarget.__streamKey.doc: The target's stream key. Secret — masked in API responses and emitted to a VIDEO-room env var at codegen time.
VideoSimulcastTarget.name: String

__VideoRoomAiPipeline.doc: The AI layer on top of the video room (docs/ADR-video-conference-pattern-family.md §8) — pure composition of existing OpenAPPL layers, no new provider system. transcription turns the session's audio into {name}Transcript segment rows (speech-to-text via a NAMED projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings provider); liveTranslation translates the live captions into target languages on the room data channel; meetingAnalysis runs LLM passes over the transcript into {name}MeetingInsight rows; smartSearch indexes transcripts + insights into the project Elasticsearch (optionally with embeddings for semantic search). Post-session shape: roomEnded event → transcription job (recording artifact from the bucket) → analysis job → index; each stage publishes its own Kafka completion event. (AI meeting/voice agents that JOIN the room as participants are a deliberately-deferred AgentHub tie-in — ADR §8b.)

VideoRoomAiPipeline.__transcription.doc: Speech-to-text over the room session. Required by liveTranslation, meetingAnalysis and (for transcript indexing) smartSearch.
VideoRoomAiPipeline.__liveTranslation.doc: Live translation of the room's captions into target languages, relayed on the room data channel. Requires transcription with mode 'live' or 'both'.
VideoRoomAiPipeline.__meetingAnalysis.doc: LLM analysis passes over the transcript — summary, action items, decisions, topics, sentiment, plus custom prompts. Requires transcription.
VideoRoomAiPipeline.__smartSearch.doc: Keyword (and optionally semantic) search over transcripts and insights, indexed into the project Elasticsearch and exposed on the room's auto search route.

__VideoLiveTranslationSettings.doc: Live caption translation for the room. Each live transcript segment is translated into the target languages by the named AI provider and relayed to participants over the room data channel as caption events (each participant's client picks the language to display). Requires aiPipeline.transcription enabled with mode 'live' or 'both'. Translated captions are ephemeral by default; when persistTranslations is true they are stored as extra {name}Transcript rows tagged with their language.

VideoLiveTranslationSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for live translation. Default: false.
VideoLiveTranslationSettings.__providerName.doc: Name of the AI provider to translate with (must match a projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name). Defaults to the transcription provider when absent.
VideoLiveTranslationSettings.__targetLanguages.doc: BCP-47 language codes to translate the live captions into (e.g. ['en', 'tr', 'de']). At least one required when enabled.
VideoLiveTranslationSettings.__persistTranslations.doc: When true, translated caption segments are also persisted as {name}Transcript rows tagged with their language (searchable). When false (default), translations are ephemeral data-channel events only.

__VideoMeetingAgent.doc: An AI meeting/voice agent that joins the video room as a participant (docs/ADR-video-live-ai-layer.md §4). agentName references an aiAgents agent deployed in the owning service. When the in-session live worker claims the room it joins the agent (autoJoin) as a participant, feeds it addressed turns per respondTo (a caption mention, a direct data-channel message, or every utterance), publishes the agent's text reply on the room data channel, and — when voiceEnabled — synthesizes the reply to speech on a published audio track. Requires an interactive room on an AI_PIPELINE_BRANDS provider (native/livekit); mention/always policies require live transcription.

VideoMeetingAgent.__agentName.doc: Name of the aiAgents agent this participant runs. Must resolve to an agent DEPLOYED IN THE OWNING SERVICE (hub-level agents without a service assignment do not yet count — docs/ADR-video-live-ai-layer.md §4d).
VideoMeetingAgent.__displayName.doc: Participant name shown to other participants in the room. Defaults to agentName when absent.
VideoMeetingAgent.__roomRoleName.doc: roomRole (from roomRoles[].name) granted to the agent participant. When absent a default role is synthesized: canSubscribe + canUseDataChannel + (voiceEnabled ? canPublishAudio), hidden:false — an AI participant is visible by default. Set an explicit hidden role for recorder-style agents.
VideoMeetingAgent.__autoJoin.doc: When true (default), the agent joins as soon as the live worker claims the room session. When false the agent is provisioned but joined on demand.
VideoMeetingAgent.__respondTo.doc: Turn policy. 'mention' (default) = respond when a final utterance contains the agent's display name; 'directMessage' = respond only to data-channel messages addressed to the agent (no transcription required); 'always' = respond to every final utterance (rate-limited).
VideoMeetingAgent.__voiceEnabled.doc: When true, the agent speaks its replies: the reply text is synthesized to speech and pushed to a published audio track. Requires a TTS-capable AI provider. Default: false.
VideoMeetingAgent.__voice.doc: TTS voice name for the spoken reply (provider-specific). Defaults to the provider's default voice.
VideoMeetingAgent.__language.doc: BCP-47 language the agent replies in (e.g. 'en', 'tr'). Defaults to the room transcription language.
VideoMeetingAgent.__bargeIn.doc: When true (default), sustained human speech while this voice agent is talking cancels its in-flight TTS reply (barge-in / turn-taking). Set false to let the agent always finish. Only meaningful when voiceEnabled. Env VIDEO_LIVE_BARGE_IN=false disables barge-in room-wide.

__VideoMeetingAgentRespondPolicy.doc.#: When a video meeting agent takes a turn (docs/ADR-video-live-ai-layer.md §4b).
__VideoMeetingAgentRespondPolicy.doc.mention: Respond when a final utterance contains the agent's display name (case-insensitive). Requires live transcription. The default.
__VideoMeetingAgentRespondPolicy.doc.directMessage: Respond only to data-channel messages addressed to the agent on topic mb:agent:<agentName>. No transcription required (text in / text out).
__VideoMeetingAgentRespondPolicy.doc.always: Respond to every final utterance (rate-limited by a minimum inter-turn interval). Requires live transcription.

__VideoTranscriptionSettings.doc: Speech-to-text configuration for the room. The provider is a NAMED projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings entry with an audio-transcription capable backend (e.g. an openai entry for whisper/gpt-4o-transcribe, or a google entry). postSession mode consumes the recording artifact from the recording bucket (requires recordingSettings.enabled); live mode streams captions to participants over the room data channel as the session runs. Output: {name}Transcript DataObject rows (sessionId, participantId, startMs, endMs, text, confidence) + a transcriptReady Kafka event.

VideoTranscriptionSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for transcription. Default: false.
VideoTranscriptionSettings.__providerName.doc: Name of the AI provider to transcribe with (must match a projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name whose backend supports audio transcription).
VideoTranscriptionSettings.__mode.doc: 'postSession' (default) = transcribe the recording artifact after the session ends (requires recordingSettings.enabled). 'live' = streaming captions during the session, relayed to participants over the data channel. 'both' = live captions AND an authoritative post-session pass.
VideoTranscriptionSettings.__language.doc: BCP-47 language pin for the audio (e.g. 'en', 'tr', 'de'). Null/absent = auto-detect.
VideoTranscriptionSettings.__diarization.doc: When true (default), transcript segments are attributed to individual speakers. Works best with recordingSettings.mode 'individual' (per-track audio); composite recordings fall back to model-side diarization.
VideoTranscriptionSettings.__transcriptDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the auto-generated transcript DataObject. Defaults to '{roomName}Transcript'. Must be a valid code name.

__VideoTranscriptionMode.doc.#: When transcription runs relative to the room session.
__VideoTranscriptionMode.doc.postSession: Transcribe the recording artifact after the session ends (requires recording). The authoritative transcript. The default.
__VideoTranscriptionMode.doc.live: Streaming captions while the session runs, relayed to participants over the room data channel. No recording required.
__VideoTranscriptionMode.doc.both: Live captions during the session AND an authoritative post-session pass over the recording.

__VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.doc: LLM meeting-analysis passes over the room transcript (requires aiPipeline.transcription.enabled). Each enabled analysis produces {name}MeetingInsight DataObject rows (sessionId, kind, content) and an insightsReady Kafka event fires when the pass completes. customAnalyses add domain-specific extraction prompts beyond the built-in toggles (e.g. 'objections raised in a sales call', 'homework assigned in a lesson').

VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for meeting analysis. Default: false.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__providerName.doc: Name of the LLM provider to analyze with (must match a projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name).
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__summary.doc: Generate a meeting summary insight. Default: true.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__actionItems.doc: Extract action items (task, owner, due hint). Default: true.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__decisions.doc: Extract decisions made during the session. Default: false.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__topics.doc: Extract the topics discussed with time ranges. Default: false.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__sentiment.doc: Analyze overall and per-participant sentiment. Default: false.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__customAnalyses.doc: Domain-specific analysis prompts beyond the built-in toggles. Each entry produces its own insight kind.
VideoMeetingAnalysisSettings.__insightDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the auto-generated insight DataObject. Defaults to '{roomName}MeetingInsight'. Must be a valid code name.

__VideoCustomAnalysis.doc: One domain-specific LLM analysis pass over the room transcript. The prompt receives the full transcript and must describe the desired extraction; the result is stored as a {name}MeetingInsight row with kind = this analysis's name.

VideoCustomAnalysis.__name.doc: Unique analysis identifier — becomes the insight row's kind. Examples: 'salesObjections', 'homeworkAssigned', 'complianceFlags'.
VideoCustomAnalysis.__prompt.doc: The analysis instruction given to the LLM together with the transcript. Describe WHAT to extract and the desired output shape. Example: 'List every customer objection raised and how the seller responded, as an array of {objection, response}.'
VideoCustomAnalysis.name: String

__VideoSmartSearchSettings.doc: Search over the room's transcripts and insights. Indexed into the project Elasticsearch (the same infrastructure services already run on) and exposed on the room's auto search route (/videoroom/{name}/search — codegen phase). With an embeddingProviderName set, segments are also embedded and the route upgrades to hybrid keyword + semantic search ('find where pricing was discussed' matches even without the word 'pricing').

VideoSmartSearchSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for smart search. Default: false.
VideoSmartSearchSettings.__indexTranscripts.doc: Index transcript segments (requires aiPipeline.transcription.enabled). Default: true.
VideoSmartSearchSettings.__indexInsights.doc: Index meeting-analysis insight rows (requires aiPipeline.meetingAnalysis.enabled). Default: true.
VideoSmartSearchSettings.__embeddingProviderName.doc: Optional name of an AI provider (projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name) used to embed segments for semantic search. Null/absent = keyword search only.

__VideoRoomEventSettings.doc: Kafka lifecycle event publication for the room. Events ride the project bus under the service's standard topic naming so other services, realtime hubs (HubKafkaEvent), event subscriptions, and the AI pipeline itself can react: roomStarted, roomEnded, participantJoined, participantLeft, recordingReady, broadcastStarted, broadcastStopped, transcriptReady, insightsReady.

VideoRoomEventSettings.__publishLifecycleEvents.doc: When true (default), the room publishes its lifecycle events to Kafka. The AI pipeline's post-session stages are driven by these events, so disabling them also disables postSession AI processing.

__VideoRoomGuardrails.doc: Safety limits for the room. All values have sensible defaults; tune per room kind (an oneToOne room is effectively capped at 2 participants regardless of maxParticipants).

VideoRoomGuardrails.__maxParticipants.doc: Maximum concurrent SFU participants in a room session (broadcast HLS viewers are NOT counted — cap those with broadcastSettings.maxViewers). Default: 50.
VideoRoomGuardrails.__maxPublishers.doc: Maximum concurrent publishing participants. Null/absent = every participant whose role allows publishing may publish. Typical for webinar/broadcast kinds (e.g. 3 speakers).
VideoRoomGuardrails.__maxDurationMinutes.doc: Maximum room session duration in minutes; the session is force-ended when exceeded. Default: 240.
VideoRoomGuardrails.__emptyTimeoutSeconds.doc: Seconds an empty room (no connected participants) is kept alive before the session auto-ends. Default: 300.
VideoRoomGuardrails.__joinTokenTTLSeconds.doc: Validity window of a minted join token in seconds. Default: 600.

__VideoRoomTokenAction.doc: Authorizes a room identity and mints its provider join token or broadcast playback grant. BusinessApiAction that runs a declared VideoRoom's authorization flow for a room record + identity and mints the provider join credential — an SFU join token carrying the resolved roomRole's media grants, or an HLS playback grant for subscribe-only access to a broadcast room. Writes `{ token, url, roomRole }` to the action context. Use inside composed workflows (e.g. mint a token at the end of a paid-ticket checkout API); simple cases use the room's auto token route instead (codegen phase).

VideoRoomTokenAction.__videoRoom.doc: Name of the target VideoRoom (must match a service videoRooms[].roomBasics.name).
VideoRoomTokenAction.__roomId.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the ID of the room record (an instance of the room's roomDataObject). Example: `{ "js": "this.meeting.id" }`.
VideoRoomTokenAction.__identity.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the participant identity encoded in the token. Defaults to the session user's id when absent.
VideoRoomTokenAction.__displayName.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the participant's display name shown to other participants. Optional.
VideoRoomTokenAction.__roomRole.doc: Optional roomRole override (must match a roomRoles[].name). When absent (recommended), the role is resolved by the room's authorization flow.

__VideoRoomControlAction.doc: Performs a provider control-plane operation on a declared VideoRoom. BusinessApiAction that performs a control-plane operation against a declared VideoRoom through its provider's server API: create or end a room session, remove/mute a participant, start/stop recording, start/stop broadcast outputs. The media itself never passes through the service — this action only drives the provider. Writes the provider response (e.g. session info, egress id) to the action context.

VideoRoomControlAction.__videoRoom.doc: Name of the target VideoRoom (must match a service videoRooms[].roomBasics.name).
VideoRoomControlAction.__roomId.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the ID of the room record the operation targets. Example: `{ "js": "this.meeting.id" }`.
VideoRoomControlAction.__participantIdentity.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the target participant identity — required by removeParticipant / muteParticipant, ignored by the other operations.

__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.#: The control-plane operation a VideoRoomControlAction performs against the room's provider.
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.createRoom: Create/open the provider room session for a room record ahead of the first join.
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.endRoom: End the room session — disconnects all participants, finalizes the session record, stops recording/broadcast.
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.removeParticipant: Disconnect one participant (by participantIdentity) from the session.
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.muteParticipant: Server-side mute of one participant's published audio (by participantIdentity).
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.startRecording: Start the provider egress recording per recordingSettings (mode + bucket).
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.stopRecording: Stop the running recording; the artifact lands in the bucket and recordingReady fires.
__VideoRoomControlOperation.doc.startBroadcast: Start the broadcast outputs per broadcastSettings (HLS + simulcast targets).

__ContentModel.doc: A declarative content model generates storage objects, editorial APIs, publishing transitions, and headless delivery. Content and optional child/version objects retain normal migrations, indexing and database-change events. On nodejs the generated editorial Business APIs support content create/get/list/update/delete, item create/update/delete/list, and version list/get; dedicated reorder and restoreVersion operations use the content pipeline. No designer-authored CRUD is required. Existing object/operation APIs are retained; contentBasics.editorialApis: none disables generated editorial APIs. Configure permissionSettings before exposing an editorial UI. Other content-runtime languages are nodejs, python, java, dotnet and rust; new editorial runtime operations require their port records.

ContentModel.__contentBasics.doc: Core identity of the content model: name (drives the auto DataObject prefix and the delivery route prefix), whether it is a singleton (exactly one live record — homepage, privacy policy) or a collection (blog posts, FAQ entries).
ContentModel.__fields.doc: The structured properties of this content — the content schema. Each field becomes a property of the synthesized {name}Content DataObject with the mapped storage type, validation, filterability, and search flags. Content without extra fields (a pure rich-body page) may declare none.
ContentModel.__bodySettings.doc: The rich-content body capability. Absent = this content has no body (pure structured fields, e.g. a pricing table row). Present = a 'body' property is synthesized in the chosen format: richText (HTML, sanitized with a fixed allowlist on every write and on public delivery, which richTextAllowlist can extend; see ContentBodySettings.format), markdown, or blocks (an ordered JSON array of typed content blocks — the portable, renderer-agnostic choice).
ContentModel.__childSettings.doc: The owned-children capability. Absent = flat content. Present = a {name}Item DataObject is synthesized whose rows belong to one content record (FAQ → FAQ items, release note → release entries, menu → menu items, landing page → sections), with its own fields, optional body, manual ordering, and optional nesting (trees). Children inherit the parent's publish state — they have no workflow of their own.
ContentModel.__mediaSettings.doc: The media capability — whether media assets (images, videos, documents, audio) can be attached to this content's media fields. Binds the content model to a service bucket (a remoteBuckets[] or nativeBuckets[] entry) that stores the binaries; media-typed fields hold asset descriptors pointing into that bucket. Required when any field (or child field) has type 'media'.
ContentModel.__routingSettings.doc: The public-delivery routing capability. Present = published records are publicly addressable: a unique 'slug' property is synthesized (generated from slugSource), the delivery API serves /content/{name}/{slug}, and optional SEO metadata (a 'seo' object property: title, description, canonical, openGraph) is synthesized for the consuming frontend. Absent = the content is API-only data (delivered by id/query, not by public route) — e.g. email templates, prompt libraries.
ContentModel.__localizationSettings.doc: The localization capability. When enabled, each record carries a 'locale' and a 'localeGroupId' — one row per language variant, grouped by localeGroupId; fields marked 'localized' differ per variant while unlocalized fields are mirrored from the default locale. The delivery API resolves ?locale= with fallback to the default locale.
ContentModel.__publishingSettings.doc: The publishing-workflow capability. Every content record ALWAYS carries the status machine (draft → published → archived); this section tunes it: scheduled publishing (publishAt/unpublishAt windows driven by the content scheduler), and authorized preview of unpublished content. Editorial transitions run through the content-layer transition routes or a ContentTransitionAction — never by raw status updates.
ContentModel.__versioningSettings.doc: The revision-history capability. When enabled, a {name}ContentVersion DataObject is synthesized and an immutable snapshot row is captured on publish (or on every update), enabling audit, diff, and restore.
ContentModel.__permissionSettings.doc: Editorial permissions: which project roles may edit content, which may run publish/archive transitions, which bypass all checks — and whether published content is publicly readable (the headless default) or requires an authenticated session.
ContentModel.__searchSettings.doc: The search capability. Published content is Elasticsearch-indexed like any DataObject; this section tunes the delivery search route: full-text search over searchable fields + body, and optional semantic search via a named embedding provider from projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.
ContentModel.__eventSettings.doc: Kafka content-lifecycle events supplement database-change events emitted by actual writes to synthesized objects. Generated editorial Business APIs use the ordinary API-event configuration. restore is un-archive; restoreVersion edits a draft without publishing and restores only a draft or archived record (otherwise 409).
ContentModel.__contentModeration.doc: Decision moderation of this model's editorial writes: an ObjectModeration block applied to the synthesized {name}Content object, and to {name}Item when the model has child items. When `enabled`, the generated editorial create and update APIs (and any designer-authored create / update API on those objects) are judged before they write; a `review` or `reject` verdict HOLDS the write (202, nothing written) in `sys_<object>ModerationReview` until a reviewer accepts it, and the accept replays it through the same API, so the content guards, version capture and events run once, as for a direct save. `moderatedProperties` names model fields, `body` or `seo`, or child-item fields; each synthesized object judges the listed names it carries, and null judges the content of each (its declared fields and body, plus `seo` on the record). Only `mode: staged` is supported (OBJECT_MODERATION_CONTENT_ON_PLACE): the delivery routes, transitions and scheduler read the content rows outside the onPlace read gate. The publish transition is not moderated: it changes visibility, not content. Optional - omit (or null) when unused.

__ContentModelBasics.doc: Core identity of the content model. The name is used as the code identifier, the delivery route prefix (/content/{name}/), and the prefix of the synthesized DataObjects ({name}Content, {name}Item, {name}ContentVersion).

ContentModelBasics.__name.doc: Unique content model identifier within the service. Used as the delivery route prefix (/content/{name}/) and the synthesized DataObject prefix. Must be a valid code name (camelCase). Examples: 'blogPost', 'faq', 'releaseNote', 'landingPage', 'teamMember'.
ContentModelBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this content is and who edits it. Used in documentation and AI assistant context.
ContentModelBasics.__singleton.doc: When true, one live content record exists per locale, and the content create guard rejects a second record. Delivery serves it at the model base path without a slug; editorial get/update address the existing record. Default: false (collection). A singleton enters the public sitemap only with an explicit routingSettings.basePath.
ContentModelBasics.__editorialApis.doc: Generated (default) emits role-gated editorial APIs for content, children and version reads, plus nodejs reorder/restoreVersion operations. Existing designer-authored object/operation APIs are retained. Set none to opt out; delivery and transition routes remain available. A golang service emits no content layer: it gets no generated editorial APIs (storage only) and the warning CONTENT_EDITORIAL_APIS_LANGUAGE_UNSUPPORTED, which none silences; author and role-gate your own APIs there.
ContentModelBasics.__contentIsInTenantLevel.doc: Multi-tenant projects only: true makes this model TENANT level, each tenant's own private content; false (the default) keeps it SAAS level, general content shared by every tenant. The default is false so existing projects keep their storage and need no migration. A tenant-level model synthesizes its content, item and version objects as tenant-level DataObjects (objectDataIsInTenantLevel true, with the <tenantName>Id column): every editorial API, transition, reorder, restore-version and draft preview acts only inside the caller's session tenant, the public delivery routes (list, slug, search, sitemap, singleton) serve only the requesting tenant's published rows (the tenant the session names, else the one the tenant codename header names, else the root tenant, the framework convention; a header naming an unknown tenant is a 404 before any content route), and slugs are unique per tenant. With no editRoles a tenant-level model is edited by superAdmin, saasAdmin, tenantOwner and tenantAdmin, each inside its own session tenant; a saas-level model by superAdmin and saasAdmin. Generated code carries it on nodejs; other languages refuse it until their port lands. Inert, with a warning, on a single-tenant project.
ContentModelBasics.__contentDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the synthesized content DataObject. Defaults to '{name}Content'. Must be a valid code name.
ContentModelBasics.name: String

__ContentEditorialApis.doc.#: Whether editorial Business APIs are synthesized for a content model.
__ContentEditorialApis.doc.generated: Generate missing editorial object/operation APIs. The default.
__ContentEditorialApis.doc.none: Keep only designer-authored editorial APIs; delivery and transition routes remain.

__ContentField.doc: One structured property of a content model (or of its child items). Fields are declared in content-authoring vocabulary (shortText, richText, media, reference, select…) and mapped to storage DataProperty types when the {name}Content DataObject is synthesized. System properties (id, slug, status, body, seo, locale, publishedAt, …) are synthesized from the model's capabilities and must NOT be declared as fields.

ContentField.__name.doc: The field name as it appears in the content record and the delivery API. Must be a valid code name and must not collide with the synthesized system properties (slug, status, body, seo, locale, localeGroupId, publishedAt, publishAt, unpublishAt, authorUserId, currentVersion, order, contentId, parentItemId). Examples: 'title', 'excerpt', 'price', 'authorName'.
ContentField.__type.doc: The content field type, mapped to a storage type at synthesis: shortText→String, longText→Text, richText→Text (HTML, sanitized on every write and on public delivery with the fixed ContentBodySettings.format richText allowlist, which keeps img data-size / data-align / loading and figure / figcaption), markdown→Text, integer→Integer, decimal→Double, boolean→Boolean, date→Date, dateTime→DateTime, select→Enum (selectOptions), multiSelect→String array (selectOptions), media→Object asset descriptor in the model's media bucket, reference→ID of another content model's record (referenceContentModel), json→Object, url/email/color→String.
ContentField.__required.doc: When true, the field must be present for the record to be SAVED (draft included). Prefer requiredToPublish for editorial completeness rules. Default: false.
ContentField.__requiredToPublish.doc: When true, the field may be empty on a draft but must be filled before the record can be PUBLISHED (checked by the publish transition). The editorial middle ground between free drafting and delivery completeness. Default: false.
ContentField.__isList.doc: When true, the field holds an ordered list of its type (a gallery of media, a list of tags, multiple references). Default: false.
ContentField.__localized.doc: When true AND the model's localizationSettings is enabled, this field differs per locale variant; unlocalized fields are mirrored from the default-locale record. Default: false.
ContentField.__unique.doc: When true, the field value must be unique across the model's records (per locale when localized). Default: false.
ContentField.__filterable.doc: When true, the field is exposed as a filter parameter on the delivery list/search routes and indexed in the database. Default: false.
ContentField.__searchable.doc: When true (default), the field participates in the delivery full-text search (text-typed fields only; non-text types ignore this flag).
ContentField.__defaultValue.doc: Optional default value applied when the field is absent at create time.
ContentField.__selectOptions.doc: The allowed values for select / multiSelect fields. Required (non-empty) for those types, ignored by every other type.
