ContentField.__referenceContentModel.doc: For reference fields: the name of the content model (in the SAME service) whose records this field points at. The stored value is the target record's id. Example: a blogPost 'category' field referencing the 'category' content model.
ContentField.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the field, surfaced in the editorial UI and the generated docs.
ContentField.name: String

__ContentFieldType.doc.#: The content-authoring field types of a ContentField, mapped to storage DataProperty types when the content DataObject is synthesized.
__ContentFieldType.doc.shortText: A single-line string (title, name, label). Stored as String.
__ContentFieldType.doc.longText: Multi-line plain text (excerpt, plain description). Stored as Text.
__ContentFieldType.doc.richText: Sanitized HTML rich text. Stored as Text.
__ContentFieldType.doc.markdown: Markdown source text. Stored as Text.
__ContentFieldType.doc.decimal: Decimal number (price, rating). Stored as Double.
__ContentFieldType.doc.date: Calendar date without time. Stored as Date.
__ContentFieldType.doc.select: One value from selectOptions. Stored as Enum.
__ContentFieldType.doc.multiSelect: Multiple values from selectOptions. Stored as a String array.
__ContentFieldType.doc.media: A media asset descriptor (storageKey, url, mimeType, size, alt) pointing into the model's mediaSettings bucket. Requires mediaSettings. Stored as Object.
__ContentFieldType.doc.reference: The id of a record of another content model in the same service (referenceContentModel). Stored as ID.
__ContentFieldType.doc.json: Arbitrary structured JSON. Stored as Object.
__ContentFieldType.doc.url: A URL string (validated). Stored as String.
__ContentFieldType.doc.email: An email string (validated). Stored as String.
__ContentFieldType.doc.color: A CSS color string (e.g. '#0f172a'). Stored as String.

__ContentBodySettings.doc: The rich-content body of a content model (or of its child items via childSettings.bodyFormat). Synthesizes a 'body' property on the content DataObject: Text for richText/markdown, Object (an ordered JSON array of typed blocks) for blocks. The blocks format is the portable choice — the frontend renders each block type itself, so the same content serves web, mobile, email, and PDF rendering.

ContentBodySettings.__format.doc: The body format. 'richText' = HTML (default — WYSIWYG editing), sanitized server-side on every write (create, update, bulk, restoreVersion, CRUD actions) and again on public delivery with a fixed allowlist (richTextAllowlist can extend it for the record body): kept are h1-h6, p, br, hr, ul, ol, li, blockquote, pre, code, b, strong, i, em, u, s, strike, sub, sup, span, mark, small, a (href, title, target, rel; http, https, mailto or relative URLs; target _blank gets rel noopener noreferrer), img (src, alt, title, width, height, plus the editor's display options data-size = 25, 50, 75 or 100, data-align = left, center or right, and loading = lazy or eager; http, https or relative src, no data: images), figure (data-align = left, center or right), figcaption and table, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th, td (colspan, rowspan), caption; a data-size, data-align or loading value outside its set removes that attribute and keeps the element; removed are script and style elements with their content, every other element (its text kept), style, class, on* and every other data-* attribute, and javascript:, vbscript:, data: and other URL schemes; 'markdown' = markdown source (developer-facing content: docs, release notes); 'blocks' = an ordered JSON array of typed content blocks (paragraph, heading, image, quote, embed, cta, …) — renderer-agnostic and the recommended format for marketing/landing content.
ContentBodySettings.__localized.doc: When true AND localizationSettings is enabled, the body differs per locale variant. Default: true (a body is almost always language-specific).
ContentBodySettings.__allowedBlocks.doc: For the blocks format only: the block type names editors may use (e.g. ['paragraph', 'heading', 'image', 'quote', 'cta']). Empty/absent = any block type. Ignored by richText/markdown.
ContentBodySettings.__richTextAllowlist.doc: For the richText format only: rules that EXTEND the fixed sanitizer allowlist for the record body (child item bodies and richText fields keep the fixed set). Each rule names one tag - a tag of the fixed set (to admit more attributes or classes on it) or one of the extra safe tags div, section, article, aside, header, footer, nav, details, summary, abbr, cite, q, dl, dt, dd, kbd, samp, var, del, ins, time, address, colgroup, col - with the attributes and exact class names it may keep. Attribute names are data-[a-z0-9-]+ or title, lang, dir, datetime, cite, open, start, reversed, scope, abbr, span, colspan, rowspan, width, height, alt; never on*, style, srcset, formaction, xlink:href, is, slot or class (classes go in the rule's classes list), and never an attribute the fixed set already governs for that tag. The tags script, style, iframe, object, embed, svg, math, form, input, textarea, base, meta, link and template can never be allowed. Validation refuses a rule outside these limits; the generated sanitizer applies the same limits again. Empty/absent = exactly the fixed allowlist. Supported for nodejs and python services; other languages refuse the setting until their sanitizer supports it.

__ContentRichTextAllowRule.doc: One rule of bodySettings.richTextAllowlist: a tag the richText body may keep, with the extra attributes and the exact class names it may carry. A value outside an attribute's pattern or length cap removes that attribute and keeps the element; a class token not in classes is removed.

ContentRichTextAllowRule.__name.doc: The tag name, lowercase (e.g. 'div', 'details', 'p'). One rule per tag.
ContentRichTextAllowRule.__attributes.doc: The attributes this tag may keep in addition to the fixed set, each with an optional value pattern and length cap.
ContentRichTextAllowRule.__classes.doc: The exact class names this tag may keep (e.g. ['note', 'warning']); every other class token is removed. Each name matches [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 64 characters.
ContentRichTextAllowRule.name: String

__ContentRichTextAllowAttribute.doc: One attribute a richTextAllowlist rule admits on its tag.

ContentRichTextAllowAttribute.__name.doc: The attribute name: data-[a-z0-9-]+ (lowercase) or one of title, lang, dir, datetime, cite, open, start, reversed, scope, abbr, span, colspan, rowspan, width, height, alt.
ContentRichTextAllowAttribute.__pattern.doc: Optional value pattern, a portable regular-expression subset: anchored ^...$, at most 128 characters, either one group of literal alternatives such as ^(note|tip|warning)$ or literals and character classes with ?, {n} or {n,m} (m at most 256) and at most one variable-length quantifier, such as ^[0-9]{1,4}$ or ^#[0-9a-f]{6}$. No *, +, ., nested groups or backreferences. Absent = any value within maxLength.
ContentRichTextAllowAttribute.__maxLength.doc: Longest value kept, 1 to 512. Default: 128. Checked before the pattern.
ContentRichTextAllowAttribute.name: String

__ContentBodyFormat.doc.#: The storage/authoring format of a content body.
__ContentBodyFormat.doc.richText: Sanitized HTML rich text — WYSIWYG editing. Stored as Text.
__ContentBodyFormat.doc.markdown: Markdown source — developer-facing content (docs, release notes). Stored as Text.
__ContentBodyFormat.doc.blocks: An ordered JSON array of typed content blocks — renderer-agnostic structured content (the headless-native choice). Stored as Object.

__ContentChildSettings.doc: The owned-children capability of a content model. Synthesizes a {name}Item DataObject whose rows belong to one content record via 'contentId' (FAQ → FAQ items, release note → release entries, menu → menu items, landing page → sections). Items carry their own declared fields and optional body, are manually ordered when mode is 'ordered', and may nest into trees when allowNesting is true (a 'parentItemId' property is synthesized). Items inherit the parent record's publish state — they have no status machine of their own and are delivered embedded in the parent's delivery payload.

ContentChildSettings.__mode.doc: 'ordered' (default) reserves an Integer order column for manual delivery ordering; use the editorial reorder operation. Quote the column as "order" in handwritten SQL. In service-library list calls, order is the sort-envelope key: put an order-column filter in the query envelope rather than the top level. 'unordered' has no order column and sorts by creation time.
ContentChildSettings.__fields.doc: The child item's own structured fields, declared exactly like the model's fields (same types, same reserved-name rules).
ContentChildSettings.__bodyFormat.doc: Optional rich body of each child item (an FAQ item's answer, a landing section's copy). Same formats as bodySettings. Absent = children have structured fields only.
ContentChildSettings.__allowNesting.doc: When true, items may nest under other items via the synthesized 'parentItemId' (documentation trees, multi-level menus). Default: false (a flat list).
ContentChildSettings.__itemDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the synthesized child DataObject. Defaults to '{name}Item'. Must be a valid code name.

__ContentChildMode.doc.#: How a content model's child items are ordered.
__ContentChildMode.doc.ordered: Items carry a manual 'order' property and are delivered in that order. The default.
__ContentChildMode.doc.unordered: No order property; delivery sorts by creation time.

__ContentMediaSettings.doc: Media fields hold bucket asset descriptors; upload through the existing service bucket routes, then attach the descriptor using the editorial update API. The model binds to a declared remoteBuckets or nativeBuckets entry in the same service. Descriptors contain storageKey, url, mimeType, size and alt; no second storage system is created.

ContentMediaSettings.__bucketName.doc: Name of the service bucket (a remoteBuckets[] or nativeBuckets[] entry in the SAME service) media assets are stored in.
ContentMediaSettings.__allowedKinds.doc: The media kinds editors may attach. Absent/empty = any kind.
ContentMediaSettings.__maxFileSizeMb.doc: Maximum size of one media asset in megabytes. Null/absent = the bucket's own limit.

__ContentMediaKind.doc.#: The kinds of media assets a content model's media fields may hold.
__ContentMediaKind.doc.image: Raster/vector images (jpeg, png, webp, svg, gif).

__ContentRoutingSettings.doc: Public delivery routing generates a slug on first publish from slugSource; drafts are addressed by id in editorial APIs. Collection delivery uses /content/{kebab-name}/{slug}; authenticated editorial preview also accepts the record id. Generated editorial writes exclude slug and publish-managed fields. Singleton delivery uses the model base route. basePath is a frontend page-path hint, not the service API prefix; singletons without an explicit basePath are omitted from the public sitemap. Optional seo metadata is attached to the delivery payload.

ContentRoutingSettings.__basePath.doc: The public frontend path this content lives under, surfaced in delivery payloads and the sitemap feed (e.g. '/blog', '/help', '/legal/privacy' for a singleton). Defaults to '/{kebab-case model name}'. Informational to the consuming frontend — the service delivery API prefix stays /content/{name}/.
ContentRoutingSettings.__slugSource.doc: Name of the declared field the slug is generated from (kebab-cased, uniquified). Must be a text-typed declared field. Defaults to 'title' — which must then exist as a field. Ignored by singleton models (their route needs no slug).
ContentRoutingSettings.__seoEnabled.doc: When true (default), a 'seo' object property (title, description, canonicalUrl, ogImage, structuredData) is synthesized and served with each routed record. It does not control the sitemap: the delivery sitemap feed lists every routed, publicRead model's published records (a singleton only with an explicit basePath), whatever this flag says.

__ContentLocalizationSettings.doc: The localization capability of a content model. When enabled, records exist as one row PER LOCALE VARIANT: every row carries a synthesized 'locale' plus a shared 'localeGroupId' that groups the variants of one logical content. Fields marked 'localized' (and the body when bodySettings.localized) differ per variant; unlocalized fields are mirrored from the default-locale row by the editorial runtime. The delivery API resolves ?locale= per request and falls back to the default locale when a variant is missing (fallbackToDefault).

ContentLocalizationSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for localization. Default: false.
ContentLocalizationSettings.__locales.doc: BCP-47 locale codes this content is authored in (e.g. ['en', 'tr', 'de']). At least one required when enabled.
ContentLocalizationSettings.__defaultLocale.doc: The authoritative locale unlocalized fields mirror from and delivery falls back to. Must be one of 'locales'. Defaults to the first entry.
ContentLocalizationSettings.__fallbackToDefault.doc: When true (default), a delivery request for a locale with no published variant serves the default-locale variant instead of 404.

__ContentPublishingSettings.doc: The publishing-workflow capability. Every content record ALWAYS carries the status machine — draft → published → archived, with 'scheduled' as the between-state of a future publishAt — plus 'publishedAt' stamped on first publish; this section tunes the behavior. Transitions run through the content-layer transition routes (or a ContentTransitionAction in a composed workflow) so the requiredToPublish checks, version capture, and lifecycle events always fire — raw status updates through the DataObject CRUD API are rejected by the synthesized guard.

ContentPublishingSettings.__schedulingEnabled.doc: When true, records may carry 'publishAt' / 'unpublishAt' timestamps and the content scheduler flips them live/offline at those times (status 'scheduled' between a publish transition with a future publishAt and the moment it goes live). Default: false.
ContentPublishingSettings.__previewEnabled.doc: When true, editorial roles can preview unpublished records by id with ?preview=true on delivery routes. The field defaults true when publishingSettings is declared; preview is off when that whole section is absent. Approval-enabled routed/singleton models also support shareable preview tokens.
ContentPublishingSettings.__approvalSettings.doc: The editorial approval-workflow capability. Absent/disabled (default) = the plain draft → published machine. Enabled = the status machine grows 'inReview' and 'approved' states with submitForReview / approve / rejectToDraft transitions, and shareable per-record preview tokens become mintable (previewEnabled permitting).

__ContentApprovalSettings.doc: Editorial approval workflow of a content model (publishingSettings.approvalSettings). When enabled, the always-present status machine grows two states — draft → inReview (submitForReview, edit-role gated) → approved (approve) / back to draft (rejectToDraft), both approve-role gated — and, with requireApprovalToPublish, publishing is only legal from 'approved' (scheduling counts: a scheduled record passed the approval check when it was scheduled). Approve/reject fire contentApproved/contentRejected lifecycle events; submitForReview fires contentSubmittedForReview. Enabling approval (with previewEnabled) also unlocks shareable per-record preview tokens on the delivery routes. All defaults are off — models without this section keep the exact P1 behavior.

ContentApprovalSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for the approval workflow. When true the model's status machine grows the 'inReview' and 'approved' states and the submitForReview / approve / rejectToDraft transitions. Default: false.
ContentApprovalSettings.__reviewRoles.doc: Role names that participate in review: they gain editorial READ access to unpublished records (?preview=true and the editorial delivery surfaces) so they can inspect content sitting inReview without needing edit or publish rights. Required (non-empty) when enabled.
ContentApprovalSettings.__approveRoles.doc: Role names allowed to run the approve / rejectToDraft transitions. Required (non-empty) when enabled — an approval workflow nobody can approve would dead-end (absoluteRoles always bypass).
ContentApprovalSettings.__requireApprovalToPublish.doc: When true, the publish transition is REJECTED unless the record is 'approved' (or 'scheduled' — approval was checked when it was scheduled): content must walk draft → inReview → approved → published. When false (default) the review states are available but publishing stays legal from any state, as before. Requires enabled.
ContentApprovalSettings.__editsResetApproval.doc: When true, a CRUD update that changes the CONTENT of an 'approved' record — a declared field, the body, or the seo object; not editorial metadata — drops it back to 'inReview' through the content pipeline and fires contentSubmittedForReview, so approval always covers what is actually published. Published records are untouched (unpublish → edit → re-approve is the flow). When false (default) editing an approved record keeps its approval, as before. Requires enabled.

__ContentVersioningSettings.doc: The revision-history capability of a content model. When enabled, a {name}ContentVersion DataObject is synthesized and an immutable snapshot row (full field + body payload, capture reason, author) is written on every publish transition — or on every update when captureOn is 'everyUpdate' — enabling audit, diff, and restore of earlier revisions.

ContentVersioningSettings.__enabled.doc: Master toggle for versioning. Default: false.
ContentVersioningSettings.__captureOn.doc: 'publish' (default) = snapshot on every publish transition (the editorially meaningful history). 'everyUpdate' = snapshot on every save (full audit trail, more rows).
ContentVersioningSettings.__maxVersions.doc: Keep at most this many snapshots per record (oldest pruned). Null/absent = keep all.
ContentVersioningSettings.__versionDataObjectName.doc: Override name for the synthesized version DataObject. Defaults to '{name}ContentVersion'. Must be a valid code name.

__ContentVersionCapture.doc.#: When a content version snapshot is captured.
__ContentVersionCapture.doc.publish: Snapshot on every publish transition — the editorially meaningful history. The default.
__ContentVersionCapture.doc.everyUpdate: Snapshot on every save — a full audit trail (more rows).

__ContentPermissionSettings.doc: Editorial permissions of a content model, expressed over the project's user roles (session.roleId). Editing (create/update/delete drafts) and publishing (publish/unpublish/schedule/archive transitions) are separate capabilities so a writer/editor split maps directly. Published-content READ access is public by default — the headless-delivery posture — and can be restricted to authenticated sessions with publicRead false (member-only knowledge bases, internal docs). Editorial access fails closed: a model that declares no editRoles is written, previewed and published only by the operators of its level until roles are declared: single-tenant superAdmin and admin; multi-tenant saas level superAdmin and saasAdmin; tenant level (contentBasics.contentIsInTenantLevel) superAdmin, saasAdmin, tenantOwner and tenantAdmin, each inside its own session tenant. On a tenant-level model declared roles are confined to the caller's tenant too.

ContentPermissionSettings.__publicRead.doc: When true (default), published records are served by the delivery routes WITHOUT authentication (public website content). When false, delivery requires an authenticated session (member/internal content).
ContentPermissionSettings.__editRoles.doc: Roles allowed to create/update/delete content and items, reorder items and restore a version to draft. Content CRUD guards also enforce this on designer-authored APIs. Empty/absent editRoles fails closed: only the operators of the model's level may edit (single-tenant superAdmin and admin; a multi-tenant saas-level model superAdmin and saasAdmin, because its rows are shared and a tenant role would write every tenant's content; a tenant-level model superAdmin, saasAdmin, tenantOwner and tenantAdmin, each inside its own session tenant). absoluteRoles bypasses the gate. A trusted system caller with no user session (a cron job of the service, a framework-internal or kafka-triggered call, a verified M2M token naming no user on an M2MAllowed api) passes the write guard of designer-authored APIs; an anonymous call (loginRequired: false) never does (warning CONTENT_ANONYMOUS_WRITE). Editorial reads (drafts, versions, preview by id) admit the edit roles (so the same operators when none are declared), publish, review and approve roles.
ContentPermissionSettings.__publishRoles.doc: Roles allowed to publish/unpublish/schedule/archive/restore (un-archive). Empty/absent falls back to editRoles; with no editRoles either, only the operators of the model's level (see editRoles) run transitions, and on a tenant-level model only inside the caller's tenant. Models without publishRoles or absoluteRoles receive the CONTENT_NO_PUBLISH_ROLES warning naming who publishes; declare actual project roles. restoreVersion edits a draft and never changes workflow state: only a draft or archived record restores; published, scheduled, inReview and approved are refused 409 (run the transition first).
ContentPermissionSettings.__absoluteRoles.doc: Role names that bypass all editorial permission checks. Examples: ['superAdmin'].

__ContentSearchSettings.doc: The search capability of a content model. The synthesized DataObjects are Elasticsearch-indexed like any DataObject; this section tunes the delivery search route (GET /content/{name}/search): full-text search over the searchable fields + body, and optional semantic search — searchable text is additionally embedded via a NAMED projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings provider so queries match by meaning ('refund my order' finds the returns policy).

ContentSearchSettings.__fulltextSearch.doc: When true (default), the delivery search route serves keyword full-text search over the model's searchable fields and body.
ContentSearchSettings.__semanticSearch.doc: When true, searchable content is ALSO embedded (embeddingProviderName) and the search route upgrades to hybrid keyword + semantic ranking. Default: false.
ContentSearchSettings.__embeddingProviderName.doc: Name of the AI provider (a projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[].name) used to embed content for semantic search. Required when semanticSearch is true.

__ContentEventSettings.doc: Content lifecycle events are published to the project Kafka bus for transitions and version capture. Synthesized objects emit database-change events when writes occur, including generated editorial writes; Business API events follow each configured API. Lifecycle publication includes contentPublished, contentUnpublished, contentScheduled, contentArchived, contentRestored, versionCaptured and versionRestored. restore means un-archive; restoring a version uses restoreVersion, which neither publishes nor unpublishes (only a draft or archived record restores; published, scheduled, inReview and approved are refused 409, so workflow state changes only through transitions and their events). Webhooks consume the enabled lifecycle events.

ContentEventSettings.__publishLifecycleEvents.doc: When true (default), the model publishes its editorial lifecycle events to Kafka. Frontend cache purge / static rebuild hooks are driven by these events, so disabling them also disables those integrations (webhooks[] included).
ContentEventSettings.__webhooks.doc: Outbound publishing webhooks of this content model. Each target receives a signed HTTP POST when a subscribed lifecycle event fires — a static-site build hook (Next/Astro/Netlify/Vercel deploy hooks are plain POST targets), a cache purge endpoint, or any downstream consumer. The webhook IS the rebuild trigger: no builder-specific adapters exist or are needed. Empty/absent = no webhooks (the default; existing models are untouched).

__ContentWebhook.doc: One outbound publishing webhook target of a content model (eventSettings.webhooks[]). The content-layer webhook dispatcher consumes the model's lifecycle Kafka topics and POSTs a JSON payload — { event, contentModel, contentId, slug?, locale?, publicPath?, occurredAt } — to the target URL for each subscribed event, with bounded retry and backoff; a dead endpoint never wedges the worker. When a secret is set, the request carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body in the `x-mindbricks-signature` header ('sha256=<hex>') so the receiver can verify authenticity. A placeholder secret counts as no secret: that delivery goes out unsigned.

ContentWebhook.__name.doc: Unique name of this webhook target within the model (e.g. 'siteBuildHook', 'cdnPurge'). Names the consumer group segment and the CONTENT_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_SECRET env override. Must be a valid codeName.
ContentWebhook.__url.doc: The absolute http(s) URL the signed event POST is sent to — a static-site build hook, a cache-purge endpoint, or any HTTP consumer.
ContentWebhook.__events.doc: The lifecycle events this target subscribes to. Empty/absent = the default pair [published, unpublished] — the go-live/go-offline signals a static rebuild needs.
ContentWebhook.__secret.doc: Optional shared secret for signing. When set, every POST carries `x-mindbricks-signature`: 'sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 hex of the raw body>'. Sensitive — masked in API responses; the generated service also honors a CONTENT_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_SECRET env var, which overrides this value. A placeholder (`ENTER_CREDENTIAL`, a `****` mask, a `$SECRET_` echo) is not a secret: it never signs, a placeholder env var never shadows a real value here, and with no real secret the delivery is sent unsigned (logged once per target as ContentWebhookSecretPlaceholder; validation warns CONTENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PLACEHOLDER).
ContentWebhook.name: String

__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.#: A content lifecycle event a webhook target can subscribe to — the events the content pipeline publishes on the model's Kafka topics.
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.published: The record went live (publish transition — scheduler publishes included).
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.unpublished: The record left the delivery surface (unpublish transition).
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.scheduled: The record was scheduled with a future publishAt.
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.restored: The record was restored from archive back to draft.
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.versionCaptured: A version snapshot was captured (publish or everyUpdate captures).
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.versionRestored: Editable snapshot fields and children were restored into draft; publishing remains a separate transition.
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.submittedForReview: The record entered review (submitForReview transition — or an editsResetApproval drop).
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.approved: The record was approved for publishing.
__ContentWebhookEvent.doc.rejected: The record was rejected back to draft.

__ContentTransitionAction.doc: BusinessApiAction that drives the publishing lifecycle of a declared ContentModel record from inside a composed workflow — publish, unpublish, schedule, unschedule, archive, restore. Runs the SAME transition pipeline as the content-layer transition routes (requiredToPublish checks, version capture, lifecycle events), so workflow-driven publishing (e.g. auto-publish a release note when a version ships, unpublish a product page when stock hits zero) stays consistent with editorial publishing. Writes the updated content record to the action context.

ContentTransitionAction.__contentModel.doc: Name of the target content model (must match a service contentModels[].contentBasics.name).
ContentTransitionAction.__contentId.doc: MScript expression evaluating to the id of the content record the transition targets. Example: `{ "js": "this.releaseNote.id" }`.
ContentTransitionAction.__publishAt.doc: For the 'schedule' transition: MScript expression evaluating to the ISO timestamp the record goes live at. Ignored by the other transitions.

__ContentTransition.doc.#: The publishing transition a ContentTransitionAction (or a content-layer transition route) runs on a content record.
__ContentTransition.doc.publish: draft/archived → published. Runs requiredToPublish checks, stamps publishedAt on first publish, captures a version when versioning is enabled, fires contentPublished. With approvalSettings.requireApprovalToPublish only legal from 'approved' (or 'scheduled').
__ContentTransition.doc.unpublish: published → draft. The record leaves the delivery surface. Fires contentUnpublished.
__ContentTransition.doc.schedule: draft → scheduled with a future publishAt; the content scheduler publishes it at that time (requires publishingSettings.schedulingEnabled). Fires contentScheduled.
__ContentTransition.doc.unschedule: scheduled → draft; clears publishAt before it went live.
__ContentTransition.doc.archive: any → archived. The record leaves the delivery surface but is kept (soft retirement). Fires contentArchived.
__ContentTransition.doc.restore: archived → draft, ready for editing/re-publishing. Fires contentRestored.
__ContentTransition.doc.submitForReview: draft → inReview (requires publishingSettings.approvalSettings.enabled). Edit-role gated; runs the requiredToPublish checks up front so incomplete content never reaches review. Fires contentSubmittedForReview.
__ContentTransition.doc.approve: inReview → approved (requires approvalSettings.enabled). approveRoles gated. Fires contentApproved.
__ContentTransition.doc.rejectToDraft: inReview/approved → draft (requires approvalSettings.enabled). approveRoles gated. Fires contentRejected.

__EventSubscription.doc: Defines a client-facing Kafka event subscription channel. Clients connect via WebSocket (namespace `/<service>-api/events/{name}`; on Node.js a Socket.IO namespace with the HTTP path `/<service>-api/socket.io/`) or SSE (`GET /<service>-api/events/{name}/stream`), `<service>-api` being the owning service's public route, and subscribe to a subset of the configured topics. Each topic is linked to a DataObject whose authorization config drives the default access control. The designer can override access levels, transform payloads, and add custom auth scripts. Authorization automatically splits mixed-access subscriptions -- less-authorized users receive only the topics they are allowed to see.

EventSubscription.__basics.doc: Core identity of the event subscription including its name, description, and transport protocol (WebSocket or SSE). The name determines the WebSocket namespace (`/<service>-api/events/{name}`) or SSE endpoint (`/<service>-api/events/{name}/stream`), `<service>-api` being the owning service's public route.
EventSubscription.__topics.doc: An array of Kafka topics exposed through this subscription. Each topic is linked to a DataObject whose authorization config drives default access control. Topics can override access levels, transform payloads, and exclude sensitive fields before delivery to clients. Note that framework-raised topics deliver the unified event ENVELOPE: `{ id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data: { _type, ...record }, old? }` — the record always sits under `data` (updates additionally carry the previous row under `old`), so payload transforms and field exclusions operate on that `data` shape. Envelopes never include a session or tokens. Use the `getKafkaEventPayloadStructure` tool to see the exact per-topic shape.
EventSubscription.__auth.doc: Authorization configuration for the subscription. Default auth derives from each topic's DataObject access level (public/protected/private). Supports absoluteRoles to bypass all checks, checkRoles to gate access, and custom MScript auth/filter logic for per-topic and per-event authorization.

__EventSubBasics.doc: Core identity of the event subscription. The name becomes the namespace path `/<service>-api/events/{name}` for WebSocket transport (a Socket.IO namespace on Node.js) or the SSE endpoint `/<service>-api/events/{name}/stream` for SSE transport, `<service>-api` being the owning service's public route.

EventSubBasics.__name.doc: Unique subscription identifier within the service. Used in the WebSocket namespace (`/<service>-api/events/{name}`) or SSE endpoint (`/<service>-api/events/{name}/stream`). Must be a valid code name (camelCase): validation converts a kebab-case value, so 'order-tracking' is stored and served as 'orderTracking'. Examples: 'dashboard', 'productUpdates', 'orderTracking'.
EventSubBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the subscription's purpose. Used in documentation and AI assistant context.
EventSubBasics.__transport.doc: The transport protocol for this subscription. Use 'websocket' for long-lived connections (finance dashboards, live tickers, admin panels) where clients dynamically subscribe/unsubscribe. Use 'sse' for short-lived, page-scoped connections (product page updates, order tracking) that open on page load and close on navigation.
EventSubBasics.name: String

__EventSubTopic.doc: A Kafka topic included in this subscription. First select the DataObject -- the available topics are derived from the DataObject's API events and DB events. Authorization defaults to the DataObject's access level (public/protected/private) but can be overridden with forceAccessLevel. The payload can be transformed or fields can be excluded before delivery to the client.

EventSubTopic.__name.doc: Client-facing event name emitted when a matching Kafka message arrives. Example: 'orderCreated', 'reviewAdded', 'inventoryChanged'.
EventSubTopic.__dataObjectName.doc: The DataObject this topic belongs to. Select the DataObject first, then choose the topic. The DataObject's authorization config (public/protected/private, tenant scoping) drives the default access control for this topic.
EventSubTopic.__topic.doc: Kafka topic to subscribe to, written as the full topic name. There is no alias syntax: a string such as 'order.created', 'review_updated' or 'dbEvent:inventory:updated' is subscribed under exactly that name, which nothing publishes (validation warns KAFKA_TOPIC_UNKNOWN_PRODUCER). The only rewrite is the project scope: a topic a PublishEventAction of this project authors, or a framework topic of this project written without its `<projectCodename>-` prefix, is consumed under the prefixed wire name. The available topics are derived from the selected DataObject's API events and DB events (DB events: `<projectCodename>-<serviceName>-service-dbevent-<objectname>-<created|updated|deleted>`); `getKafkaEventTopicsOfService` lists them.
EventSubTopic.__description.doc: Human-readable description of this topic event.
EventSubTopic.__forceAccessLevel.doc: Override the DataObject's default access level for this specific topic. Leave null (the default) to inherit the owning DataObject's own `dataObjectAccess`; a topic whose DataObject cannot be resolved in this service falls back to 'accessPrivate' and raises an EVENT_SUB_TOPIC_OBJECT_UNRESOLVED warning. Set to 'accessPublic' to make events visible to everyone, 'accessProtected' for all authenticated users, or 'accessPrivate' to require ownership.
EventSubTopic.__payloadMapping.doc: MScript expression that builds the client-facing payload from the event. Context: 'data' (the event record, the envelope's data) and 'event' (the whole event envelope: id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data, old). Its value is what the subscriber receives, then excludeFields is applied. A mapping that throws drops that event for that subscriber (logged, rate-limited); the full record is never sent in its place. Compiled into the generated service at build time. Example: `{ "js": "{ orderId: data.id, status: data.status, updatedAt: data.updatedAt }" }`. If omitted, the record is sent (minus excludeFields).
EventSubTopic.__excludeFields.doc: List of field names to strip from the payload before sending to clients. Applied after payloadMapping (if defined) or on the raw payload. Use to hide sensitive/internal fields. Example: ['internalNotes', 'costBreakdown', 'adminFlags'].
EventSubTopic.__excludeFields.doc_array: Field names to remove from the event payload before delivering to clients.
EventSubTopic.name: String

__EventSubAuth.doc: Authorization configuration for this event subscription. Default auth derives from each topic's DataObject access level -- public topics are open, protected topics require authentication (+ tenant filtering in multi-tenant), private topics require ownership (or admin role if no ownership field exists). The designer can add absoluteRoles to bypass all checks, checkRoles to gate access, and custom MScript auth/filter logic.

EventSubAuth.__absoluteRoles.doc: List of role names (from session.roleId) that bypass ALL authorization checks. Users with any of these roles receive all topics in the subscription without filtering. Examples: ['superAdmin'], ['superAdmin', 'systemAdmin'].
EventSubAuth.__checkRoles.doc: List of role names REQUIRED to use this subscription. If defined, users whose roleId is NOT in this list are rejected entirely. Use to restrict subscriptions to specific user tiers. Examples: ['admin', 'tenantAdmin', 'salesManager']. Leave empty to allow all authenticated users.
EventSubAuth.__authScript.doc: MScript evaluated at subscribe time for each requested topic, after the role and access-level checks (absoluteRoles holders are checked by it too). Must return a boolean. Context: 'session' (user session), 'topicName' (the authored Kafka topic string), 'dataObjectName' (the DataObject name). Return false to reject the topic for this user (reason `Rejected by auth script`); a script that throws rejects it too (reason `Auth script error`, logged). Compiled into the generated service at build time. Example: `{ "js": "session.subscriptionLevel >= 2 || dataObjectName == 'PublicFeed'" }`.
EventSubAuth.__filterScript.doc: MScript evaluated for each incoming Kafka event before delivery, after the default owner / tenant filter. Must return a boolean. Context: 'session' (user session), 'topicName' (the authored Kafka topic string), 'dataObjectName' (the DataObject name), 'data' (the event record, the envelope's data), 'event' (the whole event envelope: id, type, source, time, requestId, actor, data, old). Return false to skip this event for this user. A script that throws skips the event for that user (logged, rate-limited); the stream itself keeps running. Compiled into the generated service at build time. Example: `{ "js": "data.priority >= session.minPriority" }`.
EventSubAuth.__absoluteRoles.doc_array: Roles that bypass all authorization checks and receive all events unfiltered.
EventSubAuth.__checkRoles.doc_array: Roles required to subscribe. Users without one of these roles are denied.

__DbBucket.doc: A database-backed file storage bucket. Stores files as BYTEA in PostgreSQL — ideal for small files like icons, avatars, and secret documents (up to 10 MB by default). Each bucket auto-generates a data object ({name}File) with metadata properties and a BYTEA column, system upload/download routes at /bucket/{name}/, and metadata CRUD APIs. Supports configurable authorization (public/private/authenticated read, role-based access, custom auth scripts) and optional pairing with an owner data object for relational file management. Prefer RemoteBucket for large files stored at your configured cloud provider, or NativeBucket for platform-managed object storage without a cloud provider.
__SeedData.doc: A declarative seed-data record upserted into one of the service's DataObjects at service startup, after migrations run and after the kafka producer is wired. That order means the tables exist and each seeded row's create/update publishes its db-event and elastic-index messages like any other write. Each entry is `{ seedBasics, values }`: `seedBasics` holds the record's identity and upsert policy — the target `dataObject`, the `matchBy` set of property names used to locate an existing row (the idempotency key), and the `insertOnly` names seeded once and never refreshed — and `values` is the map (property → MScript) describing the record to insert when absent or refresh when present. A legacy entry carrying `dataObject`/`matchBy`/`insertOnly` FLAT beside `values` is auto-migrated into `seedBasics` with a warning, so author the nested shape. Generated as a `seed-data` BootstrapModule that runs once on boot via the db-layer. Replaces hand-written bootstrap routines (super-admin / root-tenant / admin-group); reusable by any custom service that needs initial system records. The SAME data object may appear in multiple SeedData entries (e.g. one row per subscription plan); each entry upserts independently, keyed by its `matchBy` values, so rows of one object must differ in their seeded matchBy values (SEED_ROW_NOT_DISTINGUISHABLE otherwise). Each row persists in its own storage slot keyed by that matchBy identity, so N rows survive write→read intact; the item-addressed `seedData/{<dataObject>}` path resolves the object's full row set (a single row object, or an array when several rows are stored).

SeedData.__values.doc: The record to write, as a list of property → MScript value items. Values may be literals or MScript expressions. Values for `hashed` DataProperties (e.g. password) must be PLAINTEXT — the db-layer create/update bcrypts them once on write, so pre-hashing would double-hash and make the row unauthenticatable. The seed scope provides an `md5(text)` helper for avatar fields. Compiled exactly like a BusinessApi dataClauseItems map.
SeedData.__seedBasics.doc: Target DataObject, the matchBy idempotency key, and the insert-only value names.

__SeedDataBasics.doc: Identity and upsert policy of one seed record: the target DataObject, the matchBy idempotency key, and the value names that are seeded once and never refreshed.

SeedDataBasics.__dataObject.doc: The target DataObject to upsert into. The generator resolves the db-layer get/create/update helpers from this name.
SeedDataBasics.__matchBy.doc: Property names that identify an existing row (the idempotency key). On boot the seeder looks a row up by these properties — reading each one's value from `values` — and inserts if none is found, otherwise refreshes the `values`. Defaults to ['id'] when empty.
SeedDataBasics.__insertOnly.doc: Value names (from `values`) that are seeded ONLY when the row is first inserted and never refreshed on a later boot. Values for `hashed` DataProperties (credentials) are always insert-only, implicitly; list a name here to give a non-hashed value the same seed-once contract — e.g. the super-admin `passwordChangeRequired` bootstrap flag, which a runtime password rotation clears and a reboot must not re-set.

__OAuthFlow.doc: A declarative OAuth redirect flow hosted by the service. Each flow exposes its own REST start route (redirects the browser to the provider's authorize URL) and callback route (exchanges the code for a token and fetches the user's profile via the config-driven common OAuth runtime). On the auth service the callback completes the login (find-or-register the user + mint a session) and stashes a one-time `socialCode` result the portal exchanges; every flow also publishes its `completeKafkaTopic` completion event so other services can react. Replaces the hand-written social-login router. Provider credentials come from env (e.g. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET; Apple uses TEAM_ID/KEY_ID/PRIVATE_KEY for its ES256 client secret).

OAuthFlow.__grants.doc: Identity grants — which application user identities this provider VERIFIES. Each grant maps a user verification column (e.g. emailVerified, mobileVerified) to a condition over the normalized OAuth `profile`; when the condition is truthy the runtime marks that identity verified — at login (flips the existing user's flag) and at registration (the bare-socialCode grant the register flow consumes server-side). Provider-intrinsic: a new provider (incl. KYC/wallet providers granting extra identities like a verified real name) arranges its grants here, never trusting a client-supplied flag. Most email-based providers grant `emailVerified` when `profile.emailVerified === true`; `profile.emailVerified` is the value flowBasics.emailVerification decided, not the raw provider answer. The grants do NOT decide whether a sign-in may reach an existing account: that is flowBasics.emailVerification alone. An emailVerified grant is always capped by that decision: a condition other than the canonical `profile.emailVerified === true` is evaluated ANDed with it, so it can narrow flowBasics.emailVerification but never widen it, and design time warns about it (OAUTH_EMAIL_VERIFIED_GRANT_NOT_CANONICAL).
OAuthFlow.__flowBasics.doc: Provider binding, scopes, start/callback routes, completion topic and the register policy.

__OAuthFlowBasics.doc: Identity and transport of one OAuth flow: the provider it binds to, the requested scopes, the start/callback route shape, the completion Kafka topic, and whether an unknown identity may register.

OAuthFlowBasics.__provider.doc: The OAuth provider key — one of google, apple, facebook, microsoft, github, gitlab, linkedin. Selects the authorize URL, token endpoint, profile endpoint, and credential env-var names in the common OAuth runtime.
OAuthFlowBasics.__scopes.doc: Optional space- or comma-separated scope override. When empty, the provider's default scopes are used (e.g. 'profile email' for google).
OAuthFlowBasics.__startPath.doc: REST path of the start route that redirects to the provider (e.g. '/auth/google'). Defaults to '/auth/<provider>'.
OAuthFlowBasics.__callbackPath.doc: REST path the provider redirects back to (e.g. '/auth/google/callback'). Defaults to '/auth/<provider>/callback'.
OAuthFlowBasics.__callbackMethod.doc: HTTP method of the callback route. GET for most providers; Apple posts the result (form_post), so it uses POST.
OAuthFlowBasics.__completeKafkaTopic.doc: Topic the callback publishes the OAuth completion event to (the normalized profile + outcome). On the auth service this is the social-login-complete topic; other services can consume it. Defaults to '<codename>-auth-service-oauth-complete'.
OAuthFlowBasics.__allowRegister.doc: When true (default), an OAuth login for an unknown email flags a needs-registration result the portal can complete; when false, unknown users are rejected.
OAuthFlowBasics.__emailVerification.doc: When a sign-in through this flow counts the profile email as verified: 'providerSignal' (default, the runtime's per-provider verification signal), 'requireVerification' (never) or 'trusted' (always). The callback applies it before anything else reads the profile: the identity grants see the decided emailVerified, and a sign-in reaches an EXISTING account with the profile email ONLY when the email counts as verified; otherwise it is refused with 403 errMsg_SocialLoginEmailNotVerified. A host that owns a userSocialAccount object matches the provider account link (provider + the profile subject) first, which reaches the linked user whatever this setting decides, and links the provider account at a verified-email match only when that user has no link for this provider. If the user already has a different subject linked for that provider, the email fallback is refused with 403 errMsg_AccountLinkedToAnotherProviderAccount, including in trusted mode; adding another subject requires authenticated, explicit linking. The auth service fills it from authentication.socialLogins.<provider>.emailVerification; an authored flow sets it here.

__OAuthIdentityGrant.doc: A single identity grant on an OAuthFlow: the provider VERIFIES `identity` (a user verification column) when `condition` (a JS expression over the normalized OAuth `profile`) is truthy. Applied by the OAuth runtime at login and registration to mark identities verified server-side.

OAuthIdentityGrant.__identity.doc: The user verification column this grant marks true when satisfied (e.g. 'emailVerified', 'mobileVerified'; future KYC providers: 'realNameVerified').
OAuthIdentityGrant.__condition.doc: A JS boolean expression over the normalized OAuth `profile` (e.g. "profile.emailVerified === true"). Evaluated by the runtime; truthy ⇒ the identity is granted. NOT MScript — emitted verbatim into the generated controller. For an emailVerified grant the generated callback also requires the flow's emailVerification decision (profile.emailVerified === true), so a non-canonical condition only narrows it.

DbBucket.__bucketBasics.doc: Core bucket settings: name, description, size limits, allowed file types and antivirus scanning.
DbBucket.__bucketAuthorization.doc: Read/write authorization for the bucket — who can upload and download files, via role-based access, access keys, or custom authorization scripts.
DbBucket.__ownerDataObject.doc: Optional pairing with an owner data object — each file gains a foreign-key relation to it (e.g. a product's images, a user's documents), enabling owner-filtered listing and cascading deletes.

__DbBucketBasics.doc: Core settings for the database bucket including its name, description, size limits, allowed file types, and antivirus scanning.

DbBucketBasics.__name.doc: Unique bucket identifier within the service. Used in route paths (/bucket/{name}/), table names ({name}File), and API names. Must be a valid codeName.
DbBucketBasics.name: String
DbBucketBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this bucket stores (e.g., 'User avatar images', 'Product photos', 'Signed contracts').
DbBucketBasics.__maxFileSizeMb.doc: Maximum allowed file size in megabytes. Files exceeding this limit are rejected at upload time. Default: 10 MB.
DbBucketBasics.__allowedMimeTypes.doc: Comma-separated list of allowed MIME types (e.g., 'image/png,image/jpeg,application/pdf'). If null, all MIME types are accepted. Each entry is either an exact 'type/subtype', a family wildcard 'type/*' (so 'image/*' accepts image/png, image/jpeg and every other image subtype) or '*/*' (any type); matching is case-insensitive and ignores ';' parameters, and any other shape (no slash, '*/png', ...) fails generation naming the bucket and the entry. NOTE: the runtime additionally sniffs the file's magic bytes via the file-type package — a client-spoofed Content-Type header will be rejected when the sniffed type doesn't match. ACTIVE CONTENT (HTML, XHTML, SVG, every JavaScript type, XML and any +xml type) is kept as its type only when that exact type is listed here; a wildcard ('image/*', '*/*') or no list does not admit it. An upload whose bytes, declared type or file name say active content and that is not listed by its exact name is still accepted but stored as application/octet-stream, its original name kept and its active extension left out of the storage key. Every active object is served as a download, never rendered: DbBucket downloads always send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Disposition: attachment (plus Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox for an active type), and a presigned download of an active object is signed with an attachment disposition and application/octet-stream. Generated by the nodejs, java, dotnet and python lanes.
DbBucketBasics.__virusScan.doc: When true, every uploaded file is scanned by ClamAV (configured under projectSettings.clamAvSettings, defaults to the platform ClamAV REST service at the default ClamAV host) before the file row is created. The scan is a property of the ROW, not of the upload route: EVERY path that creates a {name}File row runs it - the bucket's own upload route, a business api or designer action that writes the row itself (including a public loginRequired:false intake api, which cannot reach the upload route at all because DbBucketWriteLevel has no 'public' value), a bulk create, a seed and an in-process internal writer. An update that REPLACES the byte column is scanned too, so a clean insert followed by a payload update is not a way around it. Auto-promoted to true at generation time when bucketAuthorization.readAccess is 'public'. The outcome is recorded in the virusScanStatus column of the generated {name}File data object ('clean' | 'infected' | 'quarantined' | 'error' | 'skipped'), which the guard stamps on every scanned path - a caller cannot supply it.
DbBucketBasics.__virusScanMode.doc: How a REJECTION is reported, and whether an infected file becomes a row at all. 'block' persists nothing: on the upload route the caller gets HTTP 422 VIRUS_DETECTED (or 503 VIRUS_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE when the scanner could not run) before any row exists, and at the row-creation seam the write is refused by a THROWN typed error carrying the same status and errorCode - a business api answers 422/503 with it, a designer action propagates it under its own error policy, and a seed or internal writer fails loudly. It is never reported in band as a success. 'quarantine' persists the row already carrying virusScanStatus='quarantined' and refuses downloads of it, which is useful when you want a forensic trail or to notify the user out-of-band. The scan is AWAITED before the write on every path, so a row never exists without a verdict and there is no 'pending' state. If null, falls back to projectSettings.clamAvSettings.configuration.defaultMode (default: 'block'). That resolution happens at DESIGN time and is baked into the generated service as a literal. A deployment can still override it at runtime by setting the CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE env var to 'block' or 'quarantine' (an operational escape hatch that works in both directions); leaving it unset, empty or unrecognised means no override and this per-bucket value wins. Whether a scan that could not RUN blocks is CLAMAV_ON_ERROR (runtime default reject): the generated dev, test (preview) and stage env files of a service with a virus-scanning bucket set it to skip, so an unreachable scanner records virusScanStatus='error' and lets the file through there, while prod keeps reject; a blueprint custom variable CLAMAV_ON_ERROR overrides it on every slot. Lane status: the row-level seam (scan before every row write, verdict stamped by the framework) is honoured in nodejs, dotnet and java, and emitted by the python and golang db layers too; the DbBucket upload-route scan is honoured in nodejs, dotnet and python (java has no DbBucket upload route yet), and golang bakes the per-bucket literal and lets CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE override it in both directions; rust honours it but cannot be overridden back down to 'block'.

__DbBucketAuthorization.doc: Authorization settings for read and write access to the bucket. Controls who can upload and download files, with support for role-based access, access keys, and custom authorization scripts.

DbBucketAuthorization.__readAccess.doc: Controls who can download files from this bucket. 'public' = anyone, no session required, 'private' = only the file owner and admins (the owner is the account that uploaded the file, compared against the session-stamped uploaderUserId on the file row), 'authenticated' = any authenticated user, including other users' files, 'roles' = only holders of a readCheckRoles role. Sessionless per-file key downloads are governed separately by enableKeyAccess.
DbBucketAuthorization.__writeAccess.doc: Controls who can UPLOAD files to this bucket, and nothing else. 'authenticated' = any authenticated user, 'adminOnly' = only admin roles, 'roles' = only holders of a writeCheckRoles role. Deleting is governed separately by deleteAccess — before that split this same field gated DELETE too, so its default handed every registered account a delete primitive over every other user's files.
DbBucketAuthorization.__deleteAccess.doc: Controls who can DELETE files from this bucket — a separate decision from writeAccess, which governs upload only. 'owner' (the DEFAULT) = only the account that uploaded the file, plus admin roles. 'adminOnly' = only admin roles. 'authenticated' = ANY authenticated user may delete ANY file in the bucket, including other users' files; that is the earlier behaviour and is kept only as a deliberate opt-in. The delete gate NARROWS writeAccess and never widens it: a bucket with writeAccess 'adminOnly' stays admin-only for deletes whatever this field says. Ownership is read from the file row's uploaderUserId. RemoteBucket and NativeBucket deletes address a raw storage key: the nodejs router resolves the owner from the uploaderUserId of that key's {name}RemoteFile twin row, which its through-server /upload writes; a key with no twin row (a presigned /upload-url upload) or no recorded uploader, and the language targets that persist no twin, deny every non-admin (fail closed); widen those deliberately with 'authenticated', 'adminOnly' or writeAbsoluteRoles.
DbBucketAuthorization.__enableKeyAccess.doc: When true, any holder of a file's 12-character access key can download that file with NO session, on every bucket kind: DbBucket serves GET .../download/key/:accessKey directly, and RemoteBucket/NativeBucket honour ?accessKey= on the download route (the key is minted on the upload / upload-url response). When false or absent (the DEFAULT), key-based lookup stays behind the normal readAccess gate. Useful for shareable links; treat the key as a per-file capability credential. Unrelated to API keys, which represent a user's own rights and never grant extra authorization.
DbBucketAuthorization.__readAbsoluteRoles.doc: Roles that bypass all read authorization checks. Users with any of these roles can always download files. Every name must be a defined role; an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning.
DbBucketAuthorization.__readCheckRoles.doc: Roles required for read access when readAccess is 'roles': the user must hold at least one of them to download. Consulted ONLY by that mode — under 'public', 'private' or 'authenticated' this list has no effect. An empty list under 'roles' behaves like 'authenticated'. Every name must be a defined role (a system role, a roleItems name or value, or a customRoleLookups name): an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning, and a list whose every name is undefined while the access mode is 'roles' and readAbsoluteRoles names no defined role is that code as an error, because the bucket then admits no defined-role session.
DbBucketAuthorization.__writeAbsoluteRoles.doc: Roles that bypass all write authorization checks. Users with any of these roles can always upload files. Every name must be a defined role; an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning.
DbBucketAuthorization.__writeCheckRoles.doc: Roles required for write access when writeAccess is 'roles': the user must hold at least one of them to upload. Consulted ONLY by that mode — under 'authenticated' or 'adminOnly' this list has no effect. An empty list under 'roles' behaves like 'authenticated'. Every name must be a defined role (a system role, a roleItems name or value, or a customRoleLookups name): an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning, and a list whose every name is undefined while the access mode is 'roles' and writeAbsoluteRoles names no defined role is that code as an error, because the bucket then admits no defined-role session.
DbBucketAuthorization.__readAuthScript.doc: Custom MScript expression for read authorization; must return true to allow the download. Evaluated after the coarse readAccess/role checks and can only NARROW them — absoluteRoles still bypass everything. The request context IS the script receiver, so every field is reachable both as this.<field> (the platform-wide MScript convention) and as a bare name: session, userId, role, params, query, body, data. On a READ gate data is the FILE ROW: the script runs after the coarse checks allowed and after the file row is looked up (the DbBucket file row, or the {name}RemoteFile twin found by storageKey on a Remote/Native bucket), so a per-file rule such as this.data?.uploaderUserId === this.session?.userId is expressible. A key that resolves to no row is answered as missing (404) without running the script, so a script never reveals which keys exist. A denied file answers the same 404 NOT_FOUND as a missing one (no existence oracle), and a script that throws denies the same way. Example: this.session?.userId === this.params.ownerId.
DbBucketAuthorization.__writeAuthScript.doc: Custom MScript expression for write authorization; must return true to allow the upload. Evaluated after the coarse writeAccess/role checks and can only NARROW them — absoluteRoles still bypass everything. The request context IS the script receiver, so every field is reachable both as this.<field> (the platform-wide MScript convention) and as a bare name: session, userId, role, params, query, body, data. On a WRITE gate data is the request body, i.e. the upload metadata being stored. A script that throws denies. Example: this.session?.userId === this.data?.ownerId.

__DbBucketAccessLevel.doc.#: Read access levels for database buckets.
__DbBucketAccessLevel.doc.public: Anyone can download files — no authentication required.
__DbBucketAccessLevel.doc.private: Only the file owner and admin roles can download. The owner is the account that uploaded the file (the session-stamped uploaderUserId on the file row), never the ownerDataObject foreign key. This is the default.
__DbBucketAccessLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can download, including files uploaded by other users.
__DbBucketAccessLevel.doc.roles: Only users holding at least one of the roles in readCheckRoles can download. An empty readCheckRoles list behaves like 'authenticated'. readAbsoluteRoles bypasses this like every other mode.

__DbBucketWriteLevel.doc.#: Write access levels for database buckets.
__DbBucketWriteLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can upload files.
__DbBucketWriteLevel.doc.adminOnly: Only the project's platform operator roles can upload: superAdmin and saasAdmin on a multi-tenant project; superAdmin, admin and saasAdmin on a single-tenant project. Tenant administrators such as tenantAdmin are not admitted.
__DbBucketWriteLevel.doc.roles: Only users holding at least one of the roles in writeCheckRoles can upload. An empty writeCheckRoles list behaves like 'authenticated'. writeAbsoluteRoles bypasses this like every other mode. deleteAccess still narrows deletes separately.

__DbBucketDeleteLevel.doc.#: Delete access levels for database buckets. Separate from DbBucketWriteLevel, which governs upload only.
__DbBucketDeleteLevel.doc.owner: Only the account that uploaded the file, plus admin roles, can delete it. This is the default.
__DbBucketDeleteLevel.doc.adminOnly: Only the project's platform operator roles can delete: superAdmin and saasAdmin on a multi-tenant project; superAdmin, admin and saasAdmin on a single-tenant project. Tenant administrators such as tenantAdmin are not admitted.
__DbBucketDeleteLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can delete any file in the bucket, including files uploaded by someone else. Opt in deliberately.

__BucketVirusScanMode.doc.#: How a bucket reacts when an upload is flagged as infected by ClamAV.
__BucketVirusScanMode.doc.block: Reject the upload with HTTP 422; nothing is persisted and (for RemoteBucket) nothing is written to the storage provider.
__BucketVirusScanMode.doc.quarantine: Persist the metadata row with scanStatus='infected' (and for RemoteBucket, upload to a quarantine-prefixed key); refuse all download routes for infected records.

__CronJobRunMode.doc.#: How often a CronJob may succeed (CronJob.runMode).
__CronJobRunMode.doc.always: Run on every tick of the schedule.
__CronJobRunMode.doc.onceEver: Run until one run succeeds, then never again: on no replica, after no restart and after no redeploy. A failed or timed-out run does not count.
__CronJobRunMode.doc.oncePerStart: Run until one run succeeds in the current start era of the service. A new era begins with a new build, a new deployment revision (a rollout or rollout restart), or when every replica has stopped; a single replica restarting while others of its revision stay alive stays in the era.

__ServiceFileVisibility.doc.#: Who can reach a service file (ServiceFile.visibility).
__ServiceFileVisibility.doc.public: Served at `GET <serviceBaseUrl>/service-files/<path>` on nodejs services, and readable through `LIB.serviceFiles.*`.
__ServiceFileVisibility.doc.private: Not served; readable only through `LIB.serviceFiles.*`. Still visible to anyone who can read the service repo, so never a place for credentials.

__ClamAvProtocol.doc.#: How the runtime scanner talks to ClamAV (ClamAvSettingsConfig.protocol).
__ClamAvProtocol.doc.rest: The ClamAV REST contract of the platform service: POST <url>/api/v1/scan, multipart field FILES, one file per request, at most 100 MB, answer { success, data: { result: [ { name, is_infected, viruses } ] } }.
__ClamAvProtocol.doc.clamd: A self-hosted clamd daemon spoken to with INSTREAM over TCP on host:port.

__DbBucketOwnerConfig.doc: Optional pairing with another data object. When configured, each file in the bucket has a foreign key relation to the owner data object (e.g., a product's images, a user's documents). This enables filtering files by owner and cascading deletes.

DbBucketOwnerConfig.__hasOwnerDataObject.doc: Enable pairing this bucket with a data object. When true, each file record includes a foreign key to the specified data object.
DbBucketOwnerConfig.__configuration.doc: Configuration for the owner data-object pairing.

__DbBucketOwnerConfigSettings.doc: Configuration for the owner data object pairing.

DbBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__dataObjectName.doc: The data object to pair with (e.g., 'user', 'product'). Files in this bucket will have a relation ID pointing to records in this data object.
DbBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__relationProperty.doc: Property name for the relation ID on the bucket file record. If null, auto-generated as '{dataObjectName}Id' (e.g., 'productId'). Must be a valid codeName.
DbBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__downloadRequiresActiveOwner.doc: When true, every route of this bucket that hands back the file (download by storage key, access key or row id, the DbBucket /shared link, and the DbBucket metadata route GET /bucket/{bucket}/object/:key, which returns the file's whole row minus its byte columns) loads the file's metadata row and then the paired owner row through the owner data object's default read, which excludes soft-deleted (isActive=false) rows; if the file has no metadata row, no owner id, or the owner row is missing or inactive, the route answers 404 NOT_FOUND instead of serving the file. Evaluated AFTER the bucket's read gate, so an unauthorised caller still gets 401/403 and learns nothing. Model 'hidden' or 'merged' owners as soft-deleted rows (or any state the default read excludes) for this to apply. For RemoteBucket/NativeBucket the metadata row is the {name}RemoteFile twin looked up by storageKey, which your own managers must persist at upload (the router does not); a file without one is not served. Requires a local (same-service) owner data object. Default false: downloads never consult the owner row.

__RemoteBucket.doc: A cloud-storage-backed file bucket. Files are uploaded to an external storage provider (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, R2, or any S3-compatible store) and only their metadata is stored in the service database. Each bucket auto-generates a data object ({name}RemoteFile) with file metadata (fileName, mimeType, fileSize, storageKey, accessKey, uploaderUserId, the scan columns, etc.; designer-declared extra columns go in remoteBucketSettings.additionalColumns), system upload/download routes at /bucket/{name}/ (POST /upload multipart, POST /upload-url presigned, GET /download/:key, DELETE /object/:key — the /remotebucket/{name}/ prefix older docs cite is not mounted), and metadata CRUD APIs. Supports presigned-URL or proxy-stream download strategies, configurable authorization (public/private/authenticated read, role-based access, custom auth scripts), and optional pairing with an owner data object. Use for large files, images, videos, and documents where DbBucket's BYTEA blob storage isn't appropriate. Prefer NativeBucket when you want platform-managed object storage without configuring a cloud provider.

RemoteBucket.__bucketBasics.doc: Core bucket settings: name, description, size limits, allowed file types and antivirus scanning.
RemoteBucket.__bucketStorage.doc: Storage configuration: which named project `bucketProvider` to use, the optional physical bucket override, and how download URLs are generated.
RemoteBucket.__bucketAuthorization.doc: Read/write authorization for the remote bucket — who can upload and download files, via role-based access, access keys, or custom authorization scripts.
RemoteBucket.__ownerDataObject.doc: Optional pairing with an owner data object — each file gains a foreign-key relation to it (e.g. a product's images, a user's documents), enabling owner-filtered listing and cascading deletes.
RemoteBucket.__remoteBucketSettings.doc: Optional extension settings of the bucket's auto-generated {name}RemoteFile metadata data object. additionalColumns appends designer-declared columns after its base columns; compositeIndexSettings declares composite indexes over the twin's base, owner, tenant and additional columns using the normal DataObject CompositeIndex shape. Leave null for the fixed column set and no composite indexes.

__RemoteBucketSettings.doc: Extension settings of a RemoteBucket's auto-generated {name}RemoteFile metadata data object. The twin keeps its framework-owned base columns; this section adds designer-declared columns to it.

RemoteBucketSettings.__additionalColumns.doc: Extra columns of the {name}RemoteFile twin: full DataProperty declarations (type, enum options, default, relation, index settings), validated like the properties of an authored data object and appended after the base columns (fileName, mimeType, fileSize, storageKey, accessKey, uploaderUserId, scanStatus, scanResult, scannedAt), the owner foreign key and the tenant column. A name may not repeat one of those columns or a framework system column, case-insensitively (REMOTE_BUCKET_COLUMN_NAME_RESERVED). The upload route writes the base columns plus the columns flagged uploadSettings.fromUploadField (from the multipart field of the same name, when sent), so a required column must declare a defaultValue or defaultFn (REMOTE_BUCKET_COLUMN_REQUIRED_WITHOUT_DEFAULT); the other extra columns are written through createCrudActions / updateCrudActions and BusinessApis on the twin. A relation column may not point at a virtual data object. Adding a column to an already deployed twin goes through the boot-time schema sync, which adds it to the existing table and fills existing rows with its default (NULL for an optional column without one). Generated by the nodejs, java, dotnet, rust and python lanes; golang persists no twin, so the columns have no effect there.
RemoteBucketSettings.__compositeIndexSettings.doc: Composite indexes on the {name}RemoteFile twin, for RemoteBucket and NativeBucket. Each entry uses the normal CompositeIndex contract: indexName, ordered indexFields, onDuplicate and optional partialWhere. Field references must resolve to a base column, the configured owner foreign key, the tenant column or an additionalColumn. Use onDuplicate exactly as on a DataObject to select duplicate handling and uniqueness; there is no isUnique flag. For example, an index named ticketStatus with indexFields [ticketId, status] and onDuplicate doInsert is a lookup index. The same property validation and partial-index restrictions as an authored data object apply. The nodejs, java, dotnet and python generators share the twin injector. Rust has a separate twin injector that must mirror these indexes; golang persists no twin.

__RemoteBucketBasics.doc: Core settings for the remote bucket including its name, description, size limits, allowed file types, and antivirus scanning.

RemoteBucketBasics.__name.doc: Unique bucket identifier within the service. Used in route paths (/bucket/{name}/ — not /remotebucket/{name}/), table names ({name}RemoteFile), and API names. Must be a valid codeName.
RemoteBucketBasics.name: String
RemoteBucketBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of what this bucket stores (e.g., 'Product images', 'User documents', 'Video uploads').
RemoteBucketBasics.__maxFileSizeMb.doc: Maximum allowed file size in megabytes. Files exceeding this limit are rejected at upload time. Default: 100 MB (remote buckets can handle larger files than DbBuckets).
RemoteBucketBasics.__allowedMimeTypes.doc: Comma-separated list of allowed MIME types (e.g., 'image/png,image/jpeg,application/pdf'). If null, all MIME types are accepted. Each entry is either an exact 'type/subtype', a family wildcard 'type/*' (so 'image/*' accepts image/png, image/jpeg and every other image subtype) or '*/*' (any type); matching is case-insensitive and ignores ';' parameters, and any other shape (no slash, '*/png', ...) fails generation naming the bucket and the entry. NOTE: the runtime additionally sniffs the file's magic bytes via the file-type package — declared signature-bearing types must match the known sniff, regardless of the bucket allow-list; unknown signatures are refused. The only compatible exceptions are APNG declared PNG and Illustrator PDF declared PDF with a %PDF- container; these keep their declared type. ACTIVE CONTENT (HTML, XHTML, SVG, every JavaScript type, XML and any +xml type) is kept as its type only when that exact type is listed here; a wildcard ('image/*', '*/*') or no list does not admit it. An upload whose bytes, declared type or file name say active content and that is not listed by its exact name is still accepted but stored as application/octet-stream, its original name kept and its active extension left out of the storage key. Active objects default to attachment; serveActiveInline permits an exact declared type only on an isolated storage origin: DbBucket downloads always send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Disposition: attachment (plus Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox for an active type), and a presigned download of an active object is signed with an attachment disposition and application/octet-stream. Generated by the nodejs, java, dotnet and python lanes.
RemoteBucketBasics.__virusScan.doc: When true, every uploaded file is scanned by ClamAV (configured under projectSettings.clamAvSettings, defaults to the platform ClamAV REST service, the field's default value) BEFORE it is written to the storage provider. Auto-promoted to true at generation time when bucketAuthorization.readAccess is 'public'. Adds scanStatus / scanResult / scannedAt columns to the generated {name}RemoteFile data object. WHERE THE GUARANTEE APPLIES: the bytes of a RemoteBucket live in the storage provider and never in the row, so unlike a DbBucket this scan cannot move down to row creation - there is nothing in a {name}RemoteFile row to scan. It covers exactly the through-server upload route (POST /bucket/{name}/upload). Two paths are therefore NOT scanned and the designer must choose them knowingly: a presigned PUT from /upload-url goes straight to the provider without passing through this service, and a business api that writes a {name}RemoteFile row itself records a storageKey for bytes nothing here ever saw. An intake that must accept files from anonymous or untrusted callers should use a DbBucket, whose scan is attached to the row. Scanned buckets emit /upload-url only with allowPresignedUpload: true; validation warns whenever scanning and that opt-in are both enabled.
RemoteBucketBasics.__virusScanMode.doc: How the upload route responds when ClamAV reports an infection - for a RemoteBucket this is a property of that route, because the bytes never enter a row (see virusScan above). 'block' rejects the upload with HTTP 422 and nothing is written to the remote provider. 'quarantine' uploads to a quarantine key prefix and persists the row with scanStatus='infected', refusing both presigned URLs and proxy downloads of infected records. If null, falls back to projectSettings.clamAvSettings.configuration.defaultMode (default: 'block'). That resolution happens at DESIGN time and is baked into the generated service as a literal. A deployment can still override it at runtime by setting the CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE env var to 'block' or 'quarantine' (an operational escape hatch that works in both directions); leaving it unset, empty or unrecognised means no override and this per-bucket value wins. Lane status: honoured in nodejs, dotnet, python, php and golang (golang bakes the per-bucket literal and lets CLAMAV_DEFAULT_MODE override it in both directions), and rust honours it but cannot be overridden back down to 'block'.
RemoteBucketBasics.__imageVariants.doc: Resized copies (thumbnails, previews) the bucket creates for every image it stores. Each entry names one variant (`thumb`, `preview`, ...) and how to produce it; the declaration compiles into the generated upload route, which creates every variant SYNCHRONOUSLY with the `sharp` image library right after the original is written, before it answers. The ORIGINAL is stored unchanged; a variant is a separate object in the SAME bucket at the deterministic key `<original key without extension>__<variant name>.<format>` (for example `catalog/abc.jpg` gives `catalog/abc__thumb.webp`), auto-oriented from EXIF and stripped of metadata. The result is recorded on the `{name}RemoteFile` twin row in its `variants` column as `{ <name>: { key, url, width, height, format, size } }` and returned by the upload response; because the twin row is what the bucket's create and update events carry, a service that copies the file into a snapshot reads `variants.<name>.url` from the event. The `url` is the bucket's own download route with `?variant=<name>` (`{SERVICE_URL}/bucket/{name}/download/<original key>?variant=<name>`), which redirects to a presigned URL of the variant and falls back to the original (header `X-Bucket-Variant: original`) when the variant is not recorded. Only images the bucket itself stores are processed, recognised by their BYTES (a jpeg, png, webp, gif, avif/heif or tiff signature; an svg or any other document gets none, whatever type it declares), uploaded through POST /bucket/{name}/upload (and the in-process writeBucketObject helper). Inputs above 50 megapixels are a recorded failure, and at most IMAGE_VARIANT_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) variants render at once per process. A variant object is served only through ?variant= on its original; its own key answers 404 on the download and delete routes. Other content types, quarantined uploads and presigned /upload-url uploads (whose bytes never pass through the service) get no variants and never fail because of them; external URLs are never fetched. A variant that cannot be produced does NOT fail the upload: the original is kept, the upload answers ok, and the variant is recorded as `{ error }` so the admin backfill route POST /bucket/{name}/variants/backfill (admin roles) can create it later; that route also creates the variants of objects stored before the declaration, page by page, and skips variants that already exist. Deleting the original through DELETE /bucket/{name}/object/:key also deletes its variants. Declaring variants adds the `sharp` npm dependency to the generated service.
