Implemented for RemoteBucket in the nodejs target; on a NativeBucket the declaration is accepted with a warning and has no effect yet.
RemoteBucketBasics.__allowPresignedUpload.doc: Explicit opt-in to emit /upload-url when effective virusScan is enabled. Default false. Without it scanned buckets accept bytes only through /upload. Unscanned buckets keep /upload-url. A scanned opt-in bucket reports VIRUS_SCAN_BYPASSED_BY_PRESIGNED_INTAKE because direct provider PUTs are not scanned. Clients must echo every returned upload header; S3 and GCS bind Content-Type and the storage key in the signature. Azure relies on inert download serving.
RemoteBucketBasics.__serveActiveInline.doc: Explicit opt-in for inline active content, default false. Only exact active allowedMimeTypes entries and recorded types qualify. The actual signed storage origin must be HTTPS on a host whose registrable domain matches SERVICE_URL, FRONTEND_URL, ALLOWED_ORIGINS or COOKIE_DOMAINS; provider/shared hosting domains are always refused; both SERVICE_URL and FRONTEND_URL must be configured. Unrelated or provider storage hosts and unknown metadata stay inert. DbBucket refuses this field and proxy responses keep sandbox CSP. Public delivery continues to refuse active types. Supported in nodejs; other runtimes require ports.

__ImageVariant.doc: One resized copy of every image a bucket stores (see RemoteBucketBasics.imageVariants). The variant is produced with `sharp`: auto-orient, resize to `width` (and `height` when set) under `fit`, encode as `format` at `quality`, metadata stripped. The original is never modified.

ImageVariant.__name.doc: Variant name, unique within the bucket (case-insensitive). It is the key of the `variants` record on the twin row, the `?variant=` value of the download route and the suffix of the variant object key (`<key>__<name>.<format>`). Must be an identifier: a letter, then letters, digits or underscores, at most 40 characters.
ImageVariant.name: String
ImageVariant.__width.doc: Target width in pixels, an integer from 1 to 10000. With `fit` inside (the default) and no height, the image is scaled to this width keeping its aspect ratio.
ImageVariant.__height.doc: Optional target height in pixels (1 to 10000). Leave null to derive it from the aspect ratio. cover, contain and fill only differ from inside when a height is set.
ImageVariant.__fit.doc: How the image is fitted to width x height (the sharp `fit` option). Default inside.
ImageVariant.__format.doc: Output format of the variant object, which also gives its key extension and Content-Type. Default webp.
ImageVariant.__quality.doc: Encoder quality from 1 to 100 for webp, jpeg and avif. Default 80. png output is lossless and ignores it.
ImageVariant.__withoutEnlargement.doc: When true (the default), an image smaller than the target is never upscaled: the variant keeps the original dimensions (re-encoded in `format`).

__ImageVariantFit.doc.#: How an image variant is fitted to its target box (sharp resize fit).
__ImageVariantFit.doc.inside: Scale to fit within width x height keeping the aspect ratio; nothing is cropped. With width only: scale to that width.
__ImageVariantFit.doc.cover: Fill the whole box keeping the aspect ratio, cropping the overflow (centered).
__ImageVariantFit.doc.contain: Fit within the box keeping the aspect ratio and pad the rest (transparent, or white for jpeg).
__ImageVariantFit.doc.fill: Stretch to exactly width x height, ignoring the aspect ratio.
__ImageVariantFit.doc.outside: Scale so the image covers at least width x height keeping the aspect ratio; nothing is cropped.

__ImageVariantFormat.doc.#: Output format of an image variant.
__ImageVariantFormat.doc.webp: WebP (image/webp, key extension .webp). The default: small and supported by every current browser.
__ImageVariantFormat.doc.jpeg: JPEG (image/jpeg, key extension .jpeg); transparency is flattened onto white.
__ImageVariantFormat.doc.png: PNG (image/png, key extension .png), lossless; quality is ignored.
__ImageVariantFormat.doc.avif: AVIF (image/avif, key extension .avif); smallest output, slowest to encode.

__RemoteBucketStorage.doc: Storage configuration for the remote bucket. Selects which named project bucketProvider to use, the (optional) physical bucket override, and how download URLs are generated. For object storage without a project bucketProvider, prefer NativeBucket with NativeBucketStorage: the hosting platform manages the store.

RemoteBucketStorage.__providerName.doc: Name of the project-level bucketProvider that holds this bucket's credentials and defaults (configured under projectSettings.bucketProvidersSettings.bucketProviders). The service reads its config from BUCKET_<NAME>_* environment variables at runtime.
RemoteBucketStorage.__remoteBucketName.doc: Optional override for the physical bucket name at the provider. If null, falls back to the bucketProvider's `defaultBucketName`. The bucket must already exist at the provider — it is not auto-created. Names are checked against the bound provider: s3 uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, begins and ends alphanumeric, rejects adjacent dots, IP-shaped names and reserved prefixes/suffixes (including xn-- and -s3alias); r2 uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with alphanumeric ends; gcs allows lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, alphanumeric ends, 3-63 characters without dots or up to 222 with 1-63-character components, and rejects IP-shaped and Google-reserved names; azure uses 3-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with alphanumeric ends and no consecutive hyphens (the reserved containers $root, $web and $logs are allowed). Violations are BUCKET_NAME_INVALID errors, except s3Compatible receives warnings. The exact REPLACE_ME placeholder is a BUCKET_NAME_PLACEHOLDER warning. A RemoteBucket with no effective override or provider default is a REMOTE_BUCKET_NAME_EMPTY error. See the bucket-providers integration guide for details.
RemoteBucketStorage.__keyPrefix.doc: Optional path prefix added to every stored object key (e.g., 'avatars/' produces keys like 'avatars/{uuid}'). Useful when multiple buckets share a single physical provider bucket.
RemoteBucketStorage.__presignTTLSeconds.doc: Lifetime of a presigned URL in seconds. Default 900 (15 minutes). Downloads are always served as a short-lived presigned URL — the service authorizes the request, then the client fetches directly from the storage provider. A presigned URL is a BEARER credential — anyone holding it can fetch the object until it expires, and it CANNOT be revoked early — so the TTL is the exposure window if the URL leaks (logs, Referer headers, shared links). 15 minutes is the common industry range for user-facing downloads. Note a short TTL does NOT truncate large downloads: the signature is checked when the request STARTS, so a transfer that begins before expiry completes normally. Raise it only for batch or machine consumers that hold a URL before using it.
RemoteBucketStorage.__serverSideEncryption.doc: When true, enables server-side encryption at the provider (SSE-S3 for AWS, default encryption for GCS/Azure) by signing `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256` into every upload. Default: false - SSE is OPT-IN. An S3-compatible store with no SSE-S3 key configured (SeaweedFS's default posture, some MinIO builds) answers 500 InternalError to a PUT carrying that header, and because CreateBucket/HeadBucket never touch SSE the failure only surfaces at the first upload. Turn it on when the target store is known to accept SSE-S3 (AWS S3 always does); GCS and Azure encrypt at rest regardless and ignore the flag.
RemoteBucketStorage.__objectCacheControl.doc: Cache-Control this bucket's objects are stored and served with. Null (the default) means the framework value `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, which is right for content-addressed assets and wrong for a bucket that holds mutable documents: set for example `no-cache` for a rendered report rewritten in place through the SDK, `private, max-age=60` for a regulated bucket, `public, max-age=300` for a scratch area. The value is set on BOTH sides of the round trip - the stored object metadata (S3 `CacheControl`, GCS `metadata.cacheControl`, Azure `blobCacheControl`) and the `Cache-Control` entry of the `headers` map the presigned upload returns, plus the signed GET-side response override on S3 (`ResponseCacheControl`) and Azure (`rscc`) - because the read-time override wins over what is stored. GCS has NO cache-control response override (measured), so on GCS the stored value is the only carrier: changing this field applies to objects written AFTER the change and NEVER retroactively to objects already in the bucket. Must be a plausible Cache-Control token list (comma-separated `directive` or `directive=value`); a malformed value is an authoring-time error, because every provider stores the string verbatim and then serves it to every browser.
RemoteBucketStorage.__delivery.doc: How GET /bucket/{name}/download/:key hands out the bytes. 'presigned' (the default) authorizes the request and answers 302 with a fresh short-lived presigned URL and Cache-Control: no-store, because that URL is a bearer credential. 'public' is for a bucket that holds PUBLIC CONTENT only (catalog covers, product images): the route answers 302 to the object's STABLE URL under publicBaseUrl, cacheable with the bucket's object Cache-Control, so browsers and CDNs reuse the bytes across visits; the upload response also returns that URL as publicUrl. A public bucket offers NO presigned upload: POST /bucket/{name}/upload-url answers 405 PRESIGNED_UPLOAD_NOT_OFFERED, because a presigned PUT binds no Content-Type and its body could be served as stored from the public URL; every upload goes through the classifying POST /bucket/{name}/upload. The objects must be publicly readable at the provider (a bucket policy granting read on this bucket's keyPrefix, or a CDN in front of it); the platform does not change provider policies. 'public' is accepted only for a bucket declared as public content, otherwise the design is refused (REMOTE_BUCKET_PUBLIC_DELIVERY_*): bucketAuthorization.readAccess 'public', no readAuthScript, enableKeyAccess off, ownerDataObject.downloadRequiresActiveOwner off, publicBaseUrl set, bucketBasics.allowedMimeTypes declared and listing no active type (HTML, XHTML, SVG, JavaScript, XML), and virusScanMode 'block' (a quarantined object must never sit behind a public URL). An object whose key names an active type is still served through an inert presigned URL. Generated by the nodejs, java, dotnet and python lanes; the other languages keep presigning (warning REMOTE_BUCKET_PUBLIC_DELIVERY_NOT_PORTED).
RemoteBucketStorage.__publicBaseUrl.doc: The https URL that maps to the ROOT of the physical bucket when delivery is 'public': the S3 virtual-hosted URL (https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com), the GCS or Azure container URL, or a CDN / custom domain in front of it. The download route appends the full storage key (keyPrefix included, each segment URL-encoded): a key catalog/book-covers/abc.webp under https://cdn.example.com is served from https://cdn.example.com/catalog/book-covers/abc.webp. Must be an absolute https URL with no query string or fragment; a trailing slash is ignored. Required when delivery is 'public', ignored otherwise. Do not use a subdomain of the application's own domain: the storage origin serves user uploads.

__RemoteBucketDelivery.doc.#: How a RemoteBucket's download route hands out the bytes.
__RemoteBucketDelivery.doc.presigned: Authorize each request and answer 302 to a fresh short-lived presigned URL, never cached (the default).
__RemoteBucketDelivery.doc.public: Answer 302 to the object's stable public URL under publicBaseUrl, cacheable; only for a bucket declared as public content.

__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.#: External cloud-storage providers supported by RemoteBucket. The provider list is for EXTERNAL storage only — platform-provisioned self-hosted storage is declared via `nativeBuckets` and needs no provider entry.
__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.s3: AWS S3 — uses @aws-sdk/client-s3 and the project's amazonS3 integration.
__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.gcs: Google Cloud Storage — uses @google-cloud/storage and the project's googleCloudStorage integration.
__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.azure: Azure Blob Storage — uses @azure/storage-blob and the project's azureBlob integration.
__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.r2: Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible) — uses @aws-sdk/client-s3 with R2 endpoint.
__RemoteBucketStorageProvider.doc.s3Compatible: S3 Compatible Bucket — any external S3-compatible object store (self-managed MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, company-owned storage, ...) reached via @aws-sdk/client-s3 with a custom endpoint. NOT for platform self-hosted storage: define `nativeBuckets` instead and the hosting platform provisions its own SeaweedFS store with no provider entry.

__RemoteBucketAuthorization.doc: Authorization settings for read and write access to the remote bucket. Controls who can upload and download files, with support for role-based access, access keys, and custom authorization scripts.

RemoteBucketAuthorization.__readAccess.doc: Controls who can download files from this bucket. 'public' = anyone, no session required, 'private' = only the file owner and admins, 'authenticated' = any authenticated user, including other users' files, 'roles' = only holders of a readCheckRoles role. A Remote/Native download names a raw storage key; the nodejs router resolves the owner from the uploaderUserId of that key's {name}RemoteFile twin row, which its through-server /upload writes, so the uploader reads their own file. A key with no twin row (a presigned /upload-url upload) or no recorded uploader, and the language targets that persist no twin, fail closed to admins only — use 'authenticated' or readAbsoluteRoles when end users must read such files. Sessionless per-file key downloads are governed separately by enableKeyAccess.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__writeAccess.doc: Controls who can UPLOAD files to this bucket, and nothing else. 'authenticated' = any authenticated user, 'adminOnly' = only admin roles, 'roles' = only holders of a writeCheckRoles role. Deleting is governed separately by deleteAccess — before that split this same field gated DELETE too, so its default handed every registered account a delete primitive over every other user's files.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__deleteAccess.doc: Controls who can DELETE files from this bucket — a separate decision from writeAccess, which governs upload only. 'owner' (the DEFAULT) = only the account that uploaded the file, plus admin roles. 'adminOnly' = only admin roles. 'authenticated' = ANY authenticated user may delete ANY file in the bucket, including other users' files; that is the earlier behaviour and is kept only as a deliberate opt-in. The delete gate NARROWS writeAccess and never widens it: a bucket with writeAccess 'adminOnly' stays admin-only for deletes whatever this field says. A RemoteBucket / NativeBucket delete addresses a raw storage key: the nodejs router resolves the owner from the uploaderUserId of that key's {name}RemoteFile twin row, which its through-server /upload writes. A key with no twin row (a presigned /upload-url upload) or no recorded uploader, and the language targets that persist no twin, cannot establish ownership, so 'owner' denies every non-admin there (fail closed); widen deliberately with 'authenticated', 'adminOnly' or writeAbsoluteRoles.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__enableKeyAccess.doc: When true, any holder of a file's 12-character access key can download that file with NO session, on every bucket kind: DbBucket serves GET .../download/key/:accessKey directly, and RemoteBucket/NativeBucket honour ?accessKey= on the download route (the key is minted on the upload / upload-url response). When false or absent (the DEFAULT), key-based lookup stays behind the normal readAccess gate. Useful for shareable links; treat the key as a per-file capability credential. Unrelated to API keys, which represent a user's own rights and never grant extra authorization.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__readAbsoluteRoles.doc: Roles that bypass all read authorization checks. Users with any of these roles can always download files. Every name must be a defined role; an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__readCheckRoles.doc: Roles required for read access when readAccess is 'roles': the user must hold at least one of them to download. Consulted ONLY by that mode — under 'public', 'private' or 'authenticated' this list has no effect. An empty list under 'roles' behaves like 'authenticated'. Every name must be a defined role (a system role, a roleItems name or value, or a customRoleLookups name): an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning, and a list whose every name is undefined while the access mode is 'roles' and readAbsoluteRoles names no defined role is that code as an error, because the bucket then admits no defined-role session.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__writeAbsoluteRoles.doc: Roles that bypass all write authorization checks. Users with any of these roles can always upload files. Every name must be a defined role; an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__writeCheckRoles.doc: Roles required for write access when writeAccess is 'roles': the user must hold at least one of them to upload. Consulted ONLY by that mode — under 'authenticated' or 'adminOnly' this list has no effect. An empty list under 'roles' behaves like 'authenticated'. Every name must be a defined role (a system role, a roleItems name or value, or a customRoleLookups name): an undefined one is UNDEFINED_BUCKET_GATE_ROLE as a warning, and a list whose every name is undefined while the access mode is 'roles' and writeAbsoluteRoles names no defined role is that code as an error, because the bucket then admits no defined-role session.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__readAuthScript.doc: Custom MScript expression for read authorization; must return true to allow the download. Evaluated after the coarse readAccess/role checks and can only NARROW them — absoluteRoles still bypass everything. The request context IS the script receiver, so every field is reachable both as this.<field> (the platform-wide MScript convention) and as a bare name: session, userId, role, params, query, body, data. On a READ gate data is the FILE ROW: the script runs after the coarse checks allowed and after the file row is looked up (the DbBucket file row, or the {name}RemoteFile twin found by storageKey on a Remote/Native bucket), so a per-file rule such as this.data?.uploaderUserId === this.session?.userId is expressible. A key that resolves to no row is answered as missing (404) without running the script, so a script never reveals which keys exist. A denied file answers the same 404 NOT_FOUND as a missing one (no existence oracle), and a script that throws denies the same way. Example: this.session?.userId === this.params.ownerId.
RemoteBucketAuthorization.__writeAuthScript.doc: Custom MScript expression for write authorization; must return true to allow the upload. Evaluated after the coarse writeAccess/role checks and can only NARROW them — absoluteRoles still bypass everything. The request context IS the script receiver, so every field is reachable both as this.<field> (the platform-wide MScript convention) and as a bare name: session, userId, role, params, query, body, data. On a WRITE gate data is the request body, i.e. the upload metadata being stored. A script that throws denies. Example: this.session?.userId === this.data?.ownerId.

__RemoteBucketAccessLevel.doc.#: Read access levels for remote buckets. NativeBucket reuses this authorization section, so it applies there too.
__RemoteBucketAccessLevel.doc.public: Anyone can download files — no authentication required.
__RemoteBucketAccessLevel.doc.private: Only the file owner and admin roles can download. A Remote/Native download names a raw storage key: the nodejs router takes the owner from the uploaderUserId of that key's {name}RemoteFile twin row (written by its through-server /upload). A key with no twin row (a presigned /upload-url upload) or no recorded uploader, and the language targets that persist no twin, fail closed to the admin roles only — the uploader included. Use 'authenticated' (or absolute roles) when end users must read such files. This is the default.
__RemoteBucketAccessLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can download, including files uploaded by other users.
__RemoteBucketAccessLevel.doc.roles: Only users holding at least one of the roles in readCheckRoles can download. An empty readCheckRoles list behaves like 'authenticated'. readAbsoluteRoles bypasses this like every other mode.

__RemoteBucketWriteLevel.doc.#: Write access levels for remote buckets.
__RemoteBucketWriteLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can upload files.
__RemoteBucketWriteLevel.doc.adminOnly: Only the project's platform operator roles can upload: superAdmin and saasAdmin on a multi-tenant project; superAdmin, admin and saasAdmin on a single-tenant project. Tenant administrators such as tenantAdmin are not admitted.
__RemoteBucketWriteLevel.doc.roles: Only users holding at least one of the roles in writeCheckRoles can upload. An empty writeCheckRoles list behaves like 'authenticated'. writeAbsoluteRoles bypasses this like every other mode. deleteAccess still narrows deletes separately.

__RemoteBucketDeleteLevel.doc.#: Delete access levels for remote buckets. Separate from RemoteBucketWriteLevel, which governs upload only. NativeBucket reuses this authorization section, so it applies there too.
__RemoteBucketDeleteLevel.doc.owner: Only the account that uploaded the file, plus admin roles, can delete it. This is the default. A remote/native delete addresses a raw storage key; the nodejs router takes the owner from the uploaderUserId of that key's {name}RemoteFile twin row, and a key with no twin row or no recorded uploader denies every non-admin until the caller is provably the owner.
__RemoteBucketDeleteLevel.doc.adminOnly: Only the project's platform operator roles can delete: superAdmin and saasAdmin on a multi-tenant project; superAdmin, admin and saasAdmin on a single-tenant project. Tenant administrators such as tenantAdmin are not admitted.
__RemoteBucketDeleteLevel.doc.authenticated: Any authenticated user can delete any file in the bucket, including files uploaded by someone else. Opt in deliberately.

__RemoteBucketOwnerConfig.doc: Optional pairing with another data object. When configured, each file in the bucket has a foreign key relation to the owner data object (e.g., a product's images, a user's documents). This enables filtering files by owner and cascading deletes.

RemoteBucketOwnerConfig.__hasOwnerDataObject.doc: Enable pairing this bucket with a data object. When true, each file record includes a foreign key to the specified data object.
RemoteBucketOwnerConfig.__configuration.doc: Configuration for the owner data-object pairing.

__RemoteBucketOwnerConfigSettings.doc: Configuration for the owner data object pairing.

RemoteBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__dataObjectName.doc: The data object to pair with (e.g., 'user', 'product'). Files in this bucket will have a relation ID pointing to records in this data object.
RemoteBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__relationProperty.doc: Property name for the relation ID on the bucket file record. If null, auto-generated as '{dataObjectName}Id' (e.g., 'productId'). Must be a valid codeName.
RemoteBucketOwnerConfigSettings.__downloadRequiresActiveOwner.doc: When true, every route of this bucket that hands back the file (download by storage key, access key or row id, the DbBucket /shared link, and the DbBucket metadata route GET /bucket/{bucket}/object/:key, which returns the file's whole row minus its byte columns) loads the file's metadata row and then the paired owner row through the owner data object's default read, which excludes soft-deleted (isActive=false) rows; if the file has no metadata row, no owner id, or the owner row is missing or inactive, the route answers 404 NOT_FOUND instead of serving the file. Evaluated AFTER the bucket's read gate, so an unauthorised caller still gets 401/403 and learns nothing. Model 'hidden' or 'merged' owners as soft-deleted rows (or any state the default read excludes) for this to apply. For RemoteBucket/NativeBucket the metadata row is the {name}RemoteFile twin looked up by storageKey, which your own managers must persist at upload (the router does not); a file without one is not served. Requires a local (same-service) owner data object. Default false: downloads never consult the owner row.

__NativeBucket.doc: A self-hosted object-storage bucket backed by a platform-PROVISIONED, SeaweedFS (S3-API-compatible) store (docs/ADR-native-bucket-pattern.md, docs/ADR-seaweedfs-nativebucket.md). Full object-store semantics (presign, large files, streaming, server-side encryption) with NO cloud account, NO cloud credentials, and NO cloud cost — on-prem / data-sovereignty friendly. The designer just declares the bucket; the hosting platform provisions and manages the SeaweedFS store (lifecycle, root creds, default-bucket creation). Unlike RemoteBucket there is NO `bucketStorage.providerName` to configure — the managed store is implicit and project-scoped. Each native bucket creates a metadata data object named {name}RemoteFile (the SAME twin suffix RemoteBucket uses) holding storageKey + file info; binary content lives in the managed SeaweedFS store. That twin is materialized at BUILD time, so listBlueprint(dataObjects) does not list it, but it is nevertheless a legal childObject / fetch target at design time. Locally backed by the FARM SeaweedFS S3 gateway (mb-seaweedfs, S3 API :19900, dev creds minioadmin/minioadmin); in deploy the deployer stands up a per-project SeaweedFS store. Reuses RemoteBucket's basics/authorization/owner sub-patterns and the RemoteBucket S3 adapter under the hood. Upload and download routes are auto-generated at /nativebucket/{name}/. Prefer DbBucket for small files stored directly as BYTEA in PostgreSQL; prefer RemoteBucket when you want to configure your own cloud provider.

NativeBucket.__bucketBasics.doc: Core settings for the native bucket: name, description, size limits, allowed MIME types, and antivirus scanning. Shares the RemoteBucket basics shape.
NativeBucket.__bucketStorage.doc: Storage configuration for the native bucket: optional physical-bucket override, key prefix, and how download URLs are generated. Unlike RemoteBucket there is NO provider to name — the managed SeaweedFS store is implicit.
NativeBucket.__bucketAuthorization.doc: Authorization settings for read and write access to the native bucket. Shares the RemoteBucket authorization shape.
NativeBucket.__ownerDataObject.doc: Optional pairing with another data object. Shares the RemoteBucket owner-config shape.
NativeBucket.__remoteBucketSettings.doc: Optional extension settings of the bucket's auto-generated {name}RemoteFile metadata data object. additionalColumns appends designer-declared columns after its base columns; compositeIndexSettings declares composite indexes over the twin's base, owner, tenant and additional columns using the normal DataObject CompositeIndex shape. Leave null for the fixed column set and no composite indexes.

__NativeBucketStorage.doc: Storage configuration for a NativeBucket. Slim, provider-less variant of RemoteBucketStorage — there is NO `providerName` because the store is the platform-managed SeaweedFS (resolved from project-scoped NATIVEBUCKET_* env at runtime, forcePathStyle always true). Keeps the object-store knobs: optional physical-bucket override, key prefix, URL strategy, presign TTL, and server-side encryption.

NativeBucketStorage.__nativeBucketName.doc: Optional override for the physical bucket name in the managed SeaweedFS store. If null, falls back to the project's managed default bucket (`<codename>-native`), which the deployer/FARM creates. When set it must be a valid S3 bucket name (3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, no adjacent dots, not IP-shaped): a camelCase codename such as `kycDocs` is a design-time error (NATIVE_BUCKET_NAME_INVALID). Physical bucket names are shared by every project of the cluster, so the name must also start with the project codename and a dash (`<codename>-` followed by a name, e.g. `<codename>-kyc-docs`); any other name is a design-time error (NATIVE_BUCKET_NAME_FOREIGN). The bucket is provisioned by the hosting platform — it is not the designer's responsibility.
NativeBucketStorage.__keyPrefix.doc: Optional path prefix added to every stored object key (e.g., 'avatars/' produces keys like 'avatars/{uuid}'). Useful when multiple native buckets share the managed default physical bucket.
NativeBucketStorage.__presignTTLSeconds.doc: Lifetime of a presigned URL in seconds. Default 900 (15 minutes). Downloads are always served as a short-lived presigned URL — the service authorizes the request, then the client fetches directly from the storage provider. A presigned URL is a BEARER credential — anyone holding it can fetch the object until it expires, and it CANNOT be revoked early — so the TTL is the exposure window if the URL leaks (logs, Referer headers, shared links). 15 minutes is the common industry range for user-facing downloads. Note a short TTL does NOT truncate large downloads: the signature is checked when the request STARTS, so a transfer that begins before expiry completes normally. Raise it only for batch or machine consumers that hold a URL before using it.
NativeBucketStorage.__serverSideEncryption.doc: When true, enables server-side encryption (SSE-S3 / AES256) on the managed SeaweedFS store. Default: false - SSE is OPT-IN. The managed store only accepts the signed `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256` header when it was provisioned with an `[s3.sse] kek` in its security.toml; without one every PUT answers 500 InternalError while CreateBucket/HeadBucket still succeed (docs/ADR-seaweedfs-nativebucket.md section 8.2). Turn it on only against a store confirmed to carry a KEK.
NativeBucketStorage.__objectCacheControl.doc: Cache-Control this bucket's objects are stored and served with. Null (the default) means the framework value `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, which is right for content-addressed assets and wrong for a bucket that holds mutable documents: set for example `no-cache` for a rendered report rewritten in place through the SDK, `private, max-age=60` for a regulated bucket, `public, max-age=300` for a scratch area. The value is set on BOTH sides of the round trip - the stored object metadata (S3 `CacheControl`) and the `Cache-Control` entry of the `headers` map the presigned upload returns, plus the signed GET-side response override (`ResponseCacheControl`) - because the read-time override wins over what is stored. The managed store is S3-API, so both carriers apply; changing this field affects objects written AFTER the change and never retroactively rewrites objects already in the bucket. Must be a plausible Cache-Control token list (comma-separated `directive` or `directive=value`); a malformed value is an authoring-time error, because the store keeps the string verbatim and then serves it to every browser.

__AgentHubConfig.doc: Configuration for the AgentHub service — a centralized AI agent management platform. The hub hosts design-time agents (with runtime reconfiguration), discovers tools from all project services, and optionally allows end-users to create and manage their own agents at runtime.

AgentHubConfig.__hubSettings.doc: Hub settings chapter: the hub's core configuration (dynamic agent creation, tool discovery) and the tool sources the hub discovers tools from.
AgentHubConfig.__aiAgents.doc: The hub-hosted AI agents. Same `AIAgent` pattern as service-level agents; hub agents can use tools discovered from any project service and support runtime reconfiguration.
AgentHubConfig.__harnesses.doc: The hub-hosted agent harnesses (`AgentHarness`, docs/ADR-agent-harness.md): long-running, autonomous, skill-driven agents run by an open-source harness runtime (DeepSeek Harness `dsh` by default, `goose`, `codex`, `claude-code`, or `opencode`) that agentHub drives over the Agent Client Protocol. Each harness carries its own skills, documents and scripts, runtime-native plugins, the project tools it may call, its network and session limits, and optional Kafka triggers. A project with at least one enabled harness gets a harness runner system service; clients still talk only to agentHub. Harness names are unique within the hub. Harnesses are nodejs only (ADR D7): a project whose agentHub generates for another language is refused with AGENT_HARNESS_LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED.
AgentHubConfig.__serviceFiles.doc: Design-time static files of the agentHub service (an optional singular chapter, `ServiceFiles`, the same shape as `service.serviceFiles`). AgentHarness assets live here: every `harnesses[].assets.skills|documents|scripts` entry must name a file of this manifest, or a folder holding at least one (a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md), under `harness/<harnessName>/skills|docs|scripts/`. Upload each file with the `uploadServiceFile` tool and serviceName `agentHub`; keep harness assets private (a public file is served by the agentHub at `/service-files/<path>`). The build writes the files to `service-files/<visibility>/<path>` of the agentHub repo, and the harness runner copies a harness's declared assets from that tree, read-only, into each session. A private file is NOT secret: never put credentials in one. Null/absent when the hub carries no files.

__AgentHubSettings.doc: Hub settings chapter containing the basic configuration and tool source definitions for the Agent Hub service.

AgentHubSettings.__hubBasics.doc: Core hub settings: dynamic agent creation controls and tool discovery configuration.
AgentHubSettings.__toolSources.doc: The services the hub discovers tools from — each source maps a project service whose Business APIs become available as agent tools; use serviceName '*' to discover from all services.

__AgentHubBasics.doc: Core settings for the Agent Hub service including dynamic agent creation controls and tool discovery configuration.

AgentHubBasics.__description.doc: Human-readable description of the Agent Hub service.
AgentHubBasics.__frontendDocument.doc: Module-level UX prompt for MindUI. Describes how the agent-chat surface should be presented (chat placement, agent personalities, tool-call visibility, history, streaming, dynamic-agent UX). MindUI reads this when generating agent pages; empty falls back to a basic chat list.
AgentHubBasics.__enableDynamicAgents.doc: When true, end-users with the appropriate roles can create, configure, and run their own AI agents at runtime. When false, only design-time agents defined in this configuration are available.
AgentHubBasics.__dynamicAgentRoles.doc: Roles allowed to create and manage dynamic agents at runtime. Default: empty, which means the platform operators of the project's tenancy - superAdmin and admin in a single-tenant project, superAdmin and saasAdmin in a multi-tenant project (a multi-tenant project has no role named admin; naming admin here is an ERROR there, except the old default [superAdmin, admin], which only warns). Add additional roles as needed (e.g., 'tenantOwner').
AgentHubBasics.__approvalRoles.doc: Roles allowed to list and decide human-in-the-loop approvals — paused agent runs (approval-required tools and draft outputs) — via the hub approval API (/agent-runs/*) and, on nodejs, the same /agent-runs/* routes a business service mounts for the runs paused on its own agent routes. Default: empty, which means the platform operators of the project's tenancy - superAdmin and admin in a single-tenant project, superAdmin and saasAdmin in a multi-tenant project (a multi-tenant project has no role named admin; naming admin here is an ERROR there, except the old default [superAdmin, admin], which only warns). Machine callers (the M2M 'system' role) are NOT approvers by default; the nodejs runtime refuses a machine (M2M) session even when 'system' is listed here.
AgentHubBasics.__maxDynamicAgents.doc: Maximum number of dynamic agents that can be created at runtime. Prevents unbounded growth. Default: 50.
AgentHubBasics.__toolRefreshIntervalMinutes.doc: How often (in minutes) the hub re-discovers tools from project services. Tools can also be refreshed manually via the refresh API. Default: 5 minutes.
AgentHubBasics.__httpPort.doc: The HTTP port the generated agentHub service listens on, like a normal service's serviceOptions.httpPort. Drives the hub's local dev port, its HTTP_PORT env and the SERVICE_AGENTHUB_URL sibling binding. Leave null for the platform defaults (deployed serviceOptions port 4003; local dev port 3006).

__AgentHubToolSource.doc: Defines a service from which the Agent Hub discovers tools. Each tool source maps to a project service whose Business APIs become available as agent tools. Use serviceName '*' to discover from all services.

AgentHubToolSource.__serviceName.doc: The service to discover tools from. Use '*' to discover from all project services. Use a specific service name (e.g., 'taskManagement') to target a single service.
AgentHubToolSource.__includeApis.doc: Comma-separated list of API names to include as tools. Use '*' for all APIs. If null, all APIs from the service are included.
AgentHubToolSource.__excludeApis.doc: Comma-separated list of API names to exclude from tools. Applied after includeApis filtering. Useful when includeApis is '*' but you want to hide certain internal APIs.

__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.#: The open-source agent harness an AgentHarness runs on. agentHub drives every runtime through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) over stdio, so swapping the runtime changes no other field. Each runtime runs at a version pinned by the framework release; it never floats.
__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.dsh: DeepSeek Harness (MIT), started as `dsh-acp-app`. The default. Pre-stable (developer preview), so its version is pinned and upgraded only with a compatibility test. Speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic model API shapes; accepts plugins from its own registry or npm.
__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.goose: Goose (Apache-2.0), native ACP through `goose acp`. The stable fallback. Speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic model API shapes; it has no plugin source the runner installs (extend it with tools and skills).
__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.codex: OpenAI Codex CLI (Apache-2.0) through its ACP adapter (`codex-acp`). Speaks the OpenAI model API shape only; no plugin source.
__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.claude-code: Anthropic Claude Code through its ACP adapter (`claude-code-acp`). Not open source: its licence terms for a hosted runner are checked before release. Speaks the Anthropic model API shape only (an Anthropic-compatible endpoint such as GLM or Kimi works through a `custom` provider with apiFormat `anthropic`); accepts plugins from its own registry. Runs on an AI provider entry's key, or on the session owner's own Claude subscription (`modelSettings.auth` userSubscription, tenant or user level only).
__AgentHarnessRuntime.doc.opencode: OpenCode (MIT, npm `opencode-ai`), native ACP through `opencode acp`. Speaks the OpenAI model API shape through the runner's model gateway (its built-in OpenAI client calls the Responses API, so it needs a provider entry that serves `/responses`). Preview: not yet run on a real session. No plugin source the runner installs yet (extend it with tools and skills); no subscription login (providerKey only).

__AgentHarnessPluginSource.doc.#: Where a runtime-native AgentHarness plugin is installed from. Each runtime allows only some sources; the validator refuses the others (AGENT_HARNESS_PLUGIN_SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED).
__AgentHarnessPluginSource.doc.registry: The runtime's own plugin registry or marketplace (`dsh plugin`, the Claude Code plugin marketplace).
__AgentHarnessPluginSource.doc.npm: The public npm registry, as an exact package version (dsh only).

__AgentHarnessEgress.doc.#: Outbound network policy of the sandboxed harness process (maintainer ruling Q3). The model gateway and the session MCP endpoint are reachable in both modes.
__AgentHarnessEgress.doc.open: Outbound network is open. The default.
__AgentHarnessEgress.doc.allowlist: Outbound network is limited to networkSettings.allowedHosts.

__AgentHarnessModelAuth.doc.#: How an AgentHarness session authenticates to its model (maintainer ruling 2026-11-02).
__AgentHarnessModelAuth.doc.providerKey: The default. The runner's model gateway adds the provider key resolved for the session owner (user, then a workspace record's key, then tenant, then the application owner's key); the key never enters the sandbox and every call is metered against the cost ceilings.
__AgentHarnessModelAuth.doc.userSubscription: The session runs on the session owner's OWN vendor subscription: Claude Code on the owner's Claude plan (`claude-code` runtime, an `anthropic` entry) or Codex on the owner's ChatGPT plan (`codex` runtime, an `openai` entry). The owner stores the subscription credential at the tenant or user level of the entry (`PUT /my-provider-credentials/<providerName>` or `/tenant-provider-credentials/<providerName>` on the auth service with `kind: "subscriptionToken"`); the entry must enable the tenant or the user scope, and the application (saas) level is refused: a session whose owner holds no token fails with 428 `AI_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` and the application owner's key is never used. The runner writes the credential into that owner's session HOME only and sets no model gateway variables, so nothing is metered: `dailyCostCeilingUsd`, `maxTurns` and usage recording do not apply, and the vendor's own terms govern the plan (they may restrict third-party use of a subscription login). Frontend sessions only (a triggered session has no subscriber), and `networkSettings.egress` must be `allowlist`; the runner adds the vendor's hosts to it.

__AgentHarness.doc: An agent harness hosted by agentHub: a long-running, autonomous agent run by an open-source harness runtime (docs/ADR-agent-harness.md). It works from skills, documents and scripts, keeps a private working directory, calls the project's tools over MCP and can be extended with runtime-native plugins. agentHub drives the runtime over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP); the emitted harness runner system service starts one sandboxed process per session (bubblewrap/nsjail, no host environment, CPU/memory/time limits). The workspace is one directory per (tenant, user, harness), shared by that user's sessions and never by two users; Kafka-triggered sessions use `/<tenant>/_system/<harnessName>/`. The model key never enters the sandbox: the harness reaches its model through the runner's model gateway, which adds the key from the agentHub AI provider entry and enforces the cost ceilings. Every tool call runs as the session owner: the user's own bearer for a frontend session; for a Kafka-triggered one, the agentHub M2M service identity in the event's tenant, so a triggered session calls only the harness's m2mTools. Clients start, follow and cancel sessions through agentHub's /harnesses and /harness-sessions APIs only.

AgentHarness.__harnessBasics.doc: Identity of the harness: name, description, runtime and whether it is enabled.
AgentHarness.__modelSettings.doc: The model the harness runs on: an agentHub AI provider entry and a model id. The provider's API shape must be one the runtime speaks.
AgentHarness.__assets.doc: The skills, documents and scripts copied read-only into every session's harness home. Each is a path in the agentHub service files under `harness/<name>/skills/`, `harness/<name>/docs/` or `harness/<name>/scripts/`.
AgentHarness.__plugins.doc: Runtime-native plugins installed into this harness's profile when the runner image is built, never per user or per request. Each entry is pinned to one exact version and comes from a source the runtime allows.
AgentHarness.__toolSettings.doc: The project tools the harness may call, served to it by the per-session MCP endpoint and executed as the session owner. Same tool selection vocabulary as AIAgent.toolSettings (apiTools, m2mTools, agentTools, approvalRequiredTools), plus the platform web tools.
AgentHarness.__networkSettings.doc: Outbound network policy of the sandboxed process: open (the default) or limited to listed hosts.
AgentHarness.__sessionSettings.doc: Who may start sessions from a frontend and the per-user session, idle and workspace retention limits.
AgentHarness.__triggers.doc: Kafka triggers that start a background session of this harness when a matching event arrives. A triggered session runs as the agentHub M2M service identity in the event's tenant: it sees only the harness's M2M tools (m2mTools on M2MAllowed apis) and the web tools, and it is visible to admins.
AgentHarness.__guardrails.doc: Turn guardrails, reusing AgentGuardrails. The harness runner and agentHub enforce timeout (the wall-clock limit of one prompt turn, in ms), maxToolCalls (per prompt turn), dailyCostCeilingUsd and costCeilingScope (the same CostGovernor ceilings agents use). Only authored values count: an unset timeout is 30 minutes (1800000 ms) and an unset maxToolCalls is 200, never the AgentGuardrails defaults of 2 minutes and 25 calls, which are sized for one in-process agent request. A stored value equal to one of those AgentGuardrails defaults (120000, 25) is read as unset, because a design tool writes the defaults into a new guardrails section; author any other value to set a limit. A turn past timeout ends the session timed_out; one past maxToolCalls ends it failed. The other AgentGuardrails fields belong to the in-process agent runtime and are not applied to a harness (warning AGENT_HARNESS_GUARDRAIL_NOT_APPLIED).

__AgentHarnessBasics.doc: Identity of an AgentHarness: its unique name, description, runtime and enabled flag.

AgentHarnessBasics.__name.doc: Unique harness name within the hub (codeName). It names the harness in the agentHub APIs (`POST /harnesses/:name/sessions`), its asset folder `harness/<name>/` and its workspace directory.
AgentHarnessBasics.name: String
AgentHarnessBasics.__description.doc: What the harness is for. Shown to designers and in the hub's harness listing.
AgentHarnessBasics.__runtime.doc: The harness runtime: `dsh` (DeepSeek Harness, the default), `goose`, `codex`, `claude-code` or `opencode`. Each runtime is pinned to one version by the framework release and driven over ACP.
AgentHarnessBasics.__enabled.doc: When false, the harness is kept in the blueprint but not served: no sessions start and its triggers do not consume. A project whose harnesses are all disabled gets no harness runner.

__AgentHarnessModelSettings.doc: The model an AgentHarness runs on, and how the session authenticates to it. With `auth: providerKey` (the default) the runner's model gateway adds the provider key, so the key never enters the sandbox. With `auth: userSubscription` a Claude Code or Codex session runs on the session owner's own Claude or ChatGPT subscription, stored at the tenant or user level of the entry.

AgentHarnessModelSettings.__providerName.doc: Name of an AI provider entry in projectSettings.aiProvidersSettings.aiProviders[]. Its API shape must be one the runtime speaks: openai, xai, deepseek, moonshot, azure-openai and ollama entries are OpenAI-shaped; anthropic entries are Anthropic-shaped; a custom entry takes its shape from its apiFormat key (openai or anthropic). google, bedrock and the media providers cannot back a harness. With `auth: providerKey` only an API key through the entry (the application owner's, or a tenant's or user's own through `credentialScopes`) is used. With `auth: userSubscription` the entry names the vendor of the owner's subscription (`anthropic` for `claude-code`, `openai` for `codex`) and must enable the tenant or user scope; give a subscription harness a dedicated entry, because an owner holds one credential per entry (an API key or a subscription token).
AgentHarnessModelSettings.__auth.doc: How a session authenticates to the model. `providerKey` (the default): the runner's model gateway adds the provider key resolved for the session owner (user, then a workspace record's key, then tenant, then the application owner's key) and meters every call. `userSubscription`: the session runs on the session owner's own Claude (`claude-code`) or ChatGPT (`codex`) subscription, stored at the tenant or user level of the entry as a `subscriptionToken` credential; the application level is refused, a missing token is a 428 `AI_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, nothing is metered, frontend sessions only, `egress` must be `allowlist`, and the vendor's terms may restrict third-party use of a subscription login (validation warns, AGENT_HARNESS_SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS).
AgentHarnessModelSettings.__model.doc: The model id the harness requests, for example `deepseek-chat` or `claude-sonnet-4-5`. Null uses the provider entry's defaultModel.
AgentHarnessModelSettings.__maxTurns.doc: Upper bound on model turns in one session. Null leaves the runtime's own limit in place; the guardrails timeout and cost ceilings apply either way. Not applied with `auth: userSubscription` (the gateway does not see those calls).

__AgentHarnessAssets.doc: Skills, documents and scripts of an AgentHarness. Each entry is a path in the agentHub service files, which ride in the repo and are hash-verified at build; the runner copies them read-only into each session's harness home. A path must be relative, use `/`, have no `.` or `..` segment, and lie under the harness's own folder for its kind (AGENT_HARNESS_ASSET_OUTSIDE_FOLDER otherwise). Each entry must name one file of the `agentHub.serviceFiles` manifest, or a folder holding at least one (AGENT_HARNESS_ASSET_NOT_IN_SERVICE_FILES otherwise); upload the files with `uploadServiceFile` and serviceName `agentHub`. Keep them private: an entry resolving to a public file is warned (AGENT_HARNESS_ASSET_PUBLIC). The runner copies exactly the manifest files an entry names, never anything else in the tree. There is no other upload path.

AgentHarnessAssets.__skills.doc: Skill folders (each holding a SKILL.md) under `harness/<name>/skills/`, for example `harness/kycCheck/skills/kyc`.
AgentHarnessAssets.__scripts.doc: Scripts the harness may run inside its sandbox, under `harness/<name>/scripts/`, for example `harness/kycCheck/scripts/score.py`.

__AgentHarnessPlugin.doc: A runtime-native plugin of an AgentHarness, installed into the harness profile at runner build. The AI designer may add plugins; the validator accepts only an exact version (AGENT_HARNESS_PLUGIN_UNPINNED) from a source the runtime allows (AGENT_HARNESS_PLUGIN_SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED).

AgentHarnessPlugin.__name.doc: The plugin package name, npm style and optionally scoped (`@scope/name`).
AgentHarnessPlugin.name: String
AgentHarnessPlugin.__version.doc: One exact semver version, for example `1.4.2`. Ranges (`^1.4.0`, `~1.4`), wildcards and tags such as `latest` are refused.
AgentHarnessPlugin.__source.doc: Where the plugin is installed from: `registry` (the runtime's own registry or marketplace) or `npm`. dsh allows both, claude-code allows registry, goose, codex and opencode allow none.

__AgentHarnessToolSettings.doc: The project tools an AgentHarness may call. The per-session MCP endpoint serves exactly this list and executes each call as the session owner, so permissionCheck, tenant gates and ownership apply as for a direct API call. Every API tool is reached over the network from the harness runner, so its BusinessApi must have a REST controller.

AgentHarnessToolSettings.__apiTools.doc: Comma-separated BusinessApi names exposed as tools (the AIAgent.toolSettings.apiTools vocabulary). Each must exist in a project service and have a REST controller (AGENT_HARNESS_UNKNOWN_API_TOOL, AGENT_HARNESS_API_TOOL_NOT_EXPOSABLE). The call runs as the session owner: the user's forwarded bearer for a frontend session. A Kafka-triggered session runs as the agentHub M2M service identity and can call only the m2mTools subset.
AgentHarnessToolSettings.__m2mTools.doc: Comma-separated SUBSET of apiTools that run over the machine (M2M) identity instead of the session owner's (the AIAgent.toolSettings.m2mTools vocabulary). Each entry must be in apiTools and its BusinessApi must allow M2M callers. A harness with enabled triggers must list every apiTools entry here: a triggered session calls tools only over M2M, so any other apiTool is an error (AGENT_HARNESS_TRIGGERED_TOOL_NOT_M2M), or a warning that triggered sessions will not see it when the harness also allows frontend sessions.
AgentHarnessToolSettings.__agentTools.doc: Comma-separated names of design-time AI agents (hub or service) the harness may invoke as tools, registered as `invoke_agent_<name>`. An agent tool runs as the session owner, so a Kafka-triggered session (M2M identity) never sees it.
AgentHarnessToolSettings.__approvalRequiredTools.doc: Comma-separated tool names that pause the session for human approval before they run, through the existing approval flow (`/agent-runs/:runId/approve`). Names are the registered ones: the BusinessApi name, `invoke_agent_<name>`, `web_search`, `web_fetch_scrape`. Each must be a tool this harness has (AGENT_HARNESS_UNKNOWN_APPROVAL_TOOL). Put destructive tools here, above all on a triggered harness.
AgentHarnessToolSettings.__webTools.doc: The platform web tools of the session MCP endpoint (maintainer ruling Q3): `web_search` and `web_fetch_scrape`, each backed by a framework search or scrape integration of the project. The integration keys stay server-side and never enter the sandbox.

__AgentHarnessWebTools.doc:
Platform web tools offered to an AgentHarness through its session MCP endpoint, each backed by a root `integrations[]` entry of the project.

Declare the integration as `{ "name": "serperMain", "provider": "serper", "configuration": { "apiKey": "..." } }`. `name` is optional and defaults to the provider; a webTools value names the entry (its name, or the provider when only one entry has it). The framework brands are:

| family | provider | configuration |
|---|---|---|
| searchProvider | `serper` (Google results) | `apiKey` (required, secret), `gl`, `hl`, `timeoutMs` (default 10000), `baseUrl` |
| searchProvider | `brave` (Brave Search API) | `apiKey` (required, secret), `gl`, `hl`, `timeoutMs` (default 10000), `baseUrl` |
| scrapProvider | `zyte` (Zyte API) | `apiKey` (required, secret), `timeoutMs` (default 60000), `maxBytes` (default 2000000), `baseUrl` |

The configuration reaches the runtime as the secret env `INTEGRATION_<NAME>_CONFIG` and the `apiKey` is relocated out of the stored blueprint. Keys never appear in a log line, an error or a tool result.

`web_search` answers `{ provider, latencyMs, results: [{ title, url, snippet }] }`. Result URLs are cleaned of the tracking parameters `srsltid`, `utm_*`, `gclid` and `fbclid`. `web_fetch_scrape` fetches one public http(s) page through Zyte, as raw `html`, readable `text` or a rendered `browser` page. Private, loopback and link-local targets are refused before any call, and the content is capped at `maxBytes`.

AgentHarnessWebTools.__search.doc: The searchProvider integration (`serper` or `brave`) behind the `web_search` tool: one integration name, or an ordered comma-separated fallback chain such as `serperMain, braveBackup` (first = primary). The next provider is tried on an error, a timeout or an exhausted quota. An empty answer moves on only for a free-text query; an exact-identifier or `site:` query with no result is final, because a fallback engine that cannot exact-match would return unrelated pages. Null leaves the tool out. Each name must resolve to a project integration (AGENT_HARNESS_UNKNOWN_WEB_TOOL_PROVIDER) of the searchProvider family (AGENT_HARNESS_WEB_TOOL_PROVIDER_WRONG_CATEGORY).
AgentHarnessWebTools.__scrape.doc: The one scrapProvider integration (`zyte`) behind the `web_fetch_scrape` tool. Null leaves the tool out. It must resolve to a project integration (AGENT_HARNESS_UNKNOWN_WEB_TOOL_PROVIDER) of the scrapProvider family (AGENT_HARNESS_WEB_TOOL_PROVIDER_WRONG_CATEGORY), and names exactly one (AGENT_HARNESS_WEB_TOOL_SCRAPE_SINGLE_PROVIDER).

__AgentHarnessNetworkSettings.doc: Outbound network policy of an AgentHarness's sandboxed process (maintainer ruling Q3). The model gateway and the session MCP endpoint are always reachable.

AgentHarnessNetworkSettings.__egress.doc: `open` (the default) lets the process reach any host; `allowlist` limits it to allowedHosts.
AgentHarnessNetworkSettings.__allowedHosts.doc: Hosts the process may reach when egress is `allowlist` (at most 100). Each entry is a lowercase host name with at least two labels (`api.example.com`), the same with a leading `*.` wildcard for any sub-domain (`*.example.com`), or an IPv4 literal, each with an optional `:port`. A scheme, path, bare `*` or localhost is refused (AGENT_HARNESS_INVALID_ALLOWED_HOST). Ignored when egress is open.

__AgentHarnessSessionSettings.doc: Frontend access and per-user limits of an AgentHarness's sessions.

AgentHarnessSessionSettings.__allowFrontendSessions.doc: When true, a signed-in user may start a session with `POST /harnesses/:name/sessions` and follow it; the session acts with that user's token. When false, the harness runs only from its triggers.
AgentHarnessSessionSettings.__maxConcurrentPerUser.doc: How many live sessions one user may hold on this harness at once. Default 2, at most 20.
AgentHarnessSessionSettings.__idleTimeoutMinutes.doc: A session with no prompt and no harness activity for this many minutes is ended (status timed_out). Default 30, at most 1440.
AgentHarnessSessionSettings.__workspaceRetentionDays.doc: A (tenant, user, harness) workspace no session has touched for this many days is removed. Default 30, at most 365. Session events are kept 90 days regardless.

__AgentHarnessTrigger.doc: A Kafka trigger of an AgentHarness: a matching event starts a background session (origin `kafka`) as the agentHub M2M service identity. The session calls only the harness's M2M tools (m2mTools on M2MAllowed apis) and its web tools; in a multi-tenant project it runs in the event's tenant (tenantId). The rendered introPrompt is the first user message and the workspace is `/<tenant>/_system/<harnessName>/`. condition, introPrompt, dedupKey and tenantId are MScript expressions over `(message, topic, headers)`, the binding of AgentKafkaController.dataMapping. Event values are data, not instructions: agentHub wraps them in a quoted data block the harness is told never to obey, so keep a triggered harness's tool list to what the job needs and put destructive tools in approvalRequiredTools. A finished session raises harnessSessionCompleted or harnessSessionFailed on agentHub.

AgentHarnessTrigger.__name.doc: Unique trigger name within the harness (codeName).
AgentHarnessTrigger.name: String
AgentHarnessTrigger.__topic.doc: The Kafka topic to consume. Must be produced in the project.
AgentHarnessTrigger.__groupId.doc: Consumer group id. Null derives one from the hub, harness and trigger names.
AgentHarnessTrigger.__condition.doc: Optional synchronous MScript expression over `(message, topic, headers)`; the event starts a session only when it is truthy. An async function is refused (always truthy).
AgentHarnessTrigger.__introPrompt.doc: MScript expression over `(message, topic, headers)` that returns the session's first user message, for example a template literal: `New customer ${message.data.firstName} ${message.data.lastName} (id ${message.data.id}). Run the KYC skill and record the result with the updateCustomerKyc tool.`
AgentHarnessTrigger.__dedupKey.doc: Optional MScript expression over `(message, topic, headers)` returning a key; a second event with the same key does not start a second session (AgentKafkaGuard dedup). Null uses the event's own id.
AgentHarnessTrigger.__tenantId.doc: The tenant the triggered session runs in, as an MScript expression over `(message, topic, headers)`, for example `message.data.storeId`. Required in a multi-tenant project and refused in a single-tenant one. The value is stamped on the session (sys_harnessSession.tenantId), names the workspace `/<tenant>/_system/<harnessName>/` and rides every M2M tool call of the session as its caller tenant, so the work never crosses tenants. An event whose expression yields an empty value is dead-lettered with a reason, never run tenant-less.
AgentHarnessTrigger.__enabled.doc: When false, the trigger does not consume.
AgentHarnessTrigger.__concurrency.doc: How many events of this trigger are processed at once. Default 1, at most 64.

__BusinessApiBasics.doc: Groups a BusinessApi's core API options and authentication settings. Core identity and authentication settings of a `BusinessApi` (section) — groups `apiOptions` (name, crud type, target data object, response shape) and `authOptions` (login requirement + permission checks).

BusinessApiBasics.__apiOptions.doc: Defines the name,type, dataObject and description of the business api as well as its basic options
BusinessApiBasics.__authOptions.doc: Defines core authentication and authorization settings for a Business API. These settings cover session validation, role and ownership checks, and access scope (e.g., tenant vs. SaaS-level). While these options are sufficient for most use cases, more fine-grained access control—such as conditional permissions or contextual ownership—should be implemented using explicit access control actions (e.g., `PermissionCheckAction`, `MembershipCheckAction`, `ObjectPermissionCheckAction`).

__BusinessApiParameters.doc: Parameter sources of a `BusinessApi` (section): custom `requestParameters` (validated request inputs fed into the workflow context) and `redisParameters` (values read from Redis into the context).

BusinessApiParameters.__requestParameters.doc: The full request shape of this API — every parameter the caller can supply, declared inline. The framework binds `this.<name>` from the request based ONLY on this list. Element shape: name, type, isArray, required, httpLocation, defaultValue, transform, description, isSecret, hidden. URL placeholders in `restSettings.routePath` (e.g. `:teamId`) auto-promote into this list with `httpLocation: 'urlpath'` if not declared explicitly.
BusinessApiParameters.__redisParameters.doc: An array of parameters fetched from Redis based on dynamically computed keys. These are defined using `RedisApiParameter` and are written to the context as `this.<name>`, just like request parameters.

__BusinessApiControllers.doc: Transport bindings of a `BusinessApi` (section): the optional REST, gRPC, Kafka, SSE, cron and internal-call controller settings that expose the API. Each sub-setting is independent — an API may expose any combination of transports. The internal-call binding is not a network transport: it exposes the API to in-process `API.<name>()` calls from same-service designer scripts.

BusinessApiControllers.__restSettings.doc: Defines HTTP REST controller settings such as method and route path. Automatically generated using naming conventions, but can be customized for fine-grained control over REST behavior, parameter mapping, or URL design.
BusinessApiControllers.__grpcSettings.doc: Enables gRPC access for this Business API and configures the request and response schemas. gRPC is disabled by default unless explicitly configured.
BusinessApiControllers.__kafkaSettings.doc: Enables this Business API to be triggered by Kafka events. This controller listens for messages published to configured Kafka topics, allowing the API to respond to system-level events (e.g., file uploaded, user signed up) or external integrations. This is commonly used for decoupled orchestration between services or for reacting to events emitted by backend libraries and storage providers.
BusinessApiControllers.__sseSettings.doc: Enables Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming for this Business API. When enabled, the API can stream its response as chunks (for large datasets, file exports, LLM token streaming) or emit progress events (for long-running operations) over an SSE connection.
BusinessApiControllers.__cronSettings.doc: Schedules this Business API for automatic execution at specified intervals. Useful for background tasks, data cleanup, or scheduled jobs. Uses cron expressions to define timing.
BusinessApiControllers.__internalCallSettings.doc: Enables in-process invocation of this Business API from same-service designer scripts — payment lifecycle hooks call it as `await API.<name>(params)`. No transport is involved: the internal call controller runs the full manager pipeline directly asSystem. With one argument the session is null and all inputs must be explicit parameters. On nodejs, python, rust, java and dotnet a BusinessApi action (and, on nodejs, a hook) that has a caller session supplies it with the optional second argument, `await API.<name>(params, { session: this.session })`, to resolve the caller's tenant; ledger APIs on a tenant-scoped owner object need it too. No session is implicitly inherited through AsyncLocalStorage or the running manager, and the system authorization posture stays unchanged: role and ownership gates remain bypassed even with an explicit session. Language targets without explicit-session support retain the sessionless signature.

__BusinessApiQuery.doc: Data-access shape of a `BusinessApi` (section): the select / where / data clauses plus delete / get / list / pagination options that drive the API's primary data-object query.

BusinessApiQuery.__selectClause.doc: Specifies which fields will be selected from the main data object during a `get` or `list` operation. Leave blank to select all properties. On a `create`, `update` or `delete` API only `selectProperties` is read: it narrows the answer to the declared properties + `id` without projecting the write; `selectJoins` there is ignored.
BusinessApiQuery.__dataClauseItems.doc: Lists every dataClause field the framework writes at create / update time, with the value MScript that produces it. Top-level on the BusinessApi. Runtime composition: for each property on the data object, (1) `sessionSettings` block → auto-inject from session, (2) `staticJoin` block → run the join, expose result via `contextParameterName`, (3) otherwise → look up matching `dataClauseItems[i].name` and evaluate its `value`. Properties with none of the three are not written (auditor flags missing entries). Common value shapes: `this.<paramName>` (caller-supplied), `'<literal>'` (system-managed), `this.<paramName> || '<default>'` (caller-with-fallback), MScript like `LIB.calc(this.X)` for computed.
BusinessApiQuery.__whereClause.doc: Defines the criteria used to locate the target record(s) for the main operation. This is expressed as a query object and applies to `get`, `list`, `update`, and `delete` APIs. All API types except `list` are expected to target a single record. For `update` and `delete`, the WHERE clause is used to fetch the target instance, and the actual database mutation is performed using the fetched instance's ID to guarantee single-record safety.
BusinessApiQuery.__deleteOptions.doc: Contains settings specific to `delete` type APIs, such as soft-delete configurations or cascade options.
BusinessApiQuery.__getOptions.doc: Contains settings specific to `get` type APIs, such as instance enrichment, fallback behaviors, or object caching.
BusinessApiQuery.__listOptions.doc: Defines list-specific options including filtering logic, default sorting, and result customization for APIs that return multiple records. Applies only to `list` type APIs; ignored on every other crudType.
BusinessApiQuery.__paginationOptions.doc: Contains settings to configure pagination behavior for `list` APIs (default page size, keyset `cursorMode`, and the `unpaged` opt-out). Paginated lists take 1-based `page`/`pageSize` parameters and respond with `{ data, paging: { page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages } }`.

__VisitSignal.doc.#: What kind of consumption a visit records (visits ADR section 3). Signals are stored with their type and never merged: every consumer (a counter, a recommendation source) names the signal it reads.
__VisitSignal.doc.access: A get succeeded with no confirmation: the object was served to this actor. Weak evidence (prefetch, refresh, crawlers).
__VisitSignal.doc.view: A get confirmed by the frontend after the visible dwell time: it was on screen long enough. Medium evidence.
__VisitSignal.doc.read: A get confirmed by the frontend with a completion criterion (dwell and/or scroll): consumed. Strong evidence.
__VisitSignal.doc.seen: A list succeeded: each row of the returned page is recorded with its position. An impression only, never an interest signal.

__VisitConfirmation.doc.#: How a visit becomes countable (visits ADR section 4).
__VisitConfirmation.doc.none: Recorded and counted when the response is sent. The only mode an `access` or `seen` signal takes.
__VisitConfirmation.doc.frontend: Two steps, exactly once: the response carries `_visit { visitId, confirmPath, minVisibleSeconds, expiresAt }` and a pending row is written; the frontend POSTs confirmPath after the visible dwell time, and one guarded statement moves the row to confirmed and counts it. A retried confirm counts nothing.

__VisitCountPolicy.doc.#: Which recorded visits are COUNTED (increment the counter, feed actor state). Every visit is still kept in the history.
__VisitCountPolicy.doc.oncePerSession: One counted visit per object per session.
__VisitCountPolicy.doc.oncePerActor: One counted visit per object per actor, ever.
__VisitCountPolicy.doc.oncePerActorPerWindow: One counted visit per object per actor within `countWindowSeconds`.

__InteractionSourceOrigin.doc.#: Where an interaction source descriptor comes from (recommendation ADR section 2).
__InteractionSourceOrigin.doc.pattern: Published by a pattern's shared reader from the pattern's own config (a catalog-bound shopping cart, visit tracking, ...). Computed, never stored in the blueprint, so it cannot go stale against the pattern.
__InteractionSourceOrigin.doc.declared: Declared by the designer under `recommendationSettings.sources` for a hand-modelled data model: the event object and a property path per role.

__InteractionSourcePattern.doc.#: The pattern that publishes a `from: pattern` interaction source.
__InteractionSourcePattern.doc.shoppingCart: A catalog-bound shopping cart: completed baskets, signal `ordered` (R1).
__InteractionSourcePattern.doc.visits: A visit-tracked object's history: view / read / seen (R2).

__RecommendationListKind.doc.#: What a recommendation list is anchored on and how it is served (recommendation ADR sections 4 and 5.4).
__RecommendationListKind.doc.related: Anchor-based alternatives or companions of one item: GET /<items>/:id/recommendations/<list>.
__RecommendationListKind.doc.complementary: Anchor-based complements of one item (bought together): GET /<items>/:id/recommendations/<list>.
__RecommendationListKind.doc.personalized: Actor-based, aggregated at request time from the neighbors of the actor's recent items (R4).
__RecommendationListKind.doc.next: Anchor-based: what is consumed after this item (R4).

__RecommendationRelation.doc.#: The evidence relation a list is computed from (recommendation ADR section 3). Name the relation, not the algorithm; relations are never blended silently.
__RecommendationRelation.doc.coPurchased: Two items in one completed basket. Needs the item, group and validWhen roles.
__RecommendationRelation.doc.coConsumed: The same actor consumed both items within a window. Needs the item, actor and time roles.
__RecommendationRelation.doc.coViewed: The same session viewed both items (alternatives being compared). Never fed by purchase sources (R2).
__RecommendationRelation.doc.consumedAfter: The actor consumed B after A within a gap (R2).
__RecommendationRelation.doc.popularity: A count of interactions per item (time-decayed from R2). Needs the item and time roles.
__RecommendationRelation.doc.repeat: The same actor consumed the same item more than once (R4).
__RecommendationRelation.doc.similarContent: Embedding or attribute similarity. Cold-start fallback only (R6).

__RecommendationScoring.doc.#: How a co-occurrence pair is scored (recommendation ADR section 5.1). Raw `count` is never the default.
__RecommendationScoring.doc.count: The raw co-occurrence count. Debugging only: popular items dominate.
__RecommendationScoring.doc.cosine: nij / sqrt(ni * nj). Popularity-normalized and stable. The default.
__RecommendationScoring.doc.lift: nij * N / (ni * nj), with minSupport. Unstable on rare pairs, so opt-in.
__RecommendationScoring.doc.llr: Dunning log-likelihood ratio: the robust significance test for sparse co-occurrence.

__RecommendationEngine.doc.#: What computes a list's neighbor / popularity table (recommendation ADR section 5.3). The table is the common output contract, so the serving api does not know which engine filled it.
__RecommendationEngine.doc.sql: Co-occurrence by self-join of the source rows in the service database, top-K per item. The default, and the only engine emitted in R1.
__RecommendationEngine.doc.compute: A ComputeJob (ALS, item-kNN at scale) writing the neighbor table back (R6).

__VisitTracking.doc: Object-level visit storage (docs/ADR-object-visits-pattern.md section 2.1): WHERE the visits of this object go. The history table `sys_<Obj>Visit` is an analytics fact table (visit id, object id, tenant, actor key, user and session, signal, status, api name, controller, list attribution, the frozen `context` fields, server timestamps); the counter and the per-actor state are projections of it. The api-level `visitSettings` decides which call records a visit. Tenant and actor are stamped from the session, never accepted from the client. History and actor-state rows are personal data. No authorization or filtering decision may read a visit (ADR hard rule 1).

VisitTracking.__enabled.doc: Turns visit tracking on for this object. False (the default) leaves the block inert: no visit table, no host column, no injected api, and the object is generated exactly as without the block. The other fields are only checked while this is true.
VisitTracking.__history.doc: Keep the raw event log `sys_<Obj>Visit`, one row per visit: the analytics and recommendation source, and the truth every counter can be rebuilt from. Default true.
VisitTracking.__historyRetentionDays.doc: Raw history rows older than this many days are deleted by a generated retention cron, after rollup. Null (the default) keeps them. Emitted by slice V4; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__actorState.doc: Keep one row per (actor, object) in `sys_<Obj>VisitState` (first / last seen, first / last read, visit count): read receipts, seen, unread counts, new since your last visit. Default false. Emitted by slice V3; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__counterProperty.doc: A host column of this object incremented once per COUNTED visit (see `visitSettings.countPolicy`). When the named property does not exist the framework adds it as a framework-managed Integer column. The column is QUIET: its increments emit no db event, trigger no Elasticsearch re-projection and invalidate no entity cache, so a hot page never amplifies writes (ADR section 6.2). Null (the default) keeps no counter. An engagement metric, never an authorization or billing input.
VisitTracking.__uniqueCounterProperty.doc: A host column incremented once per DISTINCT actor; it reads `actorState`, so it requires it. Quiet like `counterProperty`. Emitted by slice V3; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__ownerReadMapping.doc: Owner-row read flags for a SINGLE-recipient object (a mailbox message, a personal notification): the use case of the retired `setAsRead`, now a by-product of visits. Applied only when the visiting actor is the row's owner (the object must declare an `isOwnerField`), through the quiet update path after the response. Each value is MScript over `{ now, signal }`, e.g. `isRead: true`, `readAt: now`. Emitted by slice V3; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__anonymousVisits.doc: Record visits that carry only an anonymous session key. The actor key is then the session id, read by the guest-cart rule (the session, else the `X-Session-Id` header the frontend mints and persists). Default true; false drops anonymous visits. Anonymous rows are not re-keyed when the visitor later logs in.
VisitTracking.__publishVisitEvent.doc: Publish `<obj>.visited` (the unified event envelope) after each counted visit. Default false. Emitted by slice V5; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__elasticLog.doc: Name of a declared ElasticLog every visit is also appended to: an optional downstream sink, the relational history stays the source of truth. Emitted by slice V5; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.
VisitTracking.__eventStream.doc: Name of a declared EventStream every visit is also appended to, through a server-side ingest that stamps actor and tenant from the session (ADR section 6.4). Emitted by slice V5; until then a declared value is reported as VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning), so the knob never silently does nothing.

__VisitSettings.doc: Api-level visit trigger (docs/ADR-object-visits-pattern.md section 2.2). It declares which call of this BusinessApi records a visit of its data object, with which signal, how the visit is confirmed and which visits are counted. The api's object must declare an enabled `objectSettings.visitTracking` (the storage decision is made once per object). The recording runs after the response, skipped on errors, idempotent replays, completed misses, unlisted controllers and `excludeRoles`. The frontend contract (the `_visit` block and the confirm route) is documented in the generated frontend prompt docs.

VisitSettings.__enabled.doc: Makes this api a visit source. False (the default) leaves the block inert. Requires an enabled `visitTracking` on the api's data object (VISIT_TRACKING_NOT_DECLARED).
VisitSettings.__signal.doc: What a successful call records (VisitSignal): `access` (a served get, unconfirmed; the default), `view` and `read` (a get confirmed by the frontend), `seen` (each row of a list page, an impression). `access`, `view` and `read` record a visit of ONE object: they require a `get` api, or `targetIdFrom` naming the visited id on an api of another crudType (a frontend confirmation, which `view` and `read` call for, requires a `get`); `seen` requires a `list` api. `access` is emitted by slice V1, `view` and `read` by V2, `seen` by V3; until then `seen` is reported as VISIT_SETTINGS_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning).
