VisitSettings.__confirmation.doc: How the visit becomes countable (VisitConfirmation): `none` (the default) counts it when the response is sent; `frontend` (slice V2) returns `_visit { visitId, confirmPath, minVisibleSeconds, expiresAt }`, writes a pending row and counts it only when the frontend confirms after the visible dwell time. `frontend` requires `minVisibleSeconds` or `minScrollPercent`, and is refused with `signal: access` (an access is unconfirmed by definition).
VisitSettings.__minVisibleSeconds.doc: Frontend confirmation: the visible dwell time, in seconds, the client measures (Page Visibility pauses the clock while the tab is hidden) before it confirms. The server verifies the ELAPSED time since it minted the visit; visibility itself is a client claim.
VisitSettings.__minScrollPercent.doc: Frontend confirmation: an optional scroll-depth criterion, 0-100. A client claim, stored on the history row for analysis and never trusted for counting.
VisitSettings.__confirmTtlSeconds.doc: How long, in seconds, a pending visit can still be confirmed. Expiry is lazy: no sweep runs, and a row stays `pending` until a confirm arrives after the TTL, which answers 410 VISIT_EXPIRED and flips that row to `expired`. An expired or never-confirmed row stays in the history and is never counted; analysis should treat a `pending` row older than the TTL as expired. Default 1800.
VisitSettings.__countPolicy.doc: Which recorded visits are COUNTED (VisitCountPolicy): `everyVisit` (the default), `oncePerSession`, `oncePerActor`, `oncePerActorPerWindow`. Every visit is still kept in the history. The policies other than `everyVisit` are emitted by slice V2 and judged against the history table: on a relational service the judgement is serialized per object (the host row is locked for the transaction); on MongoDB it is BEST EFFORT (no transaction), so two concurrent first visits of one actor (or session) may both count - the atomic per-key claim is planned in V4.
VisitSettings.__countWindowSeconds.doc: The window, in seconds, of `countPolicy: oncePerActorPerWindow`. Required by that policy, ignored by the others.
VisitSettings.__excludeRoles.doc: Roles whose calls never record a visit (admins, editors, support staff): their reads are not consumption.
VisitSettings.__controllers.doc: The controller kinds whose calls record a visit. Default ["rest"]: MCP, gRPC, Kafka, cron and internal calls are not visits unless listed here (e.g. `mcp`).
VisitSettings.__targetIdFrom.doc: An MScript that yields the id of the visited object. On a `get` with `confirmation: none` it replaces the id of the row the get resolved (the default); on an api of any other crudType it is REQUIRED for the `access`, `view` and `read` signals, since such an api has no single resolved row to take the id from. Ignored on a frontend-confirmed get (warning VISIT_TARGET_ID_IGNORED): there the visited id is the row the get and its confirm route addressed.
VisitSettings.__context.doc: Analytic dimensions frozen on every history row at visit time. Each entry is `{ name, from }`, where `from` is an MScript over the api context (the request and the fetched object), e.g. `category` from `this.product.categoryId`, `campaign` from `this.request.query.utm_campaign`. Freezing matters: a row re-categorized next month must not rewrite last month's per-category interest.

__VisitContextField.doc: One analytic dimension captured on a visit history row (visits ADR section 2.3): its name in the row's `context` JSON, and the MScript that computes it at visit time.

VisitContextField.__name.doc: The key of this dimension in the history row's `context` JSON, e.g. `category`, `campaign`, `device`.
VisitContextField.__from.doc: MScript evaluated at visit time over the api context (the request and the fetched object), e.g. `this.product.categoryId`. The value is frozen on the row.
VisitContextField.name: String

__RecommendationSettings.doc: Recommendation lists of a data object as the ITEM being recommended (docs/ADR-recommendation-engine.md section 4). The pipeline per list: candidate generation from precomputed neighbor / popularity tables, deterministic filtering, scoring and ranking, list policy, serving with a `listRequestId`, impression logging. The lists live on the item's own service and inherit the item's read gate, tenant scope and visibility. No authorization or filtering decision may come from a recommendation score or a decision provider (ADR hard rule 1).

RecommendationSettings.__enabled.doc: Turns recommendations on for this object. False (the default) leaves the block inert: no neighbor or popularity table, no refresh cron, no serving api, and the object is generated exactly as without the block. The other fields are only checked while this is true.
RecommendationSettings.__sources.doc: Interaction sources DECLARED for this object's lists (`from: declared`), for a hand-modelled data model: the event object and a property path per role. Sources a pattern publishes (a catalog-bound shopping cart, visit tracking, ...) are discovered automatically and are never stored here, so they cannot go stale against the pattern.
RecommendationSettings.__lists.doc: The recommendation lists of this object. Each list is served under the object's own routes and carries the relation and the signal that produced each item, so the UI wording stays true.

__InteractionSource.doc: A resolved descriptor of interaction records with known roles (recommendation ADR section 2). It names the event object that holds the interactions, the property path that plays each of the item, group, actor, time and weight roles, the signal label, and the records that count. Patterns publish these from their own config; a designer declares one for a hand-modelled data model. The same contract later serves trend analytics, segmentation and repeat-purchase reporting.

InteractionSource.__name.doc: A unique name of this source among the object's sources; a list's evidence names it in `source`.
InteractionSource.__from.doc: Where the descriptor comes from (InteractionSourceOrigin). A source stored in the blueprint is `declared` (the default); `pattern` descriptors are computed by the pattern's shared reader and never stored.
InteractionSource.__pattern.doc: For a `from: pattern` descriptor: the publishing pattern (InteractionSourcePattern).
InteractionSource.__patternTarget.doc: For a `from: pattern` descriptor: which instance of the pattern, when the service has several (a cart config name, a visit-tracked object name).
InteractionSource.__eventObject.doc: For a `from: declared` source: the data object whose rows are the interaction records (an order line, a play event).
InteractionSource.__itemProperty.doc: Property path, on the event object, to the item key. A path is a property of the event object or `<relation>.<property>` one relation hop away (a relation property, or the `<object>Id` foreign key of an object of the same service); deeper paths are refused (RECOMMENDATION_SOURCE_PATH_UNRESOLVED).
InteractionSource.__itemLookup.doc: The item object's property the item key matches. Default `id`; a catalog cart keyed by barcode names `barcode`.
InteractionSource.__groupProperty.doc: Property path to the group that `together` means: a basket, a session, a conversation. Required by `coPurchased` and `coViewed`.
InteractionSource.__actorProperty.doc: Property path to the actor: a user id or an anonymous session key. Relation traversal is allowed (`order.ownerId`). Required by `coConsumed`, `consumedAfter` and `repeat`.
InteractionSource.__timeProperty.doc: Property path to the interaction time. Required by the windowed and decayed relations.
InteractionSource.__signal.doc: The signal label of these interactions (`ordered`, `purchase`, `view`, `read`, `attend`, ...). Every recommendation response carries it, so a list built on `ordered` never claims `bought`.
InteractionSource.__validWhen.doc: A where-clause (MScript query) selecting the records that count, e.g. `({ status: ['placed', 'shipped'] })`. Evaluated once per refresh, so it may use literals but no request value; its keys are properties of the event object or of an object a role path reaches (`order.status`), and its operators are equality, arrays (IN), `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$exists`, `$and`, `$or` and `$not`. A clause outside that vocabulary fails the refresh rather than counting every record.
InteractionSource.__weightProperty.doc: Property path to an optional interaction strength, e.g. a line quantity.
InteractionSource.name: String

__RecommendationList.doc: One recommendation list of an item object (recommendation ADR section 4). It declares the list kind, the evidence relations that feed it, how pairs are scored, how much is precomputed and served, the deterministic filters and list policy, and the engine and refresh schedule. Presets (bought together, readers also read, trending) are authoring presets that expand into an ordinary list; they are not ontology.

RecommendationList.__name.doc: The list name, unique on the object: it names the serving route (`.../recommendations/<name>`), the `_rec.list` label of every served item, and a fallback reference. It does not key the precomputed rows: the shared neighbor / popularity tables are keyed by the relation key (relation, source set, window), so lists that resolve to the same key share rows. E.g. `boughtTogether`.
RecommendationList.__kind.doc: What the list is anchored on (RecommendationListKind): `related`, `complementary` and `next` take an anchor item; `personalized` and `buyAgain` take the actor; `trending` is global. Nodejs emits `personalized`, `buyAgain` and `next`; other language runtimes retain RECOMMENDATION_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning) for those kinds until ported. Nodejs actor lists first select the latest 500 raw actor events per evidence source in its tenant scope, then apply validWhen and windowDays. Seed selection and repeat frequency/recency are bounded approximations: invalid events occupy the budget and older repeats can be omitted. The fixed runtime constant is RECOMMENDATION_ACTOR_EVENT_WINDOW. Missing declared-source actor/time indexes can still require a database scan or sort; RECOMMENDATION_ACTOR_HISTORY_INDEX_MISSING warns for discoverable same-table source paths without a full-domain leading actor/time composite index.
RecommendationList.__evidence.doc: The relations that feed the list, each with its source and weight. Blending relations is explicit, never silent, and the response names the relation that produced each item.
RecommendationList.__scoring.doc: How co-occurrence pairs are scored (RecommendationScoring). Default `cosine`: popularity-normalized, so an item bought everywhere does not top every list.
RecommendationList.__windowDays.doc: How far back, in days, interactions count. Null removes the age cutoff. Nodejs personalized and buyAgain still select only the latest 500 raw actor events per evidence source before applying validity and this age cutoff.
RecommendationList.__decayHalfLifeDays.doc: Half-life, in days, of popularity and actor-list recency decay. Each interaction contributes `weight * 0.5^(ageDays / halfLife)` to popularity; null or omission disables popularity decay. Nodejs `personalized` and `buyAgain` use the latest interaction time and default to 30 days when null or omitted. Other list kinds and language runtimes retain RECOMMENDATION_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning) for unsupported non-popularity decay.
RecommendationList.__minSupport.doc: Minimum number of co-occurrences before a pair exists. Default 3.
RecommendationList.__maxGroupSize.doc: Groups (baskets, sessions) larger than this are sampled, which bounds the pair blow-up. Default 50.
RecommendationList.__storedNeighbors.doc: Top-K neighbors kept per item in the neighbor table. Default 50.
RecommendationList.__size.doc: Items returned per request. Default 10; the `fallback` lists fill a short list up to it.
RecommendationList.__filters.doc: Deterministic filters re-applied to every candidate at serve time (RecommendationFilters). Neighbor tables are stale by up to one refresh, so a precomputed neighbor is never returned without passing them, the item's read gate and the item get api's whereClause. A row rule of the get api that reads a request parameter cannot be applied by the list (it closes the list); express it here instead.
RecommendationList.__listPolicy.doc: Diversity and dedupe rules applied to the filtered, ranked page (RecommendationListPolicy).
RecommendationList.__rerank.doc: Optional bounded, fail-open rerank of the filtered candidate page by a decision provider (RecommendationRerank). Emitted by slice R5; until then a declared value is reported as RECOMMENDATION_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning).
RecommendationList.__fallback.doc: Names of other lists of this object, tried in order while this list returns fewer than `size` items.
RecommendationList.__engine.doc: What computes the list's table (RecommendationEngine). Default `sql`, the only engine emitted in R1; `clickhouse`, `compute` and `graph` arrive with slice R6, until then a declared value is reported as RECOMMENDATION_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning).
RecommendationList.__refreshCron.doc: Cron schedule of the refresh job that recomputes the list's table. Default every six hours.
RecommendationList.__api.doc: Serving-route options (RecommendationApi). Null serves the list on the default route behind the item's read gate: the item get api's login, roles and ownership, its whereClause applied to every candidate (on a get api with no id parameter the whereClause is a ROW FILTER: every matching candidate is served, not the get api's first row; the latest-record fallback restricts nothing), and the response redaction that get api applies to its answer (the removeFromResponse actions placed in its afterBuildOutput stage, conditional ones included) applied to every served item.
RecommendationList.__logImpressions.doc: Record every served item as a `seen` impression with its position and the `listRequestId`, the basis of click-through evaluation. Default true. Nodejs writes the final served page (after the filters, the fallback and the size limit) as `seen` rows with zero-based positions and one `listRequestId` per response, after the response and fail-open; it needs visitTracking with history on the item object (without history nothing is recorded). Other language runtimes do not record impressions yet.
RecommendationList.name: String

__RecommendationEvidence.doc: One evidence relation of a recommendation list (recommendation ADR section 3): the relation, the source that feeds it and its weight in an explicit blend.

RecommendationEvidence.__relation.doc: The evidence relation (RecommendationRelation). All implemented recommendation runtimes emit `coPurchased`, `coConsumed` and `popularity`. Nodejs also emits `coViewed` and `consumedAfter`, and serves `repeat` at request time for `buyAgain`. Other runtimes retain RECOMMENDATION_NOT_YET_EMITTED (warning) for those later relations until ported. `similarContent` remains pending R6.
RecommendationEvidence.__source.doc: The interaction source that feeds the relation: a declared source's name, or `auto` (the default) for every discovered and declared source that carries the relation's required roles. A relation is never fed by a source of the wrong kind (coViewed never by purchases).
RecommendationEvidence.__weight.doc: The relation's weight when a list blends several relations. Default 1.

__RecommendationFilters.doc: Deterministic serve-time filters of a recommendation list (recommendation ADR section 5.2). They are re-applied to every candidate while it is hydrated; none of them may be a decision-provider call.

RecommendationFilters.__visibleWhen.doc: MScript over the candidate row: the item's visibility rule (e.g. published), on top of its read gate and tenant.
RecommendationFilters.__availableWhen.doc: MScript over the candidate row: stock or availability.
RecommendationFilters.__compatibleWhen.doc: MScript over `{ anchor, candidate }` for anchor-based lists: structured compatibility, e.g. `candidate.batteryType == anchor.batteryType`. Compatibility is a filter, never a score.
RecommendationFilters.__excludeConsumedBy.doc: A source name or a signal label (`shoppingCart`, `ordered`, ...): items the calling actor (the user, or a guest cart's session) already has in a matching source that records an actor are dropped at serve time. Nodejs `buyAgain` ignores this filter because repeated acquisitions are its candidates. Nodejs `personalized` also excludes consumed items from its own evidence sources across all retained valid history, including outside its seed window.

__RecommendationListPolicy.doc: Diversity and dedupe rules of a recommendation list, applied to the filtered, ranked page.

RecommendationListPolicy.__dedupeBy.doc: Property of the item object: at most one item per value is returned (e.g. one variant per product group).
RecommendationListPolicy.__maxPerValueProperty.doc: Property of the item object whose values are capped by `maxPerValueCount` (e.g. brand).
RecommendationListPolicy.__maxPerValueCount.doc: The most items returned per value of `maxPerValueProperty`.

__RecommendationRerank.doc: Optional decision-provider rerank of a recommendation list (recommendation ADR section 7). One batched, bounded request covers the filtered candidate page, and it always fails open: a provider error returns the unreranked list. It only ranks: it never generates candidates and never filters. Emitted by slice R5.

RecommendationRerank.__providerName.doc: Name of the `projectSettings.decisionProvidersSettings.decisionProviders[]` entry that reranks.
RecommendationRerank.__model.doc: The PINNED model version the rerank runs on (decision-layer rule: a floating tag is refused).
RecommendationRerank.__instructions.doc: What the provider judges per candidate, e.g. how well the item suits the anchor and the user's recent items.
RecommendationRerank.__maxCandidates.doc: The most candidates sent in the one batched request. Default 50.
RecommendationRerank.__blend.doc: final = blend * decision score + (1 - blend) * neighbor score. Default 0.5.

__RecommendationApi.doc: Serving-route options of a recommendation list (recommendation ADR section 5.4).

RecommendationApi.__routePath.doc: Overrides the list's route path (a leading slash is added). Null serves `GET /<items>/:<item>Id/recommendations/<list>` for an anchor-based list (related, complementary, next) and `GET /<items>/recommendations/<list>` for an actor-based or global one; `<items>` is the plural item collection of the default BusinessApi routes, and each route is also mounted under `/v1`.
RecommendationApi.__exposePublic.doc: Null (the default) inherits the read gate of the item object's get api: its login, checkRoles, absoluteRoles and ownership (a login-free get api skips checkRoles, ownershipCheck and parentOwnershipChecks, and so does the list), and its whereClause, which the list APPLIES to every candidate for every caller, absolute roles included (a row rule is logic, not authorization), when it reads only constants, LIB, the addressed id and the caller's session; a whereClause or a removeFromResponse condition that reads anything else (a request parameter) closes the list to every caller (403 RECOMMENDATION_GATE_NOT_INHERITED). With a get api on the item, it never widens that gate: true is ignored (RECOMMENDATION_EXPOSE_PUBLIC_IGNORED over a login-required get api) and false forces a login. With no get api on the item: false admits any logged-in caller; true serves the list without a session only when the item's dataObjectAccess is accessPublic, and over any other object the list stays closed (RECOMMENDATION_NO_READ_GATE), as it does when unset.
